# Algomancy Comprehensive Rules

*Unofficial. Generated from this project's digital client.*

## Introduction

**This document is UNOFFICIAL.** It describes this digital client's
implementation of Algomancy, not Caleb Gannon's game. Where it and the
published Manual disagree, the Manual is the game and this document is our
client. The card text and rules text it quotes are Caleb Gannon's, used with
permission on the terms in `data/NOTICE.md`.

Edition: First generation (draft). Effective 2026-10-10. Engine at commit 76d01fa.

### How to read a rule

Under each rule are only its words, its examples and two warnings: "engine
differs" and Untested. Everything else, its provenance, is folded
under the rule as "Sources and verification" in the HTML edition and on the
review page, and is the small line beneath it in the .md and .txt editions:
the sources that state the rule, the tests bound to it, and the two marks
below. Each rule carries a **basis**, the strongest kind of source
that actually states it. A Printed rule is stated by the Manual, the
2023 Rulebook or a card's printed text, read literally; a Designer rule
by Caleb Gannon's own answer in the rules-questions threads; a Mixed
rule by more than one kind of source together. An Owner call rule is a
ruling by this project's owner, with no designer source: it is the client's
law, and it may not be the game's. An Engine only rule is stated by no
source; it is what the engine does, and it is listed in Annex P to await the
owner's sign-off.

Our own glossary is quoted where it helps, and is never counted as a source.

Where a ruling and the engine disagree, the rule states the ruling and says
"engine differs", with a link to the finding. The engine is the one that is
wrong, and the finding is filed as a bug.

Each rule's provenance also says what an independent verifier found when it
checked the rule against the engine and its tests: Confirmed, or
Partial when it could not confirm all of it, with the verifier's note.
A rule that is not confirmed shows its verdict on the fold itself. Beside the
verdict are the round it was verified in, how many tests the verifier ran,
and how many gate test files are bound to the rule through its examples or its
sources. A gate test is part of the client's test suite and runs on every
check, so it keeps demonstrating the rule after verification is over. A rule
that no executed test demonstrates is marked Untested.

### Examples are not rules

An example illustrates the rule above it: an illustration, never a rule in
its own right, and where it seems to say more than the rule, the rule wins.
Most examples are bound to a test that was run and asserts them; the test is
named in the rule's provenance. Some rules are demonstrated by a test with no
example in words; that test is named there too.

### How numbering works

Rules are numbered in three levels: section 608, rule 608.2, subrule 608.2b.
Subrule letters skip l and o. A number, once published, never moves and is
never reused. A new rule goes to the end of its section, even when it would
read better earlier. A removed rule keeps its number and reads
"[Removed: …]". Section 802 has one rule per attribute, in the engine's own
order.

## 1. Game Concepts

<a id="r100"></a>
### 100. General

<a id="r100.1"></a>**100.1.** In Algomancy, each player's goal is to eliminate all of their opponents. A player is eliminated by bringing their life total to 0. See rule 104.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.6; Manual p.6; Rulebook 2023 p.1 · Tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 412-cr-general.test.ts::cr:concepts.general.goal — bringing a player to 0 life eliminates them and the other player wins the game · Key: concepts.general.goal</sub>

<a id="r100.2"></a>**100.2.** The game is played as a series of global turns. Every player goes through each turn's phases together. See rule 500.

> *Example: One player finishing planning does not start the battle, and one player finishing deployment does not end the turn: both players move on together, into the same turn 2.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.6; Manual p.6 · Tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts · Example test: 412-cr-general.test.ts::cr:concepts.general.turns — one turn counter and one phase for the table: a phase waits for both seats, and both enter turn 2 together · Key: concepts.general.turns</sub>

<a id="r100.3"></a>**100.3.** A game combines a game mode (such as live draft or constructed) with a player setup (such as 1v1, free-for-all or teams). Any game mode can be played with any player setup. See rule 900. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.1; Manual p.6; Manual p.6 · Key: concepts.general.formats</sub>

<a id="r100.4"></a>**100.4.** *(Digital client)* The digital client this document describes plays two-player games only: 1v1 live draft and 1v1 constructed. See rule 900.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 20-draft.test.ts::createGame draft: 6-card hands, 34-constructed.test.ts::createGame constructed: per-seat decks · Key: concepts.general.digital-scope</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U01-9 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r101"></a>
### 101. Golden Rules

<a id="r101.1"></a>**101.1.** Printed text beats the general rules and the engine's defaults. Where a card's printed text says something different from a general rule or a default, the card is followed, unless the designer has stated a different intent for that card (rule 101.2). See rules 400.4b, 101.2.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Demonstrated by test: 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts::§27: Grob caches a STOLEN unit · Key: concepts.golden.printed-text-wins</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U01-11, D-U01-5 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r101.2"></a>**101.2.** Where the designer has stated that his intent for a card differs from its printed wording, the card works as the designer intended. See rule 802.

> *Example: Crevice Lurker prints "Abilities cost [one] more to activate or trigger during battle". By Caleb's stated intent it also taxes the {Resonant} attribute's trigger.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1366446116274442291#1 · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ trigger-like attributes: Crevice Lurker taxes Resonant · Key: concepts.golden.designer-intent</sub>

<a id="r101.3"></a>**101.3.** A designer answer in the rules Q&A (RAQ) takes precedence over this project's own rulings. Where the two disagree, this document states the designer's answer. See rule 101.2. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-10 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Key: concepts.golden.raq-over-rulings</sub>

<a id="r101.4"></a>**101.4.** When a card's text can be read two ways and neither reading is absurd, take the reading that lets more things happen. See rule 101.1. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Key: concepts.golden.permissive</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U01-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r101.5"></a>**101.5.** An effect that cannot do everything it says does as much as it can. A part of an effect that cannot happen does not stop the other parts from happening. This does not make half of an action happen: a fight or an exchange that has lost one of its two units does not happen at all (704). See rule 704.

> *Example: Recall: "Each player recalls a unit and loses 2 life." A player with no unit to recall still loses 2 life.*

> *Example: Amphivore carries two grafts, Flame Juggle and Ralph, and its ability runs three times. The first pass gives Amphivore to the opponent and makes three 1/1s; later passes cannot give it again, so their "If you do" makes nothing, but Flame Juggle still happens all three times.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.43; Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1353859961855148103#3 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Example tests: 179-empty-collection-branches.test.ts::Recall — the life loss happens, the recall does not, 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Amphivore with Ralph grafted · Key: concepts.golden.as-much-as-possible</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U01-15 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r101.5a"></a>**101.5a** A part of an effect that begins "If you do" happens only if the action before it was done. Parts that are not joined this way are independent. See rule 101.5.

> *Example: Shoreline Specter: "After combat, you may recall target ally. If you do, each opponent loses 2 life." If its controller declines the recall, no opponent loses life.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Shoreline Specter · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Example test: 182-correctness-sample.test.ts::Shoreline Specter: DECLINE the recall and the 2-life drain does not happen · Key: concepts.golden.as-much-as-possible.if-you-do</sub>

<a id="r101.5b"></a>**101.5b** Paying a cost is not done "as much as you can". A cost that cannot be paid in full is not paid at all, and the effect it pays for does not happen. See rule 111.

> *Example: Lost Guardian with Darkblast grafted must pay [Discard a card] twice. With one card in hand nothing is discarded and nothing happens.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353859961855148103#5 · Example test: 17-earth-b.test.ts::CR 111.14: all or nothing — one card in hand cannot pay a doubled [Discard a card] · Key: concepts.golden.as-much-as-possible.costs</sub>

<a id="r101.6"></a>**101.6.** Every effect is specific to the region it happens in. It never affects anything in another region, and it treats the players and cards in other regions as if they do not exist. A card that says "all" or "each" means all or each in this region. See rule 601. *(Engine differs, see F-U01-2.)*

> *Example: Cosmic Reversal, cast in one region, leaves a spell unit in another region alone.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 3; verifier ran 4 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.8; Manual p.19; Manual p.19; Manual p.42 · Designer: RAQ 1454169054402314362#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-29 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Example test: 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts::CR 601.1c: the board half is scoped to the region · Demonstrated by test: 243-ally-and-enemy-scope.test.ts::CR 601.4e no ally or enemy slot · Key: concepts.golden.regions</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U01-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r101.6a"></a>**101.6a** Regions limit what effects can reach and count. In the digital client they do not limit what players may see: a player may read what happens in a region they are not in. *(Digital client)* See rule 601.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-29 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 219-region-scoped-all.test.ts::§2b an event from a region you are not in is still yours to read · Key: concepts.golden.regions.information</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U01-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r102"></a>
### 102. Players, Ownership and Control

<a id="r102.1"></a>**102.1.** Each player has their own region and their own life total. See rules 601, 103.1d.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.19; Manual p.6 · Tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 412-cr-general.test.ts::cr:concepts.players.region-and-life — each seat owns a different home region, and a life loss of one seat leaves the life of the other alone · Key: concepts.players.region-and-life</sub>

<a id="r102.2"></a>**102.2.** "Each opponent" means each opponent in the region where the effect happens. See rules 101.6, 601.

> *Example: Bloated Manablub dies in a region where its opponent is present: that opponent loses 3 life and its controller loses none.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.42 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts · Example test: 412-cr-general.test.ts::cr:concepts.players.each-opponent — Bloated Manablub with the opponent present in the region takes 3 from that opponent only · Key: concepts.players.each-opponent</sub>

<a id="r102.2a"></a>**102.2a** If no opponent is in that region, an "each opponent" effect affects nobody. This is normal during deployment, when each player is alone in their own region. See rule 601.

> *Example: Bloated Manablub's "Each opponent loses 3 life" resolved in a region holding no opponent takes no life from anyone.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.42; Manual p.42 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Example test: 158-silent-region-branches.test.ts::Bloated Manablub — "Each opponent loses 3 life" · Key: concepts.players.each-opponent.none</sub>

<a id="r102.3"></a>**102.3.** "Each player" means each player in the region where the effect happens. See rule 101.6.

> *Example: Recall ("Each player recalls a unit and loses 2 life") cast in a battle makes both players present in that battle region lose 2 life.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.19 · Tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts · Example test: 15-water-b.test.ts::Recall: each player recalls a unit and loses 2 life · Key: concepts.players.each-player</sub>

<a id="r102.4"></a>**102.4.** A card's owner is the player whose card it is. A card's owner never changes, whoever controls it and whatever zone it goes to. See rules 400.4a, 400.4c. *(Engine differs, see F-U01-1.)*

> *Example: A unit whose control has been taken is recalled: the player it was stolen from is still the card's owner.*

> *Example: The same recalled unit goes to the hand of the player who controls it, not its owner's hand.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-29, 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Example tests: 246-zones-follow-control.test.ts::CR 400.4a: ownership does NOT move, 246-zones-follow-control.test.ts::CR 801.7a: a stolen unit recalled goes to the THIEF hand · Key: concepts.players.owner</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U01-10 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r102.4a"></a>**102.4a** A token is owned by the player who created it. See rule 304.

> *Example: Accelerated Germination makes two tokens owned by its caster; an Arcane Echo copy of an opposing token is owned by the copier; a token taken with Download stays owned by its creator.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts · Example test: 412-cr-general.test.ts::cr:concepts.players.owner.token — a token is owned by the player whose effect created it, and a control change does not move that · Key: concepts.players.owner.token</sub>

<a id="r102.5"></a>**102.5.** A card's controller is the player who controls it. The controller and the owner of a card can be different players. See rules 711, 400.4.

> *Example: Uglk: each player puts a unit from their own bin into play under the opponent's control. The opponent controls the unit; the card is still owned by the player whose bin it came from.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Uglk · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Example test: 93-engine-defects.test.ts::Uglk hands an opponent CONTROL of a unit without handing over the card · Key: concepts.players.controller</sub>

<a id="r102.5a"></a>**102.5a** Putting a card into play out of another player's zone makes you its controller, not its owner. See rule 400.4.

> *Example: Wake the Dead raising a unit out of the opponent's bin: the caster controls it, and the opponent still owns it.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Wake the Dead · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Example test: 93-engine-defects.test.ts::Wake the Dead raising a unit from the ENEMY bin gives the caster control, not ownership · Key: concepts.players.controller.from-other-zone</sub>

<a id="r102.6"></a>**102.6.** "You" on a card means the controller of the effect. An instruction that names no player (such as "Gain rot") is done by the controller of the effect. See rule 102.5.

> *Example: Primordial Coalescence (“Create three Wraiths and gain 2 Rot.”) gives its controller the Wraiths and the rot. Thought Extraction aimed at the opponent makes the opponent discard, and its “You gain 1 rot” still goes to its controller.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts · Example test: 412-cr-general.test.ts::cr:concepts.players.you — Primordial Coalescence and Thought Extraction controlled by a seat give that seat the Wraiths and the rot, never the other · Key: concepts.players.you</sub>

<a id="r102.6a"></a>**102.6a** On a mod, "you" means the controller of the unit the mod is on. A mod applied to another player's unit is controlled by that unit's controller, with its ability. See rule 720.

> *Example: Pathogenic Enclave augmented onto an enemy unit: when that unit despawns, its controller's tokens are deleted, not yours.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.34 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Key: concepts.players.you.mod</sub>

<a id="r102.6b"></a>**102.6b** "The deck" means the deck of the effect's controller: the shared deck in live draft, and that player's own deck in constructed. See rule 401.

> *Example: In constructed, Foretell glimpses the top card of its controller's own deck and leaves the opponent's deck alone. In live draft it glimpses the top card of the shared deck.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts · Example test: 412-cr-general.test.ts::cr:concepts.players.you.the-deck — Foretell glimpses from the own deck of its controller in constructed and from the shared deck in live draft · Key: concepts.players.you.the-deck</sub>

<a id="r102.6c"></a>**102.6c** When an effect needs a cost paid before it can happen, the player who would control the effect pays it. If that player does not pay, the effect does not happen. See rule 111.

> *Example: With an opponent's Crevice Lurker in the battle, a triggered ability asks its own controller whether to pay [one]; paying puts it on the stack.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355103348378042515#4 · Example test: 16-earth-a.test.ts::Crevice Lurker: CR 111.10g — a taxed trigger ASKS its controller · Demonstrated by test: 16-earth-a.test.ts::Crevice Lurker: CR 111.10h — declining prevents the trigger · Key: concepts.players.you.pays</sub>

<a id="r102.7"></a>**102.7.** An ally is a unit under your control in the region where the effect is happening. See rules 110, 601.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Demonstrated by test: 243-ally-and-enemy-scope.test.ts::CR 102.7 ally is measured from the EFFECT controller · Key: concepts.players.ally</sub>

<a id="r102.7a"></a>**102.7a** A unit is its own ally. Only the word "another" leaves the source out. See rule 110.

> *Example: Shoreline Specter's "recall target ally" may target the Specter itself.*

> *Example: Riftwalker's "another target ally in my formation" offers its column-mate and not itself.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Riftwalker · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Example tests: 243-ally-and-enemy-scope.test.ts::CR 110.4a an ally target offers the source, 243-ally-and-enemy-scope.test.ts::CR 102.7a the ANOTHER side · Key: concepts.players.ally.self</sub>

<a id="r102.7b"></a>**102.7b** Ally and enemy follow control, not ownership. A unit you have taken control of is your ally and its owner's enemy for as long as you control it. See rule 711.

> *Example: A Good Whale whose control was taken is offered to its new controller as an ally target, and not to its owner.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts · Example test: 412-cr-general.test.ts::cr:concepts.players.ally.control — a unit you have taken control of is on your ally menu and off the ally menu of its owner · Key: concepts.players.ally.control</sub>

<a id="r102.8"></a>**102.8.** An enemy is a unit not under your control in the region where the effect is happening. See rule 102.7.

> *Example: The same stolen Good Whale is offered to its owner as an enemy target, and not to the player who now controls it.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts · Example test: 412-cr-general.test.ts::cr:concepts.players.enemy — a unit taken from its owner is on the enemy menu of that owner and off the enemy menu of its controller · Key: concepts.players.enemy</sub>

<a id="r103"></a>
### 103. Starting the Game

<a id="r103.1"></a>**103.1.** To set up a live draft game, follow these steps in order. See rule 902. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.11; Manual p.11; Manual p.11; Manual p.11 · Key: concepts.starting.live-draft</sub>

<a id="r103.1a"></a>**103.1a** Choose the elements the deck is built from. A game of 2 or 3 players uses 3 elements. See rules 105, 902.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.11; Manual p.11 · Tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 412-cr-general.test.ts::cr:concepts.starting.live-draft.elements — a standard 1v1 live draft is built from exactly 3 elements, and a chosen trio is used as given · Key: concepts.starting.live-draft.elements</sub>

<a id="r103.1b"></a>**103.1b** Shuffle all the cards of the chosen elements together, with the hybrid cards for each pair of chosen elements, to form the shared deck. See rules 401, 902.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.11; Manual p.11; Manual p.11 · Demonstrated by test: 20-draft.test.ts::draft deck: the fire+water+earth trio is Manual-exact · Key: concepts.starting.live-draft.deck</sub>

<a id="r103.1c"></a>**103.1c** Randomly choose one player to have the initiative. See rules 500, 508.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.11; Rulebook 2023 p.2 · Tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 412-cr-general.test.ts::cr:concepts.starting.live-draft.initiative — the first initiative is a seeded coin flip: either seat can get it, and the same seed gives the same seat · Key: concepts.starting.live-draft.initiative</sub>

<a id="r103.1d"></a>**103.1d** Each player's life total starts at 30. See rule 112.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.6; Rulebook 2023 p.2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-14 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 412-cr-general.test.ts::cr:concepts.starting.live-draft.life — each seat starts a live draft (and a shared-deck game) at 30 life · Key: concepts.starting.live-draft.life</sub>

<a id="r103.1e"></a>**103.1e** Give each player two prismites. They start dormant. See rule 106.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.11; Manual p.18 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Demonstrated by test: 01-planning.test.ts::setup & planning · Key: concepts.starting.live-draft.prismites</sub>

<a id="r103.1f"></a>**103.1f** Deal each player 16 cards from the shared deck: 4 for their starting hand, 10 for their pack, and 2 for the draw of their first turn. The 4 and the 2 together are the player's opening hand of 6 cards. See rules 409, 503.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.11; Manual p.11 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-14 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 20-draft.test.ts::createGame draft: 6-card hands · Key: concepts.starting.live-draft.deal</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U01-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r103.2"></a>**103.2.** In live draft, the first turn's draw is dealt with the opening hand, so players do not draw in the draw step of the first turn. See rules 503, 103.3a.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.16; Manual p.16; Manual p.16; Rulebook 2023 p.6 · Tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 20-draft.test.ts::createGame draft: 6-card hands (opening 4 + turn-1 draws) · Key: concepts.starting.no-first-draw</sub>

<a id="r103.3"></a>**103.3.** In constructed there is no shared deck and there are no packs. Each player plays from their own deck. See rules 901, 503.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.10 · Demonstrated by test: 34-constructed.test.ts::createGame constructed: per-seat decks · Key: concepts.starting.constructed</sub>

<a id="r103.3a"></a>**103.3a** In constructed, the first turn has a draw phase like every later turn: each player draws 4 cards, then puts 2 cards from their hand on the bottom of their deck. Print gives the draw phase; no source says the first turn takes it, which is the client's convention. *(Digital client)* See rules 503, 103.3b, 103.2.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 3; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.6 · Engine: createGame · Tests: 34-constructed.test.ts::createGame constructed: per-seat decks, opening 4 + draw 4, 412-cr-general.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 34-constructed.test.ts::createGame constructed: per-seat decks, opening 4 + draw 4 · Key: concepts.starting.constructed.first-draw</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U01-13 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r103.3b"></a>**103.3b** *(Digital client)* In constructed, each player's opening hand is 4 cards. No source gives the constructed opening hand; it is the client's convention. See rules 103.3a, 103.2.

<sub>Basis: Engine only · Verified: confirmed in round 3; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Engine: createGame · Tests: 34-constructed.test.ts::createGame constructed: per-seat decks, opening 4 + draw 4, 412-cr-general.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 34-constructed.test.ts::createGame constructed: per-seat decks, opening 4 + draw 4 · Key: concepts.starting.constructed.opening-hand</sub>

<a id="r104"></a>
### 104. Ending the Game

<a id="r104.1"></a>**104.1.** A player whose life total reaches 0 is eliminated. See rule 112.

> *Example: Haunting Memories sets a player's life total to twice the number of cards in all bins. With every bin empty that is 0, and that player loses.*

> *Example: A player at 3 life takes combat damage from an unblocked attacker and the game is over.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.6; Rulebook 2023 p.1 · Example tests: 46-hybrids-ld-c.test.ts::Haunting Memories: empty bins set the target to 0, 02-combat.test.ts::win condition · Key: concepts.ending.elimination</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U01-4 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r104.1a"></a>**104.1a** A life total reaching 0 ends the game at once, even in the middle of resolving an effect or paying a cost. Nothing waits for the effect to finish. A life cost that would by itself bring its payer to 0 cannot be paid at all (111). See rules 111, 112.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::CR 802.22b {Blessed}: without the attribute the same shot is lethal · Key: concepts.ending.elimination.immediate</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U01-14 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r104.2"></a>**104.2.** A player wins when all of their opponents have been eliminated. In a two-player game, when one player is eliminated the other player wins. See rule 104.1.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.1; Manual p.6 · Demonstrated by test: 02-combat.test.ts::win condition · Key: concepts.ending.win</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U01-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r104.2a"></a>**104.2a** In a team game, a team wins when the entire opposing team has been eliminated. See rule 904. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.1 · Key: concepts.ending.win.teams</sub>

<a id="r104.3"></a>**104.3.** In a game of more than two players, the game continues after a player is eliminated. The regions on either side of the eliminated player's region become neighbours. See rules 601, 903. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.19; Manual p.19; Rulebook 2023 p.8 · Key: concepts.ending.continues</sub>

<a id="r104.3a"></a>**104.3a** When a player is eliminated, their pack is recycled: put on the bottom of the deck. See rules 408, 409. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.16; Rulebook 2023 p.6 · Key: concepts.ending.continues.pack</sub>

<a id="r104.4"></a>**104.4.** A player may concede. Conceding ends the game in the same way as that player being eliminated: the player who conceded loses. See rule 104.1.

> *Example: A player concedes during deployment: the game is over and the other player has won.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Example test: 58-playtest-round9.test.ts::CR 104.4: conceding ends the game the way a lethal blow does · Key: concepts.ending.concede</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U01-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r104.4a"></a>**104.4a** A player may concede at any time, with no priority and in any phase, even while a decision is waiting on them. See rule 104.4.

> *Example: A player who must choose a target for their own spell may concede instead; nothing else can be done until they choose.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Example test: 58-playtest-round9.test.ts::CR 104.4a: you may concede even while a decision is pending against you · Demonstrated by test: 130-seat-aware-gate.test.ts::CR D2.1e: concede is always reachable · Key: concepts.ending.concede.any-time</sub>

<a id="r104.5"></a>**104.5.** Running out of cards does not end the game. A player who has to draw from an empty deck draws as many as there are and does not lose. See rules 401, 408.

> *Example: A player with an empty deck and an empty recycle pile is told to draw 3: nothing is drawn, and nobody has won.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Example test: 300-recycle-mark.test.ts::CR 401.4 an empty deck AND an empty pile draws fewer · Key: concepts.ending.no-deck-out</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U01-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r105"></a>
### 105. Elements and Affinity

<a id="r105.1"></a>**105.1.** The printed Manual names five elements: Fire, Water, Earth, Wood and Metal. The card pool this document describes has seven: those five, plus Light and Dark. See rule 902.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.8 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 31-trios.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 31-trios.test.ts::seven elements, 35 trios: Light & Dark joined the canonical element list · Key: concepts.elements.list</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U02-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r105.2"></a>**105.2.** A hybrid card belongs to two elements. A live-draft deck is built from the cards of the selected elements together with the hybrid cards for each pair of them. See rule 902.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.11; Manual p.11 · Tests: 31-trios.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 31-trios.test.ts::ALL 10 base trios are Manual-exact: 54 per element + 5 per hybrid pair = 177 · Key: concepts.elements.hybrid</sub>

<a id="r105.3"></a>**105.3.** Affinity is a card's elemental requirement. A card shows it as element pips, and a player must meet it to play the card. See rules 202, 111.

> *Example: With three Shards and no water, a player cannot play Curio Drifter [b]; with one water resource they can.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.13; Manual p.12 · Designer: RAQ 1358299200953126963#0 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts, 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts · Example test: 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts::cr:concepts.elements.affinity — a card is offered and playable only once its pips are met: one Shard cannot play Curio Drifter, one water can · Key: concepts.elements.affinity</sub>

<a id="r105.3a"></a>**105.3a** The 2023 Rulebook calls the affinity requirement the threshold. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.3; Rulebook 2023 p.4 · Key: concepts.elements.affinity.threshold</sub>

<a id="r105.4"></a>**105.4.** A player's affinity for an element is the number of resources of that element the player has, other than dormant ones (see the dormant rule below). A requirement of N pips of one element is met when the player's affinity for that element is at least N. See rule 106.

> *Example: With two wood resources, a player meets a [g][g] requirement however many times they play such cards.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.14 · Designer: RAQ 1358299200953126963#0 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts, 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Mana question: affinity counts resources already spent — two wood pay for many gg cards · Key: concepts.elements.affinity-count</sub>

<a id="r105.4a"></a>**105.4a** Expended resources count toward affinity. Whether a resource has been expended this turn does not matter.

> *Example: All-Consuming Blaze counts two open fire resources and one expended fire resource: 3 damage.*

> *Example: Sylvan Sprouting makes a 1/1 for each wood resource, expended ones included.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1358299200953126963#0 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts, 07-cards.test.ts, 25-wood-c.test.ts · Example tests: 07-cards.test.ts::All-Consuming Blaze: damage equals your fire affinity (expended counts, dormant does not), 25-wood-c.test.ts::Sylvan Sprouting: one 1/1 per wood affinity — expended wood still counts · Key: concepts.elements.affinity-count.expended</sub>

<a id="r105.4b"></a>**105.4b** Meeting an affinity requirement uses nothing up. The same resources meet the affinity requirement of every card a player plays; only the mana cost is paid. See rule 111.

> *Example: Two wood resources and many Shards pay for many [g][g] cards in one turn: the Shards pay the mana, the two wood meet every requirement.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1358299200953126963#0; RAQ 1358299200953126963#0 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Mana question: affinity counts resources already spent — two wood pay for many gg cards · Key: concepts.elements.affinity-count.not-spent</sub>

<a id="r105.4c"></a>**105.4c** A dormant resource gives no affinity until it is activated. See rule 106.

> *Example: A dormant fire resource adds nothing to All-Consuming Blaze; two open and one expended fire resource deal 3.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Dormant Resource · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 07-cards.test.ts, 01-planning.test.ts · Example test: 07-cards.test.ts::All-Consuming Blaze: damage equals your fire affinity (expended counts, dormant does not) · Key: concepts.elements.affinity-count.dormant</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U02-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r105.5"></a>**105.5.** Prismites and Shards give no affinity. A Prismite is not wild: it meets no element's requirement. See rule 106.

> *Example: With six fire resources and two active Prismites, a player still cannot meet Dreadwave Devourer's [b][b]; two water resources meet it.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 4 gate test files · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.7 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 01-planning.test.ts, 21-fixes.test.ts, 48-playtest-hotfix.test.ts, 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts · Example test: 01-planning.test.ts::affinity gating: prismites are NOT wild · Demonstrated by test: 21-fixes.test.ts::below 3 affinity no shard; shards give mana but never affinity · Key: concepts.elements.no-affinity-resources</sub>

<a id="r105.6"></a>**105.6.** Card text can use a player's affinity as a number. "Your [r]" means the player's fire affinity: the number of fire resources they have, not counting dormant ones (see the dormant rule under 105's affinity count). See rule 107.

> *Example: A player with two open fire resources and one expended fire resource casts All-Consuming Blaze: their [r] is 3, so it deals 3 damage. A dormant fire resource would not add to it.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 6 gate test files · Printed: card: All-Consuming Blaze; card: Premonition · Designer: RAQ 1358299200953126963#0 · Tests: 07-cards.test.ts, 14-water-a.test.ts, 28-metal-c.test.ts, 09-attrs.test.ts, 25-wood-c.test.ts, 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts · Example test: 07-cards.test.ts::All-Consuming Blaze: damage equals your fire affinity (expended counts, dormant does not) · Demonstrated by tests: 14-water-a.test.ts::Premonition: Glimpse X where X is your water affinity; the permission dies with the turn, the card stays, 28-metal-c.test.ts::Self-Assembly: creates a Robot X at the source's region, X = metal affinity at resolution · Key: concepts.elements.affinity-as-number</sub>

<a id="r105.7"></a>**105.7.** Some effects let a player play a card ignoring affinity. Such a play does not check the card's affinity requirement. Ignoring affinity does not waive the mana cost: the cost is still paid unless the effect also makes the play free. See rules 403, 801.

> *Example: A glimpsed card can be played without its pips, but a player who cannot pay its mana cannot play it.*

> *Example: Tides of the Cosmos plays a fire unit for a player whose only resources are water.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Big Glimpse Card; card: Tides of the Cosmos · Designer: RAQ 1396955380000755795#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts, 396-raq-timing.test.ts, 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Example tests: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts::CR 801.9g: the glimpse waives the pips, NOT the mana — broke means refused, 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Tides 1: a free play ignores affinity — a fire unit with only water resources · Key: concepts.elements.ignoring-affinity</sub>

<a id="r105.8"></a>**105.8.** Applying a modification needs its affinity just as playing the card does. An augment from hand, a Virus applied in battle and a graft from hand or bin each require the card's affinity, and each pays its cost. See rules 720, 721, 722, 723.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.32 · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#1; RAQ 1355115946032889914#2 · Tests: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts, 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts::RAQ Mods are NOT Played: an augment from hand needs its affinity and pays its cost, 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 3: a graft comes from the bin as well as the hand, and only when its cost and affinity are met · Key: concepts.elements.mods-need-affinity</sub>

<a id="r105.9"></a>**105.9.** Each game has a set of elements. In a live draft it is the selected elements; in constructed it is all seven. An element resource a player creates, by recycling or by exchanging a Prismite, must be of one of the game's elements. See rules 106, 901, 902.

> *Example: In a fire-water-earth draft, wood and metal resources are refused and never offered.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-09-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 4 gate test files · Tests: 21-fixes.test.ts, 31-trios.test.ts, 34-constructed.test.ts, 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts · Example test: 21-fixes.test.ts::a fwe draft game refuses wood/metal resources and never offers them · Demonstrated by test: 31-trios.test.ts::createGame honors the chosen trio: deck, elements, and the recycle menu · Key: concepts.elements.game-elements</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U02-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r105.9a"></a>**105.9a** In constructed, a player may create a resource of any of the seven elements, including an element their deck has no cards of.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 34-constructed.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 34-constructed.test.ts::deckElements: it is a PRESENTATION default — all seven stay legal · Key: concepts.elements.game-elements.off-deck</sub>

<a id="r106"></a>
### 106. Resources

<a id="r106.1"></a>**106.1.** Resources are the source of mana: a player needs them to play cards. Resources are permanents, and they stay in play.

> *Example: Two open water resources are two mana and pay for Curio Drifter; a turn later every resource is still in play.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.14; Manual p.14 · Tests: 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts · Example test: 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts::cr:concepts.resources.what — an open resource is mana that pays for a card, and resources stay in play from turn to turn · Key: concepts.resources.what</sub>

<a id="r106.2"></a>**106.2.** There are three kinds of resource: element resources, Prismites and Shards. Each element resource is of one element. See rule 105.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.14; Manual p.18; Rulebook 2023 p.7 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 48-playtest-hotfix.test.ts, 308-recycle-for-prismite.test.ts · Key: concepts.resources.kinds</sub>

<a id="r106.2a"></a>**106.2a** An element resource counts one toward its controller's affinity for its element, except while it is dormant (see 105). See rule 105.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Fire Resource; Rulebook 2023 p.4 · Designer: RAQ 1358299200953126963#0 · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts, 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Fire Resource: activating your 3rd fire pays the p.18 affinity Shard — dormant, and every time · Key: concepts.resources.kinds.element</sub>

<a id="r106.3"></a>**106.3.** A resource is either dormant (face down) or active (face up). Every resource enters play dormant. Activating a resource turns it face up.

> *Example: A Shard created by Swirling Shardform enters dormant.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.18; Manual p.18 · Tests: 01-planning.test.ts, 18-earth-c.test.ts · Example test: 18-earth-c.test.ts::Swirling Shardform: spawning creates two dormant Shards · Key: concepts.resources.dormant-active</sub>

<a id="r106.3a"></a>**106.3a** Each player starts the game with two dormant Prismites. See rule 103.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.11 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 01-planning.test.ts, 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 01-planning.test.ts::prismites: dormant start, no affinity, planning exchange into any element · Key: concepts.resources.dormant-active.starting</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U02-4 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r106.3b"></a>**106.3b** A dormant resource cannot be expended for mana. It must be activated first. See rule 106.

> *Example: Three dormant fire resources give no open mana and cannot pay Ignis Sprite.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-09-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 127-token-x-and-dormant.test.ts, 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts · Example test: 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts::cr:concepts.resources.dormant-active.no-mana — a dormant resource is not mana and cannot pay a cost · Key: concepts.resources.dormant-active.no-mana</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U02-10 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r106.4"></a>**106.4.** A player may activate at most two resources per turn. Activating a Shard counts toward that limit. See rule 502.

> *Example: With a Shard and a Prismite activated, a third activation that turn is refused.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.18; Manual p.18 · Tests: 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts · Example test: 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts::cr:concepts.resources.activation — a third activation in a turn is refused, and activating a Shard counts toward the two · Key: concepts.resources.activation</sub>

<a id="r106.4a"></a>**106.4a** Resources are created and activated in the resource step of the planning phase. See rule 502.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.18 · Tests: 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts::cr:concepts.resources.activation.when — creating and activating a resource is offered in the resource step and refused once it is over · Key: concepts.resources.activation.when</sub>

<a id="r106.5"></a>**106.5.** A resource can be expended (turned sideways) once per turn for 1 mana, to pay the mana cost of a card or an ability. Expended resources refresh at the beginning of each turn. See rule 111.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.14; Manual p.14; Rulebook 2023 p.4 · Tests: 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts::cr:concepts.resources.expend — expended resources refresh at the beginning of the next turn · Key: concepts.resources.expend</sub>

<a id="r106.5a"></a>**106.5a** Mana has no element. Every resource, of whatever kind, pays generic mana.

> *Example: Shards pay the mana for [g][g] cards; the two wood resources only meet the affinity.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1358299200953126963#0 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Mana question: affinity counts resources already spent — two wood pay for many gg cards · Key: concepts.resources.expend.generic</sub>

<a id="r106.5b"></a>**106.5b** To pay a mana cost, a player expends that many un-expended resources. See rule 111.

> *Example: Rampart Guardian costs 2: of three open earth, two become expended and one stays open.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.13 · Tests: 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts · Example test: 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts::cr:concepts.resources.expend.paying — paying a mana cost expends exactly that many un-expended resources · Key: concepts.resources.expend.paying</sub>

<a id="r106.5c"></a>**106.5c** A resource is expended only to pay a cost. No action expends a resource for nothing, and mana is not kept for later use. See rule 106.5b.

> *Example: Keeper of Tithes ("At the end of [Haste], if X is not 0, create an X/X unit, where X is the number of expended resources you have") is in play, its controller has six open resources and nothing to pay for: no resource can be expended, so X is 0 and no unit is made.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RQ 1151901699108241438 · Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16 · Tests: 470-expend-only-to-pay.test.ts · Example test: 470-expend-only-to-pay.test.ts::CR 106.5: Keeper of Tithes with six open resources and nothing paid makes no token · Demonstrated by tests: 470-expend-only-to-pay.test.ts::CR 106.5: no action expends a resource except by paying a cost, 470-expend-only-to-pay.test.ts::CR 106.5: the Action union has no expend, tap, spend or float action · Key: concepts.resources.expend.only-to-pay</sub>

<a id="r106.6"></a>**106.6.** In the resource step a player may create a resource by recycling a card from hand. The resource enters dormant. There is no limit to how many resources a player creates this way. See rules 408, 502.

> *Example: Four cards recycled in one resource step make four fire resources, all dormant.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.18; Manual p.18; Manual p.18 · Tests: 308-recycle-for-prismite.test.ts, 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts · Example test: 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts::cr:concepts.resources.recycle — several recycles in one resource step, each resource enters dormant · Key: concepts.resources.recycle</sub>

<a id="r106.6a"></a>**106.6a** Recycling may create a Prismite or a Shard instead of an element resource.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.18 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 308-recycle-for-prismite.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 308-recycle-for-prismite.test.ts::CR 106.6a every hand card offers a Prismite, then a Shard, after the elements · Key: concepts.resources.recycle.prismite-shard</sub>

<a id="r106.6b"></a>**106.6b** A Prismite made by recycling is the same as a starting Prismite: it enters dormant, takes an activation, gives no affinity, and once active may be exchanged.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 308-recycle-for-prismite.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 308-recycle-for-prismite.test.ts::CR 106.6b a recycled Prismite behaves like a starting one · Key: concepts.resources.recycle.made-prismite</sub>

<a id="r106.7"></a>**106.7.** When a player activates an element resource, if they then have at least three affinity of that element, they create a Shard. The Shard enters dormant. See rule 106.

> *Example: Activating a third fire resource creates a dormant Shard.*

> *Example: With fewer than three fire, activating a fire resource creates nothing.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 4 gate test files · Printed: card: Fire Resource; card: Fire Resource; Manual p.18 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts, 15-water-b.test.ts, 16-earth-a.test.ts, 21-fixes.test.ts · Example tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Fire Resource: activating your 3rd fire pays the p.18 affinity Shard — dormant, and every time, 12-fire-a.test.ts::Fire Resource: below three affinity the clause does nothing · Key: concepts.resources.affinity-bonus</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U02-5 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r106.7a"></a>**106.7a** The resource being activated counts toward the three.

> *Example: Two active fire resources plus the one being activated make three: the Shard is created.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.7 · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts · Example test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::the resource being activated COUNTS TOWARD ITS OWN THREE — the boundary · Key: concepts.resources.affinity-bonus.self-counts</sub>

<a id="r106.7b"></a>**106.7b** The bonus is paid on every such activation, not once per game.

> *Example: A fourth fire resource activated later creates another Shard.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.7 · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts · Example test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Fire Resource: activating your 3rd fire pays the p.18 affinity Shard — dormant, and every time · Key: concepts.resources.affinity-bonus.every-time</sub>

<a id="r106.7c"></a>**106.7c** The bonus applies to every element, including those whose resource face is not among the printed cards.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.18 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::CONFORMANCE: every element pays the p.18 affinity bonus at 3 — all seven, not just the three with printed faces · Key: concepts.resources.affinity-bonus.all-elements</sub>

<a id="r106.7d"></a>**106.7d** Activating a Prismite or a Shard never creates a Shard, however many the player has.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.18 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts, 308-recycle-for-prismite.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::CONFORMANCE: a Prismite and a Shard never pay the bonus, however many you have · Key: concepts.resources.affinity-bonus.not-prismite-shard</sub>

<a id="r106.8"></a>**106.8.** A Prismite is a resource with no element. It gives no affinity, and like any resource it can be expended for 1 mana. See rule 105.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.18; Manual p.18 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 01-planning.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 01-planning.test.ts::prismites: dormant start, no affinity, planning exchange into any element · Key: concepts.resources.prismite</sub>

<a id="r106.8a"></a>**106.8a** A player may exchange an active Prismite for another resource only in the resource step of the planning phase, never in the haste step (which resources: the element-only rule below). The new resource takes the Prismite's place and keeps its current state, so an exchange never adds mana: an expended Prismite becomes an expended resource. See rules 502, 105.

> *Example: An expended active Prismite exchanged into fire becomes an expended fire resource; once the player has finished the resource step, a further exchange is refused.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.18; Manual p.18; Manual p.18 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 01-planning.test.ts, 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts · Example test: 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts::cr:concepts.resources.prismite.exchange — only an active Prismite, only in the resource step, and the new resource keeps its state · Demonstrated by test: 01-planning.test.ts::prismites: dormant start, no affinity, planning exchange into any element · Key: concepts.resources.prismite.exchange</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U02-7, D-U08-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r106.8b"></a>**106.8b** A dormant Prismite cannot be exchanged.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.18 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 01-planning.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 01-planning.test.ts::prismites: dormant start, no affinity, planning exchange into any element · Key: concepts.resources.prismite.exchange.dormant</sub>

<a id="r106.8c"></a>**106.8c** The exchange activates the new resource. If that gives the player three affinity of its element, the affinity bonus creates a Shard. The exchange does not use one of the player's two activations for the turn. See rule 106.

> *Example: A Prismite exchanged into a third copy of an element creates a Shard.*

> *Example: A Prismite exchanged into a second copy creates nothing: the bar is three.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 21-fixes.test.ts, 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts · Example tests: 21-fixes.test.ts::CR 106.8: spending a Prismite into your 3rd element copy DOES grant the shard — "then activate it", 21-fixes.test.ts::CR 106.8: a Prismite spent into your SECOND copy pays nothing — the p.18 bar is three · Key: concepts.resources.prismite.exchange.activation</sub>

<a id="r106.8d"></a>**106.8d** A Prismite may be exchanged for any non-Prismite resource: an element resource of one of the game's elements, or a Shard. It cannot be exchanged for another Prismite. *(Engine differs, see F-U02-3.)*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.18; Manual p.18 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24, 2026-09-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 308-recycle-for-prismite.test.ts, 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 308-recycle-for-prismite.test.ts::CR 106.8d what stays illegal: exchanging a Prismite into a Prismite or a Shard · Key: concepts.resources.prismite.exchange.element-only</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U02-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r106.9"></a>**106.9.** A Shard is a resource of its own kind. It enters dormant, pays one generic mana once activated, gives no affinity, and cannot be exchanged.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.7 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 48-playtest-hotfix.test.ts, 308-recycle-for-prismite.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 48-playtest-hotfix.test.ts::a Shard gives mana but no affinity and no element exchange, 308-recycle-for-prismite.test.ts::a recycled Shard is mana only: no affinity, no Shard of its own, no exchange · Key: concepts.resources.shard</sub>

<a id="r106.9a"></a>**106.9a** An effect that creates a Shard creates a Shard, never a Prismite.

> *Example: Swirling Shardform creates two dormant Shards, not Prismites.*

> *Example: Hooba-Lan's attack creates a dormant Shard for its controller.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Swirling Shardform · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 48-playtest-hotfix.test.ts, 16-earth-a.test.ts, 18-earth-c.test.ts · Example tests: 48-playtest-hotfix.test.ts::Swirling Shardform creates two dormant SHARDS, not prismites, 16-earth-a.test.ts::Hooba-Lan: attacking creates a real dormant Shard for its controller · Key: concepts.resources.shard.not-prismite</sub>

<a id="r107"></a>
### 107. Numbers, X and Symbols

<a id="r107.1"></a>**107.1.** X stands for a number that the card defines. An X in a mana cost is chosen by the player who plays the card. A token's X is set by the card that created it. Other cards define X with a "where X is …" clause. See rules 702, 304.

> *Example: Wildfire asks its caster for X; Self-Assembly with three metal makes a Robot 3.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Wildfire; Manual p.15; card: Self-Assembly · Tests: 32-cast-costs.test.ts, 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts · Example test: 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts::cr:concepts.numbers.x — X in a mana cost is chosen by the caster, a token takes its X from the creating card, and a where-X clause reads the card · Key: concepts.numbers.x</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U02-9 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r107.2"></a>**107.2.** An X spell's mana cost is X alone: the player chooses X, and pays X. Its pips are not part of its cost. See rules 111, 702.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 133-x-cost-semantics.test.ts, 32-cast-costs.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 133-x-cost-semantics.test.ts::CR 107.2 — with no Stasis Sentry an X spell costs exactly X · Key: concepts.numbers.x-cost</sub>

<a id="r107.2a"></a>**107.2a** X is chosen and paid when the spell is cast, before it goes on the stack. Only values the player can pay are offered. Responses see the X already chosen. See rule 702.

> *Example: Wildfire: its caster chooses X from the values they can pay and pays it as the spell is cast, so the spell is on the stack with that X.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 32-cast-costs.test.ts · Example test: 32-cast-costs.test.ts::Wildfire: X is chosen at cast from affordable values, paid, and stored on the item · Key: concepts.numbers.x-cost.chosen-at-cast</sub>

<a id="r107.2b"></a>**107.2b** X may be 0 unless the card says otherwise. Choosing X = 0 is legal even when it makes the effect do nothing.

> *Example: No Hand Killer can be activated with an empty hand at X = 0, and its [once] is spent.*

> *Example: Torrential Reclamation for X = 0 recalls nothing, but each player still sacrifices a unit.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22, 2026-08-25, 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 4 gate test files · Tests: 32-cast-costs.test.ts, 46-hybrids-ld-c.test.ts, 42-dark-b.test.ts, 182-correctness-sample.test.ts · Example tests: 46-hybrids-ld-c.test.ts::CR 107.2b: an empty hand still activates No Hand Killer — X = 0, and the [once] is spent, 182-correctness-sample.test.ts::Torrential Reclamation: with X = 0 the sacrifice STILL happens, and costs no life (CR 107.2b) · Demonstrated by test: 32-cast-costs.test.ts::X spells resolve from the stored X — a 0-mana caster may still cast for X = 0 · Key: concepts.numbers.x-cost.zero</sub>

<a id="r107.2c"></a>**107.2c** An X spell (a card whose mana cost is X) that prints "X can't be zero" must be cast with X of at least 1. A player who cannot pay at least 1 cannot cast it.

> *Example: Frosted Denial cannot be cast with no open mana.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Frosted Denial · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 32-cast-costs.test.ts · Example test: 32-cast-costs.test.ts::Frosted Denial: xMin 1 — with no open mana the cast is illegal (X can't be zero) · Key: concepts.numbers.x-cost.cant-be-zero</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U02-11 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r107.3"></a>**107.3.** An effect that refers to a spell's cost reads its printed cost, not what was actually paid after cost modifiers. For an X spell, that is the X it was cast for. See rule 111.

> *Example: Squish taxed up to 4 by Stasis Sentry and Tranquility is still a 2 to Arcane Concentrator and Channeled Amalgam.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1353980184042143835#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 133-x-cost-semantics.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ printed cost: Arcane Concentrator and Channeled Amalgam read a taxed Squish as a 2 · Demonstrated by test: 133-x-cost-semantics.test.ts::CR 107.3 — Channeled Amalgam reads the PAID X of an X spell (was dead against all eleven) · Key: concepts.numbers.cost-reference</sub>

<a id="r107.3a"></a>**107.3a** An X card that is not being cast has a cost of 0. This holds for an X card in a hand, a bin, the deck or the cache, and for a unit in play.

> *Example: Living Vault caches a card from hand by paying its cost: an X card in hand costs 0, so it can be cached for [0].*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 133-x-cost-semantics.test.ts, 39-light-b.test.ts · Example test: 39-light-b.test.ts::Living Vault: an X-cost card in hand is offered at pay [0] (CR 107.3a) · Demonstrated by test: 133-x-cost-semantics.test.ts::CR 111.11 — a card that was never cast has no cost: an X card in hand reads 0 · Key: concepts.numbers.cost-reference.not-cast</sub>

<a id="r107.4"></a>**107.4.** When an effect lets a player play an X spell for free, the spell is played with X = 0. An X that is a bracketed additional cost is not the mana cost: it is still chosen and paid. See rules 111, 803.

> *Example: A fulfilled prophecy releases an X spell for X = 0: no X is asked and no mana is paid.*

> *Example: Tides of the Cosmos counts an X spell as cost 0 and plays it at X = 0.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1396955380000755795#6 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts, 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 803.7j: a fulfilled prophecy releases an X spell for X = 0 — no X asked, no mana paid, 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Tides 6a: an X spell counts as cost 0 against the budget and is played at X = 0 · Key: concepts.numbers.free-play</sub>

<a id="r107.4a"></a>**107.4a** An X spell that prints "X can't be zero" therefore cannot be played for free. An effect that plays cards for free cannot play it.

> *Example: Tides of the Cosmos cannot pick Frosted Denial; an X card that may be zero is still a pick.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Frosted Denial · Designer: RAQ 1396955380000755795#7 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 404-raq-fix-tides.test.ts, 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 404-raq-fix-tides.test.ts::CR 107.4a: an X card that may not be zero is never a Tides pick; one that may be zero still is · Demonstrated by test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Tides 6: Frosted Denial (X cannot be zero) is not a card Tides can play · Key: concepts.numbers.free-play.cant-be-zero</sub>

<a id="r107.5"></a>**107.5.** Stasis Sentry gives spells with a base cost of [three] or less a base cost of [three] during battle. On an X spell it raises the X instead of the price: X must be at least 3, and the spell costs exactly X. See rule 111.

> *Example: Under a Stasis Sentry the X menu starts at 3, and X = 3 deals 3.*

> *Example: Under a Stasis Sentry, X = 3 costs [3] and X = 5 costs [5].*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Stasis Sentry · Designer: RAQ 1359629594512068770#0; RAQ 1359629594512068770#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 133-x-cost-semantics.test.ts · Example tests: 133-x-cost-semantics.test.ts::CR 107.5 (reversing the earlier price reading) — under a Stasis Sentry the X menu starts at 3, and X = 3 deals 3, 133-x-cost-semantics.test.ts::CR 107.5 — the real cast pays it: X=3 costs [3] and X=5 costs [5] under a Stasis Sentry · Key: concepts.numbers.x-minimum</sub>

<a id="r107.6"></a>**107.6.** A copy of a spell uses the original's X. The X is not chosen or paid again. See rule 710.

> *Example: Maelstrom Charger copies Volatile Toxicity: the copy uses the original's X, and no second unit is sacrificed for it.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1379132904931594372#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 138-spell-copy.test.ts, 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts · Example test: 138-spell-copy.test.ts::CR 710.8a Maelstrom Charger: the copy inherits the cast-cost receipt (CR 111.5) — Volatile Toxicity is not re-paid · Key: concepts.numbers.copy-x</sub>

<a id="r107.7"></a>**107.7.** A token's X is set by the card that created it. "Create a Crystal 3" creates a Crystal whose X is 3. See rule 304.

> *Example: A Poison created with X = 5 reads "Put 5 -1/-1 counters on target unit."*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.4; Rulebook 2023 p.4; Manual p.15 · Tests: 127-token-x-and-dormant.test.ts, 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts · Example test: 127-token-x-and-dormant.test.ts::CR D6.9/CT-33: a Poison created with X=5 says "Put 5 -1/-1 counters", from the engine · Key: concepts.numbers.token-x</sub>

<a id="r107.7a"></a>**107.7a** A Robot's X is the number of +1/+1 counters on it. It spawns with X counters, and if the number of counters changes, so does its X.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Robot · Tests: 127-token-x-and-dormant.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 127-token-x-and-dormant.test.ts::CR D6.9a/CT-33: a Robot reads its X off its COUNTERS, so it stays true as they change · Key: concepts.numbers.token-x.robot</sub>

<a id="r107.8"></a>**107.8.** A number an effect counts, such as a "where X is …" clause or an amount "equal to" or "for each" something, is counted when the effect resolves, not when it was played or triggered. See rules 704, 706, 714.

> *Example: Flamebreath Initiate removed with its trigger on the stack has no adjacent allies, so X = 0 and it still makes a Fireball 1.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 4 gate test files · Printed: card: Flamebreath Initiate · Designer: RAQ 1353895783266516992#3 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 28-metal-c.test.ts, 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 11-fire-wood.test.ts, 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ dead unit: Flamebreath Initiate removed before its trigger resolves still makes a Fireball 1 · Demonstrated by test: 28-metal-c.test.ts::Self-Assembly: creates a Robot X at the source's region, X = metal affinity at resolution · Key: concepts.numbers.amounts-at-resolution</sub>

<a id="r107.8a"></a>**107.8a** An X that a paid cost defines is read as the cost is paid. Volatile Toxicity's X is the sacrificed unit's defense as it was when the unit was sacrificed.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Volatile Toxicity · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 32-cast-costs.test.ts, 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 32-cast-costs.test.ts::Volatile Toxicity: X reads the defense snapshotted when the cost was paid · Key: concepts.numbers.amounts-at-resolution.cost-snapshot</sub>

<a id="r107.9"></a>**107.9.** When a card asks a player to choose or predict a number, there is no limit the card does not print. A player may name any number in the card's range.

> *Example: Prediction Prophet: a player predicts a life total nine higher than their current one. They gain 9 life during the battle, the prediction is matched at the start of deployment, and they get the 5/5.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Prediction Prophet · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 168-three-card-divergences.test.ts, 40-light-c.test.ts · Example test: 168-three-card-divergences.test.ts::CR 107.9 Prediction Prophet: a prediction ABOVE `life + 5` is accepted and pays out the 5/5 — the old cap would not have offered it · Key: concepts.numbers.chosen-number</sub>

<a id="r107.10"></a>**107.10.** This document writes the game's symbols in brackets, as the card data does. The element pips are [r] Fire, [b] Water, [e] Earth, [g] Wood, [m] Metal, [l] Light and [d] Dark. See rule 202.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 4 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 5 gate test files · Printed: card: Fire Resource; card: Water Resource; card: Earth Resource; card: Exhume; card: Reap the Due · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Engine: ELEMENT_OF_PIP · Tests: 07-cards.test.ts, 25-wood-c.test.ts, 28-metal-c.test.ts, 14-water-a.test.ts, 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 07-cards.test.ts::All-Consuming Blaze: damage equals your fire affinity (expended counts, dormant does not), 25-wood-c.test.ts::Sylvan Sprouting: one 1/1 per wood affinity — expended wood still counts, 28-metal-c.test.ts::Self-Assembly: creates a Robot X at the source's region, X = metal affinity at resolution · Key: concepts.numbers.symbols</sub>

<a id="r107.10a"></a>**107.10a** [x] is X generic mana. A number in brackets, as a digit or a word ([1], [three]), is that much generic mana. A number followed by pips ([3b]) is that much mana together with that affinity. See rules 202, 111.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Frosted Denial; card: Stasis Sentry · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 14-water-a.test.ts, 413-cr-elements-resources.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 14-water-a.test.ts::Lurking Slimebeast: [Battle] Ambush [3b] = 3 mana at one water pip (CR 803.6a, 107.10a) · Key: concepts.numbers.symbols.mana</sub>

<a id="r108"></a>
### 108. Cards, Tokens, Faces and Copies

<a id="r108.1"></a>**108.1.** A card is a physical Algomancy card: one with an Algomancy card back. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Key: concepts.cards.card</sub>

<a id="r108.1a"></a>**108.1a** Units, spells and spell units are cards. Card text that refers to a "card" being played includes a unit being played.

> *Example: Void Mandible ("When a nontoken card is played during battle, sacrifice me. If you do, negate that effect.") answers a {Battle} unit being played.*
