<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts · Example test: 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts::Void Mandible: a {Battle} UNIT is a card played — sacrifice, then negate · Key: concepts.cards.card.units</sub>

<a id="r108.1b"></a>**108.1b** Every card has a name, and most cards have abilities. The other parts a card can have are described in section 200. See rule 200.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.12; Manual p.12 · Tests: 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts::cr:concepts.cards.card.characteristics — every card in the pool has a name, and most have ability text · Key: concepts.cards.card.characteristics</sub>

<a id="r108.2"></a>**108.2.** A token is a unit or a spell that an effect creates directly into play. A unit token functions as a unit, and a spell token is a spell. See rule 304.

> *Example: Mycelial Mentor reads "When you create a token, target ally gains +3/+3." Its controller creates a Poison, a spell token, and the Mentor triggers just as it would for a 1/1 unit.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.15; Manual p.15; Manual p.15 · Tests: 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts · Example test: 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts::Mycelial Mentor: creating a POISON fires "when you create a token" · Key: concepts.cards.token</sub>

<a id="r108.2a"></a>**108.2a** For card text, a token is not a card: text that refers to a "card" does not include a token, even though a unit token is a unit and a spell token is a spell. The printed rules call tokens "temporary cards" to describe them to players; that does not make a token a card. See rule 702.

> *Example: A player casts a Fireball token in battle. That is playing a spell, so abilities that watch for a spell being played see it; it is not playing a card, so abilities that watch for a card being played do not.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.15 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24, 2026-09-28, 2026-10-11 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts · Example test: 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts::a spell TOKEN is a played spell but not a card · Key: concepts.cards.token.not-card</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U06-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r108.2b"></a>**108.2b** A spell token is a token wherever it is: in play, and also on the stack after it has been cast. See rules 304, 406.

> *Example: Download ("Gain control of target token") can take a Fireball token that has already been cast and is on the stack.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1353864175910387742#0; RAQ 1353864175910387742#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24, 2026-08-25, 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Download: a Fireball already cast and on the stack is a token it can take · Key: concepts.cards.token.spell-token</sub>

<a id="r108.2c"></a>**108.2c** A unit that an effect creates is a unit token, including an X/X unit whose X the creating card sets. See rule 304.

> *Example: Spawntender creates an 8/8 unit. That unit is a token, so Download ("Gain control of target token") can take it.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353864175910387742#2 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Download: a Fireball in the region and an X/X unit token are both tokens it can take · Key: concepts.cards.token.x-units</sub>

<a id="r108.2d"></a>**108.2d** A token is created in the region its source is in when the effect that creates it resolves, not in its controller's home region. See rules 304, 601.

> *Example: Life Plant attacking in the enemy region creates its 1/1 units in that region.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.15 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 98-spawn-region.test.ts · Example test: 98-spawn-region.test.ts::CR 601.5: report #83 — Life Plant attacking in the enemy region creates its 1/1s THERE, not at home · Key: concepts.cards.token.where</sub>

<a id="r108.2e"></a>**108.2e** A token is never trashed, because only a card can be trashed. A unit token can still die. See rules 801, 410.

> *Example: A unit token dying in battle does not add to the number of cards trashed in that battle.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 338-tokens-are-not-trashed.test.ts · Example test: 338-tokens-are-not-trashed.test.ts::CR 801.2i: a token unit dying in battle does not bump the trashed ledger that Dropslime reads · Key: concepts.cards.token.not-trashed</sub>

<a id="r108.3"></a>**108.3.** A card in play that transforms is the same unit with its other face up. It does not leave play or enter play, and it keeps its counters and damage. See rule 710.

> *Example: Scholar of the Void transforms into Beyond, Codex Incarnate: same unit, and its counters and damage survive.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 43-dark-c.test.ts · Example test: 43-dark-c.test.ts::CR 108.3 — the transform is the SAME unit: same id, and its counters and damage survive · Key: concepts.cards.faces</sub>

<a id="r108.3a"></a>**108.3a** A back face is not a token, and a transformed card is still a card. See rule 410.

> *Example: A transformed Scholar of the Void that died can be returned from the bin as a Scholar.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts, 43-dark-c.test.ts · Example test: 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts::a transformed Scholar that died is RECURRABLE from the bin · Key: concepts.cards.faces.back-not-token</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U03-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r108.3b"></a>**108.3b** A card can only transform into a back face it has. A unit that gains a transform ability from a mod transforms only if that unit's own card has that back face.

> *Example: Scholar of the Void augmented onto another unit cannot transform its host.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 43-dark-c.test.ts · Example test: 43-dark-c.test.ts::CR 108.3b — donated to a HOST the transform is refused · Key: concepts.cards.faces.own-back</sub>

<a id="r108.4"></a>**108.4.** A copy of a spell is a new effect on the stack. It was not played. See rules 701, 710.

> *Example: Earthbound Replicator copies a spell that targets it. The copy is not played, so it does not set off the Replicator again: one copy, and no more.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355613076506017894#4; RAQ 1355613076506017894#1 · Tests: 138-spell-copy.test.ts · Example test: 138-spell-copy.test.ts::CR 701.5 Earthbound Replicator: a copy is not PLAYED · Key: concepts.cards.copies</sub>

<a id="r108.4a"></a>**108.4a** A copy of a spell is not a token.

> *Example: Download cannot take a spell copy made by Earthbound Replicator.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355613076506017894#5; RAQ 1353864175910387742#5; RAQ 1353864175910387742#6 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Download: a spell copy made by Earthbound Replicator is not a token · Key: concepts.cards.copies.not-token</sub>

<a id="r108.4b"></a>**108.4b** A token that an effect creates as a copy of a card is a token.

> *Example: The copy Echo of Despair makes of itself is a token.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353864175910387742#3 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Download: a copy Echo of Despair makes of itself is a token · Key: concepts.cards.copies.token-copy</sub>

<a id="r108.4c"></a>**108.4c** A nontoken unit that becomes a copy of a token is still a nontoken unit. See rule 710.

> *Example: Borrower of Forms copying a Robot token is a nontoken unit, which Download cannot take.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1372468222158180424#9 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Borrower of Forms: copying a Robot token makes a nontoken unit · Key: concepts.cards.copies.mimic-not-token</sub>

<a id="r108.5"></a>**108.5.** Two copies of the same card are two different objects. Card text that says "another" or "other" compares objects, never card names. See rules 405, 110.

> *Example: A host wearing two Rotbeast augments: each Rotbeast's "my other Augments" includes the other Rotbeast.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 121-another-identity.test.ts · Example test: 121-another-identity.test.ts::CR 720.6d Rotbeast: a SECOND Rotbeast augment is "another" · Key: concepts.cards.identity</sub>

<a id="r108.5a"></a>**108.5a** An object stays the same object while it stays where it is. A unit that leaves play and comes back is a new object. See rule 410.

> *Example: Engorged Caudex recalled and played again draws again from its once-per-turn graft in the same turn.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1454169054402314362#2; RAQ 1355115946032889914#16; RAQ 1355115946032889914#16 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 calebgannon · Key: concepts.cards.identity.new-object</sub>

<a id="r109"></a>
### 109. Abilities

<a id="r109.1"></a>**109.1.** An ability is text on a card that describes the card's effects. Most cards have abilities. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.12; Manual p.12 · Key: concepts.abilities.what</sub>

<a id="r109.2"></a>**109.2.** An activated ability is written with a colon. Everything before the colon is a cost that must be paid to activate the ability; what follows the colon is its effect. See rules 705, 111.

> *Example: Living Forge reads "[three]: Create a Robot 2." With two resources its ability cannot be activated; paying three makes a Robot.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.41; Manual p.41; Manual p.41 · Tests: 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts · Example test: 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts::cr:concepts.abilities.activated — Living Forge cannot activate its ability without the cost before the colon, and paying it gives the effect after · Key: concepts.abilities.activated</sub>

<a id="r109.2a"></a>**109.2a** A player may activate an activated ability any time they have priority, in battle or in deployment, as many times as they can pay its cost, unless the ability limits itself (see [once]). See rules 703, 109.9.

> *Example: With six resources, Living Forge makes two Robots in one deployment, and makes another in battle when its controller holds priority and pays again.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.41; Manual p.41; Manual p.41 · Tests: 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts · Example test: 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts::cr:concepts.abilities.activated.when — Living Forge activates twice in one deployment and again with priority in battle, as long as its cost is paid · Key: concepts.abilities.activated.when</sub>

<a id="r109.2b"></a>**109.2b** An activated ability that is used from the hand can be used during battle even if its card has no {Battle} icon.

> *Example: Dropslime's discard-me ability can be used in battle.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts · Example test: 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts::discard-me mode is offered IN BATTLE and deals damage there · Key: concepts.abilities.activated.from-hand</sub>

<a id="r109.3"></a>**109.3.** A triggered ability happens when something else takes place. "When" and "Whenever" mark a triggered ability; one can also happen at a stated time, such as "After combat" or "At the end of turn". See rule 706.

> *Example: Skittering Blight gains its controller a rot when it spawns; Harbinger of Immolation makes a Fireball at the end of the turn; an attacking Wisp sacrifices itself after combat.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.41; Manual p.41; Manual p.41 · Tests: 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts · Example test: 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts::cr:concepts.abilities.triggered — a When ability fires on its event, an After combat ability after combat, and an At the end of turn ability at the end of the turn · Key: concepts.abilities.triggered</sub>

<a id="r109.3a"></a>**109.3a** A trigger condition is checked once, when the event happens. If it was false then, nothing that happens later makes the ability trigger; once the ability has triggered, it resolves even if the condition stops being true.

> *Example: A spell played at another unit and then retargeted onto Earthbound Replicator makes no copy: "a spell targeting me" is judged as the spell is played.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1355613076506017894#3 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 05-rulings.test.ts, 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts · Example test: 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts::CR 706.9 Earthbound Replicator: a spell played at something ELSE and retargeted onto me makes NO copy · Demonstrated by test: 05-rulings.test.ts::CR 109.3a: trigger conditions check at event time; amounts compute at resolution · Key: concepts.abilities.triggered.condition</sub>

<a id="r109.3b"></a>**109.3b** An amount a triggered ability uses is measured when the ability resolves, so responses can change it.

> *Example: Astral Tidewraith attacks: its trigger deals each player damage equal to the cards in their hand, counted as the trigger resolves, not when it triggered.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 05-rulings.test.ts · Key: concepts.abilities.triggered.amount</sub>

<a id="r109.3c"></a>**109.3c** A triggered ability checks its condition again when it resolves only if its text says so, as "if I am still in formation" does. See rule 110.8.

> *Example: Hooba-Nan says "if I am still in formation", so that is checked again on resolution: if Hooba-Nan dies with its attack trigger on the stack, no 1/1s are made.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ dead unit: Hooba-Nan gone with its trigger on the stack makes nothing · Key: concepts.abilities.triggered.recheck</sub>

<a id="r109.3d"></a>**109.3d** An ability that triggers when an ally becomes the target of a spell triggers once for each targeted ally. See rule 706.

> *Example: An enemy spell targeting two allies puts Earnest Defender's ability on the stack twice.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 136-triggers-and-modes.test.ts · Example test: 136-triggers-and-modes.test.ts::CR 109.3d: two targeted allies are TWO TRIGGERS on the stack · Key: concepts.abilities.triggered.per-target</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U03-4 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r109.4"></a>**109.4.** A static ability makes a continuous change to the game for as long as its card is in play. See rule 707.

> *Example: While Glowhaven Elder is in play, your other units are +1/+1; when it leaves play, they lose the bonus.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.41 · Tests: 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts · Example test: 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts::cr:concepts.abilities.static — Glowhaven Elder buffs the other units for exactly as long as it is in play · Key: concepts.abilities.static</sub>

<a id="r109.5"></a>**109.5.** A replacement effect, written "If … instead", changes an event as it happens. The replacement itself does not use the stack. See rules 708, 109.5a.

> *Example: With Flux Resonator in play, Living Forge's Robot 2 arrives with three counters, and no extra item goes on the stack for the replacement.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.41; Manual p.41 · Tests: 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts · Example test: 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts::cr:concepts.abilities.replacement — Flux Resonator changes the Robot counters as the Forge ability resolves, without a stack item or a priority pass of its own · Key: concepts.abilities.replacement</sub>

<a id="r109.5a"></a>**109.5a** If the substitute a replacement effect names includes a target, the event is still replaced at once, and the substitute is put on the stack as a triggered ability so that its target can be chosen. See rule 109.5.

> *Example: Beyond, Codex Incarnate's rot replacement removes the rot damage at once, then asks its controller for the target unit that gets the -1/-1 counters.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 43-dark-c.test.ts · Example test: 43-dark-c.test.ts::Beyond, Codex Incarnate: CR 112.13d — the rot replacement asks its controller for a target, and the damage never lands · Key: concepts.abilities.replacement.targeted</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U03-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r109.6"></a>**109.6.** An option a card offers as a spell is played, such as Maelstrom Charger's, is neither a triggered nor an activated ability. It does not go on the stack, it cannot be responded to, and effects on triggered or activated abilities do not apply to it. See rule 702.

> *Example: Crevice Lurker's tax on triggered abilities does not reach Maelstrom Charger's option.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1379132904931594372#3; RAQ 1379132904931594372#0 · Tests: 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts · Example test: 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts::CR 705.6 Maelstrom Charger: Crevice Lurker cannot tax it · Demonstrated by test: 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts::CR 702.3g Maelstrom Charger: the option is asked in the cast window and never reaches the stack · Key: concepts.abilities.as-you-play</sub>

<a id="r109.7"></a>**109.7.** Text after a card's [Augment] or graft symbol is active when the card is played normally, not only when the card is a mod. See rule 720.

> *Example: A Wraith token in play uses its own [Augment] text: at the start of deployment its controller puts a -1/-1 counter on an ally.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.43 · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Example test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::at the start of deployment a Wraith body shrinks a chosen ally · Key: concepts.abilities.mod-text</sub>

<a id="r109.8"></a>**109.8.** An effect can give units an ability. The ability goes to the units the effect names as it resolves; a unit that arrives afterwards does not gain it.

> *Example: Reforge the Dead's grant lasts until regroup and reaches only the units already there.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Reforge the Dead · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 27-metal-b.test.ts · Example test: 27-metal-b.test.ts::Reforge the Dead: the grant is until regroup, and only for units already there · Key: concepts.abilities.granted</sub>

<a id="r109.8a"></a>**109.8a** A granted ability is an ability the unit has. An effect that removes a unit's abilities removes the granted abilities the unit has when the removal applies; an ability granted to the unit afterwards is not removed. See rule 712.

> *Example: A unit that loses all abilities also loses an ability Reforge the Dead gave it earlier; if Reforge the Dead resolves after the removal, the unit has the new ability.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1355685844467581081#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21, 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 402-raq-fix-stripping.test.ts, 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts · Example test: 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts::cr:concepts.abilities.granted.is-ability — a Reforge the Dead grant made BEFORE an ability strip is removed; one made AFTER it still fires · Demonstrated by test: 402-raq-fix-stripping.test.ts::§8 a trigger on a mod attached after the strip still fires; one attached before it does not · Key: concepts.abilities.granted.is-ability</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U03-11 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r109.9"></a>**109.9.** An ability marked [once], and a bounded graft ([Switch1]), can be activated or triggered only once per turn. See rule 722.

> *Example: Unstable Apparition ([once]: when you play a nontoken spell, create a Fireball X) makes a Fireball for the first spell its controller plays this turn, nothing for the second, and a Fireball again next turn.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.33; Manual p.33; Rulebook 2023 p.16 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 33-trigger-fixes.test.ts, 94-bounded-uses.test.ts · Example test: 33-trigger-fixes.test.ts::Unstable Apparition: [once] resets each turn · Key: concepts.abilities.once</sub>

<a id="r109.9a"></a>**109.9a** The use is spent when the ability is activated or put on the stack, whether or not it then resolves. A fizzle, a negation, or a run that finds nothing to do does not give it back. Only a declined or impossible optional choice leaves the use unspent (rule 109.9b), even when that choice comes as the ability resolves. See rule 109.9b.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Engine: engine.ts:E.refundPart · Tests: 94-bounded-uses.test.ts, 93-engine-defects.test.ts, 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 94-bounded-uses.test.ts::a bounded trigger that is NEGATED on the stack has still spent its use, 93-engine-defects.test.ts::a bounded ability that FIZZLES for want of a target has SPENT its [once] · Key: concepts.abilities.once.spent-on-use</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U03-9 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r109.9b"></a>**109.9b** A player who declines an optional ("you may") bounded ability, or who could not be offered it at all, has not spent the use. The ability can trigger again later in the turn.

> *Example: Hexbane Shiitake declined on one spell is offered again on the next spell that turn.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 94-bounded-uses.test.ts, 93-engine-defects.test.ts · Example test: 94-bounded-uses.test.ts::Hexbane Shiitake declined on one spell is still offered on the NEXT spell that turn · Key: concepts.abilities.once.decline</sub>

<a id="r109.9c"></a>**109.9c** Activating a [once] ability with X = 0 is legal, and it spends the use.

> *Example: No Hand Killer can be activated with an empty hand, and the activation spends its [once].*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 136-triggers-and-modes.test.ts · Example test: 136-triggers-and-modes.test.ts::CR 109.9c: No Hand Killer is activatable with an EMPTY hand · Key: concepts.abilities.once.x-zero</sub>

<a id="r109.9d"></a>**109.9d** A change of controller does not give back a spent use: the limit stays with the unit.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 05-rulings.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 05-rulings.test.ts::CR 109.9d: once-per-turn budgets are per card and survive control change · Key: concepts.abilities.once.per-card</sub>

<a id="r109.9e"></a>**109.9e** Moving a mod onto another unit (Reconfigure) does not give back its spent use. See rule 720.

> *Example: A Graxxlid augment already activated this turn and moved by Reconfigure cannot be activated again that turn.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1353848722974445658#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Reconfigure vs Once per Turn: a spent Graxxlid moved by Reconfigure onto a new host is still spent · Key: concepts.abilities.once.moved-mod</sub>

<a id="r109.9f"></a>**109.9f** A unit that leaves play and is played again is a new object, and its abilities have their uses again, even in the same turn. See rule 410.

> *Example: Engorged Caudex recalled and played again draws from its [Switch1] graft a second time that turn.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#16; RAQ 1355115946032889914#16 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 calebgannon · Key: concepts.abilities.once.new-object</sub>

<a id="r109.9g"></a>**109.9g** Turning a card over does not give back a spent use: a transformed card is the same unit. See rule 108. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Key: concepts.abilities.once.transform</sub>

<a id="r109.9h"></a>**109.9h** If the cause of a graft composite is bounded, the whole composite can trigger only once per turn, unbounded grafts included. See rule 722.

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.33; Rulebook 2023 p.16 · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#14 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 94-bounded-uses.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 12: a bounded host triggers once per turn · Key: concepts.abilities.once.bounded-cause</sub>

<a id="r109.9i"></a>**109.9i** If the cause is unbounded, the composite can trigger any number of times, but each bounded graft in it is included only the first time in a turn. See rule 722.

> *Example: Omniwield Evoker activated twice in a turn creates the Robot from its bounded graft only the first time.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.33 · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#13 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 94-bounded-uses.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 12: an unbounded host activated twice · Key: concepts.abilities.once.unbounded-cause</sub>

<a id="r109.9j"></a>**109.9j** An effect that repeats a graft composite (Amphivore, Lost Guardian) repeats its bounded grafts too. See rule 722.

> *Example: Amphivore triples a bounded "Create three" graft.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1353859961855148103#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 14-water-a.test.ts, 17-earth-b.test.ts · Example test: 14-water-a.test.ts::CR 109.9j: Amphivore triples a BOUNDED [Switch1] graft · Key: concepts.abilities.once.multiplier</sub>

<a id="r109.9k"></a>**109.9k** Each mod has its own use. Two copies of the same bounded graft on one host each have one use.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 94-bounded-uses.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 94-bounded-uses.test.ts::the bounded budget of a graft rider is per MOD · Key: concepts.abilities.once.per-mod</sub>

<a id="r109.9m"></a>**109.9m** A bounded ability that works while its card is in a bin, such as Rotling's "When I leave your bin", is limited once per turn for each player and card name: copies of one card in one player's bin share one use. See rules 405, 109.9n.

> *Example: Rotling's [Switch1] works once per turn from the bin and is available again the next turn.*

> *Example: Two Rotling leaving one bin in the same turn share one [Switch1] use: the second copy is not offered it.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 43-dark-c.test.ts, 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts · Example tests: 43-dark-c.test.ts::Rotling: the [Switch1] bounds it once per turn when it does something, 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts::cr:concepts.abilities.once.bin — two copies of Rotling leaving ONE bin in the same turn share one [Switch1] use · Key: concepts.abilities.once.bin</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U03-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r109.9n"></a>**109.9n** A bounded "When I am trashed" ability is limited for each trashed card, not for each player and card name: two copies of one card trashed in the same turn each trigger. See rule 109.9m.

> *Example: Two Maw of Despair discarded in the same turn each trigger their [Switch1] Glimpse 2.*

<sub>Basis: Engine only · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Engine: engine.ts:E.fireOwnTrashTrigger · Tests: 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts · Example test: 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts::cr:concepts.abilities.once.trashed — two copies of Maw of Despair discarded in one turn each trigger their bounded trash ability · Key: concepts.abilities.once.trashed</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U03-10 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r110"></a>
### 110. Targets

<a id="r110.1"></a>**110.1.** A target is something a card or ability chooses, with the word "target", to receive its actions. The targets are selected as the card is played. See rule 702.

> *Example: Fight ("Target ally and another target unit fight") takes both units as targets as it is played.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.13; Manual p.13 · Tests: 16-earth-a.test.ts, 49-playtest-round6.test.ts · Example test: 16-earth-a.test.ts::Fight: BOTH units are cast-time targets, ally first · Key: concepts.targets.what</sub>

<a id="r110.1a"></a>**110.1a** Targets are chosen as the effect is put on the stack: when a card is played, when an ability is activated, and when a triggered ability is put on the stack. Every target of the effect is chosen then. See rules 702, 703.

> *Example: Plodding Pebble carries a grafted Leaping Lillik ("Delete target unit"). A Fireball damages the Pebble: as the trigger goes on the stack, the delete's target is chosen. With no enemy in the region, it must be one of your own units.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#15 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 68-target-conformance.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 Plodding Pebble example · Key: concepts.targets.what.on-stack</sub>

<a id="r110.1b"></a>**110.1b** Each "target" in an effect's text is a separate target. An effect that says "target" twice chooses two targets.

> *Example: Squish chooses two targets as it is played: an ally and another unit.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 68-target-conformance.test.ts · Example test: 68-target-conformance.test.ts::CR 110.1b: a card printing N targets declares N cast-time target slots · Key: concepts.targets.what.count</sub>

<a id="r110.1c"></a>**110.1c** "Up to N target" lets the player choose any number of targets from none to N, and "any number of target" lets the player choose none as well. Only such words make a target optional: without them every target is required (see rule 110.7).

> *Example: Twin Flame ("up to two target units") can be played with no targets.*

> *Example: Tilling the Graves ("Recall two target units in your bin") says no "up to": once cast, it asks for both units and offers no way to stop at one.*

> *Example: Penance ("Any number of target players each lose 1 life. Draw a card.") may be played with no target, and its caster still draws.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 4 tests, all passed; 4 gate test files · Printed: card: Penance · Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16; Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 21-fixes.test.ts, 478-required-targets-at-cast.test.ts, 477-target-minimum-sweep.test.ts, 38-light-a.test.ts · Example tests: 21-fixes.test.ts::CR 110.1c: an "up to" spell may decline every target, 478-required-targets-at-cast.test.ts::Tilling the Graves with two units in the bin is offered and asks for both with no stop, 38-light-a.test.ts::Penance: with no targets declared (min 0) the draw still happens · Key: concepts.targets.what.up-to</sub>

<a id="r110.1d"></a>**110.1d** The number of targets an effect has is the number chosen as it was put on the stack. A target that is later lost still counts.

> *Example: Twin Flame declared with two targets, one of them later removed, is still not "a single target" for Envoy of Lightning.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 3; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1397256636921417748#1 · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts · Example test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Envoy of Lightning: two DECLARED targets is not "a single target" · Key: concepts.targets.what.declared-count</sub>

<a id="r110.2"></a>**110.2.** A choice that an effect's text does not make with the word "target" is not a target. Nothing is declared for it as the effect goes on the stack, and an effect that answers targeting cannot answer it.

> *Example: Meteor Shower's rockfall chooses rather than targets, so Boon of Protection has nothing to negate.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353899470156206152#3; RAQ 1353899470156206152#3 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Meteor Shower: rockfall chooses rather than targets · Key: concepts.targets.not-target</sub>

<a id="r110.2a"></a>**110.2a** Such a choice cannot be redirected by an effect that changes targets, and it does not trigger "when I become targeted".

> *Example: The Wraith's "an ally" never fires a "becomes targeted" ability.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22, 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Example test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::CR 706.12a: a subject is not a target · Key: concepts.targets.not-target.traits</sub>

<a id="r110.2b"></a>**110.2b** Dividing or distributing an amount among a targeted player's units is not targeting those units. The division is made as the effect resolves. See rule 704.

> *Example: Channel Through targets X allies and an opponent as it is played, and divides its damage among that opponent's units only as it resolves.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Channel Through · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 69-damage-batch.test.ts, 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts · Example test: 69-damage-batch.test.ts::CR 110.2b: Channel Through declares X allies AND the opponent at cast · Key: concepts.targets.not-target.distribution</sub>

<a id="r110.2c"></a>**110.2c** The Wraith's "an ally" is not a target. The ally is chosen as the trigger resolves, from the allies in play then, so the trigger cannot lose its ally and does not fizzle while an ally is in play. With no ally in play, it fizzles. See rule 704.

> *Example: Three Wraith triggers and one 1/1 ally: only the first trigger is offered the 1/1, and it kills it. The other two put their counters on Wraiths still in play, and nothing fizzles.*

> *Example: A 1/1 carrying two Wraith augments: the first shrink kills it, and the second finds no ally in play and fizzles.*

<sub>Basis: Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16 · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts, 460-wraith-chooses-on-resolution.test.ts, 461-wraith-no-ally-and-one-ally.test.ts · Example tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::CR 706.12: three Wraith triggers and one 1/1 choose as each resolves, so only the first is offered the 1/1 and none fizzles, 461-wraith-no-ally-and-one-ally.test.ts::report 2026-10-16: a Wraith shrink that finds no ally in play asks nothing and fizzles · Key: concepts.targets.not-target.wraith</sub>

<a id="r110.3"></a>**110.3.** Only a legal target can be chosen. Whether a target is legal depends on the kind of thing the text names (a unit, an ally, a player, an effect, a card in a bin) and on any restriction written on the target itself.

> *Example: Minor Kraken ("target unit with 5 or less defense") cannot target a unit with 6 defense.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1355466429788328066#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-29 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 68-target-conformance.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ valid targets: Minor Kraken cannot aim at a unit with more than 5 defense · Key: concepts.targets.legal</sub>

<a id="r110.3a"></a>**110.3a** A clause that describes the target ("with 5 or less defense", "that targets an allied effect", "in your bin") limits which targets are legal. An "if" clause attached to the action ("delete target unit if it has a -1/-1 counter on it") does not limit the choice; it is checked as the effect resolves.

> *Example: Boon of Protection is not offered against an effect that targets nothing allied.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-08-29 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Tests: 68-target-conformance.test.ts, 23-wood-a.test.ts, 16-earth-a.test.ts · Example test: 23-wood-a.test.ts::Boon of Protection: negates an effect aimed at something allied · Demonstrated by test: 68-target-conformance.test.ts::CR 110.3: a restrictive clause on a target noun is enforced at CAST · Key: concepts.targets.legal.clause</sub>

<a id="r110.3b"></a>**110.3b** An effect on the stack can be a target. A unit in play is not an effect, so it cannot fill a target that asks for an effect. See rule 700.

> *Example: Enigmatic Warder cannot become the target of a negate that wants a spell effect.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1355466429788328066#5 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 118-stack-effect.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ valid targets: Enigmatic Warder cannot become the target of a negate that wants a spell effect · Key: concepts.targets.legal.effect</sub>

<a id="r110.3c"></a>**110.3c** "Target player" can be any player present in the region where the effect resolves, the effect's controller included. "Target opponent" is any such player other than the effect's controller. In battle both players are present. See rule 110.5b.

> *Example: Soul Siphon played in battle offers its own controller as well as the opponent as "target player".*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21, 2026-09-05 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 3; verifier ran 3 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 60-cast-time-targets.test.ts, 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts · Example test: 60-cast-time-targets.test.ts::CR 110.3c: plain "target player" ('player') may legally be YOURSELF · Demonstrated by test: 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts::cr:concepts.targets.legal.player — in deployment "target player" offers only the controller and "target opponent" offers nobody; in battle both seats · Key: concepts.targets.legal.player</sub>

<a id="r110.3d"></a>**110.3d** "Target formation" targets one player's whole side of a battle in that region: every unit arrayed there, not a column.

> *Example: Galactic Germination counts three units across two columns of the targeted formation.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Galactic Germination · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts · Example test: 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts::Galactic Germination: "target formation" is THE WHOLE SIDE · Key: concepts.targets.legal.formation</sub>

<a id="r110.3e"></a>**110.3e** A formation stays a legal target while its battle lasts, even if every unit leaves it.

> *Example: Galactic Germination aimed at a formation that has emptied creates nothing, and does not fizzle.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts · Example test: 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts::Galactic Germination: an EMPTY formation is still a formation · Key: concepts.targets.legal.formation-empty</sub>

<a id="r110.4"></a>**110.4.** An ally is a unit under your control in the region the effect is happening in. An enemy is a unit not under your control in that region. See rules 102, 601.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 243-ally-and-enemy-scope.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 243-ally-and-enemy-scope.test.ts::CR 110.4 the enemy target is the mirror · Key: concepts.targets.ally</sub>

<a id="r110.4a"></a>**110.4a** A unit is its own ally. An effect that targets "an ally" or "target ally" can choose its own source unless the text says "another".

> *Example: Shoreline Specter's "recall target ally" may target the Specter itself.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Shoreline Specter · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22, 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 243-ally-and-enemy-scope.test.ts, 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Example test: 243-ally-and-enemy-scope.test.ts::CR 110.4a an ally target offers the source · Key: concepts.targets.ally.self</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U03-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r110.4b"></a>**110.4b** Ally and enemy follow control, not ownership. A unit you have taken control of is your ally and its owner's enemy, in that region, for as long as you control it.

> *Example: An opponent ambushes with Orblish Horroth to recall target ally. Before it resolves, you take control of that unit; it is no longer their ally, and the ambush recalls nothing.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355466429788328066#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ valid targets: an Ambush whose ally changed sides before it resolves recalls nothing · Key: concepts.targets.ally.control</sub>

<a id="r110.4c"></a>**110.4c** Ally is measured from the effect's controller, never from the player making the choice.

> *Example: With the opponent's Fight on the stack, an enemy unit cannot fill its ally target, while another of the Fight controller's units can.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 3; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1355466429788328066#4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 49-playtest-round6.test.ts, 243-ally-and-enemy-scope.test.ts · Example test: 49-playtest-round6.test.ts::CR 110.9: canFillSlot enforces the slot restriction directly · Demonstrated by test: 243-ally-and-enemy-scope.test.ts::CR 102.7 ally is measured from the EFFECT controller · Key: concepts.targets.ally.effect-controller</sub>

<a id="r110.4d"></a>**110.4d** "Another" excludes whatever the sentence's other noun is. It excludes the source only when that other noun is the source ("I fight another target unit"); in "from target unit onto another target unit" it excludes only the first target. See rule 108.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 243-ally-and-enemy-scope.test.ts, 121-another-identity.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 243-ally-and-enemy-scope.test.ts::CR 110.4d across the whole another-target family · Key: concepts.targets.ally.another</sub>

<a id="r110.5"></a>**110.5.** An effect can target a unit only in the region where the effect is happening. See rule 601.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 243-ally-and-enemy-scope.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 243-ally-and-enemy-scope.test.ts::CR 110.5 nor can any other unit-shaped target · Key: concepts.targets.region</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U03-5 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r110.5a"></a>**110.5a** An effect on the stack can be targeted only by an effect in its own region, since each region has its own stack (rule 601.2a). A card in a player's bin can be targeted only by an effect that resolves in a region where that player is present. See rules 405, 406. *(Engine differs, see F-U01-2.)*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.19; Manual p.19; Manual p.19 · Designer: RAQ 1454169054402314362#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-11 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Key: concepts.targets.region.global</sub>

<a id="r110.5b"></a>**110.5b** A player's cache, and a player as a target, can be targeted only by an effect that resolves in a region where that player is present. See rule 403.

> *Example: In deployment Prismatic Observer reaches only its controller's cache; in battle it reaches both.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-05 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 293-cached-targets-are-regional.test.ts · Example test: 293-cached-targets-are-regional.test.ts::CR 110.5b in deployment a home region reaches only its own seat's cache; in battle both · Key: concepts.targets.region.cache</sub>

<a id="r110.6"></a>**110.6.** Where an effect asks for two or more targets together, one object cannot be two of them, as with Twin Flame's "up to two target units". This holds when targets are changed as well as when they are chosen.

> *Example: Divine Intervention cannot make Twin Flame target one unit twice.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355466429788328066#6 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 349-retarget-distinct-slots.test.ts · Example test: 349-retarget-distinct-slots.test.ts::CT-189 owner board: Divine Intervention cannot aim Twin Flame at one Good Whale twice · Key: concepts.targets.distinct</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U03-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r110.6a"></a>**110.6a** Different effects may target the same object. See rule 704.

> *Example: An opponent's Luminous Arc is aimed at one of your Good Whales; you answer with Organic Exchange targeting both your Good Whales. The Luminous Arc still resolves.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1454169054402314362#2 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Another set: Organic Exchange may target two of your own units · Key: concepts.targets.distinct.separate-effects</sub>

<a id="r110.7"></a>**110.7.** A card or ability that needs targets can be played only if every target it requires can be chosen at the same time, each one legal and different from the others. Every target a card names is required unless the card says "up to" or "any number" (see rule 110.1c). A card that targets nothing has no such requirement. See rule 702.

> *Example: Fight cannot be played unless its region holds an ally and another unit.*

> *Example: Rebalance, which targets nothing, can be played with no unit of its controller's.*

> *Example: Abduct ("Gain control of target unit with cost [x] or less …") against a lone cost-1 attacker can be played when its caster can pay an X of 1 or more. X = 0 is not offered, since at 0 there is no unit to take.*

> *Example: Tilling the Graves ("Recall two target units in your bin") cannot be played while its caster's bin holds fewer than two units.*

> *Example: Tidal Reversion ("For each player, recall target unit that player controls") played for free by Tides of the Cosmos takes one unit of each player, and Tides does not offer it while either player has no unit there.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 7 tests, all passed; 7 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1410252965276684418#1; RAQ 1454169054402314362#1 · Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16; Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 396-raq-timing.test.ts, 401-raq-fix-stack.test.ts, 452-abduct-x-gate.test.ts, 478-required-targets-at-cast.test.ts, 477-target-minimum-sweep.test.ts, 510-inline-play-targets.test.ts · Example tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ target requirements: Fight cannot be played, 396-raq-timing.test.ts::Rebalance is playable with no unit, 452-abduct-x-gate.test.ts::Abduct is castable against a cost-1 attacker, its X menu starts at 1, and control flips, 478-required-targets-at-cast.test.ts::Tilling the Graves is not offered with, 510-inline-play-targets.test.ts::CT-308: Tidal Reversion under Tides takes one unit of each player · Key: concepts.targets.required</sub>

<a id="r110.8"></a>**110.8.** A target that was legal when it was chosen but is not legal when the effect begins to resolve is lost, as if it had left play. See rule 704.

> *Example: A unit that grows past 5 defense before Minor Kraken resolves is not recalled.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355466429788328066#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ valid targets: a target that grows past 5 defense before Minor Kraken resolves is not recalled · Key: concepts.targets.recheck</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U03-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r110.9"></a>**110.9.** An effect that changes another effect's targets must choose each new target as that target was first chosen: legal for that target's own kind and restriction, and not an object already chosen for another target of the same part of the effect. An effect with no target that can be changed is still a legal "target effect" for it, and the change then does nothing. The client asks the player to confirm before such an effect is chosen. *(Digital client)* See rule 110.6.

> *Example: Enigmatic Warder cannot take Throw off a Cliff, which needs a unit with 4 or more defense.*

> *Example: Enigmatic Warder cannot move itself into a target already held by the same effect's other target.*

> *Example: Gravitational Correction may be aimed at Surly Stalker's trigger, which has no targets; the client first asks "This effect has no targets, so Gravitational Correction will do nothing. Continue?", and Continue sends the choice.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: partial in round 4; verifier ran 4 tests, all passed; 5 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1355466429788328066#3; RAQ 1355466429788328066#6 · Owner call · adopted 2026-10-21; Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-09-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 349-retarget-distinct-slots.test.ts, 49-playtest-round6.test.ts, 511-retarget-nothing-to-change.test.ts, 529-noop-retarget-confirm.test.ts · Example tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ valid targets: Enigmatic Warder cannot take Throw off a Cliff, 349-retarget-distinct-slots.test.ts::CT-189 canFillSlot, the Enigmatic Warder gate, refuses a sibling ref on every multi-target part, 529-noop-retarget-confirm.test.ts::CT-307 the client asks before sending a targetless pick, and Continue sends that pick · Key: concepts.targets.change</sub>

<a id="r110.9a"></a>**110.9a** A target that is kept when targets are changed is not a change, and it is not judged again then.

> *Example: Divine Intervention can keep one target of an effect while changing another.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 140-layers-and-riders.test.ts · Example test: 140-layers-and-riders.test.ts::Divine Intervention can keep one target while changing another · Key: concepts.targets.change.kept</sub>

<a id="r110.9b"></a>**110.9b** Changing an effect's targets before it resolves can save it from fizzling. See rule 704.

> *Example: A spell whose target is about to become illegal is given a legal new target by Enigmatic Warder before it resolves, and then it does not fizzle.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 3; verifier ran 2 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1354013430805434389#2 · Tests: 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts · Example test: 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts::cr:concepts.targets.change.rescue — the same spell given a new legal target by Enigmatic Warder resolves instead of fizzling · Key: concepts.targets.change.rescue</sub>

<a id="r110.10"></a>**110.10.** Applying an augment, a graft or a Virus to a unit targets that unit. See rule 720.

> *Example: Grafting onto Mohruung targets it, so its "when I become targeted" ability makes a Crystal.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 17-earth-b.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 5 · Key: concepts.targets.applying-mods</sub>

<a id="r110.10a"></a>**110.10a** A Virus being applied is an effect on the stack that targets its host. It can be redirected, and an effect that answers "target effect targeting me" or an effect targeting an ally can answer it. See rule 723.

> *Example: Graxxlid ("Negate target effect targeting me") can negate a Virus being applied to it.*

> *Example: Boon of Protection can negate a Virus being applied to an allied unit.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 16-earth-a.test.ts, 23-wood-a.test.ts · Example tests: 16-earth-a.test.ts::Graxxlid: a Virus being applied to me IS an effect targeting me, 23-wood-a.test.ts::Boon of Protection: a Virus being applied to an allied unit IS an allied target · Key: concepts.targets.applying-mods.virus</sub>

<a id="r110.11"></a>**110.11.** An ability that triggers "when I become targeted" triggers whenever its unit is targeted, by a spell, an ability, an augment, a graft or a Virus. When the effect that targeted is put on the stack, the trigger goes on the stack above it and so resolves first. When a graft targets the unit, the unit triggers first, before the graft is applied. *(Engine differs, see F-U03-5.)*

> *Example: Mohruung targeted by an augment makes a Crystal 2.*

> *Example: Grafting onto Mohruung makes a Crystal 2.*

> *Example: A spell aimed at Mohruung waits on the stack under Mohruung's trigger, so the Crystal 2 is made before the spell resolves.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 3; verifier ran 5 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 4 gate test files · Printed: card: Mohruung · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 48-playtest-hotfix.test.ts, 17-earth-b.test.ts, 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts · Example tests: 17-earth-b.test.ts::Mohruung: augment-targeting triggers a Crystal 2, 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 5, 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts::cr:concepts.targets.becomes-targeted — the trigger of Mohruung goes on the stack ABOVE the spell that targeted it, and the Crystal is made while the spell still waits · Demonstrated by test: 48-playtest-hotfix.test.ts::a spell aimed at Mohruung actually creates the Crystal 2 · Key: concepts.targets.becomes-targeted</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U03-13 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r110.12"></a>**110.12.** A unit that "must be targeted if able" (Gatekeeper of Souls) must be one of the targets of an effect whose targets are selected during battle, when it can legally be one. Once it is among the targets, the effect's other targets may be anything legal. *(Engine differs, see F-U03-2.)*

> *Example: Twin Flame aims at Gatekeeper of Souls first, then at any other unit.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Gatekeeper of Souls · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 382-gatekeeper-multi-target.test.ts · Example test: 382-gatekeeper-multi-target.test.ts::CR 110.12: a two-target spell aims at the Gatekeeper first · Key: concepts.targets.must-be-targeted</sub>

<a id="r110.12a"></a>**110.12a** With two such units in the region, each must be targeted if able: a two-target effect must target both.

> *Example: With two Gatekeepers in the region, a two-target spell targets both.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 382-gatekeeper-multi-target.test.ts · Example test: 382-gatekeeper-multi-target.test.ts::CR 110.12: two Gatekeepers · Key: concepts.targets.must-be-targeted.several</sub>

<a id="r110.12b"></a>**110.12b** "If able" means "if it is a legal target for this effect". An effect whose targets cannot be units, such as one that targets a formation, is not compelled.

> *Example: Gatekeeper of Souls does not compel Galactic Germination, which targets a formation.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts · Example test: 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts::Gatekeeper of Souls cannot compel a formation target · Key: concepts.targets.must-be-targeted.able</sub>

<a id="r110.12c"></a>**110.12c** The compulsion applies only to choosing targets. It never makes a target already chosen illegal.

> *Example: A Gatekeeper of Souls that arrives after an effect's targets were chosen does not make those targets illegal.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts · Example test: 414-cr-cards-abilities-targets.test.ts::cr:concepts.targets.must-be-targeted.choice-only — a Gatekeeper of Souls arriving after targets were chosen does not make them illegal · Key: concepts.targets.must-be-targeted.choice-only</sub>

<a id="r111"></a>
### 111. Costs

<a id="r111.1"></a>**111.1.** A cost is something a player must pay to do something: to play a card, to apply a mod, or to activate an ability. A card's mana cost, the additional costs in its brackets, and everything before the colon of an activated ability are costs. See rules 702, 705, 720.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.13; Manual p.41 · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#1 · Tests: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts::RAQ Mods are NOT Played: an augment from hand needs its affinity and pays its cost · Key: concepts.costs.what-a-cost-is</sub>

<a id="r111.1a"></a>**111.1a** A mana cost is paid by expending resources: each resource can be expended once per turn for 1 mana, to pay the mana cost of a card or of an ability. See rule 106.

> *Example: with two open resources, paying [one] for Auric Ascendant's ability and then playing Shard Sprite expends both; a second 1-cost card is not playable that turn, and both resources are open again next turn.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.14; Rulebook 2023 p.4 · Tests: 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts · Example test: 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts::cr:concepts.costs.what-a-cost-is.mana — each resource is expended once for 1 mana, for a card or an ability, and is open again next turn · Key: concepts.costs.what-a-cost-is.mana</sub>

<a id="r111.1b"></a>**111.1b** Meeting a card's affinity requirement is not paying a cost. Nothing is spent to meet it, and resources that are already expended still count toward it. See rule 105.

> *Example: a player with two Wood resources, both already expended, still meets a requirement of two Wood pips.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13 · Designer: RAQ 1358299200953126963#0 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Mana question: affinity counts resources already spent — two wood pay for many gg cards · Key: concepts.costs.what-a-cost-is.affinity-not-a-cost</sub>

<a id="r111.2"></a>**111.2.** Besides mana, a cost may require a player to pay life, gain debt, discard cards, sacrifice units, erase cards from their bin, remove counters, recall an ally or erase a mod. A cost of any kind is paid in full before the thing it pays for is put on the stack. See rule 702.4.

> *Example: Slag Spewer's "[one], Erase one of my mods:" erases the mod as the ability is activated, before anyone can respond.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Flesh Tithe; card: Deferral Drone; card: Necromantic Rebuke; card: Volatile Toxicity; card: Instrument of Reassignment · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 47-costs-events.test.ts, 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts · Example test: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts::CR 111.2 Slag Spewer · Key: concepts.costs.kinds</sub>

<a id="r111.3"></a>**111.3.** A cost that sacrifices units can be paid only with units the player controls in the region where the cost is paid. They cannot sacrifice a unit they do not control, or a unit of theirs that is in another region. See rule 601.

> *Example: when Volatile Toxicity is played in battle, its sacrifice menu offers the unit in the battle region and not the unit the player left at home.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.42; Manual p.41 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts · Example test: 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts::cr:concepts.costs.region — a sacrifice cost menu holds only units in the region where it is paid · Key: concepts.costs.region</sub>

<a id="r111.3a"></a>**111.3a** A cost that removes counters from the player's allies, or recalls an ally, likewise uses only the player's own units in the region where the cost is paid. See rule 111.3.

> *Example: Auric Ascendant’s "Recall another ally" cost offers the ally fighting beside it, never the ally at home and never itself.*

<sub>Basis: Engine only · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Engine: engine.ts:E.canPayCastCost · Tests: 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts · Example test: 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts::cr:concepts.costs.region.other-units — a [Recall another ally] menu holds only allies in the region where it is paid · Key: concepts.costs.region.other-units</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U04-13 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r111.4"></a>**111.4.** What was paid is fixed at the moment it is paid. An effect that reads a paid cost (such as "the defense of the sacrificed unit") reads it as it was when it was paid.

> *Example: Volatile Toxicity is cast by sacrificing a Good Whale (7/5). Its X is fixed at 5 as the cost is paid, and it makes a Poison 5 and a Fireball 5.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 32-cast-costs.test.ts · Example test: 32-cast-costs.test.ts::Volatile Toxicity: X reads the defense snapshotted when the cost was paid · Key: concepts.costs.receipt</sub>

<a id="r111.5"></a>**111.5.** A copy of a spell does not pay the original's additional cost again. It uses what the original paid, including the original's X. See rule 710.

> *Example: Maelstrom Charger copies a Volatile Toxicity; the copy makes its Poison and Fireball from the one sacrifice the original paid for.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1379132904931594372#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 138-spell-copy.test.ts · Example test: 138-spell-copy.test.ts::CR 710.8a Maelstrom Charger: the copy inherits the cast-cost receipt (CR 111.5) — Volatile Toxicity is not re-paid · Key: concepts.costs.copies</sub>

<a id="r111.6"></a>**111.6.** A cost that cannot be paid in full cannot be paid at all. A card whose cost cannot be paid cannot be played, and an ability whose cost cannot be paid cannot be activated; nothing is paid, and the play or activation is not offered. See rule 702.4a.

> *Example: Auric Ascendant ("[one], Recall another ally:") is not offered while it has no other ally, so its [one] is never paid.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1353859961855148103#5 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts, 47-costs-events.test.ts · Example test: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts::CR 705.4 Auric Ascendant with no other ally is NOT OFFERED — an unpayable cost gates, it does not whiff (CR 111.6) · Key: concepts.costs.unpayable</sub>

<a id="r111.6a"></a>**111.6a** A cost made of several parts is paid all or nothing. If any part cannot be paid, no part is paid, including the mana.

> *Example: Instrument of Reassignment ("[x], Sacrifice another nontoken unit:") with no other nontoken unit pays neither the mana nor anything else.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1353859961855148103#5 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts, 17-earth-b.test.ts · Example test: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts::CR 111.6a the COMPOUND half-pay hazard: an unpayable half of Instrument of Reassignment's cost pays NOTHING, neither the mana nor the unit · Key: concepts.costs.unpayable.all-or-nothing</sub>

<a id="r111.6b"></a>**111.6b** A player may pay N life only while they have more than N life. A life cost that would bring them to 0 cannot be paid. See rule 112.1.

> *Example: at exactly 9 life, Glararr's "Pay 9 life:" cannot be activated.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-08-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 38-light-a.test.ts, 47-costs-events.test.ts · Example test: 38-light-a.test.ts::Glararr: CR 111.6b — at exactly 9 life the cost cannot be paid and the activation is ILLEGAL · Key: concepts.costs.unpayable.life</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U04-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r111.7"></a>**111.7.** An activated ability's whole cost is paid when the ability is activated, before it is put on the stack. A fixed cost is paid after the ability's targets are chosen. A variable cost (one whose amount is X) is paid first, and what is paid sets X, before any target is chosen. No player may respond between the payment and the ability going on the stack, and negating the ability does not refund it. See rule 705.

> *Example: Infernal Cultivator's "Sacrifice X units:" kills the units as the ability is activated, so a negation cannot give them back.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 4 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.41 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21, 2026-08-22, 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts, 47-costs-events.test.ts, 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts · Example test: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts::CR 111.7 Infernal Cultivator · Key: concepts.costs.activation</sub>

<a id="r111.7a"></a>**111.7a** When an activated ability's cost sacrifices its own source, the source is in the bin while the ability waits on the stack.

> *Example: Throwing Boulder ("Sacrifice me: I deal 3 damage to any target.") is in the bin as soon as the ability is on the stack.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; no gate test · Key: concepts.costs.activation.sacrifice-me</sub>

<a id="r111.7b"></a>**111.7b** A printed condition on activating an ability ("Activate this ability only if …") is checked before any cost is paid. If it is not met, the ability cannot be activated. It is not checked again when the ability resolves. See rule 705.

> *Example: Throwing Boulder with no adjacent ally is not offered its ability.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Throwing Boulder · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 18-earth-c.test.ts, 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts · Example test: 18-earth-c.test.ts::CR 111.7b: with NO adjacent ally the ability is not offered, and apply() refuses it · Key: concepts.costs.activation.gate-first</sub>

<a id="r111.8"></a>**111.8.** When a triggered ability's effect says "sacrifice me. If you do, …", the sacrifice is part of the effect, not a cost: the ability goes on the stack with its source still in play, players may respond, and the source is sacrificed as the ability resolves. The sacrifice is not optional. If the source is no longer in play when the ability resolves, it cannot be sacrificed, and the "If you do" part does nothing.

> *Example: Eldritch Dreamtender's column deals combat damage to an opponent. Its ability goes on the stack with Dreamtender still in play; Dreamtender is sacrificed when the ability resolves, and only then is the opponent's hand looked at and a card discarded.*

> *Example: Dreamtender is destroyed in response to its ability. When the ability resolves, nothing is sacrificed, so no hand is looked at and nothing is discarded.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Eldritch Dreamtender; card: Cthyrian Rector; card: Void Mandible · Designer: RQ 1363535826436493614 · Tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts, 515-trigger-sacrifice-me.test.ts · Example tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts::Eldritch Dreamtender: the trigger waits on the stack with the Dreamtender in play, and it is sacrificed as the trigger resolves (CR 111.8), 515-trigger-sacrifice-me.test.ts::§2 Eldritch Dreamtender: a real response — the opponent kills it with the trigger on the stack · Demonstrated by test: 26-metal-a.test.ts::Eldritch Dreamtender: the sacrifice is MANDATORY — no decline is ever offered (CR 111.8) · Key: concepts.costs.trigger-sacrifice-me</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U04-2, D-U04-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r111.8a"></a>**111.8a** A sacrifice the text makes optional ("you may sacrifice me. If you do, …") is the player's choice. A player who declines it gets nothing from the "If you do" part.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; no gate test · Designer: RAQ 1379132904931594372#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Key: concepts.costs.trigger-sacrifice-me.optional</sub>

<a id="r111.9"></a>**111.9.** A payment that an effect's text asks for while it resolves ("you may pay [one] to …", "unless its controller pays [x]") is not a cost of putting it on the stack. The ability goes on the stack without it, and the player decides whether to pay when it resolves. See rules 702.5a, 704.

> *Example: Xenopod Progenitor's trigger goes on the stack with no payment asked; its [1] is asked as it resolves.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1397189214352703590#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ Xenopod: the trigger goes on the stack with no payment asked, and the [1] is asked as it resolves · Key: concepts.costs.resolution-payments</sub>

<a id="r111.10"></a>**111.10.** Some cards in play change what it costs to play cards or to activate or trigger abilities. Such a cost modifier works only while its source is in play, only in its source's region, and, unless it says otherwise, for every player in that region, its controller included. See rules 601, 701.2b.

> *Example: an opponent's Crevice Lurker in the battle region taxes your abilities, not only its controller's.*

> *Example: Tranquility applied as an augment still taxes spells from its host.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Tranquility · Designer: RAQ 1355103348378042515#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 18-earth-c.test.ts, 49-playtest-round6.test.ts · Example tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ Crevice Lurker: it taxes the opponent too, not only its controller, 18-earth-c.test.ts::Tranquility: the [Augment] tax is DONATED — it radiates from the mod too · Key: concepts.costs.modifiers</sub>

<a id="r111.10a"></a>**111.10a** Cost modifiers add up. Two modifiers that each add [one] add [two].

> *Example: two Crevice Lurkers make an activated [1] cost [3] in battle.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 16-earth-a.test.ts · Example test: 16-earth-a.test.ts::Crevice Lurker: CR 111.10a — two Lurkers compound: CostMod deltas SUM, so the tax is +2 · Key: concepts.costs.modifiers.sum</sub>

<a id="r111.10b"></a>**111.10b** A cost reduced below zero is zero.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; no gate test · Key: concepts.costs.modifiers.floor-zero</sub>

<a id="r111.10c"></a>**111.10c** A cost modifier applies to what its text names. One that names "spells" applies to every spell played, spell units and spell tokens included. One that names "cards" applies to every card played, units included, and not to spell tokens, which are not cards. Neither applies to applying a mod, which is not playing a card. See rules 701.1c, 701.2b, 111.10e. *(Engine differs, see F-U04-2.)*
