> *Example: Tranquility ("Spells cost [one] more") taxes a Fireball token cast in battle.*

> *Example: Arbiter of Armistice ("Cards played during battle gain [Pay 2 life]") takes no life for a spell token.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 6 tests (3 probes it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24, 2026-09-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 337-spell-tokens-are-played.test.ts, 38-light-a.test.ts, 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts · Example tests: 337-spell-tokens-are-played.test.ts::CR 702.7a: Tranquility taxes a spell token [1] in battle, 337-spell-tokens-are-played.test.ts::CR 701.1c: Arbiter of Armistice prints Cards, so a token cast pays no life · Key: concepts.costs.modifiers.noun</sub>

<a id="r111.10d"></a>**111.10d** A cost modifier may give cards an additional cost ("Cards played during battle gain [Pay 2 life]"). The player who plays the card pays it, with the card's other costs, before the card is put on the stack. If it requires a sacrifice, that player chooses the unit from their own units. A card whose imposed cost cannot be paid cannot be played.

> *Example: under an opponent's Vengeance, the player choosing the sacrifice is offered only their own units.*

> *Example: under Arbiter of Armistice, a player who cannot pay the 2 life cannot play the card.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Arbiter of Armistice; card: Vengeance · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 45-hybrids-ld-b.test.ts, 38-light-a.test.ts · Example tests: 45-hybrids-ld-b.test.ts::Vengeance: opponents' battle cards gain '[Sacrifice a unit]' — the payer picks, off a menu of THEIR units only, 38-light-a.test.ts::Arbiter of Armistice: an unpayable life tax makes the card uncastable · Key: concepts.costs.modifiers.imposed</sub>

<a id="r111.10e"></a>**111.10e** A card played as an Ambush is a card played. During battle, an imposed cost on "cards played" applies to it. See rule 803. *(Engine differs, see F-U04-2.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; no gate test · Printed: card: Arbiter of Armistice · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Key: concepts.costs.modifiers.imposed.ambush</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U04-4 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r111.10f"></a>**111.10f** A modifier that makes abilities cost more "to activate or trigger" applies to activated abilities and to triggered abilities, graft triggers and the triggers of attributes such as Alluring and Resonant included. It does not apply to static abilities, to playing or applying cards, or to an option that is neither activated nor triggered. See rules 705, 706, 707.

> *Example: Crevice Lurker taxes a graft trigger.*

> *Example: Crevice Lurker taxes Resonant's extra damage, by the designer's stated intent.*

> *Example: applying an augment during battle is not taxed.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Crevice Lurker · Designer: RAQ 1355103348378042515#1; RAQ 1355103348378042515#3; RAQ 1366446116274442291#1; RAQ 1379132904931594372#3 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 16-earth-a.test.ts, 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts · Example tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ Crevice Lurker: a graft trigger is taxed like any other, 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ trigger-like attributes: Crevice Lurker taxes Resonant, the designer intent, 16-earth-a.test.ts::Crevice Lurker: CR 720.4a — applying an augment during battle is NOT taxed (a mod is not an activation) · Key: concepts.costs.modifiers.abilities</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U04-9 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r111.10g"></a>**111.10g** When a triggered ability would be put on the stack while such a tax applies, the player who would control it chooses whether to pay the tax. If they pay, the ability is put on the stack. If they decline, or cannot pay, it does not trigger.

> *Example: with a Crevice Lurker in the battle, you decline to pay the tax on your own Origon's trigger, so Origon does not negate your first spell of the battle.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Crevice Lurker · Designer: RAQ 1355103348378042515#4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 16-earth-a.test.ts, 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ Crevice Lurker: declining the tax on your own Origon lets your own first spell resolve · Demonstrated by test: 16-earth-a.test.ts::Crevice Lurker: CR 111.10g — a taxed trigger ASKS its controller, and paying [1] puts it on the stack · Key: concepts.costs.modifiers.trigger-tax</sub>

<a id="r111.10h"></a>**111.10h** A triggered ability that does not trigger because its tax was declined or could not be paid does not use up a "[once]" or other once-per-turn limit.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 16-earth-a.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 16-earth-a.test.ts::Crevice Lurker: CR 111.10h — declining prevents the trigger and does NOT spend its [once] (CR 109.9b) · Key: concepts.costs.modifiers.trigger-tax.once</sub>

<a id="r111.10i"></a>**111.10i** A modifier that gives spells a minimum base cost ("Spells with base cost [three] or less have a base cost of [three]") raises the cost of a spell whose printed cost is a number. For a spell whose cost is X, it instead makes the smallest X that may be chosen equal to that minimum, and the spell costs exactly the X chosen. See rules 107, 702.6.

> *Example: under Stasis Sentry in battle, Wildfire's X menu starts at 3, and X = 3 deals 3.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Stasis Sentry · Designer: RAQ 1359629594512068770#0; RAQ 1359629594512068770#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 133-x-cost-semantics.test.ts, 19-hybrids.test.ts · Example test: 133-x-cost-semantics.test.ts::CR 107.5 (reversing the earlier price reading) — under a Stasis Sentry the X menu starts at 3, and X = 3 deals 3 · Key: concepts.costs.modifiers.minimum</sub>

<a id="r111.10j"></a>**111.10j** A spell token's printed cost is 0, so such a modifier makes a spell token cost its minimum.

> *Example: under Stasis Sentry, casting a Fireball token in battle costs [3].*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 337-spell-tokens-are-played.test.ts · Example test: 337-spell-tokens-are-played.test.ts::CR 111.10j: Stasis Sentry prints Spells, so a token (base cost 0) costs [3] in battle · Key: concepts.costs.modifiers.minimum.tokens</sub>

<a id="r111.10k"></a>**111.10k** A cost reduction a player has already paid for belongs to that player. It stays when its source leaves play, it applies in whatever region the player plays their next card, and it ends when its text says it ends: "the next card you play this phase" lasts until that card is played or the phase ends.

> *Example: sacrificing Deferral Drone in response does not take away the discount already paid for.*

> *Example: the discount ends when the phase ends, even within the same turn.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Deferral Drone · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 45-hybrids-ld-b.test.ts · Example tests: 45-hybrids-ld-b.test.ts::Deferral Drone: CR 111.10k — the charge SURVIVES the Drone leaving play (the owner: "you paid for it"), 45-hybrids-ld-b.test.ts::Deferral Drone: ERRATA — the charge expires at a MID-TURN phase boundary, not just the turn · Key: concepts.costs.modifiers.paid-reduction</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U04-10, D-U04-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r111.11"></a>**111.11.** When an effect refers to a card's cost, it means the card's printed cost. Cost modifiers do not change it. The cost of an X spell that is being or has just been cast is the X paid; an X card that is not being cast has a cost of 0. See rules 107, 202.

> *Example: Squish, paid at [4] under Stasis Sentry and Tranquility, is read as a 2-cost spell by Arcane Concentrator.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1353980184042143835#0; RAQ 1396955380000755795#9 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 133-x-cost-semantics.test.ts, 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ printed cost: Arcane Concentrator and Channeled Amalgam read a taxed Squish as a 2 · Demonstrated by test: 133-x-cost-semantics.test.ts::CR 111.11 — a card that was never cast has no cost: an X card in hand reads 0 · Key: concepts.costs.reading-cost</sub>

<a id="r111.12"></a>**111.12.** Some cards print another way to play or use them, with its own cost: a Prophecy or Ambush banner, or a "Discard me" line. Such a cost is paid like any other cost: its mana is spent and its affinity requirement must be met. See rules 203, 803.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 313-prophecy-affinity.test.ts, 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 313-prophecy-affinity.test.ts::CR 803.7d: mana without the affinity does not buy a prophecy, 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::CR 111.12: "Discard me" is refused without the mana · Key: concepts.costs.alternative</sub>

<a id="r111.12a"></a>**111.12a** Discarding a card through its "Discard me" line is not playing it. A player may do it whenever they hold priority in battle, and during their own deployment, unless the line itself is marked with a timing. See rule 701.

> *Example: Dropslime's discard-me line is offered in battle.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21, 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts, 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Example test: 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts::CR 111.12a: Dropslime’s discard-me mode is offered IN BATTLE and deals damage there · Key: concepts.costs.alternative.discard-me</sub>

<a id="r111.13"></a>**111.13.** A card played for free (released by a fulfilled prophecy, or played by an effect such as Tides of the Cosmos) pays no mana cost and ignores its affinity requirement. Its additional bracketed costs are still paid. See rules 702.6c, 702.4e.

> *Example: Tides of the Cosmos plays a fire unit for a player with only water resources.*

> *Example: Volatile Toxicity played by Tides still sacrifices a unit.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1396955380000755795#5 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts, 404-raq-fix-tides.test.ts, 313-prophecy-affinity.test.ts · Example tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Tides 1: a free play ignores affinity — a fire unit with only water resources, 404-raq-fix-tides.test.ts::CR 702.4e: a Tides play pays its additional cost — the sacrifice happens and Volatile Toxicity resolves · Key: concepts.costs.free</sub>

<a id="r111.13a"></a>**111.13a** An X spell played for free is played with X = 0. A card that says "X can't be zero" therefore cannot be played for free. See rule 107.

> *Example: Tides of the Cosmos cannot play Frosted Denial.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1396955380000755795#6 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts, 404-raq-fix-tides.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Tides 6: Frosted Denial (X cannot be zero) is not a card Tides can play · Key: concepts.costs.free.x</sub>

<a id="r111.14"></a>**111.14.** When an effect is repeated by a multiplier ("trigger two copies of this graft ability"), a cost the repeated effect carries is paid once for each copy. The whole multiplied cost is paid all or nothing: if it cannot all be paid, none of it is paid and that effect does not happen. See rule 722.

> *Example: under Lost Guardian, a "[Discard a card]:" graft pays twice and resolves twice.*

> *Example: with one card in hand, the doubled [Discard a card] is not paid at all.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353859961855148103#4; RAQ 1353859961855148103#5 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 17-earth-b.test.ts · Example tests: 17-earth-b.test.ts::CR 111.14: a "[cost]: effect" graft under Lost Guardian pays its cost TWICE and resolves twice, 17-earth-b.test.ts::CR 111.14: all or nothing — one card in hand cannot pay a doubled [Discard a card], so nothing is paid and nothing happens · Key: concepts.costs.multiplied</sub>

<a id="r111.15"></a>**111.15.** A cost a graft adds ("{graft} [cost]: effect") must be paid; it cannot be declined. If it cannot be paid, none of the composite ability goes on the stack: not the graft's effect, the host's own effect, or any other graft with it. The exception is a played spell that carries a {Modular} graft part: there an unpayable grafted cost skips only that part, and the spell is not withheld. See rule 722.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#10; RAQ 1355115946032889914#11 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts, 32-cast-costs.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 11: an unpayable [cost] graft keeps the whole composite off the stack — the host and the other grafts too · Key: concepts.costs.grafted</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U04-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r112"></a>
### 112. Life, Damage, Rot and Debt

<a id="r112.1"></a>**112.1.** Each player begins the game with 30 life. A player whose life is reduced to 0 is eliminated. See rules 103, 104.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.6; Manual p.6; Rulebook 2023 p.2 · Tests: 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts::cr:concepts.life.basics — players start at 30, and a player reduced to exactly 0 life loses the game · Key: concepts.life.basics</sub>

<a id="r112.1a"></a>**112.1a** A life total changes only by being gained or lost. Damage dealt to a player makes that player lose that much life, and paying life is losing it.

> *Example: Throwing Boulder's 3 damage to a player is a loss of 3 life, and the [Pay 2 life] that Arbiter of Armistice adds to a card played during battle is a loss of 2 life.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Arbiter of Vitality; card: Soul Siphon; Rulebook 2023 p.11 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts · Example test: 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts::cr:concepts.life.basics.gain-and-loss — damage to a player and a paid life cost both reach the life total as life lost · Key: concepts.life.basics.gain-and-loss</sub>

<a id="r112.1b"></a>**112.1b** An effect that makes players gain or lose life reaches only the players in its region. "Each opponent loses 1 life" means each opponent in the current region. See rule 601.

> *Example: Bloated Manablub dying in battle makes each opponent in that region lose 3 life.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.42 · Tests: 10-water-metal.test.ts, 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts · Example test: 10-water-metal.test.ts::Bloated Manablub: dying in battle → each opponent loses 3 life (region-scoped) · Key: concepts.life.basics.region</sub>

<a id="r112.2"></a>**112.2.** The life a player has lost in a battle is the sum of all their life losses in that battle. Life gained in the battle does not reduce it.

> *Example: a player loses 10, gains 8 and loses 3 in one battle; Soul Siphon makes a 13/13.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1449475896510648320#0 · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts · Example test: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Life lost: life lost in a battle adds up the losses and ignores the gains — Soul Siphon makes a 13/13 · Key: concepts.life.lost-in-battle</sub>

<a id="r112.3"></a>**112.3.** Effects that multiply life gained or lost multiply together: with n effects that each double it, the amount is multiplied by 2 to the power n. The multiplied amount is gained or lost at once, before it is checked whether the player has reached 0 life. See rule 708.

> *Example: three Arbiters of Vitality multiply a life loss by 8.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Arbiter of Vitality · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25, 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 137-multiplier-and-mode.test.ts, 45-hybrids-ld-b.test.ts · Example test: 137-multiplier-and-mode.test.ts::CR 708.6: THREE Arbiters multiply — the fold is EXPONENTIAL in n · Demonstrated by test: 137-multiplier-and-mode.test.ts::Arbiter of Vitality: a LETHAL loss is multiplied BEFORE the lethal check · Key: concepts.life.multipliers</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U15-4 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r112.4"></a>**112.4.** If a player's life total "can't change", that player neither gains nor loses life while the effect lasts.

> *Example: Suspend stops the target's life total moving in either direction for the battle.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Suspend · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts · Example test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Suspend: the target's life total can't change in either direction this battle · Key: concepts.life.cant-change</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U04-11 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r112.5"></a>**112.5.** Damage is dealt by a source to a unit or a player. Damage dealt to a unit is marked on it, and a unit whose total marked damage is greater than or equal to its defense dies. Damage dealt to a player makes them lose that much life. See rules 608, 713.

> *Example: an attacker with 2 power blocked by a 0/2 kills it, and an unblocked 1-power attacker makes the defending player lose 1 life.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13; Rulebook 2023 p.11 · Tests: 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts · Example test: 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts::cr:concepts.damage.basics — damage equal to defense kills, and unblocked damage to a player is that much life lost · Key: concepts.damage.basics</sub>

<a id="r112.5a"></a>**112.5a** Damage marked on units is removed during the regroup phase. See rule 506.

> *Example: a blocker that took 2 damage in the battle has no damage marked on it after regroup.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.26; Rulebook 2023 p.11 · Tests: 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts · Example test: 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts::cr:concepts.damage.basics.regroup — damage marked on a unit is removed at regroup · Key: concepts.damage.basics.regroup</sub>

<a id="r112.5b"></a>**112.5b** All the damage dealt to a unit is dealt, including any beyond what destroys it, and counts as damage dealt. See rule 608.6d.

> *Example: Arc Lightning deals 6 to a Vulnerable 3/8 with nowhere for its Electric damage to jump: all 12 are dealt to that unit, not just the 8 that destroy it.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1372451771632320512#2 · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Example test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Vulnerable: Electric damage with nowhere to jump is still dealt — all 6 land on the Vulnerable unit as 12 · Key: concepts.damage.basics.all-dealt</sub>

<a id="r112.6"></a>**112.6.** The source of damage is the thing that deals it. When a spell makes a unit deal damage (Squish, Fight, Battle), the unit is the source: its own attributes apply, and the spell's attributes do not. See rule 802.

> *Example: a Powerful ally squishing deals double its defense.*

> *Example: a Powerful Squish does not double.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1402292180499955884#0; RAQ 1402292180499955884#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts, 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts · Example tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Squish: the unit is the source — a Powerful ally deals double its defense, 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Squish: a Powerful Squish does not double — the spell is not the source · Key: concepts.damage.source</sub>

<a id="r112.6a"></a>**112.6a** Damage a unit deals because a spell told it to is that unit's damage, not damage from a spell effect.

> *Example: Squish damage does not trigger Ember of Life ("When one of your spell effects deals damage").*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1402292180499955884#2 · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts · Example test: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Squish: Squish damage is the unit dealing it, so Ember of Life does not trigger · Key: concepts.damage.source.unit-not-spell-effect</sub>

<a id="r112.7"></a>**112.7.** Combat damage is the damage columns deal to each other and to players in the combat damage step. All other damage is noncombat damage, including damage dealt by an ability that combat damage causes, such as Resonant's extra damage. See rule 608.

> *Example: Resonant's extra damage is not combat damage, so Oorblak does not take it in place of the player.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Conduit of Pain · Designer: RAQ 1362838395298119912#0 · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Example test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Resonant: the extra damage is not combat damage — Oorblak does not take it, the player does · Key: concepts.damage.combat-and-noncombat</sub>

<a id="r112.8"></a>**112.8.** All the damage one resolution of one effect deals is dealt at once. A recipient that the effect damages more than once is dealt the total once, and units destroyed by that damage are destroyed together, after all of it is dealt.

> *Example: Channel Through deals damage to a unit twice; Restitution triggers once, for the total.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 69-damage-batch.test.ts · Example test: 69-damage-batch.test.ts::CR 112.8: Channel Through gives a twice-hit unit ONE damage event (the Restitution report) · Demonstrated by test: 69-damage-batch.test.ts::CR 112.8: "each unit" damage kills simultaneously — every unit hears the same total · Key: concepts.damage.one-effect</sub>

<a id="r112.8a"></a>**112.8a** Each copy of an effect is a separate source and deals its damage separately.

> *Example: Meteor Shower's three Rockfalls are three separate dealings of damage.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts · Example test: 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts::cr:concepts.damage.one-effect.copies — the three Meteor Shower rockfalls are three separate dealings of damage · Key: concepts.damage.one-effect.copies</sub>

<a id="r112.9"></a>**112.9.** When a source would deal noncombat damage, its amount is worked out in this order: first, modifiers that add to it (such as Conduit of Pain's "plus 1") apply; then Powerful doubles the result; then a Vulnerable recipient is dealt double what reaches it. See rules 802, 708.

> *Example: a Powerful Bellowing Boulder beside Conduit of Pain deals (1+1)x2 = 4 to each unit.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1362838395298119912#4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts · Example test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Resonant: Conduit adds its 1 BEFORE Powerful doubles — a Powerful Bellowing Boulder deals (1+1)x2 = 4 to each unit · Key: concepts.damage.amount-order</sub>

<a id="r112.10"></a>**112.10.** Damage dealt in the form of -1/-1 counters (by a Poisonous source) is still damage dealt: it triggers abilities that trigger on a unit being dealt damage. See rule 802.

> *Example: Awoken Tomb hit by a Poisonous source makes its X/X.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1354148437355925554#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts · Example test: 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts::CR 802.18b: an un-prevented {Poisonous} hit fires "whenever I am dealt damage" (the RAQ example) · Key: concepts.damage.poisonous</sub>

<a id="r112.11"></a>**112.11.** Damage that is prevented is not dealt. It triggers nothing that triggers on damage being dealt, places no -1/-1 counters, and does not destroy a unit, even from a Deadly source. See rules 708, 608.6g.

> *Example: a Deadly source cannot kill through Phytochemical Protection.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1354148437355925554#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 24-wood-b.test.ts, 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Example test: 24-wood-b.test.ts::Phytochemical Protection: {Deadly} cannot kill through it · Demonstrated by test: 24-wood-b.test.ts::Phytochemical Protection: prevented damage is NOT dealt — no damage event fires · Key: concepts.damage.prevented</sub>

<a id="r112.12"></a>**112.12.** Damage that an effect replaces with something else (for example, damage dealt "as" rot) was still dealt. Abilities that care whether damage was dealt see it, even though the recipient took something else instead. See rules 708, 608.8a.

> *Example: a column whose face damage Blightsea Polyp turns into rot still pays out Vroot's "that much".*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 207-replaced-hit-was-dealt.test.ts · Example test: 207-replaced-hit-was-dealt.test.ts::CR 608.8a: "when my column deals combat damage" pays out through the replacement · Key: concepts.damage.replaced</sub>

<a id="r112.13"></a>**112.13.** Rot is a counter a player has. At the start of each deployment phase, each player is dealt damage equal to their rot, in initiative order. See rule 507.

> *Example: a player with 3 rot is dealt 3 damage as deployment begins.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Our glossary (not a source): Rot · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts, 42-dark-b.test.ts · Example test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::CR 112.13: rot deals damage equal to itself at the start of deployment, in initiative order · Key: concepts.rot</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U04-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r112.13a"></a>**112.13a** Rot never decreases on its own. It deals its damage again every deployment until an effect removes it.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Burn the Blight · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts, 41-dark-a.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::CR 112.13a: rot never decays — it fires again, at full size, every turn · Key: concepts.rot.never-decays</sub>

<a id="r112.13b"></a>**112.13b** The source of rot damage is the damaged player's own rot, which is a source that player controls.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::CR 112.13b: the damage source is the damaged player themselves ("your rot is a source you control") · Key: concepts.rot.source</sub>

<a id="r112.13c"></a>**112.13c** Rot damage is dealt as the deployment phase begins, before abilities that trigger "at the start of deployment". No player can respond to it. See rule 507.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 47-costs-events.test.ts, 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 47-costs-events.test.ts::CR 507.4: 'startOfDeployment' fires AFTER CR 112.13c's rot damage (the documented order), 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::CR 112.13c: rot damage cannot be responded to — deployment opens no priority window · Key: concepts.rot.timing</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U04-5 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r112.13d"></a>**112.13d** Rot damage can be replaced. A replacement that names no target replaces it on the spot. One that names a target ("put that many -1/-1 counters on target unit instead") puts a triggered ability on the stack to choose the target, and the damage is replaced whether or not that ability finds a target. See rule 708.

> *Example: Skittering Blight takes your rot damage as +1/+1 counters.*

> *Example: Beyond, Codex Incarnate asks its controller for a target, and the rot damage never lands.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Skittering Blight · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 42-dark-b.test.ts, 43-dark-c.test.ts, 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts · Example tests: 42-dark-b.test.ts::…and then eats the rot damage as +1/+1 counters (CR 112.13d replacement), 43-dark-c.test.ts::Beyond, Codex Incarnate: CR 112.13d — the rot replacement asks its controller for a target, and the damage never lands · Key: concepts.rot.replacement</sub>

<a id="r112.13e"></a>**112.13e** An effect that says "gain rot" without naming a player gives the rot to the effect's controller.

> *Example: Primordial Coalescence gives its caster 2 rot.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 43-dark-c.test.ts · Example test: 43-dark-c.test.ts::Primordial Coalescence: three Wraiths (= Wights) and 2 rot (CR 112.13) · Key: concepts.rot.who-gains</sub>

<a id="r112.14"></a>**112.14.** Debt is a counter a player has. At the end of each of their resource steps, a player pays 1 mana for each debt they have, and each mana paid removes one debt. See rule 502.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Our glossary (not a source): Debt · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts, 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::CR 502.4: debt is paid automatically when the resource step ends — 1 mana per debt · Key: concepts.debt</sub>

<a id="r112.14a"></a>**112.14a** Paying debt is not a choice and takes no action. It is the last thing in the resource step, so no resource can be expended after it in that step, and the mana spent on debt cannot be used for anything else that turn.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::CR 502.4a: debt-paid mana is genuinely gone — no more resources can be activated, and the card is unplayable · Key: concepts.debt.automatic</sub>

<a id="r112.14b"></a>**112.14b** If a player cannot pay all their debt, they pay what they can. The rest stays and is charged again at their next resource step. There is no other penalty.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts, 38-light-a.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::CR 112.14b: partial payment is fine and the remainder carries to the next turn, 38-light-a.test.ts::Greed Angel: unpayable debt carries over instead of costing life · Key: concepts.debt.partial</sub>

<a id="r112.14c"></a>**112.14c** Gaining debt can be a cost. Debt gained to pay a cost is gained when the cost is paid, and is kept even if the spell or ability is negated. See rule 111.2.

> *Example: Hyper Beam negated by Dematerialize deals no damage, and the debt its caster gained to play it stays.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Deferral Drone · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 47-costs-events.test.ts, 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts, 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts · Example test: 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts::cr:concepts.debt.as-cost — Hyper Beam negated by Dematerialize deals no damage, and the debt gained to play it stays · Demonstrated by test: 47-costs-events.test.ts::CR 112.14c: printed.gainDebt is a REAL cast cost — a negated spell still cost the debt · Key: concepts.debt.as-cost</sub>

<a id="r112.15"></a>**112.15.** Rot and debt are counters on players. An effect that removes counters from players removes them. An effect that changes the number of counters "put on" a player does not change how many are removed.

> *Example: Burn the Blight removes rot and debt from players.*

> *Example: with Proliferating Slime in play, 2 rot put on its controller's opponent arrives as 3, but removing 2 rot from that player removes exactly 2.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Burn the Blight; card: Proliferating Slime · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 41-dark-a.test.ts, 152-hand-entry.test.ts · Example tests: 41-dark-a.test.ts::Burn the Blight: removes counters from units AND the rot/debt on players, 152-hand-entry.test.ts::a counter-amount replacement does NOT scale a REMOVAL (Proliferating Slime says "put on") · Key: concepts.player-counters</sub>

<a id="r113"></a>
### 113. Timestamps

<a id="r113.1"></a>**113.1.** Effects that apply to the same layer apply in timestamp order. Where they conflict, the later effect takes precedence over the earlier one. See rule 709.

> *Example: Monke resolves in battle, so other units lose all attributes. Afterwards a player augments Chitin Shredder, a Virus, onto their unit: that unit has Powerful, because the virus is later than Monke.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1357965714807586897#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ timestamps: a virus applied AFTER Monke still gives its attribute · Key: concepts.timestamps.order</sub>

<a id="r113.2"></a>**113.2.** An effect's timestamp is when it began to apply. A static ability's effect has the timestamp of the card that carries it, a mod's has the time it was applied, and an effect from a resolved spell or ability has the time it resolved. What a card prints is older than any effect.

> *Example: an attribute granted to a unit while Suppression Field is still on the stack is lost when the spell resolves; one granted after it resolves is kept.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355845893219287132#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts · Example test: 415-cr-costs-life-timestamps.test.ts::cr:concepts.timestamps.when — a static dates from its card, a mod from when it was applied, a resolved spell from its resolution, and printed text is older than all · Key: concepts.timestamps.when</sub>

<a id="r113.3"></a>**113.3.** An effect that removes attributes or abilities removes those the object has when the effect applies. An attribute or ability the object gains afterwards is not removed. See rule 712.

> *Example: a Powerful virus attached after Suppression Field resolved makes the suppressed unit Powerful.*

> *Example: a Powerful virus attached after Transmogrifant is in play works.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1355845893219287132#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 402-raq-fix-stripping.test.ts · Example tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Suppression Field: a Powerful virus attached after it resolved makes the suppressed Bubb Powerful, 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Transmogrifant: an attribute a unit gains AFTER it is in play is not affected — a Powerful virus attached later works · Key: concepts.timestamps.removal</sub>

<a id="r113.3a"></a>**113.3a** A continuous effect that removes attributes or abilities removes the printed ones of a unit that enters play after it began, because what a card prints is older than the effect. When that effect ends, the units get them back.

> *Example: a unit entering play under Transmogrifant has no attributes, and gets them back when Transmogrifant leaves.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Transmogrifant: a unit that enters play under it has no attributes, and gets them back when Transmogrifant leaves · Key: concepts.timestamps.removal.entering</sub>

<a id="r113.3b"></a>**113.3b** What a removal effect took stays taken until that effect ends (for a removal that lasts until regroup, at regroup). The unit does not get it back by leaving the column the effect applies to. This does not stop the unit gaining an attribute or ability from a later source (rule 113.3). See rule 113.3.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16, 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 402-raq-fix-stripping.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 402-raq-fix-stripping.test.ts::§3 a temporary attribute granted before a strip is taken, and one granted after is kept · Key: concepts.timestamps.removal.stays-taken</sub>

<a id="r113.4"></a>**113.4.** When two effects set a unit's base stats, the later one applies. See rule 206.

> *Example: an opponent's Aberrant Statweaver ("Your units are base 3/3") makes their Wisp base 3/3. You cast Body Swap on your 1/1 and that Wisp: until regroup your unit is base 3/3 and the Wisp base 1/1, though the Statweaver is still in play.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1357965714807586897#1 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ timestamps: Body Swap with a Statweavered unit trades the 3/3 base for the 1/1 · Key: concepts.timestamps.base-stats</sub>

## 2. Parts of a Card

<a id="r200"></a>
### 200. General

<a id="r200.1"></a>**200.1.** An Algomancy card can show these parts: a name, a mana cost, an affinity requirement, a timing icon, stats (power and defense), a type line of types and attributes, abilities, and a set symbol. Every card has a name; the other parts appear only on the cards that need them. Some cards also print an alternative-cost banner (203) or an augment symbol (208). See rules 201, 202, 203, 204, 205, 206, 207, 208, 209. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.3; Manual p.12; Rulebook 2023 p.3; Rulebook 2023 p.3 · Key: card.general.parts</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U05-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r200.2"></a>**200.2.** The physical printed card is the source of truth for what a card says. Where the transcription a client reads differs from the printed card, the printed card governs and the transcription is corrected; the difference is not a ruling on the card. See rule 101.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25, 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 209-interdiction-rift-type-line.test.ts, 137-multiplier-and-mode.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 209-interdiction-rift-type-line.test.ts::§1 Interdiction Rift is "{Battle} Cosmic Spell" — the owner's ruling, exactly, 137-multiplier-and-mode.test.ts::CR 200.2: Arbiter of Armistice's printed type line has no {Switch}, and nothing else moved · Key: card.general.printed-card-governs</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U05-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r201"></a>
### 201. Name

<a id="r201.1"></a>**201.1.** Every card has a name.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.12; Rulebook 2023 p.3 · Tests: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts::cr:card.name.every-card — every card in the pool has a non-empty name, the one it is filed under · Key: card.name.every-card</sub>

<a id="r201.2"></a>**201.2.** "Other" and "another" compare objects, never names. Two cards with the same name are two different things, and each is "another" to the other. See rule 110.

> *Example: A unit wearing two Rotbeast augments: each Rotbeast's trigger moves the other one.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 121-another-identity.test.ts · Example test: 121-another-identity.test.ts::CR 720.6d Rotbeast: a SECOND Rotbeast augment is "another" — each moves the other · Key: card.name.another</sub>

<a id="r201.3"></a>**201.3.** Where a card speaks of a "unique" token, a token is identified by its name, its X and the stats the effect that created it set, together: a Robot 2 and a Robot 5 are two unique tokens, and so are a 3/3 and a 5/5 unit token. See rule 304.

> *Example: Automaton of Abundance: when its controller creates a Robot 3, a Robot 2 and a Robot 1 together, those are three unique tokens, so three extra Robots are made.*

> *Example: Automaton of Abundance: a 3/3 and a 5/5 unit token created together are two unique tokens, so two extra tokens are made.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Automaton of Abundance · Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16; Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts, 458-automaton-copies-stats.test.ts · Example tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts::CR 201.3: a batch of a Robot 3, a Robot 2 and a Robot 1 yields THREE extras, 458-automaton-copies-stats.test.ts::CR 304.14: a 3/3 and a 5/5 Unit Token made together are TWO unique tokens · Key: card.name.unique-token</sub>

<a id="r201.4"></a>**201.4.** A card with a back face exists as its front face in every zone other than play. A transformed card that leaves play turns back over, and is binned under its front name. A back face is not a token. See rules 108, 710.

> *Example: A transformed Scholar of the Void killed in play goes to the bin as Scholar of the Void.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts · Example test: 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts::CR 201.4: a transformed Scholar killed in play BINS as "Scholar of the Void" · Key: card.name.front-face</sub>

<a id="r201.5"></a>**201.5.** A copy takes the name of the card it copies while it is a copy, but the physical card keeps its own name: when it leaves play it is binned, erased or returned to hand as itself. See rule 710.

> *Example: A Borrower of Forms that copied a Good Whale and dies puts Borrower of Forms in the bin.*

> *Example: Recalled, it returns to the hand as Borrower of Forms.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1372468222158180424#7; RAQ 1372468222158180424#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts, 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts::CR 201.5: a Borrower that became something else still bins as BORROWER OF FORMS (ruling 1), 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Borrower of Forms: recalled, it goes back to the hand as Borrower of Forms · Key: card.name.copy</sub>

<a id="r202"></a>
### 202. Cost Orb and Pips

<a id="r202.1"></a>**202.1.** The cost orb shows the card's mana cost: the number of resources a player must expend to play it. See rules 106, 111.

> *Example: Good Whale (cost orb 6) cannot be played with five resources; played with seven, it expends six and leaves one open.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.12; Manual p.13; Rulebook 2023 p.3 · Tests: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts · Example test: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts::cr:card.cost-orb.mana-cost — Good Whale (mana 6) is refused with five resources and costs exactly six expended resources to play · Key: card.cost-orb.mana-cost</sub>

<a id="r202.2"></a>**202.2.** The pips with the cost are the card's affinity requirement. To play the card, its controller must have at least that many resources of each pip's element among their resources. The requirement is met, not paid: expended resources count toward it. See rule 105.

> *Example: Two wood resources and any number of shards can pay for many [gg] cards in one turn.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.12; Manual p.12 · Designer: RAQ 1358299200953126963#0; RAQ 1358299200953126963#0 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts, 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Mana question: affinity counts resources already spent — two wood pay for many gg cards · Key: card.cost-orb.pips</sub>

<a id="r202.3"></a>**202.3.** The pips are not part of a card's cost. Where a card or rule refers to a card's cost, it means the mana number alone. See rule 111.

> *Example: Resurrect ("cost 2 or less") can return Chitin Shredder, whose cost orb is 2 with two earth pips: its cost is 2, not 4.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Tests: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts · Example test: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts::cr:card.cost-orb.pips-not-cost — Resurrect (cost 2 or less) offers Chitin Shredder, whose cost orb is 2 with two pips, and its cost in play reads 2 · Key: card.cost-orb.pips-not-cost</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U05-15 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r202.4"></a>**202.4.** An effect that reads a card's cost reads its printed cost. Effects that make a card cost more or less to play do not change the cost other effects read. See rule 111.

> *Example: Squish paid at 4 under Stasis Sentry and Tranquility is still a 2-cost spell to Arcane Concentrator and Channeled Amalgam.*

> *Example: Tides of the Cosmos' "total cost 8 or less" is not shrunk by Tranquility.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1353980184042143835#0; RAQ 1396955380000755795#9 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ printed cost: Arcane Concentrator and Channeled Amalgam read a taxed Squish as a 2, 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Tides 8: the total cost of 8 or less reads printed costs — Tranquility does not shrink it · Key: card.cost-orb.printed-cost</sub>

<a id="r202.5"></a>**202.5.** A cost orb may show X. While a card with X in its cost is being cast, X is the amount chosen and paid, and that amount is the card's cost. See rules 107, 111.

> *Example: With Unstable Apparition in play ("create a Fireball X, where X is the spell's cost"), its controller casts Wildfire for X = 0. Wildfire's cost is 0, so no Fireball is made.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 133-x-cost-semantics.test.ts · Example test: 133-x-cost-semantics.test.ts::CR 202.5 — Unstable Apparition at X = 0: the spell really costs 0, so no Fireball · Key: card.cost-orb.x</sub>

<a id="r202.6"></a>**202.6.** A card with X in its cost has a cost of 0 wherever no X has been paid for it: in the deck, the hand, the cache, the bin, or as a unit in play. An X spell played by an effect that plays cards for free is played with X = 0. See rule 107.

> *Example: Tides of the Cosmos counts an X spell as cost 0 against its budget of 8, and plays it at X = 0.*

> *Example: Living Vault caches a card from hand by paying its cost: an X card in hand costs 0, so it can be cached for [0].*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1396955380000755795#6 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts, 39-light-b.test.ts · Example tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Tides 6a: an X spell counts as cost 0 against the budget and is played at X = 0, 39-light-b.test.ts::Living Vault: an X-cost card in hand is offered at pay [0] (CR 107.3a) · Key: card.cost-orb.x-outside-cast</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U05-13 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r202.7"></a>**202.7.** A copy has the cost of the card it copies. See rule 710.

> *Example: A Borrower of Forms that copied a Robot costs 0, so Lumengrove Lurker can recall it.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1372468222158180424#10 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Borrower of Forms: a Borrower that copied a Robot costs 0, so Lumengrove Lurker can recall it · Key: card.cost-orb.copy</sub>

<a id="r203"></a>
### 203. Alternative-Cost Banner

<a id="r203.1"></a>**203.1.** Some cards print a banner that offers another way to play the card, for a cost of its own: Ambush and Prophecy are printed this way. A banner shows its own mana cost and affinity pips, and a Prophecy banner also shows a condition. See rule 803.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Good Whale; card: Shib · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 313-prophecy-affinity.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 313-prophecy-affinity.test.ts::CR 203.1: every printed prophecy banner carries affinity pips · Key: card.banner.what</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U05-9 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r203.2"></a>**203.2.** A banner's cost is paid like any other cost, in place of the card's cost orb: its own mana is spent and its own affinity pips are required. See rules 111, 803.

> *Example: Lurking Slimebeast ambushes for 3 mana with one water pip.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 4 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 4 gate test files · Printed: card: Lurking Slimebeast · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 313-prophecy-affinity.test.ts, 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts, 14-water-a.test.ts, 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts · Example test: 14-water-a.test.ts::Lurking Slimebeast: [Battle] Ambush [3b] = 3 mana at one water pip (CR 803.6a, 107.10a) · Demonstrated by tests: 313-prophecy-affinity.test.ts::CR 803.7d: mana without the affinity does not buy a prophecy, 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::the banner is priced on its own pips, not the card's · Key: card.banner.cost</sub>

<a id="r203.3"></a>**203.3.** A banner's cost is not the card's cost. Anything that reads the card's cost reads its cost orb, even when the card is played through its banner. See rule 202.

> *Example: Lurking Slimebeast played through its Ambush banner (3 mana) still has a cost of 4, its cost orb.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1396955380000755795#2 · Tests: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts · Example test: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts::cr:card.banner.not-the-cards-cost — a unit played through its Ambush banner still costs its cost-orb mana · Key: card.banner.not-the-cards-cost</sub>

<a id="r203.4"></a>**203.4.** Prophesying pays a Prophecy banner's cost and puts the card into the cache with the banner's condition attached. Once the condition has been fulfilled, the card may be played from the cache for free and ignoring affinity, at its printed timing (see 803). See rules 403, 803.

> *Example: A fulfilled prophecy whose card needs earth affinity its controller lacks is released from the cache with nothing paid.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 313-prophecy-affinity.test.ts, 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Example test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 803.7h: a released prophecy is FREE and ignores affinity · Demonstrated by test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 803.7i: normal TIMING still applies — a {Battle} release is refused at deployment · Key: card.banner.prophecy</sub>

<a id="r203.5"></a>**203.5.** A timing icon printed in a banner governs only the play the banner offers, not the card. See rule 207.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.40; Manual p.40 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Key: card.banner.timing</sub>

<a id="r203.5a"></a>**203.5a** A [Battle] icon on an Ambush banner lets the card be played as an Ambush during battle even though the card itself has no Battle timing. See rule 803.

> *Example: Good Whale, a deployment unit, ambushes into the attacking column for [4bb] during battle.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.40; Manual p.40; card: Good Whale · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts · Example test: 08-cards2.test.ts::Good Whale: the parked Ambush mode works ([4bb], into the attacking column) · Key: card.banner.timing.ambush</sub>

<a id="r203.5b"></a>**203.5b** A [Haste] icon at the end of a Prophecy condition lets the card be prophesied during the haste step as well as during deployment. It does not change when the card may be played once the prophecy is fulfilled: that is always its printed timing. See rules 504, 803.

> *Example: Divine Intervention ("Your life is 5 or less [Haste]") may be prophesied in the haste step.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 257-prophecy-release-timing.test.ts · Example test: 257-prophecy-release-timing.test.ts::CR 504.9: a banner marked [Haste] may be prophesied during the haste step · Demonstrated by tests: 257-prophecy-release-timing.test.ts::CR 504.9a: the marker does not move a fulfilled release out of battle and into the haste step, 257-prophecy-release-timing.test.ts::CR 504.9: an UNMARKED banner is still deployment-only — the haste step refuses it · Key: card.banner.timing.prophecy-haste</sub>

<a id="r204"></a>
### 204. Type Line

<a id="r204.1"></a>**204.1.** The type line describes what the card is. It holds the card's attributes, its subtypes and its card type, and on some cards the augment symbol (208). See rule 300. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.12; Rulebook 2023 p.3; card: Good Whale; card: Trashling · Key: card.type-line.what</sub>

<a id="r204.2"></a>**204.2.** The type line of a card that can be played ends with its card type: Unit, Spell, or Spell Unit (a spell that is also a unit). A token's type line says so: Token Unit for a unit token, Spell Token for a spell token. A resource card's type line ends with Resource. See rules 301, 302, 303, 304.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13; card: Jelly; card: Robot; card: Fireball; card: Earth Resource · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-01 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts::cr:card.type-line.card-type — every printed type line ends Unit / Spell / Spell Unit / Token Unit / Spell Token / Resource, matching its kind · Key: card.type-line.card-type</sub>

<a id="r204.2a"></a>**204.2a** A Spell Unit is both a spell and a unit: an effect that asks for a unit or for a spell accepts it. See rule 303.

> *Example: A spell unit played from hand through Hooba-Pon's ability counts as playing a spell.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-01 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Hooba-Pon spell unit: it counts as playing a spell · Key: card.type-line.card-type.spell-unit</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U05-17 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r204.3"></a>**204.3.** The words of the type line other than its markers and its card type are subtypes, such as Whale, Squid or Jellyfish. A marker may stand among them. See rule 300.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Good Whale; card: Trashling · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 209-interdiction-rift-type-line.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 209-interdiction-rift-type-line.test.ts::§3 signature two: no subtype word appears on exactly one card unexplained · Key: card.type-line.subtypes</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U05-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r204.4"></a>**204.4.** An attribute printed on the type line is part of the card's rules. It is an attribute, not an ability. See rules 109, 802.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Whispering Mantid · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 262-type-line-attributes.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 262-type-line-attributes.test.ts::CR D6.10: a card whose only rules content is a type-line attribute stops saying no rules text · Key: card.type-line.attributes</sub>

<a id="r204.5"></a>**204.5.** Attributes are printed in bold yellow (gold) or purple. Yellow attributes are combat attributes, which are shared by the units in the same column of a formation (see 603 and 802). Purple attributes, such as Burst and Unstable, are non-combat attributes and are not shared in formation. See rules 603, 802, 803.

> *Example: Aberrant Statweaver attacking behind Chitin Shredder is Powerful through the column, but Chitin Shredder does not become Unstable: when it dies it is binned, while the Statweaver is erased.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.12; Manual p.12; Manual p.24; Manual p.25; Manual p.25 · Tests: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts · Example test: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts::cr:card.type-line.attribute-colours — a column shares the combat attribute Powerful, but the column-mate of an Unstable unit is not Unstable and is binned, not erased · Key: card.type-line.attribute-colours</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U05-10, D-U05-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r204.6"></a>**204.6.** Attributes apply in the order they are printed, top to bottom. See rule 709.

> *Example: A Lonely Forager (3/1) given Tough and then Balanced is 3/3; given Balanced first and then Tough, it is 3/6.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.42 · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts · Example test: 08-cards2.test.ts::CR 709.4b: layer-4 application order — Tough→Balanced ≠ Balanced→Tough · Key: card.type-line.order</sub>

<a id="r204.7"></a>**204.7.** A timing icon is not an attribute. A card whose only marking is its timing icon has no attributes. See rule 207.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Tidal Menace · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 262-type-line-attributes.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 262-type-line-attributes.test.ts::CR D6.10: a card with no attribute and no text still says nothing, and the guard does not reach it · Key: card.type-line.icons-not-attributes</sub>

<a id="r205"></a>
### 205. Text Box and Bracketed Text

<a id="r205.1"></a>**205.1.** The text box holds the card's abilities, which describe its effects. Most cards have abilities; some have none. See rule 109. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.12; Rulebook 2023 p.3 · Key: card.text-box.abilities</sub>

<a id="r205.2"></a>**205.2.** Reminder text, in italics, restates what an attribute or keyword does. An [Augment] mentioned inside reminder text is not an augment symbol (see 208.4a). See rule 208.

> *Example: Reconfigure mentions [Augment] in its reminder text, but it cannot be applied as an augment.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.24; Manual p.24 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 48-playtest-hotfix.test.ts · Example test: 48-playtest-hotfix.test.ts::a spell that merely mentions [Augment] in reminder text is not an augment · Key: card.text-box.reminder</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U05-11 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r205.3"></a>**205.3.** Text in square brackets in a text box is either an additional cost or a choice between modes. A bracketed cost must be paid, and a bracketed mode chosen, to play the card. See rules 111, 702.

> *Example: Darkblast's [Discard a card] is a cost: with no other card in hand it cannot be cast.*

> *Example: Retribution Thing's "[lost or gained]" is a mode: X is one of the two, never the sum.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.13; Manual p.13 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 45-hybrids-ld-b.test.ts, 38-light-a.test.ts · Example tests: 45-hybrids-ld-b.test.ts::Darkblast: CR 702.4a — with nothing else in hand the cost is unpayable and the CAST is illegal, 38-light-a.test.ts::CR 205.3: the printed "[lost or gained]" is a MODE, so X is one ledger and never the sum · Key: card.text-box.brackets</sub>

<a id="r205.3a"></a>**205.3a** The owner of the effect pays a bracketed cost and chooses a bracketed mode, as the card or ability is put on the stack — never on resolution. See rules 702, 703.

> *Example: Void Memory's caster declares "unit" or "spell" at cast; each opponent then discards one of that type if able.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25, 2026-09-01 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 97-mode-conformance.test.ts, 136-triggers-and-modes.test.ts · Example test: 97-mode-conformance.test.ts::CR 205.3a: Void Memory declares its half at cast, and a hand with no card of that type reveals · Demonstrated by test: 136-triggers-and-modes.test.ts::CR 205.3: the mode is FIXED at cast — a ledger that moves afterwards does not re-pick it · Key: card.text-box.brackets.who-and-when</sub>

<a id="r205.3b"></a>**205.3b** A payment written in prose rather than in brackets, such as "unless its controller pays", is not the owner's: the player it names decides it, when the effect resolves. See rule 111.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-01 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; no gate test · Key: card.text-box.brackets.unbracketed</sub>

<a id="r205.3c"></a>**205.3c** Only bracketed prose is a cost or a mode. Symbols the transcription writes in brackets, such as [Augment], [Switch1], [once] or a cost like [2] or [4bb], are not bracketed text. See rule 111.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-01 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 97-mode-conformance.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 97-mode-conformance.test.ts::CR 205.3c: nothing declares a mode it does not print · Key: card.text-box.brackets.symbols</sub>

<a id="r205.3d"></a>**205.3d** A bracketed additional cost is still paid when an effect lets the card be played for free. See rule 111.

> *Example: A card played by Tides of the Cosmos still pays its bracketed cost, and a unit played by the same Tides is not yet in play to pay it.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1396955380000755795#5 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Tides 5: an additional cost is still paid, and a unit from the same Tides is not in play to pay it · Key: card.text-box.brackets.paid-when-free</sub>

<a id="r205.4"></a>**205.4.** On a graft card the graft symbol divides an ability into a cause, before the symbol, and an effect, after it. When the card is grafted onto another, only the text after its graft symbol is added. See rule 722.

> *Example: Omniwield Evoker reads "[three]: [Switch] Put a +1/+1 counter on me." Grafted onto another unit, it adds only the +1/+1 counter to the host's ability; the [three] before the symbol is not added, so nothing is paid for it.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.33 · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#5 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 6: a grafted Omniwield Evoker adds its counter to the host trigger and charges nothing · Key: card.text-box.graft-symbol</sub>

<a id="r206"></a>
### 206. Power and Defense

<a id="r206.1"></a>**206.1.** A unit's stats are two numbers, printed power/defense. Power is how much damage the unit deals in combat. Defense is how much damage it can take before it dies. See rules 112, 608, 713.

> *Example: An unblocked Rune Channeler (4/3) deals 4 damage; a Good Whale (7/5) survives 4 damage and dies to a fifth.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.12; Rulebook 2023 p.10 · Tests: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts · Example test: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts::cr:card.stats.what — an unblocked 4/3 deals 4 combat damage; a 7/5 survives 4 damage and dies at its fifth · Key: card.stats.what</sub>

<a id="r206.2"></a>**206.2.** Stats mark a card as a unit. Spell units also have stats, and enter play as units with them when they resolve. See rules 301, 303.

> *Example: Lonely Forager, a Spell Unit, resolves into play as a 3/1 unit; Resurrect, a plain spell, goes to the bin.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.3; Rulebook 2023 p.3 · Tests: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts · Example test: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts::cr:card.stats.units — Lonely Forager, a Spell Unit, resolves into play as a 3/1 unit, while a plain spell resolves into the bin · Key: card.stats.units</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U05-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r206.3"></a>**206.3.** A unit's printed stats are the numbers shown on the card. Any difference from the printed stats is a stat change. See rule 709.

> *Example: A unit whose base stats an effect has set differently has a stat change, so it is not a "unit with no stat changes" for Leave None Pure.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.42 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 59-base-stats.test.ts · Example test: 59-base-stats.test.ts::Leave None Pure: a rewritten base counts as a stat change · Key: card.stats.printed-and-changed</sub>

<a id="r206.4"></a>**206.4.** A unit's stats are worked out in six layers, applied in this order:
1. printed stats, as shown on the card;
2. base stats, which effects can set to something other than the printed stats;
3. stat changes, such as temporary bonuses and +1/+1 or -1/-1 counters;
4. attributes, such as Tough;
5. Inverted;
6. Unaware. See rules 709, 802.

> *Example: A 0/4 Tough unit with a +1/+1 counter is a 1/10: the counter (layer 3) applies before Tough doubles defense (layer 4).*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.42; Manual p.42; Manual p.42; Manual p.42; Manual p.42; Manual p.42 · Designer: RAQ 1362832912579559664#0 · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Example test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Tough: a 0/4 Tough unit with a +1/+1 counter is a 1/10 · Key: card.stats.layers</sub>

<a id="r206.5"></a>**206.5.** An effect that makes a unit "base N/N" replaces its base stats; it does not add to them. Counters and other stat changes still apply on top. When two such effects apply, the later one wins. See rules 113, 709.

> *Example: An opponent's Aberrant Statweaver makes their Wisp base 3/3. Body Swap on your 1/1 and that Wisp makes yours base 3/3 and the Wisp base 1/1 until regroup.*

> *Example: Unmake reads base power, and counters do not count toward it.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.42; Manual p.42 · Designer: RAQ 1357965714807586897#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts, 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 28-metal-c.test.ts · Example tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ timestamps: Body Swap with a Statweavered unit trades the 3/3 base for the 1/1, 28-metal-c.test.ts::Unmake: deletes only units with BASE power 2 or less (counters don't count) · Demonstrated by test: 26-metal-a.test.ts::Aberrant Statweaver: "your units are base 3/3" — in play and virus-donated · Key: card.stats.base</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U05-5 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r206.6"></a>**206.6.** A stat change that an effect gives ("gains +1/+1") is temporary: it lasts only as long as the effect says, such as until regroup, or as long as a static ability applies. A +1/+1 or -1/-1 counter is a permanent change. A stat change is a counter only if the effect says it places counters. See rule 506.

> *Example: A Good Whale with a +1/+1 counter hit by Jelly ("gains -2/-2 until regroup") is 6/4 in battle and 8/6 after regroup.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.40; Manual p.40; Manual p.40; Manual p.40 · Tests: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts · Example test: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts::cr:card.stats.changes — a -2/-2 that Jelly gives until regroup ends at regroup while a +1/+1 counter stays · Key: card.stats.changes</sub>

<a id="r206.6a"></a>**206.6a** When a unit has both a +1/+1 counter and a -1/-1 counter, the two cancel and both are removed. See rule 706.

> *Example: A -1/-1 counter put on a unit with +1/+1 counters removes one of them, and leaves no -1/-1 counter.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.40 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ counters: after the cancelling the unit has no -1/-1 counter, so Sporebloom Siren does not delete it · Key: card.stats.changes.cancel</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U05-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r206.6b"></a>**206.6b** Every counter is a counter, whatever its sign: a card that speaks of "a counter" counts +1/+1 and -1/-1 counters alike, unless it prints a sign. See rule 112.

> *Example: Flux Resonator adds one more to -1/-1 counters too.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 120-counter-attribution.test.ts · Example test: 120-counter-attribution.test.ts::Resonator: -1/-1 counters get one more of the SAME — all counters count · Key: card.stats.changes.all-counters</sub>

<a id="r206.7"></a>**206.7.** A unit with negative power deals 0 damage. See rules 112, 608.

> *Example: A -3/1 unit attacking beside a 1/1 in an unblocked column: the column deals 1 damage.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.42; Manual p.42 · Tests: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts · Example test: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts::cr:card.stats.negative-power — a negative-power unit deals 0 combat damage and does not subtract from its column · Key: card.stats.negative-power</sub>

<a id="r207"></a>
### 207. Timing Glyph

<a id="r207.1"></a>**207.1.** A timing icon in the top right corner of a card changes when, and how, the card can be played. The icons printed there are Haste, Battle and Virus (207.3–207.5). See rule 500.

> *Example: Surly Stalker, a Battle unit, cannot be played in deployment but can be in battle; Ignis Sprite, with no icon, can be played in deployment.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.12; Manual p.13; Manual p.34 · Tests: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts · Example test: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts::cr:card.timing.what — every card has one timing (none, Haste or Battle) and Virus is its own mark; a Battle unit is refused in deployment and offered in battle · Key: card.timing.what</sub>

<a id="r207.2"></a>**207.2.** A card with no timing icon can be played only during deployment. See rule 507.

> *Example: A unit with no timing icon cannot be played in battle, except when Tides of the Cosmos lets it ignore timing.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.12 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts, 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Tides 2: a free play ignores timing — a deploy unit and a deploy spell unit, in battle · Key: card.timing.none</sub>

<a id="r207.3"></a>**207.3.** A card with the Haste icon can be played during the haste step as well as during deployment. See rules 504, 507.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.26; Rulebook 2023 p.3 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts, 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 08-cards2.test.ts::Molten Upheaval + the haste step: haste cards play between planning and battle (CR 504.1, 504.2) · Key: card.timing.haste</sub>

<a id="r207.4"></a>**207.4.** A card with the Battle icon can be played only while its player is in battle with another player. It cannot be played during deployment. See rule 505.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.13; Manual p.26; Rulebook 2023 p.3 · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 803.7i: normal TIMING still applies — a {Battle} release is refused at deployment · Key: card.timing.battle</sub>

<a id="r207.4a"></a>**207.4a** Gaining Haste does not let a Battle card be played outside battle. A Battle card that an effect lets be played as if it had Haste can still be played only in battle. See rules 504, 803.

> *Example: Dispatch Courier's grant does not let a {Battle} unit be played in the haste step.*
