<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1465292396664193171#0; RAQ 1464899726796390433#0; RAQ 1465292396664193171#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts, 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 26-metal-a.test.ts::Dispatch Courier: a {Battle} unit stays a battle card even with the grant · Demonstrated by test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Dispatch Courier: a Battle spell unit is not playable in the haste step either · Key: card.timing.battle.gaining-haste</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U05-3, D-U05-4 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r207.5"></a>**207.5.** A card with the Virus icon can also be applied as an augment from hand during battle, as well as being played and augmented normally during deployment (see 723). See rules 721, 723.

> *Example: In battle a Virus can be augmented from hand; a card without the Virus icon cannot, unless Rook allows it.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.13; Rulebook 2023 p.3 · Tests: 04-mods.test.ts, 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts · Example test: 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts::Rook: a NON-virus augment from HAND during battle — refused without it, legal with it · Demonstrated by test: 04-mods.test.ts::virus augment during battle: on the stack, donated to an enemy, text-only transfer · Key: card.timing.virus</sub>

<a id="r207.6"></a>**207.6.** A timing icon other than Virus does not change when a card can be applied as a mod. A Battle card cannot be applied as a mod during battle, and a Haste card cannot be applied in the haste step. See rule 720.

> *Example: Molten Upheaval has Haste, but it can be grafted onto Bellowing Boulder only during deployment: not in the haste step, and not in battle.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.32 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 1: a graft is offered in deployment and never in the haste step or in battle, even for a Haste card · Key: card.timing.mods</sub>

<a id="r207.7"></a>**207.7.** An effect may let a card be played ignoring its timing, as Tides of the Cosmos does ("You may play them now"). A card played that way may be played whatever its timing icon, or lack of one. See rule 701.

> *Example: Tides of the Cosmos plays a deployment unit and a deployment spell unit in battle.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Tides of the Cosmos · Designer: RAQ 1357483405276614856#0; RAQ 1396955380000755795#1 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Tides 2: a free play ignores timing — a deploy unit and a deploy spell unit, in battle · Key: card.timing.ignore</sub>

<a id="r207.7a"></a>**207.7a** An effect that only lets a card be played from somewhere else, such as the bin or the cache, does not waive its timing. Cards that waive timing say so. See rules 403, 405, 803.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 801.9f: glimpse still obeys timing, and a short deck glimpses fewer, 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 803.7i: normal TIMING still applies — a {Battle} release is refused at deployment · Key: card.timing.ignore.only-when-said</sub>

<a id="r207.8"></a>**207.8.** A timing icon printed on one line of a card, rather than on the card, governs only that line. A "Discard me" line with no icon of its own is usable in battle as well as in deployment; one printed with a Battle icon is usable only in battle. See rules 203, 801.

> *Example: Nothyr's battle-marked discard-me line is refused outside battle.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21, 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 58-playtest-round9.test.ts, 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Example test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::CR 207.8: Nothyr's battle-timing discard-me line is refused outside battle · Demonstrated by test: 58-playtest-round9.test.ts::CR 207.8: a "Discard me" line works during battle, whatever the card's own timing says · Key: card.timing.per-line</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U05-16 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r208"></a>
### 208. Augment Box

<a id="r208.1"></a>**208.1.** The augment symbol marks what a card can give to another card when it is applied as an augment. It appears either at the start of a line in the text box, or at the start of the type line, before the card's attributes. See rule 721. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.32; Rulebook 2023 p.15 · Key: card.augment-box.what</sub>

<a id="r208.2"></a>**208.2.** An augment symbol in the text box gives all the text in the paragraph after it to the card the augment is applied to. See rule 721.

> *Example: Vengeance applied as an augment gives its host "Cards your opponents play during battle gain [Sacrifice a unit]", with the host's controller as "you".*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.32; card: Vengeance · Tests: 45-hybrids-ld-b.test.ts · Example test: 45-hybrids-ld-b.test.ts::Vengeance: donated as an augment, the HOST's controller is "you" — their opponents are taxed · Key: card.augment-box.text-box</sub>

<a id="r208.3"></a>**208.3.** An augment symbol on the type line gives the type line's attributes to the card the augment is applied to. An augment gives text, never stats. See rule 721.

> *Example: Bubb's type-line augment donates {Unaware} and no stats.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.32; card: Trashling; Rulebook 2023 p.15 · Tests: 28-metal-c.test.ts, 16-earth-a.test.ts · Example test: 16-earth-a.test.ts::Bubb: 5/6 Unaware; type-line [Augment] donates Unaware (attrs only, no stats) · Demonstrated by test: 28-metal-c.test.ts::Trashling: 2/2 Unaware body; type-line [Augment] donates Unaware (attrs only) · Key: card.augment-box.type-line</sub>

<a id="r208.4"></a>**208.4.** A card that prints the augment symbol can be applied as an augment, from hand, bin or cache (see 721), whether or not its augment text does anything a client can carry out. See rule 721.

> *Example: A Pile of Rubbish can be applied as an augment from hand, from the bin, or from the cache while a glimpse lets it be played.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Tests: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts · Example test: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts::cr:card.augment-box.permission — A Pile of Rubbish, which prints the augment symbol, is applied as an augment from hand, from bin and from cache · Key: card.augment-box.permission</sub>

<a id="r208.4a"></a>**208.4a** An [Augment] mentioned inside reminder text is not an augment symbol, and does not make the card an augment. See rule 205.

> *Example: Reconfigure mentions [Augment] in its reminder text, but it cannot be applied as an augment.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 48-playtest-hotfix.test.ts · Example test: 48-playtest-hotfix.test.ts::a spell that merely mentions [Augment] in reminder text is not an augment · Key: card.augment-box.permission.reminder</sub>

<a id="r208.5"></a>**208.5.** A copy does not have the augment symbol printed on the card it copies. See rule 710.

> *Example: A Borrower of Forms that copied Bubb cannot be the first target of Reconfigure, though a real [Augment] unit in play can be.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1372468222158180424#6 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts · Example test: 416-cr-parts-of-a-card.test.ts::cr:card.augment-box.copy — Reconfigure is castable with a real [Augment] unit present and offers it, but never a Borrower that copied Bubb · Key: card.augment-box.copy</sub>

<a id="r209"></a>
### 209. Complexity Glyph

<a id="r209.1"></a>**209.1.** The set symbol shows which expansion a card belongs to. Its colour shows the card's complexity: gold means complex. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.12; Manual p.12; Rulebook 2023 p.3 · Key: card.complexity.set-symbol</sub>

<a id="r209.2"></a>**209.2.** Complexity is used to choose which cards are in a game. The Quick Start suggests that inexperienced players remove the gold-symbol cards from their decks. See rule 902.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.2; Rulebook 2023 p.2 · Tests: 297-custom-rules-resolve.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 297-custom-rules-resolve.test.ts::BL-43 resolve §3 Simple cards only leaves out exactly the cards that are not simple · Key: card.complexity.use</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U05-14 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

## 3. Card Types

<a id="r300"></a>
### 300. General

<a id="r300.1"></a>**300.1.** Apart from resource cards (106), there are three card types: unit, spell and spell unit. There are two kinds of token: unit tokens and spell tokens. See rules 106, 301, 302, 303, 304.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.3; Manual p.13; Manual p.15; Rulebook 2023 p.4; Manual p.5; Rulebook 2023 p.6 · Tests: 188-deck-stats.test.ts, 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 188-deck-stats.test.ts::§2 the unit / spell / spellUnit buckets sum to the deck, 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.general.kinds — every non-resource card is a unit, spell or spell unit, and every token is a unit token or a spell token · Key: types.general.kinds</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U06-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r300.2"></a>**300.2.** A card's type line names its type. A unit's type line ends "Unit", a spell's ends "Spell", and a spell unit's ends "Spell Unit". A token's type line also contains the word "Token": "Robot Token Unit" is a unit token, and "Spell Token" a spell token. See rule 204.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Bloomcaster; card: Download; card: Hush Mush; card: Robot; card: Fireball · Tests: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.general.type-line — the type line ends Unit, Spell or Spell Unit by type, and a token type line reads Token Unit or Spell Token · Key: types.general.type-line</sub>

<a id="r300.3"></a>**300.3.** Units, unit tokens and spell units have stats: power and defense. Spells and spell tokens have no stats. See rules 206, 301.3, 301.4.

> *Example: A Good Whale is 7/5 and a Robot token with two counters is 2/2. A Crystal ("Put X +1/+1 counters on target unit") can target the Whale, but not the Fireball token beside it: a spell token is not a unit and has no stats.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.3; Rulebook 2023 p.3; Manual p.15 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Example test: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.general.stats — units, unit tokens and spell units carry power and defense; a spell token is no unit and takes no stat change · Key: types.general.stats</sub>

<a id="r300.4"></a>**300.4.** Every unit, spell and spell unit is a card, including a unit that is in play. A token is not a card (see 304). See rule 304.

> *Example: Void Mandible, which watches for a nontoken card being played during battle, sees a {Battle} unit being played.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts · Example test: 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts::Void Mandible: a {Battle} UNIT is a card played · Key: types.general.cards</sub>

<a id="r300.5"></a>**300.5.** When printed text names a type, the noun it uses decides what it reaches.

> *Example: Tranquility ("Spells cost one more") taxes a Crystal token, but Arbiter of Armistice ("Cards played during battle") charges it no life.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Tests: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Example test: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.general.nouns — the printed noun decides: Tranquility (Spells) taxes a spell token, Arbiter of Armistice (Cards) does not · Key: types.general.nouns</sub>

<a id="r300.5a"></a>**300.5a** "Spell" includes spell units and spell tokens. See rules 303.5, 304.

> *Example: Emberflame Enlightener gives "your spells" {Powerful}, and that includes your spell tokens.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1461450216874967235#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25, 2026-09-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts · Example test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::INCLUDES your spell tokens · Key: types.general.nouns.spell</sub>

<a id="r300.5b"></a>**300.5b** "Unit" includes unit tokens and spell units, but not spell tokens. See rules 303.6, 304.9.

> *Example: The World Shepherd watches for a unit token being created; a spell token being created does not trigger it.*

> *Example: Automaton of Abundance copies unit tokens; a spell token in the same batch is not a unit and is not copied.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.15 · Designer: RAQ 1461450216874967235#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts, 26-metal-a.test.ts · Example tests: 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts::The World Shepherd: a SPELL token is not a UNIT token, 26-metal-a.test.ts::a mixed batch gets one extra per KIND, and spell tokens are not units · Key: types.general.nouns.unit</sub>

<a id="r300.5c"></a>**300.5c** "Token" with no other qualifier includes both unit tokens and spell tokens. See rule 304.

> *Example: Mycelial Mentor triggers when its controller creates a Fireball, a spell token.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts · Example test: 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts::Mycelial Mentor: a FIREBALL is a token too · Key: types.general.nouns.token</sub>

<a id="r300.5d"></a>**300.5d** "Card" never includes a token. A spell token being cast is a spell being played, but not a card being played. See rules 304.2, 701.

> *Example: Arbiter of Armistice makes cards played during battle cost 2 life more; casting a spell token costs no life.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24, 2026-09-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 337-spell-tokens-are-played.test.ts, 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts · Example test: 337-spell-tokens-are-played.test.ts::CR 701.1c: Arbiter of Armistice prints Cards · Demonstrated by test: 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts::a spell TOKEN is a played spell but not a card · Key: types.general.nouns.card</sub>

<a id="r300.5e"></a>**300.5e** "Nontoken" excludes every token.

> *Example: Void Mandible says "nontoken card"; a spell token being cast does not trigger it.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts · Example test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Void Mandible: a spell TOKEN does not trigger it · Key: types.general.nouns.nontoken</sub>

<a id="r301"></a>
### 301. Units

<a id="r301.1"></a>**301.1.** A unit is a permanent: once it enters play, it stays in play until something removes it. See rule 404.

> *Example: A Good Whale stays in play through two turns and their regroups until it is destroyed.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.13; Rulebook 2023 p.3 · Tests: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Example test: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.units.permanent — a unit stays in play through battle, regroup and the next turn until something removes it · Key: types.units.permanent</sub>

<a id="r301.2"></a>**301.2.** Units are what players use to build armies, and to attack and defend. See rules 604, 606. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.13 · Key: types.units.role</sub>

<a id="r301.3"></a>**301.3.** A unit's power is how much damage it deals in combat. See rules 206, 608.

> *Example: An unblocked The Foretold (power 3) deals 3 damage to the defending player.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.13 · Tests: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Example test: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.units.power — an unblocked unit deals damage equal to its power · Key: types.units.power</sub>

<a id="r301.4"></a>**301.4.** A unit's defense is how much damage it can sustain in battle before it dies. See rules 206, 112.

> *Example: A Good Whale (defense 5) survives a Fireball 2 with 2 damage on it, then dies to a Fireball 3.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.13 · Tests: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Example test: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.units.defense — damage accumulates on a unit, and it dies once the total reaches its defense · Key: types.units.defense</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U06-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r301.4a"></a>**301.4a** A unit that has been dealt a total amount of damage greater than or equal to its defense during battle dies. See rules 112, 713.

> *Example: A 3/3 dealt exactly 3 dies; dealt 2 it lives.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.13 · Tests: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Example test: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.units.defense.lethal — a 3/3 dealt exactly 3 dies; dealt 2 it lives · Key: types.units.defense.lethal</sub>

<a id="r301.5"></a>**301.5.** When a unit dies or is deleted, it is put into the bin. See rules 405, 304.10, 803.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13 · Tests: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.units.dies-to-bin — a unit that dies, or is deleted, is put into the bin · Key: types.units.dies-to-bin</sub>

<a id="r301.6"></a>**301.6.** A unit does not have to wait before it can attack or block: as long as a unit is in play, it can attack and block. See rules 604, 606, 301.7.

> *Example: A unit that spawned during the attack step may still be declared as a blocker.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.43; Manual p.43 · Tests: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Example test: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.units.no-summoning-sickness — a unit that spawned during the attack step may still be declared as a blocker · Key: types.units.no-summoning-sickness</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U06-4 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r301.7"></a>**301.7.** A unit that enters play during battle is placed outside of formation: it is in the region, but it is not attacking or blocking. It enters a formation only if the effect that put it into play says so. See rules 602, 604, 304.8.

> *Example: A 2/2 that Tidelurker creates mid-attack stays in the enemy region, in no column, and cannot block the counterattack.*

> *Example: A spell unit that Hooba-Pon plays spawns into an open position in Hooba-Pon's formation, because Hooba-Pon says so.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.15; Manual p.15; Manual p.43; Manual p.43 · Tests: 98-spawn-region.test.ts, 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example tests: 98-spawn-region.test.ts::Tidelurker's mid-attack 2/2 stays in the enemy region, 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Hooba-Pon spell unit: the spell part happens, then the unit spawns into the formation · Key: types.units.spawn-in-battle</sub>

<a id="r301.8"></a>**301.8.** A unit whose text says it spawns with counters enters play already carrying them. This is a fact about the unit as it arrives, not an ability: it does not use the stack, and nothing can respond to it. See rule 708.

> *Example: Aethercap Siphoner (printed 4/4, spawns with three -1/-1 counters) is already a 1/1 when an ability that watches allies spawn looks at it.*

> *Example: Nothing goes on the stack for Powerforge Synergist's or Aethercap Siphoner's spawn counters.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 139-spawn-and-play.test.ts · Example tests: 139-spawn-and-play.test.ts::Aethercap Siphoner: a spawn watcher sees the 1/1 the card prints, 139-spawn-and-play.test.ts::a card's own size is not respondable · Key: types.units.spawns-with-counters</sub>

<a id="r301.8a"></a>**301.8a** Those counters are put on the unit as it enters, by the player who spawns it. So an ability that triggers when a player puts counters on a unit triggers, and an effect that changes how many counters would be put on a unit changes them. See rules 708, 112.

> *Example: A Robot 2 created by Living Forge counts as "you put counters on an ally": its controller's Scrapyard Custodian draws a card.*

> *Example: Aethercap Siphoner arriving with its counters also counts as "you put counters on an ally".*

> *Example: With an allied Flux Resonator, Powerforge Synergist enters with three +1/+1 counters instead of two.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 5 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RQ 1154096942083743885; RQ 1465517485750096006; RQ 1352442090717708400; RQ 1354291884759187527; RQ 1378032353959608370 · Tests: 139-spawn-and-play.test.ts, 493-spawn-counters-are-put.test.ts · Example tests: 493-spawn-counters-are-put.test.ts::report #220: a Living Forge Robot is a counter put on an ally — Scrapyard Custodian draws, 139-spawn-and-play.test.ts::Aethercap Siphoner: spawning with counters IS "you put counters on an ally" — the placement a Robot's X is too, 139-spawn-and-play.test.ts::its two +1/+1 counters are scaled by an allied Flux Resonator · Key: types.units.spawns-with-counters.not-put</sub>

<a id="r301.9"></a>**301.9.** A unit that an effect "puts into play" was not played. A unit that an effect lets a player "play" was played, wherever it came from. See rule 701.

> *Example: Bloomcaster creates a 1/1 when its controller plays a unit, but not when a unit is put into play.*

> *Example: The units Wake the Dead plays out of a bin are played: Bloomcaster and Stalwart Sentinel both see them.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Tests: 11-fire-wood.test.ts, 139-spawn-and-play.test.ts, 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Example tests: 11-fire-wood.test.ts::Bloomcaster: PLAYING a unit makes a 1/1, 139-spawn-and-play.test.ts::Wake the Dead: the units it plays out of a bin are PLAYED · Key: types.units.put-vs-play</sub>

<a id="r302"></a>
### 302. Spells

<a id="r302.1"></a>**302.1.** A spell provides a one-time effect. See rule 702.

> *Example: Manufacture creates three Robots once and goes to the bin; it never enters play.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13; Rulebook 2023 p.3 · Tests: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Example test: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.spells.what — a spell (Manufacture) has its effect once and goes to the bin, never into play · Key: types.spells.what</sub>

<a id="r302.2"></a>**302.2.** When a spell resolves, it goes directly to the bin. See rules 405, 704, 303.3, 304.10.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13; Rulebook 2023 p.3; Manual p.13 · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::CR 801.2b: a spell going to the bin after RESOLVING is not trashed · Key: types.spells.to-bin</sub>

<a id="r302.3"></a>**302.3.** A spell token is a spell. See rule 304.11.

> *Example: Emberflame Enlightener's "your spells" includes its controller's spell tokens.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.15 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts · Example test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::INCLUDES your spell tokens · Key: types.spells.spell-tokens</sub>

<a id="r303"></a>
### 303. Spell Units

<a id="r303.1"></a>**303.1.** A spell unit is both a spell and a unit. Like a spell it has a one-time effect; like a unit it has stats. See rule 300.5.

> *Example: A played Jelly is a played spell, gives the target -2/-2, and then its body is a 2/1 unit in play.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.13; Rulebook 2023 p.3; Rulebook 2023 p.3 · Tests: 210-cardsearch.test.ts, 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Example test: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.spell-units.what — a played Jelly is a played spell with a one-time -2/-2, and then a unit with stats · Demonstrated by test: 210-cardsearch.test.ts::a spell unit is a unit AND a spell · Key: types.spell-units.what</sub>

<a id="r303.2"></a>**303.2.** A spell unit that has been played goes on the stack. It is not in play while it is on the stack. See rule 406.

> *Example: A Jelly that has been played sits on the stack beneath Bloomcaster's trigger; negated there, it never enters play.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1353862592661164152#1; RAQ 1353862592661164152#0 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts, 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Bloomcaster: a negated spell unit still leaves the Bloomcaster 1/1 behind · Key: types.spell-units.on-stack</sub>

<a id="r303.3"></a>**303.3.** When a spell unit resolves, its spell effect happens first. Then the unit enters play, instead of the card going to the bin. See rules 704, 404.

> *Example: Spawntender creates its 8/8, and then its own 2/2 body enters play.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.13 · Designer: RAQ 1461450216874967235#0 · Tests: 15-water-b.test.ts, 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Example test: 15-water-b.test.ts::Spawntender: creates an 8/8, then its own 2/2 body spawns · Key: types.spell-units.resolution</sub>

<a id="r303.4"></a>**303.4.** If a spell unit is prevented from resolving (it is negated, or every one of its targets has become invalid), the unit does not enter play and the card goes to the bin. See rules 704, 405.

> *Example: A spell unit played through Hooba-Pon and negated never enters play.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.13; Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1461450216874967235#1 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts, 05-rulings.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Hooba-Pon spell unit: negated, the unit does not enter play · Demonstrated by tests: 05-rulings.test.ts::a fizzled spell unit never spawns, 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Bloomcaster: a negated spell unit still leaves the Bloomcaster 1/1 behind · Key: types.spell-units.prevented</sub>

<a id="r303.5"></a>**303.5.** Playing a spell unit is playing a spell, and while it is on the stack it is a spell: anything that refers to a spell, or to an allied spell, applies to it. See rules 300.5a, 701. *(Engine differs, see F-U06-1.)*

> *Example: A spell unit played through Hooba-Pon counts as playing a spell.*

> *Example: Origon negates a spell unit when it is the first spell a player plays in the battle.*

> *Example: If Molten Riftbreaker despawns while an allied spell unit is on the stack, its "negate all allied spells" negates that spell unit.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: partial in round 4; verifier ran 5 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1461450216874967235#2; RAQ 1461450216874967235#3; RAQ 1461450216874967235#4 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Hooba-Pon spell unit: it counts as playing a spell, 396-raq-timing.test.ts::Origon negates it as the first spell, 396-raq-timing.test.ts::Molten Riftbreaker dying negates it as an allied spell · Key: types.spell-units.is-a-spell</sub>

<a id="r303.6"></a>**303.6.** A spell unit is also a unit card. An effect that lets a player play a unit lets them play a spell unit, and it is played as a spell. See rule 300.5b. *(Engine differs, see F-U06-1.)*

> *Example: Hooba-Pon offers a spell unit from the hand; its spell part happens and its body takes the open position.*

> *Example: Insidious Invitation's "play a unit from hand" lets each player play a spell unit.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Hooba-Pon · Designer: RAQ 1461450216874967235#0 · Tests: 110-literal-water.test.ts · Example tests: 110-literal-water.test.ts::Hooba-Pon: a SPELL UNIT is a unit, 110-literal-water.test.ts::lets each player play a SPELL UNIT · Key: types.spell-units.is-a-unit</sub>

<a id="r303.7"></a>**303.7.** A spell unit played during battle enters play in the region where it resolved, outside of formation, unless its own text or the effect that played it places it in a formation. See rules 301.7, 602.

> *Example: Played through Hooba-Pon, a spell unit spawns into Hooba-Pon's formation.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.43; Manual p.43; Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1461450216874967235#0 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts, 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Hooba-Pon spell unit: the spell part happens, then the unit spawns into the formation · Key: types.spell-units.in-battle</sub>

<a id="r303.8"></a>**303.8.** A spell unit that enters play without being played (for example, one put into play from a bin) does not produce its spell effect. See rules 301.9, 701.

> *Example: Exhume puts a Jelly from the bin into play: its -2/-2 does not happen, and Bloomcaster does not trigger, because the Jelly was not played.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.43; Manual p.43 · Tests: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Example test: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.spell-units.not-played — Exhume puts a Jelly from the bin into play with no spell effect, and Bloomcaster does not hear a play · Key: types.spell-units.not-played</sub>

<a id="r303.9"></a>**303.9.** A spell unit that an effect lets a player play from somewhere other than the hand is still played: its spell effect happens, and the unit enters play only if the spell resolves. See rules 301.9, 701. *(Engine differs, see F-U06-1.)*

> *Example: A Jelly that Wake the Dead plays from a bin has its spell part happen, and its body enters play only if that spell resolves.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (2 probes it wrote), 1 failed; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1461450216874967235#0; RAQ 1461450216874967235#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Key: types.spell-units.played-by-effect</sub>

<a id="r303.10"></a>**303.10.** If a spell unit's own text says that another player gains control of it, it enters play under that player's control. There is no moment when its caster controls it. Its owner does not change. See rules 102, 711.

> *Example: Hush Mush negates an opponent's effect and enters play already under that opponent's control; its caster never controls it.*

> *Example: The caster's Flourishing Flora, which watches allies spawn, does not see Hush Mush arrive.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 23-wood-a.test.ts · Example tests: 23-wood-a.test.ts::CR 303.10 #95: Hush Mush ENTERS under the negated effect's controller, 23-wood-a.test.ts::CR 303.10 #96: the CASTER's Flourishing Flora takes NO counter off Hush Mush · Key: types.spell-units.control</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U06-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r303.11"></a>**303.11.** If a spell unit's own text says it becomes a copy of something, it enters play already as that copy. Becoming the copy is not a triggered ability. See rule 710.

> *Example: Borrower of Forms has the copied unit's name, stats and attributes from the instant it enters play.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts · Example test: 26-metal-a.test.ts::CR 303.11: the body wears the borrowed IDENTITY from the instant it enters play · Demonstrated by test: 26-metal-a.test.ts::CR 303.11: becoming the copy is NOT a trigger · Key: types.spell-units.copy</sub>

<a id="r303.11a"></a>**303.11a** While a spell unit is a copy of a unit, it is not a spell unit. See rule 710.

> *Example: Cosmic Reversal returns spell units in play to their controllers' hands; a Borrower of Forms copying a unit stays in play.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1372468222158180424#11 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Borrower of Forms: while it mimics a unit it is not a spell unit · Key: types.spell-units.copy.not-spell-unit</sub>

<a id="r304"></a>
### 304. Tokens

<a id="r304.1"></a>**304.1.** Tokens are created by effects, directly into play. See rule 404.

> *Example: Manufacture creates three Robot tokens straight into play, through no hand, stack or bin.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.15; Rulebook 2023 p.4 · Tests: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Example test: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.tokens.what — tokens are created by an effect straight into play, through no hand, stack or bin · Key: types.tokens.what</sub>

<a id="r304.2"></a>**304.2.** A token is not a card. See rules 300.4, 300.5d.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24, 2026-09-28, 2026-10-11 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts::a spell TOKEN is a played spell but not a card · Key: types.tokens.not-cards</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U06-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r304.3"></a>**304.3.** A token is either a unit token or a spell token. See rule 300.1.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.15; Manual p.15 · Tests: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.tokens.kinds — a created token is either a unit token (a unit with the token flag) or a spell token · Key: types.tokens.kinds</sub>

<a id="r304.4"></a>**304.4.** A unit that an effect creates is a unit token, whether or not the effect calls it a token.

> *Example: Spawntender creates an 8/8 unit without calling it a token; it is still a token, so Download ("Gain control of target token") can take it.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Spawntender · Designer: RAQ 1353864175910387742#2 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Download: a Fireball in the region and an X/X unit token are both tokens it can take · Key: types.tokens.created-units</sub>

<a id="r304.4a"></a>**304.4a** A copy of a unit that an effect creates is a token, even when the unit copied is not. See rule 710.

> *Example: The copy Echo of Despair creates of itself is a token.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Echo of Despair · Designer: RAQ 1353864175910387742#3 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Download: a copy Echo of Despair makes of itself is a token · Key: types.tokens.created-units.copy</sub>

<a id="r304.5"></a>**304.5.** A copy of a spell made on the stack, such as one made by Earthbound Replicator or Maelstrom Charger, is not a token. See rule 710.

> *Example: Download cannot take a spell copy that Earthbound Replicator made.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353864175910387742#5; RAQ 1353864175910387742#6; RAQ 1355613076506017894#5 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Download: a spell copy made by Earthbound Replicator is not a token · Key: types.tokens.spell-copies</sub>

<a id="r304.6"></a>**304.6.** A nontoken unit that becomes a copy of a token does not become a token. See rule 710.

> *Example: A Borrower of Forms that copies a Robot token is a nontoken unit.*

> *Example: With that Borrower in play beside a real token, Download can take the token but not the Borrower.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1372468222158180424#9 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Example tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::copying a Robot token makes a nontoken unit, 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.tokens.copying-a-token — Download is playable with a Borrower copy of a Robot on board and does not offer the Borrower · Key: types.tokens.copying-a-token</sub>

<a id="r304.7"></a>**304.7.** The back face of a card that transforms is not a token. The transformed card is still a card, and in every zone other than play it is its front face. See rule 710.

> *Example: A transformed Scholar of the Void that dies goes to the bin as Scholar of the Void.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts · Example test: 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts::CR 201.4: a transformed Scholar killed in play BINS as · Key: types.tokens.back-face</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U03-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r304.8"></a>**304.8.** A token enters play in the region where the source that created it is when the effect resolves. See rules 601, 108.

> *Example: Life Plant, attacking in the enemy region, creates its 1/1s there and not at home.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.15; Manual p.15 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 98-spawn-region.test.ts · Example test: 98-spawn-region.test.ts::Life Plant attacking in the enemy region creates its 1/1s THERE · Key: types.tokens.region</sub>

<a id="r304.8a"></a>**304.8a** A unit token created during battle in an enemy region stays in that region, outside of formation. It cannot block a counterattack, and it returns to its controller's home region at regroup. See rules 301.7, 506, 610.

> *Example: Tidelurker's 2/2, created mid-attack, stays in the enemy region and cannot block the counterattack.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.15 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 98-spawn-region.test.ts · Example test: 98-spawn-region.test.ts::Tidelurker's mid-attack 2/2 stays in the enemy region · Demonstrated by test: 98-spawn-region.test.ts::the stranded 1/1s walk home at regroup · Key: types.tokens.region.mid-attack</sub>

<a id="r304.9"></a>**304.9.** A unit token is a unit. It works exactly as a unit card does, except as these rules say otherwise. See rules 301, 304.10.

> *Example: A Robot token with two counters attacks unblocked and deals 2 damage.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.15 · Tests: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Example test: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.tokens.unit-tokens — a unit token attacks and deals its power like a unit card · Key: types.tokens.unit-tokens</sub>

<a id="r304.9a"></a>**304.9a** Unit tokens stay in play through regroup. See rules 506, 304.13.

> *Example: A unit token survives regroup while a spell token beside it is erased.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.15 · Tests: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Example test: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.tokens.unit-tokens.regroup — a unit token survives regroup while a spell token beside it is erased · Key: types.tokens.unit-tokens.regroup</sub>

<a id="r304.10"></a>**304.10.** A token that leaves play goes to the zone it was sent to: a unit token that dies enters the bin, and a recalled token, unit or spell, enters its controller's hand. It really is there, so abilities that watch that zone see it. It is then erased from the game, before anything that triggered on its arrival resolves. See rules 410, 713, 405, 402.

> *Example: A unit token that dies enters the bin, is not trashed, and is then erased.*

> *Example: Rider of the Tides, which watches cards entering a hand during battle, sees a recalled unit token.*

> *Example: A Fireball recalled off the stack enters its controller's hand, Rider of the Tides sees it, and it is erased.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 4 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1355689559609839787#4; RAQ 1355689559609839787#3 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22, 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts, 15-water-b.test.ts, 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::a TOKEN dying enters the bin, is NOT trashed, and is then erased, 15-water-b.test.ts::Rider of the Tides: recalling a TOKEN triggers it too, 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Recall Spell Token: a Fireball token recalled off the stack enters its controller hand · Demonstrated by test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::CR 304.10: the erase lands before anything the visit queued can RESOLVE · Key: types.tokens.leaving-play</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U06-10, D-U06-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r304.10a"></a>**304.10a** A token that enters a bin is not trashed. See rules 801, 405.

> *Example: A unit token dying in battle does not add to the count of cards trashed in that battle.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 338-tokens-are-not-trashed.test.ts · Example test: 338-tokens-are-not-trashed.test.ts::CR 801.2i: a token unit dying in battle does not bump the trashed ledger · Key: types.tokens.leaving-play.not-trashed</sub>

<a id="r304.10b"></a>**304.10b** A unit token that dies still dies: abilities that trigger when a unit dies see it, unless they say "nontoken". See rule 713.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.tokens.leaving-play.still-dies — a dying unit token is seen by "whenever another unit dies" but not by a "nontoken unit dies" watcher · Key: types.tokens.leaving-play.still-dies</sub>

<a id="r304.11"></a>**304.11.** A spell token is a spell that is in play. Its controller may cast it from play; casting it works the same way as casting a spell from the hand. See rules 302.3, 702.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.15; Manual p.15; Rulebook 2023 p.4 · Tests: 03-stack.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 03-stack.test.ts::Fireball goes to the stack in battle, Burst casts them all at once · Key: types.tokens.spell-tokens</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-GL-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r304.11a"></a>**304.11a** A spell token can be cast only in the region it is in. See rule 601.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.15; Rulebook 2023 p.4 · Tests: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.tokens.spell-tokens.region — a spell token left at home cannot be cast in a battle in another region · Key: types.tokens.spell-tokens.region</sub>

<a id="r304.11b"></a>**304.11b** Casting a spell token is playing a spell. It is played from play, so it is played from somewhere other than the hand. See rules 701, 702, 300.5d.

> *Example: Casting a Fireball token triggers Stalwart Sentinel.*

> *Example: Tranquility ("Spells cost [one] more to play during battle") makes a spell token cost [1].*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1355689559609839787#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-28, 2026-10-10 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts, 337-spell-tokens-are-played.test.ts · Example tests: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts::casting a Fireball token triggers Stalwart Sentinel, 337-spell-tokens-are-played.test.ts::CR 702.7a: Tranquility taxes a spell token [1] in battle · Key: types.tokens.spell-tokens.played</sub>

<a id="r304.11c"></a>**304.11c** A spell token is never in a hand. An effect that counts the cards in a hand does not count spell tokens. See rules 402, 304.10.

> *Example: Dreadspawn Horror does not count spell tokens as cards in hand.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355689559609839787#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-10 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts · Example test: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts::Dreadspawn Horror does not count spell tokens as cards in hand · Key: types.tokens.spell-tokens.not-in-hand</sub>

<a id="r304.11d"></a>**304.11d** A spell token that has been cast is still a token while it is on the stack. See rule 406.

> *Example: Download can take a Fireball that has already been cast and is on the stack.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353864175910387742#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Download: a Fireball already cast and on the stack is a token it can take · Key: types.tokens.spell-tokens.on-stack</sub>

<a id="r304.11e"></a>**304.11e** A token has a mana cost, which is often 0. Effects that change the cost of playing spells apply when a spell token is cast. See rules 111, 702.

> *Example: Tranquility makes a spell token cost [1] in battle.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 337-spell-tokens-are-played.test.ts · Example test: 337-spell-tokens-are-played.test.ts::CR 702.7a: Tranquility taxes a spell token [1] in battle · Key: types.tokens.spell-tokens.cost</sub>

<a id="r304.11f"></a>**304.11f** Many tokens have an X value, set by the effect that created them: "Create a Crystal 3" creates a Crystal whose X is 3. A token's X is its size, not a cost. See rule 107.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; no gate test · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.4; Rulebook 2023 p.4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Key: types.tokens.spell-tokens.x</sub>

<a id="r304.11g"></a>**304.11g** A spell token with Burst is cast together with every other spell token of the same name that its controller has in that region. They are still separate spells. See rules 803, 702.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.15; Manual p.15 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 69-damage-batch.test.ts, 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 69-damage-batch.test.ts::CR 803.5a: Burst casts all your tokens OF THAT NAME · Key: types.tokens.spell-tokens.burst</sub>

<a id="r304.11h"></a>**304.11h** A spell token is not a unit and has no stats. An ability that refers to a unit token does not apply to a spell token. See rule 300.5b.

> *Example: The World Shepherd watches for unit tokens being created; a spell token being created does not trigger it.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts · Example test: 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts::The World Shepherd: a SPELL token is not a UNIT token · Key: types.tokens.spell-tokens.not-units</sub>

<a id="r304.12"></a>**304.12.** A spell token cannot move to another region on its own. Its controller may bring it into the enemy region with an attack, but only together with at least one attacking unit, and the move cannot be undone. See rule 604.

> *Example: A Fireball rides into the enemy region with an attacking The Foretold and stays there after the Foretold dies; with no attacking unit it stays home.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.15; Manual p.15; Rulebook 2023 p.4 · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts, 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Example test: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.tokens.spell-tokens.moving — a spell token rides into the enemy region only with an attacking unit, and stays there · Demonstrated by test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::CR 604.2c: spell tokens still travel only with units, and only from the region they stand in · Key: types.tokens.spell-tokens.moving</sub>

<a id="r304.12a"></a>**304.12a** A counterattack may bring spell tokens the same way: spell tokens that stand in the region the counterattacking units leave from may go with them. See rule 610.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::CR 610.3: declareBlocks takes spellTokens · Key: types.tokens.spell-tokens.moving.counterattack</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U06-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r304.12b"></a>**304.12b** A spell token created in an enemy region during combat can be cast there at once. See rule 304.11a.

> *Example: A Fireball created for the attacker in the enemy region during combat is castable there at once.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.15; Manual p.15 · Tests: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Example test: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.tokens.spell-tokens.moving.created-there — a Fireball created for the attacker in the enemy region during combat is castable there at once · Key: types.tokens.spell-tokens.moving.created-there</sub>

<a id="r304.13"></a>**304.13.** During regroup, every spell token still in play is erased, including unused spell tokens in their controller's own region. See rules 506, 304.9a.

> *Example: With Harbinger of Immolation in play, its controller's spell tokens stay through regroup.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.15; Manual p.15; Manual p.15; Rulebook 2023 p.4 · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts · Example test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Harbinger of Immolation: in play as a UNIT, your spell tokens stay through regroup · Demonstrated by test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::regroup default is unchanged: with no Harbinger anywhere, spell tokens are erased · Key: types.tokens.spell-tokens.regroup</sub>

<a id="r304.14"></a>**304.14.** When an effect refers to each unique token (Automaton of Abundance), two tokens are the same unique token only if they have the same name, the same X and the same stats set by the effect that created them. A token created with no stats set has its own printed stats.

> *Example: With Automaton of Abundance in play, Manufacture creates a Robot 3, a Robot 2 and a Robot 1: three unique tokens, so one extra of each is made.*

> *Example: Three Robot 2s are one unique token.*

> *Example: A 3/3 and a 5/5 unit token made together are two unique tokens, so Automaton of Abundance makes a 3/3 and a 5/5 more.*

> *Example: A unit token created with no stats set and one created as a 1/1 are one unique token.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 4 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Automaton of Abundance · Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16; Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 136-triggers-and-modes.test.ts, 458-automaton-copies-stats.test.ts · Example tests: 136-triggers-and-modes.test.ts::CR 708.9: end to end, 136-triggers-and-modes.test.ts::CR 304.14: three IDENTICAL Robot 2s, 458-automaton-copies-stats.test.ts::CR 304.14: a 3/3 and a 5/5 Unit Token made together are TWO unique tokens, 458-automaton-copies-stats.test.ts::CR 304.14: a Unit Token created with no stats and one created as a 1/1 are ONE unique token · Key: types.tokens.unique</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U06-13 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r304.14a"></a>**304.14a** An additional copy of a token (Automaton of Abundance) is created with what the effect that created the original gave it: its name, its X, and any stats that effect set ("a 3/3", "an X/X").

> *Example: With Automaton of Abundance in play, creating a 3/3 unit makes two 3/3s.*

> *Example: With Automaton of Abundance in play, Spawntender ("Create an 8/8 unit.") makes two 8/8s.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Automaton of Abundance · Tests: 458-automaton-copies-stats.test.ts · Example tests: 458-automaton-copies-stats.test.ts::CR 304.14: with Automaton of Abundance, creating a 3/3 Unit Token gives two 3/3s, 458-automaton-copies-stats.test.ts::CR 304.14: Spawntender with Automaton of Abundance makes two 8/8 Unit Tokens · Demonstrated by test: 458-automaton-copies-stats.test.ts::CR 304.14: with Automaton of Abundance, an X/X Unit Token is copied as the same X/X · Key: types.tokens.unique.copy</sub>

<a id="r304.15"></a>**304.15.** Creating a token is not playing it. A unit token that an effect created was not played. See rules 701, 304.11b.

> *Example: Manufacture creates Robot tokens. That is not playing them, so Bloomcaster and Stalwart Sentinel do not trigger.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-10-10 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Example test: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.tokens.creating-not-playing — Manufacture creating Robot tokens is not playing them (Bloomcaster, Stalwart Sentinel silent) · Key: types.tokens.creating-not-playing</sub>

<a id="r305"></a>
### 305. Modifications

<a id="r305.1"></a>**305.1.** A modification (mod) is a card that is applied to another card instead of being played. A modified card is treated as a single card with all of the text its mods add, except that a spell or a spell token that is modified gains only the mod's attributes (721). The two kinds of modification are augment and graft. See rules 720, 721, 722, 723, 724.

> *Example: Curio Drifter augmented onto a Good Whale is not played and gives the Whale Evasive; Biotoxicity is grafted; a Fireball augmented with Bloomcaster does not create 1/1s.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.32; Manual p.32; Rulebook 2023 p.15 · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts, 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Example test: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.mods.what — an augment is applied not played and makes one card; a graft is the other kind; a text-only augment gives a spell token nothing · Demonstrated by test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::CR 721.4a: a text-only augment on a token grants nothing · Key: types.mods.what</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U06-11 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r305.2"></a>**305.2.** Applying a mod is not playing a card, so an ability that triggers on playing a unit or a spell does not trigger on it. See rules 701, 720.

> *Example: A Virus applied from hand during battle is not a card being played, so Void Mandible ("When a nontoken card is played during battle…") does not trigger.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#0 · Tests: 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts · Example test: 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts::CR 701.2a holds: applying a VIRUS fires neither event · Key: types.mods.applied-not-played</sub>

<a id="r305.3"></a>**305.3.** Modifying is done during the deployment phase. A Virus can also be applied from the hand during battle. See rules 507, 723.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.13; Manual p.13 · Tests: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.mods.when — a non-Virus augment cannot be applied from hand during battle, but can in deployment · Key: types.mods.when</sub>

<a id="r305.4"></a>**305.4.** A card's augment and graft text works when the card is played normally, not only when it is applied as a mod. See rules 721, 722.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.35; Manual p.43 · Tests: 248-augment-box-scope.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 248-augment-box-scope.test.ts::§5 PIN: a card played normally still reads its own [Augment] box · Key: types.mods.text-live</sub>

<a id="r305.5"></a>**305.5.** A spell or spell unit with a graft symbol resolves normally when it is played, and can later be applied as a graft from the bin. See rule 722.

> *Example: Spawntender, a spell unit with a graft icon, resolves normally when played: it creates its 8/8 and its own body spawns.*

> *Example: A dead Leaping Lillik in the bin can be applied as a graft.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#3 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 15-water-b.test.ts · Example tests: 15-water-b.test.ts::Spawntender: creates an 8/8, then its own 2/2 body spawns, 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 4: a dead Leaping Lillik is a graft from the bin · Key: types.mods.spells</sub>

<a id="r305.6"></a>**305.6.** During deployment, a spell token in play may be augmented, with any augment and not only a Virus. The spell token gains only the mod's attributes, not its text. See rule 721.

> *Example: A Fireball augmented with a mod granting {Powerful} deals double damage when cast.*

> *Example: Carapace Devourer, an augment that is not a Virus, may augment a spell token during deployment.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 4 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts, 417-cr-card-types.test.ts · Example tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts::CR 721.4a: only ATTRIBUTES transfer, 417-cr-card-types.test.ts::cr:types.mods.spell-token-host — a non-Virus augment (Carapace Devourer) may augment a spell token in deployment · Demonstrated by tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts::CR 721.4a: a spell token is a legal augment host during deployment, 78-round17-core.test.ts::CR 721.4a: a text-only augment on a token grants nothing · Key: types.mods.spell-token-host</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U06-7, D-U06-9 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

## 4. Zones

<a id="r400"></a>
### 400. General

<a id="r400.1"></a>**400.1.** The zones of the game are the deck, the hand, the cache, play, the bin, the stack, the erased pile, the recycle pile and the pack. See rules 401, 402, 403, 404, 405, 406, 407, 408, 409.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.16 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25, 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.general.list — the engine keeps cards in exactly nine zones: deck, hand, cache, play, bin, stack, erased pile, recycle pile and pack · Key: zones.general.list</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U07-11 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r400.2"></a>**400.2.** Play and the stack are the active zones. The hand, the deck, the bin, the cache and the erased pile are inactive zones. See rules 404, 406, 803.

> *Example: A printed Unstable card is erased leaving play or the stack, and only binned leaving the hand, the deck or the cache.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Example test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.general.active — a printed Unstable card is erased leaving play or the stack, and only binned leaving the hand, the deck or the cache · Key: zones.general.active</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U07-9 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r400.2a"></a>**400.2a** Whether a zone is active matters to {Unstable}: an {Unstable} card is erased in place of entering a bin only when it leaves an active zone. A card leaving an inactive zone for a bin is binned normally, {Unstable} or not. See rules 405, 803.

> *Example: Aberrant Statweaver (printed {Unstable}) discarded from a hand goes to the bin and stays there: the hand is inactive.*

> *Example: The same card negated off the stack is erased: the stack is active.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 125-active-zone.test.ts · Example tests: 125-active-zone.test.ts::CR 803.8a: a printed-Unstable card DISCARDED FROM HAND bins and TRASHES — hand is inactive, 125-active-zone.test.ts::CR 803.8k: Aberrant Statweaver negated off the stack is ERASED, not binned · Key: zones.general.active.unstable</sub>

<a id="r400.3"></a>**400.3.** Each player has their own hand, cache, bin and erased pile. See rules 402, 403, 405, 407.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.19 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-29, 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.general.per-player — a card put in one player hand, cache, bin or erased pile leaves the other player four zones untouched · Key: zones.general.per-player</sub>

<a id="r400.4"></a>**400.4.** A card that leaves play for a bin, a hand, a cache or an erased pile goes to that zone of the player who controlled it when it left play, not to its owner's. See rules 102, 711. *(Engine differs, see F-U07-7.)*

> *Example: A unit stolen with a control-changing effect is recalled. It goes to the hand of the player who stole it.*

> *Example: A stolen unit dies. It goes to its controller's bin, and its controller trashes it.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-29, 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 4 tests (2 probes it wrote), 1 failed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 246-zones-follow-control.test.ts, 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts · Example tests: 246-zones-follow-control.test.ts::CR 801.7a: a stolen unit recalled goes to the THIEF hand, not the owner, 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts::CR 801.2e: a stolen unit that dies is trashed by its CONTROLLER, into the controller bin · Key: zones.general.follow-control</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U07-10, D-U07-4 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r400.4a"></a>**400.4a** A card's owner never changes. Changing zones, changing controller and being put into play out of another player's zone all leave the card owned by the same player.

> *Example: Wake the Dead puts a unit from the opponent's bin into play under the caster's control; the opponent still owns it.*

> *Example: A stolen unit that is recalled is still owned by the player it was stolen from.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-08-29, 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 93-engine-defects.test.ts, 246-zones-follow-control.test.ts · Example tests: 93-engine-defects.test.ts::Wake the Dead raising a unit from the ENEMY bin gives the caster control, not ownership, 246-zones-follow-control.test.ts::CR 400.4a: ownership does NOT move — only the destination does · Key: zones.general.follow-control.ownership</sub>

<a id="r400.4b"></a>**400.4b** If the effect that moves a card names where it goes, the card goes there instead.

> *Example: Pull Under: "Delete target unit. If you do, put it and all of its mods into your bin." The deleted unit and its mods go to the bin of Pull Under's caster, whoever controlled the unit.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Pull Under; card: Cosmic Reversal · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25, 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 246-zones-follow-control.test.ts, 15-water-b.test.ts, 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts · Example test: 15-water-b.test.ts::Pull Under: deletes the target; it and its mods land in YOUR bin · Demonstrated by test: 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts::Grob caches a STOLEN unit into the CONTROLLER · Key: zones.general.follow-control.printed-destination</sub>

<a id="r400.4c"></a>**400.4c** In constructed, a card's owner is the player who brought it to the game. See rule 901.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.general.follow-control.constructed-owner — in constructed every card a seat holds comes from the deck that seat brought, and a unit it plays is owned by it even after control changes · Key: zones.general.follow-control.constructed-owner</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U07-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r400.5"></a>**400.5.** An ability that works while its card is in a bin or a cache ("if I am in your bin") works only while the card is in that zone. It never works while the card is in play. See rule 706.

> *Example: Cinder Scuttler ("When you deal combat damage to an opponent, if I am in your bin, recall me.") dies in the same combat damage sub-step in which another attacker hits the opponent. It was not in the bin when the damage was dealt, so it is not recalled.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 310-zone-abilities.test.ts · Example test: 310-zone-abilities.test.ts::§3 Cinder Scuttler does NOT recall off the damage step it died in · Key: zones.general.zone-text</sub>

<a id="r400.5a"></a>**400.5a** Copies of one card in the same bin or cache share one such ability: it triggers once for that zone, not once per copy.

> *Example: Two Cinder Scuttlers in a bin: one combat hit on the opponent recalls one of them, not both.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts · Example test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Cinder Scuttler: one firing per bin, not per copy (CR 400.5a) · Key: zones.general.zone-text.one-firing</sub>

<a id="r400.5b"></a>**400.5b** "Your bin" in such an ability means the bin the card is in: the player whose bin it is controls the ability, whoever once played the card.

> *Example: Rotling ("When I leave your bin, … You may pay [1] to draw a card") leaves the opponent's bin. The opponent, whose bin it left, is the one offered the draw.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; no gate test · Printed: card: Rotling · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Key: zones.general.zone-text.your-bin</sub>

<a id="r401"></a>
### 401. Deck

<a id="r401.1"></a>**401.1.** The deck is the face-down pile that cards are drawn from and that packs are dealt from. See rule 503.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.16; Rulebook 2023 p.2 · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.deck.what — the deck is face down to every seat, a draw takes its top card, and the live-draft packs are dealt out of it · Key: zones.deck.what</sub>

<a id="r401.2"></a>**401.2.** The cards in the deck are hidden: no player may look at them or at their order. A card put on the bottom of the deck is not revealed unless the effect says so. See rule 408.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26, 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; no gate test · Key: zones.deck.hidden</sub>

<a id="r401.3"></a>**401.3.** In live draft, all players draw from one shared deck. See rule 902.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.11; Manual p.16 · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.deck.shared — in live draft both players draw from the one shared deck · Key: zones.deck.shared</sub>

<a id="r401.3a"></a>**401.3a** In constructed, there is no shared deck: each player has their own deck. See rule 901.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.10; Manual p.16 · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.deck.shared.constructed — in constructed there is no shared deck and each seat draws from its own · Key: zones.deck.shared.constructed</sub>

<a id="r401.3b"></a>**401.3b** "The deck" in card text means the deck of the effect's controller: the shared deck in live draft, that player's own deck in constructed.

> *Example: In constructed a Glimpse 1 reveals the top of the deck of the effect controller, not of the opponent.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Example test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.deck.the-deck — in constructed a Glimpse 1 reveals the top of the deck of the effect controller, not of the opponent · Key: zones.deck.the-deck</sub>

<a id="r401.4"></a>**401.4.** A player who must draw from an empty deck when the recycle pile is also empty draws as many cards as there are. Running out of cards does not make a player lose. See rules 408, 104.

> *Example: With deck and recycle pile both empty, a draw of two draws nothing and the game goes on.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 300-recycle-mark.test.ts · Example test: 300-recycle-mark.test.ts::CR 401.4 an empty deck AND an empty pile draws fewer · Key: zones.deck.empty</sub>

<a id="r402"></a>
### 402. Hand

<a id="r402.1"></a>**402.1.** Each player has a hand. Drawn cards go to the hand, and cards in the hand are played from there. See rules 503, 702.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.16; Rulebook 2023 p.15 · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.hand.what — a drawn card goes to the hand, and a card is played out of the hand · Key: zones.hand.what</sub>

<a id="r402.2"></a>**402.2.** A hand is hidden from the other players.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.hand.hidden — the server view shows a hand to its holder and only card backs to the other player · Key: zones.hand.hidden</sub>

<a id="r402.2a"></a>**402.2a** An effect that lets a player "look at" a hand shows it to that player only. An effect that makes a player "reveal" their hand shows it to every player.

> *Example: Thought Extraction aimed at its caster's own hand shows that hand to nobody else.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 4 tests (3 probes it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 173-look-at-a-hand.test.ts, 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Example test: 173-look-at-a-hand.test.ts::CR 402.2a Thought Extraction: aimed at YOUR OWN hand · Key: zones.hand.hidden.look-at</sub>

<a id="r402.3"></a>**402.3.** A spell token is never in a hand. An effect that counts or refers to the cards in a hand does not count a spell token. See rule 304.

> *Example: Dreadspawn Horror does not count spell tokens as cards in hand.*

> *Example: Astral Tidewraith's damage, equal to the number of cards in each player's hand, does not count spell tokens either.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355689559609839787#0; RAQ 1355689559609839787#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-10 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts · Example tests: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts::RAQ Spell Tokens vs Hand: Dreadspawn Horror does not count spell tokens, 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts::RAQ Spell Tokens vs Hand: Astral Tidewraith · Key: zones.hand.spell-tokens</sub>

<a id="r402.4"></a>**402.4.** A card enters a hand whenever an effect puts it there: a draw, a recall, or a move out of a bin, the stack, a cache or another hand. Several cards that enter one hand in a single move enter it together, as one event ("one or more cards enter a hand"). See rule 706.

> *Example: Collect Remains puts a card from a bin into its caster's hand during battle; Rider of the Tides sees a card enter a hand, though it was neither drawn nor recalled.*

> *Example: Two cards that move from a bin to a hand in one move enter it together: an ability watching for cards entering a hand triggers once, not twice.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 152-hand-entry.test.ts · Example tests: 152-hand-entry.test.ts::Rider of the Tides: a BIN recursion (Collect Remains) is a card entering a hand, 152-hand-entry.test.ts::a multi-card move fires exactly ONE handEntered · Key: zones.hand.entering</sub>

<a id="r402.5"></a>**402.5.** Discarding a card moves it from its hand to the bin. Discarding is not playing the card: nothing goes on the stack. See rules 405, 701, 801.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-08-21 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::discarding from hand trashes · Key: zones.hand.discard</sub>

<a id="r402.6"></a>**402.6.** Card text that restricts playing a card "from your hand" restricts only the hand. The card may still be played from any other zone an effect allows.

> *Example: Calming Force ("I can't be played from your hand.") cannot be cast from the hand, but a copy in the cache under a live permission can be played.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Calming Force · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-10-04 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts · Example test: 40-light-c.test.ts::is enforced, and not just un-offered · Key: zones.hand.only-the-hand</sub>

<a id="r403"></a>
### 403. Cache
