<a id="r403.1"></a>**403.1.** The cache is a zone of its own, beside the hand, the bin and the deck. Effects put cards into it ("cache"), out of the hand, the bin, the deck or play. See rules 801, 803.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Our glossary (not a source): Cache · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 403.1: the cache primitives move cards out of hand, bin and deck · Key: zones.cache.what</sub>

<a id="r403.2"></a>**403.2.** The cache is public. Every player can see every cached card, and any prophecy attached to it.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 403.2: the cache is PUBLIC · Key: zones.cache.public</sub>

<a id="r403.3"></a>**403.3.** Being in the cache does not by itself let a player do anything with a card.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Our glossary (not a source): Cache · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 403.3: being in the cache is NOT permission · Key: zones.cache.no-permission</sub>

<a id="r403.3a"></a>**403.3a** A cached card can be used only while a permission on it is live: a prophecy on it that has been fulfilled, or a glimpse that cached it this turn. See rules 801, 803.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts, 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts · Key: zones.cache.no-permission.live</sub>

<a id="r403.3b"></a>**403.3b** While a permission is live, the cached card can be used in every way the same card could be used from the hand: in every play mode, in every window, and as a mod.

> *Example: A glimpsed Virus in the cache is augmented onto an enemy unit during battle.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#3; RAQ 1537748882501668934#4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-04 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 370-cached-virus-in-battle.test.ts, 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts, 369-cache-is-the-hand.test.ts · Example test: 370-cached-virus-in-battle.test.ts::CR 723.2a: a glimpsed Virus in the cache goes onto an ENEMY unit in battle · Demonstrated by test: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts::CR 801.9g: a LIVE glimpse grafts for the card's mana, ignoring affinity · Key: zones.cache.no-permission.like-hand</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U07-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r403.3c"></a>**403.3c** A card used under a fulfilled prophecy costs nothing and ignores affinity. A card used under a glimpse costs its mana but ignores affinity. This holds for every way of using it, mods included.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-04 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 4 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts, 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 803.7h: a released prophecy is FREE and ignores affinity, 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts::CR 801.9g: the glimpse waives the pips, NOT the mana, 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts::CR 801.9g: a LIVE glimpse grafts for the card's mana, ignoring affinity · Key: zones.cache.no-permission.price</sub>

<a id="r403.3d"></a>**403.3d** A cached card keeps its printed timing. A permission says that the card may be used, not when.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-04 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 803.7i: normal TIMING still applies · Key: zones.cache.no-permission.timing</sub>

<a id="r403.4"></a>**403.4.** The cache is not the hand. A cached card cannot be discarded, and card text that names the hand does not reach the cache. See rule 402.6.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-04 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 369-cache-is-the-hand.test.ts · Key: zones.cache.not-the-hand</sub>

<a id="r403.5"></a>**403.5.** When a glimpse permission ends, the card stays in the cache, with no permission.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts, 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 403.5: the glimpse permission expires at end of turn · Key: zones.cache.lapse</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U07-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r403.6"></a>**403.6.** A cached card can be targeted. A player's cache can be targeted only by an effect that resolves in a region where that player is present. See rules 110, 601.

> *Example: In deployment, Prismatic Observer can recall only a card from its own player's cache.*

> *Example: In battle, with both players present, it can reach the opponent's cache.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Prismatic Observer; Manual p.19 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-05 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 293-cached-targets-are-regional.test.ts · Example tests: 293-cached-targets-are-regional.test.ts::CR 403.6 the report, 293-cached-targets-are-regional.test.ts::CR 403.6 the control · Key: zones.cache.targetable</sub>

<a id="r403.7"></a>**403.7.** When a unit in play is cached, only the card goes to the cache. Its mods go to the bin. See rules 410, 720.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::caching a unit sheds its mods to the bin · Key: zones.cache.from-play</sub>

<a id="r403.8"></a>**403.8.** A card in the cache under a live glimpse permission may be prophesied where it stands. It does not move and is not cached a second time, and the glimpse permission is used up. See rule 803.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-01 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 403.8: a GLIMPSED card with a banner may be prophesied where it stands in the cache · Key: zones.cache.prophesy-in-place</sub>

<a id="r404"></a>
### 404. Play

<a id="r404.1"></a>**404.1.** Play is the zone of the units, resources and tokens on the table. A unit stays in play until something removes it. See rules 601, 602.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.13; Manual p.18 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.play.what — a unit in play stays there through whole turns until something removes it · Key: zones.play.what</sub>

<a id="r404.1a"></a>**404.1a** A token is created directly into play, in the region where it was created. See rule 304.

> *Example: Galactic Germination cast by the attacker creates its unit tokens straight into play in the battle region.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.15; Manual p.15; Manual p.15 · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Example test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.play.tokens — Galactic Germination cast by the attacker creates its unit tokens straight into play in the battle region · Key: zones.play.tokens</sub>

<a id="r404.1b"></a>**404.1b** A spell unit enters play as it resolves, in place of going to the bin. See rule 303.

> *Example: Jelly resolves into play as a unit and does not go to the bin.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.3 · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Example test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.play.spell-units — Jelly resolves into play as a unit and does not go to the bin · Key: zones.play.spell-units</sub>

<a id="r405"></a>
### 405. Bin

<a id="r405.1"></a>**405.1.** The bin is a player's discard pile. See rule 400.3.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.44 · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.bin.what — a discarded card goes to the bin of the player who discarded it · Key: zones.bin.what</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U07-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r405.2"></a>**405.2.** A card goes to the bin when: a unit dies or is deleted; a unit is sacrificed; a spell resolves; a card is discarded; or a card that was being played is negated or fails to resolve, unless a rule sends it elsewhere. See rules 704, 801.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.41; Rulebook 2023 p.3; Manual p.34 · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.bin.entering — a unit that dies, is deleted or is sacrificed, and a discarded card, each go to the bin · Key: zones.bin.entering</sub>

<a id="r405.2a"></a>**405.2a** A spell unit that is prevented from resolving (for example because its targets became invalid) does not spawn. It goes to the bin.

> *Example: A negated Jelly, a spell unit played through Hooba-Pon, does not enter play.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.13 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts, 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Hooba-Pon spell unit: negated, the unit does not enter play · Key: zones.bin.entering.spell-unit-fails</sub>

<a id="r405.2b"></a>**405.2b** An ambushing unit whose ambush fails to resolve goes to the bin. See rule 803.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.40 · Key: zones.bin.entering.ambush-fizzle</sub>

<a id="r405.3"></a>**405.3.** A unit that dies goes to the bin of the player who controlled it when it died, unless the effect that kills it names another bin or the unit is {Unstable} (see rule 405.5). If it is a card, the player whose bin it enters trashes it; a token is never trashed. See rules 400.4, 801, 405.5, 405.4.

> *Example: Pull Under deletes an enemy unit and puts it into its caster's bin; the caster trashes it.*

> *Example: A token that Pull Under deletes enters the caster's bin but is not trashed.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Pull Under · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-29, 2026-09-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts, 15-water-b.test.ts, 338-tokens-are-not-trashed.test.ts · Example tests: 15-water-b.test.ts::Pull Under: an ENEMY unmodded victim is trashed by the CASTER, exactly once, 15-water-b.test.ts::Pull Under: a TOKEN victim enters the CASTER bin untrashed · Demonstrated by test: 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts::CR 405.3 whole pool: every unit-shaped card dies into the bin of whoever controls it · Key: zones.bin.controller</sub>

<a id="r405.4"></a>**405.4.** A card that enters a bin from any zone except the stack is trashed. A card that comes from the stack is not, and a token is never trashed. A nontoken mod erased together with its {Unstable} host is not trashed either. See 801. See rule 801.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-08-29, 2026-09-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 8 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts, 338-tokens-are-not-trashed.test.ts, 224-mod-trash.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::CR 801.2b: a spell going to the bin after RESOLVING is not trashed, 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::a TOKEN dying enters the bin, is NOT trashed, and is then erased, 224-mod-trash.test.ts::CR 720.8a: a nontoken mod erased with its Unstable host is not trashed at all · Key: zones.bin.trash</sub>

<a id="r405.4a"></a>**405.4a** A spell played for free while another effect resolves (for example by Tides of the Cosmos) and then put into the bin counts as coming from the stack, so it is not trashed.

> *Example: Tides of the Cosmos plays an ordinary spell for free; it goes to the bin and is not trashed.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 15-water-b.test.ts · Example test: 15-water-b.test.ts::CR 405.4a: Tides plays an ORDINARY spell for free → the bin, and it is NOT a trash · Key: zones.bin.trash.inline-play</sub>

<a id="r405.5"></a>**405.5.** An {Unstable} card that would enter a bin from an active zone is erased instead: it goes to the erased pile, not the bin. See 803. See rules 803, 713, 400.2a. *(Engine differs, see F-U07-6.)*

> *Example: A unit carrying a mod is {Unstable}. When it dies, it ends on the erased pile and is not left in the bin.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 4 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Abyssal Evocation · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 125-active-zone.test.ts, 224-mod-trash.test.ts, 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Example test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.bin.unstable — a modded unit that dies ends on the erased pile, not in the bin · Key: zones.bin.unstable</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U07-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r405.6"></a>**405.6.** Copies of one card in a bin cannot be told apart. A card in a bin is identified only by its name and by which copy of that name it is.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.bin.identity — a bin holds bare card names, and two copies of one card are offered as the same name told apart only by which copy · Key: zones.bin.identity</sub>

<a id="r405.6a"></a>**405.6a** "Another" said by a card in a bin excludes that one copy, not every card with its name. See rule 110.

> *Example: Blightwalker is trashed while another Blightwalker is already in the bin; the older copy is "another" and can be chosen.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 121-another-identity.test.ts · Example test: 121-another-identity.test.ts::CR 405.6a Blightwalker: a Blightwalker ALREADY in the bin is · Key: zones.bin.identity.another</sub>

<a id="r405.6b"></a>**405.6b** An effect that refers back to a card that just entered a bin ("that card", "it") means that copy. If that copy has left the bin, the effect finds nothing. It never takes a different copy of the same name.

> *Example: An {Unstable} unit dies and is erased instead of staying in the bin. Biomass Devourer's "erase it" then finds nothing, and does not erase an older copy of the same card already in that bin.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts · Example test: 26-metal-a.test.ts::CR 405.6: Biomass Devourer does NOT erase an innocent older copy when the dead one was swept · Key: zones.bin.identity.that-card</sub>

<a id="r405.7"></a>**405.7.** A card leaves a bin whenever an effect takes it out, for any reason: recalled, played, cached, erased, recycled, prophesied, or applied as a mod. A "when I leave your bin" ability triggers on every such departure.

> *Example: Writhing Host leaves the bin when it is erased to pay for a haste play.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Rotling · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 42-dark-b.test.ts · Example test: 42-dark-b.test.ts::Writhing Host (CR 504.7, 405.7): the grantor leaves through the CR 405.7 choke point · Key: zones.bin.leaving</sub>

<a id="r405.8"></a>**405.8.** An augment or graft may be applied from the bin as well as from the hand, during deployment, if its cost is paid and its affinity met. See rules 720, 721, 722.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.15; Manual p.34 · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#2 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 3 · Key: zones.bin.mods-from-bin</sub>

<a id="r405.8a"></a>**405.8a** A {Virus} card in a bin can be applied only as an ordinary mod during deployment. It cannot be used as a mod during battle. See rule 723.

> *Example: Bumblecrab, a {Virus}, sits in a player's bin. In deployment it can augment out of the bin; in battle it is offered only from the hand.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.34; Manual p.34 · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Example test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.bin.mods-from-bin.virus — a Virus card in the bin is offered as an augment in deployment, never in battle · Key: zones.bin.mods-from-bin.virus</sub>

<a id="r405.9"></a>**405.9.** A card can be played from a bin only when an effect or the card's own text allows it. The card keeps its printed timing unless the permission says it may be played "now". See rule 702.

> *Example: Abyssal Evocation lets its caster play spells from the bin in this battle; only {Battle} spells there can be played.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Abyssal Evocation; card: Trench Stalker · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts · Example test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Abyssal Evocation: ⚠ OPEN — a bin-played card obeys its PRINTED timing · Key: zones.bin.play-from-bin</sub>

<a id="r405.9a"></a>**405.9a** A card played from a bin is {Unstable} only if the permission says so. A card played from a bin under its own text does not become {Unstable}. See rule 803.

> *Example: A spell played from the bin under Abyssal Evocation gains {Unstable}, so it is erased rather than going back to the bin.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Abyssal Evocation · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts · Example test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Abyssal Evocation: a bin-played spell is {Unstable} · Key: zones.bin.play-from-bin.unstable</sub>

<a id="r406"></a>
### 406. The Stack

<a id="r406.1"></a>**406.1.** The stack is the zone where cards being played, and abilities, wait to resolve. The last thing put on the stack resolves first. See 703. See rules 703, 704.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.14; Manual p.34 · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.stack.what — two spells wait on the stack and the one put there last resolves first · Key: zones.stack.what</sub>

<a id="r406.2"></a>**406.2.** A spell unit on the stack is not yet in play. It enters play only when it resolves. See rule 303.

> *Example: Mycelial Mentor, played with Bloomcaster out, is still on the stack while Bloomcaster's 1/1 is made, so the Mentor never sees the 1/1.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353862592661164152#0 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Bloomcaster: its 1/1 resolves before the Mycelial Mentor it was played with arrives · Key: zones.stack.not-in-play</sub>

<a id="r406.3"></a>**406.3.** A spell token that has been cast is on the stack, and is still a token there. See rule 304.

> *Example: Download can take a Fireball token already cast and on the stack.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353864175910387742#1 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Download: a Fireball already cast and on the stack is a token it can take · Key: zones.stack.tokens</sub>

<a id="r406.4"></a>**406.4.** When a card on the stack resolves, is negated or fails to resolve, it goes to the bin unless it enters play or something sends it elsewhere: an {Unstable} card is erased (see rule 405.5), a card whose own text erases it goes to the erased pile (see rule 406.4a), and a recall puts it into a hand. A card that goes to the bin this way is not trashed, because it comes from the stack. See rules 704, 405.4, 405.5, 406.4a.

> *Example: A non-{Unstable} virus negated off the stack goes to the bin.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.3; Manual p.34; card: Cosmic Reversal · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 125-active-zone.test.ts, 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts · Example test: 125-active-zone.test.ts::CR 406.4 negative control: a NON-Unstable virus negated off the stack still BINS · Demonstrated by test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::CR 801.2b: a NEGATED spell is not trashed either · Key: zones.stack.leaving</sub>

<a id="r406.4a"></a>**406.4a** A spell whose text says "Erase me" goes to the erased pile when it resolves, instead of the bin. See rule 407.

> *Example: Tides of the Cosmos plays Suspend for free; Suspend goes to the erased pile, never the bin.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Suspend; card: Collect Remains · Tests: 15-water-b.test.ts, 89-self-erase.test.ts · Example test: 15-water-b.test.ts::CR 406.4a: Tides plays "Erase me." (Suspend) for free → the ERASED pile, never a bin · Key: zones.stack.leaving.self-erase</sub>

<a id="r406.4b"></a>**406.4b** A self-erasing spell that is negated or fails to resolve goes to the bin. Its "Erase me" never happened.

<sub>Basis: Engine only · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 89-self-erase.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 89-self-erase.test.ts::a NEGATED self-erase spell is binned, not erased, 89-self-erase.test.ts::a FIZZLED self-erase spell is binned too · Key: zones.stack.leaving.self-erase-negated</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U07-13 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r407"></a>
### 407. Erased Pile

<a id="r407.1"></a>**407.1.** Erasing a card takes it out of the game. An erased card goes to the erased pile. See rule 801.

> *Example: Celestial Purge takes a unit out of the game onto the erased pile: no bin and no death.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.15 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Example test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.erased.what — Celestial Purge takes a unit out of the game onto the erased pile: no bin and no death · Key: zones.erased.what</sub>

<a id="r407.1a"></a>**407.1a** The erased pile is public.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.erased.public — the server view shows each erased pile in full to both seats · Key: zones.erased.public</sub>

<a id="r407.1b"></a>**407.1b** Nothing takes a card back out of the erased pile.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21, 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.erased.final — a card on the erased pile adds nothing to the legal actions, where the same card in the bin does · Key: zones.erased.final</sub>

<a id="r407.1c"></a>**407.1c** Erasing is not dying and not trashing: an erased card never enters a bin. See rule 410.2.

> *Example: A unit erased by Banishment does not die and is not trashed.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 145-erase-routes.test.ts · Example test: 145-erase-routes.test.ts::(vii): Banishment still fires no 'died' and no 'trashed' · Key: zones.erased.not-death</sub>

<a id="r407.2"></a>**407.2.** A card that an effect erases goes to the erased pile, including a mod erased off a host that stays in play (for example to pay a cost). See rule 720.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 178-played-item-and-erased-mods.test.ts · Key: zones.erased.says-erase</sub>

<a id="r407.2a"></a>**407.2a** A mod taken off its host and put into play as a card of its own (Reclaim the Fallen) does not leave the game and does not go to the erased pile.

> *Example: A Pile of Runes is augmented onto a unit. Reclaim the Fallen targets that unit: A Pile of Runes comes off it and stands in play as a unit of its own. It never goes to the erased pile.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 178-played-item-and-erased-mods.test.ts · Example test: 178-played-item-and-erased-mods.test.ts::CR 720.9 Reclaim the Fallen: leavesGame:false · Key: zones.erased.says-erase.into-play</sub>

<a id="r407.3"></a>**407.3.** A token that ceases to exist after entering a zone is recorded on the erased pile. See rule 410.5.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts, 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::a TOKEN dying enters the bin, is NOT trashed, and is then erased · Key: zones.erased.tokens</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U07-5 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r407.3a"></a>**407.3a** A token mod is recorded on the erased pile once when its host leaves play, however the host leaves.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 129-disposal-tail.test.ts, 141-despawn-mods.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 129-disposal-tail.test.ts::CR 407.3a: a TOKEN mod reaches the erased pile however its host leaves play · Key: zones.erased.tokens.mods</sub>

<a id="r407.4"></a>**407.4.** A transformed card is recorded on the erased pile as its front face. See rule 410.3.

> *Example: A transformed Scholar of the Void erased by Banishment is recorded as Scholar of the Void.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 145-erase-routes.test.ts · Example test: 145-erase-routes.test.ts::CR 407.4 (iii) · Key: zones.erased.front-face</sub>

<a id="r408"></a>
### 408. Recycling

<a id="r408.1"></a>**408.1.** To recycle a card is to put it on the bottom of the deck. A recycled card has not left the game. See rule 801.

> *Example: A card recycled for a resource is drawn again once the rest of the deck is gone, so it never left the game.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.18; Rulebook 2023 p.7 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Example test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.recycle.what — a card recycled for a resource is drawn again once the rest of the deck is gone, so it never left the game · Key: zones.recycle.what</sub>

<a id="r408.2"></a>**408.2.** A deck has a mark where it originally ended. The recycle pile lies under the deck, past the mark, and is still part of the deck. A card put on the bottom of the deck goes past the mark, into the recycle pile, not onto the bottom of the cards still to be drawn.

<sub>Basis: Owner call · adopted 2026-10-21; Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 300-recycle-mark.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 300-recycle-mark.test.ts::CR 408.2 a recycled card stays behind the mark · Key: zones.recycle.mark</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U07-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r408.2a"></a>**408.2a** Every card put on the bottom of the deck goes past the mark, whatever put it there: recycling for a resource, the constructed put-back, the cards a glimpse did not cache, and recycled packs alike. Likewise, anything that uses the deck can reach the mark: drawing, milling, caching or revealing the top cards, a glimpse, and dealing a pack alike.

<sub>Basis: Owner call · adopted 2026-10-21; Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 6 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 300-recycle-mark.test.ts, 526-card-code-never-reads-the-deck.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 300-recycle-mark.test.ts::CR 408.2a every reader of the deck reshuffles at the mark · Key: zones.recycle.mark.scope</sub>

<a id="r408.2b"></a>**408.2b** When anything that uses the deck reaches the mark, whatever the reason, the recycle pile is shuffled and put above the mark, under the cards still left in the deck; the mark goes back to the very bottom, with an empty recycle pile behind it. An effect that reveals more cards than are above the mark reshuffles when it reaches the mark and keeps revealing until it has its full number. See rule 401.4.

<sub>Basis: Owner call · adopted 2026-10-21; Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 4 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 300-recycle-mark.test.ts, 514-deck-reads-reach-the-mark.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 300-recycle-mark.test.ts::CR 408.2b when the deck runs out the pile is shuffled in, 300-recycle-mark.test.ts::CR 408.2b a glimpse WIDER than the deck · Key: zones.recycle.mark.reshuffle</sub>

<a id="r408.2c"></a>**408.2c** Every player can see how many cards are in the recycle pile. No player may look at them.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 300-recycle-mark.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 300-recycle-mark.test.ts::CR 408.2c nothing in the pile is a card anybody can name · Key: zones.recycle.mark.public-count</sub>

<a id="r408.2d"></a>**408.2d** The order in which cards were recycled does not matter to the game.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.recycle.mark.order — the recycle pile is hidden from both seats and is shuffled before it is drawn again · Key: zones.recycle.mark.order</sub>

<a id="r408.2e"></a>**408.2e** Each deck has its own recycle pile. In live draft, all players share one pile; in constructed, each player has their own. See rule 401.3.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25, 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 300-recycle-mark.test.ts, 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 300-recycle-mark.test.ts::CR 408.2e constructed gives each seat its own pile · Key: zones.recycle.mark.whose</sub>

<a id="r408.3"></a>**408.3.** A card recycled out of a hand is not revealed unless the effect says so.

> *Example: Bripp recycles a card from a hand without naming it to the table.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 173-look-at-a-hand.test.ts, 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Example test: 173-look-at-a-hand.test.ts::CR D6.5b Bripp: "Look at target player's hand" — and the card it recycles is not named to the table either · Key: zones.recycle.hidden</sub>

<a id="r408.4"></a>**408.4.** During the resource step, a player may recycle a card from their hand to create a resource. See 502. See rules 502, 106.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.18 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 308-recycle-for-prismite.test.ts · Key: zones.recycle.for-resource</sub>

<a id="r409"></a>
### 409. The Pack

<a id="r409.1"></a>**409.1.** In live draft, each player has a pack: a face-down pile of 10 cards dealt from the deck at the start of the game, which that player drafts from. See rules 503, 902.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.16; Rulebook 2023 p.6 · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.pack.what — a live draft deals each seat a 10-card pack from the deck at the start, and the pack is what that seat drafts from · Key: zones.pack.what</sub>

<a id="r409.1a"></a>**409.1a** Constructed has no packs. See rule 901.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.16 · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.pack.what.constructed — a constructed game has no packs and no draft step · Key: zones.pack.what.constructed</sub>

<a id="r409.2"></a>**409.2.** A pack may be looked at and used only during the draft step, and no player may look at another player's pack.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.16; Manual p.16 · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.pack.private — a seat sees its own pack only while its draft step is open, and never the other pack · Key: zones.pack.private</sub>

<a id="r409.3"></a>**409.3.** In the draft step, a player combines the non-token, non-resource cards in their hand with their pack, keeps any of them, and passes the pack on with exactly 10 cards in it. See 503. See rule 503.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.6; Manual p.17 · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.pack.drafting — the draft commit merges hand and pack, keeps any cards, and passes on a pack of exactly 10 · Key: zones.pack.drafting</sub>

<a id="r409.4"></a>**409.4.** After each cycle of N+1 turns, where N is the number of players, every pack is recycled and each player is dealt a new pack of 10 cards.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.16; Manual p.16; Rulebook 2023 p.6 · Key: zones.pack.refresh</sub>

<a id="r409.4a"></a>**409.4a** In team draft, packs are never refreshed. See rule 904. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.6 · Key: zones.pack.refresh.team-draft</sub>

<a id="r409.5"></a>**409.5.** When a player is eliminated, their pack is recycled. See rule 104. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.16; Rulebook 2023 p.6 · Key: zones.pack.eliminated</sub>

<a id="r410"></a>
### 410. Zone Changes

<a id="r410.1"></a>**410.1.** A card that leaves play and comes back is a new object. It does not remember its earlier time in play.

> *Example: Engorged Caudex is recalled and played again; its once-per-turn grafted draw works again the same turn.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#16; RAQ 1355115946032889914#16 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 calebgannon: a recalled and replayed Engorged Caudex is a new object · Key: zones.changes.new-object</sub>

<a id="r410.1a"></a>**410.1a** An effect aimed at a card that has since changed zones does not affect it. An effect aimed at a card that is still in the same zone affects it only if the card is still a legal target for the slot it was chosen for; otherwise that target is lost as well. If every target is lost, the effect fails to resolve. See rules 704, 110.

> *Example: An opponent's Luminous Arc is aimed at one of your units; you answer with Organic Exchange on two of your own units. They are still in play, so the Luminous Arc still resolves.*

> *Example: An opponent ambushes with Orblish Horroth to recall target ally; you take control of that unit in response. It is no longer their ally, so nothing is recalled.*

> *Example: Minor Kraken's target grows past 5 defense before it resolves, and is not recalled.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.40 · Designer: RAQ 1454169054402314362#2; RAQ 1355466429788328066#1; RAQ 1355466429788328066#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts, 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Example tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Another set: Organic Exchange may target two of your own units, 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ valid targets: an Ambush whose ally changed sides before it resolves recalls nothing, 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ valid targets: a target that grows past 5 defense before Minor Kraken resolves is not recalled · Key: zones.changes.new-object.targets</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U07-15 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r410.1b"></a>**410.1b** Moving a mod from one unit to another is not a zone change: the mod never leaves play, and nothing despawns. See rule 720.

> *Example: Reconfigure moves Bubb and its Growing Plague onto a Robot; Growing Plague's "when I despawn" does not trigger.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353847640214999170#0; RAQ 1353847640214999170#0 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Reconfigure vs Despawn: moving Bubb and its Growing Plague onto a Robot fires no despawn · Key: zones.changes.new-object.reconfigure</sub>

<a id="r410.2"></a>**410.2.** A unit despawns whenever it leaves play, by any route: dying, being recalled, being cached, being exchanged or being erased. A "when I despawn" ability triggers whichever way the unit leaves. See rule 706.

> *Example: A Pile of Runes ("[Augment] When I despawn, create a Crystal X") is augmented onto Rune Channeler. Rune Channeler is recalled to its owner's hand: that despawn ability triggers, and a Crystal is created.*

> *Example: Demon of the Depths ("Whenever one of your units despawns…") triggers when one of your units is erased.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 141-despawn-mods.test.ts, 145-erase-routes.test.ts · Example tests: 141-despawn-mods.test.ts::CR 721.1f (i): a donated, 145-erase-routes.test.ts::CR 410.2 (i): an ERASE fires 'despawned' · Key: zones.changes.despawn</sub>

<a id="r410.2a"></a>**410.2a** A unit exchanged out of play (Hooba-Mon, Necromorph) despawns and goes to the bin, where it is trashed, but it does not die.

> *Example: Necromorph's exchange triggers no death ability, but the unit despawns and is trashed.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts, 129-disposal-tail.test.ts · Example test: 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts::exchange fires NO death trigger · Key: zones.changes.despawn.exchange</sub>

<a id="r410.3"></a>**410.3.** A transformed card exists as its front face in every zone except play. It turns back over as it leaves play, before anything sees it leave.

> *Example: A transformed Scholar of the Void that dies goes to the bin as Scholar of the Void.*

> *Example: It can then be returned from the bin as a Scholar.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts, 145-erase-routes.test.ts · Example tests: 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts::a transformed Scholar killed in play BINS as, 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts::a transformed Scholar that died is RECURRABLE from the bin · Key: zones.changes.face</sub>

<a id="r410.3a"></a>**410.3a** A unit that is copying another card (Borrower of Forms) leaves play as itself. If it dies it goes to the bin as Borrower of Forms; if it is recalled it goes to the hand as Borrower of Forms. See rule 710.

> *Example: A Borrower that became something else still goes to the bin as Borrower of Forms.*

> *Example: Recalled, it goes back to the hand as Borrower of Forms.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1372468222158180424#2; RAQ 1372468222158180424#7 · Tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts, 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts::a Borrower that became something else still bins as BORROWER OF FORMS, 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Borrower of Forms: recalled, it goes back to the hand as Borrower of Forms · Key: zones.changes.face.copies</sub>

<a id="r410.4"></a>**410.4.** When a modded unit is recalled or cached, its mods go to the bin and the unit goes on alone. A token mod ceases to exist instead (see rule 410.4c). See rules 720, 403.7, 410.4d, 410.4c.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.35; Manual p.35; Rulebook 2023 p.15 · Designer: RAQ 1372468222158180424#8 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts, 141-despawn-mods.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::CR 801.2f: recalling a modded unit trashes its MODS · Key: zones.changes.mods</sub>

<a id="r410.4a"></a>**410.4a** A mod that goes to a bin when its host leaves play goes to the bin of the host's controller. See rule 400.4.

> *Example: A virus on an opponent's unit goes to that opponent's bin when the unit leaves play.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-29 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts, 129-disposal-tail.test.ts · Example test: 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts::CR 410.4a: a MOD goes to the HOST CONTROLLER bin, superseding the destination half of the earlier owner's-bin reading · Key: zones.changes.mods.whose-bin</sub>

<a id="r410.4b"></a>**410.4b** A modded card is {Unstable}. When it dies or is erased, it and all of its mods are erased. See rules 803, 405.5.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.35; Rulebook 2023 p.15 · Key: zones.changes.mods.dies</sub>

<a id="r410.4c"></a>**410.4c** A token mod has no card of its own. It never enters a bin; when its host leaves play it ceases to exist.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-29 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts, 141-despawn-mods.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::CR 410.4c: a TOKEN mod on a dying Unstable carrier is erased, never binned or trashed · Key: zones.changes.mods.token-mod</sub>

<a id="r410.4d"></a>**410.4d** An exchange is not a death. But a modded unit is {Unstable}, so when it is exchanged out of play, it and all of its mods are erased, just as they would be if it died. See rules 410.4b, 405.5, 801.

> *Example: Hooba-Mon exchanges itself while it carries a mod; it is erased, not left in a bin.*

> *Example: An unmodded Hooba-Mon exchanged the same way stays in the bin.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.35; card: Abyssal Evocation · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 42-dark-b.test.ts, 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts, 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Example tests: 42-dark-b.test.ts::engine (CT-246; CR 410.4d erases it unbinned): Hooba-Mon exchanges a MODDED host → the host is trashed, then ERASED (not left in a bin), 42-dark-b.test.ts::CR 405.4 control: Hooba-Mon exchanges an UNMODDED host → it still BINS and stays there · Key: zones.changes.mods.exchanged</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U07-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r410.5"></a>**410.5.** A token that leaves play goes to the zone it was sent to (a hand, a bin, a cache) and really is there. It ceases to exist there the next time state-based actions are checked, which is before anything it caused to trigger can resolve. See rules 304, 713, 400.2.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355689559609839787#4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22, 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts · Key: zones.changes.tokens</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U06-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r410.5a"></a>**410.5a** A unit token that dies enters the bin and is then erased. It is not trashed. See rule 801.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1355689559609839787#4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts, 338-tokens-are-not-trashed.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::a TOKEN dying enters the bin, is NOT trashed, and is then erased · Key: zones.changes.tokens.dies</sub>

<a id="r410.5b"></a>**410.5b** A recalled token, unit or spell, enters its controller's hand and is then erased. It counts as a card entering a hand for anything that is watching. See rule 402.4.

> *Example: A Fireball token recalled off the stack enters its controller's hand, Rider of the Tides sees it, and it is erased.*

> *Example: Recalling a unit token triggers Rider of the Tides too.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1355689559609839787#3 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 15-water-b.test.ts, 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts · Example tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Recall Spell Token: a Fireball token recalled off the stack enters its controller hand, 15-water-b.test.ts::Rider of the Tides: recalling a TOKEN triggers it too · Key: zones.changes.tokens.recalled</sub>

<a id="r410.5c"></a>**410.5c** A token put into a cache enters the cache and is then erased.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::CR 410.5c: a CACHED token visits the cache and is erased out of it · Key: zones.changes.tokens.cached</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U07-14 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r410.5d"></a>**410.5d** Any spell tokens still in play are erased during regroup. See rule 506.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.15; Manual p.15 · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.changes.tokens.spell-tokens-regroup — a Fireball spell token left unused is erased at regroup · Key: zones.changes.tokens.spell-tokens-regroup</sub>

<a id="r410.6"></a>**410.6.** A card is played from the zone it came out of, even when another effect plays it as it resolves. A card played from the cache, a bin or the deck is not played from the hand. See rules 701, 702.

> *Example: Tides of the Cosmos plays cards off the top of the deck; Proph and Stalwart Sentinel ("from anywhere other than your hand") both see it.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 241-played-from-zone.test.ts · Example test: 241-played-from-zone.test.ts::CR 410.6: Tides of the Cosmos plays off the top of the deck · Key: zones.changes.played-from</sub>

<a id="r410.6a"></a>**410.6a** A spell token is cast from where it stands in play, so it is played from somewhere other than the hand. See rule 304.

> *Example: Casting a Fireball token triggers Stalwart Sentinel.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-10 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts · Example test: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts::RAQ Spell Tokens vs Hand: casting a Fireball token triggers Stalwart Sentinel · Key: zones.changes.played-from.spell-token</sub>

<a id="r410.6b"></a>**410.6b** A token created by an effect was not played and came from no zone.

> *Example: A token created by an effect was not played, so neither Proph nor Stalwart Sentinel triggers.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 241-played-from-zone.test.ts · Example test: 241-played-from-zone.test.ts::CR 410.6b: an effect-created token carries no zone at all · Key: zones.changes.played-from.created</sub>

<a id="r410.7"></a>**410.7.** When a unit leaves play for a bin, it dies (or, if it was exchanged out of play, despawns) before anything is trashed. The unit and its mods leave play; then its death or despawn happens, and the abilities that trigger on it trigger; only then is any card trashed (see rule 801.2).

> *Example: A unit with no mods dies and goes to its controller's bin. Its death comes first, then it is trashed.*

> *Example: Hooba-Mon exchanges itself for a unit card in its controller's bin. It despawns, and only then is it trashed. It does not die.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 440-cr-uncovered-rulings.test.ts, 129-disposal-tail.test.ts · Example tests: 440-cr-uncovered-rulings.test.ts::cr:zones.changes.leave-play-order — a unit that dies dies first, and is trashed after, 440-cr-uncovered-rulings.test.ts::cr:zones.changes.leave-play-order — a unit exchanged out of play despawns first, and is trashed after · Key: zones.changes.leave-play-order</sub>

## 5. Turn Structure

<a id="r500"></a>
### 500. General

<a id="r500.1"></a>**500.1.** A turn has four phases, in this order: the planning phase, the battle phase, the regroup phase and the deployment phase. See rules 501, 505, 506, 507.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.7; Manual p.7; Manual p.7; Manual p.7; Manual p.7 · Tests: 20-draft.test.ts, 08-cards2.test.ts, 419-cr-planning.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 20-draft.test.ts::haste step still works after a draft turn (gates compose) · Key: turn.general.phases</sub>

<a id="r500.2"></a>**500.2.** Turns are global: all players share the same phases and sync up at the end of each step. In a 1v1 or team game, the printed rules take some steps in initiative order: the initiative player, or team, acts first, and the non-initiative player waits to see what they did before acting (see rule 501.4 and rule 507.3). See rule 100. *(Engine differs, see F-U08-4.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; no gate test · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.5; Manual p.7; Rulebook 2023 p.5; Rulebook 2023 p.5; Rulebook 2023 p.5; Rulebook 2023 p.5; Rulebook 2023 p.5; Rulebook 2023 p.5 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-11 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Key: turn.general.global</sub>

<a id="r500.2a"></a>**500.2a** *(Digital client)* This client makes the turn fully global. In the resource step, the haste step and deployment, both players act at the same time, and neither sees what the other does until both are done (see rule D1.4). This is a digital convention: a paper game cannot hide one player's actions while the other acts.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-10-04, 2026-10-11 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; no gate test · Key: turn.general.global.digital</sub>

<a id="r500.3"></a>**500.3.** In each turn one player has the initiative. In a 1v1 game the initiative player (IT) acts first and the non-initiative player (NIT) acts after them. See rules 103, 508, 904. *(Engine differs, see F-U08-1.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.20; Manual p.20; Manual p.20; Rulebook 2023 p.5 · Key: turn.general.initiative</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U08-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r500.3a"></a>**500.3a** The initiative is not a token. The Initiative token of the physical game only marks which player has it. See rule 304. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.11; Manual p.11 · Designer: RAQ 1353864175910387742#7 · Key: turn.general.initiative.not-token</sub>

<a id="r500.4"></a>**500.4.** The battle phase is the only phase of the turn in which players can interact, because it is the only time a player can enter another player's region. Outside it, every player is alone in their own region: in deployment a player can do what they like to their own units, but no opponent is there to interact with (see rule 601.4b). See rules 501.3, 505, 703.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.7; Manual p.19; Manual p.26; Rulebook 2023 p.8; Manual p.19; Manual p.26; Rulebook 2023 p.8; Manual p.19; Manual p.26; Rulebook 2023 p.8; Manual p.19; Manual p.26; Rulebook 2023 p.8; Manual p.19; Manual p.26; Rulebook 2023 p.8 · Tests: 419-cr-planning.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 419-cr-planning.test.ts::cr:turn.general.interactive — planning and deployment give nobody priority; the battle phase does once an attack is declared · Key: turn.general.interactive</sub>

<a id="r500.5"></a>**500.5.** When the deployment phase and its end-of-turn step are over, the turn is over. The initiative and any packs pass to the next player clockwise (see 508), and the next turn begins with its planning phase. See rules 507, 508.

> *Example: After turn 1 ends, turn 2 opens with each player drawing 2 and the draft step open again.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.26; Manual p.26; Manual p.26 · Tests: 20-draft.test.ts, 419-cr-planning.test.ts · Example test: 20-draft.test.ts::turns 2-3 draw 2 and re-open the draft step; packs refresh on turn 4 (N+1 cycle) · Key: turn.general.next-turn</sub>

<a id="r501"></a>
### 501. Planning Phase

<a id="r501.1"></a>**501.1.** The planning phase is the first phase of the turn. In it, players prepare for the turn ahead by curating their hands and preparing their resources.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.7; Manual p.7 · Tests: 419-cr-planning.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 419-cr-planning.test.ts::cr:turn.planning.what — a turn opens in planning, where the only actions are curating the hand and preparing resources · Key: turn.planning.what</sub>

<a id="r501.2"></a>**501.2.** The planning phase has five steps, taken in this order.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.27; Manual p.27; Manual p.27; Manual p.27; Manual p.27 · Tests: 20-draft.test.ts, 419-cr-planning.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 419-cr-planning.test.ts::cr:turn.planning.steps — refresh and draw at the turn start, then the draft, then resources, then the haste step · Key: turn.planning.steps</sub>

<a id="r501.2a"></a>**501.2a** Refresh: each player's expended resources refresh. See rule 106.

> *Example: A resource expended to pay debt in one turn is open again for mana in the next.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.27; Manual p.14 · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts · Example test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::CR 112.14b: partial payment is fine and the remainder carries to the next turn · Key: turn.planning.steps.refresh</sub>

<a id="r501.2b"></a>**501.2b** The draw step: see 503. See rule 503. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.27 · Key: turn.planning.steps.draw</sub>

<a id="r501.2c"></a>**501.2c** The draft step: see 503. In constructed, this step is a draw of 2 and a recycle of 2. See rule 503.

> *Example: Turn 2 of constructed: the hand gains 4 (2 for the draw step, 2 for the draft step), then 2 cards are recycled, a net gain of 2.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.27 · Tests: 419-cr-planning.test.ts · Example test: 419-cr-planning.test.ts::cr:turn.planning.steps.draft — in constructed the draft step adds a draw of 2 to the draw step, and then 2 cards are recycled · Key: turn.planning.steps.draft</sub>

<a id="r501.2d"></a>**501.2d** The resource step: see 502. See rule 502. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.27 · Key: turn.planning.steps.resource</sub>

<a id="r501.2e"></a>**501.2e** The haste step: see 504. See rule 504. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.18 · Key: turn.planning.steps.haste</sub>

<a id="r501.3"></a>**501.3.** There is no player interaction in the planning phase. No player receives priority in it, and nothing a player does in it can be responded to. See rules 504.3, 703.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.7 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts, 15-water-b.test.ts, 419-cr-planning.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 419-cr-planning.test.ts::cr:turn.planning.no-interaction — nobody holds priority in the resource step, and passing priority there is refused · Key: turn.planning.no-interaction</sub>

<a id="r501.4"></a>**501.4.** In a 1v1 game, the refresh, the draw step and the draft step happen for both players simultaneously. The resource step and the haste step are taken first by the initiative player and then by the non-initiative player. See rules 500.3, 502, 504. *(Engine differs, see F-U08-1.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.27; Rulebook 2023 p.5; Rulebook 2023 p.5; Manual p.20 · Key: turn.planning.order</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U08-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r501.4a"></a>**501.4a** A step of the planning phase ends for all players together. No player begins the resource step until every player has finished the draft step. See rule 503.2. *(Engine differs, see F-U08-4.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 3; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; no gate test · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.5; Manual p.16 · Key: turn.planning.order.sync</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U08-10 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r502"></a>
### 502. Resource Step

<a id="r502.1"></a>**502.1.** The resource step is the step of the planning phase in which players create and activate resources. See rule 106.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.18 · Tests: 419-cr-planning.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 419-cr-planning.test.ts::cr:turn.resource.what — resources are created and activated in the resource step and refused in the haste step · Key: turn.resource.what</sub>

<a id="r502.2"></a>**502.2.** In the resource step, a player may take these actions. See rule 106.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.18 · Tests: 01-planning.test.ts, 419-cr-planning.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 419-cr-planning.test.ts::cr:turn.resource.actions — the resource step menu offers creating, activating and exchanging a Prismite · Key: turn.resource.actions</sub>

<a id="r502.2a"></a>**502.2a** Create a resource by recycling a card from their hand. The resource enters play dormant. There is no limit to how many resources a player may create. See rules 106, 408.

> *Example: Recycling a hand card for a fire resource puts a dormant fire resource into play and the card into the recycle pile.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.18; Manual p.18; Manual p.18 · Tests: 01-planning.test.ts, 308-recycle-for-prismite.test.ts, 419-cr-planning.test.ts · Example test: 01-planning.test.ts::setup & planning · Key: turn.resource.actions.create</sub>

<a id="r502.2b"></a>**502.2b** Activate dormant resources by turning them face up, up to two activations per turn. See rule 106.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.18 · Tests: 01-planning.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 01-planning.test.ts::setup & planning · Key: turn.resource.actions.activate</sub>

<a id="r502.2c"></a>**502.2c** Exchange an active Prismite for a resource of one of the game's elements. A dormant Prismite cannot be exchanged. See rule 106.

> *Example: Two starting Prismites are activated, then one is exchanged for a fire resource, which keeps its active state.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.18; Manual p.18 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 01-planning.test.ts · Example test: 01-planning.test.ts::prismites: dormant start, no affinity, planning exchange into any element · Key: turn.resource.actions.exchange</sub>

<a id="r502.3"></a>**502.3.** The resource step ends when every player has created and activated all the resources they want. See rule 504.

> *Example: One player declaring done leaves the other free to keep activating; the haste step opens only when both are done.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.18 · Tests: 419-cr-planning.test.ts · Example test: 419-cr-planning.test.ts::cr:turn.resource.ends — one player finishing does not end the resource step; the haste step opens only when every player is done · Key: turn.resource.ends</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U08-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r502.4"></a>**502.4.** At the end of their resource step, a player with debt pays 1 mana for each debt, and each mana paid removes one debt. The payment is automatic: it is not a choice and needs no action. See rule 112.

> *Example: A player with 5 open fire and 3 debt ends the resource step with 0 debt and 2 open mana.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts · Example test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::CR 502.4: debt is paid automatically when the resource step ends — 1 mana per debt · Key: turn.resource.debt</sub>

<a id="r502.4a"></a>**502.4a** Paying debt is the last thing in the resource step. After it the player can activate no more resources this turn, and the mana spent on debt is not available to play cards this turn. See rule 112.

> *Example: With 3 open mana and 2 debt, the player is left 1 mana: no resource action is offered and a [3] unit cannot be played in deployment.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts · Example test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::CR 502.4a: debt-paid mana is genuinely gone — no more resources can be activated, and the card is unplayable · Key: turn.resource.debt.last</sub>

<a id="r503"></a>
### 503. Draw and Draft Step

<a id="r503.1"></a>**503.1.** In the draw step, each player draws 2 cards. See rules 401, 402.

> *Example: On turn 2 of a live draft each player's 6-card hand becomes 8.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.16; Rulebook 2023 p.6 · Tests: 20-draft.test.ts · Example test: 20-draft.test.ts::turns 2-3 draw 2 and re-open the draft step; packs refresh on turn 4 (N+1 cycle) · Key: turn.draw.draw</sub>

<a id="r503.1a"></a>**503.1a** In a live draft, no player draws in the draw step of the first turn: each player's first draw was dealt with their opening hand (see 103). See rule 103.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.16; Rulebook 2023 p.6 · Designer: RAQ 1451507918171013252#0 · Tests: 20-draft.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 20-draft.test.ts::createGame draft: 6-card hands (opening 4 + turn-1 draws), 10-card packs, draft step open · Key: turn.draw.draw.first-turn</sub>

<a id="r503.1b"></a>**503.1b** Players draw in clockwise order, starting with the initiative player. See rule 500.3.

> *Example: In a live draft the initiative player takes the top 2 cards of the shared deck at the start of the turn, and the other player the next 2.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.16; Manual p.16 · Tests: 419-cr-planning.test.ts · Example test: 419-cr-planning.test.ts::cr:turn.draw.draw.order — turn draws come off the shared deck clockwise from the initiative player · Key: turn.draw.draw.order</sub>

<a id="r503.2"></a>**503.2.** In the draft step of a live draft, each player combines the cards in their hand with the cards in their pack, then chooses which cards of the combined pile to keep in hand. The rest go back into the pack. See rules 409, 902.

> *Example: A player keeps three pack cards and puts three hand cards into the pack; the hand keeps its size.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.16; Manual p.16; Manual p.16; Manual p.16 · Tests: 20-draft.test.ts · Example test: 20-draft.test.ts::a real merge: swapped cards land where chosen, hand size is conserved · Key: turn.draw.draft</sub>

<a id="r503.2a"></a>**503.2a** A player must leave exactly 10 cards in the pack, so they end the draft step with as many cards in hand as they began it with. See rule 409.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.16; Manual p.16 · Tests: 20-draft.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 20-draft.test.ts::bad commits are rejected: wrong count, duplicates, out of range, wrong mode · Key: turn.draw.draft.ten</sub>

<a id="r503.2b"></a>**503.2b** Within that limit the choice is free: a player may keep their whole hand and take nothing, exchange their whole hand for pack cards, or anything in between.

> *Example: A player who keeps their hand exactly passes the pack exactly as dealt.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.6 · Tests: 20-draft.test.ts, 419-cr-planning.test.ts · Example test: 20-draft.test.ts::no-op commit preserves hand and pack exactly; both commits pass the packs · Key: turn.draw.draft.free</sub>

<a id="r503.2c"></a>**503.2c** When a player has finished drafting, they pass their pack clockwise to the next player. The draft step is complete once every player has passed their pack. See rules 409, 501.4.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.16; Manual p.16; Manual p.16 · Tests: 20-draft.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 20-draft.test.ts::no-op commit preserves hand and pack exactly; both commits pass the packs · Key: turn.draw.draft.pass</sub>

<a id="r503.2d"></a>**503.2d** An effect may make a player skip their draft step.

> *Example: With Worldbender in play in a live draft, its controller is never offered the pack and ends the step with 3 more cards: the 2 drawn in the draw step and Worldbender's 1.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Worldbender · Tests: 28-metal-c.test.ts · Example test: 28-metal-c.test.ts::Worldbender in a live draft: the pack is never offered, the hand gains 3, and life is untouched · Key: turn.draw.draft.skip</sub>

<a id="r503.3"></a>**503.3.** After every cycle of N+1 turns, where N is the number of players, every pack is recycled and each player is dealt a new pack of 10 cards. In 1v1 this happens after the third turn, right before the fourth draft. See rules 408, 409.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.16; Manual p.16; Rulebook 2023 p.6 · Tests: 20-draft.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 20-draft.test.ts::turns 2-3 draw 2 and re-open the draft step; packs refresh on turn 4 (N+1 cycle) · Key: turn.draw.refresh</sub>

<a id="r503.3a"></a>**503.3a** So each player drafts a second time from the pack they were first dealt before the packs are refreshed.

> *Example: In 1v1, the pack a player is dealt on turn 1 comes back to them on turn 3 with what they left in it.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.16 · Tests: 20-draft.test.ts · Example test: 20-draft.test.ts::"comes back to you" (turn 1) is true: your own pack returns on turn 3 · Key: turn.draw.refresh.second-look</sub>

<a id="r503.4"></a>**503.4.** In constructed there are no packs. In the draft step each player draws 2 more cards from their own deck and then recycles 2 cards from their hand. Since this comes straight after the draw step, the two are taken together: draw 4, then recycle 2. See rules 408, 901.

> *Example: Worldbender skips the constructed draft step: its controller draws only the draw step's 2 plus Worldbender's 1, recycles nothing, and loses 3 life.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.16; Manual p.16; Manual p.16; Manual p.16; Rulebook 2023 p.6 · Designer: RAQ 1451507918171013252#1 · Tests: 34-constructed.test.ts, 28-metal-c.test.ts · Example test: 28-metal-c.test.ts::Worldbender in constructed: no draw-4-put-2-back — the hand gains 3 and 3 life is paid · Demonstrated by test: 34-constructed.test.ts::turn 2 reopens the draw phase: 4 more cards, bottoming pending again · Key: turn.draw.constructed</sub>

<a id="r503.4a"></a>**503.4a** The player chooses which 2 cards of their hand to recycle. Until they have, they can take no other planning action. See rule 408.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.6 · Tests: 34-constructed.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 34-constructed.test.ts::nothing moves until the 2 cards go back; bottoming keeps the given order · Key: turn.draw.constructed.choice</sub>

<a id="r503.4b"></a>**503.4b** The draw of 4 and the recycle of 2 happen on the first turn of a constructed game too. See rules 103, 901.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.16; Manual p.16; Manual p.16 · Tests: 34-constructed.test.ts, 419-cr-planning.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 34-constructed.test.ts::createGame constructed: per-seat decks, opening 4 + draw 4, bottoming open · Key: turn.draw.constructed.first-turn</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U01-13 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r503.5"></a>**503.5.** Drawing and drafting are actions like any other: a unit that a change in hand size leaves with 0 defense, or with damage equal to its defense, dies as soon as the action is over, except as the constructed sub-rule below says (see 713). See rule 713.

> *Example: A Dreadspawn Horror (-1/-1 for each card in hand) taken to 0 defense by the turn's draw dies at once, before any other action is taken.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-06 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 380-no-action-ends-dead.test.ts, 419-cr-planning.test.ts · Example test: 380-no-action-ends-dead.test.ts::CR 503.5: the turn draw that takes Dreadspawn Horror to 0 defense kills it at the turn flip · Key: turn.draw.state-checks</sub>

<a id="r503.5a"></a>**503.5a** In the draft step the combined pile of hand and pack is never a hand: only the cards a player keeps count toward their hand size.

> *Example: A Dreadspawn Horror whose controller holds 1 card, draws 2 and keeps 3 through the draft ends the step a 4/2 and lives.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-06 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 380-no-action-ends-dead.test.ts · Example test: 380-no-action-ends-dead.test.ts::CR 503.5a draft: 1 card in hand, then the turn draw and the draft — a 4/2 that lives · Key: turn.draw.state-checks.draft-pile</sub>

<a id="r503.5b"></a>**503.5b** In constructed, the draw of 4 and the recycle of 2 count as one step. A player's units are not checked for death until that player has recycled their 2 cards, so they are judged on the hand that remains. See rules 713, 901.

> *Example: With 1 card in hand, a Dreadspawn Horror goes through draw 4 and put back 2 and ends a 4/2.*

> *Example: With 3 cards in hand it nets to 5 and dies once its controller has put 2 back.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-06 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 380-no-action-ends-dead.test.ts · Example tests: 380-no-action-ends-dead.test.ts::CR 503.5b constructed: drawing 4 does not kill before the 2 go back — 1 card in hand ends a 4/2, 380-no-action-ends-dead.test.ts::CR 503.5b constructed: 3 cards in hand nets to 5 — it dies once its controller has bottomed · Key: turn.draw.state-checks.constructed</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U08-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r504"></a>
### 504. Haste Step

<a id="r504.1"></a>**504.1.** The haste step is the last step of the planning phase. It comes after the resource step. See rule 501.2.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.18 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 08-cards2.test.ts::Molten Upheaval + the haste step: haste cards play between planning and battle (CR 504.1, 504.2) · Key: turn.haste.what</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U08-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r504.2"></a>**504.2.** In the haste step, players may play only haste cards. See rules 207, 803.

> *Example: Molten Upheaval, a haste card, is refused in the resource step and accepted in the haste step.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.18; Manual p.18; Manual p.13 · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts, 15-water-b.test.ts · Example test: 08-cards2.test.ts::Molten Upheaval + the haste step: haste cards play between planning and battle (CR 504.1, 504.2) · Key: turn.haste.plays</sub>

<a id="r504.2a"></a>**504.2a** A card with battle timing cannot be played in the haste step, even when an effect gives it haste or lets it be played as if it had haste. This holds for units and spell units alike. See rule 207.

> *Example: Under Dispatch Courier, a battle unit in hand is still not playable in the haste step.*
