<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1465292396664193171#0; RAQ 1465292396664193171#1; RAQ 1464899726796390433#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts, 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 26-metal-a.test.ts::Dispatch Courier: a {Battle} unit stays a battle card even with the grant · Demonstrated by test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Dispatch Courier: a Battle spell unit is not playable in the haste step either · Key: turn.haste.plays.battle-stays</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U05-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r504.3"></a>**504.3.** A card played in the haste step resolves immediately. It does not use the stack, no player receives priority, and no player can respond to it. See rules 501.3, 703.

> *Example: Tidal Menace played in the haste step is in play at once as a 7/2.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.7 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 15-water-b.test.ts, 08-cards2.test.ts, 419-cr-planning.test.ts · Example test: 15-water-b.test.ts::Tidal Menace: {Haste} 7/2 — playable in the haste step, resolves immediately (CR 504.3) · Key: turn.haste.immediate</sub>

<a id="r504.4"></a>**504.4.** The haste step ends when every player has played all the haste cards they want to play, which may be none. See rule 505.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), 1 failed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.18; Manual p.18 · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts, 200-haste-step-is-unconditional.test.ts, 419-cr-planning.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 200-haste-step-is-unconditional.test.ts::CR 504.5a: no seat is auto-done, and BOTH have to close the step · Key: turn.haste.ends</sub>

<a id="r504.5"></a>**504.5.** The haste step happens every turn, whether or not any player has anything they could play in it.

> *Example: On turn 1, with only two dormant Prismites each, the step still opens for both players.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts, 200-haste-step-is-unconditional.test.ts · Example test: 08-cards2.test.ts::the haste step opens even when nobody has a legal haste play (CR 504.5) · Key: turn.haste.always</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U08-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r504.5a"></a>**504.5a** No player is treated as finished with the haste step because they have nothing to play. Each player finishes the step themselves, and a player may stay in it holding nothing they could play.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), 1 failed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 200-haste-step-is-unconditional.test.ts, 419-cr-planning.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 200-haste-step-is-unconditional.test.ts::CR 504.5a: a bluff is a real move — you may sit in the step holding nothing · Key: turn.haste.always.no-auto-done</sub>

<a id="r504.6"></a>**504.6.** The end of the haste step is an event. An ability that triggers "at the end of [Haste]" triggers then, before the battle phase begins, including in a turn in which nobody played anything in the step. See rule 706.

> *Example: Keeper of Tithes creates an X/X for its controller's expended resources as the step closes.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), 1 failed; 4 gate test files · Printed: card: Keeper of Tithes; card: Debt Plant · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 38-light-a.test.ts, 200-haste-step-is-unconditional.test.ts, 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts, 419-cr-planning.test.ts · Example test: 38-light-a.test.ts::Keeper of Tithes: at the end of [Haste] it creates an X/X for your expended resources · Demonstrated by test: 200-haste-step-is-unconditional.test.ts::CR 504.6: the step still ENDS properly — endOfHaste fires exactly once · Key: turn.haste.end-event</sub>

<a id="r504.6a"></a>**504.6a** An instruction a card carries out "during [Haste]" happens in the haste step. This client asks for it as the step ends. *(Digital client)*

> *Example: Prediction Prophet asks its controller for a number at the end of the haste step, and creates a 5/5 at the start of deployment if it matched.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Prediction Prophet · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts · Example test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Prediction Prophet: the [Haste] prediction is a real decision, and matching it creates a 5/5 (CR 504.6a) · Key: turn.haste.end-event.during</sub>

<a id="r504.7"></a>**504.7.** An effect may let a player play, in the haste step, a card that lacks haste, "as if it had [Haste]". The grant changes only when the card may be played. See rules 504.2, 803.

> *Example: Dispatch Courier lets its controller play a deploy unit in the haste step.*

> *Example: Writhing Host in its owner's bin lets them play a deploy unit in the haste step, erasing the Host as the additional cost.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Dispatch Courier; card: Writhing Host · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts, 42-dark-b.test.ts · Example tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts::Dispatch Courier: "play a unit during the mana step as if it had [Haste]", 42-dark-b.test.ts::Writhing Host (CR 504.7): a deploy unit in hand is offered at haste timing, and playing it erases the Host from the bin · Key: turn.haste.grants</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U08-4 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r504.7a"></a>**504.7a** A grant that says "Each turn" allows one such play per turn for each card that grants it: two Dispatch Couriers allow two plays.

> *Example: One Courier grants one play: a second unit in the same haste step is refused.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Dispatch Courier · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts, 419-cr-planning.test.ts · Example test: 26-metal-a.test.ts::Dispatch Courier: the "Each turn" allowance is one, and one Courier grants one · Key: turn.haste.grants.each-turn</sub>

<a id="r504.8"></a>**504.8.** Mods are applied in deployment, not in the haste step, even when the mod card has haste. The exceptions are a card that allows mods in the haste step (the sub-rule below) and a Virus applied in battle (see 723). See rules 507, 720, 723.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 4 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.26; Manual p.26 · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 40-light-c.test.ts, 419-cr-planning.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 1: a graft is offered in deployment and never in the haste step or in battle, even for a Haste card, 40-light-c.test.ts::without a Slurpr the [Haste] refusal is unchanged — modding is a deployment action · Key: turn.haste.mods</sub>

<a id="r504.8a"></a>**504.8a** A card that says so can allow mods in the haste step: Slurpr lets its controller apply other mods, augments and grafts alike, during [Haste] as if it were deployment. See rule 720.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Slurpr · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Slurpr: mods may be applied during [Haste] as if it was deployment · Key: turn.haste.mods.slurpr</sub>

<a id="r504.9"></a>**504.9.** A card whose prophecy condition ends in [Haste] may be prophesied in the haste step as well as in deployment. Any other prophecy may be prophesied only in deployment. See rule 803.

> *Example: Divine Intervention's prophecy ("Your life is 5 or less [Haste]") may be prophesied in the haste step.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 257-prophecy-release-timing.test.ts · Example test: 257-prophecy-release-timing.test.ts::CR 504.9: a banner marked [Haste] may be prophesied during the haste step · Demonstrated by test: 257-prophecy-release-timing.test.ts::CR 504.9: an UNMARKED banner is still deployment-only — the haste step refuses it · Key: turn.haste.prophesy</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U08-9 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r504.9a"></a>**504.9a** The [Haste] marker does not move a fulfilled prophecy's release: the card is played from the cache only at its printed timing. See rule 803.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 257-prophecy-release-timing.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 257-prophecy-release-timing.test.ts::CR 504.9a: the marker does not move a fulfilled release out of battle and into the haste step · Key: turn.haste.prophesy.release</sub>

<a id="r505"></a>
### 505. Battle Phase

<a id="r505.1"></a>**505.1.** The battle phase is the only interactive phase of the game. In it players manage their units across the regions: they attack into other regions or keep units back to defend. See rules 601, 604.

> *Example: Player A attacks with a Good Whale: the Whale moves into Player B's region, and Player A enters that region too.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.7; Manual p.7 · Tests: 02-combat.test.ts · Example test: 02-combat.test.ts::combat math: columns, flying, piercing overflow, deaths · Key: turn.battle.what-it-is</sub>

<a id="r505.1a"></a>**505.1a** A player can interact with opponents and their units only during the battle phase. See rules 507, 601.

> *Example: In deployment, an effect that targets a cached card can reach only its controller's own cache; once an attack brings both players into a region in battle, it can reach the opponent's cache too.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.19; Manual p.19 · Tests: 293-cached-targets-are-regional.test.ts · Example test: 293-cached-targets-are-regional.test.ts::CR 110.5b in deployment a home region reaches only its own seat · Key: turn.battle.what-it-is.only-interaction</sub>

<a id="r505.1b"></a>**505.1b** An effect that applies "during battle" applies only in the battle phase. It does not apply in the haste step or in deployment. See rules 504, 507.

> *Example: Crevice Lurker makes abilities cost [one] more "during battle". Outside battle the same activation costs its printed [1].*

> *Example: Counter Thief takes counters placed "during battle"; outside battle it does nothing.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Crevice Lurker · Designer: RAQ 1355103348378042515#0 · Tests: 16-earth-a.test.ts, 182-correctness-sample.test.ts, 45-hybrids-ld-b.test.ts · Example tests: 16-earth-a.test.ts::Crevice Lurker: CR 505.1b — outside battle the same activation costs its printed [1], 182-correctness-sample.test.ts::Counter Thief: OUTSIDE battle it does nothing · Key: turn.battle.what-it-is.during-battle</sub>

<a id="r505.2"></a>**505.2.** Battle is made of four steps: the attack step, the block step, the combat step and the after-combat step. They take place separately inside each region. See rules 604, 606, 608, 609.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.20; Manual p.20 · Tests: 02-combat.test.ts, 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 02-combat.test.ts::1v1 counterattack: NIT sends units at block time, they attack in round 2 · Key: turn.battle.steps</sub>

<a id="r505.2a"></a>**505.2a** In a region that is not attacked, the combat step and the after-combat step are skipped. See rule 609.

> *Example: When both players decline to attack, neither round has a combat step, and the battle phase ends with no priority window at all.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.20 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 165-token-loss-warning.test.ts · Example test: 165-token-loss-warning.test.ts::[CT-55] a battle both players decline opens no priority window at all · Key: turn.battle.steps.unattacked</sub>

<a id="r505.2b"></a>**505.2b** An attack step in which no attack is declared opens no priority window. If both battle rounds are declined, the battle phase has no priority window at all. See rules 506, 605.

> *Example: The initiative player declines to attack, then the non-initiative player declines too: the game goes to regroup without either player getting priority, so a Fireball token held for the battle is erased unused.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 165-token-loss-warning.test.ts, 21-fixes.test.ts · Example test: 165-token-loss-warning.test.ts::[CT-55] a battle both players decline opens no priority window at all · Key: turn.battle.steps.declined-no-window</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U09-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r505.3"></a>**505.3.** In 1v1 and team games the battle phase has two battle rounds. In round 1 the initiative team attacks into the non-initiative team's regions. In round 2 the non-initiative team's counterattackers attack into the initiative team's regions. See rules 500, 610.

> *Example: The initiative player attacks in round 1; the units the non-initiative player sent at blocks attack in round 2.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.20; Manual p.20; Rulebook 2023 p.5 · Tests: 02-combat.test.ts · Example test: 02-combat.test.ts::1v1 counterattack: NIT sends units at block time, they attack in round 2 · Key: turn.battle.rounds</sub>

<a id="r505.3a"></a>**505.3a** Round 1 runs in this order: (1) the initiative team declares its attacks, sending units into non-initiative regions; (2) a priority window; (3) the non-initiative team declares its blocking formations and may at the same time send units out to counterattack; (4) a priority window; (5) the combat step, in which all units in formation deal combat damage at the same time; (6) the after-combat step, the last priority window in that region. See rules 604, 605, 606, 607, 608, 609, 610.

> *Example: The initiative player attacks with a 2/2 Curio Drifter; the non-initiative player blocks nothing and sends a Rune Channeler to counterattack. The unblocked Drifter deals 2, and after the after-combat window round 2 begins.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.20; Manual p.20; Manual p.20; Manual p.20; Manual p.20 · Tests: 02-combat.test.ts, 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts · Example test: 02-combat.test.ts::1v1 counterattack: NIT sends units at block time, they attack in round 2 · Key: turn.battle.rounds.round-1</sub>

<a id="r505.3b"></a>**505.3b** Units sent out to counterattack leave the region at once, and are treated as if they do not exist until round 1 is finished. See rule 610.

> *Example: A Rune Channeler sent to counterattack is absent for the rest of round 1, and arrives in the initiative player's region for round 2.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.20; Manual p.20 · Tests: 02-combat.test.ts · Example test: 02-combat.test.ts::1v1 counterattack: NIT sends units at block time, they attack in round 2 · Key: turn.battle.rounds.counterattackers-absent</sub>

<a id="r505.3c"></a>**505.3c** Round 2 runs in this order: (1) the non-initiative team puts its counterattacking units into formation; (2) a priority window; (3) the initiative team declares its blocking formation; (4) a priority window; (5) the combat step; (6) the after-combat step, the last priority window in that region before regroup. See rule 610.

> *Example: The counterattacking Rune Channeler arrives in the initiative player's region, attacks, is not blocked and deals 4; after the after-combat window the game goes through regroup to deployment.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.20; Manual p.20; Manual p.20 · Tests: 02-combat.test.ts · Example test: 02-combat.test.ts::1v1 counterattack: NIT sends units at block time, they attack in round 2 · Key: turn.battle.rounds.round-2</sub>

<a id="r505.3d"></a>**505.3d** Each team gets only one chance to attack in a battle phase. There is no counterattack in round 2. See rule 610.

> *Example: The non-initiative player sent a Rune Channeler at blocks and attacks with it in round 2; the initiative player may block it but cannot send a unit of their own out, and the battle phase ends after round 2.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.5; Rulebook 2023 p.5 · Tests: 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts · Example test: 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts::cr:turn.battle.rounds.one-attack-each — in round 2 the initiative player cannot send units out to counterattack, and the battle phase ends after round 2 · Key: turn.battle.rounds.one-attack-each</sub>

<a id="r505.3e"></a>**505.3e** The non-initiative team may declare attacks in round 2 even if the initiative team declared none in round 1. It may then attack with any of its units, because it never had a block step in which to send counterattackers. See rule 610.

> *Example: The initiative player could attack and declines; the non-initiative player then attacks in round 2 with a unit that was never sent.*

> *Example: Only the non-initiative player has a unit; the initiative player declares no attack, and in round 2 that unit attacks from home.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.20 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts, 21-fixes.test.ts · Example tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Temporal Rift thread: the non-initiative player still attacks when the initiative player declines, 21-fixes.test.ts::REGRESSION: NIT can attack in round 2 when IT had no units in round 1 · Key: turn.battle.rounds.nit-attacks-alone</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U13-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r505.3f"></a>**505.3f** If round 1 had a battle, only the units sent out at the block step can attack in round 2. If none were sent, there is no round 2. See rule 610.

> *Example: The initiative player attacks, the non-initiative player blocks and sends nobody: the battle phase ends after round 1, and the unit that stayed home is untouched.*

> *Example: A Good Whale that stayed home while a Rune Channeler was sent out cannot be declared as a round-2 attacker.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.21 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 21-fixes.test.ts, 02-combat.test.ts · Example tests: 21-fixes.test.ts::round 2 after a real round-1 battle still restricts to the sent counterattackers, 02-combat.test.ts::1v1 counterattack: NIT sends units at block time, they attack in round 2 · Key: turn.battle.rounds.no-round-2</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U09-4 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r505.4"></a>**505.4.** Battle is resolved one region at a time. Once players begin interacting in a region, every step of battle is completed in that region before those players can interact anywhere else. See rule 601.

> *Example: In 1v1, every step of round 1 finishes in the non-initiative player's region before round 2 starts in the initiative player's region.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.21 · Tests: 02-combat.test.ts · Example test: 02-combat.test.ts::1v1 counterattack: NIT sends units at block time, they attack in round 2 · Key: turn.battle.region-order</sub>

<a id="r505.4a"></a>**505.4a** The regions resolve in clockwise order, starting with the region to the left of the initiative player, so the initiative player's region resolves last. See rule 904.

> *Example: In a four-player game the region to the initiative player's left resolves first and the initiative player's own region last.*

> *Example: In 1v1, round 1 is fought in the non-initiative home region and the initiative home region comes last, in round 2.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.21; Manual p.21 · Tests: 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts · Example test: 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts::cr:turn.battle.region-order.clockwise — in 1v1 the initiative player home region is fought last, in round 2 · Key: turn.battle.region-order.clockwise</sub>

<a id="r505.4b"></a>**505.4b** In 1v1, round 1 is fought in the non-initiative player's region, and round 2, if there is one, in the initiative player's region. See rules 601, 610.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.21; Manual p.21 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 02-combat.test.ts, 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 02-combat.test.ts::1v1 counterattack: NIT sends units at block time, they attack in round 2 · Key: turn.battle.region-order.one-v-one</sub>

<a id="r505.4c"></a>**505.4c** While a region's battle is being resolved, units in any other region, including units that stayed home and counterattackers that were sent away, are treated as if they do not exist. See rules 601, 610.

> *Example: Player A attacks with a Rune Channeler and leaves a Good Whale at home. Player B casts Luminous Arc: it can target the attacking Channeler, but not the Whale that stayed home.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.21; Manual p.21 · Tests: 05-rulings.test.ts · Example test: 05-rulings.test.ts::CR 601.1a: regions are exclusive · Key: turn.battle.region-order.others-absent</sub>

<a id="r505.5"></a>**505.5.** In free-for-all games there are no battle rounds: all players declare their attacks at the same time, using intent cards. See rules 903, 905. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.7; Rulebook 2023 p.9 · Key: turn.battle.ffa</sub>

<a id="r505.6"></a>**505.6.** Anything counted "in this battle" is counted separately for each region, and the count starts again at the start of each battle phase. Things that happen outside the battle phase are not counted. See rule 601.

> *Example: During a battle a player discards a card, then their attacking unit dies in combat: two cards have been trashed in this battle. At the next battle phase the count starts again from zero.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Burning Vengeance · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts, 11-fire-wood.test.ts, 47-costs-events.test.ts · Example test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::CR 505.6: battleCounters count trashes per battle and reset between battles · Demonstrated by test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::CR 505.6: a trash outside battle counts for nothing · Key: turn.battle.this-battle</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U09-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r505.6a"></a>**505.6a** The life a player has lost in a battle is the total of every loss in that battle. Life gained in the battle does not reduce it. See rule 112.

> *Example: A player loses 10, gains 8, then loses 3: they have lost 13 life in this battle, and Soul Siphon makes a 13/13.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1449475896510648320#0 · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts · Example test: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Life lost: life lost in a battle adds up the losses and ignores the gains · Key: turn.battle.this-battle.life-lost</sub>

<a id="r506"></a>
### 506. Regroup Phase

<a id="r506.1"></a>**506.1.** Regroup is a global step that takes place once battle has ended in every region. It resets the game between battles. See rule 505.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.26; Manual p.26 · Tests: 183-end-battle-round-paths.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 183-end-battle-round-paths.test.ts::CR D2.6b: every path funnels through startRegroup · Key: turn.regroup.what-it-is</sub>

<a id="r506.1a"></a>**506.1a** No player gets priority or takes any game action during regroup.

> *Example: When the last player passes in the after-combat window, the game goes through regroup and straight into deployment; no one is given priority in between.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.26 · Tests: 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts · Example test: 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts::cr:turn.regroup.what-it-is.no-actions — the last after-combat pass lands straight in deployment, with nobody holding priority · Key: turn.regroup.what-it-is.no-actions</sub>

<a id="r506.1b"></a>**506.1b** Regroup comes before the deployment phase, not at the end of the turn. So a spell token made, or a temporary change applied, during deployment lasts until the regroup after the next battle. See rule 507.

> *Example: Overbloom played in deployment gives +7/+7 "until regroup"; the bonus lasts through the next battle and is gone after its regroup.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.26; Manual p.26 · Tests: 24-wood-b.test.ts, 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts · Example test: 24-wood-b.test.ts::Overbloom: target unit gains +7/+7 until regroup (deploy timing) · Key: turn.regroup.what-it-is.before-deployment</sub>

<a id="r506.2"></a>**506.2.** Regroup does these things, in this order: (1) all players and units return to their own regions; (2) all damage on units is removed; (3) all temporary stat changes are removed; (4) all units leave formation. All spell tokens are also erased. See rule 602.

> *Example: After a battle the attacker is back home, both players are back in their own regions, its marked damage and its -2/-2 are gone, there is no formation, and the spell token is erased.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.26; Manual p.26; Manual p.26; Manual p.26; Manual p.26 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 05-rulings.test.ts · Example test: 05-rulings.test.ts::CR 506.2: regroup runs its exact sequence · Key: turn.regroup.sequence</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U09-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r506.2a"></a>**506.2a** Each unit that is not in its controller's home region returns there. This includes a unit that was created in another region. See rules 601, 108.

> *Example: Life Plant's 1/1s, created in the enemy region during an attack, walk home at regroup.*

> *Example: The attacker and the counterattacker are both back in their home regions after regroup.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.26 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 98-spawn-region.test.ts, 02-combat.test.ts, 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts · Example tests: 98-spawn-region.test.ts::the stranded 1/1s walk home at regroup, 02-combat.test.ts::1v1 counterattack: NIT sends units at block time, they attack in round 2 · Key: turn.regroup.sequence.return</sub>

<a id="r506.2b"></a>**506.2b** Each player who entered another region during battle stops being present there, and is present only in their own region again. See rule 601.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.19; Manual p.19 · Tests: 05-rulings.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 05-rulings.test.ts::CR 506.2: regroup runs its exact sequence · Key: turn.regroup.sequence.players</sub>

<a id="r506.2c"></a>**506.2c** All damage on units is removed. See rule 112.

> *Example: A Good Whale carrying 1 marked damage has none after regroup.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.26; Rulebook 2023 p.11 · Tests: 05-rulings.test.ts · Example test: 05-rulings.test.ts::CR 506.2: regroup runs its exact sequence · Key: turn.regroup.sequence.damage</sub>

<a id="r506.2d"></a>**506.2d** All temporary stat changes are removed. An effect that lasts "until regroup" ends here. See rule 709.

> *Example: Overbloom's +7/+7 "until regroup" is gone after the next regroup.*

> *Example: Jelly's -2/-2 on an attacker is gone after regroup.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.26; card: Overbloom · Tests: 24-wood-b.test.ts, 05-rulings.test.ts, 03-stack.test.ts · Example tests: 24-wood-b.test.ts::Overbloom: target unit gains +7/+7 until regroup (deploy timing), 05-rulings.test.ts::CR 506.2: regroup runs its exact sequence · Key: turn.regroup.sequence.temporary</sub>

<a id="r506.2e"></a>**506.2e** All units leave formation. See rule 602.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.26; Manual p.7 · Tests: 05-rulings.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 05-rulings.test.ts::CR 506.2: regroup runs its exact sequence · Key: turn.regroup.sequence.formation</sub>

<a id="r506.2f"></a>**506.2f** All spell tokens in play are erased, including unused spell tokens in a player's own region. See rules 304, 407.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.26; Manual p.15; Manual p.15 · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::regroup default is unchanged: with no Harbinger anywhere, spell tokens are erased · Key: turn.regroup.sequence.spell-tokens</sub>

<a id="r506.2g"></a>**506.2g** A card can keep spell tokens through regroup. While Harbinger of Immolation's [Augment] text applies, its controller's spell tokens are not erased; they keep their X, and they still lose their temporary changes. Other players' spell tokens are still erased. See rules 721, 101.

> *Example: With Harbinger of Immolation in play as a unit, your spell tokens stay through regroup.*

> *Example: With Harbinger of Immolation in play, your Fireball 7 token survives regroup still a Fireball 7, but any temporary changes on it are gone.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Harbinger of Immolation · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts · Example tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Harbinger of Immolation: in play as a UNIT, your spell tokens stay through regroup, 12-fire-a.test.ts::Harbinger of Immolation: a surviving token keeps its X · Demonstrated by test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Harbinger of Immolation: only YOUR tokens stay · Key: turn.regroup.sequence.spell-tokens.harbinger</sub>

<a id="r506.2h"></a>**506.2h** A spell token erased at regroup takes its mods with it. See rules 720, 304.

> *Example: A Fireball token augmented during deployment and not cast is erased at regroup, and its augment is erased with it.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.35 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts · Example test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::CR 506.2h: an augmented token erased at regroup takes its mod with it · Key: turn.regroup.sequence.spell-tokens.mods</sub>

<a id="r506.3"></a>**506.3.** Unit tokens are not erased at regroup. They stay in play like other units. See rule 304.

> *Example: The 1/1 unit tokens Life Plant made in the enemy region are still in play after regroup, back in their home region.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.15 · Tests: 98-spawn-region.test.ts · Example test: 98-spawn-region.test.ts::the stranded 1/1s walk home at regroup · Key: turn.regroup.unit-tokens-stay</sub>

<a id="r507"></a>
### 507. Deployment Phase

<a id="r507.1"></a>**507.1.** The deployment phase is the last phase of each turn. In it players build up their forces for the next battle by playing cards, activating abilities, and modifying cards with graft and augment. See rule 720.

> *Example: In deployment a player plays Ignis Sprite (its spawn trigger makes a Fireball) and then Flame Juggle.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.26; Manual p.26; Manual p.26 · Tests: 01-planning.test.ts · Example test: 01-planning.test.ts::deployment: casting, spawn triggers, spell tokens · Key: turn.deploy.what-it-is</sub>

<a id="r507.1a"></a>**507.1a** Any card can be played during deployment except a battle card, which can be played only in the battle phase. See rules 207, 803.

> *Example: In deployment a player plays Flame Juggle and gets a Fireball token. Fireball is a battle card, so the token cannot be cast until the battle phase.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.26; Manual p.26 · Tests: 01-planning.test.ts · Example test: 01-planning.test.ts::battle-timed Fireball is NOT castable during deployment · Key: turn.deploy.what-it-is.no-battle-cards</sub>

<a id="r507.1b"></a>**507.1b** During deployment each player is alone in their own region. A player cannot interact with other players or their units, and treats every other player as if they did not exist. See rules 601, 505.

> *Example: Beyond's rot replacement says "target unit", and in deployment only its controller's own units are offered.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.26; Manual p.42 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 43-dark-c.test.ts, 293-cached-targets-are-regional.test.ts · Example test: 43-dark-c.test.ts::CR 507.1b — the target list is your own units, even with an enemy standing in the region · Key: turn.deploy.what-it-is.alone</sub>

<a id="r507.1c"></a>**507.1c** An effect in deployment that refers to opponents finds none. "Each opponent loses 1 life" does not affect any other player. See rule 601.

> *Example: Thoughtripper trashed outside battle makes no opponent discard, because no opponent is present.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.42; Manual p.42 · Tests: 43-dark-c.test.ts · Example test: 43-dark-c.test.ts::Thoughtripper: CR 601.4d — trashed outside battle, no opponent is present to discard · Key: turn.deploy.what-it-is.no-opponents</sub>

<a id="r507.2"></a>**507.2.** Modifications are applied during deployment. A mod may be applied from the hand or the bin, and a glimpsed mod also from the cache. See rules 720, 403.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.27 · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#4 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 3 · Key: turn.deploy.mods</sub>

<a id="r507.2a"></a>**507.2a** Grafting is done during deployment, whatever the card's speed, even for a card with Haste, and never in battle. A graft can be applied in the haste step only where an effect lets mods be applied then as if it were deployment, such as Slurpr's. See rules 722, 504.

> *Example: With a Slurpr in its controller's region, a graft lands during the haste step.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 3; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Slurpr · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#0; RAQ 1355115946032889914#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Engine: apply.ts:doGraft, apply.ts:hasteModAllowed · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 40-light-c.test.ts, 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts · Example test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Slurpr: a GRAFT lands during [Haste] too · Demonstrated by test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 1: a graft is offered in deployment · Key: turn.deploy.mods.graft-only</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U09-11 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r507.2b"></a>**507.2b** During deployment a player may augment a spell token they have in play. Only the augment's attributes pass to the token. See rules 721, 304.

> *Example: A Fireball 3 token augmented in deployment with Chitin Shredder gains {Powerful}, and when cast in battle it deals 6.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Engine: apply.ts:doAugment, engine.ts:stackAugmentAttrs · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts · Example test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::CR 721.4a: only ATTRIBUTES transfer · Demonstrated by test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::CR 721.4a: a spell token is a legal augment host during deployment · Key: turn.deploy.mods.spell-token</sub>

<a id="r507.3"></a>**507.3.** In 1v1 and team games the printed rules have the initiative team deploy first. Its players deploy in any order they wish, and then the non-initiative team does the same. See rules 500, 904. *(Engine differs, see F-U09-3.) (Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

> *Example: In a 2v2 game both initiative players finish deploying before either non-initiative player begins.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.38; Manual p.38; Rulebook 2023 p.5 · Key: turn.deploy.order</sub>

<a id="r507.3a"></a>**507.3a** *(Digital client)* In this client both players deploy at the same time. Neither sees what the other does in deployment until both are done, and either may finish first. See rule D6.

> *Example: The non-initiative player is offered plays at once, and can finish deploying while the initiative player is still acting.*

> *Example: During deployment Player A plays Ignis Sprite; nothing of it appears in Player B's game log while deployment is under way.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24, 2026-09-01 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 21-fixes.test.ts, 203-reveal-waits-for-the-barrier.test.ts · Example tests: 21-fixes.test.ts::both seats deploy at once: NIT may act and finish before IT, 203-reveal-waits-for-the-barrier.test.ts::CR D6.1a: a hidden step with no reveal in it leaks nothing either (the negative control) · Demonstrated by test: 21-fixes.test.ts::legalActions OFFERS deploy plays to both seats at once · Key: turn.deploy.order.simultaneous</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U08-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r507.4"></a>**507.4.** The deployment phase begins in this order: (1) each player is dealt damage equal to their rot, in initiative order; (2) then abilities that trigger "at the start of deployment" trigger. See rule 112.

> *Example: A player controls Beyond, Codex Incarnate and has 2 rot. At the start of deployment the rot comes first: Beyond asks them to pick a unit (they pick their Good Whale), and only after that do 'at the start of deployment' abilities trigger.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts, 43-dark-c.test.ts · Example test: 43-dark-c.test.ts::CR 507.4 — the start-of-deployment event still fires after the rot replacement stopped to ask · Demonstrated by test: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::CR 112.13: rot deals damage equal to itself at the start of deployment, in initiative order · Key: turn.deploy.start</sub>

<a id="r507.4a"></a>**507.4a** All abilities that trigger at the start of deployment are put on the stack before any of them resolves. See rules 703, 706.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::CR 507.4a: every start-of-deployment trigger is on the stack before any of them resolves · Key: turn.deploy.start.triggers</sub>

<a id="r507.5"></a>**507.5.** Deployment uses the stack. Each player's plays and triggered abilities in deployment go on that player's own deployment stack, and that stack normally resolves without anyone having to act. *(Digital client)* See rule 703.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-01 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 276-deployment-stack.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 276-deployment-stack.test.ts::CR 507.5: the play really went ON a stack · Key: turn.deploy.stack</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U09-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r507.5a"></a>**507.5a** *(Digital client)* A decision one player must answer during deployment does not make the other player wait: the other player may keep playing, and their own deployment stack keeps resolving. See rule D6.

> *Example: Player B is answering a choice; meanwhile Player A plays a card in deployment and it resolves.*

> *Example: Player B has three Wraiths, and their start-of-deployment triggers are asking B to choose. Meanwhile Player A can still act, and can even finish deploying; B's triggers then resolve normally.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25, 2026-09-01 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 276-deployment-stack.test.ts, 130-seat-aware-gate.test.ts · Example tests: 276-deployment-stack.test.ts::CR 507.5a: seat 1 is mid-question and seat 0, 130-seat-aware-gate.test.ts::CR 507.5a: a Wraith pile suspends its own seat, not the other one · Key: turn.deploy.stack.no-waiting</sub>

<a id="r508"></a>
### 508. Passing the Initiative

<a id="r508.1"></a>**508.1.** The end of turn is a special step after deployment finishes. In it, abilities that trigger "at the end of turn" resolve. See rule 706.

> *Example: Harbinger of Immolation creates a Fireball X at the end of turn.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.26; Manual p.27; card: Harbinger of Immolation · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts, 99-endofturn.test.ts · Example test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Harbinger of Immolation: end of turn → Fireball X · Demonstrated by test: 99-endofturn.test.ts::a choice raised inside a real endTurn() is asked, answered, and the turn still flips · Key: turn.initiative.end-of-turn</sub>

<a id="r508.1a"></a>**508.1a** No player can play cards during the end-of-turn step, either after the end-of-turn triggers or in response to them.

> *Example: While a General Smof end-of-turn trigger is asking its question, neither player is offered a card, spell token, ability, graft or augment, and an Ignis Sprite play is refused.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.26; Manual p.26 · Tests: 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts · Example test: 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts::cr:turn.initiative.end-of-turn.no-responses — while an end-of-turn trigger is asking, no seat is offered a play and a play is refused · Key: turn.initiative.end-of-turn.no-responses</sub>

<a id="r508.2"></a>**508.2.** After deployment and the end of turn, the turn is over. The next turn begins with the planning phase. See rule 501.

> *Example: Once both players are done deploying and the end-of-turn trigger is answered, the turn number goes up by one and the phase is planning.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.26; Manual p.26 · Tests: 99-endofturn.test.ts, 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts · Example test: 99-endofturn.test.ts::a choice raised inside a real endTurn() is asked, answered, and the turn still flips · Key: turn.initiative.turn-over</sub>

<a id="r508.3"></a>**508.3.** When the turn is over, the initiative token is passed to the next player clockwise. In 1v1 and team games this means the initiative alternates between the teams every turn. See rules 500, 904.

> *Example: The player without the initiative this turn has it once the turn ends, declares the first attack of the next battle, and the turn after that it passes back.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.26; Manual p.26; Rulebook 2023 p.5 · Tests: 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts · Example test: 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts::cr:turn.initiative.pass — when the turn ends the initiative goes to the other player, who attacks first in the next battle, and it alternates back · Key: turn.initiative.pass</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U09-9 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r508.3a"></a>**508.3a** Draft packs are passed in the draft step: each player passes their pack clockwise to the next player when they finish drafting, and the draft step is complete once all players have passed their pack. The end-of-turn passing of "any draft packs" with the initiative names this same pass; a pack is not passed a second time when the turn ends. See rules 503, 902.

> *Example: After both players finish drafting, each holds the pack the other drafted from.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: partial in round 3; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.16; Manual p.16; Rulebook 2023 p.6; Manual p.26; Rulebook 2023 p.5 · Engine: apply.ts:doDraftCommit, engine.ts:passPacks · Tests: 20-draft.test.ts, 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts · Example test: 20-draft.test.ts::no-op commit preserves hand and pack exactly; both commits pass the packs · Key: turn.initiative.pass.packs</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U09-10 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r508.4"></a>**508.4.** The initiative token is not a token. An effect that refers to tokens never affects it. See rule 304.

> *Example: Download says "Gain control of target token"; it cannot be used to take the initiative token.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; no gate test · Designer: RAQ 1353864175910387742#7 · Key: turn.initiative.not-a-token</sub>

## 6. Regions, Formations and Battle

<a id="r600"></a>
### 600. General

<a id="r600.1"></a>**600.1.** Units are the basis of combat. They attack opponents, enter other players' regions and defend against units that enter their own. Combat takes place inside regions (rule 601), with the units that take part arranged in formations (rule 602) made up of columns (rule 603). See rules 601, 602, 603.

> *Example: Two units attack into the opponent's region. The defender blocks one of them; the other is unblocked and deals its damage to the defending player.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.22; Rulebook 2023 p.10 · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.general.units — an attacking unit enters the defending player region, an unblocked attacker damages that player, and a defending unit blocks an attacker · Key: combat.general.units</sub>

<a id="r601"></a>
### 601. Regions

<a id="r601.1"></a>**601.1.** All gameplay takes place inside regions. There is one region for each player, and each player starts in their own region.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.19; Rulebook 2023 p.8 · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.regions.definition — a new game has one region per player, and each player starts present only in their own region · Key: combat.regions.definition</sub>

<a id="r601.1a"></a>**601.1a** Each region is isolated from every other region. Nothing in one region interacts with anything in another region, and each region treats the players and cards in other regions as if they don't exist. See rule 601.8.

> *Example: Towering Colossus prints “Enemies gain +2/+2.” An enemy unit standing in a different region from the Colossus does not get the bonus.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.19; Manual p.42; Rulebook 2023 p.8 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 243-ally-and-enemy-scope.test.ts · Example test: 243-ally-and-enemy-scope.test.ts::CR 601.4e a static that says ENEMIES does not reach an enemy in another region · Key: combat.regions.definition.isolated</sub>

<a id="r601.1b"></a>**601.1b** Every effect is specific to the region it takes place in, and never affects anything in another region. Read every card as if it said “in this region”: “Delete target unit” means “Delete target unit in this region”, and “Each player sacrifices two units” means “Each player in this region sacrifices two units in this region”.

> *Example: Ghord's controller sacrifices a unit, and each opponent sacrifices a nontoken unit. Only the opponent's units in Ghord's region can be sacrificed this way.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.19; Manual p.19; Rulebook 2023 p.8 · Designer: RAQ 1454169054402314362#0 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts, 12-fire-a.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Another set: a Ghord sacrifice reaches only the opponent units in its own region · Key: combat.regions.definition.every-effect-local</sub>

<a id="r601.1c"></a>**601.1c** “All” means all in this region. An effect that affects or counts “all” of something affects or counts only the ones in its own region.

> *Example: Cosmic Reversal recalls all other spell units. A spell unit that its opponent left at home, outside the battle region, is not recalled.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.8 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-29 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts · Example test: 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts::CR 601.1c: the board half is scoped to the region, like every other all · Key: combat.regions.definition.all</sub>

<a id="r601.1d"></a>**601.1d** A static ability sees and affects only things in its own region. A triggered ability triggers only on events in its own region: a spell played in one region does not trigger an ability of a unit in another region.

> *Example: Flourishing Flora watches for another ally spawning. An ally that spawns in a different region does not trigger it.*

> *Example: Crevice Lurker makes abilities cost [one] more during battle. It taxes both players' abilities in its region, the opponent's as well as its controller's.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.42; Manual p.42; Manual p.21 · Tests: 243-ally-and-enemy-scope.test.ts, 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example tests: 243-ally-and-enemy-scope.test.ts::CR 601.4e a trigger that watches for another ALLY does not see one spawn in another region, 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ Crevice Lurker: it taxes the opponent too, not only its controller · Key: combat.regions.definition.statics-and-triggers</sub>

<a id="r601.1e"></a>**601.1e** A player cannot sacrifice a unit that is in a different region, even a unit they control, and cannot do so to pay a cost in their current region.

> *Example: A player's only units are at home, outside the battle region, when Cull says "Each player sacrifices a unit." They sacrifice nothing.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.41; Manual p.42 · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.regions.definition.sacrifice — Cull makes each player sacrifice a unit, and a player whose only units are in another region sacrifices nothing · Key: combat.regions.definition.sacrifice</sub>

<a id="r601.2"></a>**601.2.** Every unit and every spell token in play is in exactly one region at a time.

> *Example: A unit attacks and a Fireball token rides along with it. Both are now in the battle region and no longer in their home region.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.regions.exclusive — every unit and spell token in play names one region, and an attacking unit and the spell token riding with it leave their home region for the battle region · Key: combat.regions.exclusive</sub>

<a id="r601.2a"></a>**601.2a** The stack, the bins, the hands and the caches are bound by the regional rule like everything else (rule 101.6). Each region has its own stack. No player owns it: it is shared by the players present in that region, and only they can put effects on it or respond to them. A player's bin, hand and cache are tied to that player: an effect can affect them only in a region where that player is present (rule 601.4c). See rule 601.4c. *(Engine differs, see F-U01-2.)*

> *Example: During deployment, an effect that targets a cached card can reach only its controller's own cache. In battle, where both players are present, it can reach either cache.*

> *Example: Frosted Denial, cast while battle resolves in one region, cannot negate an effect that was played in another region.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.19; Manual p.19; Manual p.19; Manual p.19 · Designer: RAQ 1454169054402314362#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-09-01, 2026-10-11 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.regions.exclusive.no-region-zones — cached and binned cards carry no region, no region holds a stack, and a cache is reachable only where its owner is present · Key: combat.regions.exclusive.no-region-zones</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U01-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r601.3"></a>**601.3.** The regions are arranged in a circle. Each player's region has two neighbouring regions, one to the left and one to the right, except in a two-player game, where each region has one neighbouring region. See rules 903, 904.

> *Example: In a two-player game there is only one region to attack into: the attackers go into the opponent's region, and the counterattack goes into the first attacker's region.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.19; Manual p.19; Manual p.19 · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.regions.arrangement — in a two-player game each region has one neighbour: an attack names no destination and goes into the opponent region, and the counterattack into the attacker region · Key: combat.regions.arrangement</sub>

<a id="r601.3a"></a>**601.3a** When a player is eliminated, the regions on either side of theirs become neighbours, and the game continues. See rules 104, 903. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.8; Manual p.19 · Key: combat.regions.arrangement.elimination</sub>

<a id="r601.3b"></a>**601.3b** In a team game, once a player's neighbouring opponents have been eliminated, that player may send attacks through allied regions into the nearest enemy region. See rule 904. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.8 · Key: combat.regions.arrangement.teams</sub>

<a id="r601.4"></a>**601.4.** A player is always present in their own region. A player who attacks into another region becomes present in that region as well, and stays present there until regroup, even if every unit they sent into it is removed. See rule 604.

> *Example: A player attacks into the opponent's region. From then until regroup, both players are present there, so a unit that dies in that region dies in front of both of them.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.19; Manual p.19; Manual p.19; Manual p.19 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 314-prophecy-units-die.test.ts, 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example test: 314-prophecy-units-die.test.ts::CR 803.7m: combat puts the attacker in the region, so both seats see every death in it · Key: combat.regions.presence</sub>

<a id="r601.4a"></a>**601.4a** Attacking is the only way a player enters another player's region. A player who declares no attack does not enter the region they could have attacked. See rule 604.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.8 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.regions.presence.only-by-attacking — a player who declares no attack does not enter the region it could have attacked · Key: combat.regions.presence.only-by-attacking</sub>

<a id="r601.4b"></a>**601.4b** Outside the battle phase, every player is alone in their own region. A player cannot interact with any other player, or with another player's units, outside the battle phase. See rules 505, 507.

> *Example: During deployment, Prismatic Observer can recall a card from its controller's own cache only. The opponent's cache is out of reach, because the opponent is not in the Observer's region.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.19; Manual p.19; Manual p.26; Manual p.42 · Tests: 293-cached-targets-are-regional.test.ts · Example test: 293-cached-targets-are-regional.test.ts::CR 403.6 the report: Prismatic Observer sacrificed in deployment cannot reach the opponent's cache · Key: combat.regions.presence.outside-battle</sub>

<a id="r601.4c"></a>**601.4c** While a player is present in a region, effects in that region can affect that player, and that player's hand, bin, cache and resources. While a player is not present, effects in that region cannot affect any of them.

> *Example: In battle, both players are present in the battle region, so Prismatic Observer may recall a card from either player's cache.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.19; Manual p.19 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-29, 2026-09-05 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 293-cached-targets-are-regional.test.ts · Example test: 293-cached-targets-are-regional.test.ts::CR 403.6 the control: in battle the Observer reaches the opponent's cache, as printed · Key: combat.regions.presence.player-things</sub>

<a id="r601.4d"></a>**601.4d** “Each opponent” and “each player” mean each such player who is present in the effect's region. If no such player is present, that part of the effect does nothing. See rule 102.

> *Example: A player sacrifices Bloated Manablub during deployment. “Each opponent loses 3 life” reaches nobody, because no opponent is in that player's region.*

> *Example: Rebalance resolves in a region where no opponent is present. No unit changes hands.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.42; Manual p.42; Manual p.42 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 158-silent-region-branches.test.ts, 208-region-scoping-is-absolute.test.ts · Example tests: 158-silent-region-branches.test.ts::Bloated Manablub — "Each opponent loses 3 life" in a region holding no opponent says so and takes no life, 208-region-scoping-is-absolute.test.ts::Rebalance — no opponent in the region: nobody is asked, no unit changes hands, and it says so · Key: combat.regions.presence.each-opponent</sub>

<a id="r601.4e"></a>**601.4e** An ally is a unit under your control in the region where the effect is happening. An enemy is a unit in that region that is not under your control. A unit in another region is neither. See rule 110.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 243-ally-and-enemy-scope.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 243-ally-and-enemy-scope.test.ts::CR 601.4e no ally or enemy slot in the pool can see a unit in another region · Key: combat.regions.presence.ally-enemy</sub>

<a id="r601.4f"></a>**601.4f** At regroup, every player and every unit returns to its own region: a unit returns to its controller's region (see rule 506). See rule 506.

> *Example: Life Plant's 1/1s, created in the enemy region during an attack, return to their controller's region at regroup.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.26 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 98-spawn-region.test.ts · Example test: 98-spawn-region.test.ts::the stranded 1/1s walk home at regroup · Key: combat.regions.presence.regroup</sub>

<a id="r601.5"></a>**601.5.** A unit or spell token created by an effect is created in the region where the effect's source is when the effect resolves. That need not be its controller's own region. See rules 602.2a, 304.

> *Example: Life Plant attacks into the opponent's region, and its controller loses life there. Its 1/1s are created in the opponent's region, not at home.*

> *Example: Tidelurker attacks and creates a 2/2 in the enemy region. That 2/2 cannot block the counterattack in its controller's own region.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.15; Rulebook 2023 p.4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 98-spawn-region.test.ts · Example tests: 98-spawn-region.test.ts::CR 601.5: report #83 — Life Plant attacking in the enemy region creates its 1/1s THERE, 98-spawn-region.test.ts::CR 304.8a inverts the withdrawn home-region reading: Tidelurker's mid-attack 2/2 stays in the enemy region and CANNOT block the counterattack · Key: combat.regions.created</sub>

<a id="r601.6"></a>**601.6.** Battle is resolved one region at a time. Once players have begun interacting inside a region, every step of battle is completed in that region before those players can interact anywhere else. See rules 505, 610.

> *Example: The non-initiative player sends a counterattacker at block time. Battle in the first region runs through to its end before the counterattack battle begins in the other region.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.21; Manual p.21 · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.regions.one-at-a-time — the first battle round runs every one of its steps in the defending region before the counterattack round begins in the other region · Key: combat.regions.one-at-a-time</sub>

<a id="r601.6a"></a>**601.6a** While battle is being resolved in a region, units in any other region are treated as if they don't exist.

> *Example: A unit with an “After combat” ability stays at home while its controller attacks. When battle ends in the opponent's region, the ability does not trigger.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.21; Manual p.21 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ after combat: the control, an after-combat unit in ANOTHER region makes nothing · Key: combat.regions.one-at-a-time.others-dont-exist</sub>

<a id="r601.6b"></a>**601.6b** Regions are resolved in clockwise order starting with the region to the left of the initiative player, so the initiative player's region resolves last. In a two-player game, battle is resolved first in the non-initiative player's region and then, if there was a counterattack, in the initiative player's region. See rules 505, 610.

> *Example: The initiative player attacks into the non-initiative player's region. After that battle, the counterattack is fought in the initiative player's region.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.21; Manual p.21; Manual p.21; Manual p.21 · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.regions.one-at-a-time.order — in a two-player game the first battle is in the non-initiative region and the counterattack battle is in the initiative region · Key: combat.regions.one-at-a-time.order</sub>

<a id="r601.7"></a>**601.7.** An “After combat” ability works for a unit that is present in the region where the battle happened, whether or not that unit is in a formation. It does not trigger in a region where no battle took place. See rule 609.

> *Example: A unit with an “After combat” ability is in the battle region but outside the formation. Its ability still triggers after combat.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1356667460211966060#0 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ after combat: an after-combat trigger fires for a unit in the battle region that is not in formation · Key: combat.regions.after-combat-presence</sub>

<a id="r601.8"></a>**601.8.** Regions limit what effects can reach and count. The printed statement that there is “zero information or interaction between regions” is read as a limit on effects: no effect carries information from one region into another. It does not hide anything from players: a player may see what happens in a region they are not present in. See rule 601.1a.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 3; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.19 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-08-29 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts, 219-region-scoped-all.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.regions.information — a log line stamped with another region is visible to both seats · Key: combat.regions.information</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U01-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r602"></a>
### 602. Formations

<a id="r602.1"></a>**602.1.** When units attack or block, they are placed in a formation. The units a player attacks with make up that player's attacking formation; the units a player blocks with make up that player's defending formation. See rules 604, 606.

> *Example: A player attacks with three units in two columns; those three units are the attacking formation. The two units the defender blocks with are the defending formation.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.22; Manual p.23 · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.formations.definition — the units declared as attackers make up the attacking formation and the units declared as blockers make up the defending formation · Key: combat.formations.definition</sub>

<a id="r602.1a"></a>**602.1a** A formation has a front row and a back row, and any number of columns. Each column of a formation holds at most two units: one in the front row and one in the back row. See rule 603.1.

> *Example: A player may attack five columns wide, but cannot put three units in one column.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.22; Manual p.22; Rulebook 2023 p.10 · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.formations.definition.shape — a formation may be many columns wide, but a column of three units is refused on either side · Key: combat.formations.definition.shape</sub>

<a id="r602.1b"></a>**602.1b** An attacking formation is set during the attack step. A defending formation is set during the block step. See rules 604, 606.

> *Example: The defender cannot declare blockers during the attack step, and the attacker cannot change the attack once the block step has begun.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.22; Rulebook 2023 p.10 · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.formations.definition.when-set — attacks are declared only in the attack step and blocks only in the block step · Key: combat.formations.definition.when-set</sub>

<a id="r602.1c"></a>**602.1c** A player's formation is that player's whole side of the battle in that region: every unit they have arrayed there, in every column. It is not a single column. An effect that targets a formation targets one player's whole side. See rule 110.

> *Example: Galactic Germination targets an attacking formation of three units in two columns. It creates three 1/1s.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts · Example test: 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts::Galactic Germination: "target formation" is THE WHOLE SIDE · Key: combat.formations.definition.whole-side</sub>

<a id="r602.1d"></a>**602.1d** A formation remains a formation for as long as its battle lasts, even when every unit in it has been removed. An effect that counts the units in an empty formation counts zero.

> *Example: Galactic Germination targets a formation, and every unit in it dies before the spell resolves. It resolves and creates no units.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts, 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example test: 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts::Galactic Germination: an EMPTY formation is still a formation · Key: combat.formations.definition.empty</sub>

<a id="r602.1e"></a>**602.1e** Once a formation is set, its units are locked in their positions until regroup, when they all leave formation. A unit's position changes only as rules 602.3–602.5 describe, or when an effect moves it. See rules 602.3, 602.4, 602.5, 506.

> *Example: Riftwalker's ability switches its position with another ally in its formation.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.22; Manual p.22; Manual p.26; card: Riftwalker · Tests: 28-metal-c.test.ts · Example test: 28-metal-c.test.ts::Riftwalker: [one] switches my position with a target ally in my formation · Key: combat.formations.definition.locked</sub>

<a id="r602.2"></a>**602.2.** A unit can be in a battle region without being in a formation. A unit outside the formation is neither attacking nor blocking.

> *Example: A defending unit stands in the battle region but is not declared as a blocker. It blocks nothing, and the unblocked attacker deals its damage to the defending player.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.15 · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.formations.outside — a defending unit in the battle region that is not in the defending formation neither blocks nor takes combat damage · Key: combat.formations.outside</sub>

<a id="r602.2a"></a>**602.2a** A unit that spawns during battle, whether created by an effect or played as a spell unit, is placed in its region outside the formation, unless the card says otherwise. See rules 602.6, 602.7.

> *Example: Aberrant Populace attacks and creates two Wisps. The Wisps are in the battle region, outside the formation.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.15; Manual p.43; Manual p.43; card: Aberrant Populace · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts, 98-spawn-region.test.ts · Example test: 08-cards2.test.ts::Aberrant Populace: attack → two Wisps out of formation · Key: combat.formations.outside.spawned</sub>

<a id="r602.2b"></a>**602.2b** A unit that comes under another player's control during a battle, after the formations are set, leaves its formation, unless the effect that changes its control itself gives it a position. It stays out of every formation for the rest of that battle, attacking and blocking for nobody, and joins its new controller's side at regroup. See rule 711.

> *Example: Download steals an enemy Robot token after blocks. The Robot leaves the formation and takes no further part in the battle.*

> *Example: At regroup, the stolen Robot joins its new controller's side.*

> *Example: After attacks, the defender casts Organic Exchange on an attacking Bubb and their own 1/1, which is in no formation. The two swap positions as the card says: the 1/1 takes Bubb's attack slot and deals the combat damage, and Bubb is in no formation.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 3; verifier ran 4 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Organic Exchange · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 145-erase-routes.test.ts, 24-wood-b.test.ts, 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example tests: 145-erase-routes.test.ts::CR 711.3 (viii): Download — a Robot token stolen mid-battle is OUT of the formation, 145-erase-routes.test.ts::CR 711.3 (ix): Download — the stolen Robot token joins its NEW controller's side at regroup, 24-wood-b.test.ts::Organic Exchange: control swaps and the attack slot passes to the exchanged unit · Key: combat.formations.outside.stolen</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U10-11 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r602.3"></a>**602.3.** The front row of a column must be filled before a unit can be placed in its back row. So a column of a formation holds no unit, one unit in its front row, or two units. It never holds a unit in its back row alone.

> *Example: While building an attack, a player puts a unit in the back slot of an empty column. When the attack is declared, that unit stands in the front row.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.22; Rulebook 2023 p.10 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 64-formation-collapse.test.ts, 55-ui-formation.test.ts · Example test: 55-ui-formation.test.ts::building an attack: a back unit with nobody in front moves up on Done · Key: combat.formations.front-first</sub>

<a id="r602.4"></a>**602.4.** If a unit in the front row of a column leaves the formation, the unit behind it moves up into the front row. This happens whenever it occurs during the battle: before blocks, after blocks and during combat damage.

> *Example: Blocks have been declared. The front unit of an attacking column dies; the unit behind it moves to the front of that column.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.22; Rulebook 2023 p.10 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 64-formation-collapse.test.ts · Example test: 64-formation-collapse.test.ts::CR 602.4 (Manual): the back row promotes AFTER blocks too · Key: combat.formations.promotion</sub>

<a id="r602.5"></a>**602.5.** If the last unit in a column of an attacking formation leaves it before blocks are declared, the columns on either side close in to fill the gap, so the line has no empty column.

> *Example: A three-column attack loses the only unit of its middle column during the attack window. The right-hand column moves left, and the line is two columns wide.*
