<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.22; Rulebook 2023 p.10; Rulebook 2023 p.10 · Tests: 64-formation-collapse.test.ts · Example test: 64-formation-collapse.test.ts::CR 602.5: a middle column emptied before blocks collapses · Key: combat.formations.collapse</sub>

<a id="r602.5a"></a>**602.5a** After blocks are declared, columns never move to fill a gap. A column emptied after blocks stays in the line as a hole for the rest of the battle, even if its blockers are removed too. See rule 608.4e.

> *Example: After blocks, the only attacker in the middle column dies. The column stays where it is, empty, and the columns to its right do not move.*

> *Example: Later in the same battle the blockers of that column die too. The hole still does not close.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.22 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 64-formation-collapse.test.ts, 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example tests: 64-formation-collapse.test.ts::CR 602.5a (Manual): after blocks are declared, an emptied column stays as a HOLE, 64-formation-collapse.test.ts::CR 602.5a (Manual): the hole is permanent · Key: combat.formations.collapse.after-blocks</sub>

<a id="r602.5b"></a>**602.5b** Rules 602.4 and 602.5 apply however a unit leaves its formation: it may die, be recalled, cached or erased, or leave in any other way.

> *Example: Before blocks, the only unit of a middle column is recalled to its owner's hand. The line closes up just as it would after a death.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.22; Manual p.22 · Tests: 64-formation-collapse.test.ts · Example test: 64-formation-collapse.test.ts::CR 602.5b: a unit RECALLED out of a middle column closes the gap too · Key: combat.formations.collapse.any-removal</sub>

<a id="r602.5c"></a>**602.5c** A formation closes up immediately when a unit leaves it, as a state-based action. An ability that triggers on that unit leaving play sees the formation already closed up. See rule 713.

> *Example: Before blocks, the only unit of a middle column dies. By the time any ability that triggers on the death looks at the formation, the gap has already closed.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 64-formation-collapse.test.ts · Example test: 64-formation-collapse.test.ts::CR 602.5c: the gap is closed before any observer runs · Key: combat.formations.collapse.immediate</sub>

<a id="r602.5d"></a>**602.5d** A defending formation may have empty columns, and they are never closed up. See rule 606.

> *Example: The defender blocks the first and third attacking columns and leaves the second unblocked. The defending formation keeps its gap.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.23; Rulebook 2023 p.11 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 66-formation-placement.test.ts · Example test: 66-formation-placement.test.ts::CR 602.5d: a blocking formation may legitimately have EMPTY columns · Key: combat.formations.collapse.defending</sub>

<a id="r602.6"></a>**602.6.** When an effect creates a unit, or puts one into play, “in my formation” or “in formation” without naming a position, the effect's controller chooses the position as the effect resolves.

> *Example: Hooba-Lin's host attacks, and its trigger creates a 1/1 “in my formation”. As the trigger resolves, Hooba-Lin's controller chooses where in the formation the 1/1 goes.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 66-formation-placement.test.ts, 108-formation-class.test.ts · Example test: 108-formation-class.test.ts::BL-24 Hooba-Lin (augment): the host attacks → the ask, and the 1/1 lands in the chosen slot · Key: combat.formations.placement</sub>

<a id="r602.6a"></a>**602.6a** The positions such a unit may take are: a new column at either end of the line; the back slot of any column that holds exactly one unit; and the front slot of a hole left after blocks (rule 602.5a). See rules 602.5a, 602.6k.

> *Example: An attacking line has two columns, the first with two units and the second with one. The legal positions are a new column at the left end, the back slot of the second column, and a new column at the right end.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 66-formation-placement.test.ts · Example test: 66-formation-placement.test.ts::CR 602.6a: a two-unit column offers no back slot · Demonstrated by test: 66-formation-placement.test.ts::CR 602.6a: a placement can FILL a CR 602.5a hole, and can never create one · Key: combat.formations.placement.legal-positions</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U10-4 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r602.6b"></a>**602.6b** “Either side of the existing units” means the two ends of the line. A unit is never put into a new column between two existing columns.

> *Example: An attacking line has three columns. A unit placed “in my formation” may open a new column at the left or right end, but never between the first and second columns.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 66-formation-placement.test.ts · Example test: 66-formation-placement.test.ts::CR 602.6b: "either side" means the two ENDS · Key: combat.formations.placement.ends-only</sub>

<a id="r602.6c"></a>**602.6c** A defending formation never gains a new column at its ends this way. A unit placed into a defending formation may go into the back slot of a blocking column that holds one unit. After blocks have been declared, and until combat damage has been dealt, it may also stand in front of an attacking column that still has an attacker and no blocker, and that column is then blocked (see rule 606). See rules 606, 607, 602.6j.

> *Example: The defender's only blocking column already holds two units. An effect that puts a unit into the defender's formation has no position for it.*

> *Example: After blocks, the defender plays Tiderunner Initiate in front of an unblocked attacker. That column is now blocked, and the attacker deals its combat damage to the Tiderunner.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 3; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1366447016653361192#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22, 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 66-formation-placement.test.ts, 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts, 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example tests: 66-formation-placement.test.ts::CR 602.6c: a full BLOCKING formation offers nothing, 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts::CR 608.4d a Tiderunner put in front of an unblocked attacker fights it · Key: combat.formations.placement.defending</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U10-4, D-U11-5 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r602.6d"></a>**602.6d** If exactly one position is legal, the unit goes there and no choice is asked. If no position is legal, the effect places nothing.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 66-formation-placement.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 66-formation-placement.test.ts::CR 602.6d: exactly one legal placement is auto-picked · Key: combat.formations.placement.one-or-none</sub>

<a id="r602.6e"></a>**602.6e** “My formation” means the formation the effect's source is in. If the source is in play but not in any formation when the effect resolves, the effect places nothing and creates nothing. See rule 602.2b.

> *Example: Hooba-Lin's host attacks, then is stolen before the trigger resolves, so it is in play but out of the formation. No 1/1 is created.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 108-formation-class.test.ts · Example test: 108-formation-class.test.ts::CR 602.6e Hooba-Lin: alive but out of the formation (CR 711.3) → no token, no question · Key: combat.formations.placement.source-formation</sub>

<a id="r602.6f"></a>**602.6f** If the effect's source has left play while its effect is on the stack, “my formation” means the formation the source was in when it left play, and the effect still places the unit there. See rules 714, 602.6k. *(Engine differs, see F-U10-6.)*

> *Example: Hooba-Lin attacks and is killed with its trigger on the stack. The 1/1 is still created, in the formation Hooba-Lin was in.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 3; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1353895783266516992#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 108-formation-class.test.ts, 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example test: 108-formation-class.test.ts::CR 714.4 Hooba-Lin: killed under its own attack trigger · Key: combat.formations.placement.source-gone</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U10-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r602.6g"></a>**602.6g** An effect whose text says “if I am still in formation” does nothing if its source is no longer in the formation when the effect resolves, including when the source has left play.

> *Example: Hooba-Nan attacks and is killed with its trigger on the stack. The trigger creates no 1/1s.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Hooba-Nan; card: Rousing Spirit · Designer: RAQ 1353895783266516992#1 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ dead unit: Hooba-Nan gone with its trigger on the stack makes nothing · Key: combat.formations.placement.still-in-formation</sub>

<a id="r602.6h"></a>**602.6h** An amount that counts units in “my formation” is counted as the effect resolves. Units that have left the formation by then are not counted. If the source itself has left play, the amount counts the formation it was in. See rule 603.2d.

> *Example: Embermaw Fledgling attacks and dies in combat. Its after-combat trigger still counts the attacking units of the formation it was in.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Embermaw Fledgling · Designer: RAQ 1353895783266516992#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 401-raq-fix-stack.test.ts · Example test: 401-raq-fix-stack.test.ts::CR 714.4 Embermaw Fledgling gone before its after-combat trigger resolves · Key: combat.formations.placement.counting</sub>

<a id="r602.6i"></a>**602.6i** If an effect lets a player play a spell unit into a formation (as Hooba-Pon does), the spell part happens first. If it resolves, the unit then spawns into the formation. See rule 303.

> *Example: Hooba-Pon attacks and its controller plays a spell unit from hand through it. The spell resolves, and then the unit appears in the chosen position.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Hooba-Pon · Designer: RAQ 1461450216874967235#0 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Hooba-Pon spell unit: the spell part happens, then the unit spawns into the formation · Key: combat.formations.placement.spell-unit</sub>

<a id="r602.6j"></a>**602.6j** After blocks, while the defending formation still holds at least one unit, a unit placed into it may also take the front slot of a blocking column whose blockers have all left it. The unit then blocks that column. See rules 602.6c, 602.6a, 602.6k.

> *Example: The defender's only blocker in the second column dies after blocks. An effect that puts a unit into the defender's formation may put it in front of the second attacking column.*

<sub>Basis: Engine only · Verified: confirmed in round 3; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Engine: formationSlots · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.formations.placement.defending-emptied-block — after blocks a blocking column whose blocker died offers its front slot, and a unit placed there blocks that column · Key: combat.formations.placement.defending-emptied-block</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U10-9 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r602.6k"></a>**602.6k** A player with no unit standing in a formation in the battle, because they have not formed one or because every unit in it has left, is offered no position in it, not even a hole, and a unit cannot be played or placed into it. Rules 602.6c and 602.6f are the exceptions. See rules 602.1d, 602.6f, 602.7c, 602.6c.

> *Example: The attacker has attacked and the defender has not yet declared blocks. The defender stands in no formation, so an effect that puts a unit into the defender's formation has nowhere to put it.*

> *Example: After blocks, every attacking unit dies. The attacker then plays Tiderunner Initiate; it cannot be played into the attacking line, not even into a hole, and enters play outside any formation.*

> *Example: The defender declares no blockers. An effect that puts a unit into the defender's formation may still put it in front of the unblocked attacking column (rule 602.6c); the attacker is offered no such spot.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22, 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: partial in round 3; verifier ran 4 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Tests: 66-formation-placement.test.ts, 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts, 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example tests: 66-formation-placement.test.ts::CR 602.6k: a formation you are not standing in cannot be joined at all, 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.formations.placement.empty-formation — after blocks every attacking unit dies, the attacker is offered no position, not even the hole, and Tiderunner Initiate enters play outside any formation, 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts::CR 607.2c the attacker is never offered a blocking spot · Key: combat.formations.placement.empty-formation</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U10-10 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r602.7"></a>**602.7.** Some cards say they may be played into a formation (Tiderunner Initiate, Trench Stalker). The position is chosen as the card is cast, from the positions rule 602.6 allows, and the unit is already in that position when it enters play. See rules 602.6, 702.

> *Example: Tiderunner Initiate's spot is asked for while it is being cast, and it enters play already standing in that spot.*

> *Example: No moment exists in which the Tiderunner is in the region but outside the formation, so the opponent cannot respond to it there.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Tiderunner Initiate; card: Trench Stalker · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 108-formation-class.test.ts, 73-play-into-formation.test.ts · Example tests: 108-formation-class.test.ts::BL-24 Tiderunner Initiate: the spot is asked in the CAST window, 73-play-into-formation.test.ts::CR 602.7 the opponent’s response window cannot catch it outside the line · Key: combat.formations.play-into</sub>

<a id="r602.7a"></a>**602.7a** If the chosen position no longer exists when the card resolves, the unit enters play in the region, outside the formation.

> *Example: Tiderunner Initiate is cast to go behind an attacker, and the attacker dies before it resolves. The Tiderunner enters the region outside the formation.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 73-play-into-formation.test.ts · Example test: 73-play-into-formation.test.ts::CR 602.7a the slot is RE-DERIVED at resolution · Key: combat.formations.play-into.spot-gone</sub>

<a id="r602.7b"></a>**602.7b** Playing such a card into the formation is optional. Its controller may instead play it so that it enters the region outside the formation.

> *Example: When casting Tiderunner Initiate, its controller may choose to have it stay out of the formation.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Tiderunner Initiate · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 73-play-into-formation.test.ts · Example test: 73-play-into-formation.test.ts::CR 602.7b "stay out of formation" is still on the menu · Key: combat.formations.play-into.optional</sub>

<a id="r602.7c"></a>**602.7c** Such a card can be played into a formation only if its controller has a formation in that battle that still holds at least one unit: they attacked, or they declared blocks, and not every unit in it has left. As an exception, after blocks are declared and until combat damage has been dealt, the defending player may play it in front of an unblocked attacking column (rule 602.6c) even if they declared no blockers. Otherwise it is played normally, outside any formation. See rules 602.6c, 602.6k.

> *Example: Before blocks, the defending player has no formation. They cast Tiderunner Initiate; nothing is asked and it enters play outside any formation.*

> *Example: After blocks, the defender plays a unit in front of an unblocked attacking column. That column is blocked, and stays blocked when the unit is removed.*

> *Example: After blocks, every attacking unit dies. The attacker plays Tiderunner Initiate; nothing is asked and it enters play outside any formation.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-08-22, 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 3; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Tests: 73-play-into-formation.test.ts, 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts, 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example tests: 73-play-into-formation.test.ts::CR 602.7c with NO formation of your own the play is legal and asks nothing, 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Blocked: a unit played in as a blocker after blocks blocks that column, 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.formations.play-into.needs-formation — after blocks every attacker dies, and the attacker casts Tiderunner Initiate: nothing is asked and it enters play outside any formation · Key: combat.formations.play-into.needs-formation</sub>

<a id="r603"></a>
### 603. Columns, Adjacency and Edges

<a id="r603.1"></a>**603.1.** A column is one file of the battle line: the attacking units in it and the defending units placed in front of it. Each side of a column holds at most two units. A defending unit placed in front of an attacking column blocks that whole column. See rules 602.1a, 606, 608.1c.

> *Example: One unit blocks a column of two attackers. Neither attacker deals damage to the defending player.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.23; Manual p.23; Manual p.23 · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.columns.definition — one blocker in front of a two-unit attacking column blocks the whole column, so neither attacker damages the defending player · Key: combat.columns.definition</sub>

<a id="r603.1a"></a>**603.1a** Combat attributes are shared by the units in the same column of a formation, and are not shared with units to their left or right (see rule 802.1). See rules 802.1, 712.

> *Example: A unit with Flying attacks in the front of a column. The unit behind it has Flying too; the unit in the next column does not.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.24; Manual p.24; Manual p.24 · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.columns.definition.shared-attributes — Flying on the front unit of a column is shared with the unit behind it and not with the unit in the next column · Key: combat.columns.definition.shared-attributes</sub>

<a id="r603.1b"></a>**603.1b** A defending unit may also block in a column where there is no attacker (a side-block). Side-block columns stand beside the attacking line, on either side of it (see rule 606). Any number of units may side-block, and each may stand in a column of its own. See rule 606.

> *Example: Two defending units block where no attacker is, each in its own column beside the attack.*

> *Example: A single 2/5 attacks; the defender side-blocks to its left with a 1/1. The 1/1 stands in a new column left of the attack, the attacking column stays unblocked, and it deals 2 to the defender.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.23; Manual p.23 · Designer: RAQ 1366447016653361192#3 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts · Example tests: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts::side-blocks: two units block where no attacker is, each its own column, 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts::CR 606.4a a side-block on the left opens a column before column 1 · Key: combat.columns.definition.side-blocks</sub>

<a id="r603.1c"></a>**603.1c** Two side-blocking units may stand in the same side-block column, one in its front slot and one in its back slot. See rule 603.1b.

<sub>Basis: Engine only · Verified: confirmed in round 3; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Engine: checkBlocks · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.columns.definition.side-block-shared-column — two units side-block in one column beside the attack, one in the front slot and one in the back slot · Key: combat.columns.definition.side-block-shared-column</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U10-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r603.2"></a>**603.2.** A unit in a formation is adjacent to its left, right, front and back neighbours in that formation. *(Engine differs, see F-U10-3.)*

> *Example: Inspiration gives +2/+2 to its controller's units adjacent to it in formation, and to no others.*

> *Example: The defender blocks the first and third attacking columns and leaves the second unblocked. The two blockers are not neighbours, so an Inspiration in one does not buff the other.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.22; Rulebook 2023 p.10; Manual p.23 · Tests: 23-wood-a.test.ts, 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example test: 23-wood-a.test.ts::Inspiration: +2/+2 to your units adjacent to it in formation · Key: combat.columns.adjacency</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U10-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r603.2a"></a>**603.2a** A unit in a formation has at most three adjacent positions: the same row of the column to its left, the same row of the column to its right, and the other slot of its own column. The other row of a neighbouring column is diagonal, and is not adjacent. Where a line ends, there is a position past the end only as rule 603.3 allows. See rule 603.3. *(Engine differs, see F-U10-3.)*

> *Example: Hooba-Nan stands in the front row of a middle column. Its adjacent slots are the front rows of the columns on either side and the slot behind it, and nothing diagonal.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.22 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 66-formation-placement.test.ts, 23-wood-a.test.ts, 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example test: 23-wood-a.test.ts::Hooba-Nan in the middle: both sides and below, and nothing diagonal · Key: combat.columns.adjacency.positions</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U10-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r603.2b"></a>**603.2b** Adjacency exists only in a formation. A unit that is not in a formation has no adjacent units and no adjacent slots.

> *Example: During deployment, Throwing Boulder stands in its region beside an allied unit, but neither is in a formation. Its ability (“only if I have an adjacent ally”) cannot be activated.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.22; Manual p.22 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 66-formation-placement.test.ts, 18-earth-c.test.ts · Example test: 18-earth-c.test.ts::CR 111.7b: out of formation there are no adjacent slots at all · Key: combat.columns.adjacency.only-in-formation</sub>

<a id="r603.2c"></a>**603.2c** An amount based on adjacency, such as the number of adjacent allies, is counted as the effect resolves. See rule 706.

> *Example: Flamebreath Initiate attacks with one ally in the column beside it. X is 1, so it creates a Fireball 2. Attacking alone, X is 0 and the Fireball is 1.*

> *Example: Flamebreath Initiate attacks beside an ally, and the ally is destroyed while the trigger waits. X is 0 when the trigger resolves.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Flamebreath Initiate · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 11-fire-wood.test.ts, 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example tests: 11-fire-wood.test.ts::Flamebreath Initiate: attack → Fireball X+1, X = adjacent allies, 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.columns.adjacency.at-resolution — Flamebreath Initiate attacks beside an ally, the ally is destroyed while the trigger waits, and X is 0 when it resolves · Key: combat.columns.adjacency.at-resolution</sub>

<a id="r603.2d"></a>**603.2d** A unit that has left play has no adjacent units. If it left play with its effect on the stack, an amount counting the units adjacent to it is 0. See rules 602.6f, 714.

> *Example: Flamebreath Initiate attacks and is removed with its trigger on the stack. X is 0, so the trigger still creates a Fireball 1.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353895783266516992#3 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ dead unit: Flamebreath Initiate removed before its trigger resolves · Key: combat.columns.adjacency.left-play</sub>

<a id="r603.3"></a>**603.3.** The empty column just past each end of an attacking line exists. For a unit in the front row at either end of an attacking line, the front-row slot of a new column past that end is an adjacent slot.

> *Example: Hooba-Nan stands alone in an attacking line. Its trigger creates three 1/1s: one in a new column on each side and one behind it.*

> *Example: Hooba-Nan is at the right end of a longer line, with a unit to its left. Its trigger creates two 1/1s: one in a new column past the right end and one behind it.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 66-formation-placement.test.ts, 23-wood-a.test.ts · Example tests: 23-wood-a.test.ts::Hooba-Nan alone: behind it AND a new column past each end, 23-wood-a.test.ts::Hooba-Nan on the edge of the line: the open side and behind · Key: combat.columns.edges</sub>

<a id="r603.3a"></a>**603.3a** Past the end of the line, only the front-row slot is adjacent. A unit in the back row at the end of the line has no adjacent slot past that end, because the front row must be filled first (rule 602.3). See rule 602.3.

> *Example: Hooba-Nan stands in the back row of the column at the end of the line. Its trigger creates no 1/1 past the edge.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 23-wood-a.test.ts · Example test: 23-wood-a.test.ts::Hooba-Nan in the BACK row at the edge · Key: combat.columns.edges.front-only</sub>

<a id="r603.3b"></a>**603.3b** A defending formation has no adjacent slots past its ends.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 66-formation-placement.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 66-formation-placement.test.ts::CR 603.3 adjacency: a BACK-row unit and a BLOCKING line have nothing past the edge · Key: combat.columns.edges.attacking-only</sub>

<a id="r603.4"></a>**603.4.** Text that names positions relative to the unit itself, such as “my empty adjacent slots” or “the empty slot behind me”, refers to exactly those positions. Its controller does not choose among positions as they do under rule 602.6. See rule 602.6.

> *Example: Rousing Spirit attacks, and a cheap unit from its controller's bin is put into the empty slot behind it.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Hooba-Nan; card: Rousing Spirit · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 13-fire-b.test.ts, 23-wood-a.test.ts · Example test: 13-fire-b.test.ts::Rousing Spirit: attack → a cheap bin unit fills the slot behind me · Key: combat.columns.positional-text</sub>

<a id="r603.5"></a>**603.5.** A formation can grow at either end without limit.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.22; Manual p.22; Rulebook 2023 p.10 · Tests: 66-formation-placement.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 66-formation-placement.test.ts::CR 603.5: formations scale infinitely in width · Key: combat.columns.width</sub>

<a id="r603.5a"></a>**603.5a** When the columns of a line move (a new column opens at the left end, or the line closes up under rule 602.5), each block and each effect that applies to a particular column moves with that column.

> *Example: A new column opens at the left end of a line that has already been blocked. Every blocker still blocks the same attackers as before.*

> *Example: A Swift column led by Dune Drifter has already dealt its damage first. Its controller then plays Tiderunner Initiate into a new column on the left; the Drifter's column shifts right but still counts as having struck, so it does not deal damage again.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Tests: 66-formation-placement.test.ts, 64-formation-collapse.test.ts, 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts · Example tests: 66-formation-placement.test.ts::CR 603.5a: opening a column on the LEFT re-keys every block and every column counter, 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts::CR 608.2e a struck mark moves with its column when a new column opens on the left · Demonstrated by test: 64-formation-collapse.test.ts::CR 603.5a: a column-scoped battle counter rides the collapse to the new index · Key: combat.columns.width.columns-keep-identity</sub>

<a id="r604"></a>
### 604. Attacking

<a id="r604.1"></a>**604.1.** Attacking is how a player brings units, and the spell tokens that travel with them, into a neighbouring enemy region for battle. Attacks are declared in the attack step, the first step of a battle round (see 505). See rules 505, 601.

> *Example: The initiative player declares an attack with one unit. That unit moves into the other player's region, and at regroup it returns home.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.20; Manual p.20; Manual p.20 · Tests: 02-combat.test.ts, 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Example test: 02-combat.test.ts::1v1 counterattack: NIT sends units at block time, they attack in round 2 · Key: combat.attack.general</sub>

<a id="r604.1a"></a>**604.1a** Units attack players directly. They do not attack individual units unless a spell directs them to. See rule 608.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.20 · Tests: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.pairing — an unblocked attacking column hits the player · Key: combat.attack.general.players</sub>

<a id="r604.1b"></a>**604.1b** In a two-player game and in team games, each team gets one chance to attack per turn. In the first battle round the initiative player attacks into the non-initiative player's region; in the second battle round the non-initiative player attacks with the units it sent to counterattack or, if the first round had no attack, with any of its units (see 505, 610 and rule 604.4a). See rules 505, 610, 604.4a.

> *Example: The initiative player attacks with a 2/2. The non-initiative player sends a 4/3 to counterattack while declaring blocks. After the first round's combat, the 4/3 attacks in the second round.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.20; Manual p.20; Rulebook 2023 p.5; Manual p.20 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 02-combat.test.ts, 396-raq-timing.test.ts, 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Example test: 02-combat.test.ts::1v1 counterattack: NIT sends units at block time, they attack in round 2 · Key: combat.attack.general.rounds</sub>

<a id="r604.2"></a>**604.2.** To attack, the attacking player chooses which of its units go and places them in an attacking formation (see 602). The attacking formation is set in the attack step, and from then on its units are locked in position. See rule 602.

> *Example: A player with three units attacks with two of them, side by side in two columns. The third stays at home.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.22; Manual p.22 · Tests: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Example test: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts::cr:combat.attack.declaring — a player with three units attacks with two side by side; the third stays home, and the formation cannot be declared again · Key: combat.attack.declaring</sub>

<a id="r604.2a"></a>**604.2a** Attacking is optional: a player may declare no attack. The exception is a counterattack: a sent counterattacker that is still able to attack must attack (see rule 610.4e). See rule 604.4.

> *Example: The initiative player has a unit that could attack and declares no attack. The battle moves to the second round.*

> *Example: The non-initiative player sent three units to counterattack. In round 2, declaring no attack is refused.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.20 · Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts, 479-empty-attack-and-committed-counterattack.test.ts · Example tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Temporal Rift thread: the non-initiative player still attacks when the initiative player declines, 479-empty-attack-and-committed-counterattack.test.ts::CT-298 every sent counterattacker must be in the formation and the counterattack cannot be declined · Key: combat.attack.declaring.optional</sub>

<a id="r604.2b"></a>**604.2b** There is no summoning sickness. A unit may attack, or block, however recently it entered play. See rules 504, 606.2a.

> *Example: A 2/2 enters play during the battle phase, just before attacks are declared. It may attack at once, and it deals 2 to the defending player.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.43; Manual p.43 · Tests: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Example test: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts::cr:combat.attack.declaring.no-summoning-sickness — a unit that entered play during the battle phase, before the declaration, may attack · Key: combat.attack.declaring.no-summoning-sickness</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U11-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r604.2c"></a>**604.2c** Spell tokens may go with an attack, but only together with at least one unit, and only spell tokens the attacking player controls in the region the attack leaves from. Spell tokens sent with a counterattack are not optional in round 2: they must ride (see rule 610.3). See rules 304, 606.5a.

> *Example: A player sending a counterattack names a Poison token and no unit when declaring blocks. The declaration is refused.*

> *Example: A player declares an attack naming a Poison token and no unit. The Poison does not go: with no unit, the declaration is no attack at all.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 4 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.15; Manual p.15; Rulebook 2023 p.4 · Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16; Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts, 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts, 479-empty-attack-and-committed-counterattack.test.ts · Example tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts::CR 604.2c: spell tokens still travel only with units, and only from the region they stand in, 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts::cr:combat.attack.declaring.spell-tokens — an attack naming a spell token and no unit is not refused: it is taken as declining to attack, and the token stays home · Key: combat.attack.declaring.spell-tokens</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U11-10 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r604.2d"></a>**604.2d** Bringing a spell token into another region with an attack cannot be undone. See rule 304.

> *Example: A Poison token goes along with an attack into the enemy region. In the counterattack, fought in its owner home region, the token is still in the enemy region and cannot be cast.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.4 · Tests: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Example test: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts::cr:combat.attack.declaring.tokens-irreversible — a spell token brought along with an attack stays in that region for the rest of the battle and cannot be cast back home in the counterattack · Key: combat.attack.declaring.tokens-irreversible</sub>

<a id="r604.2e"></a>**604.2e** A unit targeted by an Alluring trigger may not be declared as an attacker, or sent to counterattack, for the rest of the battle phase (see 802.15). See rules 802.15, 610.

> *Example: An Alluring attacker targets a defending unit. That unit cannot be sent out to counterattack when blocks are declared.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Example test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::CR 604.2e: a lured unit cannot be sent out to counterattack · Demonstrated by test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::CR 604.2e: a lured unit may not be declared as an attacker (a guard, by hand) · Key: combat.attack.declaring.lured</sub>

<a id="r604.2f"></a>**604.2f** In the second battle round, the attacking player may attack only with the units it sent to counterattack in the first round, unless the first round had no attack (see 604 and 610). Every sent unit still there and able to attack must be in the formation, and every spell token sent with them must ride along; only the formation's shape is chosen (see rule 610.4b). See rules 610, 604.4a.

> *Example: The non-initiative player sent one unit to counterattack and kept another at home. In the second round, only the sent unit may attack.*

> *Example: Three units were sent. Attacking with only two of them is refused; any formation holding all three is accepted.*

> *Example: A Fireball token sent with the counterattack is left behind: the declaration is refused.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 5 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.20 · Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16; Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 02-combat.test.ts, 21-fixes.test.ts, 479-empty-attack-and-committed-counterattack.test.ts · Example tests: 02-combat.test.ts::1v1 counterattack: NIT sends units at block time, they attack in round 2, 479-empty-attack-and-committed-counterattack.test.ts::CT-298 every sent counterattacker must be in the formation and the counterattack cannot be declined, 479-empty-attack-and-committed-counterattack.test.ts::CT-298 every sent spell token must ride with a counterattack of several units · Key: combat.attack.declaring.round-two</sub>

<a id="r604.3"></a>**604.3.** When an attack is declared, the attacking units, and the spell tokens with them, move into the region attacked. They remain there until the regroup phase, when they return to their own region (see 506). See rules 506, 601.

> *Example: A unit that counterattacked into the initiative player's region is back in its own region once regroup is over.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.20; Rulebook 2023 p.9; Manual p.27 · Tests: 02-combat.test.ts · Example test: 02-combat.test.ts::1v1 counterattack: NIT sends units at block time, they attack in round 2 · Key: combat.attack.effects</sub>

<a id="r604.3a"></a>**604.3a** Once a player has sent attacking units into an enemy region, that player is present there and may interact with things in that region using spells and effects (see 601). See rule 601.

> *Example: After an attack, both players are present in the battle region, so each sees every death in it.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.20; Manual p.20 · Tests: 314-prophecy-units-die.test.ts · Example test: 314-prophecy-units-die.test.ts::CR 803.7m: combat puts the attacker in the region, so both seats see every death in it · Key: combat.attack.effects.presence</sub>

<a id="r604.3b"></a>**604.3b** The units in the attacking formation are the attacking units. A unit that arrives in the battle region outside the formation, such as one created there during the battle, is not attacking. See rules 602, 607.2.

> *Example: Aberrant Populace attacks and creates two Wisps. The Wisps are in the battle region but not in the formation, so they are not attacking.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.15; Manual p.15; card: Aberrant Populace · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts · Example test: 08-cards2.test.ts::Aberrant Populace: attack → two Wisps out of formation · Key: combat.attack.effects.attacking-units</sub>

<a id="r604.3c"></a>**604.3c** Abilities that trigger when a unit attacks trigger as the attack is declared. They are put on the stack before the attack window opens, so players can respond to them in that window (see 605 and 706). See rules 605, 706, 802.15.

> *Example: Tempest Wrangler attacks and its Alluring trigger goes on the stack. In the attack window the defending player negates it with Containment Protocol, and no unit is lured.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Palewing · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 108-formation-class.test.ts, 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ trigger-like attributes: Containment Protocol negates a waiting Alluring trigger · Demonstrated by test: 108-formation-class.test.ts::BL-24 Hooba-Bot (played as a unit): attack → the ask · Key: combat.attack.effects.triggers</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U11-9 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r604.3d"></a>**604.3d** A unit attacks alone when it is the only unit in its attacking formation. Spell tokens that travel with it do not count as company. See rule 802.14.

> *Example: Whispering Mantid (Sneaky) attacking by itself cannot be blocked; attacking beside another unit, it can.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Surly Stalker · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts · Example test: 08-cards2.test.ts::Whispering Mantid: Sneaky — unblockable only when attacking alone (CR 802.14) · Key: combat.attack.effects.alone</sub>

<a id="r604.4"></a>**604.4.** If the attacking player declares no attack, there is no combat in that round: no attack window, no block step, no block window, no combat damage step and no after combat step. A counterattack cannot be declined this way while a sent counterattacker is able to attack (see rule 610.4e). See rules 505, 609.

> *Example: Both players decline to attack. The whole battle phase passes with no priority window at all.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.20 · Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16; Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 165-token-loss-warning.test.ts, 479-empty-attack-and-committed-counterattack.test.ts · Example test: 165-token-loss-warning.test.ts::[CT-55] a battle both players decline opens no priority window at all · Key: combat.attack.decline</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U11-1, D-U11-11 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r604.4a"></a>**604.4a** If the initiative player declares no attack in the first battle round, the non-initiative player may still attack in the second battle round, and may attack with any of its units. See rule 610.

> *Example: The initiative player declines to attack. The non-initiative player, who sent nobody to counterattack, attacks in the second round with a unit that stayed at home.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.20 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts, 21-fixes.test.ts, 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Temporal Rift thread: the non-initiative player still attacks when the initiative player declines · Key: combat.attack.decline.next-round</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U13-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r605"></a>
### 605. Attack Window

<a id="r605.1"></a>**605.1.** The attack window is the priority window that follows the declaration of an attack, in the region attacked. See rule 703.

> *Example: An attack is declared. Priority goes to the initiative player, then to the other player; when both pass, the step moves on.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.20; Manual p.27; Rulebook 2023 p.13 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.priority.window — in an empty attack window each player receives priority in turn · Key: combat.attack-window.general</sub>

<a id="r605.1a"></a>**605.1a** The initiative player receives priority first in the attack window (see 703). See rule 703.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.30; Rulebook 2023 p.13 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts, 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.priority.window — in an empty attack window each player receives priority in turn · Key: combat.attack-window.general.initiative-first</sub>

<a id="r605.1b"></a>**605.1b** When all players pass priority in succession with the stack empty, the attack window ends and the block step begins (see 606). See rules 606, 703.

> *Example: Luminous Arc is cast in the attack window; two passes resolve it and a new window opens. Two more passes on the empty stack end the attack window.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.13 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.priority.window.resolve — two passes resolve the top item · Key: combat.attack-window.general.end</sub>

<a id="r605.1c"></a>**605.1c** Until blocks are declared, a column of the attacking formation that loses its last unit closes up: the columns on its sides move in to fill the gap (see 602). See rules 602, 607.1b.

> *Example: The middle column of a three-column attack is killed in the block step, before blocks are declared. The right-hand column slides left into the gap, and the attack is two columns wide.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.22; Rulebook 2023 p.10 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 64-formation-collapse.test.ts, 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Example test: 64-formation-collapse.test.ts::CR 602.5: a middle column emptied before blocks collapses · Key: combat.attack-window.general.gravity</sub>

<a id="r605.1d"></a>**605.1d** If every attacking unit is removed during the attack window, the attacking player is still present in the region for the rest of the battle phase. See rules 601, 606.7.

> *Example: The only attacker is destroyed in the attack window. Its controller may still cast spells in that region later in the battle phase.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.19; Manual p.19 · Tests: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Example test: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts::cr:combat.attack-window.general.still-present — the attacking player stays present after its only attacker is destroyed in the attack window · Key: combat.attack-window.general.still-present</sub>

<a id="r606"></a>
### 606. Blocking

<a id="r606.1"></a>**606.1.** Blocking is how a player who has been attacked defends. In the block step, the defending player may place its units in front of the attacking formation. See rules 602, 608.

> *Example: Two columns attack, a 3/5 and a 4/5; the defending player places a 2/5 in front of the 3/5. That column is blocked and the two units deal damage to each other; the unblocked 4/5 hits the player.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.23; Manual p.23; Manual p.23 · Tests: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Example test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.pairing — an unblocked attacking column hits the player · Key: combat.blocks.general</sub>

<a id="r606.1a"></a>**606.1a** The blocking units form the defending formation. Like any formation, it has a front row and a back row (see 602). See rule 602.

> *Example: Two units block one attacking column, one in the front row and one behind it. The attacker damages the front one.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.23; Manual p.22 · Tests: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Example test: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts::cr:combat.blocks.general.formation — two blockers in one column stand front and back: they are adjacent to each other and the front one takes the damage · Key: combat.blocks.general.formation</sub>

<a id="r606.1b"></a>**606.1b** Unlike an attacking formation, the defending formation may have empty columns: the defending player need not block every attacking column, and an empty blocking column is never closed up. See rule 602.

> *Example: Against a three-column attack, the defending player blocks only the third column. The first two columns are unblocked, and the attack stays three columns wide.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.11; Manual p.23 · Tests: 66-formation-placement.test.ts, 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Example test: 66-formation-placement.test.ts::CR 602.5d: a blocking formation may legitimately have EMPTY columns · Key: combat.blocks.general.empty-columns</sub>

<a id="r606.1c"></a>**606.1c** The defending player may declare no blockers at all.

> *Example: The defending player declares no blocks and sends a unit to counterattack; the attacker's unblocked column hits the defending player.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.23 · Tests: 02-combat.test.ts · Example test: 02-combat.test.ts::1v1 counterattack: NIT sends units at block time, they attack in round 2 · Key: combat.blocks.general.none</sub>

<a id="r606.1d"></a>**606.1d** Blocks are declared once. Once declared, the defending formation is set and its units are locked in position. A unit can join it later only by an effect that puts a unit into formation (see 607). See rules 602, 607.2.

> *Example: After declaring blocks, the defending player cannot declare them again to move a blocker from one column to another.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.22; Manual p.22 · Tests: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Example test: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts::cr:combat.blocks.general.locked — blocks cannot be declared a second time in the block window · Key: combat.blocks.general.locked</sub>

<a id="r606.1e"></a>**606.1e** A blocking unit stands in one slot of the defending formation, so it blocks only the attacking column it stands in front of. See rule 602.

> *Example: One blocker cannot block two attacking columns at once; to block both, the defending player needs a unit in front of each.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.23 · Engine: apply.ts:checkBlocks · Tests: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Example test: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts::cr:combat.blocks.general.one-column — one unit may not block two attacking columns · Key: combat.blocks.general.one-column</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U11-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r606.1f"></a>**606.1f** An empty blocking column keeps its place in the defending formation. Two blockers with an empty blocking column between them are not neighbours, so they are not adjacent (see 603). See rules 603, 606.4g. *(Engine differs, see F-U11-3.)*

> *Example: Against a three-column attack, the defending player blocks the first and third columns. The two blockers are not adjacent: the empty middle blocking column lies between them.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.22; Manual p.23 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Key: combat.blocks.general.gap-adjacency</sub>

<a id="r606.2"></a>**606.2.** The defending player may block with units it controls in the battle region. See rule 601.

> *Example: A unit created in the enemy region during the first round's attack is not in its controller's region when the counterattack arrives, so it cannot block it.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.23 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 98-spawn-region.test.ts · Example test: 98-spawn-region.test.ts::CR 304.8a inverts the withdrawn home-region reading: Tidelurker's mid-attack 2/2 stays in the enemy region and CANNOT block the counterattack · Key: combat.blocks.who</sub>

<a id="r606.2a"></a>**606.2a** A unit may block however recently it entered play (see 604). See rule 604.2b.

> *Example: A unit that entered the defending player's region during the attack window may be declared as a blocker.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.43 · Tests: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Example test: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts::cr:combat.blocks.who.recent — a unit that entered the defending region during the attack window may block · Key: combat.blocks.who.recent</sub>

<a id="r606.2b"></a>**606.2b** Whether a unit is able to block a column depends only on that unit and that column. It never depends on what the defending player chose to do with its other units, except where two Alluring duties name the same unit (see 802.15). See rule 802.15.

> *Example: An Alluring column lures a defending unit. The defending player cannot excuse it by putting it on another column instead; it is still able to block the Alluring column, so it must.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Example test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::CR 606.2b UFAB: an Alluring column may not be side-stepped by blocking the OTHERS · Key: combat.blocks.who.able</sub>

<a id="r606.2c"></a>**606.2c** These attributes change which units may block a column, or how many it takes: Flying (802.2), Feeble (802.12), Evasive (802.13), Sneaky (802.14), Alluring (802.15) and Pure (802.25). See rules 802.2, 802.12, 802.13, 802.14, 802.15, 802.25.

> *Example: Only a Flying unit can block a Flying column, but a Pure unit ignores Flying and can block it too.*

> *Example: Wisps are Feeble and cannot block.*

> *Example: Curio Drifter is Evasive, so its column needs two blockers.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Air Plant; card: Spectrogenesis; card: Just a Unit · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts, 08-cards2.test.ts, 07-cards.test.ts · Example tests: 40-light-c.test.ts::Just a Unit: {Pure} blocks a Flying column, and only it can, 08-cards2.test.ts::Spectrogenesis: three Wisps; Feeble means they cannot block, 07-cards.test.ts::Curio Drifter: Evasive requires two blockers · Key: combat.blocks.who.attributes</sub>

<a id="r606.2d"></a>**606.2d** A unit sent to counterattack leaves the region and is treated as if it does not exist until the first battle round is over, so it cannot also block (see 610). See rules 610, 606.5.

> *Example: The defending player has one unit. It may block, or it may be sent to counterattack, but not both.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.20; Manual p.20 · Tests: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Example test: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts::cr:combat.blocks.who.not-sent — a unit may not both block and be sent to counterattack · Key: combat.blocks.who.not-sent</sub>

<a id="r606.2e"></a>**606.2e** A unit targeted by an Alluring trigger must block that Alluring column if it is able to. If the column is blocked at all, the lured unit must be one of its blockers (see 802.15). See rules 802.15, 802.13.

> *Example: An Alluring column lures unit A. The defending player tries to block that column with unit B instead. The declaration is refused.*

> *Example: The Alluring column is also Evasive and the defending player has only the lured unit. It cannot block an Evasive column alone, so it need not block it, and may block another column.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1460216519731577027#0; RAQ 1460216519731577027#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts, 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts · Example tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::CR 606.2e: a substitute is not good enough — the lured unit must be in the column, 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Alluring: a lone lured unit cannot block an Evasive column · Key: combat.blocks.who.lured</sub>

<a id="r606.2f"></a>**606.2f** Alluring duties never leave the defending player without a legal block declaration. However many Alluring triggers have resolved, the game offers the defending player at least one block declaration, and every declaration it offers is legal. See rule 802.15.

> *Example: Two attacking columns both have Alluring, and their triggers targeted the same defending unit. The defending player is still offered a legal declaration.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts, 06-fuzz.test.ts · Example test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::CR 606.2f: legalActions always offers a legal declaration (the fuzz-1993 hang) · Key: combat.blocks.who.always-legal</sub>

<a id="r606.3"></a>**606.3.** An attacking column is blocked once a defending unit has been placed in front of it. The whole column is blocked, however many attacking units it holds. See rule 608.

> *Example: A column of two attackers is blocked by one unit. Neither attacker deals combat damage to the defending player.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.23; Rulebook 2023 p.11 · Designer: RAQ 1366447016653361192#0 · Tests: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Example test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.pairing.blocked — the Manual p.23 example · Key: combat.blocks.blocked</sub>

<a id="r606.3a"></a>**606.3a** A blocked column stays blocked for the rest of the battle round, even if every unit blocking it leaves, whether it dies, is recalled, is erased or changes control. See rules 608, 607.2a.

> *Example: The only blocker dies in the block window. The vanilla attacker's column is still blocked and deals no damage to the defending player.*

> *Example: The only blocker is stolen by Download mid-combat. The column is still blocked.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.23; Rulebook 2023 p.11 · Designer: RAQ 1366447016653361192#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 157-blocked-stays-blocked.test.ts, 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Example tests: 157-blocked-stays-blocked.test.ts::CR 606.3a: a blocker that DIES leaves the column blocked, 157-blocked-stays-blocked.test.ts::CR 606.3a: a blocker STOLEN mid-combat (Download) leaves the column blocked · Key: combat.blocks.blocked.stays</sub>

<a id="r606.3b"></a>**606.3b** A blocked column deals no combat damage to the defending player, except as Piercing allows (see 608 and 802.16). See rules 608, 802.16.

> *Example: A blocked non-Piercing column whose blocker died before damage deals nothing to the defending player.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.23 · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Example test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Piercing: a blocked NON-Piercing column whose blocker died deals nothing to the player · Key: combat.blocks.blocked.no-damage-through</sub>

<a id="r606.4"></a>**606.4.** A defending unit may be placed blocking where no attacker is, as long as at least one attacking unit is left in the attacking formation (see rule 606.7). This is a side-block, and the blocking column it makes is a side-blocking column. See rules 602, 603.

> *Example: One unit attacks. The defending player places two units to the side of it, each in its own column, and leaves the attacker unblocked.*

> *Example: The only attacker is destroyed before blocks: a side-block beside the empty attack is refused.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.23; Manual p.23 · Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16; Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts, 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts, 479-empty-attack-and-committed-counterattack.test.ts · Example tests: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts::side-blocks: two units block where no attacker is, 479-empty-attack-and-committed-counterattack.test.ts::CT-297 an emptied attacking formation cannot be blocked head-on or to the side · Key: combat.blocks.side</sub>

<a id="r606.4a"></a>**606.4a** Side-blocks may stand on either side of the attacking formation.

> *Example: A unit side-blocks to the left of a one-column attack. A new column opens before the attacking column, and the attacking column is still unblocked.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts · Example test: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts::CR 606.4a a side-block on the left opens a column before column 1 · Key: combat.blocks.side.either-side</sub>

<a id="r606.4b"></a>**606.4b** Any number of units may side-block, each as its own column.

> *Example: Two units side-block beside a one-column attack; each makes its own side-blocking column.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1366447016653361192#3 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts · Example test: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts::side-blocks: two units block where no attacker is · Key: combat.blocks.side.any-number</sub>

<a id="r606.4c"></a>**606.4c** A block declaration may reach no further out from the attacking formation than it has blocking columns, so a single side-block stands next to the attacking formation.

> *Example: Against a one-column attack, a single side-block may stand right beside the attack on either side, but not three columns out.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts · Example test: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts::CR 606.4c side-blocks reach no further out than the declaration is wide · Key: combat.blocks.side.reach</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U11-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r606.4d"></a>**606.4d** A side-blocking column counts as a blocked column.

> *Example: Roving Quillback attacks alone and two units side-block beside it. Quillback deals 1 damage to the defending player for each blocked column: 2, for the two side-blocking columns.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1366447016653361192#2; RAQ 1366447016653361192#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts · Example test: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts::side-blocks: two units block where no attacker is · Key: combat.blocks.side.counts-as-blocked</sub>

<a id="r606.4e"></a>**606.4e** A side-block blocks no attacker. It does not count as blocking a lone Sneaky attacker, and no Flying or Evasive rule applies to it. See rules 802.2, 802.13, 802.14.

> *Example: A lone Sneaky unit attacks. A unit side-blocking beside it is allowed, and the Sneaky unit is still unblocked.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Example test: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts::cr:combat.blocks.side.blocks-nothing — a side-block beside a lone Sneaky attacker is allowed and the Sneaky unit is still unblocked · Key: combat.blocks.side.blocks-nothing</sub>

<a id="r606.4f"></a>**606.4f** A side-blocking column deals no combat damage, Piercing included, because no attacker stands in front of it (see 608). See rules 608, 802.16.

> *Example: A 5/5 Piercing unit side-blocks. It deals no combat damage to the attacking player.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1365594171867664445#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts · Example test: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts::CR 606.4f a Piercing side-blocker deals no combat damage to the attacking player · Key: combat.blocks.side.no-damage</sub>

<a id="r606.4g"></a>**606.4g** Side-blocking units are part of the defending formation, so they are adjacent to their neighbours in it (see 603). See rule 603.

> *Example: A unit side-blocks next to a unit blocking the attacking column. The two are adjacent, which matters to cards that count adjacent units.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.23; Manual p.23 · Tests: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Example test: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts::cr:combat.blocks.side.adjacency — a side-blocker is adjacent to the blocker beside it · Key: combat.blocks.side.adjacency</sub>

<a id="r606.5"></a>**606.5.** In the first battle round, the defending player declares at the same time as its blocks which of its units it sends to counterattack (see 610). See rule 610.

> *Example: The non-initiative player declares no blocks and sends one unit; that unit takes no part in the first round and attacks in the second.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.20; Manual p.20; Manual p.27 · Tests: 02-combat.test.ts · Example test: 02-combat.test.ts::1v1 counterattack: NIT sends units at block time, they attack in round 2 · Key: combat.blocks.counterattack</sub>

<a id="r606.5a"></a>**606.5a** Spell tokens may go with the counterattacking units, under the same conditions as with an attack (see 604). A spell token sent this way must then ride with the counterattack in round 2 (see rule 610.3). See rules 604.2c, 610.

> *Example: The defending player sends a unit to counterattack and names a Poison token to go with it. The token leaves with the unit and arrives with it for round 2.*

<sub>Basis: Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16; Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 4 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts, 479-empty-attack-and-committed-counterattack.test.ts · Example test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::CR 610.3: declareBlocks takes spellTokens · Key: combat.blocks.counterattack.tokens</sub>

<a id="r606.5b"></a>**606.5b** In the second battle round the defending player declares blocks only. There are no further counterattacks. See rule 610.

> *Example: In the second round the initiative player blocks the counterattack; it cannot send units to attack back.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.5; Manual p.20 · Tests: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Example test: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts::cr:combat.blocks.counterattack.second-round — in round 2 the defender may not send counterattackers · Key: combat.blocks.counterattack.second-round</sub>

<a id="r606.6"></a>**606.6.** Abilities that trigger when a unit blocks trigger as blocks are declared. They are put on the stack before the block window opens (see 607 and 706). See rules 607, 706.

> *Example: Spewing Mushroom says 'When I attack or block'. Declared as a blocker, it creates its Poison.*

> *Example: Palewing blocks and its controller discards a card.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Spewing Mushroom · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 182-correctness-sample.test.ts, 42-dark-b.test.ts · Example tests: 182-correctness-sample.test.ts::Spewing Mushroom: BLOCKING fires it too, 42-dark-b.test.ts::Palewing: blocking discards too · Key: combat.blocks.triggers</sub>

<a id="r606.7"></a>**606.7.** If no attacking unit is left when the block step begins, nothing can be blocked: no defending unit may be placed blocking, in front of the attack or to the side of it. In the first battle round the defending player may still send units to counterattack; otherwise the block declaration is empty. The battle round then continues. See rule 605.1d.

> *Example: The only attacker is destroyed before blocks. The defending player cannot block, not even to the side, but may still send a unit to counterattack, or declare nothing; the block window follows.*

> *Example: With the attack emptied, a side-block on either side is refused, with or without a unit sent to counterattack.*

> *Example: In the second battle round the lone counterattacker is destroyed before blocks: the initiative player can neither block nor send anything.*

<sub>Basis: Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16 · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts, 479-empty-attack-and-committed-counterattack.test.ts · Example tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::CR 606.2f: an attack that has collapsed to nothing still lets the defender declare, 479-empty-attack-and-committed-counterattack.test.ts::CT-297 an emptied attacking formation cannot be blocked head-on or to the side, but counterattackers may still be sent, 479-empty-attack-and-committed-counterattack.test.ts::CT-297 an emptied counterattack in round 2 leaves the defender nothing to declare · Key: combat.blocks.empty-attack</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U11-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r607"></a>
### 607. Block Window

<a id="r607.1"></a>**607.1.** The block window is the priority window that follows the declaration of blocks. See rule 703.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.20; Manual p.27; Manual p.30 · Tests: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.overview — the step begins only once blocks are declared · Key: combat.block-window.general</sub>

<a id="r607.1a"></a>**607.1a** When all players pass priority in succession with the stack empty, the block window ends and the combat damage step begins (see 608). See rule 608.

> *Example: After blocks, the first pass deals no damage; the second pass starts the combat damage step.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.11; Rulebook 2023 p.11 · Tests: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Example test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.overview — the step begins only once blocks are declared · Key: combat.block-window.general.end</sub>

<a id="r607.1b"></a>**607.1b** Once blocks have been declared, a column that loses its last unit is not closed up; the columns stay where they are for the rest of the battle round (see 602). See rules 602, 605.1c.

> *Example: After blocks, the middle attacking column dies. It stays as a hole, and the columns beside it do not move.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.22 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 64-formation-collapse.test.ts · Example test: 64-formation-collapse.test.ts::CR 602.5a (Manual): after blocks are declared, an emptied column stays as a HOLE · Key: combat.block-window.general.locked</sub>

<a id="r607.1c"></a>**607.1c** A unit behind a removed unit still moves up to the front row after blocks have been declared (see 602). See rule 602.

> *Example: After blocks, the front unit of a column dies; the unit behind it moves to the front.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.22 · Tests: 64-formation-collapse.test.ts · Example test: 64-formation-collapse.test.ts::CR 602.4 (Manual): the back row promotes AFTER blocks too · Key: combat.block-window.general.promotion</sub>

<a id="r607.2"></a>**607.2.** After blocks have been declared, a unit that joins the defending formation (for example Tiderunner Initiate, played into an open spot) may be placed in front of an attacking column that has no blocker. That column is then blocked. See rules 602, 702.

> *Example: The defending player declares no blocks, then plays Tiderunner Initiate in front of the unblocked attacker. The attacker deals its damage to the Tiderunner, not to the player.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Tiderunner Initiate · Designer: RAQ 1366447016653361192#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts, 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts · Example test: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts::CR 608.4d a Tiderunner put in front of an unblocked attacker fights it · Key: combat.block-window.late-blocker</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U11-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r607.2a"></a>**607.2a** A column blocked this way stays blocked if that unit later leaves, like any blocked column (see 606). See rule 606.3a.

> *Example: Tiderunner Initiate is played in front of an unblocked attacker and is then removed. The column is still blocked.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1366447016653361192#1 · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts · Example test: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Blocked: a unit played in as a blocker after blocks · Key: combat.block-window.late-blocker.stays</sub>

<a id="r607.2b"></a>**607.2b** The defending player may block this way even if it declared no blockers.
