> *Example: The defending player declared no blocks; Tiderunner Initiate is still offered the spot in front of the attacker.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts · Example test: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts::CR 608.4d a Tiderunner put in front of an unblocked attacker fights it · Key: combat.block-window.late-blocker.no-prior-blocks</sub>

<a id="r607.2c"></a>**607.2c** Only a unit joining the defending formation can be placed this way. A unit joining the attacking formation is never placed in a blocking position.

> *Example: After blocks, the attacking player is offered no blocking spot; the defending player is offered one, in front of the unblocked column.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts · Example test: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts::CR 607.2c the attacker is never offered a blocking spot · Key: combat.block-window.late-blocker.defender-only</sub>

<a id="r607.2d"></a>**607.2d** A unit can be placed this way from the block window until the combat damage step is over. See rule 608.

> *Example: In the window between the Swift and normal damage sub-steps, the defending player plays Tiderunner Initiate in front of an unblocked attacking column. The column is blocked for the normal sub-step.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Example test: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts::cr:combat.block-window.late-blocker.when — between the Swift and normal sub-steps a Tiderunner put in front of the unblocked normal column blocks it for the normal sub-step · Key: combat.block-window.late-blocker.when</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U11-5 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r607.2e"></a>**607.2e** A unit placed this way was not declared as a blocker, so the events of the block declaration do not happen for it. See rule 606.6.

> *Example: After blocks, the defending player plays Tiderunner Initiate in front of an unblocked attacker. It now blocks that column, but it was never declared as a blocker, so nothing that happens when blocks are declared happens for it.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Example test: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts::cr:combat.block-window.late-blocker.not-declared — no blocked event fires for a unit placed in front of an attacker after blocks · Key: combat.block-window.late-blocker.not-declared</sub>

<a id="r607.3"></a>**607.3.** An ability that triggers "after the blocking step" triggers once blocks have been declared, and resolves in the block window. See rule 706.

> *Example: Roving Quillback attacks and two units side-block. Once both players pass in the block window, its trigger resolves and the defending player loses 2 life, before any combat damage.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Roving Quillback · Tests: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts · Example test: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts::side-blocks: two units block where no attacker is · Key: combat.block-window.after-blocking-triggers</sub>

<a id="r608"></a>
### 608. Combat Damage Step

<a id="r608.1"></a>**608.1.** The combat damage step is the step of a battle in which the units in formation deal combat damage. It begins once blocks have been declared and all players have passed priority in the window that follows them, and it is followed by the after combat step (see rule 609). See rules 607, 609.

> *Example: A 2/5 attacks and is blocked by a 2/5. After blocks, the block window opens; once both players pass, each deals 2 to the other, and then the after combat step begins.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.20; Rulebook 2023 p.11; Manual p.27 · Tests: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Example test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.overview — the step begins only once blocks are declared and both players pass, and the after combat step follows it · Key: combat.damage.overview</sub>

<a id="r608.1a"></a>**608.1a** The combat damage step takes place separately in each region where a battle takes place. A region that was not attacked has no combat damage step. See rules 601, 609.

> *Example: The first attacker declares no attack, so the defending player's region has no combat damage step. The second player then attacks, and the only combat damage step of the turn is in the first player's region.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.20; Manual p.20 · Tests: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Example test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.overview.per-region — a battle round with no attack has no combat damage step · Key: combat.damage.overview.per-region</sub>

<a id="r608.1b"></a>**608.1b** All combat damage is dealt simultaneously, unless an ability changes when a column deals its damage. Swift and Sluggish are the attributes that do (see rule 608.2). See rules 608.2, 802.4, 802.5.

> *Example: A 3/3 attacks and is blocked by a 3/3. Both are dealt 3 at the same time, so both die.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.23; Manual p.23; card: Rime Wraith · Tests: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Example test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.overview.simultaneous — two 3/3s in one exchange both deal their damage before either dies · Key: combat.damage.overview.simultaneous</sub>

<a id="r608.1c"></a>**608.1c** Combat damage is dealt by columns. The attacking units of one column deal their combat damage together, as one source, and so do the blocking units of one column. In this section, each of these two groups is called a half-column: a column has an attacking half and a blocking half. See rules 603, 802.20.

> *Example: Two Slinks (Thieving) attack in one column and are not blocked. The column is one source of combat damage, so its controller draws one card, not two.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.23; card: Blightsea Polyp · Designer: RAQ 1460213341011050536#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts · Example test: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Thieving: two Thieving units in one column draw ONE card · Key: combat.damage.overview.column-source</sub>

<a id="r608.2"></a>**608.2.** The combat damage step has three damage sub-steps, taken in this order: the Swift sub-step, the normal sub-step and the Sluggish sub-step. Each half-column strikes (deals its combat damage) only in the sub-steps that rule 608.2a gives it. The two halves of one column are scheduled separately. See rules 802.4, 802.5.

> *Example: Dune Drifter (2/1, Swift) is blocked by a 1/5, and Ambling Mountaintop (Sluggish) attacks unblocked. The Drifter deals 2 in the Swift sub-step, the 1/5 strikes back in the normal sub-step and kills it, and the Mountaintop deals its damage last.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.43; Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1540678747953569832#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts, 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Example test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.substeps — Swift, then normal, then Sluggish, and the two halves of one column strike in their own sub-steps · Key: combat.damage.substeps</sub>

<a id="r608.2a"></a>**608.2a** A half-column that has Swift strikes in the Swift sub-step. A half-column that has Sluggish strikes in the Sluggish sub-step. A half-column that has neither strikes in the normal sub-step. See rules 802.4, 802.5.

> *Example: Dune Drifter (2/1, Swift) and Rune Channeler (4/3) attack in one column and are blocked by a 2/2. The attacking half deals its 6 damage in the Swift sub-step; when that sub-step ends the 2/2 has been destroyed and the attackers are undamaged.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Rime Wraith; card: Rime Wraith; Manual p.25 · Tests: 02-combat.test.ts, 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts · Example test: 02-combat.test.ts::Swift: swift column deals damage first · Key: combat.damage.substeps.schedule</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-18, D-U12-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r608.2b"></a>**608.2b** Whether a half-column has Swift or Sluggish depends on the combat attributes its units share: an attribute of any unit in a column is shared by every unit in that column (see rule 603). When a unit leaves a column, the other units in it lose the attributes that unit was sharing at once. See rules 603, 802.1.

> *Example: Dune Drifter (Swift) and Lithoghul attack in one column, so Lithoghul would strike in the Swift sub-step. If Dune Drifter is recalled, Lithoghul at once strikes in the normal sub-step instead.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.24; Rulebook 2023 p.12; Manual p.24 · Engine: colAttrs · Tests: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Example test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.substeps.column-attributes — a unit leaving a column takes the Swift it shared with it · Key: combat.damage.substeps.column-attributes</sub>

<a id="r608.2c"></a>**608.2c** A half-column that has both Swift and Sluggish strikes twice: once in the Swift sub-step and once in the Sluggish sub-step. It does not strike in the normal sub-step. See rules 802.4, 802.5.

> *Example: Rime Wraith (2/1, Swift and Sluggish) and Vroot (4/4) attack in one column and are not blocked. The column deals 6 in the Swift sub-step and 6 more in the Sluggish sub-step.*

> *Example: Rime Wraith attacks alone and is not blocked. It deals 2 in the Swift sub-step, nothing strikes in the normal sub-step, and it deals 2 more in the Sluggish sub-step.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 4 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1363298910528864318#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25, 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 134-column-and-substep.test.ts, 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts, 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts, 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Example tests: 134-column-and-substep.test.ts::§5 — a {Swift}{Sluggish} column strikes twice, 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts::CR 608.2c a {Swift}{Sluggish} column strikes in two sub-steps · Key: combat.damage.substeps.swift-and-sluggish</sub>

<a id="r608.2d"></a>**608.2d** If either half of a column contains a Pure card, neither half of that column has Swift or Sluggish for that exchange, so both halves strike in the normal sub-step. See rule 802.25.

> *Example: A printed Swift column blocked by a Pure unit strikes in the normal sub-step.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-20, 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Example test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::threads {Pure}: a printed {Swift} column blocked by a Pure unit strikes in the NORMAL sub-step · Key: combat.damage.substeps.pure</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r608.2e"></a>**608.2e** A half-column that has struck in the Swift sub-step does not strike in the normal sub-step, even if the unit that gave it Swift has since left the column, and even if a new unit has since been put into that column. A half-column that has struck in the normal sub-step does not strike in the Sluggish sub-step, even if it has since gained Sluggish. A half-column that struck in the Swift sub-step and has Sluggish in the Sluggish sub-step strikes again then (rule 608.2c). This record belongs to the half-column, not to the units in it, and it stays with that column if the columns are renumbered (for example, when a new column is opened to its left). See rule 603.

> *Example: Dune Drifter (2/1, Swift) and a 3/3 attack in one column; a 1/1 attacks in another. The Swift column deals 5 in the Swift sub-step. Dune Drifter is then recalled. In the normal sub-step only the 1/1's column strikes.*

> *Example: After Dune Drifter's column strikes in the Swift sub-step, Dune Drifter is recalled and Tiderunner Initiate is played into the emptied column. Tiderunner Initiate deals no normal combat damage.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1363298910528864318#1; RAQ 1363298910528864318#3; RAQ 1363298910528864318#4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Engine: struck · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts, 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts · Example tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Swift: a column that dealt Swift damage deals no normal damage, 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Swift: a Tiderunner played into an emptied Swift column deals no normal damage · Demonstrated by test: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts::CR 608.2e a struck mark moves with its column when a new column opens on the left · Key: combat.damage.substeps.struck-mark</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-16 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r608.2f"></a>**608.2f** Whether a half-column strikes in a sub-step is determined as that sub-step begins, from the units then in the column and the attributes they then share. See rule 603.

> *Example: A column strikes in the Swift sub-step and then gains Sluggish. It strikes again in the Sluggish sub-step.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.24 · Designer: RAQ 1363298910528864318#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts · Example test: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Swift: a Swift column that gains Sluggish strikes again in the Sluggish sub-step · Key: combat.damage.substeps.live-attributes</sub>

<a id="r608.3"></a>**608.3.** A combat damage step is split if, when the step begins, half-columns are scheduled to strike in two or more different sub-steps. Otherwise it is unsplit. Only Swift and Sluggish can split a step. See rules 802.4, 802.5.

> *Example: Dune Drifter (Swift) is blocked by a unit without Swift or Sluggish. The attacking half strikes in the Swift sub-step and the blocking half in the normal one, so the step is split.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1363298910528864318#0; RAQ 1540678747953569832#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts, 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Example test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.split — a Swift attacking half over a normal blocking half splits the step into two sub-steps with a window between them · Key: combat.damage.split</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-9 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r608.3a"></a>**608.3a** In an unsplit step, all combat damage is dealt at once, as one step. No player receives priority during it, and abilities that trigger during it wait until the after combat step (see rule 608.9b). See rules 609, 703.

> *Example: Lithoghul (4/4) and Geode (1/1) attack in separate columns and are not blocked. Neither has Swift or Sluggish, so the step is unsplit; the 5 damage is dealt at once and the game goes straight to the after combat step.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1363298910528864318#0; RAQ 1540678747953569832#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16, 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts, 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts · Example test: 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts::CR 608.3a the control: with no {Swift} and no {Sluggish} anywhere · Key: combat.damage.split.unsplit</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r608.3b"></a>**608.3b** In a split step, each sub-step that was scheduled, when the step began, to have a half-column strike in it is a separate step. After each such sub-step except the last scheduled one, the abilities that triggered during it are put on the stack and players receive priority; the next sub-step deals no damage until that stack has resolved and all players have passed priority in succession with it empty. State-based changes (deaths, back-row units moving forward, lost shared attributes) have already happened when this window opens. See rules 703, 706.

> *Example: Bripp (4 power) and Bloated Manablub (2 power) attack in normal columns, and Adversary of the Deep (2/2, Sluggish; 'Whenever a player loses life, put that many +1/+1 counters on me') attacks in a third column. None are blocked. The normal sub-step deals 6; the step stops, Adversary's trigger resolves with priority, and Adversary strikes in the Sluggish sub-step for 8.*

> *Example: At the boundary, the stack holds Adversary of the Deep's trigger. Its controller has the initiative and receives priority first; the other player may respond once they pass.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 9 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1540678747953569832#2; RAQ 1363298910528864318#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Engine: pumpCombatDamage · Tests: 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts, 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts, 21-fixes.test.ts · Example tests: 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts::CR 802.5b the report, 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts::CR 608.3b the boundary is a real priority window · Key: combat.damage.split.boundary-window</sub>

<a id="r608.3c"></a>**608.3c** A sub-step in which no half-column was scheduled to strike when the step began is not a separate step: no window opens after it. A scheduled sub-step keeps its window even if every half-column scheduled for it has since been destroyed. No window opens after the last scheduled sub-step; a half-column that still strikes in a later sub-step (rule 608.2f) strikes without a window before it, and then the after combat step begins.

> *Example: Dune Drifter (Swift) and Lithoghul attack in separate columns and are not blocked. Half-columns strike in the Swift and normal sub-steps and nothing strikes in the Sluggish sub-step, so there is exactly one window, between the Swift and normal sub-steps.*

> *Example: Dune Drifter (Swift) and a 1/1 attack in separate columns and are not blocked. At the window after the Swift sub-step, Dune Drifter's column gains Sluggish. The 1/1 strikes in the normal sub-step and no window follows; Dune Drifter's column then strikes in the Sluggish sub-step, and the after combat step begins.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Engine: pumpCombatDamage · Tests: 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts, 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Example tests: 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts::CR 608.3c an EMPTY sub-step opens no window, 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.split.empty-substep — a column that gains Sluggish after the last scheduled sub-step strikes with no window before it, then after combat begins · Key: combat.damage.split.empty-substep</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-10 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r608.3d"></a>**608.3d** Which sub-steps are separate steps is determined once, when the combat damage step begins. A unit that dies, leaves or loses an attribute during the step does not make a split step unsplit.

> *Example: Dune Drifter (Swift) attacks beside Lithoghul and is blocked by another Dune Drifter. Both Swift units destroy each other in the Swift sub-step; the window before the normal sub-step still opens, and the death triggers can be answered there.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts · Example test: 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts::CR 608.3d damageSubs is fixed when the step opens · Key: combat.damage.split.schedule-fixed</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-11 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r608.3e"></a>**608.3e** Between sub-steps, the game's state is updated before anything else: units with lethal damage are destroyed, a unit behind a removed unit moves to the front row, and attributes shared by a removed unit are lost. A unit destroyed in an earlier sub-step deals no damage in a later one, and damage in a later sub-step is assigned to the formation as it then stands. Columns do not close gaps after blocks have been declared. See rules 602, 603.

> *Example: Dune Drifter (2/1, Swift) is blocked by a 2/2 in front of a 4/3. Its Swift damage destroys the 2/2; the 4/3 is already in front when the boundary window opens, and in the normal sub-step it destroys Dune Drifter while taking no damage.*

> *Example: A blocking column whose attacker was destroyed in an earlier sub-step deals nothing in a later sub-step.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.22; Manual p.22; Manual p.24 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-09-16, 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 05-rulings.test.ts, 64-formation-collapse.test.ts · Example tests: 05-rulings.test.ts::CR 608.3e: formation recalc between damage sub-steps is immediate, 64-formation-collapse.test.ts::CR 608.4e (ruling): a hole deals nothing in a LATER sub-step either · Key: combat.damage.split.state-between</sub>

<a id="r608.4"></a>**608.4.** Each attacking half-column deals its combat damage either to the defending player or to the blocking half-column in front of it, and each blocking half-column deals its combat damage to the attacking half-column it blocks. Piercing can also carry combat damage to a player (see rule 802.16). An attacking column is blocked once a blocking unit has been placed in front of it, normally in the block step (see rule 606) or later as rule 608.4d allows. See rules 606, 802.16.

> *Example: A 3/5 and a 4/5 attack in two columns; a 2/5 blocks the 3/5. The 3/5 deals 3 to the blocker, the blocker deals 2 to the 3/5, and the 4/5 deals 4 to the defending player.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.11; Rulebook 2023 p.11; Manual p.23 · Tests: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Example test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.pairing — an unblocked attacking column hits the player, a blocked one hits its blocker, and the blocker hits the column it blocks · Key: combat.damage.pairing</sub>

<a id="r608.4a"></a>**608.4a** An attacking half-column that is not blocked deals its combat damage to the defending player.

> *Example: Slink (2/3) attacks and is not blocked. The defending player is dealt 2 combat damage.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.23; Manual p.20 · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 09-attrs.test.ts · Example test: 09-attrs.test.ts::Thieving: Slink draws when its column deals combat damage to a player · Key: combat.damage.pairing.unblocked</sub>

<a id="r608.4b"></a>**608.4b** An attacking half-column that is blocked deals its combat damage to the units of the blocking half-column in front of it, and that blocking half-column deals its combat damage to the units of the attacking half-column. A blocked attacking half-column deals no combat damage to the defending player, except as Piercing allows (see rule 802.16). See rule 802.16.

> *Example: The column of Living Forge and A Pile of Rubbish deals a combined 3 damage to the Tiderunner Initiate blocking it; the Tiderunner deals 2 back, all to Living Forge because it is in the front. (from the Manual p.23)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.23; Manual p.23; Manual p.23 · Tests: 02-combat.test.ts, 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Example test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.pairing.blocked — the Manual p.23 example: Living Forge and A Pile of Rubbish deal 3 to the blocking Tiderunner Initiate, which deals 2 back, and the player takes nothing · Key: combat.damage.pairing.blocked</sub>

<a id="r608.4c"></a>**608.4c** Once an attacking column is blocked, it remains blocked for the rest of the battle, however its blockers leave the blocking half-column: destroyed, recalled, erased or stolen. If no blocking unit remains when that column strikes, an attacking half-column without Piercing deals no combat damage at all, and one with Piercing deals all of its damage to the defending player (see rule 802.16). See rules 606, 802.16.

> *Example: A vanilla attacker is blocked; the blocker is then recalled before damage. The column stays blocked and the defending player is dealt no damage.*

> *Example: Good Whale (7/5, Piercing) is blocked by a 1/1 that dies before damage. All 7 of its damage is dealt to the defending player.*

> *Example: A 7/5 without Piercing is blocked by a 1/1 that dies before damage. It deals nothing to the defending player.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.23; Rulebook 2023 p.11 · Designer: RAQ 1365594171867664445#1 · Tests: 157-blocked-stays-blocked.test.ts, 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Example tests: 157-blocked-stays-blocked.test.ts::CR 606.3a: a blocker that is RECALLED leaves the column blocked, 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Piercing: a Piercing column whose blocker died before damage puts its full power into the player, 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Piercing: a blocked NON-Piercing column whose blocker died deals nothing to the player · Key: combat.damage.pairing.stays-blocked</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-15 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r608.4d"></a>**608.4d** If, after blocks have been declared and before combat damage is over, a unit is put into the defending formation in front of an unblocked attacking column, that column becomes blocked, and it stays blocked if that unit later leaves. The defending player may do this even if they declared no blockers. See rules 606, 607.

> *Example: Tiderunner Initiate is played in front of an unblocked attacker after blocks; the attacker deals its damage to the Tiderunner instead of the defending player.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1366447016653361192#1; RAQ 1366447016653361192#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts, 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts · Example test: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts::CR 608.4d a Tiderunner put in front of an unblocked attacker fights it · Key: combat.damage.pairing.late-blocker</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-22, D-U12-4 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r608.4e"></a>**608.4e** A blocking half-column with no attacking unit left in front of it when it would strike deals no combat damage, even if it has Piercing. See rule 802.16.

> *Example: Good Whale (7/5, Piercing) blocks a column whose only attacker is destroyed in the block window. Good Whale deals no damage to the attacking player and takes none.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1365594171867664445#3 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 64-formation-collapse.test.ts · Example test: 64-formation-collapse.test.ts::CR 608.4e (ruling): a hole deals and takes no damage — Piercing included · Key: combat.damage.pairing.attackers-gone</sub>

<a id="r608.4f"></a>**608.4f** A unit blocking where no attacking unit is (a side-block) forms a blocking half-column with no attacker in front of it. It deals no combat damage, even if it has Piercing, and it never makes the combat damage step split. See rules 606, 802.16.

> *Example: A Piercing unit side-blocks. It deals no combat damage to the attacking player.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.23 · Designer: RAQ 1365594171867664445#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts · Example test: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts::CR 606.4f a Piercing side-blocker deals no combat damage to the attacking player · Key: combat.damage.pairing.side-block</sub>

<a id="r608.5"></a>**608.5.** A half-column's combat damage is the combined power of the units in it when it strikes, counted as rule 608.5c describes. See rule 206.

> *Example: A 1/1 and a 2/2 attack in one column beside a Swift column. In the window after the Swift sub-step the 1/1 gets two +1/+1 counters, so the column deals 3 + 2 = 5 in the normal sub-step.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.23; Rulebook 2023 p.10 · Tests: 02-combat.test.ts, 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Example test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.amount — a column deals the combined power of its units as it is when it strikes, read after a pump between sub-steps · Key: combat.damage.amount</sub>

<a id="r608.5a"></a>**608.5a** A unit with 0 power deals no damage, but it does not stop its column from dealing the combined power of the other units in it. A half-column whose combined power is 0 deals no combat damage.

> *Example: Zephyrzoa, reduced to 0 power, is in a column with a powered unit. The column deals combat damage and Zephyrzoa's 'when my column deals combat damage' ability triggers.*

> *Example: Zephyrzoa, reduced to 0 power, attacks alone. Its column deals no combat damage and its ability does not trigger.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 134-column-and-substep.test.ts · Example tests: 134-column-and-substep.test.ts::CR 608.9a — Zephyrzoa: a 0-power anchor in a POWERED column still fires, 134-column-and-substep.test.ts::CR 608.9a — Zephyrzoa: alone in a 0-POWER column it hears nothing · Key: combat.damage.amount.zero-power</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-5 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r608.5b"></a>**608.5b** Powerful doubles a half-column's combined power once, before that damage is divided among its recipients (see rule 802.10). Vulnerable does not change the amount a half-column deals; it doubles what a Vulnerable unit is dealt (see rule 802.11). See rules 802.10, 802.11.

> *Example: Chitin Shredder (Powerful) attacks unblocked; the defending player is dealt double its column's power.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1362838395298119912#2; RAQ 1372451771632320512#3 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 09-attrs.test.ts, 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Example test: 09-attrs.test.ts::Powerful: Chitin Shredder deals double combat damage to a player · Key: combat.damage.amount.modifier-order</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-19, D-U12-7, D-U12-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r608.5c"></a>**608.5c** When a half-column's combined power is counted, a unit with negative power counts as 0: it deals no damage and does not reduce its column's damage. In an exchange in which Unaware applies, each unit's printed power is used. See rule 802.9.

> *Example: Lithoghul (4/4) and a -2/3 token attack in one column and are not blocked. The column deals 4.*

> *Example: A Robot token with nine +1/+1 counters (a 9/9) attacks and is blocked by Bubb, which is Unaware. In that exchange both read their printed stats: the Robot is a 0/0, so it dies and deals Bubb no damage.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.42; Manual p.42 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 05-rulings.test.ts, 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Example tests: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.amount.counting — a negative-power unit counts as 0 and does not reduce its column, 05-rulings.test.ts::CR 802.9d: an Unaware blocker and what it blocks BOTH read at printed · Key: combat.damage.amount.counting</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r608.6"></a>**608.6.** When a half-column deals combat damage to the units of the opposing half-column, its damage is divided among those units, starting with the front unit and then the unit behind it. See rule 602.

> *Example: Living Forge and A Pile of Rubbish attack in one column and are blocked by Tiderunner Initiate. All 2 of the Tiderunner’s damage goes to Living Forge, in front; none goes to A Pile of Rubbish behind it. (from the Manual p.23)*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.23 · Designer: RAQ 1353888077625561108#2 · Tests: 100-elective-assign.test.ts, 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Example test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.assignment — the Manual p.23 example: the blocking half-column damage goes to the front unit first, none to the unit behind it · Key: combat.damage.assignment</sub>

<a id="r608.6a"></a>**608.6a** The controller of the half-column dealing the damage divides it: the attacking player divides an attacking half-column's damage among the blocking units, and the defending player divides a blocking half-column's damage among the attacking units. See rule 608.6.

> *Example: A 4-power attacker is blocked by two 1/1s. The attacking player is asked how to divide the 4.*

> *Example: The defending player divides a blocking half-column's damage and may put all of it on the front attacker.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.43 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 100-elective-assign.test.ts · Example tests: 100-elective-assign.test.ts::CR 608.6c: the ATTACKER is asked, 100-elective-assign.test.ts::CR 608.6a: the BLOCK-side strike multi-assigns too · Key: combat.damage.assignment.chooser</sub>

<a id="r608.6b"></a>**608.6b** Lethal damage (rule 608.6e) must be assigned to a unit before any damage is assigned to the unit behind it.

> *Example: Rune Channeler (4 power) is blocked by a 2/3 in front of a 1/1. Its controller may put 3 or 4 on the 2/3, but not less than 3, since 3 is the 2/3's lethal damage.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.23 · Designer: RAQ 1353888077625561108#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 100-elective-assign.test.ts · Example test: 100-elective-assign.test.ts::CR 608.6b: amounts below the front unit · Key: combat.damage.assignment.lethal-first</sub>

<a id="r608.6c"></a>**608.6c** A unit may be assigned more than lethal damage. The dealing player may assign all of a half-column's damage to the front unit and none to the unit behind it, even if there is enough to destroy both.

> *Example: A 4-power attacker is blocked by a 1/1 in front of a 1/1. The attacking player assigns all 4 to the front 1/1; the back 1/1 is untouched.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1353888077625561108#1 · Tests: 100-elective-assign.test.ts · Example test: 100-elective-assign.test.ts::CR 608.6c: the ATTACKER is asked · Key: combat.damage.assignment.overkill</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r608.6d"></a>**608.6d** All combat damage assigned to a unit is dealt to that unit, including any beyond its lethal damage; none of it is lost. A half-column without Piercing that has at least one unit to deal damage to assigns all of its damage to those units, so none of it reaches the player; any of its damage still unassigned when the last unit is reached is assigned to that unit. See rules 802.16, 608.4c.

> *Example: Rune Channeler (4/3, no Piercing) is blocked by a 1/1. All 4 damage is dealt to the 1/1; none is lost and none reaches the player.*

> *Example: An overkill combat hit on Mirage Scuttler marks the whole amount, not only the lethal part.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.23 · Designer: RAQ 1353888077625561108#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 05-rulings.test.ts, 24-wood-b.test.ts, 17-earth-b.test.ts · Example tests: 05-rulings.test.ts::CR 608.6d: without Piercing the excess is not lost, it lands on the unit, 17-earth-b.test.ts::Mirage Scuttler: an overkill combat hit marks the WHOLE amount · Key: combat.damage.assignment.dealt-in-full</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-20 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r608.6e"></a>**608.6e** Lethal damage, for assignment, is the smallest amount of the half-column's damage that would destroy the unit, given the damage already marked on it: its remaining defense; half of that, rounded up, if the unit is Vulnerable; 1 if the half-column has Deadly. In an exchange in which Unaware applies, the unit's printed defense, less the damage already marked on it, is used. In an exchange involving a Pure card, neither Vulnerable nor Deadly changes lethal damage. See rules 802.3, 802.9, 802.11, 802.25.

> *Example: A 10-power Piercing half-column blocked by a Vulnerable 3/8 must assign 4 to it, and the other 6 may go to the player.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 7 tests (5 probes it wrote), all passed; 4 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1353888077625561108#3; RAQ 1372451771632320512#3 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-20, 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 100-elective-assign.test.ts, 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 134-column-and-substep.test.ts, 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Example test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Vulnerable: a 10-power Piercing column into a Vulnerable 3/8 assigns 4 and 6 goes to the player · Demonstrated by test: 100-elective-assign.test.ts::CR 608.6e: {Deadly} floors are 1 · Key: combat.damage.assignment.lethal-defined</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-17 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r608.6f"></a>**608.6f** If the opposing half-column has only one unit, all of the damage is assigned to that unit; with Piercing, the dealing player may instead send damage beyond that unit's lethal damage to its controller (see rule 802.16). See rule 802.16.

> *Example: A Piercing attacker with 10 power is blocked by a lone Vulnerable 3/8. It may assign all 10 to that unit (dealt as 20), and then none reaches the player.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1353888077625561108#0; RAQ 1372451771632320512#4 · Tests: 05-rulings.test.ts, 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts · Example test: 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts::CR 802.16c: a Piercing attacker may put all 10 into a lone Vulnerable 3/8 · Key: combat.damage.assignment.lone-unit</sub>

<a id="r608.6g"></a>**608.6g** Damage prevention on a unit does not change its lethal damage. Lethal damage is worked out as if the unit were not protected, and the prevention applies when the damage is dealt (rule 608.7a). See rule 708.

> *Example: A shielded 0/5 Awoken Tomb is in front of a 5/6. At least 5 must be assigned to the Tomb before any is assigned to the 5/6.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353888077625561108#8 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Example test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Excessive: a shielded Awoken Tomb in front must still be assigned its 5 · Key: combat.damage.assignment.shields-ignored</sub>

<a id="r608.6h"></a>**608.6h** In each sub-step, every half-column's damage is divided before any damage in that sub-step is dealt.

> *Example: Two 10/20 attackers are each blocked by two 1/3s. Both attackers are asked how to divide their damage, and no damage is dealt until both have answered.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 2 gate test files · Tests: 100-elective-assign.test.ts, 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Example test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.assignment.timing — both columns are asked for their split before any damage of the sub-step is dealt · Key: combat.damage.assignment.timing</sub>

<a id="r608.7"></a>**608.7.** All the combat damage of one sub-step is dealt simultaneously. Damage dealt to a unit is marked on it; a Vulnerable unit is dealt double the damage assigned to it (see rule 802.11), and a Poisonous source deals its damage to units in the form of -1/-1 counters (see rule 802.18). See rules 802.11, 802.18.

> *Example: Crumbling Ancient (Vulnerable) is marked with double the combat damage assigned to it.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.23; card: Blightmound · Designer: RAQ 1372451771632320512#4 · Tests: 09-attrs.test.ts · Example test: 09-attrs.test.ts::Vulnerable: Crumbling Ancient marks double the combat damage it receives · Key: combat.damage.dealing</sub>

<a id="r608.7a"></a>**608.7a** Prevention applies as combat damage is dealt. Damage that is prevented is not dealt: it is not marked, it places no -1/-1 counters, it does not trigger abilities that trigger on a unit being dealt damage, and it cannot destroy a unit through Deadly. See rule 708.

> *Example: A 12-power half-column is blocked by an Awoken Tomb under Phytochemical Protection in front of a 5/6. The 5 combat damage assigned to the Tomb is prevented: none is marked, and the Tomb’s “when I am dealt damage” ability does not trigger.*

> *Example: A Deadly half-column cannot destroy a unit whose damage is prevented.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 5 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1354148437355925554#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 24-wood-b.test.ts, 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Example tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Excessive: a shielded Awoken Tomb in front must still be assigned its 5 before anything goes behind it, 24-wood-b.test.ts::Phytochemical Protection: {Deadly} cannot kill through it · Key: combat.damage.dealing.prevention</sub>

<a id="r608.7b"></a>**608.7b** After a sub-step's damage has been dealt, units with lethal damage, and units dealt damage by a Deadly source, are destroyed before the next sub-step begins. See rules 713, 802.3.

> *Example: A Swift half-column destroys its 2/2 blocker in the Swift sub-step; the blocker never strikes back in the normal sub-step.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 02-combat.test.ts, 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts · Example test: 02-combat.test.ts::Swift: swift column deals damage first · Key: combat.damage.dealing.deaths</sub>

<a id="r608.7c"></a>**608.7c** Damage marked on units remains until the regroup phase, when it is removed. See rule 506.

> *Example: An attacker and its blocker each have 2 damage marked in the first battle of the turn. Both still have 2 damage marked when the second battle begins; it is removed in the regroup phase.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 2 gate test files · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.11; Manual p.27 · Tests: 05-rulings.test.ts, 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Example test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.dealing.regroup — damage from the first battle of the turn is still marked when the second battle starts, and is removed in regroup · Key: combat.damage.dealing.regroup</sub>

<a id="r608.8"></a>**608.8.** Combat damage is dealt to a player in two ways: by an unblocked attacking half-column (rule 608.4a), and as Piercing excess from an attacking half-column, or from a blocking half-column with an attacker in front of it (see rule 802.16). Combat damage dealt to a player causes that player to lose that much life, unless an effect replaces that damage or changes the life lost. See rules 112, 802.16.

> *Example: A Piercing attacker is not blocked; all of its damage is dealt to the defending player.*

> *Example: A blocking Piercing half-column with an attacker in front of it deals its excess to the attacking player.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Adversary of the Deep; Manual p.23 · Designer: RAQ 1365594171867664445#3 · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Example tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Piercing: an unblocked Piercing column hits the player, 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Piercing: a defending Piercing column with an attacker in front of it carries its excess to the attacker · Key: combat.damage.player</sub>

<a id="r608.8a"></a>**608.8a** Combat damage to a player that an effect replaces (for example, Blightsea Polyp's rot) was still dealt. An ability that triggers when a column deals combat damage to a player still triggers, and reads the damage dealt, even if the player lost no life. See rules 708, 112.

> *Example: A fully replaced combat hit still counts as dealt: Vroot's 'that much' pays out the damage its column dealt, not the life the player lost.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26, 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 207-replaced-hit-was-dealt.test.ts · Example test: 207-replaced-hit-was-dealt.test.ts::CR 608.8a: the payout is the DAMAGE DEALT, not the life lost · Key: combat.damage.player.replaced-still-dealt</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-21 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r608.8b"></a>**608.8b** Damage dealt by an ability that a source's combat damage causes, such as Resonant's extra damage, is not combat damage, even when it is dealt during or because of combat. See rule 802.19.

> *Example: Resonant's extra damage to a player is not combat damage, so Oorblak does not take it; the player does.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1362838395298119912#0 · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts · Example test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Resonant: the extra damage is not combat damage · Key: combat.damage.player.not-combat</sub>

<a id="r608.8c"></a>**608.8c** If combat damage that would be dealt to a player is dealt to a unit instead (as Oorblak's ability does), the replacement applies to that damage once. Without Piercing, all of that damage is dealt to the unit. With Piercing, the damage beyond the unit's lethal damage is still combat damage that would be dealt to the player: another such effect that has not applied (a second Oorblak) may take it, the same one may not, and what none takes is dealt to the player. A redirect applies before an effect that changes how combat damage is dealt to a player (Blightsea Polyp); that effect applies only to damage actually dealt to the player, such as Piercing excess no redirect took. See rules 708, 802.16.

> *Example: 10 Piercing combat damage that would be dealt to a player is redirected into a 2/4 Oorblak. 4 destroy it, and the other 6 are dealt to the player.*

> *Example: A non-Piercing overkill redirected into Oorblak is absorbed whole; nothing reaches the player.*

> *Example: 10 Piercing combat damage and two 2/4 Oorblaks: 4 destroy the first, the 6 left are still combat damage and the second takes 4 of them, and 2 reach the player.*

> *Example: With three 2/4 Oorblaks the third takes the last 2, and nothing reaches the player.*

> *Example: Blightsea Polyp and Oorblak, in either order: Oorblak takes the column's damage, and no rot is gained. With a Piercing column, the excess past the Oorblak reaches the player and is dealt as 1 rot.*

> *Example: Blightsea Polyp beside two Oorblaks: the player chooses only between the Oorblaks, and no rot is gained.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 4 tests, all passed; 4 gate test files · Printed: card: Oorblak; card: Blightsea Polyp · Designer: RAQ 1397188292239163454#0; RAQ 1397188292239163454#0; RQ 1442982460034912287 · Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16 · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 17-earth-b.test.ts, 469-replacement-chain-damage.test.ts, 471-oorblak-order-and-polyp.test.ts · Example tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Oorblak: 10 Piercing combat damage redirected into a 2/4 Oorblak, 17-earth-b.test.ts::Oorblak: a NON-Piercing overkill is absorbed whole, 469-replacement-chain-damage.test.ts::CR 708.4: two Oorblaks and 10 Piercing — 4 destroy the first, 469-replacement-chain-damage.test.ts::CR 708.4: three Oorblaks and 10 Piercing, 471-oorblak-order-and-polyp.test.ts::CR 608.8c: Polyp, Oorblak and a Piercing column — the excess past the Oorblak is dealt to the player, as 1 rot, 471-oorblak-order-and-polyp.test.ts::CR 608.8c: Polyp beside two Oorblaks — the question is about the Oorblaks only, and no rot · Key: combat.damage.player.redirect</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-13 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r608.9"></a>**608.9.** An ability that triggers on combat damage, or on something combat damage causes (such as a unit being destroyed), triggers when that event happens, during the combat damage step, and its trigger condition is checked then. It is put on the stack later, as rules 608.9b and 608.9c describe, and only then are its targets chosen. See rules 706, 703.

> *Example: Lithoghul attacks and is blocked by a Geode. In the damage step the Geode deals 1 to Lithoghul, and Lithoghul's 'whenever I am dealt damage' ability triggers then; nothing goes on the stack or resolves until the after combat step.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1540678747953569832#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30, 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts · Example test: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts::CR 608.9: a combat-damage trigger is announced INSIDE the damage step · Key: combat.damage.triggers</sub>

<a id="r608.9a"></a>**608.9a** An ability that triggers 'when my column deals combat damage' triggers in each sub-step in which its own column deals combat damage, and only for damage its own column dealt; another column's damage does not trigger it. A 0-power unit with such an ability triggers if its column's combined power is greater than 0. See rule 706.

> *Example: A Swift and Sluggish column with Vroot strikes twice, and Vroot's ability triggers twice.*

> *Example: Vroot's 'that much' is its own column's damage, not the total dealt to the player by every column.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-08-25, 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 134-column-and-substep.test.ts, 166-face-damage-attribution.test.ts · Example tests: 134-column-and-substep.test.ts::§5 — a {Swift}{Sluggish} column strikes twice, 166-face-damage-attribution.test.ts::CR 608.9a — Vroot: "[Augment] When my column deals combat damage, each opponent gains that much life" · Key: combat.damage.triggers.my-column</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-14 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r608.9b"></a>**608.9b** In an unsplit step, every ability that triggered during the combat damage step is put on the stack in the after combat step, together with the abilities that trigger at the start of the after combat step, as one batch. The initiative player puts all of theirs on the stack first, in the order they choose, and then the other player puts theirs; each player may interleave the two kinds in any order. All players may respond to them. See rules 609, 706.

> *Example: One player's combat-damage trigger and after-combat trigger are put in order together, in one choice.*

> *Example: The initiative player's triggers go on the stack first and sit at the bottom.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1540678747953569832#0; RAQ 1540678747953569832#1 · Tests: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts, 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Example tests: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts::CR 608.9b THE RAQ BATCH, 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts::CR 609.3c RAQ STACK ORDER · Key: combat.damage.triggers.unsplit</sub>

<a id="r608.9c"></a>**608.9c** In a split step, the abilities that triggered during a sub-step other than the last scheduled one are put on the stack, in the same order as in rule 608.9b, at the window after that sub-step, and resolve before the next sub-step deals damage (rule 608.3b). The abilities that trigger during the last sub-step in which damage is dealt join the after combat batch as in rule 608.9b. See rules 609, 706.

> *Example: In a split step, a death trigger from the Swift sub-step resolves at the window before the normal sub-step, not after combat.*

> *Example: With Sluggish last, a death in the Sluggish sub-step joins the after combat batch.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1540678747953569832#2; RAQ 1540678747953569832#3 · Tests: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts, 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts · Example tests: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts::CR 608.9c: in a SPLIT damage step a death trigger resolves at the boundary, 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts::RAQ Combat Damage & After Combat: with Sluggish last · Key: combat.damage.triggers.split</sub>

<a id="r608.9d"></a>**608.9d** Abilities that trigger during the combat damage step trigger during battle, so an effect that makes abilities cost more to trigger during battle applies to them. See rules 111, 706.

> *Example: Crevice Lurker taxes a combat-damage trigger; on the same board without the Lurker there is no tax.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Crevice Lurker · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts · Example test: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts::CR 111.10g WIDENED BY CR 608.9d: · Key: combat.damage.triggers.tax</sub>

<a id="r608.9e"></a>**608.9e** An ability that works only while its card is in the bin can trigger on combat damage only if the card is already in the bin when that damage is dealt. A unit destroyed by combat damage is not in the bin while that same damage is dealt, but a unit destroyed in an earlier sub-step is. See rules 405, 706.

> *Example: Cinder Scuttler is destroyed in the same sub-step in which another of its controller's columns deals combat damage to the opponent. It does not return.*

> *Example: A Swift unit destroys Cinder Scuttler in the Swift sub-step; in the normal sub-step its controller deals combat damage to the opponent, and it returns.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Cinder Scuttler · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 310-zone-abilities.test.ts · Example tests: 310-zone-abilities.test.ts::§3 Cinder Scuttler does NOT recall off the damage step it died in, 310-zone-abilities.test.ts::§4 but a Swift unit bins it BEFORE the normal step · Key: combat.damage.triggers.bin-cards</sub>

<a id="r609"></a>
### 609. After Combat

<a id="r609.1"></a>**609.1.** The after combat step is the last step of a battle round. It follows the combat damage step, in the region where that battle is fought, and it is the last priority window for interaction in that region before regroup. See rules 505.2, 608.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.20; Manual p.20; Manual p.27 · Tests: 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts::cr:turn.battle.steps — a battle round steps through · Key: combat.after.what-it-is</sub>

<a id="r609.1a"></a>**609.1a** A region in which no battle takes place has no after combat step. A battle round in which no attack is declared has no after combat step. See rules 505.2a, 604.4.

> *Example: Both players decline to attack. Neither region has a combat damage step or an after combat step, and the battle phase opens no priority window at all.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.20; Manual p.43 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 165-token-loss-warning.test.ts · Example test: 165-token-loss-warning.test.ts::[CT-55] a battle both players decline opens no priority window at all · Key: combat.after.what-it-is.battled-regions-only</sub>

<a id="r609.1b"></a>**609.1b** In a game with two battle rounds, each round that has a battle has its own after combat step, in the region where that round is fought: the first round's in the non-initiative player's region, and the second round's in the initiative player's region. See rules 505.3, 505.4b, 610.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.20; Manual p.20; Manual p.27 · Tests: 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts::cr:turn.battle.rounds.round-1 — round 1 walks · Key: combat.after.what-it-is.each-round</sub>

<a id="r609.2"></a>**609.2.** The after combat step is a priority window. The initiative player receives priority first, then priority passes to the non-initiative player in the region. When all players pass priority in succession with the stack empty, the after combat step ends. See rule 703.

> *Example: After combat, the initiative player passes, the non-initiative player casts a spell, and both then pass. The spell resolves and the initiative player receives priority again. When both pass with the stack empty, the step ends.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.30; Manual p.30; Manual p.30; Manual p.30 · Tests: 424-cr-after-combat.test.ts · Example test: 424-cr-after-combat.test.ts::cr:combat.after.window — initiative first; a spell cast in the window resolves after both pass, priority returns to the initiative player; two passes on an empty stack end the step · Key: combat.after.window</sub>

<a id="r609.2a"></a>**609.2a** When the after combat step of the first battle round ends and units were sent to counterattack, the battle phase does not end: the second battle round begins (see rule 610). See rule 610.

> *Example: With counterattackers sent, passing in round 1's after-combat window does not end the battle.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.21; Manual p.21; Manual p.21 · Tests: 77-playtest-round17.test.ts · Example test: 77-playtest-round17.test.ts::[66] the after-combat window of round 1 does NOT end the battle when counterattackers were sent · Key: combat.after.window.then-round-two</sub>

<a id="r609.2b"></a>**609.2b** When the after combat step of the last battle round ends, the battle phase ends and regroup begins. The last battle round is the second round, or the first round if no units were sent to counterattack. See rules 506, 610.4.

> *Example: When the last player passes in the final after-combat window, the game goes through regroup and into deployment; no one is given priority in between.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.20; Manual p.20; Manual p.27 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts, 21-fixes.test.ts · Example test: 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts::cr:turn.regroup.what-it-is.no-actions · Key: combat.after.window.then-regroup</sub>

<a id="r609.3"></a>**609.3.** An ability that triggers "after combat" triggers when the after combat step begins. It is put on the stack in the after combat step, and players may respond to it there. See rules 109.3, 706.

> *Example: Smouldering Inferno, played as a unit, sacrifices itself after combat.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1540678747953569832#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 07-cards.test.ts, 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts · Example test: 07-cards.test.ts::Smouldering Inferno played as a unit sacrifices itself after combat · Key: combat.after.triggers</sub>

<a id="r609.3a"></a>**609.3a** An "after combat" ability of a unit triggers if that unit is present in the region where the battle is happening. The unit need not be in a formation. See rule 601.7.

> *Example: A unit with an after-combat ability that stands in the battle region outside the formation still triggers.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1356667460211966060#0 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 424-cr-after-combat.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ after combat: an after-combat trigger fires for a unit in the battle region that is not in formation · Key: combat.after.triggers.presence</sub>

<a id="r609.3b"></a>**609.3b** An "after combat" ability does not trigger in a region where no battle took place. A unit in a region other than the one where the battle is fought does not trigger. See rules 505.4c, 601.7.

> *Example: A unit with an after-combat ability that stays in another region does not trigger.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.43; Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1356667460211966060#0 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ after combat: the control, an after-combat unit in ANOTHER region makes nothing · Key: combat.after.triggers.no-battle</sub>

<a id="r609.3c"></a>**609.3c** Abilities that triggered during the combat damage step and are still waiting are put on the stack in the after combat step together with the "after combat" abilities, as one batch. The initiative player puts all of theirs on the stack first, then the non-initiative player puts theirs, so the non-initiative player's resolve first. Each player chooses the order of their own and may interleave the two kinds. See rules 608.9b, 706.

> *Example: One player's combat-damage trigger and after-combat trigger are put in order together, in one choice.*

> *Example: The initiative player's triggers go on the stack first and sit at the bottom.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1540678747953569832#0; RAQ 1540678747953569832#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts, 424-cr-after-combat.test.ts · Example tests: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts::CR 608.9b THE RAQ BATCH, 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts::CR 609.3c RAQ STACK ORDER · Key: combat.after.triggers.batch</sub>

<a id="r609.3d"></a>**609.3d** When Swift or Sluggish splits the combat damage step, only the abilities that triggered in the last sub-step in which damage is dealt join the after combat batch. Those that triggered in an earlier sub-step have already resolved before the next sub-step (see rule 608.9c). See rules 608.3, 608.9c.

> *Example: With Swift in the battle, a unit that dies in the last (normal) sub-step has its death trigger in the after-combat batch.*

> *Example: With Sluggish last, a death in the Sluggish sub-step joins the after-combat batch.*

> *Example: In a split damage step a death trigger from an earlier sub-step resolves at the boundary, not after combat.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1540678747953569832#3; RAQ 1540678747953569832#2 · Tests: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts, 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts · Example tests: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts::RAQ Combat Damage & After Combat: with Swift in the battle, 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts::RAQ Combat Damage & After Combat: with Sluggish last, 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts::CR 608.9c: in a SPLIT damage step a death trigger resolves at the boundary · Key: combat.after.triggers.split-last</sub>

<a id="r610"></a>
### 610. Counterattacks and Later Battle Rounds

<a id="r610.1"></a>**610.1.** A counterattack is the non-initiative team's attack in a battle phase with two battle rounds. The non-initiative team sends its counterattacking units out during the block step of the first battle round, and they attack in the second battle round. See rules 505.3, 606.5.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.20; Manual p.20; Rulebook 2023 p.5 · Tests: 02-combat.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 02-combat.test.ts::1v1 counterattack: NIT sends units at block time, they attack in round 2 · Key: combat.counterattack.what-it-is</sub>

<a id="r610.1a"></a>**610.1a** Units are sent to counterattack only in the first battle round, at the same time as the non-initiative team declares its blocks. Sending counterattackers is optional. See rules 606.5, 606.5b.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.27; Manual p.20 · Tests: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts, 21-fixes.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts::cr:combat.blocks.counterattack.second-round · Key: combat.counterattack.what-it-is.when-sent</sub>

<a id="r610.2"></a>**610.2.** Counterattacking units leave their region as soon as they are sent. From then until the first battle round ends they are in no region, and they are treated as if they do not exist. See rules 505.3b, 606.2d.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.20; Manual p.20; Rulebook 2023 p.5 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 22-playtest3.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 22-playtest3.test.ts::a SENT Towering Colossus host radiates nothing in the region it left · Key: combat.counterattack.sent</sub>

<a id="r610.2a"></a>**610.2a** A sent counterattacker's static abilities apply to nothing while it is away, not even to itself. See rule 707.

> *Example: Bubb carries Towering Colossus ("Enemies gain +2/+2"), so an enemy 1/1 attacking into Bubb's region is a 3/3. When Bubb is sent to counterattack, the attacker is a 1/1 again at once.*

> *Example: A sent Prickly Protector ("I gain +1/+1 for each other ally") does not give itself that bonus while it is away.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.20 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 424-cr-after-combat.test.ts, 22-playtest3.test.ts · Example tests: 22-playtest3.test.ts::a SENT Towering Colossus host radiates nothing in the region it left, 424-cr-after-combat.test.ts::cr:combat.counterattack.sent.no-statics — a sent Prickly Protector does not give itself its own bonus while away · Key: combat.counterattack.sent.no-statics</sub>

<a id="r610.2b"></a>**610.2b** A sent counterattacker cannot be targeted and cannot be sacrificed while it is away. See rule 110.

> *Example: The initiative player casts a spell that targets a unit in the round-1 battle region. A unit that was sent to counterattack is not offered as a target.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.20 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 424-cr-after-combat.test.ts · Example test: 424-cr-after-combat.test.ts::cr:combat.counterattack.sent.not-targetable — a sent counterattacker is not offered as a target; a unit that stayed is · Key: combat.counterattack.sent.not-targetable</sub>

<a id="r610.2c"></a>**610.2c** A sent counterattacker does not count as a unit in the region it left. A unit that stays behind does not count a sent counterattacker as an ally. See rule 601.

> *Example: Prickly Protector, carrying a -1/-1 counter, is alive only because it has one other ally. When that ally is sent to counterattack, the Protector stays home, no longer counts it, and dies.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.20 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 250-ally-count-and-absence.test.ts · Example test: 250-ally-count-and-absence.test.ts::scope: a unit left at home still loses the ally that counterattacked away · Key: combat.counterattack.sent.not-counted</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U13-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r610.2d"></a>**610.2d** Spell tokens sent with counterattackers are away with them, and cannot be cast until they return. See rule 610.3.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.20 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 22-playtest3.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 22-playtest3.test.ts::a sent spell token is not enumerable (castSpellToken) while absent · Key: combat.counterattack.sent.tokens</sub>

<a id="r610.2e"></a>**610.2e** A sent counterattacker is not checked for death while it is away. It is checked as soon as it returns at the start of the second battle round. See rule 713.

> *Example: Prickly Protector with a -1/-1 counter, alive only through its own static, survives being declared as a counterattacker.*

> *Example: A Prickly Protector sent out alone survives the send, and dies on arrival in the enemy region, where it has no ally to count.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 250-ally-count-and-absence.test.ts · Example tests: 250-ally-count-and-absence.test.ts::Prickly Protector survives being declared as a counterattacker, 250-ally-count-and-absence.test.ts::a counterattacker sent out alone survives the send and dies on arrival · Key: combat.counterattack.sent.no-death-check</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U13-5 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r610.3"></a>**610.3.** Spell tokens may go with counterattacking units, under the same conditions as with an attack (see rule 604.2c). A counterattack made only of spell tokens is not allowed: spell tokens need at least one counterattacking unit to go with. A spell token sent with a counterattack is committed as the units are: in round 2 it must ride with the counterattacking formation, with the formation as a whole rather than with any one unit. If every unit sent with it has died, it cannot ride and is not owed: it reaches no priority window, and is erased unused at regroup. See rules 604.2c, 606.5a.

> *Example: Three units and a Fireball token were sent. In round 2 a formation that leaves the Fireball behind is refused.*

> *Example: The only unit sent with a Fireball token dies before round 2: no attack is possible, the battle phase ends with no window, and the token is erased at regroup.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 5 tests, all passed; 4 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.20 · Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16; Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts, 77-playtest-round17.test.ts, 424-cr-after-combat.test.ts, 479-empty-attack-and-committed-counterattack.test.ts · Example tests: 479-empty-attack-and-committed-counterattack.test.ts::CT-298 every sent spell token must ride with a counterattack of several units, 479-empty-attack-and-committed-counterattack.test.ts::CT-298 a sent token whose units all died is not owed and never reaches a window · Demonstrated by tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts::CR 610.3: declareBlocks takes spellTokens, and they ride out with the counterattackers, 77-playtest-round17.test.ts::[67] a token-only counterattack is refused by the engine · Key: combat.counterattack.tokens</sub>

<a id="r610.4"></a>**610.4.** The second battle round begins only once the first battle round has completely finished, its after combat step included. In a two-player game it is fought in the initiative player's region. See rules 505.4b, 609.2.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.5; Manual p.21; Manual p.21 · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.regions.one-at-a-time — the first battle round runs every one of its steps · Key: combat.counterattack.round-two</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U09-4 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r610.4a"></a>**610.4a** When the second battle round begins, the sent counterattackers, and the spell tokens sent with them, reappear in the region they are attacking. See rule 610.2.

> *Example: The non-initiative player sent two units. When round 1's after combat step ends, both appear in the initiative player's region, ready to be put into formation.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.27 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 424-cr-after-combat.test.ts, 02-combat.test.ts · Example test: 424-cr-after-combat.test.ts::cr:combat.counterattack.round-two.return — sent units and a sent spell token reappear in the region they attack when round 2 begins · Key: combat.counterattack.round-two.return</sub>

<a id="r610.4b"></a>**610.4b** If the first battle round had a battle, only the units sent to counterattack can attack in the second battle round, and every one of them still there and able to attack must attack. In its attack step the non-initiative team puts all of them into formation, in any shape; the shape is chosen then, not when the units are sent. Every spell token sent with them that is still there rides along too (see rule 610.3). A sent unit that died on its return is not owed. See rule 604.2f.

> *Example: The non-initiative player sent Conduit of Pain at block time. In round 2 it is the only unit they can attack with, and it must attack: declining is refused.*

> *Example: Three units were sent. Declining, or leaving one off to the side, is refused; any shape that holds all three is accepted.*

> *Example: Two units were sent and one dies on its return: the other alone is owed, and it forms by itself.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 4 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.20; Manual p.27; Rulebook 2023 p.5; Rulebook 2023 p.5 · Designer: RQ 1171229657740345384 · Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16; Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 32-cast-costs.test.ts, 02-combat.test.ts, 479-empty-attack-and-committed-counterattack.test.ts · Example tests: 32-cast-costs.test.ts::forcedAction: a single sent counterattacker IS auto-formed, 479-empty-attack-and-committed-counterattack.test.ts::CT-298 every sent counterattacker must be in the formation and the counterattack cannot be declined, 479-empty-attack-and-committed-counterattack.test.ts::CT-251 a lone sent counterattacker is formed for the player and one that died on arrival is owed nothing · Key: combat.counterattack.round-two.attackers</sub>

<a id="r610.4c"></a>**610.4c** If the first battle round had a battle and no units were sent to counterattack, there is no second battle round. The battle phase ends after the first round's after combat step. See rules 505.3f, 609.2b.

> *Example: With no counterattack sent, no battle is fought in the initiative player's region.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.21; Manual p.21 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts, 21-fixes.test.ts · Example test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.regions.one-at-a-time.order — with no counterattack sent · Key: combat.counterattack.round-two.none-sent</sub>

<a id="r610.4d"></a>**610.4d** If the initiative team declared no attack in the first battle round, the non-initiative team may still attack in the second battle round. It may attack with any of its units, since it never had a block step in which to send counterattackers. See rules 505.3e, 604.4a.

> *Example: The initiative player could attack and declines; the non-initiative player may then attack with any unit.*
