<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.20 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts, 21-fixes.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Temporal Rift thread: the non-initiative player still attacks when the initiative player declines · Key: combat.counterattack.round-two.no-round-one</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U13-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r610.4e"></a>**610.4e** The non-initiative team may decline to attack in the second battle round only when no unit it sent to counterattack is still there and able to attack, or when the first battle round had no attack (see rule 610.4d). A counterattack with such a unit cannot be declined. A declined second round has no battle and opens no priority window, and the battle phase ends. See rules 604.2a, 604.4.

> *Example: Two units were sent. In round 2 declining is refused, and so is leaving one of them behind; every formation offered holds both.*

> *Example: The initiative player declined to attack in round 1. In round 2 the non-initiative player may decline too, and the battle phase ends.*

> *Example: The initiative player's spell tokens at home cannot be cast in any round-1 window. If the non-initiative player's only counterattacker then dies on its return, round 2 has no attack, and those tokens never become castable this battle.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 4 tests, all passed; 4 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.20 · Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16; Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 424-cr-after-combat.test.ts, 32-cast-costs.test.ts, 165-token-loss-warning.test.ts, 479-empty-attack-and-committed-counterattack.test.ts · Example tests: 424-cr-after-combat.test.ts::cr:combat.counterattack.round-two.may-decline — declining is refused while a sent unit lives, 479-empty-attack-and-committed-counterattack.test.ts::CT-298 a second round after a first round with no attack is a fresh attack and may still be declined, 165-token-loss-warning.test.ts::[CT-55] the premise: a round-2 defender really is holding castable tokens when the attacker declines · Key: combat.counterattack.round-two.may-decline</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U13-3, D-U13-4 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r610.4f"></a>**610.4f** In the second battle round the initiative team declares blocks only. It cannot send units to counterattack, because each team gets only one chance to attack. See rules 505.3d, 606.5b.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.20; Rulebook 2023 p.5 · Tests: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts, 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts::cr:combat.attack.general.rounds · Key: combat.counterattack.round-two.no-counter</sub>

<a id="r610.4g"></a>**610.4g** In every priority window of the second battle round, the initiative player receives priority first, although it is now the defending player. See rules 605.1a, 703.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.30 · Tests: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts::cr:combat.attack-window.general.initiative-first · Key: combat.counterattack.round-two.initiative-priority</sub>

<a id="r610.4h"></a>**610.4h** While the second battle round is resolved, units in the region where the first round was fought are treated as if they do not exist. They include the units the initiative team attacked with and any unit created there during the first round, so none of them can block in the second round. See rules 505.4c, 304.8a.

> *Example: Tidelurker's 2/2, created mid-attack in the enemy region, stays there and cannot block the counterattack.*

> *Example: A spell token the initiative player keeps at home cannot be cast in any round-1 window, and can be cast in round 2's windows.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.21; Manual p.21 · Tests: 424-cr-after-combat.test.ts, 98-spawn-region.test.ts, 165-token-loss-warning.test.ts · Example tests: 98-spawn-region.test.ts::CR 304.8a inverts the withdrawn home-region reading: Tidelurker's mid-attack 2/2 stays in the enemy region and CANNOT block the counterattack, 165-token-loss-warning.test.ts::[CT-55] the premise · Key: combat.counterattack.round-two.other-region-absent</sub>

<a id="r610.5"></a>**610.5.** A battle phase has at most two battle rounds. After the second round's after combat step, battle ends and regroup begins. See rules 505.3d, 506.

> *Example: In round 2 the initiative player cannot send units out to counterattack, and the battle phase ends after round 2.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.5; Rulebook 2023 p.5; Manual p.20 · Tests: 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts · Example test: 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts::cr:turn.battle.rounds.one-attack-each · Key: combat.counterattack.no-later-rounds</sub>

<a id="r610.6"></a>**610.6.** In team games, combat is first resolved completely in every region the initiative team attacked. Then combat is resolved in the regions the non-initiative team counterattacked. See rules 505.4, 904. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

> *Example: In a 2v2 game the initiative team attacks both non-initiative regions. Both of those battles are resolved, one region at a time, before any counterattack battle in an initiative region begins.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; no gate test · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.9; Rulebook 2023 p.9; Manual p.27 · Key: combat.counterattack.teams</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U13-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

## 7. Spells, Abilities and Effects

<a id="r700"></a>
### 700. General

<a id="r700.1"></a>**700.1.** An effect is anything on the stack. Whenever a card is played, or an ability is activated or triggered, it is added to the stack as an effect. A unit or spell unit on the stack is an effect too. See rule 703.

> *Example: a {Battle} unit being played sits on the stack and can be chosen by an effect that says "target effect" (Dematerialize).*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.28; Manual p.28 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 118-stack-effect.test.ts · Example test: 118-stack-effect.test.ts::CR 700.1: a unit on the stack is a legal "target effect" (Dematerialize) · Key: effects.general.effect</sub>

<a id="r700.1a"></a>**700.1a** A spell effect is an effect that is a spell: a spell, a spell unit or a spell token on the stack. A unit on the stack is an effect but not a spell effect, and neither is an Ambush, since the card played as an Ambush is a unit: a card that says "spell effect" cannot affect either of them.

> *Example: Null Drone ("target spell effect") cannot choose a plain unit on the stack, but can choose a spell unit.*

> *Example: Dreadwave Devourer ("Negate target spell effect") cannot target an Ambush on the stack, and the Ambush resolves.*

> *Example: A spell unit and a spell token on the stack are spell effects; an Ambush is not.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RQ 1127377066195697725; RQ 1138951204257402973 · Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16; Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 118-stack-effect.test.ts, 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts, 476-ambush-spell-sweep.test.ts · Example tests: 118-stack-effect.test.ts::"target spell effect" refuses a plain unit but takes a spell unit, 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts::cr:keywords.abilities.ambush.spell-effect — Dreadwave Devourer, which negates a target spell effect, cannot target an Ambush, 476-ambush-spell-sweep.test.ts::the predicate: an Ambush is not a spell effect, a spell unit and a spell token are · Key: effects.general.effect.spell-effect</sub>

<a id="r700.1b"></a>**700.1b** A nonspell effect is any effect that is not a spell effect: a triggered ability, an activated ability, a Virus being applied, a unit on the stack, or an Ambush.

> *Example: Nothyr ("negate up to one target nonspell effect") can choose a {Battle} unit on the stack.*

> *Example: Nothyr can also choose an Ambush on the stack.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 4 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RQ 1127377066195697725 · Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16; Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 118-stack-effect.test.ts, 114-literal-dark.test.ts, 475-ambush-is-not-a-spell.test.ts · Example tests: 118-stack-effect.test.ts::Nothyr's "target nonspell effect" reaches a unit on the stack, 114-literal-dark.test.ts::Nothyr: an AMBUSH is a nonspell effect, so it is in reach (report 218) · Key: effects.general.effect.nonspell-effect</sub>

<a id="r700.2"></a>**700.2.** Casting a spell is playing it. The printed rules use "cast" and "play" for the same act, and casting a spell token is playing a spell. See rule 701.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; no gate test · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.13; Manual p.30 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30, 2026-09-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Key: effects.general.cast-is-play</sub>

<a id="r700.3"></a>**700.3.** Players interact by playing cards and activating abilities in response to one another. All interaction uses the stack (rule 703). See rule 703.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.14 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.general.interaction — a spell, a battle unit, a virus and an activated ability played in battle all go on the stack · Key: effects.general.interaction</sub>

<a id="r701"></a>
### 701. Playing and Applying

<a id="r701.1"></a>**701.1.** Only units and spells are played, whatever zone they are played from. Applying a modification is not playing a card (701.2).

> *Example: Godray and Monke played from hand, and Trench Stalker played from the bin, are plays; a Virus applied to the attacker is not.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 105-semantics-playwatch.test.ts, 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts, 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.playing.what-is-played — a unit and a spell played from hand and a unit played from the bin are plays; a virus applied is not · Key: effects.playing.what-is-played</sub>

<a id="r701.1a"></a>**701.1a** Playing a spell unit is playing a spell.

> *Example: a spell unit played through Hooba-Pon counts as a spell played.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1461450216874967235#2 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Hooba-Pon spell unit: it counts as playing a spell · Key: effects.playing.what-is-played.spell-unit</sub>

<a id="r701.1b"></a>**701.1b** Casting a spell token is playing a spell. A spell token is never in a hand; it is cast from play, so it is played from somewhere other than the hand. See rule 702.7.

> *Example: casting a Fireball token triggers Stalwart Sentinel ("when you play a card from anywhere other than your hand").*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1355689559609839787#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-28, 2026-10-10 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts, 337-spell-tokens-are-played.test.ts · Example test: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts::casting a Fireball token triggers Stalwart Sentinel · Key: effects.playing.what-is-played.spell-token</sub>

<a id="r701.1c"></a>**701.1c** A token is not a card. An ability or cost modifier that refers to a "card" being played does not apply to a spell token being cast; one that refers to a "spell" does; one that refers to a "nontoken spell" does not. See rule 108.

> *Example: Arbiter of Armistice ("Cards played during battle gain [Pay 2 life]") does not make a spell token cost life.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 337-spell-tokens-are-played.test.ts · Example test: 337-spell-tokens-are-played.test.ts::CR 701.1c: Arbiter of Armistice prints Cards, so a token cast pays no life · Key: effects.playing.what-is-played.token-not-card</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U06-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r701.1d"></a>**701.1d** Creating a token is not playing it. See rule 304.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts · Key: effects.playing.what-is-played.token-creation</sub>

<a id="r701.1e"></a>**701.1e** An ability that triggers whenever its controller plays a unit works only while its card is in play. A card that is being played is on the stack, not in play, so its own play does not trigger it, whether or not the ability says "another". See rule 706.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-11 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 444-no-self-hearing-play.test.ts · Key: effects.playing.what-is-played.includes-itself</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U14-11 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r701.2"></a>**701.2.** Applying a modification (an augment, a graft, or a Virus) is not playing a card. A modification is applied, whether it comes from a hand, a bin, a cache or elsewhere. Applying a modification is a special action. See rule 720.

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.32 · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 105-semantics-playwatch.test.ts, 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts, 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.playing.applying — a graft from hand and a virus from the cache are applied, never played · Key: effects.playing.applying</sub>

<a id="r701.2a"></a>**701.2a** An ability that triggers when a player plays a unit, a spell or a card does not trigger when a modification is applied, including one applied from the bin.

> *Example: Ravenous Fireslinger does not trigger when its controller applies an augment, and does trigger on a real spell.*

> *Example: Applying a Virus during battle is not playing a card, so Void Mandible does not react to it.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 105-semantics-playwatch.test.ts, 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts · Example tests: 105-semantics-playwatch.test.ts::Ravenous Fireslinger: CR 701.2a, 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts::CR 701.2a holds: applying a VIRUS fires neither event · Key: effects.playing.applying.no-play-triggers</sub>

<a id="r701.2b"></a>**701.2b** A modifier to the cost of playing cards does not change the cost of applying a modification. A modification still needs its own affinity and its own mana cost to be applied. See rule 111.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.32 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-08-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts::RAQ Mods are NOT Played: a Virus in battle needs its affinity and pays its cost · Key: effects.playing.applying.cost</sub>

<a id="r701.2c"></a>**701.2c** Tides of the Cosmos is the one exception. Although it says "play", it may put a Virus card onto a unit as a Virus, and it may play a card as an Ambush or a Prophecy. It cannot graft a card or apply a non-Virus augment.

> *Example: a Virus card that Tides of the Cosmos plays as a Virus is attached to a unit and never enters play.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#2; RAQ 1396955380000755795#2; RAQ 1396955380000755795#3; RAQ 1357483405276614856#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 404-raq-fix-tides.test.ts, 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 404-raq-fix-tides.test.ts::CR 701.2c: a Virus card played by Tides as a Virus augments a unit and never enters play · Key: effects.playing.applying.tides</sub>

<a id="r701.3"></a>**701.3.** Putting a card into play is not playing it. Whether an effect plays a card or puts it into play is decided by the verb the effect prints.

> *Example: Covenant of the Damned puts a unit from the bin into play; only Covenant itself was played.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.43 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.playing.put-into-play — a unit put into play by Covenant of the Damned is not played · Key: effects.playing.put-into-play</sub>

<a id="r701.3a"></a>**701.3a** A spell unit that enters play without being played (for example, one put into play from a bin) does not produce its spell effect.

> *Example: Covenant of the Damned puts Lonely Forager into play from the bin; Forager does not draw a card.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.43; Manual p.43 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.playing.put-into-play.spell-unit — Lonely Forager put into play from the bin by Covenant of the Damned draws no card · Key: effects.playing.put-into-play.spell-unit</sub>

<a id="r701.4"></a>**701.4.** A card played during the resolution of another effect is played. During battle it is put on the stack and can be responded to (rule 703.5), and abilities that trigger on a play see it. See rule 703.5. *(Engine differs, see F-U14-3.)*

> *Example: Tides of the Cosmos plays a unit, and Bloomcaster's "Whenever you play a unit" triggers on it.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1396955380000755795#8 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 169-mid-resolution-window.test.ts, 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Tides 7: a free play is a play · Key: effects.playing.mid-resolution</sub>

<a id="r701.4a"></a>**701.4a** A card played by an effect is played from the zone it came out of. If it came out of a hand, it is played from the hand. If it came out of the cache, a bin, the deck or anywhere else, it is not played from the hand.

> *Example: Tides of the Cosmos plays a card off the top of the deck, so Proph and Stalwart Sentinel see a play from somewhere other than the hand.*

> *Example: Hooba-Pon plays a unit from its controller's hand, so neither Proph nor Stalwart Sentinel triggers.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 241-played-from-zone.test.ts · Example tests: 241-played-from-zone.test.ts::CR 410.6: Tides of the Cosmos plays off the top of the deck, 241-played-from-zone.test.ts::CR 701.4a: Hooba-Pon plays from the hand · Key: effects.playing.mid-resolution.zone</sub>

<a id="r701.5"></a>**701.5.** A copy of a spell is not played. It does not trigger abilities that trigger on playing, and it is not counted as a played spell. See rule 710.

> *Example: Earthbound Replicator does not copy its own copy.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355613076506017894#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 138-spell-copy.test.ts · Example test: 138-spell-copy.test.ts::a copy is not PLAYED, so it fires no play event · Key: effects.playing.copy-not-played</sub>

<a id="r702"></a>
### 702. Casting Spells

<a id="r702.1"></a>**702.1.** To play a card, a player must meet its affinity requirement, pay its mana cost, select its targets as it is played, and resolve whatever is inside its brackets (an additional cost to pay or a mode to choose). See rules 105, 110, 111.

> *Example: Arc Lightning (rr, cost 4) cannot be played with four water resources (no affinity) or with only two fire resources (not enough mana); with two fire and two water it can.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.13; Manual p.13; Manual p.13 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.casting.requirements — Arc Lightning is not playable without its affinity, nor without its mana, and is with both · Key: effects.casting.requirements</sub>

<a id="r702.1a"></a>**702.1a** A player must meet a card's affinity requirement to be able to play it, unless an effect lets it be played ignoring affinity. See rule 105.

> *Example: Tides of the Cosmos plays a fire unit for a player who has only water resources.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13 · Designer: RAQ 1396955380000755795#0 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Tides 1: a free play ignores affinity · Key: effects.casting.requirements.affinity</sub>

<a id="r702.1b"></a>**702.1b** To pay a card's mana cost, the player expends a number of unexpended resources equal to that cost. See rule 106.

> *Example: playing Arc Lightning, cost 4, expends four of the player’s unexpended resources.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.13 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.casting.requirements.mana — playing Arc Lightning (cost 4) expends four unexpended resources · Key: effects.casting.requirements.mana</sub>

<a id="r702.1c"></a>**702.1c** A card can be played only when its timing allows (rule 207). A card with no timing icon can be played only during deployment. See rules 207, 504.

> *Example: Lonely Forager has no timing icon: it can be played in deployment but not in battle.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.casting.requirements.timing — a card with no timing icon is playable in deployment and not in battle · Key: effects.casting.requirements.timing</sub>

<a id="r702.2"></a>**702.2.** A card in the cache under a live permission may be played in every way it could be played from the hand. It is still not in the hand. See rule 403.

> *Example: a glimpsed Virus in the cache can be applied onto an enemy unit in battle.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-04 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 369-cache-is-the-hand.test.ts, 370-cached-virus-in-battle.test.ts · Example test: 370-cached-virus-in-battle.test.ts::CR 723.2a: a glimpsed Virus in the cache goes onto an ENEMY unit in battle · Key: effects.casting.other-zones</sub>

<a id="r702.2a"></a>**702.2a** A card played from the cache or a bin under a permission still obeys its own printed timing; the permission itself never waives timing. Apart from the timing grants that also work from the cache (rule 702.2d), only an effect that says the card may be played now, such as Tides of the Cosmos, lets it ignore its timing. See rules 207, 405.

> *Example: Tides of the Cosmos plays a deploy-timing unit in battle.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1396955380000755795#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25, 2026-10-04 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts, 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Tides 2: a free play ignores timing · Key: effects.casting.other-zones.timing</sub>

<a id="r702.2b"></a>**702.2b** A card that says it can't be played from your hand is restricted from that zone only. It may still be played from another zone that allows it.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Calming Force · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts · Key: effects.casting.other-zones.hand-restriction</sub>

<a id="r702.2c"></a>**702.2c** Permission to play a card "as if it had [Haste]" does not let a {Battle} card be played outside battle. See rule 504.

> *Example: Dispatch Courier cannot let a {Battle} spell unit be played in the haste step.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1465292396664193171#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Dispatch Courier: a Battle spell unit is not playable in the haste step either · Key: effects.casting.other-zones.haste-grant</sub>

<a id="r702.2d"></a>**702.2d** The rules that widen a card's timing when it is played from hand also widen it when it is played from the cache: a haste grant such as Dispatch Courier's, the erase-funded haste play of Writhing Host, Ambush, and the battle {Virus} augment window. See rules 504, 702.2c.

> *Example: a glimpsed {Virus} card in the cache can be augmented onto a unit in a battle window, as it could from hand.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-10-04 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: partial in round 3; verifier ran 4 tests (a probe it wrote), 1 failed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 369-cache-is-the-hand.test.ts, 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.casting.other-zones.cache-widening — a glimpsed Virus in the cache augments onto a unit in a battle window · Key: effects.casting.other-zones.cache-widening</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U14-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r702.3"></a>**702.3.** Playing a card follows the steps below, in order. Everything the play needs is declared and paid before the card is put on the stack, so no player can respond to an undeclared or unpaid play.

> *Example: while Sacrificial Burst’s target and sacrifice are being chosen, nothing is on the stack and the opponent has no action; it reaches the stack only once both are done.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#12 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25, 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.casting.procedure — while Sacrificial Burst is being declared and paid it is not on the stack and the opponent cannot act · Key: effects.casting.procedure</sub>

<a id="r702.3a"></a>**702.3a** Step 1: if the card has an X, the player chooses X. A variable additional cost (one whose amount is X) is paid at this step, and the amount paid is X. The card's mana cost is paid at the start of the play. See rule 107.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-08-21 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; no gate test · Key: effects.casting.procedure.x</sub>

<a id="r702.3b"></a>**702.3b** Step 2: the player chooses any {Modular} modifications for the card. See rule 724.

> *Example: Spellbind asks for its {Modular} mods as it is played; the chosen mod goes on the stack with it.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.casting.procedure.modular — Spellbind asks for its Modular mods as it is played, and the chosen mod rides onto the stack with it · Key: effects.casting.procedure.modular</sub>

<a id="r702.3c"></a>**702.3c** Step 3: the player declares every target the card's text names (rule 110). See rule 110.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 68-target-conformance.test.ts · Key: effects.casting.procedure.targets</sub>

<a id="r702.3d"></a>**702.3d** Step 4: if a bracket in the card's text offers a choice of modes, the owner of the effect chooses one. See rule 702.5.

> *Example: Wither and Bloom declares which half it is before anyone may respond.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-01 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 97-mode-conformance.test.ts · Example test: 97-mode-conformance.test.ts::CR 702.5: Wither and Bloom declares which half before anyone may respond · Key: effects.casting.procedure.modes</sub>

<a id="r702.3e"></a>**702.3e** Step 5: a card that may be played into a formation has its place in the formation chosen. See rule 602.

> *Example: Tiderunner Initiate’s place in the formation is chosen as it is played, before it is on the stack.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.casting.procedure.spot — Tiderunner Initiate has its formation spot chosen as it is played, and the spot rides on the stack · Key: effects.casting.procedure.spot</sub>

<a id="r702.3f"></a>**702.3f** Step 6: the player pays the card's fixed additional costs, after everything else has been declared. See rule 111.

> *Example: Sacrificial Burst asks for its target before its sacrifice; Trench Stalker asks for its formation spot before its two discards.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21, 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.casting.procedure.fixed-costs — Sacrificial Burst asks for its target before its sacrifice, and Trench Stalker for its spot before its discards · Key: effects.casting.procedure.fixed-costs</sub>

<a id="r702.3g"></a>**702.3g** Step 7: options that a card offers "as you play" a spell (Maelstrom Charger) are taken. Such an option is not an effect: it never goes on the stack and cannot be responded to. See rule 710.

> *Example: the Maelstrom Charger option is asked while the spell is played and never reaches the stack.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1379132904931594372#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts · Example test: 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts::CR 702.3g Maelstrom Charger: the option is asked in the cast window and never reaches the stack · Key: effects.casting.procedure.as-you-play</sub>

<a id="r702.3h"></a>**702.3h** Step 8: the card is put on the stack as an effect (rule 703). See rule 703.

> *Example: once Arc Lightning has been declared and paid, it is on the stack as a spell effect controlled by its player, and no longer in hand.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.28; Manual p.28 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.casting.procedure.stack — once declared and paid, Arc Lightning is on the stack as a spell effect, out of the hand · Key: effects.casting.procedure.stack</sub>

<a id="r702.4"></a>**702.4.** Every cost of playing a card is paid before the card is put on the stack. No player can respond to the payment, or between a cost and the effect it pays for. See rule 111.

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; no gate test · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#12 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Key: effects.casting.costs</sub>

<a id="r702.4a"></a>**702.4a** A card whose costs cannot all be paid cannot be played.

> *Example: with nothing to sacrifice, Tides of the Cosmos does not offer Volatile Toxicity.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 404-raq-fix-tides.test.ts · Example test: 404-raq-fix-tides.test.ts::with nothing to sacrifice, Tides does not offer Volatile Toxicity · Key: effects.casting.costs.unpayable</sub>

<a id="r702.4b"></a>**702.4b** Negating a card does not refund the costs paid to play it. See rule 704.4.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; no gate test · Key: effects.casting.costs.no-refund</sub>

<a id="r702.4c"></a>**702.4c** A unit sacrificed to pay a cost is gone before the card is played, so it does not see that card being played.

> *Example: Ravenous Fireslinger sacrificed to pay for Sacrificial Burst does not trigger on it.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1460212274936414381#0 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ cost vs trigger: a unit sacrificed to pay a spell cost never sees that spell played · Key: effects.casting.costs.sacrifice-gone</sub>

<a id="r702.4d"></a>**702.4d** A cost cannot be paid with something that does not exist yet: not with units the effect itself would create, and not with a unit played by the same effect, which is on the stack and not in play.

> *Example: Volatile Toxicity played by Tides of the Cosmos cannot sacrifice a Towering Colossus played by the same Tides.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#12 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Tides 5: · Key: effects.casting.costs.not-yet-in-play</sub>

<a id="r702.4e"></a>**702.4e** A card played during another effect's resolution pays its bracketed additional cost exactly as if it were played from a hand.

> *Example: a Trench Stalker played through Hooba-Pon discards two cards.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 404-raq-fix-tides.test.ts · Example test: 404-raq-fix-tides.test.ts::CR 702.4e: a unit played by Hooba-Pon pays its additional cost · Key: effects.casting.costs.mid-resolution</sub>

<a id="r702.5"></a>**702.5.** A printed square bracket in a card's text is either an additional cost or a choice of modes. The owner of the effect pays that cost or chooses that mode, when the effect is played or put on the stack, and at no other time. See rules 205, 111.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.13 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-01 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Key: effects.casting.brackets</sub>

<a id="r702.5a"></a>**702.5a** A payment an effect's text asks for without brackets, such as "unless its controller pays [x]", is not a cost of playing. It is made while the effect resolves, by the player the text names (rule 704.1). See rule 704.1.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-09-01 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; no gate test · Key: effects.casting.brackets.unbracketed-payment</sub>

<a id="r702.6"></a>**702.6.** X is chosen when the card is played, before it is put on the stack. Only values the player can pay may be chosen, and responses see the X already fixed. When X counts targets ("X target units"), all X targets are required: only an X that many legal targets can fill may be chosen, and at X = 0 the card needs no target. See rule 107.

> *Example: Blight's End ("Augment a Wight onto X target units") with one unit in the battle offers X of 0 or 1, and at X = 1 it must take that unit.*

> *Example: Blight's End cast for X = 2 with two units asks for both and never offers a stop after one.*

> *Example: Torrential Reclamation ("Recall X target nontoken allies") with no ally in the fight can be cast only for X = 0.*

<sub>Basis: Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16; Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 6 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 478-required-targets-at-cast.test.ts, 477-target-minimum-sweep.test.ts · Example tests: 478-required-targets-at-cast.test.ts::Blight End with one unit in the battle offers X up to 1 only, and X = 1 needs its target, 478-required-targets-at-cast.test.ts::Blight End with two units asks for both at X = 2, never offering a stop at one, 478-required-targets-at-cast.test.ts::Torrential Reclamation with no ally in the fight is castable at X = 0 only · Key: effects.casting.x</sub>

<a id="r702.6a"></a>**702.6a** If a card says X can't be zero, X must be at least 1. A player with less open mana than the smallest legal X cannot play the card.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; no gate test · Key: effects.casting.x.minimum</sub>

<a id="r702.6b"></a>**702.6b** A variable additional cost sets X. The player pays it one unit at a time until they stop, and the amount paid is X.

> *Example: a player removes two +1/+1 counters for Discharge, one at a time, then stops; X is 2 and Discharge deals 2 damage.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.casting.x.variable-cost — Discharge with two counters removed one at a time has X = 2 and deals 2 · Key: effects.casting.x.variable-cost</sub>

<a id="r702.6c"></a>**702.6c** An X spell released for free by a fulfilled prophecy is cast with X = 0. A variable bracketed cost on it is still collected. See rule 803.

> *Example: a fulfilled prophecy releases an X spell; no X is asked, X is 0 and no mana is paid.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Example test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 803.7j: a fulfilled prophecy releases an X spell for X = 0 · Key: effects.casting.x.free</sub>

<a id="r702.7"></a>**702.7.** A spell token is cast from play, and only in the region the token is in. Otherwise it is cast the same way as a spell from the hand. See rule 304.

> *Example: In the attack window the defending player casts their Fireball 3 token in the battle region. They choose its target, the attacking player, and it goes on the stack, where the attacker may respond; when both pass it deals 3.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.4; Rulebook 2023 p.4 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.casting.spell-tokens — casting a spell token asks for its target and puts it on the stack, as a spell from hand would · Key: effects.casting.spell-tokens</sub>

<a id="r702.7a"></a>**702.7a** A modifier to the cost of playing spells applies to casting a spell token, and a spell token cast counts as a spell played. See rule 111.

> *Example: Tranquility makes a spell token cost [1] more in battle.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 337-spell-tokens-are-played.test.ts · Example test: 337-spell-tokens-are-played.test.ts::CR 702.7a: Tranquility taxes a spell token [1] in battle · Key: effects.casting.spell-tokens.taxed</sub>

<a id="r702.7b"></a>**702.7b** A spell token with Burst is cast together with all of its controller's spell tokens of the same name in the same region as it. They are still separate spells. See rules 803, 703.4.

> *Example: A player with two Fireballs in the battle region casts one; both go on the stack. A Fireball the same player has in another region is not cast.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.4; Rulebook 2023 p.4; Rulebook 2023 p.4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-01 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.casting.spell-tokens.burst — both battle-region Fireballs are cast together and one in another region is not · Key: effects.casting.spell-tokens.burst</sub>

<a id="r702.8"></a>**702.8.** A card or ability that needs targets can be played only if every target it requires can be chosen at the same time, each one legal and different from the others. Every target is required unless the card says "up to" or "any number". A triggered ability's targets are required in the same way: if a legal target exists, it must take one, even one of its controller's own units. A triggered ability whose "you may" governs its target ("you may recall target ally") offers the decline at the time its targets are chosen: its controller chooses a target or declines, and a declined ability does nothing. Once it has one target, every other target it needs is required. Choosing a target is choosing to use it, so no second "you may" is asked as it resolves; a payment its text asks for is still asked then (see rule 111.9). See rule 110.

> *Example: Fight cannot be played unless the region holds an ally and another unit.*

> *Example: Tidal Reversion cannot be played while one player has no unit to recall.*

> *Example: Unstable Singularity ("When I die, Delete target unit.") dies in deployment with only its controller's other unit on the board: its trigger must target that unit, with no option to choose none, and deletes it.*

> *Example: Shoreline Specter ("After combat, you may recall target ally. If you do, each opponent loses 2 life.") offers the decline beside its allies as its trigger goes on the stack. Declined, nothing is recalled and no opponent loses life.*

> *Example: Shoreline Specter given a target recalls that ally and each opponent loses 2 life, with no further question as it resolves.*

> *Example: Chombot ("You may move up to two counters from target unit onto another target unit") may be declined before its first target; once one is chosen, the second is required.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 9 tests, all passed; 6 gate test files · Printed: card: Shoreline Specter · Designer: RAQ 1410252965276684418#0; RAQ 1410252965276684418#1; RAQ 1410252965276684418#3 · Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16, 2026-10-21; Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 401-raq-fix-stack.test.ts, 477-target-minimum-sweep.test.ts, 478-required-targets-at-cast.test.ts, 182-correctness-sample.test.ts, 512-may-target-decline.test.ts · Example tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ target requirements: Fight cannot be played without an ally and another unit in the region, 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ target requirements: Tidal Reversion is not playable while one player has no unit to recall, 477-target-minimum-sweep.test.ts::a must-target trigger with only the controllers own units as targets picks one of them, 512-may-target-decline.test.ts::CT-309 Shoreline Specter declined at the target step: no recall and no life loss, 512-may-target-decline.test.ts::CT-309 Shoreline Specter given a target recalls it and drains with no further prompt, 512-may-target-decline.test.ts::CT-309 Chombot: once one target is picked both are required, and a decline does not spend the use · Key: effects.casting.targets-required</sub>

<a id="r702.8a"></a>**702.8a** A card that targets nothing has no target requirement.

> *Example: Rebalance can be played by a player with no unit.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1454169054402314362#1 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::Rebalance is playable with no unit of your own · Key: effects.casting.targets-required.untargeted</sub>

<a id="r702.8b"></a>**702.8b** A triggered graft composite whose targeted part has no legal target is not put on the stack at all, and its untargeted parts do not happen either. See rules 722, 706. *(Engine differs, see F-U14-1.)*

> *Example: Megadeath grafted with Resurrect, and no unit of cost 2 or less in the bin: no Poison 5 is made.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1410252965276684418#2 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ target requirements: a graft trigger with a required target and none available makes nothing at all · Key: effects.casting.targets-required.graft-trigger</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U14-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r703"></a>
### 703. The Stack and Priority

<a id="r703.1"></a>**703.1.** The stack is "first in, last out". A new effect is put on top of the effects already there. When it is time to resolve, the top effect resolves first, so the effect put on last resolves first.

> *Example: Mycelial Mentor is played with Bloomcaster out. Bloomcaster's trigger goes on the stack above the Mentor, so its 1/1 is made before the Mentor arrives and the Mentor never sees it.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.14; Rulebook 2023 p.14 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Bloomcaster: its 1/1 resolves before the Mycelial Mentor it was played with arrives · Key: effects.priority.stack</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U01-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r703.1a"></a>**703.1a** An effect put on the stack does not resolve immediately. This gives the other players in the region a chance to respond to it.

> *Example: Luminous Arc is cast at a unit; the unit is undamaged while the Arc waits on the stack, and the other player may respond.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.28; Manual p.28 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.priority.stack.not-immediate — a cast Luminous Arc waits on the stack, its target untouched, while the other player may respond · Key: effects.priority.stack.not-immediate</sub>

<a id="r703.1b"></a>**703.1b** New effects can be added on top of the stack after it has started resolving, between the resolutions of the effects on it.

> *Example: two Luminous Arcs are on the stack; after the top one resolves, a third Arc is cast and resolves before the one still waiting.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.14; Manual p.28 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.priority.stack.add-while-resolving — after the top of a two-item stack resolves, a new spell goes on above the remaining item and resolves first · Key: effects.priority.stack.add-while-resolving</sub>

<a id="r703.1c"></a>**703.1c** A triggered ability put on the stack can be responded to like any other effect. See rule 706.

> *Example: Xenopod Progenitor's trigger is negated on the stack, and its controller is never asked to pay its [1].*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.28 · Designer: RAQ 1397189214352703590#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-29 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts, 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ Xenopod: negated on the stack, it never asks for the [1] · Key: effects.priority.stack.triggers-respondable</sub>

<a id="r703.2"></a>**703.2.** Priority is the ability to take game actions such as playing cards or activating abilities. A player with priority can take such actions; a player without priority cannot.

> *Example: In the attack window only the initiative player, who holds priority, may play a card; the other player cannot until they receive priority.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.30; Manual p.30 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.priority.priority — only the player with priority may play a card · Key: effects.priority.priority</sub>

<a id="r703.2a"></a>**703.2a** A player who uses priority to take an action may keep priority and take further actions. Each action goes on the stack as an effect; none of them happens immediately. *(Engine differs, see F-U14-2.) (Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), 1 failed; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.30; Manual p.30 · Key: effects.priority.priority.hold</sub>

<a id="r703.2b"></a>**703.2b** When a player passes priority after taking one or more actions, each other player receives priority, so that they can respond. This continues until all players pass priority in succession.

> *Example: after a cast the other player receives priority and responds; the first player then receives priority again, and the top item resolves only after both pass in succession.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.30; Manual p.30 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.priority.priority.pass — after an action the other player receives priority, and the item resolves only once both pass in succession · Key: effects.priority.priority.pass</sub>

<a id="r703.2c"></a>**703.2c** A player cannot respond to another player passing priority. A player who passes may not get another chance to act.

> *Example: the defender passes on an Arc and the attacker passes; the Arc resolves at once, with no further chance for the defender.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.13 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.priority.priority.no-response-to-pass — after one player passes, the other passing resolves the item with no further chance for the first · Key: effects.priority.priority.no-response-to-pass</sub>

<a id="r703.2d"></a>**703.2d** All players on a team share priority and can act in whichever order they choose among themselves. Teams pass and receive priority as one. See rule 904. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.30; Manual p.30 · Key: effects.priority.priority.teams</sub>

<a id="r703.3"></a>**703.3.** A priority window is a sequence in which the players (or teams) each receive priority in order.

> *Example: in an empty attack window the initiative player receives priority, then the other player; when both have passed the step ends.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.30; Manual p.30 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.priority.window — in an empty attack window each player receives priority in turn, initiative first, and then the step moves on · Key: effects.priority.window</sub>

<a id="r703.3a"></a>**703.3a** In a priority window the initiative player receives priority first. If they decline to act, priority passes clockwise to the next non-initiative player in the region. If the initiative player is not in the region, priority begins with the player nearest to the initiative player, clockwise. See rules 508, 903.

> *Example: the defender casts a spell, which resolves; the new window opens with the initiative player, not the caster.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.30; Manual p.30; Manual p.30 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.priority.window.order — a new window opens with the initiative player even when the other player cast the item that just resolved · Key: effects.priority.window.order</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U14-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r703.3b"></a>**703.3b** In each region, the attack step, the block step and the after combat step each have a priority window. The combat damage step has a priority window only between its sub-steps, and only when Swift or Sluggish units split it (rule 608). See rules 604, 605, 607, 608, 609.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.30 · Designer: RAQ 1363298910528864318#0 · Tests: 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts · Key: effects.priority.window.steps</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U14-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r703.3c"></a>**703.3c** When all players pass priority in succession with an effect on the stack, the top effect resolves. All players then receive priority in order again, which is a new priority window. When all players pass priority with the stack empty, the game moves to the next step.

> *Example: two passes resolve Luminous Arc; a new window opens in the same step with the initiative player; two passes on the empty stack end the step.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.30; Manual p.30; Rulebook 2023 p.13 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.priority.window.resolve — two passes resolve the top item, a new window opens, and two passes on the empty stack end the step · Key: effects.priority.window.resolve</sub>

<a id="r703.4"></a>**703.4.** When several effects are put on the stack at the same time, each player chooses the order of their own. The initiative player puts all of theirs on first, then the non-initiative player, so the non-initiative player's effects resolve first. See rule 706.

> *Example: with one trigger per player, the initiative player's trigger is at the bottom of the stack.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.43; Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1540678747953569832#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts · Example test: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts::CR 609.3c RAQ STACK ORDER · Key: effects.priority.simultaneous</sub>

<a id="r703.4a"></a>**703.4a** Cards played by one effect at the same time are separate effects, put on the stack at the same time in an order their controller chooses.

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1396955380000755795#4 · Tests: 169-mid-resolution-window.test.ts · Key: effects.priority.simultaneous.same-effect</sub>

<a id="r703.4b"></a>**703.4b** A Burst group of spell tokens goes on the stack all at once. Its caster chooses the order, one token at a time, and aims each; the token chosen first resolves first. The other players receive priority only when the whole group is on the stack. See rule 803.

> *Example: the first Fireball picked ends on top of the stack.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-01 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 358-burst-order.test.ts · Example test: 358-burst-order.test.ts::CR 803.5d: the caster picks each Fireball in RESOLVE order and aims it · Key: effects.priority.simultaneous.burst</sub>

<a id="r703.5"></a>**703.5.** A card played during another effect's resolution waits on the stack until that resolution has finished. Only then do players receive priority, and they may respond to the played card before it resolves. See rule 701.4. *(Engine differs, see F-U14-3.)*

> *Example: a card Tides of the Cosmos plays for free can be answered on the stack.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), 1 failed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1396955380000755795#4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 169-mid-resolution-window.test.ts · Example test: 169-mid-resolution-window.test.ts::a free play is still a play, so it can be answered on the stack · Key: effects.priority.mid-resolution</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U14-5 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r703.6"></a>**703.6.** Once an effect has begun to resolve, no player can respond to it. It can no longer be targeted, negated or augmented.

> *Example: while Premonition is resolving, the other player is offered nothing, it is not a legal target, and a negation or a Virus aimed at it is refused.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.priority.resolving — while Premonition is resolving it cannot be targeted, negated, augmented or responded to · Key: effects.priority.resolving</sub>

<a id="r703.7"></a>**703.7.** Deployment uses the stack, but each player has a stack of their own there. Only that player sees it and holds priority over it; no other player can respond to it or is made to wait on it. *(Digital client)* See rule 507.

> *Example: In deployment a player plays a deploy-timing spell at their Earthbound Replicator; the spell goes on that player's own stack, so the Replicator can copy it.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-01 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 138-spell-copy.test.ts · Example test: 138-spell-copy.test.ts::CR 507.5/CT-176: a deploy-timing play names a REAL stack item · Key: effects.priority.deployment</sub>

<a id="r703.8"></a>**703.8.** There is no priority in the haste step. Haste cards are played there as special actions. See rule 504.

> *Example: Molten Upheaval played in the haste step makes its Fireball at once; no one has priority and nothing waits on a stack.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.priority.haste-step — in the haste step nobody has priority and a haste card resolves at once with no stack · Key: effects.priority.haste-step</sub>

<a id="r704"></a>
### 704. Resolution and Fizzling

<a id="r704.1"></a>**704.1.** When an effect resolves, its instructions are carried out in the order printed, and a later instruction sees the results of an earlier one. The exception is target legality: it is judged once, as the effect begins to resolve (rule 704.5), so an earlier instruction cannot make a later instruction's target illegal. See rule 704.5.

> *Example: Finality ("Negate all other effects. Erase all cards in bins.") erases the cards it has just negated, because they are in bins by its second sentence.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: partial in round 3; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22, 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Engine: markIllegalTargets · Tests: 61-negation.test.ts · Example test: 61-negation.test.ts::Finality erases the very cards it just negated · Key: effects.resolution.order</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U14-10, D-U14-13 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r704.1a"></a>**704.1a** Choices an effect makes that are not targets (how to divide damage among a player's units, which card to discard, whether to pay an optional amount inside the effect) are made while it resolves. See rule 702.5.

> *Example: Xenopod Progenitor's trigger goes on the stack with no payment asked; its [1] is asked as it resolves.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1397189214352703590#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ Xenopod: the trigger goes on the stack with no payment asked · Key: effects.resolution.order.choices</sub>

<a id="r704.1b"></a>**704.1b** No priority window opens around a payment or choice made while an effect resolves.

> *Example: while Premonition asks its controller which card to cache, the other player has no action; the choice made, Premonition finishes without any pass.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.resolution.order.no-window — the choice Premonition asks while resolving opens no priority window, and the item finishes as soon as it is made · Key: effects.resolution.order.no-window</sub>

<a id="r704.2"></a>**704.2.** When a spell resolves it goes to its controller's bin. When a spell unit resolves it enters play as a unit instead. See rule 405.

> *Example: a resolved Luminous Arc is in its controller’s bin; a resolved Jelly is in play as a unit.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.13 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-29 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.resolution.destination — a resolved spell goes to its controller bin, and a resolved spell unit enters play · Key: effects.resolution.destination</sub>

<a id="r704.2a"></a>**704.2a** A card that goes to a bin from the stack is not trashed. See rule 801.

> *Example: two Luminous Arcs reach the bin from the stack, one resolved and one fizzled; neither is trashed.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.resolution.destination.not-trashed — a spell that resolves into the bin and one that fizzles into it fire no trashed event · Key: effects.resolution.destination.not-trashed</sub>

<a id="r704.2b"></a>**704.2b** A spell token never goes to a bin; it is erased. See rule 304.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.4; Rulebook 2023 p.4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 61-negation.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.destination.token</sub>

<a id="r704.2c"></a>**704.2c** A spell that is Unstable, or that carries a Virus applied to it on the stack, is erased instead of going to a bin, whether it resolves, fizzles or is negated. See rule 723.

> *Example: a spell played from the bin under Abyssal Evocation is Unstable, so it is erased and not put back in the bin.*

> *Example: a spell played from the bin under Abyssal Evocation that fizzles is erased too.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22, 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts, 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Abyssal Evocation: a bin-played spell is {Unstable}, 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.resolution.destination.unstable — a spell played from the bin under Abyssal Evocation that fizzles is erased, not binned · Key: effects.resolution.destination.unstable</sub>

<a id="r704.2d"></a>**704.2d** A copy of a spell has no card. When it resolves or leaves the stack, nothing goes to a bin. See rule 710.

> *Example: a resolved copy of Suspend bins nothing, and its "Erase me." erases nothing.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 138-spell-copy.test.ts · Example test: 138-spell-copy.test.ts::a resolved copy bins nothing · Key: effects.resolution.destination.copy</sub>

<a id="r704.3"></a>**704.3.** A spell unit's spell effect happens first; if it resolves, the unit then enters play. If the spell unit is prevented from resolving (negated, or with its targets made invalid), the unit does not enter play and the card goes to the bin. See rule 303.

> *Example: a spell unit played through Hooba-Pon has its spell part happen, then spawns into the formation.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13 · Designer: RAQ 1461450216874967235#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Hooba-Pon spell unit: the spell part happens, then the unit spawns into the formation · Key: effects.resolution.spell-unit</sub>

<a id="r704.4"></a>**704.4.** A negated effect is removed from the stack at once, when the effect that negates it resolves. It does not resolve.

> *Example: one mass negate removes all its victims from the stack together, with no extra priority rounds.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 61-negation.test.ts · Example test: 61-negation.test.ts::CR 704.4: a mass negate empties the stack of its victims AT ONCE · Key: effects.resolution.negation</sub>

<a id="r704.4a"></a>**704.4a** A negated spell, spell unit, unit, ambush or Virus goes to its controller's bin, and a negated Virus cannot be used as a Virus again. A negated spell token is erased. A negated triggered or activated ability just leaves the stack, because it has no card of its own.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.34; Manual p.34 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 61-negation.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 61-negation.test.ts::CR 704.4a: a negated spell TOKEN is erased, never binned · Key: effects.resolution.negation.destination</sub>

<a id="r704.4b"></a>**704.4b** A negated unit or spell unit never enters play.

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1461450216874967235#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 118-stack-effect.test.ts, 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 118-stack-effect.test.ts::CR 704.4b: negating a unit on the stack · Key: effects.resolution.negation.no-arrival</sub>

<a id="r704.5"></a>**704.5.** As an effect begins to resolve, each target it declared is checked again by the rule it was chosen under: its kind, its printed restriction, its region, and being different from the other targets. A target that fails the check is lost, exactly like a target that has left play. See rule 110.

> *Example: an Ambush whose ally was stolen in response recalls nothing.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355466429788328066#1; RAQ 1355466429788328066#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ valid targets: an Ambush whose ally changed sides before it resolves recalls nothing · Key: effects.resolution.recheck</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U03-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r704.5a"></a>**704.5a** The check is made once, as the effect begins to resolve. An earlier part of the effect cannot make a later part's target illegal in the middle of its resolution. *(Engine differs, see F-U14-9.) (Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Key: effects.resolution.recheck.once</sub>

<a id="r704.5b"></a>**704.5b** A target remains the same object while it stays where it is. A target that changes zone (to a hand, a bin, and so on) is gone, and the effect does not follow it to a new object. A target that stays put is still a legal target even if another effect also targets it. See rule 410.

> *Example: Organic Exchange may target two of its controller's own units, and another spell aimed at one of them still resolves.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.40 · Designer: RAQ 1454169054402314362#2 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::Organic Exchange may target two of your own units · Key: effects.resolution.recheck.same-object</sub>

<a id="r704.5c"></a>**704.5c** Several effects may target the same unit, even if together they would do more than destroying it takes. If an earlier one removes it, the later ones lose that target.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; no gate test · Key: effects.resolution.recheck.shared-target</sub>

<a id="r704.5d"></a>**704.5d** Changing an effect's targets before it resolves can save it from fizzling. See rule 110.

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1354013430805434389#2 · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts · Key: effects.resolution.recheck.retarget</sub>

<a id="r704.6"></a>**704.6.** An effect fizzles if, as it resolves, it has lost all of its targets. A fizzled effect does nothing, and a fizzled spell goes to the bin. See rule 110.

> *Example: Arc Lightning’s only target dies before it resolves; Arc Lightning fizzles, deals no damage and goes to the bin.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1354013430805434389#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts, 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.resolution.fizzle — Arc Lightning whose only target died fizzles, does nothing, and goes to the bin · Key: effects.resolution.fizzle</sub>

<a id="r704.6a"></a>**704.6a** When an effect fizzles, none of it happens, including parts of it that had no target.

> *Example: Spewing Mushroom carries the grafts Biotoxicity ("create three Poison 1") and Technological Superiority, which targets the Mushroom itself. The Mushroom attacks, and the opponent deletes it with Leaping Lillik before its trigger resolves. Its only target is gone, so the whole trigger fizzles: not even Biotoxicity's Poisons are made.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1354013430805434389#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts · Example test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::CR 722.4f: a graft composite that loses its ONLY target fizzles whole · Key: effects.resolution.fizzle.whole</sub>

<a id="r704.6b"></a>**704.6b** If an effect has lost some but not all of its targets, it resolves as best it can against those that remain, untargeted parts included.

> *Example: Tidal Reversion still recalls the other unit when one of its targets is removed.*

> *Example: Twin Flame loses one of its two targets before it resolves; the remaining target still takes its 2 damage.*

> *Example: Spewing Mushroom carries Biotoxicity and two Technological Superiority grafts; when it attacks, the two targeted parts aim at the Mushroom and at an enemy 1/1. The 1/1 dies before the trigger resolves. One target remains, so it still resolves: all four Poison tokens are made.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1410252965276684418#4; RAQ 1354013430805434389#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts, 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ target requirements: Tidal Reversion still recalls the other unit when one target is removed, 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.resolution.fizzle.partial — Twin Flame with one of two targets gone still damages the other, 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.resolution.fizzle.partial — a graft composite with two targets losing one still runs its untargeted part · Demonstrated by test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::CR 704.6b: one surviving target carries the untargeted grafts through · Key: effects.resolution.fizzle.partial</sub>

<a id="r704.6c"></a>**704.6c** An effect that needs two of its targets together (a fight or an exchange) does nothing if it loses one of them. It does not fizzle.

> *Example: Fight that loses one of its two targets does nothing to the survivor.*

> *Example: Organic Exchange that loses one of its two targets exchanges nothing; the survivor stays with its controller.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1354013430805434389#1 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ fizzles: Fight that loses one of its two targets does nothing to the survivor, 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.resolution.fizzle.pair — Organic Exchange that loses one target exchanges nothing · Key: effects.resolution.fizzle.pair</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U14-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r704.6d"></a>**704.6d** An effect that has no targeting part anywhere cannot fizzle. Nor can a part whose target was optional ("up to") and was left empty: declaring no target was a legal choice, and the rest of the effect still happens. See rule 704.6g.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::CR 704.6d: an item that declares NO target anywhere never fizzles · Key: effects.resolution.fizzle.untargeted</sub>

<a id="r704.6e"></a>**704.6e** An ambush is a targeted effect. If its target is removed, the ambush fizzles and the ambushing unit is put into the bin. See rule 803.

> *Example: the ally targeted by Lurking Slimebeast’s ambush dies; the ambush fizzles and Slimebeast goes to the bin.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.40; Manual p.40 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.resolution.fizzle.ambush — Lurking Slimebeast whose ambush target died fizzles and goes to the bin · Key: effects.resolution.fizzle.ambush</sub>

<a id="r704.6f"></a>**704.6f** A Virus whose target has become invalid when it resolves is put into the bin, and cannot be used as a Virus again. See rule 723.

> *Example: a Virus’s host dies before the Virus resolves; the Virus goes to the bin and is not offered as a Virus from there.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.34; Manual p.34 · Tests: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Example test: 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts::cr:effects.resolution.fizzle.virus — a virus whose host died before it resolved goes to the bin and is not offered as a virus again · Key: effects.resolution.fizzle.virus</sub>

<a id="r704.6g"></a>**704.6g** An effect with a required target that never had a legal candidate fizzles, although it declared no target. See rule 704.6d.
