<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::CR 704.6g: a required target with no legal candidate at cast still fizzles · Key: effects.resolution.fizzle.never-had-target</sub>

<a id="r704.7"></a>**704.7.** An effect stays on the stack, and still resolves, if its source leaves play. See rule 714.

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353895783266516992#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ dead unit: an effect stays on the stack when its unit dies and still resolves · Key: effects.resolution.source-gone</sub>

<a id="r704.7a"></a>**704.7a** Where such an effect reads its source (its attributes, power, defense, or the formation it stood in), it uses the source's last-known state: what the source was at the moment it left play. See rule 714.

> *Example: Bellowing Boulder dies with its ping on the stack; the ping is still Deadly, from its last state.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1353895783266516992#6 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 401-raq-fix-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ dead unit: Bellowing Boulder dead with its ping on the stack still pings with Deadly, its last state · Key: effects.resolution.source-gone.last-known</sub>

<a id="r704.7b"></a>**704.7b** An effect that acts on its source itself, or that says "if I am still in formation", does nothing if the source is gone. See rule 714.

> *Example: Hooba-Nan dies with its attack trigger on the stack; the trigger creates no 1/1s.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353895783266516992#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ dead unit: Hooba-Nan gone with its trigger on the stack makes nothing · Key: effects.resolution.source-gone.needs-body</sub>

<a id="r705"></a>
### 705. Activated Abilities

<a id="r705.1"></a>**705.1.** An activated ability is written with a colon (":"). Everything before the colon is the cost of activating the ability; everything after it is the effect the ability has. See rule 109.2.

> *Example: Glook's "[once] Discard X cards: Glimpse 1, X times" — discarding X cards is the cost, and glimpsing X times is the effect.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.41; Manual p.41; Manual p.41 · Tests: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts · Example test: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts::CR 705.3b Glook · Key: effects.activated.what</sub>

<a id="r705.2"></a>**705.2.** An activated ability may print a timing icon of its own. An ability marked {Battle} can be activated only during battle, and one marked {Deployment} only during deployment. The icon is checked when the ability is activated. See rules 109.2a, 109.2b.

> *Example: Grox's ability is marked {Battle}, so it cannot be activated during deployment.*

> *Example: Cadaverous Cultivator's {Battle} ability is refused when activated outside battle, rather than doing nothing when it resolves.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 43-dark-c.test.ts, 45-hybrids-ld-b.test.ts · Example tests: 43-dark-c.test.ts::Grox: CR 705.2 — the printed [Battle] marker is enforced at ACTIVATION, 45-hybrids-ld-b.test.ts::Cadaverous Cultivator: CR 705.2 — [Battle] is enforced at ACTIVATION, not at resolution · Key: effects.activated.timing-icon</sub>

<a id="r705.3"></a>**705.3.** To activate an ability, the player takes the steps below, in order. Everything is chosen and paid before the ability is put on the stack, so no player can respond between the payment of its cost and the ability going on the stack. See rules 111.7, 703.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts::CR 705.3 nothing may act INSIDE the cast window · Key: effects.activated.procedure</sub>

<a id="r705.3a"></a>**705.3a** Step 1: the game checks that the ability can be activated: its timing allows it, any printed condition on it ("Activate this ability only if …") is met, every part of its cost can be paid, and every target it requires has a legal choice. If any check fails, the ability cannot be activated and nothing is paid. See rules 111.6a, 111.7b.

> *Example: Instrument of Reassignment costs [x] and "sacrifice another nontoken unit". With only a token beside it, it cannot be activated, and the 3 open mana are not spent either.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22, 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts, 426-cr-abilities-and-replacement.test.ts · Example test: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts::CR 111.6a the COMPOUND half-pay hazard · Key: effects.activated.procedure.gates</sub>

<a id="r705.3b"></a>**705.3b** Step 2: if the cost has a variable part (a printed [x], "Discard X cards", "Sacrifice X units"), the player pays it, one at a time, until they stop. The amount paid is X. See rules 111.7, 702.6b.

> *Example: Celestial Shifter's "[x]" is paid while activating, so the opponent sees X before deciding whether to respond.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21, 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts · Example test: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts::CR 705.3b Celestial Shifter · Key: effects.activated.procedure.variable-cost</sub>

<a id="r705.3c"></a>**705.3c** Step 3: the player declares the ability's targets. See rule 110.

> *Example: Slag Spewer's target is declared before its mod is erased to pay the cost.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts · Example test: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts::CR 111.2 Slag Spewer · Key: effects.activated.procedure.targets</sub>

<a id="r705.3d"></a>**705.3d** Step 4: the player pays the rest of the cost: its mana, including any tax on activating abilities (rule 111.10f), and any life, debt, sacrifice or other fixed part. See rules 111.7, 111.10f.

> *Example: Auric Ascendant's "Recall another ally" is paid before the ability is on the stack, so the opponent already knows which ally left.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-08-21 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts · Example test: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts::the RECALL is a cost, named before the opponent answers · Key: effects.activated.procedure.fixed-costs</sub>

<a id="r705.3e"></a>**705.3e** Step 5: the ability is put on the stack as an effect, and players receive priority as rule 703 describes. See rule 703.

> *Example: Infernal Cultivator's sacrificed units are gone while the ability waits on the stack, so negating it refunds nothing.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts · Example test: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts::CR 111.7 Infernal Cultivator · Key: effects.activated.procedure.stack</sub>

<a id="r705.4"></a>**705.4.** If a part of an ability's cost names something that is not there to pay with (no other ally to recall, no mod to erase), the ability cannot be activated. Nothing is paid, and a [once] on the ability is not used. See rules 111.6, 109.9b.

> *Example: Auric Ascendant with no other ally cannot be activated, so its [one] is not paid and its [once] is kept.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts · Example test: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts::CR 705.4 Auric Ascendant with no other ally is NOT OFFERED · Key: effects.activated.cost-cannot-whiff</sub>

<a id="r705.5"></a>**705.5.** An activated ability that a mod gives its host is an ability of the host. The host's controller activates it, and "I" and "me" in it mean the host. See rule 720.

> *Example: Living Forge augmented onto another unit lets that unit's controller activate "[three]: create a Robot 2" through the mod.*

> *Example: Aurozoa's "[Augment] Pay 1 life: Recall me" recalls the host when Aurozoa is a mod.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22, 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 27-metal-b.test.ts, 46-hybrids-ld-c.test.ts · Example tests: 27-metal-b.test.ts::Living Forge: donated on a host, the [three] ability activates via the mod, 46-hybrids-ld-c.test.ts::Aurozoa: "[Augment] Pay 1 life: Recall me" — on itself and donated to a host · Key: effects.activated.from-mod</sub>

<a id="r705.6"></a>**705.6.** Some actions are not activated abilities, and rules and effects that apply to activating abilities do not apply to them: applying a mod (an augment or a graft), playing a card as an Ambush, casting a spell token, using a resource, and taking an option a card offers as a spell is played (rule 109.6). See rules 109.6, 701.2, 111.10f.

> *Example: during battle Crevice Lurker taxes activated abilities, but applying an augment costs nothing extra.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24, 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 16-earth-a.test.ts, 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts · Example test: 16-earth-a.test.ts::Crevice Lurker: CR 720.4a — applying an augment during battle is NOT taxed (a mod is not an activation) · Key: effects.activated.not-activations</sub>

<a id="r706"></a>
### 706. Triggered Abilities

<a id="r706.1"></a>**706.1.** A triggered ability is an ability that happens when something else takes place. "When" and "Whenever" mark a triggered ability. A triggered ability can also happen at a stated time, such as "After combat" or "At the end of turn". See rule 109.3.

> *Example: Embermaw Fledgling's "after combat" ability creates an X/X unit after combat.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.41; Manual p.41; Manual p.41; Manual p.41 · Tests: 11-fire-wood.test.ts · Example test: 11-fire-wood.test.ts::Embermaw Fledgling: after combat → X/X, X = attacking units in my formation · Key: effects.triggered.what</sub>

<a id="r706.2"></a>**706.2.** A triggered ability triggers at the moment its event happens, and whether it triggers is decided then (rule 109.3a). It is put on the stack afterwards, at one of the times this section gives, and its targets are chosen and its costs paid only as it is put on the stack. See rules 109.3a, 111.8.

> *Example: a "whenever I am dealt damage" ability triggers inside the combat damage step, but is put on the stack, and has its target chosen, after the step.*

> *Example: the {Alluring} trigger chooses its target as it goes on the stack, and can then be negated.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24, 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts, 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Example tests: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts::CR 608.9: a combat-damage trigger is announced INSIDE the damage step and pushed to the stack AFTER it, 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::the trigger goes on the stack, targets at cast (CR 110.1a), and can be NEGATED · Key: effects.triggered.two-moments</sub>

<a id="r706.3"></a>**706.3.** Triggered abilities that have triggered are put on the stack at the times below, depending on when they triggered.

> *Example: Eminence of the Barrens damaged by a spell in battle has its trigger on the stack as soon as the spell has resolved, while Lithoghul damaged in combat triggers inside the damage step and is put on the stack only in the after combat step.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-29 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 3 gate test files · Tests: 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts, 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts, 426-cr-abilities-and-replacement.test.ts · Example test: 426-cr-abilities-and-replacement.test.ts::cr:effects.triggered.when-stacked — a triggered ability is put on the stack, and when depends on when it triggered: at once outside the damage step, after combat inside it · Key: effects.triggered.when-stacked</sub>

<a id="r706.3a"></a>**706.3a** During battle, outside the combat damage step: as soon as the action or resolution that made them trigger is complete, on top of anything already on the stack. Players then receive priority and may respond to them. See rule 703.

> *Example: Eminence of the Barrens dealt damage by a spell in battle puts its trigger on the stack, and the opponent may respond to it.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-08-29 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts · Example test: 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts::CR 706.3a: a trigger fired OUTSIDE the damage step reaches the stack and IS respondable · Key: effects.triggered.when-stacked.battle</sub>

<a id="r706.3b"></a>**706.3b** During the combat damage step: they wait. They are put on the stack in the after combat step, or at a window between damage sub-steps, as rules 608.9b and 608.9c describe. See rules 608.9b, 608.9c.

> *Example: a "when I die" ability of a unit killed by combat damage waits with the others and goes on the stack after combat.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1540678747953569832#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts · Example test: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts::CR 608.9b: a combat DEATH trigger waits with the rest · Key: effects.triggered.when-stacked.combat-damage</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U04-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r706.3c"></a>**706.3c** During deployment: on the deployment stack of the player who controls them (rule 703.7). All the abilities that trigger at the same moment are put on that stack before any of them resolves. See rule 703.7.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::CR 507.4a: every start-of-deployment trigger is on the stack before any of them resolves · Key: effects.triggered.when-stacked.deployment</sub>

<a id="r706.3d"></a>**706.3d** In the end-of-turn step: they resolve as special actions. No player can play cards in response to them (rule 508.1a). See rule 508.1a.

> *Example: while an end-of-turn trigger is asking its controller a question, neither player may play a card.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.26; Manual p.26; Manual p.26 · Tests: 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts · Example test: 420-cr-battle-regroup-deploy.test.ts::cr:turn.initiative.end-of-turn.no-responses · Key: effects.triggered.when-stacked.end-of-turn</sub>

<a id="r706.4"></a>**706.4.** An ability that triggers on a card being played, or on something being targeted, is put on the stack above the effect that made it trigger, so it resolves first. It still resolves if that effect is negated afterwards.

> *Example: Mycelial Mentor is played while Bloomcaster is in play. Bloomcaster's 1/1 is created before the Mentor arrives, so the Mentor does not see that token being created.*

> *Example: a spell unit that is negated after Bloomcaster triggered still leaves Bloomcaster's 1/1 behind.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353862592661164152#0; RAQ 1353862592661164152#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Bloomcaster: its 1/1 resolves before the Mycelial Mentor it was played with arrives, 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Bloomcaster: a negated spell unit still leaves the Bloomcaster 1/1 behind · Key: effects.triggered.above-cause</sub>

<a id="r706.5"></a>**706.5.** Triggered abilities that are put on the stack at the same time are put there in the order of rule 703.4: each player orders their own, the initiative player puts all of theirs on first, and the non-initiative player's resolve first. A player may order their own abilities in any way, whatever made each of them trigger. See rule 703.4.

> *Example: a player with a "when I die" ability triggered by combat damage and an "after combat" ability orders the two in one choice.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.43; Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1540678747953569832#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts · Example test: 239-damage-triggers-after-combat.test.ts::CR 608.9b THE RAQ BATCH · Key: effects.triggered.order</sub>

<a id="r706.6"></a>**706.6.** A triggered ability triggers once each time its event happens. If one action makes the event happen several times, the ability triggers that many times. See rule 109.3d.

> *Example: an enemy spell that targets two allies triggers Earnest Defender twice, and two 1/1s are created.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 136-triggers-and-modes.test.ts · Example test: 136-triggers-and-modes.test.ts::CR 109.3d: two targeted allies are TWO TRIGGERS on the stack, not one that makes two · Key: effects.triggered.once-per-event</sub>

<a id="r706.6a"></a>**706.6a** Several cards that enter a hand together in one move are one event. An ability that triggers when a card, or one or more cards, enters a hand triggers once for that move.

> *Example: Rider of the Tides is attacking. Its controller plays Tilling the Graves, returning Curio Drifter and Bumblecrab from the bin to hand in one move. That is one entry into the hand, so the Rider triggers once and gets +2/+2, not +4/+4.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 152-hand-entry.test.ts · Example test: 152-hand-entry.test.ts::a multi-card move fires exactly ONE handEntered, like a multi-card draw · Key: effects.triggered.once-per-event.one-move</sub>

<a id="r706.6b"></a>**706.6b** Each mod that Reconfigure moves onto a new host is applied to that host separately. An ability that triggers whenever a mod is applied triggers once for each of them. See rule 721.

> *Example: Reconfiguring a unit carrying three mods onto Perpetual Construct triggers it three times.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353856176558706769#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Reconfigure onto Perpetual Construct · Key: effects.triggered.once-per-event.moved-mods</sub>

<a id="r706.7"></a>**706.7.** A triggered ability triggers only on events in the region its card is in. An event in another region does not trigger it, even when the event involves its controller. See rule 601.

> *Example: Refuse Reclaimer does not grow when a unit dies in a region it is not in.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.42; Manual p.21 · Tests: 28-metal-c.test.ts · Example test: 28-metal-c.test.ts::Refuse Reclaimer: a death in a region it is not in leaves it cold (CR 601.1d) · Key: effects.triggered.region</sub>

<a id="r706.7a"></a>**706.7a** An "after combat" ability triggers only in a region where a battle took place. See rule 609.

> *Example: A unit with an "after combat" ability in a region where no battle happened does not trigger.*

> *Example: a unit with an "after combat" ability that stands in the battle region but in no formation still triggers.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.43; Manual p.43 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ after combat: the control, an after-combat unit in ANOTHER region makes nothing, 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ after combat: an after-combat trigger fires for a unit in the battle region that is not in formation · Key: effects.triggered.region.after-combat</sub>

<a id="r706.8"></a>**706.8.** An ability of a unit that triggers on its own death ("When I die") triggers when the unit dies, although the unit has then left play. The ability is put on the stack in the region where the unit died. See rule 714.

> *Example: A "when I die" ability of a unit that died in the battle region can target things in the battle region, not in its controller's home region.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22, 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 62-death-facts.test.ts · Example test: 62-death-facts.test.ts::CR 714.9a: a "when I die" trigger resolves in the region the unit DIED in · Key: effects.triggered.own-death</sub>

<a id="r706.8a"></a>**706.8a** An ability that triggers when its unit despawns ("When I despawn"), including one a mod gives its host, triggers whichever way the unit leaves play: when it dies, when it is recalled, and when it is cached.

> *Example: a host carrying Growing Plague that is recalled to its hand triggers Growing Plague's despawn ability.*

> *Example: the same host cached triggers it too.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 141-despawn-mods.test.ts · Example tests: 141-despawn-mods.test.ts::CR 721.1f (i), 141-despawn-mods.test.ts::CR 721.1f (ii) · Key: effects.triggered.own-death.despawn</sub>

<a id="r706.8b"></a>**706.8b** Moving a unit and its mods onto another unit (Reconfigure) is not a despawn: the unit does not change zones, so its "When I despawn" abilities do not trigger. See rule 721.

> *Example: Bubb wearing Growing Plague is Reconfigured onto a Robot; Growing Plague does not trigger.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353847640214999170#0 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Reconfigure vs Despawn · Key: effects.triggered.own-death.reconfigure</sub>

<a id="r706.8c"></a>**706.8c** Units that die together hear each other. A unit destroyed in the same batch of deaths as other units still triggers on their deaths, and on their cards being trashed, as it would have had it survived. See rule 713.

> *Example: Muck Rummager killed by combat damage alongside two allies still draws for its controller trashing those allies.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 258-simultaneous-disposal-listeners.test.ts · Example test: 258-simultaneous-disposal-listeners.test.ts::CR 706.8c: Muck Rummager hears an ally trashed in the same combat-damage batch it dies in · Key: effects.triggered.own-death.same-batch</sub>

<a id="r706.9"></a>**706.9.** An ability that triggers when a spell is played targeting something reads the targets the spell declared as it was played. A target changed onto that thing later does not make the ability trigger, and a target changed away from it later does not undo the trigger. See rule 109.3a.

> *Example: a spell played at another unit and then retargeted onto Earthbound Replicator makes no copy.*

> *Example: a spell played at Earthbound Replicator and then retargeted away still makes its copy.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355613076506017894#3 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts · Example tests: 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts::CR 706.9 Earthbound Replicator: a spell played at something ELSE and retargeted onto me makes NO copy, 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts::CR 706.9 Earthbound Replicator: a spell played AT ME and retargeted away still makes its copy · Key: effects.triggered.targets-as-played</sub>

<a id="r706.10"></a>**706.10.** An "If you do" clause in a triggered ability is part of that ability, not a separate triggered ability. It resolves as part of the ability, and it is not put on the stack or taxed separately.

> *Example: Eminence of the Barrens attacks under an enemy Crevice Lurker and is damaged by a spell. Its controller is asked the Crevice Lurker tax once for the trigger, and the [one] to fight is asked while that same trigger resolves, and is never taxed itself: each trigger costs 2 in all, the tax plus the fight.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 426-cr-abilities-and-replacement.test.ts · Example test: 426-cr-abilities-and-replacement.test.ts::cr:effects.triggered.if-you-do — Eminence of the Barrens under an enemy Crevice Lurker is taxed once per trigger, and its pay-to-fight is asked inside that one trigger · Key: effects.triggered.if-you-do</sub>

<a id="r706.11"></a>**706.11.** {Alluring} and {Resonant} work as triggered abilities of the unit or source that has them. What they do is put on the stack, so it can be responded to and negated, and an effect that taxes triggered abilities applies to it. See rules 802, 111.10f.

> *Example: Crevice Lurker taxes the {Alluring} trigger, and declining the tax stops the lure.*

> *Example: Containment Protocol negates an {Alluring} trigger waiting on the stack.*

> *Example: a {Resonant} source's extra damage waits on the stack after combat as that source's ability, and can be negated.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1366446116274442291#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts · Example tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ trigger-like attributes: Crevice Lurker taxes the Alluring trigger, 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ trigger-like attributes: Containment Protocol negates a waiting Alluring trigger, 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts::the Resonant rider waits on the stack after combat, as its source, and can be negated · Key: effects.triggered.attributes</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U15-1, D-U15-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r706.12"></a>**706.12.** Some triggered abilities choose a unit without targeting it, such as a Wraith's start-of-deployment ability choosing "an ally". The unit is chosen as the ability begins to resolve, from the units in play then. Several such abilities resolve one at a time, each choosing among the units still in play, so a unit an earlier one destroyed is not offered to a later one. One that finds no unit to choose fizzles. See rule 704.5c.

> *Example: three Wraith abilities and one 1/1 ally: only the first is offered the 1/1 and kills it; the other two put their counters on Wraiths still in play, and nothing fizzles.*

> *Example: all three Wraith abilities are on the stack before the first one asks for its ally, and each asks only after the one before it has fully resolved.*

> *Example: a Wraith with no other ally is its own only ally. Its ability chooses it without asking and it shrinks to 2/2; nothing fizzles.*

> *Example: a 1/1 carrying two Wraith augments: the first ability kills it, and the second finds no ally in play and fizzles.*

<sub>Basis: Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16 · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 4 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts, 460-wraith-chooses-on-resolution.test.ts, 461-wraith-no-ally-and-one-ally.test.ts · Example tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::CR 706.12: three Wraith triggers and one 1/1 choose as each resolves, so only the first is offered the 1/1 and none fizzles, 460-wraith-chooses-on-resolution.test.ts::report 2026-10-16: three Wraith triggers and a 1/1 ask nothing before the first resolves, 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::CR 706.12: a lone Wraith is its own only ally — it shrinks itself without asking, and nothing fizzles, 461-wraith-no-ally-and-one-ally.test.ts::report 2026-10-16: a Wraith shrink that finds no ally in play asks nothing and fizzles · Key: effects.triggered.chosen-unit</sub>

<a id="r706.12a"></a>**706.12a** Choosing a unit this way is not targeting it. It does not trigger "when I become targeted" abilities, and it cannot be redirected.

> *Example: a Wraith ability choosing Mohruung does not give its controller a Crystal.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Example test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::CR 706.12a: a subject is not a target · Key: effects.triggered.chosen-unit.not-target</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U15-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r706.13"></a>**706.13.** An ability that triggers on a card being played, and then acts on what was played ("negate that effect"), acts on the item that play put on the stack. Another item with the same name and the same controller is not it, whether it is older or newer. A copy of the played spell is not it either, because a copy is not played (see rule 701.5). See rule 701.5.

> *Example: Two Burgeons by the same player are on the stack, and only the second one's play makes Void Mandible trigger. The Mandible negates the second Burgeon, not the first.*

> *Example: A copy of Burgeon sits below a newly played Burgeon. Void Mandible negates the played Burgeon and leaves the copy alone.*

> *Example: Origon negates the spell whose play made it trigger, even with an identical spell above it on the stack.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Void Mandible · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 178-played-item-and-erased-mods.test.ts, 162-item-identity-and-truthful-events.test.ts · Example tests: 178-played-item-and-erased-mods.test.ts::Void Mandible: with two same-card same-seat spells up, it negates THE ONE THE EVENT NAMES, 178-played-item-and-erased-mods.test.ts::Void Mandible: a COPY on the stack is never negated — CR 706.13, a copy was not played, 162-item-identity-and-truthful-events.test.ts::Origon negates the item the play event NAMES, with a second identical spell above it on the stack · Key: effects.triggered.that-item</sub>

<a id="r707"></a>
### 707. Static Abilities

<a id="r707.1"></a>**707.1.** A static ability states a change that its card continuously makes to the game for as long as the card is in play. See rule 109.4.

> *Example: Prickly Protector's "+1/+1 for each other ally" is counted again whenever its stats are read.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.41 · Tests: 24-wood-b.test.ts · Example test: 24-wood-b.test.ts::Prickly Protector: +1/+1 per other ally · Key: effects.static.what</sub>

<a id="r707.2"></a>**707.2.** A static ability does not use the stack. It cannot be responded to or negated, and an effect that changes what abilities cost to activate or trigger does not apply to it.

> *Example: Crevice Lurker does not tax Tranquility's "spells cost [one] more"; Tranquility still adds exactly one.*

> *Example: Aetherflux Golem's "I gain +2/+2" never goes on the stack, so Containment Protocol cannot negate it.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1355103348378042515#3 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 142-static-conformance.test.ts · Example tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ Crevice Lurker: a static ability is not taxed, 142-static-conformance.test.ts::CR 721.1e: Aetherflux Golem is a STATIC · Key: effects.static.no-stack</sub>

<a id="r707.3"></a>**707.3.** Only triggered abilities and activated abilities put anything on the stack. A triggered ability says "When" or "Whenever" or names a time such as "After combat"; {Alluring} and {Resonant} also work as triggered abilities; an activated ability is written with a colon. A sentence that states a standing fact ("I gain +2/+2", "Spells cost [one] more to play during battle") is a static ability, and a sentence that says "instead", "as" or "if" and names no target is a replacement effect. Neither goes on the stack, except that a replacement whose substitute names a target puts that substitute on the stack. See rules 708.1, 109.5a, 706.1, 706.11, 705.1, 708.2a.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.41; Manual p.41 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-08-25, 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 142-static-conformance.test.ts, 88-replacement-conformance.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 142-static-conformance.test.ts::a card whose whole printed text is continuous declares NOTHING that reaches the stack, 88-replacement-conformance.test.ts::a card whose whole text is an untargeted replacement declares NO ability at all · Key: effects.static.printed-form</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U15-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r707.4"></a>**707.4.** A static ability applies continuously to everything it describes, including units that enter play after it began to apply. When its source leaves play, the change ends. See rule 709.

> *Example: a unit that enters play while Transmogrifant is in play has no attributes, and gets them back when Transmogrifant leaves.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355845893219287132#0; RAQ 1355845893219287132#0 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Transmogrifant: a unit that enters play under it has no attributes · Key: effects.static.continuous</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U15-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r707.4a"></a>**707.4a** A unit that enters play while a static ability applies to it enters with the change already made. An ability that triggers on the unit entering play sees the unit as changed.

> *Example: under Sandstone Defender a 1/1 enters as a 1/3, so Nectar Ridge Oracle ("an ally spawns with greater defense than power") draws.*

> *Example: under Infernal Wispweaver a 0/1 Wisp enters as a 2/2, so Nectar Ridge Oracle does not draw.*

> *Example: Animated Spark's +X/+0 applies to a unit that spawns mid-battle from the moment it spawns.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355633589890584636#0; RAQ 1355633589890584636#1; RAQ 1355633589890584636#2 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Nectar Ridge: under Sandstone Defender, 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Nectar Ridge: under Infernal Wispweaver, 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Nectar Ridge: Animated Spark statics a unit that spawns mid-battle · Key: effects.static.continuous.on-arrival</sub>

<a id="r707.4b"></a>**707.4b** A static ability that changes stats ("I gain +2/+2") puts no counters on the unit. Effects that count, move, double or remove counters do not see the change, and it ends as soon as its source stops applying it.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 142-static-conformance.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 142-static-conformance.test.ts::CR 721.1e: Aetherflux Golem is a STATIC, like the two cards printing its sentence · Key: effects.static.continuous.not-counters</sub>

<a id="r707.5"></a>**707.5.** A card's statement that it enters play with counters ("I spawn with two +1/+1 counters") is not a triggered ability. The unit enters play already holding those counters; nothing goes on the stack, and an ability that triggers on the unit entering play sees it with them.

> *Example: Aethercap Siphoner (printed 4/4, "I spawn with three -1/-1 counters on me") is seen as a 1/1 by an ability that triggers when it spawns.*

> *Example: neither Powerforge Synergist's nor Aethercap Siphoner's counters can be responded to.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 139-spawn-and-play.test.ts · Example tests: 139-spawn-and-play.test.ts::Aethercap Siphoner: a spawn watcher sees the 1/1 the card prints, not the printed 4/4, 139-spawn-and-play.test.ts::Powerforge Synergist / Aethercap Siphoner: "I spawn with N counters" never reaches the stack · Key: effects.static.spawn-counters</sub>

<a id="r707.5a"></a>**707.5a** The player who spawns the unit puts those counters on it, so everything that applies when counters are put on a unit applies to them: a replacement effect that changes how many are put, a replacement effect that puts them on another unit instead, and an ability that triggers when counters are put on a unit. A unit whose counters are put on another unit instead enters without them. See rules 708.4, 713.2.

> *Example: under an allied Flux Resonator a Robot 2 enters as a 3/3.*

> *Example: Aethercap Siphoner's own -1/-1 counters count as its controller putting counters on an ally, so Scrapyard Custodian draws.*

> *Example: Aethercap Siphoner spawned during a battle triggers Pestilent Mycelion ("whenever one or more -1/-1 counters are put on a unit").*

> *Example: During battle, a Robot 2 created where a Counter Thief is enters with no counters: the two counters are placed on the Counter Thief instead, and the Robot, a 0/0, dies.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 5 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Counter Thief · Designer: RQ 1154096942083743885; RQ 1478900090147045427; RQ 1465517485750096006; RQ 1378032353959608370 · Tests: 27-metal-b.test.ts, 139-spawn-and-play.test.ts, 493-spawn-counters-are-put.test.ts · Example tests: 27-metal-b.test.ts::Flux Resonator: an allied Robot spawns with one more counter (report #88), 139-spawn-and-play.test.ts::Aethercap Siphoner: spawning with counters IS "you put counters on an ally" — the placement a Robot's X is too, 493-spawn-counters-are-put.test.ts::Caleb 2026-03-05: Aethercap Siphoner spawned in battle triggers Pestilent Mycelion, 493-spawn-counters-are-put.test.ts::Counter Thief, DURING BATTLE: a Robot's spawn counters land on the Thief, and the 0/0 Robot dies · Key: effects.static.spawn-counters.modifiers</sub>

<a id="r707.6"></a>**707.6.** A static ability applies only in the region its source is in. See rule 601.

> *Example: Rotspore Herald ("Everything is {deadly}") in its home region does not make a spell resolving in the battle region deadly.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.42; Manual p.42 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 107-semantics-statics.test.ts · Example test: 107-semantics-statics.test.ts::Rotspore Herald: CR 601.1d — the scope is the REGION · Key: effects.static.region</sub>

<a id="r707.7"></a>**707.7.** A static ability applies to everything its text names, with no limit its text does not state. "Everything" means every unit, spell and spell token in its region, on both sides.

> *Example: with Rotspore Herald in the region, a spell that deals 1 damage destroys a 7/5.*

> *Example: a Fireball 1 spell token in Rotspore Herald's region is {Deadly} too.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24, 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 107-semantics-statics.test.ts · Example tests: 107-semantics-statics.test.ts::Rotspore Herald: CR 707.7 — a SPELL resolving in the region is deadly, 107-semantics-statics.test.ts::Rotspore Herald: CR 707.7 — a SPELL TOKEN standing in the region is deadly too · Key: effects.static.literal</sub>

<a id="r707.7a"></a>**707.7a** A static ability that names "spells" applies to spell tokens too, because spell tokens are spells. See rule 108.2.

> *Example: Emberflame Enlightener says "Your units and spells gain {Powerful}". Its controller's Fireball token is a spell, so it has {Powerful} too.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 111-literal-fire.test.ts · Example test: 111-literal-fire.test.ts::Emberflame and Envoy of Lightning ask the SAME question about a spell token · Key: effects.static.literal.spell-tokens</sub>

<a id="r707.8"></a>**707.8.** A static ability that applies to effects with a number of targets ("spell effects with a single target") counts the targets the effect declared as it was played, including targets that have since become illegal.

> *Example: Twin Flame played at two units is not "a single target" for Envoy of Lightning, even after one of them is removed.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts · Example test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Envoy of Lightning: two DECLARED targets is not · Key: effects.static.declared-targets</sub>

<a id="r707.9"></a>**707.9.** A static ability or replacement effect that a mod gives its host works from the host. "I" and "me" mean the host, "you" and "your" mean the host's controller, and it applies in the host's region. See rule 720.

> *Example: Transmogrifant as a mod gives "your other units +2/+2" from its host.*

> *Example: Crevice Lurker as a mod taxes abilities in its host's region.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Tests: 28-metal-c.test.ts, 16-earth-a.test.ts, 87-replacement-layer.test.ts · Example tests: 28-metal-c.test.ts::Transmogrifant: the augment-donated static anchors on the host, 16-earth-a.test.ts::Crevice Lurker: CR 707.9 — donated as an augment, the HOST's region carries the tax · Demonstrated by test: 87-replacement-layer.test.ts::a donated [Augment] replacement reads from its HOST · Key: effects.static.from-mod</sub>

<a id="r707.10"></a>**707.10.** A permission a card grants ("You may play one unit with no abilities from your bin each deployment") is a standing fact, not an ability that goes on the stack. Using it cannot be responded to, and an effect that negates activated or triggered abilities cannot stop it. (engine differs, see F-U15-1) *(Digital client)* *(Engine differs, see F-U15-1.)*

> *Example: Containment Protocol cannot stop a player using The Bonesculptor's permission, because there is nothing on the stack to negate.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; no gate test · Key: effects.static.permission</sub>

<a id="r708"></a>
### 708. Replacement and Prevention Effects

<a id="r708.1"></a>**708.1.** A replacement effect is an ability that changes an event as it happens, written "If … instead". It replaces the event, rather than triggering in response to it. See rule 109.5.

> *Example: Flux Resonator ("if one or more counters would be put on a unit by an allied source, put that many counters plus one instead") makes a counter put on an ally one more.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.41; Manual p.41 · Tests: 27-metal-b.test.ts · Example test: 27-metal-b.test.ts::Flux Resonator: a counter you put on an allied unit becomes one more · Key: effects.replacement.what</sub>

<a id="r708.2"></a>**708.2.** A replacement effect does not use the stack. It cannot be responded to, and an effect that negates triggered and activated effects (Containment Protocol) cannot stop it or undo what it did.

> *Example: Containment Protocol on the stack cannot negate Nullbringer's life-gain replacement.*

> *Example: Conduit of Pain's extra damage never reaches the stack, so nothing can negate it.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.41 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 87-replacement-layer.test.ts, 12-fire-a.test.ts · Example tests: 87-replacement-layer.test.ts::Containment Protocol on the stack cannot negate a life-gain replacement, 12-fire-a.test.ts::Conduit of Pain: the extra damage never reaches the stack · Key: effects.replacement.no-stack</sub>

<a id="r708.2a"></a>**708.2a** A replacement effect whose substitute names a target is the one exception (rule 109.5a): the event is replaced at once, and the substitute goes on the stack as a triggered ability. If the substitute later has no legal target or fizzles, the replaced event still does not happen. See rule 109.5a.

> *Example: Beyond, Codex Incarnate replaces its controller's rot damage with -1/-1 counters on a target unit; the damage never lands, whatever becomes of the counters.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 43-dark-c.test.ts · Example test: 43-dark-c.test.ts::Beyond, Codex Incarnate: CR 112.13d — the rot replacement asks its controller for a target, and the damage never lands · Key: effects.replacement.no-stack.targeted</sub>

<a id="r708.3"></a>**708.3.** The event a replacement effect replaces does not happen, and the substitute happens instead. Abilities that trigger on the replaced event do not trigger. When the substitute is still damage (damage dealt "as" rot), the damage was still dealt (rule 112.12). See rule 112.12.

> *Example: under Nullbringer a player who would gain life loses that much instead; nothing that triggers on gaining life triggers.*

> *Example: a Robot that Cosmic Conspirator replaces with a Fireball is never created, so nothing that triggers on a unit spawning triggers for it.*

> *Example: with Blightsea Polyp in play, Zephyrzoa's column still deals combat damage to the opponent, although the opponent gains rot instead of losing life.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 87-replacement-layer.test.ts, 210-zephyrzoa-hears-a-replaced-hit.test.ts · Example tests: 87-replacement-layer.test.ts::a replaced life gain fires no lifeGained, 87-replacement-layer.test.ts::a replaced token creation fires no spawned, 210-zephyrzoa-hears-a-replaced-hit.test.ts::CR 608.8a: Zephyrzoa fires on a hit that was REPLACED and cost no life · Key: effects.replacement.substitute</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-21 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r708.4"></a>**708.4.** A replacement effect applies to an event only once. What it produces is not replaced again by the same effect, unless a new event occurs. See rules 608.8c, 708.4a.

> *Example: 10 {Piercing} combat damage redirected into a 2/4 Oorblak: 4 destroy it, and the other 6 reach the player; the same Oorblak does not take them again.*

> *Example: two Nullbringers turn one life gain into one loss, not into a gain again.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1397188292239163454#0; RQ 1442982460034912287 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 40-light-c.test.ts · Example tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Oorblak: 10 Piercing combat damage redirected into a 2/4 Oorblak, 40-light-c.test.ts::Nullbringer: two copies do not stack · Key: effects.replacement.once</sub>

<a id="r708.4a"></a>**708.4a** If two or more replacement effects could apply to one event, they apply one at a time. Each applies at most once, to the event as the earlier ones left it, and only if that event still matches its own text; one that has applied does not apply again, so nothing loops. The player the event affects (the player who would be dealt the damage, the player whose rot it is, or the controller of the unit the counters would be put on) chooses the order in which they apply, except where rule 608.8c fixes it. When only one such effect applies, nothing is asked. *(Digital client)*

> *Example: two Oorblaks and combat damage that would be dealt to their controller: the first to apply takes all of it, and the other takes 0, because the damage is no longer being dealt to that player.*

> *Example: the player who would be dealt the damage chooses which of two Oorblaks applies first, and that one takes it.*

> *Example: two Counter Thieves: the counters the first redirects onto itself are still being placed on a unit, so the second, which has not applied, takes them; they end on the second to apply.*

> *Example: the controller of the unit the counters were meant for chooses the order of two Counter Thieves; choosing the second to apply last puts the counters on it.*

> *Example: two Counter Thieves do not pass the same counters back and forth: each applies once.*

> *Example: two Automatons of Abundance turn one created token into three: 1, then 2, then 3.*

> *Example: two Skittering Blights: the player whose rot it is chooses which one takes it as counters; the other has nothing left to replace.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 9 tests, all passed; 7 gate test files · Printed: card: Oorblak; card: Counter Thief · Designer: RAQ 1397188292239163454#0; RQ 1442982460034912287; RQ 1442981461476245685; RQ 1442981580535496807; RQ 1442981663603687588 · Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16 · Tests: 469-replacement-chain-damage.test.ts, 468-replacement-chain-redirects.test.ts, 471-oorblak-order-and-polyp.test.ts, 472-counter-thief-and-rot-order.test.ts, 459-automatons-chain.test.ts, 46-hybrids-ld-c.test.ts, 40-light-c.test.ts · Example tests: 469-replacement-chain-damage.test.ts::CR 708.4: two Oorblaks and combat damage to you — one takes all of it, the other takes 0, 471-oorblak-order-and-polyp.test.ts::CR 708.4a: two Oorblaks and combat damage — the player being hit is asked which takes it, and the answer decides it, 468-replacement-chain-redirects.test.ts::CR 708.4: two Counter Thieves chain — the second takes the counters from the first, once, 472-counter-thief-and-rot-order.test.ts::CR 708.4a: two Counter Thieves — choosing the second puts them on the second (the owner, 2026-10-16), 46-hybrids-ld-c.test.ts::Counter Thief: two thieves do not ping-pong, 459-automatons-chain.test.ts::CR 708.4: two Automatons of Abundance turn one created token into three, 472-counter-thief-and-rot-order.test.ts::CR 708.4a: two Skittering Blights — the player is asked which takes their rot · Key: effects.replacement.once.one-applies</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-13, D-U15-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r708.5"></a>**708.5.** Replacement effects that only change an amount ("that many plus one instead") all apply: each applies once, and their changes add up. A modifier does not apply to its own change, but two copies of the same card are two modifiers and both apply.

> *Example: two Conduits of Pain make 1 damage from an allied source into 3.*

> *Example: two allied Flux Resonators make a Robot X spawn with X plus 2 counters.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts, 27-metal-b.test.ts, 87-replacement-layer.test.ts · Example tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Conduit of Pain: two Conduits both apply, and neither applies to itself, 27-metal-b.test.ts::Flux Resonator: two allied Resonators give a spawn X plus TWO (summed) · Key: effects.replacement.amount-modifiers</sub>

<a id="r708.6"></a>**708.6.** Effects that double an amount ("Double all life gain and life loss") multiply together. With n of them applying to the same amount, it is multiplied by 2 to the power n.

> *Example: three Arbiters of Vitality multiply a life loss by 8.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 137-multiplier-and-mode.test.ts · Example test: 137-multiplier-and-mode.test.ts::CR 708.6: THREE Arbiters multiply · Key: effects.replacement.multipliers</sub>

<a id="r708.6a"></a>**708.6a** When modifiers that add to an amount and an effect that doubles it apply to the same amount, the additions are made first and the result is doubled. See rule 112.9.

> *Example: a {Powerful} Bellowing Boulder with Conduit of Pain deals (1+1)x2 = 4 damage to each unit.*

> *Example: Conduit of Pain and Arbiter of Vitality: the 1 is added before the life loss is doubled.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30, 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 137-multiplier-and-mode.test.ts · Example tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Resonant: Conduit adds its 1 BEFORE Powerful doubles, 137-multiplier-and-mode.test.ts::the multiplier composes with a REAL additive mod end to end · Key: effects.replacement.multipliers.additive-first</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U15-4 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r708.6b"></a>**708.6b** A multiplied life loss is lost all at once, as one loss of the whole amount, and only then does the game check whether the player has lost. See rule 104.

> *Example: Arbiter of Vitality doubles a lethal loss before the game checks whether the player has lost.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 137-multiplier-and-mode.test.ts · Example test: 137-multiplier-and-mode.test.ts::Arbiter of Vitality: a LETHAL loss is multiplied BEFORE the lethal check · Demonstrated by test: 137-multiplier-and-mode.test.ts::the multiplier is a REPLACEMENT, not a second helping · Key: effects.replacement.multipliers.lethal</sub>

<a id="r708.7"></a>**708.7.** When a replacement that changes the number of counters and a replacement that redirects them both apply to the same placement, the number is changed first, and the redirect then moves the whole changed number.

> *Example: a Counter Thief beside a Flux Resonator steals the extra counter too.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 87-replacement-layer.test.ts · Example test: 87-replacement-layer.test.ts::an AmountMod runs BEFORE the redirect · Key: effects.replacement.amount-before-redirect</sub>

<a id="r708.8"></a>**708.8.** A replacement effect applies only to what its own text names. One that applies when counters "would be put on" a unit does not apply when counters are removed.

> *Example: Proliferating Slime does not change how many counters Burn the Blight removes.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 152-hand-entry.test.ts, 455-counter-removal-is-not-placement.test.ts · Example test: 455-counter-removal-is-not-placement.test.ts::CR 708.8 example: Proliferating Slime does not change how many counters Burn the Blight removes · Key: effects.replacement.scope</sub>

<a id="r708.8a"></a>**708.8a** Counters of either sign are counters. A replacement effect that adds to counters being put on a unit adds -1/-1 counters to -1/-1 counters, as it adds +1/+1 counters to +1/+1 counters.

> *Example: Flux Resonator makes two -1/-1 counters its controller puts on a unit into three.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 120-counter-attribution.test.ts · Example test: 120-counter-attribution.test.ts::Resonator: -1/-1 counters get one more of the SAME · Key: effects.replacement.scope.all-counters</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U05-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r708.8b"></a>**708.8b** Whether counters are put "by an allied source", or put by "you", depends on whose effect put them, not on whose unit they land on. Counters that a redirect moves are still put by the player whose effect put them.

> *Example: counters an opponent's effect puts on your unit do not get your Flux Resonator's extra counter.*

> *Example: counters your effect puts on an enemy unit do.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RQ 1362265958088966396 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 120-counter-attribution.test.ts · Example tests: 120-counter-attribution.test.ts::Resonator: an ENEMY's placement onto your own unit is not an allied source, 120-counter-attribution.test.ts::Resonator: counters YOU put on an ENEMY unit are plus one too · Key: effects.replacement.scope.who-put</sub>

<a id="r708.8c"></a>**708.8c** Moving counters from one unit onto another removes them from the first and puts them on the second. Only the second half puts counters on a unit, so a replacement effect that applies when counters would be put on a unit changes how many arrive, not how many leave. See rule 708.8b.

> *Example: Your Flux Resonator is in play and you cast Scrap For Parts ("Move all counters from target unit onto another target unit"), moving an enemy unit's two +1/+1 counters onto your unit: the enemy unit is left with none, and your unit gets three.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Scrap For Parts; card: Flux Resonator · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 455-counter-removal-is-not-placement.test.ts · Example test: 455-counter-removal-is-not-placement.test.ts::a MOVE removes from the source and puts on the destination: Flux Resonator enlarges only the put · Key: effects.replacement.scope.move</sub>

<a id="r708.9"></a>**708.9.** All the tokens one resolution of one effect creates are created together. A replacement effect that acts on "each unique token you created" sees all of them at once, and a token is unique by its name, its X and the stats the effect that created it set, together.

> *Example: Automaton of Abundance with Manufacture (a Robot 3, a Robot 2 and a Robot 1) creates three extra Robots.*

> *Example: three identical Robot 2s created together are one unique token and yield one extra.*

> *Example: a 3/3 and a 5/5 unit token created together are two unique tokens and yield two extras.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Automaton of Abundance · Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16; Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 136-triggers-and-modes.test.ts, 87-replacement-layer.test.ts, 458-automaton-copies-stats.test.ts · Example tests: 136-triggers-and-modes.test.ts::CR 708.9: end to end, 136-triggers-and-modes.test.ts::CR 304.14: three IDENTICAL Robot 2s, 458-automaton-copies-stats.test.ts::CR 304.14: a 3/3 and a 5/5 Unit Token made together are TWO unique tokens · Key: effects.replacement.token-batch</sub>

<a id="r708.10"></a>**708.10.** When an effect says a player's life total can't change, a gain or loss of life for that player does not happen at all, and no replacement effect applies to it.

> *Example: with the life total locked by Suspend, Nullbringer has no gain of life to turn into a loss.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 87-replacement-layer.test.ts · Example test: 87-replacement-layer.test.ts::a locked life total stops the replacement layer too · Key: effects.replacement.locked-life</sub>

<a id="r708.11"></a>**708.11.** A prevention effect ("if damage would be dealt …, prevent it") is not a replacement effect. Prevented damage is not dealt at all (rule 112.11), while damage a replacement effect changes is still dealt (rule 112.12). See rules 112.11, 112.12.

> *Example: a unit shielded by Phytochemical Protection and hit by a {Poisonous} unit takes no -1/-1 counters and does not trigger on being dealt damage.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1354148437355925554#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 24-wood-b.test.ts · Example test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Poisonous: a shielded Jollyglop · Demonstrated by test: 24-wood-b.test.ts::Phytochemical Protection: prevented damage is NOT dealt · Key: effects.replacement.prevention</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U15-5 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r708.11a"></a>**708.11a** A prevention effect on a unit prevents all the damage dealt to it, including any beyond what would destroy it.

> *Example: a lone shielded blocker is assigned the whole of a column's damage, and all of it is prevented.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353888077625561108#7 · Tests: 24-wood-b.test.ts · Example test: 24-wood-b.test.ts::Phytochemical Protection: the whole hit is prevented, not just the lethal part · Key: effects.replacement.prevention.whole-hit</sub>

<a id="r708.11b"></a>**708.11b** Prevention applies to the damage as it would be dealt, after the recipient's own doubling ({Vulnerable}). It does not change how damage is assigned or how much is lethal (rule 608.6g). See rule 608.6g.

> *Example: a shield changes what is dealt to a unit, never how much of a {Piercing} hit goes past it.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts · Example test: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts::Piercing vs a damage-shielded unit · Key: effects.replacement.prevention.when</sub>

<a id="r709"></a>
### 709. Continuous Effects and Timestamps

<a id="r709.1"></a>**709.1.** A continuous effect changes the game for a period of time rather than once. It comes either from a static ability, and lasts as long as that ability is in play, only in its region; or from an effect that says how long it lasts, such as "until regroup". See rules 206.6, 113, 707.

> *Example: Sudden Bloom gives your units in its region +1/+1 until regroup, and the bonus is gone after regroup.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.40; Manual p.40 · Tests: 25-wood-c.test.ts · Example test: 25-wood-c.test.ts::Sudden Bloom: your in-region units get +1/+1 until regroup · Key: effects.continuous.what</sub>

<a id="r709.2"></a>**709.2.** A continuous effect applies to a unit that enters play while the effect applies, from the moment it enters. The unit enters play already changed, so an ability that looks at the unit as it enters sees the changed unit. See rule 707.

> *Example: under Sandstone Defender ("Your other units gain +0/+2") a 1/1 enters as a 1/3, so Nectar Ridge Oracle ("When another ally with greater defense than power spawns, draw a card") draws.*

> *Example: under Infernal Wispweaver a 0/1 Wisp enters as a 2/2, so Nectar Ridge Oracle does not draw.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355633589890584636#0; RAQ 1355633589890584636#2 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Nectar Ridge: under Sandstone Defender, 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Nectar Ridge: under Infernal Wispweaver · Key: effects.continuous.enters-modified</sub>

<a id="r709.3"></a>**709.3.** When the source of a static ability leaves play, its continuous effect ends at once. The units it was changing are again what they would be without it, and they get back any attributes and abilities it had removed. See rule 712.

> *Example: a unit that entered play under Transmogrifant has no attributes; when Transmogrifant leaves play it has them again.*

> *Example: when Infernal Wispweaver leaves play, Wisps sacrifice themselves after combat again.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1355845893219287132#0 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 12-fire-a.test.ts · Example tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Transmogrifant: a unit that enters play under it has no attributes, 12-fire-a.test.ts::Infernal Wispweaver: the suppression ends the instant the weaver does · Key: effects.continuous.ends</sub>

<a id="r709.4"></a>**709.4.** A unit's stats are worked out layer by layer, in the order of rule 206.4. Every effect in one layer applies before any effect in the next layer, whatever order the effects began in. Within one layer, effects apply in timestamp order (rule 113). See rules 206.4, 113.1.

> *Example: An effect that makes a unit base 4/4 applies over Apex Prime's copy effect whether the copy began before it or after it, because base stats are a later layer than the copy.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.42 · Designer: RAQ 1357965714807586897#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts · Example test: 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts::CR 709.4: a later setBase wins over a copy · Key: effects.continuous.layers</sub>

<a id="r709.4a"></a>**709.4a** Before those layers, a copy effect decides which card the unit's printed stats come from. A unit that is a copy of a card has that card's printed stats as its layer 1, and every later layer applies to them (rule 710). See rule 710.

> *Example: a Unit Token that becomes a copy of Good Whale and is Unaware reads as a 7/5, Good Whale's printed stats.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts · Example test: 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts::CR 709.4a: {Unaware} reads the COPIED face's printed stats · Key: effects.continuous.layers.copy</sub>

<a id="r709.4b"></a>**709.4b** In layer 4, Tough and Balanced apply in the order the unit has them, from top to bottom. A Tough unit that attacks with a Balanced unit behind it has its defense doubled, then its stats balanced. Where a Balanced unit gets Tough from a mod, the Manual's answer gives both orders: Tough "augmented onto" a Balanced unit doubles, then balances; Tough "applied to" a Balanced unit balances, then doubles (D-U16-1). The engine takes a unit's printed attributes first, in type-line order, then those from its mods in the order the mods were applied, then those its column shares with it, front to back, so it balances first (the owner ruling of 2026-08-18 calls this order the engine's own reading; engine differs from the "augmented onto" reading, see F-U16-4). *(Digital client)* See rule 802. *(Engine differs, see F-U16-4.)*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: not verified (the text changed after verification); 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.42; Manual p.42; Manual p.42; Manual p.42; Manual p.42; Manual p.42 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 08-cards2.test.ts::CR 709.4b: layer-4 application order · Key: effects.continuous.layers.attribute-order</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U16-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r709.4c"></a>**709.4c** An attribute is either present or not. A unit that has the same attribute from several sources has it once, and it applies once.

> *Example: two Reality Benders on one unit make it Inverted once; they do not cancel out.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 79-round17-layers.test.ts · Example test: 79-round17-layers.test.ts::CR 709.4c layer 5: {Inverted} applies ONCE however many sources grant it · Key: effects.continuous.layers.once</sub>

<a id="r709.4d"></a>**709.4d** Inverted (layer 5) applies after all of layer 4, whatever order the unit gained its attributes in. A unit that is Tough and Inverted has the same stats whichever of the two it gained first. See rule 802.

> *Example: a 1/4 that is Tough and Inverted is a 1/0, in either grant order.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.42 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 79-round17-layers.test.ts · Example test: 79-round17-layers.test.ts::CR 709.4d: the TWO-attribute case, in either grant order · Key: effects.continuous.layers.inverted-last</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U16-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r709.5"></a>**709.5.** A unit's stats are worked out all at once. A unit whose stats would reach 0 defense partway through the calculation does not die for that; only the final result counts (rule 713). See rule 713.

> *Example: a 1/1 with a -1/-1 counter that is Inverted is a 2/2, never a dead 0/0 on the way.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 79-round17-layers.test.ts · Example test: 79-round17-layers.test.ts::CR 802.1k layer 5: hitting 0 mid-calculation is not death · Key: effects.continuous.one-calculation</sub>

<a id="r709.6"></a>**709.6.** An effect that exchanges the base stats of two units (Body Swap) gives each unit the other's base stats as they are when it resolves. It is a base rewrite of its own, later than any base rewrite already applying, so it wins over one. See rules 206.5, 113.4.

> *Example: your 1/1 and an enemy Wisp that Aberrant Statweaver makes base 3/3 are exchanged: your unit becomes base 3/3 and the Wisp base 1/1, until regroup.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Body Swap · Designer: RAQ 1357965714807586897#1 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ timestamps: Body Swap with a Statweavered unit · Key: effects.continuous.base-exchange</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U05-5 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r709.7"></a>**709.7.** An effect that doubles a unit's power or defense until regroup gives the unit a temporary stat change (layer 3) of the size that makes the final stat, after every layer, twice what it was. Because the change is in layer 3, it is still there if an attribute in a later layer stops applying.

> *Example: a 1/10 Tough unit (a 1/5, doubled) doubled by Burgeon gets +0/+5 and is a 1/20. If it then loses Tough to Monke, it is a 1/10.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Burgeon · Designer: RAQ 1362832912579559664#1; RAQ 1362832912579559664#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 140-layers-and-riders.test.ts · Example test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Tough: Burgeon on that 1/10 makes it 1/20 · Key: effects.continuous.doubling</sub>

<a id="r709.8"></a>**709.8.** Where an effect that switches a unit's power and defense until regroup (Invasive Reassignment) applies in the stat layers is an open ruling. The engine applies it as a temporary stat change worked out from the unit's stats when it resolves, so a stat change that comes afterwards applies on top and is not switched. *(Digital client)*

> *Example: An 8/3 unit switched by Invasive Reassignment is a 3/8; if it then gets +2/+0 it is a 5/8, not switched again.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Invasive Reassignment · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 27-metal-b.test.ts, 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts · Example test: 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts::cr:effects.continuous.switch — an 8/3 switched by Invasive Reassignment is a 3/8, and a later +2/+0 makes it a 5/8 · Demonstrated by test: 27-metal-b.test.ts::Invasive Reassignment: switches power and defense until regroup · Key: effects.continuous.switch</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U16-4 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r710"></a>
### 710. Copies and Faces

<a id="r710.1"></a>**710.1.** A unit that becomes a copy of a card takes that card's name, printed stats, attributes and text in place of its own. The physical card does not change: in every zone other than play it is still its own card (rule 410.3a). See rules 201.5, 410.3a.

> *Example: a Borrower of Forms that copies a unit takes its name, its attributes and its text.*

> *Example: a unit that is a copy dies and its own card goes to the bin, not the copied card.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Borrower of Forms; card: Apex Prime · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts, 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts · Example tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts::CR 710.1: Borrower of Forms takes the NAME, the attributes and the card TEXT, 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts::CR 710.1: a copy DYING puts the PHYSICAL card in the bin · Key: effects.copies.becoming</sub>

<a id="r710.1a"></a>**710.1a** While a unit is a copy, its mana cost and its card type are those of the card it copies. A Borrower of Forms that copied a Robot costs 0, and while it copies a unit it is not a spell unit. See rules 202.7, 303.11a.

> *Example: a Borrower of Forms that copied a Robot costs 0, so Lumengrove Lurker can recall it.*

> *Example: while it copies a unit, Cosmic Reversal's "and spell units" does not recall it.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1372468222158180424#10; RAQ 1372468222158180424#11 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Borrower of Forms: a Borrower that copied a Robot costs 0, 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Borrower of Forms: while it mimics a unit it is not a spell unit · Key: effects.copies.becoming.cost-and-type</sub>

<a id="r710.1b"></a>**710.1b** Counters and marked damage belong to the unit, not to the card it copies. A unit keeps them when it becomes a copy, and keeps them when the copy ends.

> *Example: a 1/1 that becomes a 7/5 until regroup and takes two -1/-1 counters dies when the copy ends at regroup.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts · Example test: 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts::CR 710.6: an until-regroup face lapses at regroup, and the revert can be lethal · Key: effects.copies.becoming.unit-facts</sub>

<a id="r710.2"></a>**710.2.** A unit that becomes an "exact copy" (Borrower of Forms) also takes the stat changes and the counters of the unit it copies, and its card text including the text of its mods. Its layer-1 stats are the copied unit's base stats.

> *Example: Borrower of Forms erases its target and takes its stats and counters.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Borrower of Forms · Designer: RAQ 1372468222158180424#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts · Example test: 26-metal-a.test.ts::Borrower of Forms: erases the target and takes its stats and counters · Key: effects.copies.exact</sub>

<a id="r710.2a"></a>**710.2a** A copy of a modded unit has what the mods say, but no mod is copied. The copy is not modded, so it is not Unstable. Its copied grafts run as part of its graft cause, and each copied augment gives it that augment's [Augment] box. See rules 722, 721, 803.

> *Example: a Borrower of Forms that copied a unit carrying a Powerful virus is Powerful, and is not modded or Unstable.*
