> *Example: A Borrower of Forms that copied a Bellowing Boulder with Flame Juggle grafted has the Boulder's whole trigger, Flame Juggle's grafted part included.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1372468222158180424#1; RAQ 1372468222158180424#4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09, 2026-10-10 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 406-copied-augments.test.ts, 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts · Example tests: 406-copied-augments.test.ts::CR 710.2a: a Borrower that copied a unit carrying a Powerful virus is Powerful, 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Borrower of Forms: a Borrower that copied a Bellowing Boulder · Key: effects.copies.exact.mods</sub>

<a id="r710.2b"></a>**710.2b** More grafts may be added to a copy of a grafted unit, but they go underneath the copied grafts. See rule 722.

> *Example: A graft added to a Borrower of Forms that copied a grafted unit resolves below the copied grafts.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1372468222158180424#5 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Borrower of Forms: a graft added to a Borrower · Key: effects.copies.exact.mods.underneath</sub>

<a id="r710.2c"></a>**710.2c** When a copy of a modded unit leaves play, only its own card goes anywhere. Nothing is binned or erased for the mods it copied, because it has none. A mod later put on the copy is a real mod, and makes it Unstable as usual. See rules 410.3a, 410.4b.

> *Example: a Borrower of Forms that copied a unit with a virus dies, and only Borrower of Forms goes to the bin.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09, 2026-10-10 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 406-copied-augments.test.ts, 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts · Example test: 406-copied-augments.test.ts::CR 710.2c: when that copy dies, only Borrower of Forms goes to the bin · Key: effects.copies.exact.mods.leaving</sub>

<a id="r710.2d"></a>**710.2d** A [once] ability from a copied augment can be used once per turn on the copy, exactly as if a real mod of that card were on it. See rule 109.9.

> *Example: a Borrower of Forms that copied a Graxxlid-augmented unit can use Graxxlid's ability once per turn.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-10 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 406-copied-augments.test.ts · Example test: 406-copied-augments.test.ts::CR 710.2d: a Borrower that copied a Graxxlid-augmented unit can use Graxxlid · Key: effects.copies.exact.mods.once</sub>

<a id="r710.3"></a>**710.3.** If a unit becomes a copy more than once, the latest copy applies. It does not have two faces.

> *Example: an Apex Prime copy made when attacking and another made when blocking leave the unit one copy, the later one.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts · Example test: 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts::CR 710.3: attacking and then blocking leaves ONE face, not two · Key: effects.copies.latest</sub>

<a id="r710.4"></a>**710.4.** A copy of a unit that is itself a copy copies what that unit currently is, not the card printed on it.

> *Example: a copy of a Borrower of Forms that copied a virused unit carries the copied virus's text too.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-10-10 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts, 406-copied-augments.test.ts · Example test: 406-copied-augments.test.ts::CR 710.4: a copy of the copy chains · Demonstrated by test: 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts::CR 710.4: a copy of a COPY chains through the face · Key: effects.copies.of-a-copy</sub>

<a id="r710.5"></a>**710.5.** An effect that creates a copy of its own source ("create a copy of me") creates a token copy of what the source currently is. The token has none of the source's counters and none of its mods. See rules 304.4a, 714.

> *Example: Hooba-God, killed under its own attack trigger, still creates a copy of what it was.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 108-formation-class.test.ts, 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts · Example test: 108-formation-class.test.ts::Hooba-God: killed under its own attack trigger · Key: effects.copies.create-copy-of-me</sub>

<a id="r710.6"></a>**710.6.** A copy that lasts until regroup (Apex Prime) ends at regroup. The unit is its own card again, still with its counters, and it dies if its own stats cannot survive them. See rules 506.2d, 713.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Apex Prime · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts::CR 710.6: an until-regroup face lapses at regroup, and the revert can be lethal · Key: effects.copies.until-regroup</sub>

<a id="r710.7"></a>**710.7.** An ability that gives a unit "all abilities" of other units (Ancient One) gives it everything in those units' text boxes, including the text their mods give them, but not their attributes, their name or their stats. The unit has the text only while the other units qualify, and loses it the moment they stop.

> *Example: Ancient One has an adjacent ally's static ability, and loses it when the column breaks.*

> *Example: an adjacent ally's attributes are not given to Ancient One.*

> *Example: Ancient One keeps its own name and stats.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Ancient One; card: Ancient One · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts, 117-copy-everything.test.ts · Example tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts::CR 710.7: Ancient One radiates an adjacent ally's STATIC, and stops when the column breaks, 117-copy-everything.test.ts::CR 710.7: attributes are the ONE thing an adjacent ally does not donate, 26-metal-a.test.ts::CR 710.7: Ancient One projects an adjacent ally's face WITHOUT taking its name or its body · Key: effects.copies.all-abilities</sub>

<a id="r710.7a"></a>**710.7a** In text a unit gets this way, "I" and "me" mean the unit that has the text, not the unit it came from.

> *Example: next to Gatekeeper of Souls ("I must be targeted if able"), it is the Ancient One that must be targeted.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 117-copy-everything.test.ts · Example test: 117-copy-everything.test.ts::CR 710.7: an adjacent Gatekeeper of Souls makes the ANCIENT ONE must-be-targeted · Key: effects.copies.all-abilities.i-is-me</sub>

<a id="r710.8"></a>**710.8.** A copy of a spell is put on the stack above the spell it copies, so it resolves first. It is an effect on the stack like any other: players may respond to it, and it can be targeted and negated. See rules 108.4, 703, 704.2d.

> *Example: Earthbound Replicator's copy goes on the stack above the original, so it resolves first.*

> *Example: the copy can be chosen as a "target effect" and negated by Dematerialize.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1379132904931594372#0; RAQ 1355613076506017894#4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 138-spell-copy.test.ts · Example tests: 138-spell-copy.test.ts::CR 710.8 Earthbound Replicator: the copy is a real stack item, pushed ABOVE the original, 138-spell-copy.test.ts::the copy is offered as a "target effect" and Dematerialize negates it · Key: effects.copies.spells</sub>

<a id="r710.8a"></a>**710.8a** A copy of a spell keeps what the original declared when it was cast: its X, its mode and its targets. Additional costs the original paid are not paid again. The copy is given new targets only if the card that makes it says so. See rule 107.6.

> *Example: Maelstrom Charger's copy of Volatile Toxicity uses the original's sacrifice, which is not paid again.*

> *Example: A copy of Fight keeps both targets the original declared.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Earthbound Replicator · Designer: RAQ 1379132904931594372#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 138-spell-copy.test.ts · Example tests: 138-spell-copy.test.ts::CR 710.8a Maelstrom Charger: the copy inherits the cast-cost receipt, 138-spell-copy.test.ts::the copy keeps EVERY target the spell declared · Key: effects.copies.spells.declared</sub>

<a id="r710.8b"></a>**710.8b** A copy of a spell targets what it targets: an ability that triggers when something becomes a target sees the copy's targets, although the copy was not played. See rule 108.4.

> *Example: an enemy plays Burgeon on an attacker beside Earnest Defender and copies it with Maelstrom Charger, keeping the targets. Earnest Defender triggers twice, once for the spell and once for its copy.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts · Example test: 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts::cr:effects.copies.spells.targets — Earnest Defender triggers for the targets of a copied Burgeon as well as the original · Key: effects.copies.spells.targets</sub>

<a id="r710.8c"></a>**710.8c** A copy of a spell has no card. An instruction on it to erase itself erases nothing, and however many copies resolve, only the original card goes to a bin. See rule 704.2d.

> *Example: a resolved copy of Suspend puts nothing in a bin and its "Erase me." erases nothing; the original Suspend is erased once.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 138-spell-copy.test.ts · Example test: 138-spell-copy.test.ts::CR 710.8c Maelstrom Charger: a resolved copy bins nothing · Key: effects.copies.spells.no-card</sub>

<a id="r710.8d"></a>**710.8d** A copy of a spell carries the {Modular} mods the original was cast with, so their [Augment] attributes apply to the copy too. See rule 724.

> *Example: Spellbind cast with Primordial Coalescence as a Modular mod and copied with Maelstrom Charger: the copy on the stack carries the same mods as the original.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts · Example test: 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts::cr:effects.copies.spells.modular — a copy of Spellbind cast with Primordial Coalescence carries the same Modular mods · Key: effects.copies.spells.modular</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U16-10 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r710.9"></a>**710.9.** A card that transforms in play is the same unit with its other face up: its name, stats and text are those of the face that is up. It keeps that face while it stays in play, and turns back over as it leaves play (rule 410.3). See rules 108.3, 410.3.

> *Example: Scholar of the Void transforms into Beyond, Codex Incarnate and is still the same unit.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Scholar of the Void · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 43-dark-c.test.ts, 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts · Example test: 43-dark-c.test.ts::CR 108.3 — the transform is the SAME unit · Key: effects.faces.face-up</sub>

<a id="r711"></a>
### 711. Control Change

<a id="r711.1"></a>**711.1.** When a player gains control of a unit, the unit changes sides: it becomes that player's unit, an ally of that player's units and an enemy of its former controller's. Its owner does not change. See rules 102.4, 102.5, 102.7b.

> *Example: a stolen unit recalled goes to the hand of the player who controls it, and its owner is unchanged.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 246-zones-follow-control.test.ts · Example test: 246-zones-follow-control.test.ts::CR 400.4a: ownership does NOT move · Key: effects.control.what</sub>

<a id="r711.2"></a>**711.2.** A unit's mods change controller with it. The unit's new controller controls the mods and their text, so text a mod gives the unit refers to the new controller. See rules 102.6a, 720.

> *Example: Mindspore Fiend gives away a modded blocker, and its mods go with it.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.15; Manual p.34 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 25-wood-c.test.ts, 24-wood-b.test.ts · Example test: 24-wood-b.test.ts::Mindspore Fiend gives away a MODDED blocker · Demonstrated by test: 25-wood-c.test.ts::CR 711.2: a stolen unit takes its MODS with it · Key: effects.control.mods</sub>

<a id="r711.3"></a>**711.3.** A unit whose controller changes leaves its formation. If this happens during a battle, the unit stays in the battle out of formation for the rest of that battle: it attacks for nobody and blocks for nobody. It joins its new controller's side at regroup. See rules 602, 506.2a.

> *Example: a Robot token stolen by Download mid-battle is out of the formation for the rest of the battle.*

> *Example: the stolen Robot joins its new controller's side at regroup.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 145-erase-routes.test.ts · Example tests: 145-erase-routes.test.ts::CR 711.3 (viii): Download, 145-erase-routes.test.ts::CR 711.3 (ix): Download · Key: effects.control.formation</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U16-11 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r711.3a"></a>**711.3a** If a unit that was blocking changes controller, the attacking column it blocked stays blocked. See rules 606, 607.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; no gate test · Key: effects.control.formation.block-stays</sub>

<a id="r711.4"></a>**711.4.** A unit given to a player who is not present in the region where it stands (for example, during deployment) goes at once to that player's home region, with its mods. During a battle both players are present in the battle region, so the unit stays there. See rules 101.6, 506.2b.

> *Example: Mindspore Fiend gives away a modded blocker after combat, and it stays in the battle region.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 24-wood-b.test.ts, 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts · Example test: 24-wood-b.test.ts::Mindspore Fiend gives away a MODDED blocker · Key: effects.control.region</sub>

<a id="r711.5"></a>**711.5.** An effect that exchanges control of two units and swaps their positions (Organic Exchange) leaves both units in formation: each takes the other's place, which is on its new controller's side.

> *Example: Organic Exchange swaps control, and the attack slot passes to the exchanged unit.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Organic Exchange · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 24-wood-b.test.ts · Example test: 24-wood-b.test.ts::Organic Exchange: control swaps and the attack slot passes to the exchanged unit · Key: effects.control.exchange-positions</sub>

<a id="r711.6"></a>**711.6.** An effect that would give control of a unit to the player who already controls it, or of a unit that has gone, changes nothing. An "If you do" that depends on the handover does not happen (rule 101.5a). See rule 101.5a.

> *Example: Amphivore carries the grafts Flame Juggle and Ralph, and its trigger runs them three times. The first time, Ralph gives Amphivore to the opponent and creates three 1/1s. The second and third times the opponent already controls it, so nothing changes hands and no more 1/1s are made; Flame Juggle still runs all three times.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353859961855148103#3 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Amphivore with Ralph grafted · Key: effects.control.no-change</sub>

<a id="r711.7"></a>**711.7.** A unit that leaves play goes to the zones of the player who controls it, not of its owner, unless the effect names another player's zone (rule 405.3). See rules 405.3, 410.4a.

> *Example: a stolen unit recalled goes to the thief's hand.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 246-zones-follow-control.test.ts · Example test: 246-zones-follow-control.test.ts::CR 801.7a: a stolen unit recalled goes to the THIEF hand · Demonstrated by test: 246-zones-follow-control.test.ts::CR 400.4b: an explicit destination still wins · Key: effects.control.zones</sub>

<a id="r711.8"></a>**711.8.** A mod is controlled by the controller of the unit it is on. When a mod is moved onto another unit (Rotbeast, Reconfigure), its controller becomes that unit's controller. See rules 720, 410.1b.

> *Example: an augment Rotbeast moves onto an enemy takes its Unstable and its static ability with it.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.34; card: Rotbeast · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts · Example test: 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts::CR 720.7d Rotbeast: a moved augment takes {Unstable} and its static with it · Key: effects.control.mod-moved</sub>

<a id="r712"></a>
### 712. Stripping and Suppression

<a id="r712.1"></a>**712.1.** Some effects make a unit lose all its attributes, all its abilities, or both ("loses all attributes and abilities"). While the unit has lost them, they do not apply. See rule 113.3.

> *Example: Monke makes other units lose all attributes and abilities during battle.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Suppression Field; card: Monke · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 27-metal-b.test.ts · Example test: 27-metal-b.test.ts::Monke: CR 712.1 — other units lose all attributes and abilities during battle · Key: effects.stripping.what</sub>

<a id="r712.1a"></a>**712.1a** Losing all abilities takes everything the unit's text does by itself: its triggered abilities, its activated abilities (which cannot be activated), its static abilities and cost changes, and its replacement effects, whether printed on it, given by its mods or granted to it. A unit that loses its abilities stops applying its static abilities at once, whether a one-time effect (Suppression Field) or a continuous one (Transmogrifant, Monke) took them; two continuous strips that each fall under the other are rule 712.5. See rule 712.5.

> *Example: a copy silenced by Suppression Field stops applying the static it copied.*

> *Example: With Transmogrifant and Sandstone Defender in play, Sandstone Defender has lost its abilities, so a 1/1 token gets only Transmogrifant's +2/+2 and is a 3/3.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 4 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Transmogrifant · Designer: RAQ 1355845893219287132#0 · Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16; Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts, 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts, 462-continuous-strip-silences-statics.test.ts · Example tests: 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts::CR 712.1a, 710.1: suppression is a veto ABOVE copy — a silenced copy radiates nothing, 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts::cr:effects.stripping.what.abilities — Sandstone Defender stripped by Transmogrifant stops giving +0/+2, so a 1/1 token is 3/3 · Key: effects.stripping.what.abilities</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U16-14 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r712.1b"></a>**712.1b** Stats are not abilities. A unit that has lost its abilities keeps its stats, its counters and its stat changes; Tough and Balanced stop changing its stats only because they are attributes. It can still be targeted, block, die, and be grafted onto.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 27-metal-b.test.ts, 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 27-metal-b.test.ts::Formless: CR 712.1 — "and loses all attributes", abilities untouched · Key: effects.stripping.what.not-stats</sub>

<a id="r712.1c"></a>**712.1c** Erasing a unit's mods is a separate instruction from making it lose its abilities. Losing abilities silences the text its mods give it; erasing the mods removes them.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; no gate test · Printed: card: Suppression Field · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Key: effects.stripping.what.erase-mods</sub>

<a id="r712.2"></a>**712.2.** A strip takes what the unit has when the strip applies. An attribute or ability the unit gains afterwards (a mod attached later, an attribute or ability granted later, a static ability that starts applying later) is not taken. See rules 113.3, 113.3a, 113.3b.

> *Example: after Suppression Field resolves on Bubb, Protective Adaptations gives Bubb Piercing, and it has it.*

> *Example: a virus applied after Monke still gives its attribute.*

> *Example: A continuous strip takes a mod attached before it began, and leaves one attached after.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1355685844467581081#0; RAQ 1355845893219287132#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 402-raq-fix-stripping.test.ts · Example tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Suppression Field: an attribute granted after it resolved still applies, 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ timestamps: a virus applied AFTER Monke, 402-raq-fix-stripping.test.ts::§1 a static stripper takes a mod attached BEFORE it arrived · Key: effects.stripping.timestamp</sub>

<a id="r712.3"></a>**712.3.** When an effect that removes attributes (Formless, Suppression Field) is aimed at a unit in a formation, every unit in that unit's column loses its attributes, whichever unit they came from. Only the loss of attributes reaches the column: the rest of the effect, such as the loss of abilities or Formless's "base 4/4", applies to the target alone. See rule 712.8.

> *Example: Formless takes Blessed off the whole column, not just its target.*

> *Example: Suppression Field aimed at either unit of a column takes both Unaware and Flying from both.*

> *Example: Formless's base 4/4 still hits the target alone.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 4 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Formless · Designer: RAQ 1355845893219287132#3 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16, 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 299-formless-column.test.ts, 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 402-raq-fix-stripping.test.ts · Example tests: 299-formless-column.test.ts::CR 712.3 the report, 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Suppression Field: aimed at either unit of a column, 299-formless-column.test.ts::CR 712.3 the base rewrite still hits the TARGET alone · Key: effects.stripping.column</sub>

<a id="r712.3a"></a>**712.3a** A target that is not in a column (outside battle, or out of formation) loses only its own attributes.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 299-formless-column.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 299-formless-column.test.ts::CR 712.3a a target with no column · Key: effects.stripping.column.alone</sub>

<a id="r712.3b"></a>**712.3b** Each unit in the column loses its attributes as its own state, until the effect ends. A unit that leaves the column does not get them back, and a unit that joins the column afterwards keeps its own. See rule 113.3b.

> *Example: Formless is aimed at a unit whose column-mate is Blessed. The column-mate loses Blessed, stays without it for the rest of the battle after combat damage is over, and gets it back at regroup.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 299-formless-column.test.ts · Example test: 299-formless-column.test.ts::CR 712.3b the stamp outlives the column · Demonstrated by test: 299-formless-column.test.ts::CR 712.3b a unit that joins the column afterwards keeps its own attributes · Key: effects.stripping.column.per-unit</sub>

<a id="r712.3c"></a>**712.3c** A unit that has lost its attributes can still get attributes from a column it joins later, by sharing. It does not share the attributes it lost.

> *Example: a stripped Bubb that later joins a Balanced unit's column is Balanced, and the column is not Unaware.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355845893219287132#4 · Tests: 402-raq-fix-stripping.test.ts · Example test: 402-raq-fix-stripping.test.ts::§5 a stripped unit that joins a Balanced column later is Balanced · Key: effects.stripping.column.regain</sub>

<a id="r712.4"></a>**712.4.** An effect that switches off one named behaviour stops only that behaviour; it does not take the unit's other abilities. Only "loses all abilities" takes them all.

> *Example: Infernal Wispweaver stops a Wisp sacrificing itself after combat, and the Wisp keeps an ability it was given.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Infernal Wispweaver · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 249-suppression-scope.test.ts · Example test: 249-suppression-scope.test.ts::§2 a Wisp keeps an ability it was given · Key: effects.stripping.one-clause</sub>

<a id="r712.5"></a>**712.5.** Two continuous strips whose sources each fall under the other do not both apply: the newer one applies, and the source of the older one loses its abilities, so the older strip does not apply. If the newer source leaves play, the older strip applies again. Where only one of the two sources falls under the other's strip, that source loses its abilities, even if it came into play later (rule 113.3a).

> *Example: With two Transmogrifants in play, a 1/1 token is a 3/3: only the newer Transmogrifant's +2/+2 applies. The older one gets the newer one's +2/+2 and has lost its abilities; when the newer one leaves play, the older one applies again.*

> *Example: Two Monkes in battle: the newer Monke keeps its abilities, and the older one loses them.*

> *Example: The Everywhere comes into play under its controller's Transmogrifant: it loses its abilities, so the card it names keeps its abilities.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RQ 1145226276911714384; RQ 1148449043282927626; RQ 1148463157115887656 · Tests: 462-continuous-strip-silences-statics.test.ts, 28-metal-c.test.ts · Example tests: 462-continuous-strip-silences-statics.test.ts::462 two Transmogrifants in play: only the newer applies, a token gets +2/+2 once, 462-continuous-strip-silences-statics.test.ts::462 two Monkes in battle: the newer applies, the older is silenced, 462-continuous-strip-silences-statics.test.ts::462 a stripper only one way under another: The Everywhere entering under Transmogrifant is silenced, so what it names keeps its abilities · Key: effects.stripping.mutual</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U16-5 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r712.6"></a>**712.6.** The Everywhere's controller names a card during the haste step. Every unit with that name in The Everywhere's region loses all abilities, for as long as The Everywhere is in that region. Naming another card replaces the first, and a card that is not in play may be named.

> *Example: an enemy copy is silenced only once The Everywhere attacks into its region.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: The Everywhere · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 38-light-a.test.ts · Example test: 38-light-a.test.ts::The Everywhere: the silence is CONTINUOUS · Demonstrated by tests: 38-light-a.test.ts::The Everywhere: naming a card during [Haste] silences EVERY copy of it IN MY REGION, 38-light-a.test.ts::The Everywhere: a second naming replaces the first · Key: effects.stripping.named-card</sub>

<a id="r712.7"></a>**712.7.** Text a copy has from the mods of the unit it copied is part of the copy's own card text. An effect that makes the copy lose all attributes and abilities takes it, and "erase all of its mods" finds no mod to erase. See rule 710.2a.

> *Example: Suppression Field strips the augment text a Borrower of Forms copied.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-10 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 406-copied-augments.test.ts · Example test: 406-copied-augments.test.ts::CR 712.7: the copied augment text is the copy's card text · Key: effects.stripping.copied-text</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U16-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r712.8"></a>**712.8.** Units in the same column of a formation share their combat attributes: each unit in the column has every combat attribute any unit in it has. See rules 204.5, 802.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.24; Rulebook 2023 p.12 · Tests: 79-round17-layers.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 79-round17-layers.test.ts::CR 802.1c layer 5: {Inverted} is shared down the COLUMN · Key: effects.column-share</sub>

<a id="r712.8a"></a>**712.8a** A unit in a column has the column's attributes for everything it does while it is in the column, not only for combat damage. An ability it activates, or damage it deals by an effect, uses them too.

> *Example: an ability fired by a unit in a Blessed column gains its controller life.*

> *Example: Powerful from the column doubles that damage too.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts · Example tests: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts::CR 802.22e the report, 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts::CR 712.8a every source-side attribute rides the same line · Key: effects.column-share.everything</sub>

<a id="r712.8b"></a>**712.8b** Columns exist only in battle. Outside battle a unit shares no attributes with anything.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts::CR 712.8b outside battle there are no columns at all · Key: effects.column-share.battle-only</sub>

<a id="r712.8c"></a>**712.8c** Attributes are shared only within a column, never with the units to the left or right.

> *Example: Good Whale attacks with a unit behind it in its column and another unit in the next column. The unit behind it has Piercing; the unit in the next column does not.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.24; Rulebook 2023 p.12 · Tests: 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts · Example test: 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts::cr:effects.column-share.columns-only — a unit in the same column as Good Whale shares its Piercing, and one in the next column does not · Key: effects.column-share.columns-only</sub>

<a id="r712.8d"></a>**712.8d** When a unit leaves a column, the other units in it lose at once the attributes it was sharing with them.

> *Example: once the Deadly unit leaves Bellowing Boulder's column, the Boulder's ping is not Deadly.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.24; Manual p.24 · Designer: RAQ 1353895783266516992#5 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::once the Deadly partner leaves the column, the Boulder ping is not Deadly · Key: effects.column-share.leaving</sub>

<a id="r712.8e"></a>**712.8e** Non-combat attributes, such as Unstable, Burst and Modular, are not shared. A modded unit is Unstable, but the units in its column are not. See rules 204.5, 803.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.25 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts::CR 712.8e a modded (therefore Unstable) unit does not make its column-mate Unstable · Key: effects.column-share.non-combat</sub>

<a id="r712.8f"></a>**712.8f** Two questions are each unit's own, whatever its column shares: a unit with Feeble cannot block even in a column with other units, and an Alluring trigger comes from the unit that has Alluring. See rule 802.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts::CR 802.12a {Feeble} block legality, 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts::CR 802.15d {Alluring} still originates from the unit that prints it · Key: effects.column-share.own-questions</sub>

<a id="r713"></a>
### 713. State Checks

<a id="r713.1"></a>**713.1.** State checks are made by the game itself, at safe points. In a state check, every unit that should be dead dies, and every token that is in a zone where it cannot exist ceases to exist. See rules 713.2, 713.5.

> *Example: a lethally damaged unit and a dead unit token both go at the next safe point; the card reaches the bin, the token is erased, and a token recalled to a hand is erased from it.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25, 2026-10-06 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 2 gate test files · Tests: 380-no-action-ends-dead.test.ts, 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts · Example test: 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts::cr:effects.state.what — at a safe point a lethally damaged unit dies, a dead unit token is erased instead of staying in the bin, and a recalled token is erased from the hand · Key: effects.state.what</sub>

<a id="r713.2"></a>**713.2.** A unit dies in a state check if its defense is 0 or less, or if the damage marked on it is greater than or equal to its defense. See rules 112.5, 206.

> *Example: the turn's draw takes Dreadspawn Horror ("I gain -1/-1 for each card in your hand") to 0 defense, and it dies.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.40; Manual p.13 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-06 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 380-no-action-ends-dead.test.ts, 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts · Example test: 380-no-action-ends-dead.test.ts::CR 503.5: the turn draw that takes Dreadspawn Horror to 0 defense kills it at the turn flip · Key: effects.state.lethal</sub>

<a id="r713.3"></a>**713.3.** The end of every action is a safe point, so no action ends with a unit standing that should have died: not a draw, a draft, a recycle or a resource activation. An action that is waiting on a player's decision has not ended and is not at a safe point; it is checked when the answer comes and the action finishes. The one exception is Constructed's draw phase, where drawing 4 and putting 2 back are judged as one step: a player's units are not checked while that player still has the 2 cards to put back. See rules 503.5, 503.5b, 112.8, 713.3a.

> *Example: in Constructed, Dreadspawn Horror with 3 cards in hand is still in play after the draw of 4, and dies once its controller has put 2 back (5 cards in hand).*

> *Example: in Constructed, Dreadspawn Horror with 1 card in hand is a 4/2 after the draw phase and lives.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-06 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 3; verifier ran 4 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 380-no-action-ends-dead.test.ts · Example tests: 380-no-action-ends-dead.test.ts::CR 503.5b constructed: 3 cards in hand nets to 5, 380-no-action-ends-dead.test.ts::CR 503.5b constructed: drawing 4 does not kill before the 2 go back · Demonstrated by test: 380-no-action-ends-dead.test.ts::CR 713.3: a planning action that does not settle still ends with the dead unit gone · Key: effects.state.when</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U08-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r713.3a"></a>**713.3a** Deaths are also checked while an effect is still resolving, not only at safe points. Each time an effect puts counters on a unit, and after each part of an effect made of several parts, units that should be dead die at once, before the rest of the effect happens. See rules 713.3, 713.6.

> *Example: Pestilent Titan attacks and its trigger puts a -1/-1 counter on each unit. A 1/1 token dies as soon as it gets its counter, before the next unit gets one.*

<sub>Basis: Engine only · Verified: confirmed in round 3; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Engine: engine.ts:addCounters, engine.ts:checkDeaths · Tests: 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts · Example test: 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts::cr:effects.state.when.mid-resolution — the Pestilent Titan trigger kills a 1/1 before the next unit gets its counter · Key: effects.state.when.mid-resolution</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U16-16 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r713.4"></a>**713.4.** A unit can die in a state check from a change no damage caused: a new base, a stat change, a mod it loses, or a combination of attributes (Tough and Inverted) that leaves its defense at 0 or less. See rules 709.4d, 802.

> *Example: Rampart Guardian makes a unit Tough, then Reality Bender makes it Inverted, and it dies with no damage on it.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-21, 2026-08-25, 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 79-round17-layers.test.ts · Example test: 79-round17-layers.test.ts::CR 713.4: report #114 · Key: effects.state.no-damage-needed</sub>

<a id="r713.4a"></a>**713.4a** Pure does not save a unit from a state-check death. Pure hides attributes in a combat exchange; it does not change the unit's stats. See rule 802.

> *Example: a Pure 1/3 that is also Tough and Inverted reads 1/0 and dies in the state check.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts · Example test: 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts::cr:effects.state.no-damage-needed.pure — a Pure 1/3 that is Tough and Inverted reads 1/0 and still dies in the state check · Key: effects.state.no-damage-needed.pure</sub>

<a id="r713.5"></a>**713.5.** In a state check, a token that is in any zone other than play or the stack (a hand, a bin, a cache) ceases to exist. This happens before anything its arrival there caused to trigger is put on the stack. See rules 410.5, 407.3.

> *Example: A Hooba-Mon token is exchanged out of play by Skittering Blight. It goes to the bin, and the state check then erases it from there.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22, 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 129-disposal-tail.test.ts · Example test: 129-disposal-tail.test.ts::CR 410.7 (iv): a TOKEN body with no mods takes the token sweep · Key: effects.state.tokens</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U16-13 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r713.6"></a>**713.6.** Units that die in the same state check die together. Each of them still sees the others leave: an ability of one that triggers when another unit dies, or when a card is trashed, triggers for the others in the same batch. See rules 112.8, 706.

> *Example: Muck Rummager dies from combat damage in the same batch as an ally, and still triggers on that ally being trashed.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 258-simultaneous-disposal-listeners.test.ts · Example test: 258-simultaneous-disposal-listeners.test.ts::CR 706.8c: Muck Rummager hears an ally trashed in the same combat-damage batch it dies in · Key: effects.state.together</sub>

<a id="r713.6a"></a>**713.6a** A unit that dies in the batch does not see its own departure that way, and it is not a legal target or an ally for a count while the batch is dealt with.

> *Example: Cthyrian Culler dying alone makes nobody lose life for its own trash; dying beside an ally, it triggers once, for the ally.*

> *Example: Splort dies in the same batch as an ally; its trigger for the ally cannot target either dead unit.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Tests: 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts · Example tests: 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts::cr:effects.state.together.limits — Cthyrian Culler dying alone does not hear its own trash, and dying beside an ally hears only the ally, 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts::cr:effects.state.together.limits — Splort dying with an ally fires for the ally, and neither dead body is offered as a target · Key: effects.state.together.limits</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U16-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r713.7"></a>**713.7.** A unit sent out to counterattack, which does not exist until round 1 ends, is not checked for death while it is away. It is checked as it comes back. See rules 505.3b, 610.

> *Example: Prickly Protector, alive only through its own static, survives being declared as a counterattacker.*

> *Example: a counterattacker sent out alone survives the send and dies on arrival.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 250-ally-count-and-absence.test.ts · Example tests: 250-ally-count-and-absence.test.ts::Prickly Protector survives being declared as a counterattacker, 250-ally-count-and-absence.test.ts::a counterattacker sent out alone survives the send and dies on arrival · Key: effects.state.absent</sub>

<a id="r713.7a"></a>**713.7a** A unit that stays home does not count a unit that has gone to counterattack as an ally. See rule 102.7.

> *Example: Prickly Protector, carrying a -1/-1 counter, is alive only because it has one other ally. When that ally is sent to counterattack, the Protector stays home, no longer counts it, and dies.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 250-ally-count-and-absence.test.ts · Example test: 250-ally-count-and-absence.test.ts::scope: a unit left at home still loses the ally that counterattacked away · Key: effects.state.absent.home</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U13-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r713.8"></a>**713.8.** A unit that is destroyed dies: by a state check, by being sacrificed, or by being deleted. An {Unstable} unit that is destroyed still dies. A unit that leaves play any other way, by being recalled, cached, exchanged or erased, does not die. See rules 410.2, 407.1c.

> *Example: Banishment erases a unit, and no death is recorded.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25, 2026-09-20, 2026-10-11 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 145-erase-routes.test.ts, 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts · Example test: 145-erase-routes.test.ts::(vii): Banishment still fires no · Key: effects.state.dying</sub>

<a id="r714"></a>
### 714. Last-Known State

<a id="r714.1"></a>**714.1.** A unit's last-known state is what it was at the instant it left play: its card and the face it showed, its controller, its region, its attributes (including those its column shared with it), its power and defense, and the formation it stood in. See rule 704.7.

> *Example: Deathglow Strider, sharing Piercing in a Good Whale column with a +1/+1 counter, is destroyed before its after-combat trigger resolves; the trigger remembers a 3/4 Piercing Deathglow Strider of its controller, in that region and formation.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1353895783266516992#4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts · Example test: 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts::cr:effects.last-known.what — Deathglow Strider gone before its trigger resolves is remembered with its card, face, controller, region, column-shared Piercing, stats and formation · Key: effects.last-known.what</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U16-9 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r714.2"></a>**714.2.** An effect whose source has left play has the attributes its source had when it left, including attributes shared with it by its column then. See rule 704.7a.

> *Example: Bellowing Boulder dies with a Deadly unit beside it and its ping on the stack; the ping is still Deadly.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353895783266516992#4 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ dead unit: Bellowing Boulder dead with its ping on the stack · Key: effects.last-known.attributes</sub>

<a id="r714.3"></a>**714.3.** An effect whose source has left play that uses its source's power or defense uses the power or defense the source had when it left.

> *Example: Deathglow Strider (printed 2/3) with a +1/+1 counter is a 3/4. It leaves play before its after-combat trigger resolves; the trigger deals 4 to each opponent, its last-known defense, not its printed 3.*

> *Example: Spewing Mushroom (printed 1/3) gets +2/+0 and leaves play before its attack trigger resolves; the trigger creates a Poison 3, from its last-known power 3.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 3; verifier ran 4 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 401-raq-fix-stack.test.ts, 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts · Example tests: 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts::cr:effects.last-known.stats — Deathglow Strider 3/4 with a counter, gone before its trigger resolves, deals its last-known 4, not its printed 3, 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts::cr:effects.last-known.stats — Spewing Mushroom at +2/+0, gone before its attack trigger resolves, makes a Poison 3 · Demonstrated by tests: 401-raq-fix-stack.test.ts::CR 714.3 Deathglow Strider, 401-raq-fix-stack.test.ts::CR 714.3 Spewing Mushroom · Key: effects.last-known.stats</sub>

<a id="r714.4"></a>**714.4.** An effect whose source has left play that refers to the source's formation ("in my formation", "attacking units in my formation") uses the formation the source stood in when it left, for the rest of that battle. See rules 602, 704.7a.

> *Example: Hooba-Lin, killed under its own attack trigger, remembers its formation and the 1/1 joins it.*

> *Example: Embermaw Fledgling, gone before its trigger resolves, still counts the attackers it stood with.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1353895783266516992#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 108-formation-class.test.ts, 401-raq-fix-stack.test.ts · Example tests: 108-formation-class.test.ts::CR 714.4 Hooba-Lin: killed under its own attack trigger, 401-raq-fix-stack.test.ts::CR 714.4 Embermaw Fledgling · Key: effects.last-known.formation</sub>

<a id="r714.5"></a>**714.5.** A count of the allies adjacent to a source that has left play is 0.

> *Example: Flamebreath Initiate removed before its trigger resolves still makes a Fireball 1 (X = 0).*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353895783266516992#3 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ dead unit: Flamebreath Initiate removed · Key: effects.last-known.adjacent</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U16-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r714.6"></a>**714.6.** An effect whose source has left play that makes a copy of the source copies what the source was when it left. See rule 710.5.

> *Example: Echo of Despair, gone before its after-combat trigger resolves, still makes its copy.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Tests: 401-raq-fix-stack.test.ts, 108-formation-class.test.ts, 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts · Example test: 401-raq-fix-stack.test.ts::CR 714.6 Echo of Despair · Key: effects.last-known.face</sub>

<a id="r714.7"></a>**714.7.** While its source is still in play, an effect reads the source as it is when the effect resolves, not as it was when the effect was put on the stack. See rules 107.8, 109.3b.

> *Example: Deadly given back to Bellowing Boulder before its ping resolves makes the ping Deadly again.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353895783266516992#6; RAQ 1353895783266516992#6 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::Deadly given back to the Boulder before its ping resolves makes the ping Deadly again · Key: effects.last-known.live-source</sub>

<a id="r714.8"></a>**714.8.** A source that is still in play but out of formation (for example, a unit stolen mid-battle, rule 711.3) stands in no formation. An effect that places units in its formation, or counts it, does nothing. See rule 711.3.

> *Example: a Hooba-Lin alive but out of the formation makes no token.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-28, 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 108-formation-class.test.ts · Example test: 108-formation-class.test.ts::CR 602.6e Hooba-Lin: alive but out of the formation · Key: effects.last-known.out-of-formation</sub>

<a id="r714.9"></a>**714.9.** The facts of how a unit left play are fixed as it leaves: the region it left from, the counters it carried, whether it was a token, how it left, and where its card went. Abilities that trigger on its leaving use those facts.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 62-death-facts.test.ts, 427-cr-continuous-effects.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 62-death-facts.test.ts::CR 714.9: the death event carries token, verb, owner, region and destination · Key: effects.last-known.departure-facts</sub>

<a id="r714.9a"></a>**714.9a** An ability that triggers on its own source leaving play ("when I die") resolves in the region the source left from, not in its controller's home region. See rule 101.6.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 62-death-facts.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 62-death-facts.test.ts::CR 714.9a: a "when I die" trigger resolves in the region the unit DIED in · Key: effects.last-known.departure-facts.region</sub>

<a id="r720"></a>
### 720. Modifications, General

<a id="r720.1"></a>**720.1.** A modification (mod) changes a card's abilities by combining cards together. A card that can be a mod carries one of two mod symbols: the augment symbol (721) or the graft symbol (722). See rules 721, 722, 305.

> *Example: Aetherflux Golem (augment) and Flame Juggle (graft) are offered as mods; The Foretold, with neither symbol, is not.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.32 · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Example test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.mods.what — only a card with the augment or graft symbol is offered as a mod, and applying one changes the host · Key: effects.mods.what</sub>

<a id="r720.1a"></a>**720.1a** Virus and Modular are not further kinds of mod. A Virus is a card that can also be applied as an augment during battle (723). Modular lets mods be applied to a card as it is played (724). See rules 723, 724.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.34; card: Spellbind · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.mods.what.virus-modular — a Virus applied in battle is an augment action and attaches as an augment; no virus or modular kind of mod exists · Key: effects.mods.what.virus-modular</sub>

<a id="r720.2"></a>**720.2.** Applying a mod is a special action, which a player may perform during the deployment phase. See rule 507.2.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.32 · Designer: RAQ 1357483405276614856#1 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 1: · Key: effects.mods.special-action</sub>

<a id="r720.2a"></a>**720.2a** A timing icon other than Virus does not change when a card can be applied as a mod. A Battle card cannot be applied as a mod during battle, except under a card that lets cards be augmented as if they were Viruses (723.5) or to a Modular card as it is played (724). See rules 207.6, 723.5, 724, 720.2b.

> *Example: Burning Vengeance, a Battle card, is not offered as a mod during battle, but it is offered to Spellbind, a Modular card, played in battle.*

> *Example: Hooba-Lin, a Haste augment card, cannot be applied as a mod in the haste step when no card such as Slurpr allows it.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 4 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.32; card: Rook; card: Spellbind · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Example tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.mods.special-action.timing-icons — a {Battle} graft card is not offered as a mod in battle, but is on the menu of a Spellbind cast in battle, 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.mods.special-action.timing-icons — a {Haste} augment card (Hooba-Lin) is neither offered nor accepted as a mod in the haste step without Slurpr · Key: effects.mods.special-action.timing-icons</sub>

<a id="r720.2b"></a>**720.2b** A mod can be applied outside deployment only where a rule or a card says so: a Virus during battle (723.2); a card augmented in battle under a card that lets it be augmented as if it were a Virus, such as Rook (723.5); a mod applied in the haste step under a card that allows it, such as Slurpr (504.8a); and a mod applied to a Modular card as it is played (724). No other card widens the window. See rules 723, 504.8a, 724.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Rook; card: Slurpr; Manual p.34 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 40-light-c.test.ts::without a Slurpr the [Haste] refusal is unchanged · Key: effects.mods.special-action.exceptions</sub>

<a id="r720.2c"></a>**720.2c** An effect that lets a player play cards does not let them apply mods. Tides of the Cosmos cannot graft a card or apply a non-Virus augment; it may only put a Virus card onto a unit as a Virus. See rule 701.2c.

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1396955380000755795#3; RAQ 1357483405276614856#1; RAQ 1537748882501668934#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts, 404-raq-fix-tides.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Tides 4:, 404-raq-fix-tides.test.ts::CR 701.2c: a Virus card played by Tides as a Virus augments a unit and never enters play · Key: effects.mods.special-action.tides</sub>

<a id="r720.3"></a>**720.3.** Applying a mod is not playing a card, from whatever zone the mod comes. An ability that triggers when a player plays a unit, a spell or a card does not trigger when a mod is applied. See rules 701.2, 701.2a.

> *Example: Stalwart Sentinel counts a spell played from the bin, but not a mod applied from the bin.*

> *Example: A Virus applied during battle is not a spell: Origon does not negate it, and it does not count as a spell played.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 105-semantics-playwatch.test.ts, 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts · Example tests: 105-semantics-playwatch.test.ts::Stalwart Sentinel: CR 405.9, 105-semantics-playwatch.test.ts::Origon: a virus applied during battle is not a spell · Key: effects.mods.not-played</sub>

<a id="r720.4"></a>**720.4.** To apply a mod, a player must meet the mod card's affinity requirement and pay its mana cost, wherever the mod comes from. See rules 105.8, 720.4b.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.32 · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#1 · Tests: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts::RAQ Mods are NOT Played: an augment from hand needs its affinity and pays its cost, 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts::RAQ Mods are NOT Played: a Virus in battle needs its affinity and pays its cost · Key: effects.mods.cost</sub>

<a id="r720.4a"></a>**720.4a** A modifier to the cost of playing cards or spells does not change the cost of applying a mod, and a modifier to the cost of activating or triggering abilities does not apply to applying a mod either. See rules 701.2b, 111.10.

> *Example: Under Crevice Lurker, applying an augment during battle costs only its own mana.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24, 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 16-earth-a.test.ts, 40-light-c.test.ts · Example test: 16-earth-a.test.ts::Crevice Lurker: CR 720.4a — applying an augment during battle is NOT taxed · Key: effects.mods.cost.not-taxed</sub>

<a id="r720.4b"></a>**720.4b** A mod applied from the cache is priced by the permission that lets it be used. Under a fulfilled prophecy it costs nothing and ignores affinity. Under a glimpse this turn it costs its mana but ignores affinity. See rules 403.3c, 720.5a.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts, 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts::CR 801.9g: a LIVE glimpse grafts for the card's mana, ignoring affinity, 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts::CR 803.7k: a FULFILLED prophecy still grafts for free, affinity and all, 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts::CR 801.9g: the glimpse waives the pips, NOT the mana · Key: effects.mods.cost.cache</sub>

<a id="r720.5"></a>**720.5.** A mod may be applied from the player's hand or from their bin. See rule 405.8.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.32; Rulebook 2023 p.15 · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#2 · Tests: 04-mods.test.ts, 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 04-mods.test.ts::grafts can be applied from the bin, 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 3 · Key: effects.mods.zones</sub>

<a id="r720.5a"></a>**720.5a** A mod may also be applied from the cache, but only while a permission to use that card is live: a fulfilled prophecy, or a glimpse this turn. A cached card with no live permission cannot be applied as a mod. See rules 403.3b, 720.4b.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts, 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts::CR 801.9i: an expired glimpse is not a graft, not an augment, not anything, 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts::CR 803.7k: an UNFULFILLED prophecy cannot be grafted · Key: effects.mods.zones.cache</sub>

<a id="r720.6"></a>**720.6.** A mod becomes part of the card it is applied to, its host. A modified card is treated as a single card with all of the additional text from its mods; the mods are not separate from it. See rule 305.1.

> *Example: Aetherflux Golem augmented onto a unit gives that unit +2/+2 and is not a unit of its own.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.32; Rulebook 2023 p.15 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-29 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Example test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.mods.one-card — an augment becomes part of its host: the host has its text, and the mod is not a separate unit · Key: effects.mods.one-card</sub>

<a id="r720.6a"></a>**720.6a** A mod is controlled by its host's controller. A player who augments a card onto an opponent's unit gives that opponent control of the mod and all of its text. See rule 102.6a.

> *Example: In battle, a player applies Corrupting Blight as a Virus to an opponent's Bubb. The opponent now controls the Blight, so its "you" is the opponent: after combat, a player who doesn't control Bubb gains control of it, and Bubb ends up with the player who applied the Blight.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.34; Manual p.34; Rulebook 2023 p.15 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-29 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 23-wood-a.test.ts · Example test: 23-wood-a.test.ts::Corrupting Blight: defects after combat when played normally; steals the host as a Virus · Key: effects.mods.one-card.control</sub>

<a id="r720.6b"></a>**720.6b** On a mod's text, "you" means the host's controller. See rule 102.6a.

> *Example: Oorblak applied as a Virus to an opponent's unit: the combat damage that would be dealt to that opponent is dealt to their own unit instead.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25, 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 17-earth-b.test.ts · Example test: 17-earth-b.test.ts::Oorblak: as a Virus, "me" is the HOST · Key: effects.mods.one-card.you</sub>

<a id="r720.6c"></a>**720.6c** On a mod's text, "I", "me" and "my" mean the host.

> *Example: Life Leech applied as a Virus gives its host, not the Leech, +3/+3 when its controller pays 5 life.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts, 17-earth-b.test.ts · Example test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Life Leech: donated as a Virus, "I" is the HOST · Key: effects.mods.one-card.me</sub>

<a id="r720.6d"></a>**720.6d** On a mod's text, "other" and "another" exclude only that mod itself, not other mods made from copies of the same card.

> *Example: A host wearing two Rotbeast augments: each Rotbeast moves the other.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 121-another-identity.test.ts · Example test: 121-another-identity.test.ts::CR 720.6d Rotbeast: a SECOND Rotbeast augment is "another" · Key: effects.mods.one-card.other</sub>

<a id="r720.6e"></a>**720.6e** When a unit changes controller, its mods change controller with it. See rule 711.

> *Example: Download steals a unit token that carries an augment; the augment changes controller with it.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 3 gate test files · Tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts, 24-wood-b.test.ts, 04-mods.test.ts · Example test: 26-metal-a.test.ts::Download steals a MODDED unit token · Key: effects.mods.one-card.control-change</sub>

<a id="r720.6f"></a>**720.6f** There is no limit to the number of mods a card can have.

> *Example: Six Aetherflux Golems augmented onto one unit give it +12/+12.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.33; Rulebook 2023 p.15 · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Example test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.mods.one-card.no-limit — six augments are applied to one unit and every one of them counts · Key: effects.mods.one-card.no-limit</sub>

<a id="r720.7"></a>**720.7.** As long as a card is modded, it has {Unstable}: when it dies or is erased, it and all of its mods are erased. See rules 410.4b, 803.

> *Example: A unit carrying Ephemeral Skywalker as an augment dies; both cards are erased and neither reaches the bin.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.35; Rulebook 2023 p.15 · Tests: 04-mods.test.ts, 224-mod-trash.test.ts · Example test: 04-mods.test.ts::augments: type-line attribute grant, unstable erasure · Key: effects.mods.unstable</sub>

<a id="r720.7a"></a>**720.7a** If a modded card leaves play without dying or being erased, for example when it is returned to a hand, its mods are put into the bin and the card goes on alone. See rules 410.4, 410.4a.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.35; Manual p.35; Manual p.35 · Tests: 141-despawn-mods.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 141-despawn-mods.test.ts::CR 801.2f (iv): a nontoken mod is binned and trashed exactly once on all three routes · Key: effects.mods.unstable.leave-play</sub>

<a id="r720.7b"></a>**720.7b** When a modded unit is cached, its mods do not follow it into the cache; they go to the bin. See rule 403.7.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::caching a unit sheds its mods to the bin · Key: effects.mods.unstable.cache</sub>

<a id="r720.7c"></a>**720.7c** A token mod has no card of its own. It never enters a bin: however its host leaves play, the token mod is erased. See rules 410.4c, 407.3a.

> *Example: A unit carrying a Wraith token as an augment is recalled, cached or killed. Whichever way it leaves, the Wraith goes to no bin and is not trashed: it is erased.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 141-despawn-mods.test.ts, 129-disposal-tail.test.ts · Example test: 141-despawn-mods.test.ts::CR 407.3a (v): a token mod reaches the erased pile exactly once · Key: effects.mods.unstable.token-mod</sub>

<a id="r720.7d"></a>**720.7d** The {Unstable} that a mod gives goes with the mod. A unit stops having {Unstable} for this reason when its last mod leaves it, and a unit a mod is moved onto has it from then on. See rule 720.10.

> *Example: Rotbeast moves its host's other augments onto an enemy; the enemy becomes Unstable and the augment's static goes with it.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts · Example test: 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts::CR 720.7d Rotbeast: a moved augment takes {Unstable} and its static with it · Key: effects.mods.unstable.moves</sub>

<a id="r720.7e"></a>**720.7e** A copy of a modded unit (Borrower of Forms) is not itself modded and does not have {Unstable} for that reason. A mod applied to the copy afterwards makes it {Unstable} in the ordinary way. See rule 710.

> *Example: A Borrower of Forms that has resolved becomes Unstable when a mod is attached to it.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1372468222158180424#3 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts, 26-metal-a.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Borrower of Forms: a mod attached to it after it resolved makes it Unstable · Demonstrated by test: 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts::CR 720.7e: a Borrower that copied a modded unit dies to the bin · Key: effects.mods.unstable.copy</sub>

<a id="r720.8"></a>**720.8.** When a host is recalled or cached and its nontoken mods are left in a bin, each of those mods is trashed, and the host's controller is the player who trashes it. See rule 405.4.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-29 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 224-mod-trash.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 224-mod-trash.test.ts::CR 720.8: a mod trashed on a recall is trashed by the host controller, not by its owner, 224-mod-trash.test.ts::CR 720.8: a cached host attributes its left-behind mods the same way a recalled one does · Key: effects.mods.trash</sub>

<a id="r720.8a"></a>**720.8a** A nontoken mod erased together with its {Unstable} host is not trashed. The host's single trash counts for the whole unit. See rule 405.4.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-29 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 224-mod-trash.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 224-mod-trash.test.ts::CR 720.8a: a nontoken mod erased with its Unstable host is not trashed at all · Key: effects.mods.trash.erased-with-host</sub>

<a id="r720.9"></a>**720.9.** An effect or a cost can erase a mod off a host that stays in play. The mod card goes to the erased pile of the mod's controller. The host stays in play, and can die if losing the mod leaves it unable to survive. See rules 407.2, 407.2a. *(Engine differs, see F-U17-1.)*

> *Example: Return to Nature negates everything on the stack and erases all mods in the region.*

> *Example: A mod on a stolen unit is erased off it; it goes to the erased pile of the player who stole the unit, not its owner's.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26, 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 5 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 4 gate test files · Tests: 17-earth-b.test.ts, 178-played-item-and-erased-mods.test.ts, 246-zones-follow-control.test.ts, 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Example tests: 17-earth-b.test.ts::Return to Nature: negates everything on the stack and erases all mods in the region, 246-zones-follow-control.test.ts::CR 720.9: the erased pile files a stolen mod under the THIEF · Key: effects.mods.erase-off-host</sub>

<a id="r720.9a"></a>**720.9a** A token mod erased off a host that stays in play is not recorded on the erased pile, because a token is not a card. See rule 720.7c. *(Engine differs, see F-U17-4.)*

> *Example: A Wraith token mod erased off a host that stays in play, as the payment of a cost, is not filed on the erased pile.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Example test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.mods.erase-off-host.token — a Wraith token mod erased off a living host as a cost (eraseMod) is not filed on the erased pile · Key: effects.mods.erase-off-host.token</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U07-5 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r720.10"></a>**720.10.** An effect can move a mod from one host to another (Reconfigure, Rotbeast). Moving a mod is not a zone change: the mod never leaves play, and nothing despawns. See rules 410.1b, 721.5.

> *Example: Reconfigure moves Bubb and its Growing Plague onto a Robot; Growing Plague's "when I despawn" does not trigger.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1353847640214999170#0 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Reconfigure vs Despawn · Key: effects.mods.moving</sub>

<a id="r720.10a"></a>**720.10a** A moved mod is controlled by its new host's controller. See rule 720.6a.

> *Example: Rotbeast moves augments onto an enemy unit; the enemy now controls them, along with their text.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; no gate test · Key: effects.mods.moving.control</sub>

<a id="r720.10b"></a>**720.10b** Moving a mod does not refresh it. A once-per-turn ability on the mod that was already used this turn stays used on the new host. See rule 109.9e.

> *Example: A Graxxlid used this turn and moved by Reconfigure cannot be used again this turn.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1353848722974445658#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Reconfigure vs Once per Turn · Demonstrated by test: 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts::CR 720.10b: a moved mod carries its spent augment budget · Key: effects.mods.moving.once</sub>

<a id="r720.10c"></a>**720.10c** Moving a mod is not applying it. An ability that triggers when a mod is applied does not trigger when a mod is moved, unless the moving effect says the mods are augmented (721.5a). See rule 721.5a.

> *Example: Rotbeast moves its Curio Drifter augment onto an enemy Perpetual Construct, which makes no unit.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25, 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Example test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.mods.moving.not-applying — Rotbeast moving an augment onto Perpetual Construct fires no mod-applied event and makes no unit · Key: effects.mods.moving.not-applying</sub>

<a id="r720.11"></a>**720.11.** A mod's effects take their timestamp from when the mod was applied. A mod applied after an effect that removes attributes and abilities on the same layer (Monke) still gives its attribute and ability. See rules 709, 113.2.

> *Example: A Virus applied after Monke's effect began still gives its attribute.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1357965714807586897#0 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ timestamps: a virus applied AFTER Monke still gives its attribute · Key: effects.mods.timestamps</sub>

<a id="r720.12"></a>**720.12.** An ability that triggers when a mod is applied to its unit triggers once for each mod applied. See rule 721.5a.

> *Example: Perpetual Construct makes an X/X for an applied mod, X the mod's cost.*

> *Example: Reconfigure moves three mods onto Perpetual Construct: three triggers, a 1/1, a 3/3 and a 4/4.*
