<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Perpetual Construct · Designer: RAQ 1353856176558706769#0 · Tests: 17-earth-b.test.ts, 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example tests: 17-earth-b.test.ts::Perpetual Construct: an applied mod creates an X/X, X = the mod's cost, 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Reconfigure onto Perpetual Construct · Key: effects.mods.applied-triggers</sub>

<a id="r721"></a>
### 721. Augment

<a id="r721.1"></a>**721.1.** Augment is a modification. An augment adds the text that follows its augment symbol to the card it is applied to. See rule 208.

> *Example: Aetherflux Golem, a 1/1 whose augment text is "I gain +2/+2", gives its host +2/+2.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.32; Rulebook 2023 p.15 · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Example test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.augment.what — an augment adds the text after its augment symbol to the host, not the rest of the card · Key: effects.augment.what</sub>

<a id="r721.1a"></a>**721.1a** An augment symbol at the start of a paragraph in the text box gives the host that whole paragraph. See rule 208.2.

> *Example: Growing Plague applied as an augment gives its host "When I despawn, each other player draws two cards."*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.32 · Tests: 23-wood-a.test.ts · Example test: 23-wood-a.test.ts::Growing Plague: draws on spawn; despawn (as augment) makes each other player draw two · Key: effects.augment.what.text-box</sub>

<a id="r721.1b"></a>**721.1b** An augment symbol on the type line gives the host the attributes on that type line. It gives no stats. See rule 208.3.

> *Example: Bubb ([Augment] {Unaware}) gives its host Unaware, and not its 5/6.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.32; card: Chitin Shredder · Tests: 16-earth-a.test.ts, 04-mods.test.ts · Example test: 16-earth-a.test.ts::Bubb: 5/6 Unaware; type-line [Augment] donates Unaware (attrs only, no stats) · Key: effects.augment.what.type-line</sub>

<a id="r721.1c"></a>**721.1c** On a host, only the augment's own augment text works. The rest of the augment card's text, including body text printed outside the augment paragraph and attributes printed before a text-box augment symbol, does nothing for the host. See rule 208.1.

> *Example: Infernal Wispweaver played as a unit gives your wisps +2/+1. Applied as an augment, it gives its host only "At the end of turn, create a wisp"; the +2/+1 for your wisps, printed outside the augment paragraph, does nothing.*

> *Example: Smouldering Inferno has {Piercing} on its type line and "[Augment] After combat, sacrifice me" in its text box. Applied as a Virus to an attacking Rune Channeler, it does not give the Channeler Piercing, and after combat the Channeler sacrifices itself.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 248-augment-box-scope.test.ts, 04-mods.test.ts · Example tests: 248-augment-box-scope.test.ts::§3 GUARD: a card that prints both halves radiates its body clause from play, never from a mod, 04-mods.test.ts::virus augment during battle: on the stack, donated to an enemy, text-only transfer · Key: effects.augment.what.box-only</sub>

<a id="r721.1d"></a>**721.1d** A card that is played normally reads its whole text, its augment text included. See rules 305.4, 109.7.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.43; Manual p.35 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 248-augment-box-scope.test.ts, 16-earth-a.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 248-augment-box-scope.test.ts::§5 PIN: a card played normally still reads its own [Augment] box · Key: effects.augment.what.played</sub>

<a id="r721.1e"></a>**721.1e** Augment text keeps its kind on the host. A static ability given by an augment ("I gain +2/+2") is a continuous effect on the host for as long as the mod is attached; it is not a triggered ability and does not use the stack. See rule 707.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 142-static-conformance.test.ts, 16-earth-a.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 142-static-conformance.test.ts::CR 721.1e: Aetherflux Golem is a STATIC · Key: effects.augment.what.kind-kept</sub>

<a id="r721.1f"></a>**721.1f** Augment text that triggers on the host's own departure ("When I despawn") triggers whichever way the host leaves play: when it dies, is recalled or is cached. See rule 410.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 141-despawn-mods.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 141-despawn-mods.test.ts::CR 721.1f (i): a donated "[Augment] When I despawn" fires on a RECALL, 141-despawn-mods.test.ts::CR 721.1f (ii): a donated "[Augment] When I despawn" fires on a CACHE · Key: effects.augment.what.despawn</sub>

<a id="r721.2"></a>**721.2.** A card can be applied as an augment if it prints the augment symbol, in its text box or on its type line, whether or not its augment text does anything. See rule 208.4.

> *Example: Chitin Shredder prints the augment symbol only on its type line and has no text box, and it can be applied as an augment.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.32 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Example test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.augment.which-cards — a card with the augment symbol on its type line and an empty text box (Chitin Shredder) is applied as an augment · Key: effects.augment.which-cards</sub>

<a id="r721.3"></a>**721.3.** To apply an augment, the player takes these steps in order: (1) meets the augment's affinity requirement; (2) pays its mana cost; (3) selects a target to apply it onto; (4) places the augment card beneath the target, with its text box visible beneath the target's. See rules 720.4, 110.10.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.32; Manual p.32; Manual p.32 · Tests: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 408-raq-new-threads.test.ts::RAQ Mods are NOT Played: an augment from hand needs its affinity and pays its cost · Key: effects.augment.procedure</sub>

<a id="r721.4"></a>**721.4.** During deployment a player can augment only their own units. An opponent's unit can be augmented only with a Virus during battle (723.2), or under a card that lets cards be augmented as if they were Viruses (723.5). See rules 723.2, 723.5.

> *Example: In deployment Curio Drifter can augment your own unit but not an opponent unit; in battle Aetherflux Golem (a Virus) can augment the attacking enemy.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.32; Manual p.32; Rulebook 2023 p.15 · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Example test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.augment.hosts — in deployment an augment goes only onto your own unit; in battle a Virus may go onto an opposing unit · Key: effects.augment.hosts</sub>

<a id="r721.4a"></a>**721.4a** During deployment a player may also augment a spell token they have in play, with any augment, not only a Virus. The token gains only the augment's attributes. See rules 305.6, 507.2b.

> *Example: An augmented token deals {Powerful} damage when cast.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts · Example test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::CR 721.4a: only ATTRIBUTES transfer · Demonstrated by test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::CR 721.4a: a spell token is a legal augment host during deployment · Key: effects.augment.hosts.spell-token</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U06-9 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r721.4b"></a>**721.4b** An augment applied to a spell, on the stack (723.4) or as it is played through Modular (724), gives the spell only its type-line attributes. Augment text and static abilities give a spell nothing, but applying such an augment is still legal. See rules 723.4, 724.4.

> *Example: An augment-text mod applied to Spellbind is accepted and does nothing.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts, 91-modular.test.ts, 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts · Example test: 91-modular.test.ts::CR 724.4b: an [Augment]-TEXT mod is accepted and does nothing · Demonstrated by test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::CR 721.4a: a text-only augment on a token grants nothing, and says so · Key: effects.augment.hosts.spell</sub>

<a id="r721.5"></a>**721.5.** Reconfigure augments a unit and all of its mods onto another unit. Its first target must have the augment symbol. See rule 720.10.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Reconfigure; card: Reconfigure · Tests: 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts, 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts::Reconfigure: moves target augment unit AND its mods onto another target unit · Key: effects.augment.reconfigure</sub>

<a id="r721.5a"></a>**721.5a** Each mod Reconfigure moves is applied to the new host. An ability that triggers when a mod is applied to that unit triggers once for each moved mod. See rule 720.12.

> *Example: Bubb with two mods reconfigured onto Perpetual Construct makes three tokens, one per mod applied.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353856176558706769#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Reconfigure onto Perpetual Construct · Key: effects.augment.reconfigure.each-applied</sub>

<a id="r721.5b"></a>**721.5b** A unit that has become a copy of a card with the augment symbol does not have that symbol, so it cannot be Reconfigure's first target. See rules 208.5, 710.

> *Example: A Borrower of Forms that copied an augment unit cannot be chosen as Reconfigure's first target.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; no gate test · Designer: RAQ 1372468222158180424#6 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Key: effects.augment.reconfigure.copy</sub>

<a id="r721.6"></a>**721.6.** An effect can augment a card onto a unit when it resolves. When the effect augments a token ("Augment a Wraith onto an ally"), the token is created directly as a mod of that unit. See rule 304.

> *Example: An augmented Wraith gives its host its first line: at the start of deployment the host puts a -1/-1 counter on an ally, here itself, its only ally, so a 4/4 host becomes 3/3.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Wraith; card: Blight's End; card: Xzydris · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Example test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::CR 721.1a: an augmented Wraith donates BOTH lines to its host · Demonstrated by test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::CR 721.6: "augment a Wraith onto a unit" makes the same token, directly as a mod · Key: effects.augment.by-effect</sub>

<a id="r722"></a>
### 722. Graft

<a id="r722.1"></a>**722.1.** Graft is a modification that combines several effects under a single cause. It is marked by the graft symbol, written [Switch] (unbounded) or [Switch1] (bounded) in the card text this document quotes. See rule 205.4.

> *Example: Flame Juggle grafted onto Oracle of the Flame: one sacrifice of the Oracle creates its own Fireball 1 and Flame Juggle's three Fireball 1s.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.33; Manual p.33; card: Oracle of the Flame · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Example test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.graft.what — a graft puts a second effect under the host cause: one sacrifice of Oracle of the Flame makes both effects · Key: effects.graft.what</sub>

<a id="r722.1a"></a>**722.1a** A graft card's ability has a cause, before the graft symbol, and an effect, after it. Oracle of the Flame's cause is "Sacrifice me" and its effect is "Create a Fireball 1". See rule 205.4.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.33; Manual p.33; Rulebook 2023 p.16 · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.graft.what.cause-effect — Oracle of the Flame cause is Sacrifice me and its effect is Create a Fireball 1 · Key: effects.graft.what.cause-effect</sub>

<a id="r722.1b"></a>**722.1b** When a card is grafted, only what follows its graft symbol is added to the host. Everything printed before the symbol, its cost and cause included, is ignored. See rule 205.4.

> *Example: A grafted Omniwield Evoker adds "Put a +1/+1 counter on me" to the host's ability; its own cost of three, printed before the graft symbol, is not paid.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#5 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 6 · Key: effects.graft.what.after-symbol</sub>

<a id="r722.1c"></a>**722.1c** A graft card still works as written when it is played normally. A spell or spell unit with a graft symbol resolves normally when it is played, and can later be grafted from the bin. See rules 305.5, 305.4.

> *Example: Once Leaping Lillik has died, it can be grafted from the bin.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.35 · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#3 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 4 · Key: effects.graft.what.played</sub>

<a id="r722.2"></a>**722.2.** Both cards must have the graft symbol. The host must be a unit in play with a graft cause of its own.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.33; Rulebook 2023 p.16 · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#1 · Tests: 04-mods.test.ts, 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 04-mods.test.ts::grafting requires the graft symbol on both cards and a cause on the host, 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 2 · Key: effects.graft.requirements</sub>

<a id="r722.3"></a>**722.3.** Applying a graft follows the same cost and timing as an augment: from the hand or the bin, during deployment, paying the card's cost and meeting its affinity. See rules 720.4, 720.5.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.33; Manual p.33; Manual p.33 · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#2 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 3 · Key: effects.graft.applying</sub>

<a id="r722.3a"></a>**722.3a** A graft is applied only in deployment, never in the haste step or in battle, even when the graft card has Haste. The exceptions are a card that allows mods in the haste step, such as Slurpr (504.8a), and a Modular card, to which a graft card may be applied as the Modular card is played, in battle too (724). See rules 504.8a, 507.2a, 724, 720.2b.

> *Example: With Slurpr in play, a graft can be applied during the haste step.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Slurpr; card: Spellbind · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#0; RAQ 1355115946032889914#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 40-light-c.test.ts, 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Example test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Slurpr: a GRAFT lands during [Haste] too · Demonstrated by test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 1: · Key: effects.graft.applying.deployment-only</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U17-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r722.3b"></a>**722.3b** A card that lets cards be augmented in battle as if they were Viruses (Rook) does not let a card be grafted in battle. See rule 723.5.

> *Example: With Rook in play, Curio Drifter is offered as an augment in battle, but Flame Juggle is not offered as a graft.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Rook · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Example test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.graft.applying.not-by-rook — with Rook in play an augment card is offered in battle but a graft card is not · Key: effects.graft.applying.not-by-rook</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U17-5 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r722.3c"></a>**722.3c** Applying a graft targets the host. An ability that triggers when its unit becomes targeted (Mohruung) triggers first, before the graft is attached. See rules 110.10, 110.11.

> *Example: Grafting onto Mohruung targets it, so it makes its Crystal.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#4 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 5 · Key: effects.graft.applying.targets</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U03-13 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r722.3d"></a>**722.3d** A player applying a new graft may insert it at any position below the host's own card, but may not re-order the grafts already applied.

> *Example: A new graft slides between two already applied, whose order stays fixed.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.33; Manual p.33; Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#9 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 04-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 10 · Demonstrated by test: 04-mods.test.ts::graft insert position: below the base, order controls resolution · Key: effects.graft.applying.position</sub>

<a id="r722.4"></a>**722.4.** Each grafted effect is added to the cause of the host's own card. The host's ability then reads "cause: effect 1 AND effect 2 AND effect 3 …", in the order the grafts sit.

> *Example: Accelerated Germination grafted onto Oracle of the Flame reads "Sacrifice me: Create a Fireball 1 AND (once per turn) create two 1/1 units."*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.33; Manual p.33; Rulebook 2023 p.16 · Key: effects.graft.composite</sub>

<a id="r722.4a"></a>**722.4a** The host's own graft cause decides when the whole composite triggers or can be activated.

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#6 · Tests: 04-mods.test.ts, 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 04-mods.test.ts::graft composition: composite fires as ONE stack item, top-to-bottom · Key: effects.graft.composite.top-cause</sub>

<a id="r722.4b"></a>**722.4b** The composite is a single ability. It goes on the stack as one item, resolves all at once, and a single negation stops all of it. See rule 703.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.33; Manual p.33; Rulebook 2023 p.16 · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#7 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 04-mods.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 8, 04-mods.test.ts::composite is ONE stack item in battle · Key: effects.graft.composite.one-ability</sub>

<a id="r722.4c"></a>**722.4c** The composite resolves from top to bottom: the host's own effect first, then each graft in the order it sits. See rule 704.

> *Example: On a Mohruung host, Overbloom grafted above Spewing Mushroom makes a Poison 8; grafted below it, a Poison 1.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.33; Manual p.33 · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#8 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 9 · Key: effects.graft.composite.order</sub>

<a id="r722.4d"></a>**722.4d** Every target of the composite is declared when it is put on the stack. A part that requires a target must take one if any is legal, even one of the player's own units. See rules 110, 702.8b.

> *Example: Plodding Pebble, with Leaping Lillik ("Delete target unit") grafted under it, attacks into an empty region and is hit by a Fireball 1. As its trigger goes on the stack, the delete must take a target: with no enemy unit there, Plodding Pebble itself is legal, and the player cannot choose no target.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#15; RAQ 1355115946032889914#15 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 Plodding Pebble example · Key: effects.graft.composite.targets</sub>

<a id="r722.4e"></a>**722.4e** A triggered composite with a part that requires a target, when that part has no legal target, is not put on the stack at all. Its untargeted parts do not happen either. See rule 702.8b. *(Engine differs, see F-U14-1.)*

> *Example: Megadeath with Resurrect grafted attacks with no cheap unit in the bin: no Poison 5 either.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1410252965276684418#2 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ target requirements: a graft trigger with a required target and none available makes nothing at all · Key: effects.graft.composite.no-target</sub>

<a id="r722.4f"></a>**722.4f** A composite fizzles when it has lost all of its targets, and then none of it happens, its untargeted parts included. While at least one target remains, every part resolves as far as it can. Only a composite that was never targeted cannot fizzle: one with no part that calls for a target, or one whose only target was optional ("up to one") and none was chosen (see rule 704.6g). See rule 704.

> *Example: Spewing Mushroom carries Biotoxicity and Technological Superiority as grafts. It attacks, and its composite trigger targets Spewing Mushroom, the only target it declares. The opponent deletes the Mushroom with Leaping Lillik in response: the composite fizzles, and Biotoxicity's untargeted Poisons are not created either.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts · Example test: 78-round17-core.test.ts::CR 722.4f: a graft composite that loses its ONLY target fizzles whole · Demonstrated by tests: 78-round17-core.test.ts::CR 704.6b: one surviving target carries the untargeted grafts through, 78-round17-core.test.ts::CR 704.6d: an item that declares NO target anywhere never fizzles, 78-round17-core.test.ts::CR 704.6g: a required target with no legal candidate at cast still fizzles · Key: effects.graft.composite.fizzle</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U17-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r722.4g"></a>**722.4g** A graft composite is a triggered or activated ability like any other. A modifier to the cost of activating or triggering abilities (Crevice Lurker) applies to it. See rule 111.10f.

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355103348378042515#1 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ Crevice Lurker: a graft trigger is taxed like any other · Key: effects.graft.composite.tax</sub>

<a id="r722.5"></a>**722.5.** A graft is either unbounded ([Switch]) or bounded ([Switch1]). An unbounded graft can trigger any number of times; a bounded graft can trigger only once per turn. See rule 109.9.

> *Example: Plodding Pebble's bounded graft gives one counter per turn.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.33; Manual p.33; Rulebook 2023 p.16 · Tests: 17-earth-b.test.ts, 04-mods.test.ts · Example test: 17-earth-b.test.ts::Plodding Pebble: dealt damage → a +1/+1 counter, once per turn ([Switch1]) · Key: effects.graft.bounded</sub>

<a id="r722.5a"></a>**722.5a** Under an unbounded cause, the composite can fire any number of times, but each bounded graft in it is included only the first time in a turn. See rule 109.9i.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.33 · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#13 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 04-mods.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 12: an unbounded host activated twice · Key: effects.graft.bounded.unbounded-cause</sub>

<a id="r722.5b"></a>**722.5b** Under a bounded cause, the whole composite fires only once per turn, its unbounded grafts included. See rule 109.9h.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.33 · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#14 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 04-mods.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 12: a bounded host triggers once per turn · Key: effects.graft.bounded.bounded-cause</sub>

<a id="r722.5c"></a>**722.5c** Each grafted card has its own use. Two copies of the same bounded graft on one host each have one use. See rule 109.9k.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 94-bounded-uses.test.ts · Key: effects.graft.bounded.per-mod</sub>

<a id="r722.5d"></a>**722.5d** A unit that leaves play and comes back is a new object, so its bounded graft can be used again the same turn. See rule 410.

> *Example: A recalled and replayed Engorged Caudex draws from its bounded graft again the same turn.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#16 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 calebgannon · Key: effects.graft.bounded.new-object</sub>

<a id="r722.6"></a>**722.6.** A graft printed "{graft} [cost]: effect" adds a cost to the composite. That cost must be paid; it cannot be declined. See rule 111.15.

> *Example: A grafted Immolate's sacrifice is paid as the composite goes on the stack, and the player cannot decline it.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#11 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 32-cast-costs.test.ts · Example test: 32-cast-costs.test.ts::grafted Immolate: the carrier must pay the cost at composite cast time · Demonstrated by test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 11: a payable [cost] graft must be paid · Key: effects.graft.costs</sub>

<a id="r722.6a"></a>**722.6a** If a grafted cost cannot be paid, the whole composite stays off the stack: the host's own effect and every other graft with it. See rule 111.15.

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#10 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Graft 101 point 11: an unpayable [cost] graft keeps the whole composite off the stack, 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts::CR 722.6a: an activated graft cause whose grafted [cost] cannot be paid is not offered at all · Key: effects.graft.costs.unpayable</sub>

<a id="r722.6b"></a>**722.6b** The cost is paid as the composite goes on the stack. No player can respond to the payment, and units the composite itself would create cannot pay it. See rule 111.

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1355115946032889914#12 · Tests: 17-earth-b.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 17-earth-b.test.ts::graft under Lost Guardian pays its cost TWICE and resolves twice · Key: effects.graft.costs.instant</sub>

<a id="r722.7"></a>**722.7.** Some graft causes trigger several copies of the graft ability as one single trigger: Lost Guardian two, Amphivore and Witness of the Crossing three. The copies are one effect on the stack. See rule 111.14.

> *Example: Amphivore's combat damage to an opponent triggers its grafts three times, in one trigger.*

> *Example: Lost Guardian's after-combat trigger runs each graft twice as one trigger.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Lost Guardian; card: Amphivore; card: Witness of the Crossing · Designer: RAQ 1353859961855148103#0 · Tests: 14-water-a.test.ts, 17-earth-b.test.ts, 40-light-c.test.ts · Example tests: 14-water-a.test.ts::Amphivore: combat damage to an opponent triggers grafts thrice (one trigger), 17-earth-b.test.ts::Lost Guardian: after combat, each attached graft triggers twice as one trigger · Key: effects.graft.multiplier</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U17-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r722.7a"></a>**722.7a** The copies run top to bottom, then top to bottom again, once for each copy. See rule 722.4c.

> *Example: Amphivore with Plodding Pebble and Bellowing Boulder goes counter, damage, counter, damage, counter, damage.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353859961855148103#1 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Amphivore: a tripled composite runs its grafts top to bottom · Key: effects.graft.multiplier.order</sub>

<a id="r722.7b"></a>**722.7b** A bounded graft under a multiplier is repeated too. See rule 109.9j.

> *Example: Amphivore triples a bounded "Create three" graft into nine Fireballs.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1353859961855148103#2 · Tests: 14-water-a.test.ts, 17-earth-b.test.ts · Example test: 14-water-a.test.ts::CR 109.9j: Amphivore triples a BOUNDED [Switch1] graft · Demonstrated by test: 17-earth-b.test.ts::CR 722.7b: Lost Guardian repeats a BOUNDED [Switch1] graft too · Key: effects.graft.multiplier.bounded</sub>

<a id="r722.7c"></a>**722.7c** Each copy of a targeted graft chooses its targets separately. See rule 110.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 14-water-a.test.ts, 40-light-c.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 14-water-a.test.ts::CR 722.7c: a TARGETED graft under Amphivore aims each of its three copies separately · Key: effects.graft.multiplier.targets</sub>

<a id="r722.7d"></a>**722.7d** A cost in a repeated graft is paid once for each copy. If the multiplied cost cannot be paid in full, none of it is paid, and the composite stays off the stack (722.6a). See rules 111.14, 722.6a.

> *Example: With one card in hand, a doubled [Discard a card] cannot be paid: nothing is paid and nothing happens.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353859961855148103#4; RAQ 1353859961855148103#5 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 17-earth-b.test.ts · Example test: 17-earth-b.test.ts::CR 111.14: all or nothing — one card in hand cannot pay a doubled [Discard a card] · Key: effects.graft.multiplier.costs</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U17-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r722.7e"></a>**722.7e** A copy that cannot do part of its effect does the rest. Ralph grafted under a multiplier gives the host away and makes three 1/1s on the first pass only; the later passes cannot give it away, and the rest of the composite still runs every time. See rule 101.

> *Example: Amphivore with Ralph grafted: the first pass gives the host away and makes three 1/1s, the later passes give nothing, and the other graft runs three times.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353859961855148103#3 · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example test: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Amphivore with Ralph grafted · Key: effects.graft.multiplier.as-far-as-possible</sub>

<a id="r722.8"></a>**722.8.** A unit that has become a copy of a grafted unit runs the whole copied composite. More grafts may be added to it, but only below the copied grafts. See rule 710.

> *Example: A Borrower that copied a Bellowing Boulder with Flame Juggle grafted runs the whole copied composite.*

> *Example: A graft added to that Borrower resolves below the copied grafts.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1372468222158180424#4; RAQ 1372468222158180424#5 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts · Example tests: 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Borrower of Forms: a Borrower that copied a Bellowing Boulder, 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Borrower of Forms: a graft added to a Borrower · Key: effects.graft.copies</sub>

<a id="r723"></a>
### 723. Virus

<a id="r723.1"></a>**723.1.** Virus is a timing icon. A Virus card can be applied as an augment from the hand during battle, as well as being played and augmented normally during deployment. See rule 207.5.

> *Example: Aetherflux Golem augments the attacker from hand during battle; in deployment it may be played as a unit or augmented.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.34; Manual p.34; Rulebook 2023 p.3 · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Example test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.virus.what — a Virus is applied as an augment from hand in battle, and in deployment it may be played or augmented normally · Key: effects.virus.what</sub>

<a id="r723.1a"></a>**723.1a** A Virus applied in battle is an augment: it gives its host its augment text or its type-line attributes (721.1), and an ability that triggers when a player applies an augment triggers on it. See rule 721.1.

> *Example: Morphic Mentor's controller applies an augment in battle and the Mentor gets +2/+2; an enemy's augment does not count.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.34; card: Morphic Mentor · Tests: 17-earth-b.test.ts · Example test: 17-earth-b.test.ts::Morphic Mentor: your battle augment gives +2/+2 until regroup; an enemy augment does not · Key: effects.virus.what.augment</sub>

<a id="r723.1b"></a>**723.1b** Virus changes when a card may be augmented, not what it may be augmented onto. In deployment a Virus is applied like any other augment. See rule 721.4.

> *Example: In deployment Aetherflux Golem, a Virus, can augment your own unit but not an opponent unit.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.34 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Example test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.virus.what.timing-not-host — in deployment a Virus is offered onto your own unit only, like any augment · Key: effects.virus.what.timing-not-host</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U06-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r723.2"></a>**723.2.** During a battle, a player who has priority may apply a Virus from their hand onto any unit in the battle's region, their own or an opponent's. See rule 703.

> *Example: A player applies Smouldering Inferno from hand to the opponent's attacker; the Virus goes on the stack and the host is modded when it resolves.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.34; Manual p.34 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 04-mods.test.ts, 370-cached-virus-in-battle.test.ts · Example test: 04-mods.test.ts::virus augment during battle: on the stack, donated to an enemy, text-only transfer · Key: effects.virus.battle</sub>

<a id="r723.2a"></a>**723.2a** A Virus may also be applied in battle from the cache, while a permission to use it is live, at the cache's price (720.4b). With no live permission it cannot. See rules 403.3b, 720.4b.

> *Example: A glimpsed Virus in the cache goes onto an enemy unit in battle, ignoring affinity.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#3 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-04 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 370-cached-virus-in-battle.test.ts, 369-cache-is-the-hand.test.ts · Example test: 370-cached-virus-in-battle.test.ts::CR 723.2a: a glimpsed Virus in the cache goes onto an ENEMY unit in battle · Demonstrated by tests: 370-cached-virus-in-battle.test.ts::CR 723.2a: a Virus whose prophecy is fulfilled augments in battle for FREE, 370-cached-virus-in-battle.test.ts::CR 723.2a: an EXPIRED glimpse is still nothing in battle · Key: effects.virus.battle.cache</sub>

<a id="r723.2b"></a>**723.2b** A Virus in a bin cannot be applied during battle by its Virus ability. From the bin it can be applied as an ordinary mod during deployment, and outside deployment only where another card opens a window: augmenting in battle under a card such as Rook (723.5), applying to a Modular card as it is played (724), or applying in the haste step under a card such as Slurpr (504.8a). See rules 405.8a, 723.5, 724, 504.8a, 720.2b.

> *Example: Bumblecrab, a Virus, is offered from the hand in battle but not from the bin; in deployment it is offered from the bin.*

> *Example: With a Rook in the battle's region, a card is augmented out of the bin during battle.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 3; verifier ran 4 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.34; Manual p.34; card: Rook; card: Spellbind; card: Slurpr · Tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts, 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts, 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Example tests: 418-cr-zones.test.ts::cr:zones.bin.mods-from-bin.virus — a Virus card in the bin is offered as an augment in deployment, never in battle, 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts::Rook: augmenting from the BIN during battle takes the card out of the BIN, not the hand · Key: effects.virus.battle.not-bin</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U17-14 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r723.2c"></a>**723.2c** A Virus applied to an opponent's unit is controlled by that opponent, with its ability (720.6a). A Virus whose text works against its host's controller therefore works against the opponent. See rule 720.6a.

> *Example: Smouldering Inferno augmented onto an opposing unit forces it to sacrifice itself after combat.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.34; Manual p.34; Manual p.34 · Tests: 04-mods.test.ts · Example test: 04-mods.test.ts::virus augment during battle: on the stack, donated to an enemy, text-only transfer · Key: effects.virus.battle.control</sub>

<a id="r723.3"></a>**723.3.** Applying a Virus in battle uses the stack. The Virus goes on the stack as an effect that targets its host, and it can be responded to, redirected and negated. See rules 110.10a, 703.

> *Example: A Virus being applied to Graxxlid is an effect targeting Graxxlid, which Graxxlid can negate.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.34; Manual p.34 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 16-earth-a.test.ts, 23-wood-a.test.ts, 04-mods.test.ts · Example test: 16-earth-a.test.ts::Graxxlid: a Virus being applied to me IS an effect targeting me · Key: effects.virus.stack</sub>

<a id="r723.3a"></a>**723.3a** A Virus that is negated, or whose target has become invalid, is put into the bin and cannot be used as a Virus again. See rules 704.4a, 704.6f.

> *Example: A Virus aimed at a spell on the stack: the spell leaves the stack first, so the Virus fizzles and goes to the bin.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.34; Manual p.34 · Tests: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts, 04-mods.test.ts · Example test: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts::CR 723.3a: a virus whose host leaves the stack first fizzles to the bin · Demonstrated by test: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts::CR 723.4b: negating the CARRIER erases it too; negating the VIRUS ITSELF bins it · Key: effects.virus.stack.negated</sub>

<a id="r723.3b"></a>**723.3b** A Virus being applied is not a spell. An effect that negates spells, or counts the spells played, does not see it. See rule 700.1b.

> *Example: Origon does not negate a Virus applied in battle, and its first-spell count is untouched.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 04-mods.test.ts, 105-semantics-playwatch.test.ts · Example test: 105-semantics-playwatch.test.ts::Origon: a virus applied during battle is not a spell · Demonstrated by test: 04-mods.test.ts::a virus is not a "spell effect" (negation scoping); a negated virus does not mod · Key: effects.virus.stack.not-a-spell</sub>

<a id="r723.4"></a>**723.4.** During battle a Virus may be augmented onto a spell on the stack, the player's own or an opponent's. The spell gains only the Virus's attributes (721.4b). See rule 721.4b.

> *Example: Chitin Shredder on Arc Lightning doubles its damage.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts · Example test: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts::CR 723.4: the powerful guy on a giant fireball · Demonstrated by test: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts::CR 723.4: you can hit an ENEMY spell · Key: effects.virus.spell-host</sub>

<a id="r723.4a"></a>**723.4a** Spells, spell units and spell tokens on the stack are legal hosts for a Virus. See rule 723.4e.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts::CR 723.4a: a spell TOKEN is a legal host too · Key: effects.virus.spell-host.which</sub>

<a id="r723.4b"></a>**723.4b** A spell carrying a Virus is modded, so it is {Unstable}: the spell and the Virus are erased instead of going to a bin, whether the spell resolves, fizzles or is negated. See rule 704.2c.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.35 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts, 91-modular.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts::CR 723.4b ⚠: a spell that carried a virus is Unstable, 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts::CR 723.4b: negating the CARRIER erases it too · Key: effects.virus.spell-host.erased</sub>

<a id="r723.4c"></a>**723.4c** A spell unit carrying a Virus is not erased when it resolves. It enters play with the Virus attached as an augment, and so has {Unstable}. See rule 303.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts::CR 723.4c: a spell UNIT carries its virus into play as an augment mod · Key: effects.virus.spell-host.spell-unit</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U17-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r723.4d"></a>**723.4d** A spell that has begun to resolve cannot have a Virus applied to it. See rule 703.6.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts::CR D6.3: a resolving item cannot be responded to, negated or targeted · Key: effects.virus.spell-host.resolving</sub>

<a id="r723.4e"></a>**723.4e** Triggered and activated abilities, Viruses, units being cast and Ambushes on the stack are not legal hosts for a Virus. See rule 723.4a.

<sub>Basis: Engine only · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Engine: apply.ts:STACK_VIRUS_HOSTS · Tests: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 67-resolving-and-stack-viruses.test.ts::CR 723.4e: only SPELLS are legal hosts · Key: effects.virus.spell-host.not-hosts</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U17-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r723.5"></a>**723.5.** A card can let other cards be augmented during battle as if they were Viruses. Rook: "You may augment cards from hand and bin during battle as if they were [Virus]." See rule 720.2b.

> *Example: Applying a non-Virus augment from hand during battle is not allowed without Rook, and is with it.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Rook · Tests: 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts · Example test: 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts::Rook: a NON-virus augment from HAND during battle · Demonstrated by test: 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts::Rook: augmenting from the BIN during battle takes the card out of the BIN, not the hand · Key: effects.virus.permission</sub>

<a id="r723.5a"></a>**723.5a** Such a card gives the augmented card the Virus ability itself, so the augment may go onto an opponent's unit or onto a spell on the stack. See rule 723.4.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 136-triggers-and-modes.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 136-triggers-and-modes.test.ts::CR 723.5a: a Rook-enabled augment lands on an ENEMY unit during battle, 136-triggers-and-modes.test.ts::CR 723.5a: a Rook-enabled augment reaches a SPELL ON THE STACK · Key: effects.virus.permission.confers</sub>

<a id="r723.5b"></a>**723.5b** Such a card reaches only the zones it names. Rook names the hand and the bin, so a non-Virus card in the cache cannot be augmented in battle through Rook. See rule 723.2a.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Rook · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-04 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts::Rook: it prints "hand and bin", so the CACHE stays shut · Key: effects.virus.permission.zones</sub>

<a id="r723.5c"></a>**723.5c** Such a permission belongs to the controller of the card that grants it (the host's controller, when it is a mod), and works only in that card's region. See rule 720.6b.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts, 136-triggers-and-modes.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts::Rook: the permission is REGION-scoped, and does not reach the opponent, 29-hybrids-wm-a.test.ts::Rook: the [Augment] half works, and the permission belongs to the HOST · Key: effects.virus.permission.region</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U17-10 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r724"></a>
### 724. Modular

<a id="r724.1"></a>**724.1.** Modular is an attribute. A player may apply mods from their hand and/or bin to a Modular card as it is played, paying their costs. See rule 802.26.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Spellbind · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts, 91-modular.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::{Modular}: mods are applied at cast time, paid for, and ride on the stack item · Key: effects.modular.what</sub>

<a id="r724.1a"></a>**724.1a** Spellbind is the only card that prints Modular.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Spellbind · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.modular.what.pool — Spellbind is the only card in the pool with Modular · Key: effects.modular.what.pool</sub>

<a id="r724.2"></a>**724.2.** Any card in the player's hand or bin whose cost they can pay may be applied to a Modular card: a graft, an augment, a Virus, or a card that can do nothing on a spell.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 91-modular.test.ts::CR 724.2: the {Modular} menu offers every card you can pay for, 91-modular.test.ts::CR 724.2: a card in the BIN is offered beside the hand, and an unaffordable one is not · Key: effects.modular.any-card</sub>

<a id="r724.2a"></a>**724.2a** A mod that does nothing on a spell is still a legal choice, and its cost is still paid. See rule 721.4b.

> *Example: Sparkwraith's augment text applied to Spellbind is accepted and does nothing.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Example test: 91-modular.test.ts::CR 724.4b: an [Augment]-TEXT mod is accepted and does nothing · Key: effects.modular.any-card.no-op</sub>

<a id="r724.2b"></a>**724.2b** Each mod's cost is paid as it is applied, while the Modular card is cast. Applying it is not playing it. See rule 720.3.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Spellbind · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 91-modular.test.ts::CR 724.3: "you still pay their costs" · Key: effects.modular.any-card.cost</sub>

<a id="r724.3"></a>**724.3.** The mods are chosen and paid for while the Modular card is being cast, before it reaches the stack, and they go on the stack with it. The caster may apply none. See rule 702.3b.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Spellbind · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::{Modular}: the caster may decline, and a non-modular spell is never asked · Key: effects.modular.when</sub>

<a id="r724.4"></a>**724.4.** A graft applied to a Modular spell adds its effect to the spell's ability as an extra part. See rule 722.4.

> *Example: A player casts Spellbind and applies Primordial Coalescence from their bin to it. When Spellbind resolves, Primordial Coalescence's graft effect happens too: three Wraiths, and its 2 Rot on top of Spellbind's one.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Example test: 91-modular.test.ts::CR 724.5: the flashback line · Demonstrated by test: 91-modular.test.ts::CR 724.4: a GRAFT mod still contributes its [Switch] effect as an extra part · Key: effects.modular.effects</sub>

<a id="r724.4a"></a>**724.4a** A type-line augment applied to a Modular spell gives its attributes to the spell's effect. See rule 721.4b.

> *Example: {Powerful} turns a Spellbind-carried Twin Flame from 2 damage into 4.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Example test: 91-modular.test.ts::CR 724.4a: a type-line [Augment] mod really donates · Key: effects.modular.effects.attributes</sub>

<a id="r724.4b"></a>**724.4b** Augment text and static abilities applied to a Modular spell do nothing, because a spell has no body for them to work on. See rule 721.4b.

> *Example: Sparkwraith on Spellbind: a spell played while it rides the stack puts no counter anywhere.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Example test: 91-modular.test.ts::CR 724.4b: an [Augment]-TEXT mod is accepted and does nothing · Key: effects.modular.effects.text</sub>

<a id="r724.4c"></a>**724.4c** A grafted cost on a Modular spell's graft part must be paid if it can be. If it cannot, only that part is skipped, and the spell still resolves. See rule 722.6.

> *Example: Spellbind carrying a grafted Immolate with no unit to sacrifice: the Immolate part is skipped, and Spellbind still gives its rot.*

> *Example: Spellbind carrying a grafted Immolate, with a unit to sacrifice: the cost is paid, the unit is sacrificed and a card is drawn. Declining is not offered.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts · Example test: 428-cr-modifications.test.ts::cr:effects.modular.effects.graft-cost — Spellbind carrying a grafted Immolate with a unit to sacrifice offers no decline, sacrifices the unit and draws · Key: effects.modular.effects.graft-cost</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U04-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r724.5"></a>**724.5.** A Modular card with any mod applied is modded, so it has {Unstable}: it and all of its mods are erased instead of going to a bin, whether it resolves, fizzles or is negated. See rules 720.7, 723.4b.

> *Example: A graft card replayed from the bin by Spellbind is erased, so it cannot be used that way twice.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.35 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts, 43-dark-c.test.ts · Example test: 91-modular.test.ts::CR 724.5: the flashback line · Demonstrated by tests: 91-modular.test.ts::CR 724.5: a NEGATED modded Spellbind is erased too, 91-modular.test.ts::CR 803.8f:  · Key: effects.modular.unstable</sub>

<a id="r724.5a"></a>**724.5a** A Modular card with no mod applied does not have {Unstable}, and goes to the bin like any other spell.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 91-modular.test.ts::CR 724.5a: an UNMODDED {Modular} spell is not Unstable · Key: effects.modular.unstable.unmodded</sub>

## 8. Keywords

<a id="r800"></a>
### 800. General

*No rules drafted yet.*

<a id="r801"></a>
### 801. Keyword Actions

<a id="r801.1"></a>**801.1.** Card text uses some verbs with a fixed game meaning: these are keyword actions, defined in this section. Where a card prints reminder text for a keyword action, the printed reminder states its meaning, and it wins over any paraphrase of it. See rules 802, 803.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Tests: 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts::cr:keywords.actions.general — where a card prints the reminder for a keyword action, the reminder a player is shown is that printed sentence and not our paraphrase · Key: keywords.actions.general</sub>

<a id="r801.2"></a>**801.2.** A card is trashed when it enters a bin from any zone except the stack. See rule 405.4.

> *Example: A card discarded from a hand enters a bin from the hand, so it is trashed.*

> *Example: A card that leaves a cache for a bin is trashed.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-09-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 5 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts, 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Example tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::discarding from hand trashes, by the owner of the bin it enters, 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 801.2: a card leaving the cache for a BIN is trashed (classified automatically) · Key: keywords.actions.trash</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U18-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.2a"></a>**801.2a** Discarding a card, sacrificing it, milling it and a card dying into a bin are all ways of trashing it. See rules 801.3, 801.4, 801.5.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::CR 801.2a: milling from the deck trashes one event per card, 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::CR 801.2a: sacrificing and dying both trash — the card enters a bin from PLAY · Key: keywords.actions.trash.ways</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U18-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.2b"></a>**801.2b** A card that goes to a bin from the stack is not trashed, whether it resolved, was negated or failed to resolve. A card played for free during another effect's resolution and then put into the bin counts as coming from the stack. See rules 405.4a, 704.2a.

> *Example: A spell Tides of the Cosmos plays for free off the deck goes to the bin afterwards and is not trashed.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts, 15-water-b.test.ts · Example test: 15-water-b.test.ts::CR 405.4a: Tides plays an ORDINARY spell for free → the bin, and it is NOT a trash · Demonstrated by tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::CR 801.2b: a spell going to the bin after RESOLVING is not trashed (it comes from the stack), 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::CR 801.2b: a NEGATED spell is not trashed either · Key: keywords.actions.trash.not-from-stack</sub>

<a id="r801.2c"></a>**801.2c** Erasing a card is not trashing it: an erased card never enters a bin. See rules 407.1c, 801.6.

> *Example: Banishment erases a unit: no death and no trash happen.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 145-erase-routes.test.ts · Example test: 145-erase-routes.test.ts::(vii): Banishment still fires no 'died' and no 'trashed' · Key: keywords.actions.trash.not-erase</sub>

<a id="r801.2d"></a>**801.2d** A token is never trashed, because only a card can be trashed. A unit token that dies still enters the bin and still dies, but its trip through the bin is not a trash: no "when I am trashed" ability triggers for it, its own included. See rules 108.2e, 304.10a.

> *Example: A token copy of Dropslime that dies does not trigger its own "When I am trashed".*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 338-tokens-are-not-trashed.test.ts · Example test: 338-tokens-are-not-trashed.test.ts::CR 801.2d: a token copy of an own-trash card does not fire its own when-I-am-trashed · Demonstrated by test: 338-tokens-are-not-trashed.test.ts::CR 801.2i: a token unit dying in battle does not bump the trashed ledger that Dropslime reads · Key: keywords.actions.trash.tokens</sub>

<a id="r801.2e"></a>**801.2e** The player whose bin the card enters is the player who trashes it. A unit that dies goes to its controller's bin, so its controller trashes it; when an effect sends the card to another player's bin, that player trashes it. See rules 405.3, 711.

> *Example: A stolen unit that dies goes to the bin of the player who controls it, and that player trashes it.*

> *Example: Pull Under deletes an enemy unit and puts it into the caster's bin: the caster trashes it.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-08-29 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts, 15-water-b.test.ts · Example tests: 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts::CR 801.2e: a stolen unit that dies is trashed by its CONTROLLER, into the controller bin, 15-water-b.test.ts::Pull Under: an ENEMY unmodded victim is trashed by the CASTER, exactly once (CR 801.2e, binTo) · Key: keywords.actions.trash.trasher</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U18-11 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.2f"></a>**801.2f** When a modded unit is recalled or cached, each nontoken mod it carried is left behind in a bin and is trashed there. The host's controller trashes it, not the mod's owner. See rules 410.4, 403.7.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-29 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 224-mod-trash.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 224-mod-trash.test.ts::CR 720.8: a mod trashed on a recall is trashed by the host controller, not by its owner, 224-mod-trash.test.ts::CR 720.8: a cached host attributes its left-behind mods the same way a recalled one does · Key: keywords.actions.trash.mods-left-behind</sub>

<a id="r801.2g"></a>**801.2g** A nontoken mod that is erased together with its {Unstable} host is not trashed. The host's departure is the whole unit's; the mod has no trash of its own. See rules 405.4, 720.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-29 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 224-mod-trash.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 224-mod-trash.test.ts::CR 720.8a: a nontoken mod erased with its Unstable host is not trashed at all · Key: keywords.actions.trash.mods-erased-with-host</sub>

<a id="r801.2h"></a>**801.2h** An {Unstable} card that dies in play is erased instead of entering the bin, so it is not trashed. An {Unstable} card that goes to a bin from an inactive zone (a hand, the deck or a cache) enters the bin and is trashed. See rules 405.5, 400, 803. *(Engine differs, see F-U18-1.)*

> *Example: Aberrant Statweaver (printed {Unstable}) discarded from a hand goes to the bin and is trashed: the hand is inactive.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Abyssal Evocation · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 125-active-zone.test.ts · Example test: 125-active-zone.test.ts::CR 803.8a: a printed-Unstable card DISCARDED FROM HAND bins and TRASHES — hand is inactive · Key: keywords.actions.trash.unstable-death</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U07-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.2i"></a>**801.2i** An effect that counts cards trashed counts only cards. A token dying never adds to the count.

> *Example: Dropslime deals damage equal to the cards trashed this battle, and the tokens that died in it do not count.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Dropslime · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 338-tokens-are-not-trashed.test.ts · Example test: 338-tokens-are-not-trashed.test.ts::CR 801.2i: Dropslime deals damage for the CARDS trashed this battle and not for the tokens · Key: keywords.actions.trash.count-cards-only</sub>

<a id="r801.3"></a>**801.3.** To discard a card is to put it from a hand into the bin. A discarded card is trashed. Discarding is not playing the card, and a cached card cannot be discarded. See rules 402.5, 403.4, 801.2.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-08-21, 2026-10-04 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts, 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 35-rot-debt-trash.test.ts::discarding from hand trashes, by the owner of the bin it enters, 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts::cr:keywords.actions.discard — a discard from a hand puts nothing on the stack and is not played, and a cached card cannot be discarded · Key: keywords.actions.discard</sub>

<a id="r801.4"></a>**801.4.** To sacrifice a unit is for a player to choose a unit they control and put it into their bin. A sacrificed unit dies. See rules 111.3, 111.8.

> *Example: Immolate sacrifices a unit to draw a card.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.41 · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts · Example test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Immolate: sacrifice a unit to draw a card · Key: keywords.actions.sacrifice</sub>

<a id="r801.4a"></a>**801.4a** A player can sacrifice only something they control. An effect may make an opponent sacrifice something; that opponent sacrifices one of their own units and chooses which.

> *Example: General Smof: after combat each present player sacrifices a unit of their own choice.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.41; Manual p.41; Manual p.41 · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts, 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts · Example test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::General Smof: after combat, each present player sacrifices a unit of their choice · Key: keywords.actions.sacrifice.control</sub>

<a id="r801.4b"></a>**801.4b** A player can sacrifice only a unit in the region where the effect or cost happens, never one of their units in another region. See rules 601.1e, 111.3.

> *Example: Ghord's sacrifice makes each opponent in Ghord's region sacrifice a unit there, and reaches no other region.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.41 · Designer: RAQ 1454169054402314362#0 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Another set: a Ghord sacrifice reaches only the opponent units in its own region · Key: keywords.actions.sacrifice.region</sub>

<a id="r801.4c"></a>**801.4c** A player told to sacrifice a unit who has no unit in the region sacrifices nothing. See rule 101.5.

> *Example: Cull's "each player sacrifices a unit" with nobody holding a unit in the region kills nothing.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.41 · Tests: 179-empty-collection-branches.test.ts · Example test: 179-empty-collection-branches.test.ts::Cull — "each player sacrifices a unit" with nobody holding a unit here says so and kills nothing · Key: keywords.actions.sacrifice.none-available</sub>

<a id="r801.5"></a>**801.5.** To delete a unit is one way for it to die: the unit dies, and it is removed from play into the bin. Abilities that trigger when a unit dies, its own "When I die" included, trigger. Unless the effect names another bin, it goes to the bin a dying unit would go to. See rules 301.5, 405.2, 405.3.

> *Example: Throw off a Cliff deletes a unit with 4 or more defense: it goes to the bin, as a death.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: partial in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.13; card: Throw off a Cliff; card: Pull Under · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-11 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 182-correctness-sample.test.ts, 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts · Example test: 182-correctness-sample.test.ts::Throw off a Cliff: only defense>=4 is offered, and the target is DELETED (bin, a death) · Key: keywords.actions.delete</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U18-9 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.5a"></a>**801.5a** An effect that deletes a unit and names where it goes overrides the usual bin. Pull Under puts the deleted unit and all of its mods into its caster's bin, where they stay. See rule 801.2e.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Pull Under · Tests: 15-water-b.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 15-water-b.test.ts::Pull Under: deletes the target; it and its mods land in YOUR bin (not erased, not owner-binned) · Key: keywords.actions.delete.named-bin</sub>

<a id="r801.6"></a>**801.6.** To erase a card is to take it out of the game: it goes to the erased pile. When card text says "erase", the erased pile is where the card goes. See rules 407.1, 407.2, 410.2.

> *Example: Celestial Purge erases its target unit: it goes to no bin.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 14-water-a.test.ts · Example test: 14-water-a.test.ts::Celestial Purge: erases target unit (no bin) · Key: keywords.actions.erase</sub>

<a id="r801.6a"></a>**801.6a** Erasing a unit is neither a death nor a trash. It is a despawn. See rules 407.1c, 410.2.

> *Example: Banishment erases a unit: it does not die and is not trashed, but it does despawn.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 145-erase-routes.test.ts · Example test: 145-erase-routes.test.ts::(vii): Banishment still fires no 'died' and no 'trashed' · Key: keywords.actions.erase.not-death</sub>

<a id="r801.7"></a>**801.7.** To recall a card is to put it into a hand. Printed recalls take a card from play, from a bin, from the stack or from a cache. See rules 402.4, 410.2.

> *Example: Vaporweave Eidolon recalls itself from play to its controller's hand, at no cost.*

> *Example: Eldritch Reclaimer recalls a unit from its controller's bin to their hand.*

> *Example: Prismatic Observer recalls an enemy's cached card to its owner's hand.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 4 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 4 gate test files · Printed: card: Eldritch Reclaimer; card: Vaporweave Eidolon; card: Cosmic Reversal; card: Prismatic Observer · Tests: 15-water-b.test.ts, 14-water-a.test.ts, 38-light-a.test.ts, 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts · Example tests: 15-water-b.test.ts::Vaporweave Eidolon: [zero]: recall me — a free activated self-recall, 14-water-a.test.ts::Eldritch Reclaimer: recalls a unit from your bin to your hand, spawns 4/2, 38-light-a.test.ts::Prismatic Observer: sacrifice to recall a cached card (either cache, in battle) and gain 3 life · Key: keywords.actions.recall</sub>

<a id="r801.7a"></a>**801.7a** A unit recalled from play goes to the hand of the player who controls it, not necessarily its owner, unless the effect names another hand. Recalling does not change who owns the card. See rules 102, 711.

> *Example: A stolen unit that is recalled goes to the thief's hand, not its owner's.*

> *Example: Cosmic Reversal recalls a stolen spell unit to the hand of the player who controls it.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 246-zones-follow-control.test.ts, 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts · Example tests: 246-zones-follow-control.test.ts::CR 801.7a: a stolen unit recalled goes to the THIEF hand, not the owner, 229-cosmic-and-control.test.ts::CR 801.7a: a STOLEN spell unit is recalled to the seat that CONTROLS it · Key: keywords.actions.recall.destination</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U07-10 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.7b"></a>**801.7b** A recalled {Unstable} unit goes to the hand as a card. {Unstable} changes only a move into a bin, so a recall is not affected by it. See rules 803, 410.4.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Abyssal Evocation · Tests: 125-active-zone.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 125-active-zone.test.ts::CR 803.8j: RECALLING an Unstable unit puts the CARD IN HAND — Unstable never fires · Key: keywords.actions.recall.unstable</sub>

<a id="r801.7c"></a>**801.7c** Recalling a card from a bin moves it from that bin to its player's hand. "Recall target unit in your bin" can reach only a card in that player's own bin. See rule 405.7.

> *Example: Delver of Mysteries recalls a chosen spell from its controller's bin.*

> *Example: Eldritch Reclaimer, cast with both players in the battle, can pick a unit in its caster's own bin, never one in the opponent's bin.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Eldritch Reclaimer; card: Delver of Mysteries · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts, 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts · Example tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Delver of Mysteries: recalls a chosen spell from the bin, then spawns 2/2, 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts::cr:keywords.actions.recall.from-bin — Eldritch Reclaimer offers a unit in its own bin and never one in the opponent bin, even with both players in the battle · Key: keywords.actions.recall.from-bin</sub>

<a id="r801.7d"></a>**801.7d** Recalling a spell effect on the stack negates it and puts the card into its controller's hand. A recalled spell token enters its controller's hand and is then erased. See rules 704.4, 410.5b.

> *Example: Cosmic Reversal recalls the other spell effects on the stack to their controllers' hands.*

> *Example: Dream Lapse recalls a cast Fireball token: it enters its controller's hand, so Rider of the Tides grows, and then it is erased.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Cosmic Reversal · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 14-water-a.test.ts, 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts · Example tests: 14-water-a.test.ts::Cosmic Reversal: recalls all other spell effects on the stack to hands, 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts::CR 801.7d: Dream Lapse recalls a cast Fireball token · Key: keywords.actions.recall.from-stack</sub>

<a id="r801.7e"></a>**801.7e** When an effect tells a player to recall a unit and they have none to recall, the recall does nothing, but the rest of the effect still happens unless it depends on the recall ("If you do"). See rule 101.5.

> *Example: Recall ("Each player recalls a unit and loses 2 life"): a player with no unit to recall still loses 2 life.*

> *Example: Shoreline Specter: if the recall is declined, the life drain that follows "If you do" does not happen.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Shoreline Specter · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 179-empty-collection-branches.test.ts, 182-correctness-sample.test.ts · Example tests: 179-empty-collection-branches.test.ts::Recall — the life loss happens, the recall does not, and the card now says which, 182-correctness-sample.test.ts::Shoreline Specter: DECLINE the recall and the 2-life drain does not happen · Key: keywords.actions.recall.nothing-to-recall</sub>

<a id="r801.8"></a>**801.8.** To cache a card is to put it into a player's cache. A unit cached from play goes to its controller's cache unless the effect names another, and its mods go to the bin. See rules 403.1, 403.7, 410.5c.

> *Example: A stolen unit that is cached goes to the thief's cache.*

> *Example: Grob caches a stolen unit into its controller's cache, as its text says.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Grob · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25, 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 246-zones-follow-control.test.ts, 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts · Example tests: 246-zones-follow-control.test.ts::CR 801.8: a stolen unit cached goes to the THIEF cache, 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts::§27: Grob caches a STOLEN unit into the CONTROLLER’s cache · Key: keywords.actions.cache</sub>

<a id="r801.8a"></a>**801.8a** Caching a card does not by itself let anyone use it. A cached card can be played or used as a mod only while a permission on it is live: a glimpse that cached it this turn, a fulfilled prophecy, or the text of the effect that cached it. See rules 403.3, 403.3a, 801.9.

> *Example: Murkdrop Distiller caches a trashed card; its own text then lets its controller play it until end of turn.*
