<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Murkdrop Distiller · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 182-correctness-sample.test.ts · Example test: 182-correctness-sample.test.ts::Murkdrop Distiller: a trashed card may be cached, and cached is where it goes · Key: keywords.actions.cache.no-permission</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U18-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.9"></a>**801.9.** Glimpse N means: reveal the top N cards of the deck, cache one of them, and recycle the rest. See rules 403, 408.2a.

> *Example: Oracle of Foretelling's Glimpse 5 caches one of the five revealed cards.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Premonition · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 14-water-a.test.ts, 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Example test: 14-water-a.test.ts::Oracle of Foretelling: Glimpse 5 caches ONE of the five · Demonstrated by test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 801.9: Glimpse N reveals N, caches exactly ONE of the glimpser's choice and recycles the rest · Key: keywords.actions.glimpse</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U18-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.9a"></a>**801.9a** The player who glimpses chooses which of the revealed cards to cache.

> *Example: In a Glimpse 3, choosing the last revealed card caches it and recycles the two above it.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Example test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 801.9a: choosing the LAST revealed card recycles the two above it, in order · Key: keywords.actions.glimpse.choice</sub>

<a id="r801.9b"></a>**801.9b** Glimpse 1 reveals the top card of the deck and caches it. There is no choice to make and nothing to recycle.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Visionary Construct · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 801.9b: Glimpse 1 raises no decision · Key: keywords.actions.glimpse.one</sub>

<a id="r801.9c"></a>**801.9c** "Glimpse 1, X times" is X separate glimpses of one card each, not one Glimpse X.

> *Example: Glook discards X cards when activated and then glimpses 1, X times.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Glook · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts · Example test: 167-variable-ability-costs.test.ts::CR 705.3b Glook "[once] Discard X cards: Glimpse 1, X times" · Key: keywords.actions.glimpse.repeated</sub>

<a id="r801.9d"></a>**801.9d** A glimpse reveals from the glimpser's own deck. When an effect makes another player glimpse ("Its controller Glimpses 3"), that player reveals from their own deck, not from the deck of the player who controls the effect. In live draft every player's deck is the one shared deck. See rules 401, 902.

> *Example: Celestial Purge cast by one player erases an enemy unit; that unit's controller glimpses, chooses the card to cache and caches it in their own cache.*

> *Example: In constructed, a player who glimpses reveals the top of their own deck, caches from it and recycles the rest into their own pile; the other player's deck is untouched.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Dematerialize; card: Celestial Purge · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 14-water-a.test.ts, 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts · Example tests: 14-water-a.test.ts::Celestial Purge: erases target unit (no bin); its controller Glimpses 3, 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts::cr:keywords.actions.glimpse.whose-deck — in constructed a glimpse reads the deck of the glimpser and leaves the other deck untouched · Key: keywords.actions.glimpse.whose-deck</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U18-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.9e"></a>**801.9e** Until end of turn, the glimpser may play the cached card as if it were in their hand, ignoring affinity. See rules 403.3a, 403.3b.

> *Example: A card with affinity its glimpser cannot meet can be played from the cache, for its mana only.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Premonition · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Example test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 801.9e: a card with no affinity is ILLEGAL from hand but LEGAL from cache, for mana only · Key: keywords.actions.glimpse.permission</sub>

<a id="r801.9f"></a>**801.9f** A card played under a glimpse permission still costs its mana, and still obeys its printed timing. Only the affinity requirement is waived. See rules 403.3c, 403.3d.

> *Example: A glimpsed {Battle} card cannot be played in deployment.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts, 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Example test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 801.9f: glimpse still obeys timing, and a short deck glimpses fewer · Demonstrated by test: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts::CR 801.9g: the glimpse waives the pips, NOT the mana — broke means refused · Key: keywords.actions.glimpse.permission.cost-timing</sub>

<a id="r801.9g"></a>**801.9g** The same permission lets the glimpser apply the cached card as a mod, on the same terms (its mana, ignoring affinity): an augment or graft during deployment, and a {Virus} during battle. See rules 403.3b, 721, 722, 723.

> *Example: A glimpsed {Virus} in the cache goes onto an enemy unit in battle.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#3; RAQ 1537748882501668934#4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts, 370-cached-virus-in-battle.test.ts · Example test: 370-cached-virus-in-battle.test.ts::CR 723.2a: a glimpsed Virus in the cache goes onto an ENEMY unit in battle, ignoring affinity · Demonstrated by test: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts::CR 801.9g: a LIVE glimpse grafts for the card's mana, ignoring affinity · Key: keywords.actions.glimpse.permission.mods</sub>

<a id="r801.9h"></a>**801.9h** While the permission is live, a glimpsed card with a prophecy banner may be prophesied where it stands in the cache, in the same window and for the same cost as from the hand. Doing so uses up the glimpse permission. See rules 403.8, 801.14, 803.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-01 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 403.8: a GLIMPSED card with a banner may be prophesied where it stands in the cache · Key: keywords.actions.glimpse.permission.prophesy</sub>

<a id="r801.9i"></a>**801.9i** The permission ends at end of turn. The card stays in the cache, and it can no longer be played, prophesied or applied as a mod there. See rule 403.5.

> *Example: Premonition's permission dies with the turn; the card stays cached.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Premonition · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-09-20, 2026-10-01 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts, 14-water-a.test.ts · Example test: 14-water-a.test.ts::Premonition: Glimpse X where X is your water affinity; the permission dies with the turn, the card stays · Demonstrated by test: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts::CR 801.9i: an expired glimpse is not a graft, not an augment, not anything · Key: keywords.actions.glimpse.permission.ends</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U07-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.10"></a>**801.10.** To recycle a card is to put it on the bottom of the deck. A recycled card goes past the deck's mark into the recycle pile. See rules 408.1, 408.2, 106.6.

> *Example: Tides of the Cosmos recycles the revealed cards it did not play.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.7; Manual p.16 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26, 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 15-water-b.test.ts, 300-recycle-mark.test.ts · Example test: 15-water-b.test.ts::Tides of the Cosmos: reveal 8, play up to two with total cost ≤ 8 for free, recycle the rest · Demonstrated by test: 300-recycle-mark.test.ts::CR 408.2 a recycled card stays behind the mark while the deck still has cards · Key: keywords.actions.recycle</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U07-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.11"></a>**801.11.** When two units fight, each deals damage equal to its power to the other. See rule 112.

> *Example: The spell Battle makes two target units fight: each deals damage equal to its power to the other.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Fight; card: Eminence of the Barrens · Tests: 16-earth-a.test.ts · Example test: 16-earth-a.test.ts::Battle: two target units fight (mutual power damage; both targets at cast) · Key: keywords.actions.fight</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U18-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.11a"></a>**801.11a** Each fighting unit is the source of the damage it deals, with its own current attributes. Attributes the fight spell itself has do not apply to that damage. See rules 112.6, 802.

> *Example: A fighter that gained {Powerful} deals double damage.*

> *Example: A {Powerful} virus on the Fight spell does not double either fighter's damage.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1402292180499955884#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts · Example tests: 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts::CR 801.11a: Fight — a fighter that GAINED Powerful deals double, 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts::Fight — a Powerful virus on the Fight spell does not double either fighter · Key: keywords.actions.fight.source</sub>

<a id="r801.11b"></a>**801.11b** Damage dealt in a fight is dealt by the units, not by the spell or ability that made them fight. Abilities that look for damage dealt by a spell effect do not see it. See rule 112.6.

> *Example: Squish's damage is dealt by the unit, so Ember of Life does not trigger; Fight and Battle work the same way.*

> *Example: Fight makes a 3-power unit deal 3 damage, and Ember of Life does not trigger; a spell dealing damage in the same setup does trigger it.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1402292180499955884#2 · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts, 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts · Example tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Squish: Squish damage is the unit dealing it, so Ember of Life does not trigger, 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts::cr:keywords.actions.fight.not-spell-damage — the 3 damage Fight makes a unit deal does not trigger Ember of Life · Key: keywords.actions.fight.not-spell-damage</sub>

<a id="r801.11c"></a>**801.11c** A fight needs both of its units. If one of them is gone when the fight would happen, nothing happens: the remaining unit deals and is dealt no damage. The effect does not fizzle. See rules 704.6c, 101.5.

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1354013430805434389#1 · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 429-cr-keyword-actions.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ fizzles: Fight that loses one of its two targets does nothing to the survivor · Key: keywords.actions.fight.lost-one</sub>

<a id="r801.12"></a>**801.12.** Rockfall N means: each player chooses one of their units, and the source of the rockfall deals N damage to each chosen unit. See rule 112.

> *Example: A Fast Pile of Rocks dies and rockfalls 4: each player picks one of their own units, and each takes exactly 4.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: A Fast Pile of Rocks; card: Meteor Shower · Tests: 182-correctness-sample.test.ts · Example test: 182-correctness-sample.test.ts::A Fast Pile of Rocks: on MY death each player picks one of THEIR OWN units for exactly 4 · Key: keywords.actions.rockfall</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U18-4 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r801.12a"></a>**801.12a** Rockfall chooses; it does not target. No targets are declared when it goes on the stack, and an effect that stops targeting cannot stop it. See rule 110.

> *Example: Boon of Protection has nothing to negate when a Meteor Shower falls on its unit.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353899470156206152#3; RAQ 1353899470156206152#3 · Tests: 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example test: 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Meteor Shower: rockfall chooses rather than targets, so Boon of Protection has nothing to negate · Key: keywords.actions.rockfall.chooses</sub>

<a id="r801.12b"></a>**801.12b** Each player must choose a living unit of theirs in the region. A player with no unit there chooses none, and takes no part in that rockfall. See rule 601.1b.

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353899470156206152#4 · Tests: 93-engine-defects.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 93-engine-defects.test.ts::Meteor Shower with no unit anywhere to hit announces each empty rockfall · Key: keywords.actions.rockfall.living-unit</sub>

<a id="r801.12c"></a>**801.12c** [Removed: No card prints "Rockfall N, X times": Meteor Shower copies itself twice instead (its current card, owner 2026-10-18), and each copy is its own spell] Replaced by 710.8.

<a id="r801.13"></a>**801.13.** "Exchange" is printed in four senses, each read from its card: exchanging a unit in play for a unit card in a bin (Hooba-Mon, Necromorph), exchanging control of two units (Organic Exchange), exchanging control of a unit for a spell another player played (Hexbane Shiitake), and exchanging the base stats of two units (Body Swap). See rules 711, 106.8.

> *Example: Hexbane Shiitake gives itself away and takes control of an enemy spell.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 5 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Necromorph; card: Organic Exchange; card: Body Swap; card: Hexbane Shiitake · Tests: 24-wood-b.test.ts, 23-wood-a.test.ts, 26-metal-a.test.ts · Example test: 23-wood-a.test.ts::Hexbane Shiitake: exchanges the carrier for an enemy spell and retargets it ([once]) · Demonstrated by tests: 24-wood-b.test.ts::Organic Exchange: control swaps and the attack slot passes to the exchanged unit, 26-metal-a.test.ts::Body Swap: exchanges the base stats of two target units until regroup · Key: keywords.actions.exchange</sub>

<a id="r801.13a"></a>**801.13a** When a unit in play is exchanged for a unit card in a bin, the unit leaving play despawns and goes to the bin, where it is trashed, but it does not die. See rules 410.2a, 410.4d, 704.6c.

> *Example: Necromorph's exchange fires no death trigger, but the unit despawns and is trashed.*

> *Example: Hooba-Mon exchanging an unmodded host: the host goes to the bin and stays there.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts, 42-dark-b.test.ts · Example tests: 135-exchange-and-zones.test.ts::CR 801.13a: Necromorph’s exchange fires NO death trigger — but it despawns and it trashes, 42-dark-b.test.ts::CR 405.4 control: Hooba-Mon exchanges an UNMODDED host → it still BINS and stays there · Key: keywords.actions.exchange.unit-for-bin</sub>

<a id="r801.14"></a>**801.14.** To prophesy a card is to pay the cost on its prophecy banner and put it into the cache with its prophecy attached. Prophecy itself is 803. See rules 803, 403.8.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-10-01 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 801.9h: the real card — a glimpsed Vengeance is offered its prophecy in deployment · Key: keywords.actions.prophesy</sub>

<a id="r802"></a>
### 802. Attributes

<a id="r802.1"></a>**802.1. General.** Attributes are qualities that a card or a token can have (see rule 204). An attribute applies whenever the card or token has it, in combat or not. Some attributes change how a unit engages in combat; others change the card in other ways (see rule 802.1b). See rule 204.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; no gate test · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.3; Rulebook 2023 p.4; Manual p.25; Rulebook 2023 p.3; Rulebook 2023 p.4; Manual p.25; Rulebook 2023 p.3; Rulebook 2023 p.4; Manual p.25; Rulebook 2023 p.3; Rulebook 2023 p.4; Manual p.25; Rulebook 2023 p.3; Rulebook 2023 p.4; Manual p.25; Rulebook 2023 p.3; Rulebook 2023 p.4; Manual p.25; Rulebook 2023 p.12; Manual p.24 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-11 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Key: attr.general</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-GL-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.1a"></a>**802.1a** Cards with attributes carry reminder text, in italics, to help players remember what each attribute does. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.24; Manual p.24 · Key: attr.general.reminder</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.1b"></a>**802.1b** Attributes are combat attributes or non-combat attributes. Combat attributes are printed in gold. Non-combat attributes, such as Burst and Unstable, are printed in purple and generally have nothing to do with combat. See rules 204, 803. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.24; Manual p.25; Manual p.25 · Key: attr.general.kinds</sub>

<a id="r802.1c"></a>**802.1c** Combat attributes are shared by the units in the same column of a formation: while a unit is in a column, it has every combat attribute that any unit in that column has. See rules 603.1a, 602.

> *Example: A token attacking in a column behind a Flying unit has Flying too.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.24; Rulebook 2023 p.12 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.columns.definition.shared-attributes — Flying on the front unit of a column is shared · Key: attr.general.shared</sub>

<a id="r802.1d"></a>**802.1d** Attributes are not shared with the units to the left or right of a unit. They are shared only within its column. See rule 603.1a.

> *Example: A unit attacking in the next column beside a Flying unit does not have Flying.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.24; Rulebook 2023 p.12 · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.columns.definition.shared-attributes — Flying on the front unit of a column is shared · Key: attr.general.shared.not-sideways</sub>

<a id="r802.1e"></a>**802.1e** A unit has the attributes of its column for everything it does while it is in the column, not only for combat damage. Damage it deals with its abilities has those attributes too. See rule 112.6.

> *Example: Lithoghul stands in a battle column with Flzzz, which is Blessed. An ability of Lithoghul deals 3 damage to an enemy unit: Lithoghul has Blessed from its column, so its controller gains 3 life.*

> *Example: Bellowing Boulder, in a column with a Deadly unit, pings with Deadly.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1353895783266516992#5 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts, 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example tests: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts::CR 802.22e the report, 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ dead unit: Bellowing Boulder in a column with a Deadly unit pings with Deadly · Key: attr.general.shared.all-purposes</sub>

<a id="r802.1f"></a>**802.1f** Columns exist only during a battle. Outside a battle no unit is in a column, so no attribute is shared. See rules 602, 603.

> *Example: Outside battle, a unit standing beside a Blessed unit gains nothing from it.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts, 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Example test: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts::CR 712.8b outside battle there are no columns at all · Key: attr.general.shared.combat-only</sub>

<a id="r802.1g"></a>**802.1g** When a unit leaves a column, the other units in that column immediately lose the attributes it was sharing with them. See rules 603.1a, 608.2b.

> *Example: Once the Deadly unit leaves Bellowing Boulder's column, the Boulder's ping is not Deadly.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.24; Manual p.24; Rulebook 2023 p.12 · Designer: RAQ 1353895783266516992#5 · Tests: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts, 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ dead unit: once the Deadly partner leaves the column, the Boulder ping is not Deadly · Demonstrated by test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.substeps.column-attributes — a unit leaving a column takes the Swift it shared with it · Key: attr.general.shared.leaving</sub>

<a id="r802.1h"></a>**802.1h** Non-combat attributes are not shared in formation. A unit that is Unstable, or has Burst or Modular, does not give that attribute to the other units in its column. See rule 803.

> *Example: A modded (and so Unstable) unit does not make its column-mate Unstable.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.25 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts · Example test: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts::CR 712.8e a modded (therefore Unstable) unit does not make its column-mate Unstable · Key: attr.general.noncombat-not-shared</sub>

<a id="r802.1i"></a>**802.1i** A card either has an attribute or does not. Having the same attribute from more than one source has no extra effect.

> *Example: Two sources granting Inverted to one unit invert its stat changes once, not twice.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 79-round17-layers.test.ts · Example test: 79-round17-layers.test.ts::CR 709.4c layer 5: {Inverted} applies ONCE however many sources grant it · Key: attr.general.present-or-not</sub>

<a id="r802.1j"></a>**802.1j** Four attributes change a unit's stats. Tough and Balanced apply in the fourth stat layer, Inverted in the fifth and Unaware in the sixth and last (see rule 206.4). See rules 206.4, 709.

> *Example: A 1/4 with Tough, Balanced and Inverted is a -6/0.*

> *Example: A unit with both Inverted and Unaware is read at its printed stats: Unaware applies last.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.42 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 79-round17-layers.test.ts, 92-unaware.test.ts · Example tests: 79-round17-layers.test.ts::CR 802.8b layer 5: Caleb's worked example — a 1/4 Tough Balanced Inverted is a -6/0, 92-unaware.test.ts::{Inverted} and {Unaware} on one unit: layer 6 goes last, so Bubb is a 5/6 · Key: attr.general.stat-attributes</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U16-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.1k"></a>**802.1k** A unit's stats are worked out through all the stat layers before it is checked for death. A unit whose defense would be 0 or less part-way through the calculation, but not at the end of it, does not die. See rules 206.4, 713.

> *Example: A 1/1 with a -1/-1 counter and Inverted is a live 2/2, never a dead 0/0.*

> *Example: Child of Aether, a 2/0 with Balanced, is a 2/2 and survives.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 79-round17-layers.test.ts, 08-cards2.test.ts · Example tests: 79-round17-layers.test.ts::CR 802.1k layer 5: hitting 0 mid-calculation is not death, 08-cards2.test.ts::Child of Aether: Balanced (power & defense = max) keeps a 2/0 alive · Key: attr.general.stats-then-death</sub>

<a id="r802.1m"></a>**802.1m** When Tough and Balanced both apply to a unit, they apply one after the other, from top to bottom. If Tough is augmented onto a Balanced unit, or a Tough unit attacks with a Balanced unit behind it, the unit has its defense doubled, then its stats balanced. If Tough is applied to a Balanced unit, it has its stats balanced, then its defense doubled. Attributes granted by a unit's augments apply in the order the mods were gained, the first attached first, and attributes shared from its column apply from front to back. An attribute the unit has from more than one source takes the position of the first. See rules 206.4, 721. *(Engine differs, see F-U19-5.)*

> *Example: A 3/1 augmented with Rampart Guardian (Tough) and then Child of Aether (Balanced) is a 3/3; augmented in the other order it is a 3/6.*

> *Example: Child of Aether prints Balanced and is a 2/0. Augmented with Rampart Guardian (Tough), its defense is doubled (still 2/0), then its stats balanced: it is a 2/2.*

> *Example: Rampart Guardian (0/4, Tough) attacks with Child of Aether (Balanced) behind it: its defense is doubled (0/8), then its stats balanced, and it is an 8/8.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: partial in round 3; verifier ran 3 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.42; Manual p.42; Manual p.42; Manual p.42; Manual p.42; Manual p.42 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts, 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Example tests: 08-cards2.test.ts::CR 709.4b: layer-4 application order — Tough→Balanced ≠ Balanced→Tough, 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.general.application-order — a Tough unit attacking with a Balanced unit behind it is doubled, then balanced: Rampart Guardian is an 8/8 · Key: attr.general.application-order</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U16-1, D-U19-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.1n"></a>**802.1n** A Pure card, and every card interacting with it, ignores all its other attributes in that interaction (see rule 802.25). This includes the attributes that change stats: in an interaction with a Pure card, Tough, Balanced, Inverted and Unaware do not apply. See rule 802.25. *(Engine differs, see F-U19-1, F-U19-2.)*

> *Example: Rampart Guardian (a 0/4 with Tough) is dealt 5 damage by a Pure source. In that interaction it ignores Tough, so its defense is 4 and it dies.*

> *Example: An Unaware source dealing 3 damage to a Pure unit pumped from 2/3 to 4/5 does not read it at its printed 2/3: it survives, where a pumped non-Pure 2/3 dies.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 3; verifier ran 5 tests (5 probes it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Just a Unit; Manual p.42 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-05 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Example test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.general.pure — Unaware is off in a Pure pairing outside combat: an Unaware source does not collapse a pumped Pure recipient to its printed stats · Key: attr.general.pure</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U19-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.2"></a>**802.2. Flying.** Flying is a combat attribute. Its reminder text reads "Only flying units can block flying units."

> *Example: A Flying 3/1 attacks; a ground unit may not block it, and a unit with Flying may.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Air Plant; Manual p.24 · Our glossary (not a source): Flying · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Example test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.flying — Air Plant prints the reminder, and only a flying unit may block a Flying attacker · Key: attr.flying</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.2a"></a>**802.2a** An attacking column that has Flying can't be blocked by a unit that does not have Flying. See rule 606.2c.

> *Example: A ground 2/2 cannot block a column holding Ephemeral Skywalker (Flying).*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Greed Angel; Manual p.24 · Tests: 02-combat.test.ts, 40-light-c.test.ts, 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Example test: 02-combat.test.ts::combat math: columns, flying, piercing overflow, deaths · Demonstrated by test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Just a Unit: {Pure} blocks a Flying column, and only it can · Key: attr.flying.blocking</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U19-5 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.2b"></a>**802.2b** Because Flying is shared, a unit attacking in the same column as a Flying unit has Flying too, and the whole column can't be blocked by units that do not have Flying (see rule 802.1). See rule 802.1.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.24; Rulebook 2023 p.12 · Tests: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 421-cr-regions-formations.test.ts::cr:combat.columns.definition.shared-attributes — Flying on the front unit of a column is shared · Key: attr.flying.column</sub>

<a id="r802.2c"></a>**802.2c** If the Flying unit leaves an attacking column before blockers are declared, the other units in that column lose Flying, and the column can then be blocked by units without Flying. See rules 802.1, 606.

> *Example: Ephemeral Skywalker (Flying) attacks with a 1/1 token in one column; the Skywalker is destroyed before blocks, the token loses Flying, and Rune Channeler, which does not fly, blocks it.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.12; Rulebook 2023 p.12; Manual p.24 · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Example test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.flying.removed — after the Flying unit leaves the attacking column, a ground unit may block the rest · Key: attr.flying.removed</sub>

<a id="r802.2d"></a>**802.2d** Flying does not restrict a block when the attacking column or the blocking unit includes a Pure card. A Pure unit can block a Flying column. See rule 802.25.

> *Example: Just a Unit (Pure, no Flying) blocks a column holding Ephemeral Skywalker (Flying) and kills it.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts · Example test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Just a Unit: {Pure} blocks a Flying column, and only it can · Key: attr.flying.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.2e"></a>**802.2e** A unit without Flying is not able to block a Flying column, so an Alluring trigger cannot compel it to block that column (see rules 606.2e and 802.15). See rules 606.2e, 802.15.

> *Example: A lured unit with no Flying, facing a Flying Alluring column, may leave that column unblocked.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Example test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::CR 802.2e: a lured unit with no {Flying} is not able against a Flying column · Key: attr.flying.lured</sub>

<a id="r802.3"></a>**802.3. Deadly.** Deadly is a combat attribute. Its reminder text reads "Any damage from a deadly source will kill a unit."

> *Example: Tidepool Terror (1/2 Deadly) is blocked by a 5/9; its 1 damage kills the blocker.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Rotspore Herald; Manual p.25 · Our glossary (not a source): Deadly · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Example test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.deadly — Rotspore Herald prints the reminder, and 1 combat damage from a Deadly attacker kills a 5/9 blocker · Key: attr.deadly</sub>

<a id="r802.3a"></a>**802.3a** A unit dealt any nonzero amount of damage by a Deadly source is destroyed, whatever its defense. A Deadly source that deals 0 damage destroys nothing.

> *Example: A Deadly source dealing 2 noncombat damage destroys a 5/6.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Rotspore Herald · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts · Example test: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts::Deadly: 2 points of NON-COMBAT damage kills a 5/6 outright · Demonstrated by test: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts::Deadly: ZERO damage kills nothing · Key: attr.deadly.any-amount</sub>

<a id="r802.3b"></a>**802.3b** Deadly does not reduce the damage its source deals. A Deadly source deals all of its damage; Deadly changes only how much of it is lethal. See rule 608.6d.

> *Example: A 10-power Deadly column blocked by a 1/1 deals all 10 to it.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 134-column-and-substep.test.ts, 05-rulings.test.ts · Example test: 134-column-and-substep.test.ts::CR 802.3b — a 10-power {Deadly} column deals all 10 to a 1/1 blocker · Key: attr.deadly.no-cap</sub>

<a id="r802.3c"></a>**802.3c** In combat damage assignment, lethal damage for each unit a Deadly half-column deals damage to is 1 (see rule 608.6e). Once the front unit has been assigned at least 1, the dealing player may assign damage to the unit behind it. See rules 608.6e, 608.6b.

> *Example: A Deadly and Piercing column over two blockers assigns 1 to each, and the rest may go to the player.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1353888077625561108#3; RAQ 1353888077625561108#6 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 100-elective-assign.test.ts · Example test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Excessive: Deadly + Piercing over two blockers · Key: attr.deadly.combat-share</sub>

<a id="r802.3d"></a>**802.3d** A unit dealt combat damage by a Deadly source is destroyed in the same damage sub-step, before the next sub-step begins (see rule 608.7b). See rule 608.7b.

> *Example: Paired with a Swift unit in its column, a Deadly unit kills what it hits before that unit can strike back.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.25 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Example test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.deadly.timing — a Deadly and Swift column kills its blocker in the Swift sub-step, before the blocker strikes · Key: attr.deadly.timing</sub>

<a id="r802.3e"></a>**802.3e** Deadly applies to all damage its source deals, not only combat damage, including damage dealt through spells and abilities. See rule 112.7.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts, 82-attr-interactions.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts::CR 802.3e: a plain {Deadly} effect source kills a unit · Key: attr.deadly.noncombat</sub>

<a id="r802.3f"></a>**802.3f** A spell or a spell token can have Deadly. Damage it deals is then Deadly damage. See rules 302, 304.

> *Example: With Rotspore Herald in the region, a Fireball 1 kills any unit it hits.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24, 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts · Example test: 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts::CR 802.3f, in the owner's words: "a fireball 1 with deadly would kill any unit" · Demonstrated by test: 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts::CR 802.3f: a {Deadly} donated to a SPELL on the stack kills through the spell · Key: attr.deadly.spells</sub>

<a id="r802.3g"></a>**802.3g** A source with both Deadly and Poisonous that deals damage to a unit both destroys it and puts the -1/-1 counters on it (see rule 112.10). See rules 112.10, 802.18.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts, 82-attr-interactions.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts::CR 802.3g: {Deadly} + {Poisonous} effect damage still kills · Key: attr.deadly.poisonous</sub>

<a id="r802.3h"></a>**802.3h** If all the damage a Deadly source would deal to a unit is prevented, no damage is dealt, and Deadly does not destroy the unit (see rule 112.11). See rules 112.11, 608.7a.

> *Example: A shielded blocker dealt combat damage by a Deadly column is not destroyed.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts, 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Example test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.dealing.prevention — a shielded blocker dealt COMBAT damage gets no damage event, nothing marked, and no Deadly kill · Demonstrated by test: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts::Deadly + Poisonous: PREVENTION still stops both halves · Key: attr.deadly.prevention</sub>

<a id="r802.3i"></a>**802.3i** Deadly has no effect on damage dealt to a player. See rule 112.5.

> *Example: An unblocked Carapace Devourer (3/3, Deadly) costs the defending player exactly 3 life.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Example test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.deadly.players — an unblocked Deadly 3/3 costs the defending player exactly 3 life · Key: attr.deadly.players</sub>

<a id="r802.3j"></a>**802.3j** Deadly does not apply in an interaction with a Pure card (see rule 802.25). See rules 802.25, 608.6e.

> *Example: Just a Unit (Pure) blocking a Deadly unit is not killed by 1 damage.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-20, 2026-09-05 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts, 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts · Example test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Just a Unit: {Pure} switches off Deadly · Demonstrated by test: 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts::§2 a Pure recipient: the source's Powerful and Deadly do nothing to it · Key: attr.deadly.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.4"></a>**802.4. Swift.** Swift is a combat attribute. Its reminder text reads "Swift units deal combat damage first."

> *Example: Dune Drifter (2/1 Swift) is blocked by a 2/2; the blocker dies before it strikes, and the Drifter survives undamaged.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Rime Wraith; Manual p.25 · Our glossary (not a source): Swift · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Example test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.swift — Rime Wraith prints the reminder, and a Swift 2/1 kills a 2/2 blocker before it can strike back · Key: attr.swift</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-GL-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.4a"></a>**802.4a** A half-column that has Swift deals its combat damage in the Swift sub-step, before the normal and Sluggish sub-steps (see rule 608.2a). See rules 608.2, 608.2a.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Rime Wraith; Manual p.25 · Tests: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.substeps — Swift, then normal, then Sluggish · Key: attr.swift.schedule</sub>

<a id="r802.4b"></a>**802.4b** A unit destroyed by Swift damage in the Swift sub-step deals no combat damage in the later sub-steps. See rule 608.7b.

> *Example: A Swift attacker kills a 2/2 blocker, which never strikes back.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.25; Manual p.25 · Tests: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Example test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.overview.simultaneous — a Swift attacker deals its damage first · Key: attr.swift.kill-first</sub>

<a id="r802.4c"></a>**802.4c** A half-column with both Swift and Sluggish deals combat damage twice: once in the Swift sub-step and once in the Sluggish sub-step, with normal damage from other units in between (see rule 608.2c). See rules 608.2c, 802.5.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.43; Manual p.43 · Designer: RAQ 1363298910528864318#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts, 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts, 134-column-and-substep.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.substeps.swift-and-sluggish · Key: attr.swift.with-sluggish</sub>

<a id="r802.4d"></a>**802.4d** A half-column that has dealt combat damage in the Swift sub-step does not deal combat damage in the normal sub-step, even if it has since lost Swift (see rule 608.2e). See rule 608.2e.

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1363298910528864318#1 · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Swift: a column that dealt Swift damage deals no normal damage · Key: attr.swift.struck</sub>

<a id="r802.4e"></a>**802.4e** When a Swift half-column strikes and another half-column will strike in a later sub-step, the combat damage step is split: the abilities that triggered on the Swift damage go on the stack and resolve, with priority, before normal damage is dealt (see rules 608.3b and 608.9c). See rules 608.3b, 608.9c.

> *Example: Dune Drifter (Swift) and Lithoghul attack in separate columns and are not blocked. The damage step splits once: Dune Drifter strikes, then there is a window to respond, then Lithoghul strikes. No Sluggish unit is in the battle, so there is no second split.*

> *Example: Flowstone Arcanite's counters from the Swift step land at the boundary, in time to save an ally.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1540678747953569832#2; RAQ 1363298910528864318#0 · Our glossary (not a source): Swift · Tests: 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts, 21-fixes.test.ts · Example tests: 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts::CR 608.3c an EMPTY sub-step opens no window, 21-fixes.test.ts::Flowstone Arcanite (CR 802.4e): the Swift-step counters land at the boundary · Key: attr.swift.split</sub>

<a id="r802.4f"></a>**802.4f** In an exchange involving a Pure card, Swift does not apply, so the exchange strikes in the normal sub-step (see rule 608.2d). See rules 608.2d, 802.25.

> *Example: Dune Drifter (2/1, Swift) is blocked by Just a Unit (2/3, Pure): both strike in the normal sub-step, and the Drifter dies.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Example test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.swift.pure — a Swift attacker blocked by a Pure unit strikes in the normal sub-step, together with the blocker · Key: attr.swift.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.5"></a>**802.5. Sluggish.** Sluggish is a combat attribute. Its reminder text reads "Sluggish units deal combat damage last."

> *Example: Ambling Mountaintop (4/5 Sluggish) is blocked by a 5/4; the blocker strikes first and kills it, and is never struck.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Rime Wraith · Our glossary (not a source): Sluggish · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Example test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.sluggish — Rime Wraith prints the reminder, and a Sluggish 4/5 dies to a 5/4 blocker before it can strike · Key: attr.sluggish</sub>

<a id="r802.5a"></a>**802.5a** A half-column that has Sluggish deals its combat damage in the Sluggish sub-step, after the Swift and normal sub-steps (see rule 608.2a). See rules 608.2, 608.2a.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Rime Wraith · Tests: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.substeps — Swift, then normal, then Sluggish · Key: attr.sluggish.schedule</sub>

<a id="r802.5b"></a>**802.5b** Because a Sluggish half-column strikes in a later sub-step of a split step, abilities that triggered on the earlier sub-steps' damage resolve before it deals its damage (see rule 608.9c). See rules 608.9c, 608.3b.

> *Example: Adversary of the Deep (Sluggish) grows from the 6 life lost in the normal sub-step before it strikes, and deals 8.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1540678747953569832#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts · Example test: 297-damage-substeps-are-steps.test.ts::CR 802.5b the report · Key: attr.sluggish.after-triggers</sub>

<a id="r802.5c"></a>**802.5c** A half-column that has dealt combat damage in the normal sub-step does not deal combat damage in the Sluggish sub-step, even if it has since gained Sluggish. A half-column that dealt damage in the Swift sub-step and has gained Sluggish deals damage again in the Sluggish sub-step (see rule 608.2e). See rule 608.2e.

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1363298910528864318#3; RAQ 1363298910528864318#2 · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Swift: a column that dealt normal damage deals no Sluggish damage, 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Swift: a Swift column that gains Sluggish strikes again · Key: attr.sluggish.after-normal</sub>

<a id="r802.5d"></a>**802.5d** In an exchange involving a Pure card, Sluggish does not apply, so the exchange strikes in the normal sub-step (see rule 608.2d). See rules 608.2d, 802.25.

> *Example: Ambling Mountaintop (4/5, Sluggish) is blocked by Just a Unit (2/3, Pure): both strike in the normal sub-step.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Example test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.sluggish.pure — a Sluggish attacker blocked by a Pure unit strikes in the normal sub-step, together with the blocker · Key: attr.sluggish.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.6"></a>**802.6. Tough.** Tough is an attribute. A Tough unit's defense is doubled.

> *Example: Rampart Guardian (0/4, Tough) is a 0/8, and a unit it is augmented onto has its defense doubled.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.42; Manual p.35 · Our glossary (not a source): Tough · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts · Example test: 08-cards2.test.ts::Rampart Guardian: Tough doubles defense (layer 4), own and via augment · Key: attr.tough</sub>

<a id="r802.6a"></a>**802.6a** Tough doubles a unit's defense after counters and other +X/+X changes to it have been applied. See rules 206.4, 802.1.

> *Example: Rampart Guardian (0/4, Tough) with a +1/+1 counter is a 1/10.*

> *Example: Rampart Guardian (0/4, Tough) with a -1/-1 counter has defense 6: the counter makes it 3, then Tough doubles it.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.42; Manual p.42 · Designer: RAQ 1362832912579559664#0 · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Example tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Tough: a 0/4 Tough unit with a +1/+1 counter is a 1/10, 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.tough.after-counters — a 0/4 Tough unit with a -1/-1 counter has defense 6: the counter applies first, then the doubling · Key: attr.tough.after-counters</sub>

<a id="r802.6b"></a>**802.6b** Tough does not change a unit's power.

> *Example: A 0/4 Tough unit with a -1/-1 counter is a -1/6: its power is not doubled.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.42 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Example test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.tough.power — a 0/4 Tough unit with a -1/-1 counter is a -1/6: its power is not doubled · Key: attr.tough.power</sub>

<a id="r802.6c"></a>**802.6c** If an effect doubles a Tough unit's defense, the defense the unit then has is double what it had. The doubling is a stat change applied before Tough doubles the result, so if the unit later loses Tough, that change stays and is no longer doubled. See rules 709, 712.

> *Example: Burgeon on a 1/10 Tough unit makes it 1/20 (a +0/+5 under Tough); if Monke then takes its Tough, it is a 1/10.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1362832912579559664#1 · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 140-layers-and-riders.test.ts · Example test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Tough: Burgeon on that 1/10 makes it 1/20, and losing Tough to Monke leaves 1/10 · Demonstrated by test: 140-layers-and-riders.test.ts::Burgeon doubling a {Tough} unit's defense gives the printed number · Key: attr.tough.doubling</sub>

<a id="r802.7"></a>**802.7. Balanced.** Balanced is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "The power and defense of balanced units are equal to the greater of the two."

> *Example: Child of Aether (2/0, Balanced) is a 2/2.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Brough · Our glossary (not a source): Balanced · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts · Example test: 08-cards2.test.ts::Child of Aether: Balanced (power & defense = max) keeps a 2/0 alive · Key: attr.balanced</sub>

<a id="r802.7a"></a>**802.7a** Balanced compares the unit's power and defense after its counters and other stat changes, and after any attribute that applied before it, have been applied. See rules 206.4, 802.1.

> *Example: A 1/4 with Tough and Balanced: Tough makes it 1/8, then Balanced makes it 8/8.*

> *Example: A 1/3 with two +1/+1 counters and Balanced is a 5/5.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.42 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Example test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.balanced.after-changes — Balanced reads after counters: a 1/3 with two +1/+1 counters and Balanced is a 5/5 · Key: attr.balanced.after-changes</sub>

<a id="r802.8"></a>**802.8. Inverted.** Inverted is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "Invert the stat changes of inverted units. For example, -1/+2 would become +1/-2."

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Its Dark Bubb; Manual p.25 · Our glossary (not a source): Inverted · Tests: 43-dark-c.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 43-dark-c.test.ts::Its Dark Bubb: the printed reminder text, verbatim · Key: attr.inverted</sub>

<a id="r802.8a"></a>**802.8a** Inverted inverts the net change to a unit's stats. An Inverted unit's power is its base power minus the net change to its power, and its defense is its base defense minus the net change to its defense. It is worked out on the total change, not on each change separately. See rule 206.4.

> *Example: Malformed Monstrosity (10/9) with its -7/-7, in a column with Reality Bender, is a 17/16.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.25; Manual p.25 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 79-round17-layers.test.ts, 43-dark-c.test.ts · Example test: 79-round17-layers.test.ts::CR 802.8a layer 5: the owner's Malformed Monstrosity · Demonstrated by test: 43-dark-c.test.ts::Its Dark Bubb: MULTI-SOURCE — layer 5 negates the NET change, not each source on its own · Key: attr.inverted.net</sub>

<a id="r802.8b"></a>**802.8b** The changes Inverted inverts include those that Tough and Balanced make. Inverting Tough removes the defense Tough added; it does not halve the defense. See rules 802.6, 802.7.

> *Example: A 1/4 with Tough and Balanced is an 8/8; with Inverted too it is a -6/0.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 79-round17-layers.test.ts · Example test: 79-round17-layers.test.ts::CR 802.8b layer 5: Caleb's worked example — a 1/4 Tough Balanced Inverted is a -6/0 · Key: attr.inverted.attributes</sub>

<a id="r802.8c"></a>**802.8c** Setting a unit's base stats is not a stat change that Inverted inverts: the new base stats are what Inverted inverts from. See rule 206.5.

> *Example: A unit made base 3/3 by Aberrant Statweaver, with no other changes, is a 3/3 whether or not it is Inverted.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 79-round17-layers.test.ts · Example test: 79-round17-layers.test.ts::CR 802.8c layer 5: a base REWRITE is the thing inverted FROM, never inverted itself · Key: attr.inverted.base</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U19-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.8d"></a>**802.8d** If a unit has both Tough and Inverted, its defense is minus twice the net change to its defense from base. So it has 0 or less defense, and dies, unless that net change is a reduction, in which case its defense is twice the reduction. See rules 802.6, 713.

> *Example: A 1/4 with Tough and Inverted is a 1/0, in either grant order, and dies.*

> *Example: A 1/3 with one -1/-1 counter, Tough and Inverted survives as a 2/2.*

> *Example: Inverted on the front unit of a column and Tough on the back unit: both units have both attributes, and both die.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 79-round17-layers.test.ts · Example tests: 79-round17-layers.test.ts::CR 709.4d: the TWO-attribute case, in either grant order, 79-round17-layers.test.ts::CR 802.8d: the special case his wording misses, 79-round17-layers.test.ts::CR 802.8d: the column wipe · Key: attr.inverted.tough</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U19-9 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.9"></a>**802.9. Unaware.** Unaware is an attribute. An Unaware card, and every card interacting with it, ignores all stat changes: each is read at the stats printed on it.

> *Example: Bubb with two +1/+1 counters is still a 5/6. A 3/3 with four +1/+1 counters attacks into Bubb: it deals 3 and dies to 5.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1402292180499955884#3 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Our glossary (not a source): Unaware · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Example test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.unaware — Unaware Bubb ignores its own counters, and a pumped 3/3 blocked by Bubb is read at its printed 3/3 · Key: attr.unaware</sub>

<a id="r802.9a"></a>**802.9a** An Unaware card's own power and defense are always the ones printed on it, for every purpose, including whether it has died. Counters, temporary changes, continuous effects and the other stat attributes do not change them. See rules 206.4, 713.

> *Example: A +1/+1 counter on Bubb (5/6, Unaware) leaves it a 5/6.*

> *Example: Bubb survives 100 -1/-1 counters.*

> *Example: Tough donated onto Bubb does nothing.*

> *Example: Reconfigure moves Bubb onto a Robot token, which gains Unaware: it ignores its own +1/+1 counters and dies as a 0/0.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 4 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1353847640214999170#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 92-unaware.test.ts, 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 79-round17-layers.test.ts · Example tests: 92-unaware.test.ts::a +1/+1 counter on Bubb leaves it a 5/6, 92-unaware.test.ts::Bubb would also survive 100 -1/-1 counters just fine, 92-unaware.test.ts::{Tough} donated onto Bubb does nothing, 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Reconfigure vs Despawn: moving Bubb and its Growing Plague onto a Robot · Key: attr.unaware.self</sub>

<a id="r802.9b"></a>**802.9b** Setting a unit's base stats is a stat change too. An Unaware unit whose base stats an effect sets is still read at its printed stats. See rule 206.5.

> *Example: Aberrant Statweaver ("your units are base 3/3") leaves Bubb a 5/6.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 92-unaware.test.ts · Example test: 92-unaware.test.ts::a base REWRITE is ignored too · Key: attr.unaware.base</sub>

<a id="r802.9c"></a>**802.9c** When an Unaware card deals damage or is dealt damage, every card in that interaction is read at its printed stats: the other card as well as the Unaware one. See rule 112.6.

> *Example: Unaware Bubb squishing a Robot 10 kills it: the Robot is read as its printed 0/0.*

> *Example: A Robot 10 squishing Unaware Bubb deals its printed defense, 0.*

> *Example: Two units fight: Bubb reads a Robot 7 as a 0/0 and kills it.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1402292180499955884#3; RAQ 1402292180499955884#4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts, 92-unaware.test.ts · Example tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Squish: Unaware Bubb squishing a Robot 10 kills it, 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Squish: a Robot 10 squishing Unaware Bubb, 92-unaware.test.ts::two units FIGHT: Bubb reads a Robot 7 as a 0/0 · Key: attr.unaware.interaction</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U19-10 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.9d"></a>**802.9d** In combat, the interaction is the exchange between an attacking half-column and the half-column blocking it. If a unit on either side is Unaware, every unit on both sides deals and is dealt combat damage at its printed stats. See rules 608.5c, 608.6e.

> *Example: Bubb blocks a 3/3 pumped to 5/5 and takes 3, the attacker's printed power.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Tests: 92-unaware.test.ts, 05-rulings.test.ts, 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts · Example test: 92-unaware.test.ts::Bubb blocks a pumped 3/3 and takes the attacker's PRINTED 3 · Demonstrated by tests: 92-unaware.test.ts::an Unaware ATTACKER collapses the exchange the same way a blocker does, 423-cr-combat-damage.test.ts::cr:combat.damage.assignment.lethal-defined — in an Unaware exchange · Key: attr.unaware.combat</sub>

<a id="r802.9e"></a>**802.9e** A unit dealt damage in such an interaction is destroyed if the damage is lethal for its printed defense, even if the stats it has outside the interaction would let it survive. See rule 713.

> *Example: Bubb blocking a Robot token kills it, however many +1/+1 counters it has.*

> *Example: Haboob's 1 damage kills any unit with a printed defense of 1.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 92-unaware.test.ts · Example tests: 92-unaware.test.ts::"Bubb blocking a Robot token would kill it, 92-unaware.test.ts::"Haboob kills anything that has 1 defense printed at the card level" · Key: attr.unaware.death</sub>

<a id="r802.9f"></a>**802.9f** Outside such an interaction, an Unaware card does not change the stats of the other cards.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 92-unaware.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 92-unaware.test.ts::NEGATIVE CONTROL: a Robot token that nobody Unaware is fighting is its full size · Key: attr.unaware.outside</sub>

<a id="r802.9g"></a>**802.9g** A spell can be Unaware. A spell has no stats of its own, so its Unaware only makes the cards it deals damage to be read at their printed stats. See rule 302.

> *Example: Haboob (an Unaware spell) deals 1 damage to each unit and kills every unit with a printed defense of 1.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 92-unaware.test.ts · Example test: 92-unaware.test.ts::"Haboob kills anything that has 1 defense printed at the card level" · Key: attr.unaware.spells</sub>

<a id="r802.9h"></a>**802.9h** Unaware does not stop a card being targeted. An effect can put counters or other stat changes on an Unaware card; they stay on it but do not change its stats while it is Unaware. See rule 110.

> *Example: Poison with X = 6, targeting Bubb (a 5/6, Unaware), puts six -1/-1 counters on it; Bubb is still a 5/6.*

> *Example: A Robot 10 may Squish Unaware Bubb, targeting Bubb. The Robot, interacting with Unaware Bubb, is read at its printed 0/0, so it deals 0 and Bubb takes no harm.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 3; verifier ran 3 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1402292180499955884#4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts, 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Example tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.unaware.targets — Poison X=6 may target Unaware Bubb: six -1/-1 counters go on, and Bubb stays a 5/6, 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Squish: a Robot 10 squishing Unaware Bubb deals its printed defense, 0 · Key: attr.unaware.targets</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U19-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.10"></a>**802.10. Powerful.** Powerful is a combat attribute. Its reminder text reads "Powerful sources deal double damage".

> *Example: When Chitin Shredder (1/2, Powerful) is the source of 3 damage from an effect, 6 is dealt; attacking unblocked, it costs the defending player 2 life.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Emberflame Enlightener · Our glossary (not a source): Powerful · Tests: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Example test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.powerful — Emberflame Enlightener prints the reminder, and a Powerful source deals double in combat and by effect · Key: attr.powerful</sub>

<a id="r802.10a"></a>**802.10a** A Powerful half-column's combat damage is doubled once, as a whole, before it is divided among its recipients, whether they are units or a player. A unit without Powerful in a Powerful column has its damage doubled along with the rest (see rule 608.5b). See rule 608.5b.

> *Example: Chitin Shredder (Powerful) deals double combat damage to a player.*

> *Example: A vanilla unit in front of Chitin Shredder has its damage doubled too.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1362838395298119912#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 09-attrs.test.ts · Example tests: 09-attrs.test.ts::Powerful: Chitin Shredder deals double combat damage to a player, 09-attrs.test.ts::Powerful: column-shares · Key: attr.powerful.combat</sub>

<a id="r802.10b"></a>**802.10b** If a modifier that adds to the damage also applies, the addition is made first and Powerful doubles the result (see rule 112.9). See rule 112.9.

> *Example: A Powerful Bellowing Boulder's 1 damage with Conduit of Pain is (1+1)x2 = 4 to each unit.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1362838395298119912#4 · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Example test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Resonant: Conduit adds its 1 BEFORE Powerful doubles · Key: attr.powerful.additive</sub>

<a id="r802.10c"></a>**802.10c** Powerful also doubles damage its source deals through spells and abilities, to units and players alike. See rule 112.9.

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1362838395298119912#4; RAQ 1362838395298119912#3 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 09-attrs.test.ts, 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 09-attrs.test.ts::Powerful: doubles effect damage from a Powerful source · Key: attr.powerful.noncombat</sub>

<a id="r802.10d"></a>**802.10d** A spell can have Powerful. Damage a Powerful spell deals is doubled. See rule 302.

> *Example: With Emberflame Enlightener in its region, a player's spell deals double damage.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Emberflame Enlightener · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts · Example test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Emberflame Enlightener: your SPELLS gain {Powerful} too · Key: attr.powerful.spells</sub>

<a id="r802.10e"></a>**802.10e** When a spell makes a unit deal damage, as Squish, Fight and Battle do, the unit is the source: the unit's own Powerful, including Powerful it shares from its column, applies, and Powerful on the spell does not (see rule 112.6). See rule 112.6.

> *Example: Squish makes a Powerful ally deal double its defense.*

> *Example: A Powerful Squish does not double.*

> *Example: Squish on a 1/3 that shares Powerful from Chitin Shredder in its column deals 6.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1402292180499955884#0; RAQ 1402292180499955884#1 · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts, 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts, 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Example tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Squish: the unit is the source, 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Squish: a Powerful Squish does not double, 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.powerful.unit-source — Squish on a unit that shares Powerful from its column deals double · Key: attr.powerful.unit-source</sub>

<a id="r802.10f"></a>**802.10f** Powerful does not apply in an interaction with a Pure card (see rule 802.25). See rule 802.25.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts::§1 a Pure source: its own Powerful does not double · Key: attr.powerful.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.11"></a>**802.11. Vulnerable.** Vulnerable is an attribute. A Vulnerable unit is dealt double the damage that would be dealt to it.

> *Example: Crumbling Ancient (Vulnerable) is dealt double the combat damage assigned to it.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1372451771632320512#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Our glossary (not a source): Vulnerable · Tests: 09-attrs.test.ts · Example test: 09-attrs.test.ts::Vulnerable: Crumbling Ancient marks double the combat damage it receives · Key: attr.vulnerable</sub>

<a id="r802.11a"></a>**802.11a** Because the damage is doubled when it is dealt, lethal damage for a Vulnerable unit, when assigning, is half its remaining defense, rounded up (see rule 608.6e). See rule 608.6e.

> *Example: Arc Lightning (6 damage, Electric) on a Vulnerable 3/8: 4 of the 6 destroy it, and the other 2 may jump on.*

> *Example: A 10-power Piercing column blocked by a Vulnerable 3/7 assigns it 4 (half of 7, rounded up), and 6 go through.*

> *Example: A Vulnerable 3/8 with 2 damage marked needs 3, so a 10-power Piercing column sends 7 through.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 4 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1372451771632320512#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Example tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Vulnerable: Arc Lightning on a Vulnerable 3/8, 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.vulnerable.lethal — a Vulnerable 3/7 needs 4 (half of 7 rounded up), so a 10-power Piercing column sends 6 through, 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.vulnerable.lethal — lethal is half the remaining defense: a Vulnerable 3/8 with 2 damage marked needs 3, so 7 of 10 pierce · Key: attr.vulnerable.lethal</sub>

<a id="r802.11b"></a>**802.11b** Damage assigned to a Vulnerable unit counts as that much of the source's damage; the unit is then dealt double that amount. Any damage the source keeps on a Vulnerable unit, including the rest of a column's damage, is doubled on that unit. See rules 608.6d, 608.7.

> *Example: A Piercing attacker may put all 10 of its damage into a lone Vulnerable 3/8, which is dealt 20.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1372451771632320512#4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 09-attrs.test.ts, 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts · Example test: 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts::CR 802.16c: a Piercing attacker may put all 10 into a lone Vulnerable 3/8 · Key: attr.vulnerable.receipt</sub>

<a id="r802.11c"></a>**802.11c** Piercing excess past a Vulnerable unit is measured in the source's damage before the doubling: only the source damage beyond what the unit needs is excess (see rule 802.16). See rule 802.16.

> *Example: A 10-power Piercing column blocked by a Vulnerable 3/8 assigns 4 to it, and 6 goes to the player.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1372451771632320512#3 · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 09-attrs.test.ts, 82-attr-interactions.test.ts · Example test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Vulnerable: a 10-power Piercing column into a Vulnerable 3/8 assigns 4 · Key: attr.vulnerable.piercing</sub>

<a id="r802.11d"></a>**802.11d** If a Powerful source deals damage to a Vulnerable unit, both apply: the source's damage is doubled, and the unit is dealt double that. See rule 112.9.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts::Powerful (source) and Vulnerable (receiver) both apply to one effect hit · Key: attr.vulnerable.powerful</sub>

<a id="r802.11e"></a>**802.11e** A Pure Vulnerable unit, and a Vulnerable unit in an interaction with a Pure card, is not dealt double damage. See rule 802.25. *(Engine differs, see F-U19-3.)*

> *Example: Chitin Shredder (Powerful), made Pure, deals 2 damage to Crumbling Ancient (Vulnerable, 3/8). It is dealt 2: neither Powerful nor Vulnerable doubles it, and the Ancient survives.*

> *Example: Crumbling Ancient (Vulnerable) made Pure is dealt 2 by a 2-damage effect, not 4.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: partial in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-20, 2026-09-05 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts, 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Example tests: 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts::§2 a Pure recipient's own Vulnerable is off too, 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.vulnerable.pure — a Vulnerable unit that is itself Pure is dealt 2 by a 2-damage effect, not 4 · Key: attr.vulnerable.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.12"></a>**802.12. Feeble.** Feeble is an attribute. A Feeble unit can't block.

> *Example: Spectrogenesis creates three Wisps (Feeble); none of them can block.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Spectrogenesis · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Our glossary (not a source): Feeble · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts, 86-ui-block-refusal.test.ts, 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Example test: 08-cards2.test.ts::Spectrogenesis: three Wisps; Feeble means they cannot block · Demonstrated by tests: 86-ui-block-refusal.test.ts::#77: {Feeble} — the unit that cannot block is the one that is named, 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.feeble — Bripp prints Feeble, so the block-refusal guards that use it are not vacuous · Key: attr.feeble</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U19-11 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.12a"></a>**802.12a** Whether a unit can block depends on its own Feeble only. A Feeble unit can't block even if it shares a column with units that are not Feeble, and Feeble that a unit would share from its column does not stop it blocking. See rules 802.1, 606.2.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts::CR 802.12a {Feeble} block legality is still the unit's own question · Key: attr.feeble.own</sub>

<a id="r802.12b"></a>**802.12b** A Pure unit that is Feeble can block: Pure makes it ignore its own Feeble (see rule 802.25). See rule 802.25.

> *Example: Just a Unit (Pure) granted Feeble can still be declared as a blocker.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-20, 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 177-glossary-conformance.test.ts, 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts · Example test: 430-cr-attributes-1.test.ts::cr:attr.feeble.pure — a Pure unit granted Feeble is accepted as a blocker · Key: attr.feeble.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.12c"></a>**802.12c** A Feeble unit is not able to block, so an Alluring trigger that targets it cannot compel it to block (see rules 606.2e and 802.15). See rules 606.2e, 802.15.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::CR 802.12c: a {Feeble} lured unit is not able, so it is not compelled · Key: attr.feeble.lured</sub>

<a id="r802.13"></a>**802.13. Evasive.** Evasive is an attribute. Its reminder text, printed under the type line, reads "Evasive units require two blockers." See rules 802.1, 606.2c.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1460216519731577027#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Our glossary (not a source): Evasive · Tests: 07-cards.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 07-cards.test.ts::Curio Drifter: Evasive requires two blockers · Key: attr.evasive</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.13a"></a>**802.13a** A column with Evasive cannot be blocked by a single unit. To block it, the defending player must place two units in front of it. See rules 606.2c, 602.
