> *Example: An Evasive Curio Drifter attacks. The defender may block it with two units placed in front of it, one behind the other, but not with one.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1460216519731577027#0; RAQ 1460216519731577027#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 07-cards.test.ts, 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts · Example test: 07-cards.test.ts::Curio Drifter: Evasive requires two blockers · Key: attr.evasive.two-blockers</sub>

<a id="r802.13b"></a>**802.13b** Evasive does not apply if either the Evasive column or the units blocking it include a Pure card. A single Pure unit can block an Evasive column on its own (see rule 802.25). See rule 802.25.

> *Example: Just a Unit (Pure) blocks an Evasive column by itself.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-20, 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts · Example test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Just a Unit: {Pure} blocks an Evasive column alone · Key: attr.evasive.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.14"></a>**802.14. Sneaky.** Sneaky is an attribute. Its reminder text, printed under the type line, reads "Sneaky units can't be blocked if attacking alone." See rules 802.1, 606.2c.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Our glossary (not a source): Sneaky · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 08-cards2.test.ts::Whispering Mantid: Sneaky · Key: attr.sneaky</sub>

<a id="r802.14a"></a>**802.14a** An attacking column with Sneaky cannot be blocked if its unit is the only attacking unit in the attacking formation. See rule 606.

> *Example: Whispering Mantid attacks alone and cannot be blocked. Attacking with another unit, it can be.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts · Example test: 08-cards2.test.ts::Whispering Mantid: Sneaky · Key: attr.sneaky.alone</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-2, D-U20-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.14b"></a>**802.14b** Spell tokens that go with an attack do not count as attacking units for Sneaky. A Sneaky unit attacking with only spell tokens beside it is attacking alone. See rule 604.2c.

> *Example: A Sneaky unit attacks together with two Fireball spell tokens. It is still attacking alone and cannot be blocked.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.sneaky.spell-tokens — a Sneaky unit attacking with two riding Fireball spell tokens is still alone and cannot be blocked · Key: attr.sneaky.spell-tokens</sub>

<a id="r802.14c"></a>**802.14c** Two Sneaky units attacking together are not alone. Both can be blocked.

> *Example: Two Whispering Mantids attack in different columns. The defender may block either or both.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.sneaky.two-sneaky — two Whispering Mantids attacking in two columns are not alone, and both can be blocked · Key: attr.sneaky.two-sneaky</sub>

<a id="r802.14d"></a>**802.14d** A side-block does not block a lone Sneaky attacker. The defending player may side-block beside it, and it stays unblocked (see rule 606.4e). See rule 606.4e.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 422-cr-attacking-blocking.test.ts::cr:combat.blocks.side.blocks-nothing — a side-block beside a lone Sneaky attacker · Key: attr.sneaky.side-block</sub>

<a id="r802.14e"></a>**802.14e** A Pure unit ignores Sneaky, so it can block a lone Sneaky attacker (see rule 802.25). See rule 802.25.

> *Example: A lone Sneaky unit attacks. The defender can block it with Just a Unit (Pure), and with no other unit.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.sneaky.pure — Just a Unit (Pure) can block a lone Sneaky attacker, and a plain unit cannot · Key: attr.sneaky.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.15"></a>**802.15. Alluring.** Alluring is an attribute. Its reminder text, printed under the type line, reads "When an alluring column attacks, target enemy can't attack and must block it this combat if able." See rules 802.1, 604.2e, 606.2e.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Our glossary (not a source): Alluring · Tests: 15-water-b.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 15-water-b.test.ts::Tempest Wrangler: {Alluring} 1/3 · Key: attr.alluring</sub>

<a id="r802.15a"></a>**802.15a** When an attacking column with Alluring is declared, Alluring triggers. The trigger goes on the stack and targets one enemy unit, chosen by the attacking player from the enemy units in the battle region as the trigger is put on the stack. See rules 706, 110.

> *Example: Two attacking columns, one Alluring, against one possible blocker: the Alluring trigger targets that blocker, which then must block the Alluring column.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts, 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::CR 802.15a: the minimal form · Key: attr.alluring.trigger</sub>

<a id="r802.15b"></a>**802.15b** Alluring does not stack. An attacking column with Alluring has one Alluring trigger, however many of its units have Alluring.

> *Example: Two Alluring units attack in one column. Alluring triggers once.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Example test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::CR 802.15b: {Alluring} does not stack · Key: attr.alluring.one-per-column</sub>

<a id="r802.15c"></a>**802.15c** Each attacking column with Alluring has its own trigger. Two Alluring columns make two triggers, which may target the same unit or different units.

> *Example: Two Alluring columns attack. Each triggers, and both triggers may target the same defending unit.*

> *Example: Two Alluring columns target two different units. Each of those units must block its column.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Example tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::CR 802.15c: two Alluring COLUMNS are two triggers, and may name the same unit, 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::CR 802.15c: two Alluring columns naming DIFFERENT units compel both · Key: attr.alluring.per-column</sub>

<a id="r802.15d"></a>**802.15d** Alluring is shared by the units of its column, but the column's Alluring trigger comes from the unit that has Alluring itself, not from the units it is shared with. See rule 802.1.

> *Example: Tempest Wrangler attacks in a column with a vanilla unit. The trigger is Tempest Wrangler's.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22, 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts · Example test: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts::CR 802.15d {Alluring} still originates from the unit that prints it · Key: attr.alluring.source</sub>

<a id="r802.15e"></a>**802.15e** When the Alluring trigger resolves, its target cannot attack: it cannot be declared as an attacker or sent to counterattack for the rest of the battle phase (see rule 604.2e). See rules 604.2e, 610.

> *Example: A lured unit cannot be sent out to counterattack when blocks are declared.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Example test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::CR 604.2e: a lured unit cannot be sent out to counterattack · Key: attr.alluring.cannot-attack</sub>

<a id="r802.15f"></a>**802.15f** When the Alluring trigger resolves, its target must block the Alluring column in that battle round if it is able to. If the column is blocked at all, the target must be one of its blockers (see rule 606.2e). See rule 606.2e.

> *Example: The defender has two units able to block and tries to leave the Alluring column unblocked by putting both on other columns. That is not allowed: the lured unit must block the Alluring column.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1460216519731577027#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Example test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::CR 606.2b UFAB · Key: attr.alluring.must-block</sub>

<a id="r802.15g"></a>**802.15g** Whether the target is able to block the Alluring column depends only on that unit and that column. If the target could not block the column by itself (because the column is Evasive and needs two blockers, the target is Feeble, the column has Flying and the target does not, or the column is a lone Sneaky attacker), the defending player may leave the column unblocked, and the target may block another column. See rules 606.2b, 802.13.

> *Example: A lone lured unit cannot block an Alluring and Evasive column by itself, so it need not block it, and it may block another column.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1460216519731577027#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts, 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Example test: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Alluring: a lone lured unit cannot block an Evasive column · Key: attr.alluring.able</sub>

<a id="r802.15h"></a>**802.15h** An Alluring and Evasive column can be blocked only by two units, one of which is the target. The defending player chooses between blocking it with the target and one other unit, and not blocking it at all; blocking it with two other units is not allowed. See rule 802.13.

> *Example: The target is A and the defender also has B and C. A+B and A+C may block the column; B+C may not.*

> *Example: The defender has only A and B. They block the column with A+B, or leave it unblocked.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1460216519731577027#1; RAQ 1460216519731577027#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts · Example tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Alluring: with three units, A+B or A+C may block the Evasive column, but never B+C, 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Alluring: with two units, the lured one blocks the Evasive column with the other, or nobody blocks it · Key: attr.alluring.evasive</sub>

<a id="r802.15i"></a>**802.15i** If, when the Alluring trigger would resolve, the unit with Alluring is no longer in an attacking column, or its column no longer has Alluring, the trigger does nothing.

> *Example: The attacker's Alluring unit is killed while its trigger is on the stack. The trigger does nothing, and the targeted unit may attack and block freely.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Example test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::CR 802.15i: killing the allurer while the trigger is ON the stack fizzles it · Key: attr.alluring.allurer-gone</sub>

<a id="r802.15j"></a>**802.15j** Once the Alluring trigger has resolved, removing the unit with Alluring does not undo it: its target still cannot attack. If the Alluring column ceases to exist, the duty to block it ends with it.

> *Example: After the trigger resolves, the Alluring attacker is killed in the attack window. The lured unit may block another column, but it still cannot be sent to counterattack.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Example test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::CR 802.15j: killing the allurer AFTER it resolves frees the block but not the attack · Key: attr.alluring.after-resolution</sub>

<a id="r802.15k"></a>**802.15k** If two Alluring triggers have targeted the same unit, it cannot block both columns. Blocking either of those columns with it satisfies both triggers, and the other column may then be blocked by other units or left unblocked.

> *Example: Two Alluring columns both target unit A. A blocks the first column. The second column may be blocked by B alone, or left unblocked.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts, 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.alluring.two-duties — one unit lured by two columns blocks one of them, and the other column may be blocked by another unit or left unblocked · Key: attr.alluring.two-duties</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-4 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.15m"></a>**802.15m** An Alluring trigger from a lone Sneaky attacker compels no unit, because no unit is able to block that attacker (see rule 802.14), unless its target is Pure. See rule 802.14.

> *Example: A lone Sneaky and Alluring unit attacks. The defender declares no blocks, and that is legal.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Example test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::CR 802.15m: a lone {Sneaky} + {Alluring} attacker is not a stuck state · Key: attr.alluring.lone-sneaky</sub>

<a id="r802.15n"></a>**802.15n** An Alluring column that contains a Pure card does not trigger at all (see rule 802.25). See rule 802.25.

> *Example: An Alluring column with Just a Unit in it attacks. No Alluring trigger is put on the stack.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-20, 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Example test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::CR 802.15n: an Alluring column that is itself {Pure} never even triggers · Key: attr.alluring.pure-column</sub>

<a id="r802.15p"></a>**802.15p** A Pure unit ignores the attributes that would stop it blocking, so a Pure target is able to block any Alluring column: it must block even a Flying Alluring column, and it satisfies an Evasive Alluring column by itself. See rule 802.25.

> *Example: A lured Pure unit must block a Flying Alluring column.*

> *Example: A lured Pure unit blocks an Evasive Alluring column alone.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Example tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::a {Pure} lured unit is able against a Flying Alluring column, 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::a {Pure} lured unit discharges an EVASIVE Alluring column alone · Key: attr.alluring.pure-target</sub>

<a id="r802.15q"></a>**802.15q** The Alluring trigger is a triggered ability. It can be negated while it is on the stack, and an effect that makes triggered abilities cost more to trigger (Crevice Lurker) applies to it: if that cost is not paid, the trigger does not happen. See rules 111.10f, 706.

> *Example: Crevice Lurker is in play. The attacker declines to pay for the Alluring trigger, and nothing is lured.*

> *Example: Containment Protocol negates a waiting Alluring trigger.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1366446116274442291#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ trigger-like attributes: Crevice Lurker taxes the Alluring trigger, 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ trigger-like attributes: Containment Protocol negates a waiting Alluring trigger · Key: attr.alluring.tax-and-negate</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U15-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.16"></a>**802.16. Piercing.** Piercing is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "Excess damage from piercing sources is dealt to the recipient's controller." See rules 802.1, 608.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Protective Adaptations; Rulebook 2023 p.11 · Our glossary (not a source): Piercing · Tests: 14-water-a.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 14-water-a.test.ts::Protective Adaptations: the target also gains piercing until regroup · Key: attr.piercing</sub>

<a id="r802.16a"></a>**802.16a** Excess damage, for Piercing, is the damage a source deals to a unit beyond that unit's lethal damage. A unit's lethal damage is worked out after Powerful has doubled the source's damage; it is reduced for a Vulnerable unit, which is dealt double what reaches it; it is 1 if the source has Deadly; and damage already dealt to the unit counts towards it, including damage dealt to it earlier by the same effect (see rule 608.6e). See rules 608.6e, 802.3, 802.10, 802.11.

> *Example: A Powerful Piercing source deals 3 to a 1/1. The 3 is doubled to 6; 1 is lethal; 5 is excess.*

> *Example: A 10-power Piercing column is blocked by a Vulnerable 3/8. Lethal damage is 4, which is dealt as 8; the other 6 is excess.*

> *Example: One effect names the same unit twice with Piercing. The unit is given its lethal damage once, and the rest of both hits is excess.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1372451771632320512#3 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts, 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 09-attrs.test.ts · Example tests: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts::Piercing + Powerful: the excess is what is left after the doubling, 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Vulnerable: a 10-power Piercing column into a Vulnerable 3/8 assigns 4 and 6 goes to the player, 82-attr-interactions.test.ts::Piercing: a unit named twice in one batch is overkilled ONCE · Key: attr.piercing.excess</sub>

<a id="r802.16b"></a>**802.16b** A half-column with Piercing that deals combat damage to the units of the opposing half-column must assign lethal damage to each of those units, front to back. Any of its damage that is not assigned to a unit is dealt to the player who controls those units. See rules 608.6, 608.8.

> *Example: A Piercing column with 10 power is blocked by a 1/2 in front of a 1/3. It must assign 2 to the front unit and 3 to the back unit; the other 5 may be dealt to the defending player.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1353888077625561108#4; RAQ 1353888077625561108#5 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Excessive: Piercing pays lethal to the front AND the back, and only the rest reaches the player · Key: attr.piercing.combat</sub>

<a id="r802.16c"></a>**802.16c** Excess is elective. After each unit has been assigned its lethal damage, the dealing player may assign any part of the remaining damage to those units, including all of it, and only the damage no unit is assigned is dealt to the player. See rule 608.6c.

> *Example: A 10-power Piercing attacker is blocked by a lone Vulnerable 3/8. The attacker may put all 10 into it (dealt as 20), and none reaches the player.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1353888077625561108#5; RAQ 1372451771632320512#4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts · Example test: 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts::CR 802.16c: a Piercing attacker may put all 10 into a lone Vulnerable 3/8 · Demonstrated by test: 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts::CR 802.16c: a Piercing split may keep part of the excess on the back unit and send the rest · Key: attr.piercing.elective</sub>

<a id="r802.16d"></a>**802.16d** An unblocked attacking half-column with Piercing deals its combat damage to the defending player, as any unblocked half-column does. See rule 608.4a.

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1365594171867664445#0 · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Piercing: an unblocked Piercing column hits the player · Key: attr.piercing.unblocked</sub>

<a id="r802.16e"></a>**802.16e** If an attacking half-column with Piercing is blocked but no blocking unit is left in front of it when it strikes, all of its damage is excess and is dealt to the defending player. A blocked half-column without Piercing deals no damage in that case (see rule 608.4c). See rules 608.4c, 606.3a.

> *Example: A Piercing column's only blocker dies before damage. The column is still blocked, and its full power is dealt to the defending player.*

> *Example: The same position without Piercing deals nothing to the player.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1365594171867664445#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 02-combat.test.ts · Example tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Piercing: a Piercing column whose blocker died before damage puts its full power into the player, 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Piercing: a blocked NON-Piercing column whose blocker died deals nothing to the player · Key: attr.piercing.dead-block</sub>

<a id="r802.16f"></a>**802.16f** A blocking half-column with Piercing deals excess combat damage to the attacking player only if there is an attacking unit in front of it when it strikes. If no attacking unit is in front of it (its attackers are all gone, or it is a side-block), it deals no combat damage at all (see rules 608.4e and 608.4f). See rules 608.4e, 608.4f.

> *Example: A Piercing side-blocker deals no combat damage to the attacking player.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1365594171867664445#3 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22, 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts, 64-formation-collapse.test.ts · Example test: 400-raq-fix-blocks.test.ts::CR 606.4f a Piercing side-blocker deals no combat damage to the attacking player · Demonstrated by test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Piercing: a defending Piercing column with an attacker in front of it carries its excess to the attacker · Key: attr.piercing.defending</sub>

<a id="r802.16g"></a>**802.16g** If the Piercing source also has Deadly, lethal damage is 1 for each unit, so all damage beyond 1 for each unit may be excess. See rule 802.3.

> *Example: A Deadly and Piercing column is blocked by two units. It assigns 1 to each, and the rest may go to the player.*

> *Example: A 10-power Deadly and Piercing column is blocked by one unit: 1 kills it and the other 9 may pierce.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1353888077625561108#6 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 134-column-and-substep.test.ts, 82-attr-interactions.test.ts · Example tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Excessive: Deadly + Piercing over two blockers, 134-column-and-substep.test.ts::CR 802.3b — {Deadly} + {Piercing}: 1 kills the blocker and the other 9 pierce · Key: attr.piercing.deadly</sub>

<a id="r802.16h"></a>**802.16h** Damage prevention on a unit does not change how much must be assigned to it before there is excess. Excess is worked out as though the unit were unprotected. See rules 608.6g, 708.

> *Example: A Piercing column is blocked by a shielded 0/5 in front of a 5/6. It must assign 5 to the shielded unit and 6 to the unit behind; the rest may go to the player.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1353888077625561108#10 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 82-attr-interactions.test.ts · Example test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Excessive: with Piercing, 5 to the shielded Tomb · Demonstrated by test: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts::Piercing vs a damage-shielded unit · Key: attr.piercing.prevention</sub>

<a id="r802.16i"></a>**802.16i** Piercing excess is dealt as part of the same damage as the rest, at the same time. It is not a triggered ability, and no player can act between the damage dealt to the units and the excess dealt to the player.

> *Example: A Piercing effect deals 5 to a 1/1. The unit's 1 and the 4 to its controller are dealt together, with nothing on the stack in between.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-10-10 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Our glossary (not a source): Piercing · Tests: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts · Example test: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts::Piercing: 5 effect damage to a 1/1 kills it and the other 4 hit its controller · Key: attr.piercing.same-damage</sub>

<a id="r802.16j"></a>**802.16j** Piercing applies to noncombat damage too. A Piercing source that deals noncombat damage to a unit must deal that unit its lethal damage first. The dealing player may then keep any of the excess on that unit; the rest of the excess is dealt to that unit's controller. See rule 112.7.

> *Example: Squish makes Bubb, in a column with Good Whale (Piercing), deal 6 to a 1/1. The dealing player may keep all 6 on the 1/1, or send up to 5 to its controller.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1402292180499955884#5 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-10 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 405-raq-noncombat-piercing.test.ts, 82-attr-interactions.test.ts · Example test: 405-raq-noncombat-piercing.test.ts::CR 802.16j Squish: Bubb with Good Whale's Piercing · Demonstrated by test: 405-raq-noncombat-piercing.test.ts::CR 802.16j control: no Piercing, no question · Key: attr.piercing.noncombat</sub>

<a id="r802.16k"></a>**802.16k** For noncombat damage, the dealing player is the controller of the source unit, even if another player controls the spell that made it deal damage (for Squish, Fight and Battle the unit is the source; see rule 112.6). If the source is not a unit in play (a spell, or a unit that has left play), the controller of the effect decides. See rule 112.6.

> *Example: A Battle makes an opponent's Piercing unit fight. The opponent, who controls that unit, places its excess.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-10 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 405-raq-noncombat-piercing.test.ts, 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 405-raq-noncombat-piercing.test.ts::CR 802.16k Battle: the question belongs to the Piercing unit's controller, not the caster · Key: attr.piercing.noncombat-chooser</sub>

<a id="r802.16m"></a>**802.16m** Each unit's excess is dealt to that unit's controller. If one effect deals Piercing damage to units controlled by different players, each player is dealt the excess from their own units.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Protective Adaptations · Tests: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts::Piercing in a BATCH: each unit's excess goes to THAT unit's controller · Key: attr.piercing.recipients</sub>

<a id="r802.16n"></a>**802.16n** A unit in a column with a Piercing unit has Piercing while that column exists, for the noncombat damage it deals as well as for combat damage (see rule 802.1). See rule 802.1.

> *Example: Bubb, in a column with Good Whale, squishes with Piercing: the excess reaches the player.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1402292180499955884#5 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 405-raq-noncombat-piercing.test.ts, 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts · Example test: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Squish: Bubb in a column with Good Whale squishes with Piercing · Key: attr.piercing.column</sub>

<a id="r802.16p"></a>**802.16p** If Piercing combat damage that would be dealt to a player is dealt to a unit instead (as Oorblak's ability does), that unit is dealt its lethal damage and the rest is still Piercing excess. That excess is still combat damage that would be dealt to the player: another such effect that has not applied (a second Oorblak) may take it, the same one may not, and what none takes is dealt to the player (see rule 608.8c). See rule 608.8c.

> *Example: 10 Piercing combat damage is redirected into a 2/4 Oorblak. 4 kill it and the other 6 reach the player.*

> *Example: 5 Piercing combat damage is redirected into Oorblak on a 1/1 host. 1 kills the host and the remaining 4 reach the player.*

> *Example: 10 Piercing combat damage and two 2/4 Oorblaks: each takes 4 and dies, and 2 reach the player.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 4 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1397188292239163454#0; RAQ 1397188292239163454#0 · Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16; Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 17-earth-b.test.ts, 469-replacement-chain-damage.test.ts · Example tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Oorblak: 10 Piercing combat damage redirected into a 2/4 Oorblak, 17-earth-b.test.ts::Oorblak: Caleb's case — 5 Piercing redirected, 1 kills the body, the remaining 4 hit the player, 469-replacement-chain-damage.test.ts::CR 708.4: two Oorblaks and 10 Piercing — 4 destroy the first · Key: attr.piercing.redirect</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-23 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.16q"></a>**802.16q** If a source has both Electric and Piercing, excess that reaches a unit with no further unit to jump to is Piercing excess: the dealing player may keep any of it on that unit, and the rest is dealt to that unit's controller (see rule 802.17). See rule 802.17.

> *Example: A 6-damage Electric and Piercing hit lands on a lone 1/2 with no neighbour. The dealing player chooses how much of the 4 excess stays on it; the rest goes to its controller.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-10-10 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 405-raq-noncombat-piercing.test.ts · Example test: 405-raq-noncombat-piercing.test.ts::CR 802.16q Electric + Piercing: where the chain dead-ends, the Piercing half is elective too · Key: attr.piercing.electric</sub>

<a id="r802.16r"></a>**802.16r** Piercing does not apply in an interaction involving a Pure card (see rule 802.25). See rule 802.25.

> *Example: A 6-power Piercing column is blocked by Just a Unit (Pure). All 6 are dealt to Just a Unit; none reaches the defending player.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts, 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.piercing.pure — a 6-power Piercing column blocked by Just a Unit sends nothing to the defending player · Key: attr.piercing.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.17"></a>**802.17. Electric.** Electric is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "Excess damage from electric sources can be directed to an adjacent unit, recursively." See rule 802.1.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Envoy of Lightning; card: Arc Lightning · Our glossary (not a source): Electric · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Vulnerable: Arc Lightning on a Vulnerable 3/8 · Key: attr.electric</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-15 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.17a"></a>**802.17a** When an Electric source deals a unit more than its lethal damage, the excess may be dealt to a unit adjacent to that unit instead. The unit the excess jumps to is dealt the lethal damage it needs, and any excess beyond that may jump again, to a unit adjacent to it. See rules 603.2, 802.16.

> *Example: Arc Lightning (6, Electric) hits a Vulnerable 3/8. 4 kill it (dealt as 8), and the other 2 may jump to an adjacent unit.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Envoy of Lightning · Designer: RAQ 1372451771632320512#0 · Tests: 05-rulings.test.ts, 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Example test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Vulnerable: Arc Lightning on a Vulnerable 3/8 · Key: attr.electric.jump</sub>

<a id="r802.17b"></a>**802.17b** The excess never jumps to a unit it has already been dealt to in that chain.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Our glossary (not a source): Electric · Tests: 05-rulings.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 05-rulings.test.ts::CR 802.17: electric excess follows a controller-chosen non-overlapping path, atomically · Key: attr.electric.no-revisit</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.17c"></a>**802.17c** The Electric source's controller chooses where the excess goes at each jump. *(Engine differs, see F-U20-1.)*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 05-rulings.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 05-rulings.test.ts::CR 802.17: electric excess follows a controller-chosen non-overlapping path, atomically · Key: attr.electric.chooser</sub>

<a id="r802.17d"></a>**802.17d** Each jump is optional. At any jump, the source's controller may instead keep all the remaining excess on the unit it has reached; it is then all dealt to that unit and goes no further. This is so even when there is only one unit to jump to.

> *Example: Arc Lightning hits a Vulnerable 3/8 with a unit beside it. Its controller keeps all 6 on the 3/8 (dealt as 12), and nothing jumps.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1372451771632320512#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Example test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Vulnerable: Electric "can be" · Key: attr.electric.optional</sub>

<a id="r802.17e"></a>**802.17e** Excess that has no unit to jump to is dealt to the last unit it reached; it is not lost. If the source also has Piercing, that excess is Piercing excess instead (see rule 802.16). See rule 802.16q.

> *Example: Arc Lightning hits a lone Vulnerable 3/8 with nothing beside it. All 6 land on it, dealt as 12.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1372451771632320512#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Example test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Vulnerable: Electric damage with nowhere to jump is still dealt · Key: attr.electric.dead-end</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.17f"></a>**802.17f** Adjacency for Electric is adjacency in a formation (see rule 603.2). A unit that is not in a formation has no adjacent unit, so Electric excess dealt to it has nowhere to jump. See rule 603.2b.

> *Example: During the deployment phase no unit is in a formation, so an Electric spell's excess stays on the unit it hit.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Envoy of Lightning · Engine: engine.ts:adjacentInFormation · Tests: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.electric.adjacency — outside a battle no unit is adjacent, so Electric excess stays on the unit it hit and nothing is asked · Key: attr.electric.adjacency</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-21 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.17g"></a>**802.17g** The whole Electric chain is part of one damage event. No formation changes happen while the excess is distributed. See rule 112.8.

> *Example: An Electric chain of three units is dealt in one damage event; the units it kills die together afterwards.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 05-rulings.test.ts · Example test: 05-rulings.test.ts::CR 802.17: electric excess follows a controller-chosen non-overlapping path, atomically · Key: attr.electric.atomic</sub>

<a id="r802.17h"></a>**802.17h** Lethal damage along the chain is worked out as it is for Piercing (see rule 802.16): a Vulnerable unit needs only half, and damage already dealt to it by the same effect counts. See rule 802.16a.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1372451771632320512#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22, 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Vulnerable: Arc Lightning on a Vulnerable 3/8 · Key: attr.electric.lethal</sub>

<a id="r802.17i"></a>**802.17i** Envoy of Lightning makes "your spell effects with a single target" Electric. A spell effect has a single target if it was cast with exactly one target.

> *Example: Twin Flame cast with one target under Envoy of Lightning is Electric.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Envoy of Lightning · Designer: RAQ 1397256636921417748#0 · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts · Example test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Envoy of Lightning: your single-target spell effects are Electric · Key: attr.electric.single-target</sub>

<a id="r802.17j"></a>**802.17j** A spell effect cast with two targets does not have a single target, even if one of its targets has become illegal by the time it resolves. See rule 110.

> *Example: Twin Flame is cast with two targets and one is removed. It is not Electric under Envoy of Lightning.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1397256636921417748#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts · Example test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Envoy of Lightning: two DECLARED targets is not "a single target", even after one is removed · Key: attr.electric.single-target.declared</sub>

<a id="r802.18"></a>**802.18. Poisonous.** Poisonous is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "Poisonous sources damage units in the form of -1/-1 counters." See rule 802.1.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Blightmound · Our glossary (not a source): Poisonous · Tests: 09-attrs.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 09-attrs.test.ts::Poisonous: Noxious Sporefiend deals combat damage as permanent -1/-1 counters · Key: attr.poisonous</sub>

<a id="r802.18a"></a>**802.18a** Damage a Poisonous source deals to a unit is put on that unit as that many -1/-1 counters instead of being marked on it. See rule 112.5.

> *Example: Noxious Sporefiend deals 2 combat damage to a unit; the unit gets two -1/-1 counters and no marked damage.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Blightmound · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 09-attrs.test.ts, 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts · Example test: 09-attrs.test.ts::Poisonous: Noxious Sporefiend deals combat damage as permanent -1/-1 counters · Demonstrated by test: 09-attrs.test.ts::Poisonous: effect damage becomes -1/-1 counters and can kill · Key: attr.poisonous.form</sub>

<a id="r802.18b"></a>**802.18b** Poisonous damage is damage dealt. Abilities that trigger when a unit is dealt damage trigger on it (see rule 112.10). See rule 112.10.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1354148437355925554#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts, 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts::CR 802.18b: an un-prevented {Poisonous} hit fires "whenever I am dealt damage" · Key: attr.poisonous.is-damage</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-9 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.18c"></a>**802.18c** For damage assignment and for Piercing, a unit's lethal damage is the same whether the source is Poisonous or not. See rules 802.16a, 608.6e.

> *Example: A Poisonous and Piercing effect deals 5 to a 1/1. One counter is lethal, and the other 4 may pierce.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts · Example test: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts::Piercing + Poisonous: the counters are lethal at the same number, so the rest still pierces · Key: attr.poisonous.lethal</sub>

<a id="r802.18d"></a>**802.18d** A source with both Deadly and Poisonous destroys the unit it damages and also puts the -1/-1 counters on it. See rule 802.3.

> *Example: Deadly and Poisonous damage kills the unit, and the -1/-1 counter lands on it before it dies.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts, 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts · Example test: 82-attr-interactions.test.ts::Deadly DOES kill through Poisonous — and the counter lands too (CR 802.18d) · Key: attr.poisonous.deadly</sub>

<a id="r802.18e"></a>**802.18e** Powerful doubles a Poisonous source's damage, and so doubles the -1/-1 counters it puts on a unit. See rule 802.10.

> *Example: A Powerful Poisonous effect hit of 2 becomes 4 counters and kills a 4/3.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts · Example test: 206-deadly-everywhere.test.ts::CR 802.18e: {Powerful} doubles a {Poisonous} effect hit too · Key: attr.poisonous.powerful</sub>

<a id="r802.18f"></a>**802.18f** If a Poisonous source's damage to a unit is prevented, no damage is dealt and no -1/-1 counters are put on it. See rules 112.11, 708.

> *Example: Sporebloom Siren (2/2, Poisonous) attacks; the defender casts Phytochemical Protection on Jollyglop and blocks with it. The 2 damage is prevented: Jollyglop gets no -1/-1 counters and makes no 1/1s, and Phytochemical Protection puts two +1/+1 counters on it.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1354148437355925554#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 24-wood-b.test.ts, 387-raq-combat.test.ts, 82-attr-interactions.test.ts · Example test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Poisonous: a shielded Jollyglop hit by a Poisonous unit · Key: attr.poisonous.prevention</sub>

<a id="r802.18g"></a>**802.18g** Poisonous changes only damage dealt to units. Damage a Poisonous source deals to a player is ordinary damage.

> *Example: An unblocked Poisonous column with 3 power makes the defending player lose 3 life.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Blightmound · Tests: 42-dark-b.test.ts, 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.poisonous.players — an unblocked Poisonous column with 3 power makes the defending player lose 3 life · Key: attr.poisonous.players</sub>

<a id="r802.18h"></a>**802.18h** Poisonous damage triggers Resonant like any other damage (see rule 802.19). See rule 802.19.

> *Example: A Poisonous and Resonant source deals 2 to a unit. The unit gets two -1/-1 counters, and the Resonant trigger deals 2 to its controller.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.poisonous.resonant — a Poisonous Resonant hit of 2 puts two -1/-1 counters on the unit, and the Resonant trigger deals 2 to its controller · Key: attr.poisonous.resonant</sub>

<a id="r802.18i"></a>**802.18i** Poisonous does not apply in an interaction involving a Pure card (see rule 802.25). See rule 802.25.

> *Example: A Poisonous column is blocked by Just a Unit. Just a Unit is dealt ordinary marked damage, not -1/-1 counters.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.poisonous.pure — a Poisonous column blocked by Just a Unit marks ordinary damage, not -1/-1 counters · Key: attr.poisonous.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.18j"></a>**802.18j** The -1/-1 counters a Poisonous source's combat damage puts on a unit are put by that source's controller (see rule 708.8b). See rule 708.8b.

> *Example: A Poisonous blocker deals combat damage to the attacker: its -1/-1 counters on the attacker are put by the defending player, so the defender's Wandering Blightshell ("When you put a counter on an enemy, [Switch1] Draw a card.") draws a card.*

> *Example: A Poisonous attacker's -1/-1 counters on its blocker are put by the attacking player, and the attacker's Wandering Blightshell draws.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Blightmound; card: Wandering Blightshell · Tests: 454-poisonous-counter-attribution.test.ts · Example tests: 454-poisonous-counter-attribution.test.ts::Poisonous BLOCKER: its -1/-1 counters on the attacker are put by the defender, and Blightshell draws, 454-poisonous-counter-attribution.test.ts::Poisonous ATTACKER: its -1/-1 counters on the blocker are put by the attacker, and Blightshell draws · Key: attr.poisonous.who-puts</sub>

<a id="r802.19"></a>**802.19. Resonant.** Resonant is an attribute. Its reminder text, printed under the type line, reads "Whenever a resonant source deals damage to a unit, it deals that much damage to that unit's controller." See rule 802.1.

> *Example: Resonant Form's combat damage to a unit also hits that unit's controller.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1362838395298119912#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Our glossary (not a source): Resonant · Tests: 09-attrs.test.ts · Example test: 09-attrs.test.ts::Resonant: Resonant Form combat damage to a unit also hits its controller · Key: attr.resonant</sub>

<a id="r802.19a"></a>**802.19a** Resonant is a triggered ability of the Resonant source. When the source deals damage to a unit, the trigger goes on the stack, and when it resolves the source deals that much damage to that unit's controller. See rule 706.

> *Example: The Resonant trigger from combat damage waits on the stack after combat, as its source's trigger, and can be negated.*

> *Example: A Resonant effect deals 1 to a unit; the trigger then deals 1 to its controller as damage from the source.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1362838395298119912#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts · Example tests: 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts::the Resonant rider waits on the stack after combat, 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts::CR 802.19a: effect damage riders too · Key: attr.resonant.trigger</sub>

<a id="r802.19b"></a>**802.19b** The damage Resonant deals to the controller is not combat damage, even when the damage that triggered it was (see rule 608.8b). See rules 608.8b, 112.7.

> *Example: Oorblak, which takes combat damage that would be dealt to its controller, does not take Resonant's extra damage; the player does.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1362838395298119912#0 · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Example test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Resonant: the extra damage is not combat damage · Key: attr.resonant.not-combat</sub>

<a id="r802.19c"></a>**802.19c** "That much damage" is the damage the unit was dealt: after Vulnerable doubled it and after any prevention. If all of the damage to the unit is prevented, Resonant does not trigger. See rules 802.11, 112.11.

> *Example: A Resonant source deals 2 to a Vulnerable unit, which is dealt 4. The Resonant trigger deals 4 to that unit's controller.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.resonant.amount — a Resonant source dealing 2 to a Vulnerable unit, which is dealt 4, makes a Resonant trigger that deals 4 to its controller · Key: attr.resonant.amount</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-20 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.19d"></a>**802.19d** Resonant's damage is damage from the Resonant source, so everything that changes that source's damage applies to it: an allied Conduit of Pain adds 1 to it, and Powerful doubles it, even though the damage that triggered it was already doubled. See rules 802.10, 112.9.

> *Example: A Powerful Resonant 2/4 deals 4 combat damage to a unit, and then 8 to that unit's controller.*

> *Example: With Conduit of Pain, a Resonant 2/4 deals 2 combat damage to a unit and then 3 to its controller.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1362838395298119912#1; RAQ 1362838395298119912#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Example tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Resonant: a Powerful Resonant 2/4 deals 4 combat damage, 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Resonant: Conduit of Pain adds 1 to the Resonant damage · Key: attr.resonant.modifiers</sub>

<a id="r802.19e"></a>**802.19e** When both apply to Resonant's damage, an added amount (Conduit of Pain's 1) is added before Powerful doubles (see rule 112.9). See rule 112.9.

> *Example: A Powerful Resonant 2/4 with Conduit of Pain deals 4 combat damage, then (4+1)x2 = 10 to the controller.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1362838395298119912#3 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Example test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Resonant: Resonant + Powerful + Conduit — 4 combat, then (4+1)x2 = 10 to the face · Key: attr.resonant.order</sub>

<a id="r802.19f"></a>**802.19f** Resonant triggers for each unit the source deals damage to. An effect that damages several units makes one Resonant trigger for each damaged unit.

> *Example: A Resonant, Powerful Bellowing Boulder with Conduit of Pain deals 4 to each unit, then 10 to a controller for each damaged unit.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1362838395298119912#5 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 387-raq-combat.test.ts · Example test: 387-raq-combat.test.ts::RAQ Resonant: Bellowing Boulder with Resonant + Powerful + Conduit · Key: attr.resonant.each-unit</sub>

<a id="r802.19g"></a>**802.19g** Resonant triggers only on damage dealt to a unit. Damage a Resonant source deals to a player does not trigger it.

> *Example: An unblocked Resonant column deals 3 combat damage to the defending player. Resonant does not trigger.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1362838395298119912#1 · Tests: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.resonant.units-only — an unblocked Resonant column dealing 3 combat damage to the defending player does not trigger Resonant · Key: attr.resonant.units-only</sub>

<a id="r802.19h"></a>**802.19h** Because Resonant is a triggered ability, an effect that makes triggered abilities cost more to trigger (Crevice Lurker) applies to it, and if that cost is not paid the trigger does not happen. It can be negated while it is on the stack. See rule 111.10f.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1366446116274442291#1 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts, 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ trigger-like attributes: Crevice Lurker taxes Resonant, 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts::the Resonant rider waits on the stack after combat · Key: attr.resonant.tax-and-negate</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-10, D-U20-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.19i"></a>**802.19i** A Resonant trigger caused by combat damage is put on the stack and resolved as other triggers caused by combat damage are (see rules 608 and 609). See rule 609.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 399-raq-fix-combat.test.ts::the Resonant rider waits on the stack after combat · Key: attr.resonant.combat-timing</sub>

<a id="r802.19j"></a>**802.19j** If the Resonant source has left play by the time its trigger resolves, the trigger still deals its damage, reading the source as it last was in play. See rule 714.

> *Example: A Powerful Resonant unit deals 1 to a unit, which is dealt 2, and then leaves play with its Resonant trigger waiting. The trigger still deals double damage, 4, because the unit was Powerful when it left play.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.resonant.source-gone — a Powerful Resonant source that leaves play with its trigger waiting still deals doubled damage · Key: attr.resonant.source-gone</sub>

<a id="r802.19k"></a>**802.19k** Resonant does not apply in an interaction involving a Pure card (see rule 802.25). See rule 802.25.

> *Example: A Resonant column is blocked by Just a Unit. No Resonant trigger happens for the damage dealt to Just a Unit.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.resonant.pure — a Resonant column blocked by Just a Unit triggers no Resonant · Key: attr.resonant.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.20"></a>**802.20. Thieving.** Thieving is an attribute. Its reminder text, printed under the type line, reads "Whenever a thieving source deals combat damage to an opponent, draw a card." See rule 802.1.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Our glossary (not a source): Thieving · Tests: 09-attrs.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 09-attrs.test.ts::Thieving: Slink draws when its column deals combat damage to a player · Key: attr.thieving</sub>

<a id="r802.20a"></a>**802.20a** When a column with Thieving deals combat damage to an opponent, the column's controller draws a card.

> *Example: Slink attacks unblocked and deals combat damage to the defending player. Its controller draws a card.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 09-attrs.test.ts · Example test: 09-attrs.test.ts::Thieving: Slink draws when its column deals combat damage to a player · Key: attr.thieving.draw</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-16 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.20b"></a>**802.20b** The column is the source of the combat damage, so a Thieving column draws one card each time it deals combat damage to an opponent, however many Thieving units it holds and however much damage it deals.

> *Example: Two Thieving units in one column deal combat damage to a player. Their controller draws one card.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1460213341011050536#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts · Example test: 388-raq-blocks-and-windows.test.ts::RAQ Thieving: two Thieving units in one column draw ONE card · Key: attr.thieving.per-column</sub>

<a id="r802.20c"></a>**802.20c** Piercing excess counts: a blocked Thieving column whose Piercing excess is dealt to the opponent draws a card. See rule 802.16.

> *Example: A Thieving and Piercing column is blocked by a 1/1 and deals 3 of excess to the defending player. Its controller draws a card.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.thieving.piercing — a Thieving and Piercing column blocked by a 1/1 deals 3 of excess to the defending player, and its controller draws a card · Key: attr.thieving.piercing</sub>

<a id="r802.20d"></a>**802.20d** If combat damage a Thieving column deals to an opponent is replaced (for example, by Blightsea Polyp, which deals it as rot), the damage was still dealt, and the column's controller still draws a card (see rule 608.8a). See rules 608.8a, 112.12.

> *Example: Blightsea Polyp turns a Thieving column's combat damage to the defending player into 1 rot. The attacker still draws a card.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Tests: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.thieving.replaced — a Thieving column whose hit to the defending player Blightsea Polyp turns into 1 rot costs no life, and its controller still draws a card · Key: attr.thieving.replaced</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-21 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.20e"></a>**802.20e** Thieving applies only to combat damage. Noncombat damage a Thieving source deals to an opponent does not draw a card.

> *Example: A Thieving unit deals 2 noncombat damage to an opponent. No card is drawn.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.thieving.combat-only — 2 noncombat damage from a Thieving source to an opponent draws nothing · Key: attr.thieving.combat-only</sub>

<a id="r802.21"></a>**802.21. Reaping.** Reaping is an attribute. Its reminder text, printed under the type line, reads "When a reaping source kills one or more units, draw a card. It loses reaping until regroup." See rule 802.1.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Our glossary (not a source): Reaping · Tests: 07-cards.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 07-cards.test.ts::Flame of History: Reaping · Key: attr.reaping</sub>

<a id="r802.21a"></a>**802.21a** When a Reaping source kills one or more units, its controller draws one card, however many units it killed.

> *Example: Flame of History kills a unit and its controller draws a card.*

> *Example: Seismomancy kills a unit by damage and draws exactly once.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 4 gate test files · Tests: 07-cards.test.ts, 18-earth-c.test.ts, 263-reaping-counts-the-kill.test.ts · Example tests: 07-cards.test.ts::Flame of History: Reaping, 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts::Seismomancy: a kill by DAMAGE still pays {Reaping} exactly once · Key: attr.reaping.draw</sub>

<a id="r802.21b"></a>**802.21b** A unit counts as killed by a Reaping source however the source killed it: by damage, by -1/-1 counters, by changing its stats, or by destroying it outright.

> *Example: Invasive Reassignment swaps a 0/4 into a 4/0, which dies. Reaping draws a card.*

> *Example: Noxious Demise kills a 1/1 with a -1/-1 counter. Reaping draws a card.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts · Example tests: 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts::Invasive Reassignment: a kill by a STAT SWAP pays {Reaping}, 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts::Noxious Demise: a kill by a -1/-1 COUNTER pays {Reaping} · Demonstrated by test: 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts::Invasive Reassignment: a swap that kills NOBODY draws nothing · Key: attr.reaping.any-kill</sub>

<a id="r802.21c"></a>**802.21c** After a Reaping source's kill has drawn a card, the source loses Reaping until regroup. *(Engine differs, see F-U20-4.)*

> *Example: If a unit had Reaping and killed a blocker in the first battle round, it would draw a card and then have no Reaping in the second round.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; no gate test · Key: attr.reaping.loses</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-11 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.22"></a>**802.22. Blessed.** Blessed is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "Damage dealt by a blessed source causes its controller to gain that much life." See rule 802.1.

> *Example: Godray deals 3 damage to any target, and Blessed gains its controller 3.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Blessed Thing; card: Godray · Our glossary (not a source): Blessed · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts · Example test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Godray: 3 damage to any target · Key: attr.blessed</sub>

<a id="r802.22a"></a>**802.22a** When a Blessed source deals damage, its controller gains that much life. This applies to combat and noncombat damage, and to damage dealt to units and to players.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Blessed Thing · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts, 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::CR 802.22a {Blessed}: combat damage to a player gains too, 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::CR 802.22a {Blessed}: combat damage to a UNIT gains as well, 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::CR 802.22a {Blessed}: effect damage gains its controller exactly that much life · Key: attr.blessed.gain</sub>

<a id="r802.22b"></a>**802.22b** The life is gained at the same time as the damage is dealt. It is not a triggered ability and does not use the stack, and it is gained before it is checked whether any player has reached 0 life.

> *Example: A player at low life is dealt lethal damage by an opponent at the same moment their own Blessed source deals damage. They gain the life first, and survive if it is enough.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Example test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::CR 802.22b {Blessed}: the gain lands BEFORE the lethal check · Key: attr.blessed.simultaneous</sub>

<a id="r802.22c"></a>**802.22c** A Blessed source cannot kill its own controller with its own damage: damage it deals to its own controller is matched by the life that player gains at the same time.

> *Example: Godray aimed at a player damages them and heals its controller on the same check.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts, 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Godray: aimed at a player it damages AND heals on the same check · Key: attr.blessed.own-damage</sub>

<a id="r802.22d"></a>**802.22d** Blessed applies only to damage dealt. A kill without damage, and damage that is prevented, gain no life. See rule 112.11.

> *Example: Noxious Demise carrying a Blessed Thing virus kills a unit with a -1/-1 counter. No life is gained.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts · Example test: 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts::{Blessed} does not fire on a non-damage kill · Key: attr.blessed.damage-only</sub>

<a id="r802.22e"></a>**802.22e** A unit in a column with a Blessed unit has Blessed while that column exists, so damage its abilities deal gains its controller life too (see rule 802.1). See rule 802.1.

> *Example: Lithoghul attacks in a column with Flzzz (Blessed) and uses an ability to deal 3 damage. Lithoghul has Blessed from its column, so its controller gains 3 life.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts · Example test: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts::CR 802.22e the report · Key: attr.blessed.column</sub>

<a id="r802.22f"></a>**802.22f** Blessed does not apply in an interaction involving a Pure card (see rule 802.25). See rule 802.25.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts::§4 a Pure {Blessed} source gains nothing · Key: attr.blessed.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.23"></a>**802.23. Afflicting.** Afflicting is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "When an afflicting source kills one or more units, those units' controllers gain a rot." See rules 802.1, 112.13.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Umbral Decay · Our glossary (not a source): Afflicting · Tests: 42-dark-b.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 42-dark-b.test.ts::Umbral Decay: two -1/-1 counters · Key: attr.afflicting</sub>

<a id="r802.23a"></a>**802.23a** When an Afflicting source kills one or more units, each player who controlled one of those units gains one rot.

> *Example: Umbral Decay kills a unit with its counters. That unit's controller gains a rot.*

> *Example: Umbral Decay's target survives, shrunk. Nobody gains a rot.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Umbral Decay · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts, 42-dark-b.test.ts · Example tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::CR 802.23c {Afflicting}: a -1/-1 COUNTER kill gives the dead unit's controller a rot, 42-dark-b.test.ts::Umbral Decay: a survivor just shrinks, and nobody gains a rot · Key: attr.afflicting.rot</sub>

<a id="r802.23b"></a>**802.23b** A player gains one rot for each kill, however many of their units the source killed at once.

> *Example: An Afflicting source kills two units of one player at once. That player gains one rot.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Example test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::CR 802.23b {Afflicting}: ONE rot per controller per kill event · Key: attr.afflicting.one-rot</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-12 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.23c"></a>**802.23c** A unit counts as killed by an Afflicting source however the source killed it: by damage, by -1/-1 counters, by changing its stats, or by destroying it outright.

> *Example: Umbral Decay's counter kill gives a rot and draws nothing.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts, 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts · Example test: 156-reaping-and-formation.test.ts::Umbral Decay: an {Afflicting} counter-kill rots and draws NOTHING · Demonstrated by test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::CR 802.23c {Afflicting}: a -1/-1 COUNTER kill gives the dead unit's controller a rot · Key: attr.afflicting.any-kill</sub>

<a id="r802.23d"></a>**802.23d** Afflicting applies to kills by combat damage as well. An Afflicting column that kills units in combat gives their controllers rot.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Umbral Decay · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts, 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::CR 802.23d {Afflicting}: a plain COMBAT kill counts too · Key: attr.afflicting.combat</sub>

<a id="r802.23e"></a>**802.23e** Afflicting does not apply in an interaction involving a Pure card (see rule 802.25). See rule 802.25.

> *Example: An Afflicting column kills Just a Unit (Pure) in combat. Its controller gains no rot.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.afflicting.pure — an Afflicting column that kills Just a Unit gives its controller no rot · Key: attr.afflicting.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.24"></a>**802.24. Lethal.** Lethal is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "Any combat damage from a lethal unit will kill a player." See rule 802.1.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Gublin · Our glossary (not a source): Lethal · Tests: 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts::Gublin: {Lethal} · Key: attr.lethal</sub>

<a id="r802.24a"></a>**802.24a** If a column with Lethal deals any combat damage to a player, however little, that player is killed (see rule 104). See rule 104.1.

> *Example: Gublin (1/4) attacks unblocked and deals 1 combat damage to the defending player, who is killed.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Gublin · Tests: 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts, 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Example test: 44-hybrids-ld-a.test.ts::Gublin: {Lethal} · Demonstrated by test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::CR 802.24a {Lethal}: any combat damage from a lethal unit kills the player · Key: attr.lethal.kills</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-17 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.24b"></a>**802.24b** Lethal applies only to combat damage dealt to a player. It does not change noncombat damage, or damage dealt to units.

> *Example: A Lethal unit blocked by a 2/2 kills it as any unit would; Lethal does nothing to the blocker.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Gublin · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.lethal.combat-only — a Lethal unit blocked by a 2/2 kills it as any unit would, and the defending player is untouched · Key: attr.lethal.combat-only</sub>

<a id="r802.24c"></a>**802.24c** If a Lethal column's combat damage to a player is replaced (for example, by Blightsea Polyp, which deals it as rot), the damage was still dealt, so the player is still killed. See rules 608.8a, 112.12.

> *Example: Blightsea Polyp turns a Lethal column's combat damage into 1 rot. The player is still killed.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23, 2026-08-28 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts, 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::CR 802.24c {Lethal} still kills THROUGH the Blightsea replacement · Key: attr.lethal.replaced</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U12-21 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.24d"></a>**802.24d** [Removed: no source states how Lethal meets prevention of damage to a player, and no card in the pool prevents damage to a player; the owner ruling of 2026-08-23 on prevented damage is about damage to units. See D-U20-22.]

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: not verified; no gate test · Key: attr.lethal.prevented</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-22 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.25"></a>**802.25. Pure.** Pure is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "Pure cards and cards they are interacting with ignore all other attributes." See rule 802.1.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Our glossary (not a source): Pure · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Just a Unit: the exchange is attribute-blind in BOTH directions · Key: attr.pure</sub>

<a id="r802.25a"></a>**802.25a** A Pure card ignores its own other attributes too. See rule 802.12.

> *Example: An Alluring column that is itself Pure ignores its own Alluring and never triggers.*

> *Example: A Pure unit that is also Feeble can block.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Example test: 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::CR 802.15n: an Alluring column that is itself {Pure} never even triggers · Key: attr.pure.own</sub>

<a id="r802.25b"></a>**802.25b** In combat, an interaction is one attacking half-column and the blocking half-column paired with it. If either contains a Pure card, the attributes of both are ignored for that exchange. See rule 608.4.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Just a Unit · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 40-light-c.test.ts::Just a Unit: the exchange is attribute-blind in BOTH directions · Key: attr.pure.combat-interaction</sub>

<a id="r802.25c"></a>**802.25c** In a combat exchange involving a Pure card, neither side has Piercing, Deadly, Powerful, Poisonous, Resonant, Blessed, Afflicting or Thieving, and a Vulnerable unit in it is not dealt double. Neither side has Swift or Sluggish, so both strike in the normal sub-step (see rule 608.2d). See rules 608.2d, 608.6e.
