> *Example: Just a Unit switches off a Deadly attacker's Deadly.*

> *Example: A printed Swift column blocked by a Pure unit strikes in the normal sub-step.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts, 53-playtest-round7.test.ts · Example tests: 40-light-c.test.ts::Just a Unit: {Pure} switches off Deadly, 53-playtest-round7.test.ts::threads {Pure} · Key: attr.pure.combat-damage</sub>

<a id="r802.25d"></a>**802.25d** When blocks are declared, a Pure card in either the attacking column or the units blocking it switches off Flying, Evasive and the lone Sneaky attacker's protection for that column, and a Pure unit's own Feeble does not stop it blocking. See rules 802.2, 802.12, 802.13, 802.14.

> *Example: Just a Unit can block a Flying column, and only it can among the defender's units.*

> *Example: Just a Unit blocks an Evasive column alone.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 40-light-c.test.ts · Example tests: 40-light-c.test.ts::Just a Unit: {Pure} blocks a Flying column, and only it can, 40-light-c.test.ts::Just a Unit: {Pure} blocks an Evasive column alone · Key: attr.pure.blocking</sub>

<a id="r802.25e"></a>**802.25e** Pure does not change a unit's printed stats: a Pure 2/3 is destroyed by 3 damage. But Tough, Balanced and Inverted are attributes, so in an interaction involving a Pure card they do not apply (rule 802.1n). See rules 802.6, 802.7, 802.8. *(Engine differs, see F-U19-1.)*

> *Example: A Tough 0/4 blocks a column containing Just a Unit (Pure). Tough does not apply in that exchange, so the blocker has 4 defense, not 8.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests (3 probes it wrote), all passed; no gate test · Printed: card: Just a Unit; Manual p.42 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Key: attr.pure.stat-attributes</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U19-2 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.25f"></a>**802.25f** Unaware is an attribute, so in combat it does not apply in an exchange involving a Pure card: the units in that exchange are read at their current stats, not their printed ones (rule 802.1n). See rule 802.9. *(Engine differs, see F-U19-2.)*

> *Example: Bubb (Unaware) blocks a column containing Just a Unit (Pure) that has a +1/+1 counter. Unaware does not apply in that exchange, so the counter counts.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; no gate test · Printed: card: Just a Unit; Manual p.42 · Key: attr.pure.unaware-combat</sub>

<a id="r802.25g"></a>**802.25g** Outside combat, an interaction is one effect and one recipient of its damage. Pure applies to each such pairing separately.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-05 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts::§3 one batch, two recipients · Key: attr.pure.noncombat</sub>

<a id="r802.25h"></a>**802.25h** A Pure source deals plain damage to every recipient: its own Powerful, Deadly, Piercing, Electric, Poisonous, Resonant, Blessed and Unaware do not apply, against units or players.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-05 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts::§1 a Pure source · Key: attr.pure.noncombat.source</sub>

<a id="r802.25i"></a>**802.25i** A Pure recipient is dealt plain damage by any source: the source's attributes do not apply to it, and neither do its own Vulnerable and Unaware.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-05 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts::§2 a Pure recipient: the source's Powerful and Deadly do nothing to it, 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts::§2 a Pure recipient's own Vulnerable is off too · Key: attr.pure.noncombat.recipient</sub>

<a id="r802.25j"></a>**802.25j** A recipient that is not Pure, damaged by the same effect as a Pure recipient, is dealt damage with all attributes applying.

> *Example: A Powerful source deals 1 to Just a Unit and 1 to Bubb in one resolution: 1 to the first and 2 to the second.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-05 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts · Example test: 290-pure-outside-combat.test.ts::§3 one batch, two recipients · Key: attr.pure.noncombat.others</sub>

<a id="r802.25k"></a>**802.25k** During a battle, a unit in a column with a Pure unit has Pure for noncombat damage too, as a source and as a recipient (see rule 802.1). See rule 802.1.

> *Example: A unit stands in a column with Just a Unit. A Powerful spell deals 1 damage to it: it is dealt 1, not 2.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.pure.column — a unit attacking in a column with Just a Unit is dealt 1, not 2, by a Powerful effect dealing 1 · Key: attr.pure.column</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-19 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.25m"></a>**802.25m** Pure does not change what can be targeted. See rule 110.

> *Example: Arc Lightning, which says "any target", can target Just a Unit like any other unit.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-05 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts · Example test: 431-cr-attributes-2.test.ts::cr:attr.pure.not-targeting — a target-unit damage spell (Arc Lightning) can target Just a Unit · Key: attr.pure.not-targeting</sub>

<a id="r802.26"></a>**802.26. Modular.** Modular is an attribute. Its reminder text reads "You can apply mods to a modular card from your hand and/or bin as it is played. You still pay their costs." See rule 720.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Spellbind · Our glossary (not a source): Modular · Tests: 43-dark-c.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 43-dark-c.test.ts::Spellbind: {Modular} carrier · Key: attr.modular</sub>

<a id="r802.26a"></a>**802.26a** As a Modular card is played, its controller may apply mods to it from their hand and from their bin, paying each mod's cost. The mods go onto the stack with the card (see rule 702.3b). See rule 702.3b.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 4 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: card: Spellbind · Tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts, 91-modular.test.ts, 425-cr-casting-and-stack.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::{Modular}: mods are applied at cast time, 37-attrs-wight.test.ts::{Modular}: the caster may decline · Key: attr.modular.when</sub>

<a id="r802.26b"></a>**802.26b** Any card in the player's hand or bin whose cost they can pay may be applied to a Modular card, including a card that will do nothing as a mod there. No other condition restricts what may be applied.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 91-modular.test.ts::CR 724.2: the {Modular} menu offers every card you can pay for, 91-modular.test.ts::CR 724.2: a card in the BIN is offered beside the hand · Key: attr.modular.anything</sub>

<a id="r802.26c"></a>**802.26c** Applying a mod to a Modular card is not playing that mod (see rule 701.2). See rule 701.2.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1537748882501668934#0 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 91-modular.test.ts::CR 724.3: "you still pay their costs" · Key: attr.modular.not-played</sub>

<a id="r802.26d"></a>**802.26d** A graft mod applied to a Modular spell adds its graft effect to the spell as an extra part, and the spell and its grafted effects resolve as one. See rule 722.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.33 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 91-modular.test.ts::CR 724.4: a GRAFT mod still contributes its [Switch] effect as an extra part · Key: attr.modular.graft</sub>

<a id="r802.26e"></a>**802.26e** A mod whose type line grants attributes as an augment gives those attributes to the Modular spell's effect. See rule 721.

> *Example: A Powerful mod applied to Spellbind carrying Twin Flame turns its 2 damage into 4.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Example test: 91-modular.test.ts::CR 724.4a: a type-line [Augment] mod really donates · Key: attr.modular.attributes</sub>

<a id="r802.26f"></a>**802.26f** An augment mod's text-box ability does nothing on a Modular spell: a spell cannot gain static or triggered abilities that way.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 91-modular.test.ts::CR 724.4b: an [Augment]-TEXT mod is accepted and does nothing · Key: attr.modular.text-augment</sub>

<a id="r802.26g"></a>**802.26g** A Modular card with a mod applied is modded, so it is Unstable: when it leaves the stack, whether it resolved, failed to resolve or was negated, it and its mods are erased instead of going to a bin. An unmodded Modular card goes to the bin as usual. See rules 803, 405.

> *Example: A graft card in the bin is applied to Spellbind, resolves with it, and is erased, so it cannot be applied this way again.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.35 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts · Example test: 91-modular.test.ts::CR 724.5: the flashback line · Demonstrated by tests: 91-modular.test.ts::CR 724.5: a NEGATED modded Spellbind is erased too, 91-modular.test.ts::CR 724.5a: an UNMODDED {Modular} spell is not Unstable · Key: attr.modular.unstable</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U20-14 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r802.26h"></a>**802.26h** Modular is not shared with the other units of a column. See rule 802.1. *(Engine differs, see F-U20-3.)*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts · Key: attr.modular.not-shared</sub>

<a id="r803"></a>
### 803. Other Keyword Abilities

<a id="r803.1"></a>**803.1.** Some keywords are not combat attributes. Burst and Unstable are printed in purple text and are called non-combat attributes: they describe a card, and generally have nothing to do with combat. The other keywords in this section (Haste, Battle, [once], Ambush and Prophecy) are timing marks, limits and ways to play a card. See rules 802, 720, 204.5.

> *Example: A modded Chitin Shredder attacks in a column with a vanilla unit: the vanilla unit shares its Powerful, but it does not become Unstable.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.25; Manual p.25 · Tests: 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts · Example test: 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts::cr:keywords.abilities.non-combat — Burst and Unstable are not combat attributes: a column shares Powerful but not Unstable · Key: keywords.abilities.non-combat</sub>

<a id="r803.1a"></a>**803.1a** Non-combat attributes are not shared in formation. A unit with Burst or Unstable does not give it to the other units in its column. See rules 712.8e, 802.1.

> *Example: A modded unit is Unstable; a unit in the same column is not, and when it dies it goes to the bin.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.25 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25, 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts, 125-active-zone.test.ts · Example test: 125-active-zone.test.ts::CR 803.1a: Unstable is NOT shared in formation · Demonstrated by test: 298-column-attrs-outside-combat.test.ts::CR 712.8e a modded (therefore Unstable) unit does not make its column-mate Unstable · Key: keywords.abilities.non-combat.not-shared</sub>

<a id="r803.2"></a>**803.2.** Haste is a timing keyword. A card with Haste can be played during the haste step as well as during deployment. See rules 207.3, 504.

> *Example: Tidal Menace, a {Haste} 7/2, can be played in the haste step.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.13; Manual p.13 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 15-water-b.test.ts, 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts · Example test: 15-water-b.test.ts::Tidal Menace: {Haste} 7/2 · Demonstrated by test: 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts::cr:keywords.abilities.haste — a Haste card is also offered and playable during deployment, not only in the haste step · Key: keywords.abilities.haste</sub>

<a id="r803.2a"></a>**803.2a** Printed text that names the "mana step" means the haste step. See rule 504.1.

> *Example: Dispatch Courier says "play a unit during the mana step as if it had [Haste]": its controller may play a unit in the haste step.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.3; card: Dispatch Courier · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts · Example test: 26-metal-a.test.ts::Dispatch Courier: "play a unit during the mana step as if it had [Haste]" · Key: keywords.abilities.haste.mana-step</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U05-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r803.2b"></a>**803.2b** An effect can let a card without Haste be played in the haste step "as if it had [Haste]", as Dispatch Courier does. This changes only when the card may be played. See rules 504.7, 803.3a.

> *Example: With Dispatch Courier in play, its controller can play a unit without Haste in the haste step, once each turn.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Dispatch Courier · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts · Example test: 26-metal-a.test.ts::Dispatch Courier: "play a unit during the mana step as if it had [Haste]" · Demonstrated by test: 26-metal-a.test.ts::Dispatch Courier: no Courier, no OFFER · Key: keywords.abilities.haste.grants</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U05-4 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r803.3"></a>**803.3.** Battle is a timing keyword. A card with Battle can be played only while its player is in battle with another player. It cannot be played during deployment. See rules 207.4, 505.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.13; Manual p.13; Manual p.13; Rulebook 2023 p.3; Rulebook 2023 p.3 · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 803.7i: normal TIMING still applies · Key: keywords.abilities.battle</sub>

<a id="r803.3a"></a>**803.3a** Gaining Haste does not let a Battle card be played outside battle. A Battle unit or Battle spell unit that an effect lets be played "as if it had [Haste]" still cannot be played in the haste step. See rules 207.4a, 504.2a.

> *Example: Dispatch Courier's grant does not let a {Battle} unit be played in the haste step.*

> *Example: Nor does Dispatch Courier let a {Battle} spell unit be played in the haste step.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1464899726796390433#0; RAQ 1465292396664193171#0; RAQ 1465292396664193171#1 · Tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts, 396-raq-timing.test.ts · Example tests: 26-metal-a.test.ts::Dispatch Courier: a {Battle} unit stays a battle card even with the grant, 396-raq-timing.test.ts::RAQ Dispatch Courier: a Battle spell unit is not playable in the haste step either · Key: keywords.abilities.battle.haste</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U05-3 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r803.3b"></a>**803.3b** A [Battle] icon printed in front of one ability or play mode, rather than as the card's timing, governs that line only. An activated ability marked [Battle] can be activated only during battle; an Ambush marked [Battle] can be played during battle even if the card itself has no Battle timing (803.6b). See rules 207.8, 203.5.

> *Example: Grox's [Battle] ability cannot be activated outside battle.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.40; card: Grox · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 43-dark-c.test.ts · Example test: 43-dark-c.test.ts::Grox: CR 705.2 — the printed [Battle] marker is enforced at ACTIVATION · Key: keywords.abilities.battle.per-line</sub>

<a id="r803.4"></a>**803.4.** [once] is a keyword that limits an ability: an ability marked [once] can be activated or triggered only once per turn, tracked for each card. Its rules are in 109.9. See rule 109.9.

> *Example: Unstable Apparition's [once] trigger fires once in a turn and again the next turn.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 33-trigger-fixes.test.ts · Example test: 33-trigger-fixes.test.ts::Unstable Apparition: [once] resets each turn · Key: keywords.abilities.once</sub>

<a id="r803.5"></a>**803.5.** Burst is a non-combat attribute printed on spell tokens. When a player casts a spell token with Burst, they cast every spell token of the same name that they control in that region at the same time. It is all or nothing. See rules 304.11g, 702.7b.

> *Example: Casting one Fireball in the battle region casts every Fireball its controller has there.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.15; Manual p.15; Manual p.15; Rulebook 2023 p.4; Rulebook 2023 p.4; card: Fireball · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-10-01 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 03-stack.test.ts, 69-damage-batch.test.ts · Example test: 03-stack.test.ts::Fireball goes to the stack in battle, Burst casts them all at once · Key: keywords.abilities.burst</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U21-4 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r803.5a"></a>**803.5a** Spell tokens with different names are separate Burst groups. A player with a Poison and a Fireball may cast one, let it resolve, and then cast the other. See rule 304.11g.

> *Example: Casting a Fireball casts the other Fireballs and leaves a Poison alone.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 69-damage-batch.test.ts · Example test: 69-damage-batch.test.ts::CR 803.5a: Burst casts all your tokens OF THAT NAME, and leaves the others alone · Key: keywords.abilities.burst.by-name</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U21-10 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r803.5b"></a>**803.5b** Spell tokens cast together by Burst are still individual spells. They are played at the same time. See rule 304.11g.

> *Example: Two Fireballs cast together go on the stack as two items, each with its own target.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.15; Manual p.15; Rulebook 2023 p.4 · Tests: 358-burst-order.test.ts · Example test: 358-burst-order.test.ts::CR 803.5d: the caster picks each Fireball in RESOLVE order and aims it · Key: keywords.abilities.burst.individual</sub>

<a id="r803.5c"></a>**803.5c** Each spell token in a Burst group chooses its own targets. The tokens do not have to share a target. See rule 110.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-08-22 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 358-burst-order.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 358-burst-order.test.ts::CR 803.5d: the caster picks each Fireball in RESOLVE order and aims it · Key: keywords.abilities.burst.targets</sub>

<a id="r803.5d"></a>**803.5d** A Burst group goes on the stack all at once. Its caster chooses the order one token at a time, in the order the tokens will resolve, and aims each as it is chosen; the token chosen first resolves first. The other players receive priority only when the whole group is on the stack. A lone token is not ordered. See rule 703.4b.

> *Example: The Fireball picked first ends on top of the stack.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-01 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 358-burst-order.test.ts, 358-burst-order-ui.test.ts · Example test: 358-burst-order.test.ts::CR 803.5d: the caster picks each Fireball in RESOLVE order and aims it · Demonstrated by test: 358-burst-order.test.ts::CR 803.5d: a lone token is not asked to be ordered · Key: keywords.abilities.burst.order</sub>

<a id="r803.6"></a>**803.6.** Ambush is a keyword that lets a unit card be played during battle with the effect "Recall target ally, put me into their position in play." See rule 203.1.

> *Example: Mirage Walker's Ambush recalls an ally and takes its formation slot.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Good Whale; Manual p.40; Manual p.40 · Tests: 14-water-a.test.ts · Example test: 14-water-a.test.ts::Mirage Walker: ambush [4bb] recalls an ally and takes its formation slot (CR 803.6e) · Key: keywords.abilities.ambush</sub>

<a id="r803.6a"></a>**803.6a** An Ambush is paid for with the cost printed beside the keyword, not the card's own cost: that mana is spent and its affinity pips are required. See rules 203.2, 203.3.

> *Example: Lurking Slimebeast's Ambush [3b] costs 3 mana and needs one water pip.*

> *Example: With four fire mana and no water pip, Lurking Slimebeast cannot be played as an Ambush [3b]; with one water and three fire it can, and exactly 3 mana is spent.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Lurking Slimebeast · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 14-water-a.test.ts, 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts · Example tests: 14-water-a.test.ts::Lurking Slimebeast: [Battle] Ambush [3b] = 3 mana at one water pip (CR 803.6a, 107.10a), 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts::cr:keywords.abilities.ambush.cost — 4 mana with no water pip cannot Ambush [3b]; 1 water and 3 fire can, and spend exactly 3 · Key: keywords.abilities.ambush.cost</sub>

<a id="r803.6b"></a>**803.6b** An Ambush can be played only during battle. The [Battle] icon in front of the keyword lets the card be played as an Ambush during battle even if the card itself has no Battle timing. See rules 203.5a, 803.3b.

> *Example: Good Whale, a deploy-timing unit, is played as an Ambush in battle into the attacking column.*

> *Example: During deployment, Lurking Slimebeast can be played normally, but not as an Ambush.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.40; Manual p.40; Manual p.40 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts, 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts · Example tests: 08-cards2.test.ts::Good Whale: the parked Ambush mode works, 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts::cr:keywords.abilities.ambush.timing — an Ambush is neither offered nor accepted during deployment · Key: keywords.abilities.ambush.timing</sub>

<a id="r803.6c"></a>**803.6c** The target of an Ambush must be an ally of the Ambush's controller in the battle region. An opponent's unit is never a legal target, even through an effect that redirects targets. See rule 110.

> *Example: An Ambush can target the attacking ally, but not an enemy unit in the battle region, nor an ally that stayed home.*

> *Example: An opposing Enigmatic Warder tries to redirect an Ambush onto itself: the Ambush still recalls its own ally, and the Warder stays in play.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1355466429788328066#4 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 243-ally-and-enemy-scope.test.ts, 49-playtest-round6.test.ts, 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts · Example tests: 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts::cr:keywords.abilities.ambush.target — the Ambush menu holds only allies of the caster in the battle region, 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts::cr:keywords.abilities.ambush.target — a redirect (Enigmatic Warder) cannot move an Ambush onto a unit of the opponent · Demonstrated by test: 243-ally-and-enemy-scope.test.ts::CR 110.4 the ambush legality gate asks for the same ally the ambush effect will · Key: keywords.abilities.ambush.target</sub>

<a id="r803.6d"></a>**803.6d** An Ambush is a targeted effect on the stack. Players can respond to it before it resolves. See rule 703.

> *Example: The ally can be removed in response, and then the Ambush fizzles.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.40 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts · Example test: 08-cards2.test.ts::Ambush fizzles when the target is removed · Key: keywords.abilities.ambush.stack</sub>

<a id="r803.6e"></a>**803.6e** When an Ambush resolves, the target ally is recalled and the ambushing unit is put directly into the ally's position in play: into its formation slot if it was in formation, attacking or blocking, and otherwise into the battle region outside formation. See rules 801.7, 801.7a.

> *Example: Orblish Horroth ambushing a blocker takes the blocker's formation slot.*

> *Example: Mirrorback Ambusher recalls an ally and takes its position.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.40 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts, 14-water-a.test.ts, 19-hybrids.test.ts · Example tests: 08-cards2.test.ts::Orblish Horroth: Ambush swaps into the blocker, 19-hybrids.test.ts::Mirrorback Ambusher: Ambush [2be] recalls an ally and takes its position (CR 803.6e) · Key: keywords.abilities.ambush.resolution</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U21-1 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r803.6f"></a>**803.6f** If, as the Ambush resolves, its target is gone or is no longer an ally of the Ambush's controller, the Ambush fizzles: nothing is recalled, and the ambushing card is put into the bin. Its controller loses both units. See rules 704.6e, 405.2b.

> *Example: An Ambush whose ally changed sides before it resolved recalls nothing.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.40; Manual p.40; Manual p.40 · Designer: RAQ 1355466429788328066#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 08-cards2.test.ts, 390-raq-stack.test.ts · Example test: 390-raq-stack.test.ts::RAQ valid targets: an Ambush whose ally changed sides before it resolves recalls nothing · Demonstrated by test: 08-cards2.test.ts::Ambush fizzles when the target is removed · Key: keywords.abilities.ambush.fizzle</sub>

<a id="r803.6g"></a>**803.6g** Ambushing a unit that is the target of another effect saves it. The other effect does not change targets to the ambushing unit; it fails to resolve (fizzles). See rule 704.

> *Example: A Fireball is aimed at a unit, and that unit's controller answers with an Ambush on it. The unit returns to its hand; the Fireball fizzles, and the ambusher takes no damage.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.40; Manual p.40; Manual p.40; Manual p.40 · Tests: 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts · Example test: 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts::cr:keywords.abilities.ambush.saves — ambushing the target of a Fireball saves it; the Fireball fizzles and does not hit the ambusher · Key: keywords.abilities.ambush.saves</sub>

<a id="r803.6h"></a>**803.6h** An Ambush on the stack is not a spell effect: the card played as an Ambush is a unit, not a spell. An effect that targets, negates or recalls spell effects cannot affect it, but one that names an effect, or a nonspell effect, can. A negated Ambush puts its ambushing card into the bin. See rules 700.1a, 704.4a.

> *Example: Nothyr ("negate up to one target nonspell effect") can target an Ambush on the stack and negate it; the ambushing card goes to the bin.*

> *Example: Void Mandible negates an Ambush on the stack: the ambusher never takes the slot and its target is not recalled.*

> *Example: Dreadwave Devourer, which negates a target spell effect, cannot target an Ambush on the stack, and the Ambush resolves.*

> *Example: Cosmic Reversal ("Recall all other spell effects and spell units") recalls a spell on the stack and leaves an Ambush beside it, which then resolves.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 6 tests, all passed; 4 gate test files · Designer: RQ 1127377066195697725; RQ 1138951204257402973 · Owner call · adopted 2026-10-16 · Tests: 114-literal-dark.test.ts, 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts, 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts, 475-ambush-is-not-a-spell.test.ts · Example tests: 475-ambush-is-not-a-spell.test.ts::Nothyr negates an Ambush: it is a nonspell effect (report 218), 119-play-and-token-events.test.ts::Void Mandible: an AMBUSH is a card played too, 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts::cr:keywords.abilities.ambush.spell-effect — Dreadwave Devourer, which negates a target spell effect, cannot target an Ambush, 475-ambush-is-not-a-spell.test.ts::Cosmic Reversal recalls the spell but not the Ambush, which stays and resolves (report 218) · Key: keywords.abilities.ambush.spell-effect</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U21-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r803.6i"></a>**803.6i** A card in the cache under a live permission can be played as an Ambush, as it could from the hand. Under a fulfilled prophecy it is free; under a glimpse its controller pays the Ambush mana but ignores the affinity. See rules 702.2d, 403.3c.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-04 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 370-cached-virus-in-battle.test.ts, 369-cache-is-the-hand.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 370-cached-virus-in-battle.test.ts::CR 803.6i: a glimpsed Ambush card ambushes out of the cache · Key: keywords.abilities.ambush.cache</sub>

<a id="r803.6j"></a>**803.6j** An effect that plays a card for free, such as Tides of the Cosmos, may play an Ambush card as an Ambush. The Ambush cost is not paid, and a limit on the card's cost reads its main cost, not its Ambush cost. See rule 701.2c.

> *Example: Tides of the Cosmos plays Mirrorback Ambusher as an Ambush: the ally leaves play and the ambusher stands in its place.*

> *Example: With 3 of the Tides budget left, Lurking Slimebeast (main cost 4, Ambush 3) cannot be chosen, but Mirage Walker (main cost 3, Ambush 4) can, and playing it as an Ambush spends no mana.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1396955380000755795#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 404-raq-fix-tides.test.ts, 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts · Example tests: 404-raq-fix-tides.test.ts::CR 803.6j: an Ambush card played by Tides as an Ambush takes an ally place, 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts::cr:keywords.abilities.ambush.tides — the Tides budget reads the MAIN cost, and an Ambush via Tides pays nothing · Key: keywords.abilities.ambush.tides</sub>

<a id="r803.7"></a>**803.7.** Prophecy is a keyword printed on a card's banner as a cost and a condition. A card with a Prophecy banner may be prophesied: its controller pays the banner's cost, and the card moves to the cache with its prophecy attached. See rules 203.4, 801.14, 403.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 803.7: a card with no banner cannot be prophesied at all · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy</sub>

<a id="r803.7a"></a>**803.7a** An effect can give a card a prophecy as it caches the card. The prophecy works as a printed one does once the card is in the cache. See rule 403.

> *Example: Grob caches a unit with 'One Battle Passes' attached, and the prophecy is fulfilled once a battle has passed.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Waxen Witness; card: Grob · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts, 39-light-b.test.ts · Example test: 39-light-b.test.ts::Grob: on attack, up to one unit's controller caches it with 'One Battle Passes' · Demonstrated by test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 803.7a: a cached unit can carry a granted prophecy (Grob / Waxen Witness) · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.granted</sub>

<a id="r803.7b"></a>**803.7b** A card may be prophesied only during deployment. A card whose prophecy condition ends in a [Haste] icon may also be prophesied during the haste step. See rule 504.9.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts, 257-prophecy-release-timing.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 803.7b: prophesying is a DEPLOYMENT action, 257-prophecy-release-timing.test.ts::CR 504.9: a banner marked [Haste] may be prophesied during the haste step · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.window</sub>

<a id="r803.7c"></a>**803.7c** A card is prophesied from its controller's hand. It may be prophesied from the bin only if the card says so, and from the cache only while a glimpse permission on it is live; a card prophesied in the cache stays where it is. See rules 403.8, 801.9h.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Angel of Anguish · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-10-01 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 803.7c: only a card that SAYS SO may be prophesied from the bin, 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 403.8: a GLIMPSED card with a banner may be prophesied where it stands in the cache · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.from</sub>

<a id="r803.7d"></a>**803.7d** Prophesying costs the banner's cost: its mana is spent and its affinity pips are required. See rules 203.2, 111.12.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 313-prophecy-affinity.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 313-prophecy-affinity.test.ts::CR 803.7d: mana without the affinity does not buy a prophecy · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.cost</sub>

<a id="r803.7e"></a>**803.7e** A prophecy's condition counts forward from the moment the card is prophesied. "Two Turns Pass" means two turns after the card was prophesied, not two turns of the game.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 803.7: "One Turn Passes" counts from the PROPHESYING · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.forward</sub>

<a id="r803.7f"></a>**803.7f** In a 1v1 game, both battles of a turn count toward "One Battle Passes". See rule 505.

> *Example: A card prophesied with "One Battle Passes" in deployment, after that turn's two battle rounds, is fulfilled once the first battle round of the next turn is over.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Example test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 803.7: "One Battle Passes" · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.battles</sub>

<a id="r803.7g"></a>**803.7g** Once a prophecy's condition has been met, the prophecy stays fulfilled, even if the state that met it goes away.

> *Example: A card prophesied on "your life is 5 or less" stays playable after its controller gains life back.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Example test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 803.7g: a fulfilled prophecy LATCHES · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.latch</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U21-5 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r803.7h"></a>**803.7h** Once the prophecy is fulfilled, the card may be played from the cache for free, ignoring affinity, as if it were in its controller's hand. See rules 403.3c, 111.13.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts, 313-prophecy-affinity.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 803.7h: a released prophecy is FREE and ignores affinity · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.release</sub>

<a id="r803.7i"></a>**803.7i** A fulfilled prophecy changes what the card costs, not when it may be played. The card is played at its own printed timing, and a [Haste] icon in the banner does not move the release. See rule 504.9a.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-19, 2026-08-30 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts, 257-prophecy-release-timing.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 803.7i: normal TIMING still applies, 257-prophecy-release-timing.test.ts::CR 803.7i: a fulfilled prophecy on a battle card is offered at a BATTLE window · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.release-timing</sub>

<a id="r803.7j"></a>**803.7j** An X spell released by a fulfilled prophecy is cast with X = 0. A variable bracketed cost on it is a cost, not its X, and is still paid. See rule 702.6c.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 36-cache-prophecy.test.ts::CR 803.7j: a fulfilled prophecy releases an X spell for X = 0 · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.x</sub>

<a id="r803.7k"></a>**803.7k** A card whose prophecy is fulfilled may also be grafted or augmented from the cache, for free and ignoring affinity. Until the prophecy is fulfilled, the card cannot be played, grafted or augmented from the cache at all. See rules 403.3a, 403.3c, 720.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts::CR 803.7k: an UNFULFILLED prophecy cannot be grafted, 315-cache-mod-permission.test.ts::CR 803.7k: a FULFILLED prophecy still grafts for free · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.mods</sub>

<a id="r803.7m"></a>**803.7m** A condition that counts units dying, such as Vengeance's "13 Units Die", counts only the deaths its controller witnessed: deaths in a region where that player was present. A player is present in their own region, and in an enemy region once they have attacked into it, until regroup. See rules 601, 604.3a.

> *Example: A player attacks into the opponent's region with a unit, so both players are present there. Two of the opponent's units die in that region: each player counts two deaths toward "Units Die".*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-20 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 314-prophecy-units-die.test.ts · Example test: 314-prophecy-units-die.test.ts::CR 803.7m: combat puts the attacker in the region · Demonstrated by test: 314-prophecy-units-die.test.ts::CR 803.7m: a death is counted only by the seats that were in the region · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.units-die</sub>

<a id="r803.7n"></a>**803.7n** An effect that plays a card for free, such as Tides of the Cosmos, may play a card with a Prophecy banner as a Prophecy: the card is cached with its prophecy attached, and the banner cost is not paid. See rule 701.2c.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Designer: RAQ 1396955380000755795#2 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-09 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 404-raq-fix-tides.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 404-raq-fix-tides.test.ts::CR 803.7n: a card played by Tides as a Prophecy is cached with its banner · Key: keywords.abilities.prophecy.tides</sub>

<a id="r803.8"></a>**803.8.** Unstable is a non-combat attribute. If an Unstable card would enter a bin from an active zone (play or the stack), it is erased instead. See rules 405.5, 407, 803.8a.

> *Example: Aberrant Statweaver, printed {Unstable}, dies into the erased pile, not the bin.*

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Abyssal Evocation; Manual p.25 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 17-earth-b.test.ts · Example test: 17-earth-b.test.ts::Aberrant Statweaver: printed {Unstable} · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable</sub>

<a id="r803.8a"></a>**803.8a** Unstable applies only to a card leaving an active zone. The active zones are play and the stack. An Unstable card that goes to a bin from a hand, the deck, a bin or the cache is put into the bin normally, and is trashed. See rules 400.2a, 405.5.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 125-active-zone.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 125-active-zone.test.ts::CR 803.8a: a printed-Unstable card DISCARDED FROM HAND, 125-active-zone.test.ts::CR 803.8a: a printed-Unstable card binned from the CACHE · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable.active-zone</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U21-6, D-U21-9 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r803.8b"></a>**803.8b** A card may print Unstable on its type line. Oorblak and Aberrant Statweaver do. See rule 204.

> *Example: Oorblak, unmodded, is erased when it dies.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Aberrant Statweaver; card: Oorblak · Tests: 17-earth-b.test.ts, 125-active-zone.test.ts · Example test: 17-earth-b.test.ts::Oorblak: printed {Unstable} · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable.printed</sub>

<a id="r803.8c"></a>**803.8c** An effect may give a card Unstable. It is often given to cards played from the bin, so that they cannot be used more than once: Abyssal Evocation and Spell Excavation give the spells they let you play from the bin Unstable until regroup. See rule 405.9a.

> *Example: A spell played from the bin under Abyssal Evocation is erased after it resolves, never re-binned.*

> *Example: A spell played under Spell Excavation is erased rather than re-binned.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: card: Abyssal Evocation; Manual p.25 · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts, 15-water-b.test.ts · Example tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Abyssal Evocation: a bin-played spell is {Unstable}, 15-water-b.test.ts::Spell Excavation: GRANTS the bin play until regroup · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable.granted</sub>

<a id="r803.8d"></a>**803.8d** Unstable given "until regroup" lasts until regroup, even after the permission that came with it has ended. A spell unit played under such a grant passes it to the unit it puts into play. See rule 506.

> *Example: A bin-played spell unit body is still Unstable in the second battle round, after the permission to play spells from the bin has ended, and stops being Unstable at regroup.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests (2 probes it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 12-fire-a.test.ts, 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts · Example test: 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts::cr:keywords.abilities.unstable.until-regroup — the stamp outlives the in-this-battle permission into round 2, and ends at regroup · Demonstrated by test: 12-fire-a.test.ts::Abyssal Evocation: a bin-played SPELL UNIT stamps its BODY · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable.until-regroup</sub>

<a id="r803.8e"></a>**803.8e** A card is Unstable for as long as it is modded. When a modded card dies or is erased, it and all of its mods are erased. See rules 410.4b, 720.

> *Example: A modded host exchanged out of play by Hooba-Mon is erased with its mods, which reach the erased pile.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.35; Manual p.35; Rulebook 2023 p.15 · Tests: 42-dark-b.test.ts, 37-attrs-wight.test.ts · Example test: 42-dark-b.test.ts::CR 410.4d: the mods reach the public ERASED pile with the Unstable body (CR 410.4b) · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable.modded</sub>

<a id="r803.8f"></a>**803.8f** A spell is modded, and so Unstable, when a Virus is applied to it on the stack or a mod is applied to it through {Modular}. When it leaves the stack it is erased with its mods. See rules 704.2c, 723, 802.26.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22, 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 91-modular.test.ts, 125-active-zone.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 91-modular.test.ts::CR 803.8f: the {Modular} window and the virus window agree, 91-modular.test.ts::CR 724.5a: an UNMODDED {Modular} spell is not Unstable · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable.modded-spell</sub>

<a id="r803.8g"></a>**803.8g** A copy of a modded unit is not Unstable when it is made, because it has no mods of its own. A mod attached to it afterwards makes it Unstable in the usual way. See rule 710.2a.

> *Example: A Borrower of Forms that copied a modded unit is not Unstable and dies to the bin.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 3 tests, all passed; 3 gate test files · Designer: RAQ 1372468222158180424#1; RAQ 1372468222158180424#3 · Tests: 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts, 393-raq-mods.test.ts, 26-metal-a.test.ts · Example test: 26-metal-a.test.ts::CR 710.2a: copying a MODDED unit inherits the mods TEXT, and the copy is NOT {Unstable} · Demonstrated by tests: 403-raq-fix-mods.test.ts::CR 720.7e: a Borrower that copied a modded unit dies to the bin, 393-raq-mods.test.ts::RAQ Borrower of Forms: a mod attached to it after it resolved makes it Unstable · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable.copy</sub>

<a id="r803.8h"></a>**803.8h** Moving a mod moves its Unstable with it. The unit the mod leaves stops being Unstable when its last mod is gone, unless something else makes it Unstable; the unit it moves to becomes Unstable. See rule 720.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 151-copy-and-moved-mods.test.ts::CR 720.7d Rotbeast: a moved augment takes {Unstable} · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable.moved-mod</sub>

<a id="r803.8i"></a>**803.8i** Unstable replaces where the card goes, not its death. An Unstable unit that is destroyed still dies: its death triggers and other abilities that watch for a unit dying see it. See rules 713.8, 801.2h.

> *Example: A modded unit is destroyed. A whenever-another-unit-dies ability triggers, then the unit is erased, not binned.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-22, 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 3 gate test files · Tests: 42-dark-b.test.ts, 43-dark-c.test.ts, 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts · Example test: 432-cr-keyword-abilities.test.ts::cr:keywords.abilities.unstable.still-dies — a modded (Unstable) unit that is destroyed still dies: a death watcher triggers, then it is erased · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable.still-dies</sub>

<a id="r803.8j"></a>**803.8j** Unstable does not stop a unit from being recalled. A recalled Unstable unit goes to the hand as a card; if it was modded, its mods are put into the bin. See rule 801.7b.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.35; Manual p.35; Manual p.35 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 125-active-zone.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 125-active-zone.test.ts::CR 803.8j: RECALLING an Unstable unit puts the CARD IN HAND · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable.recall</sub>

<a id="r803.8k"></a>**803.8k** An Unstable card that leaves the stack for a bin, because it resolved, fizzled or was negated, is erased instead. See rules 704.2c, 406.4.

> *Example: Aberrant Statweaver negated off the stack is erased.*

> *Example: A printed-Unstable virus whose host dies fizzles to the erased pile.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 125-active-zone.test.ts · Example tests: 125-active-zone.test.ts::CR 803.8k: Aberrant Statweaver negated off the stack is ERASED, 125-active-zone.test.ts::CR 803.8k: a printed-Unstable virus whose HOST DIES · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable.stack</sub>

<a id="r803.8m"></a>**803.8m** An effect that itself says to put a card into a bin overrides Unstable. Pull Under ("Delete target unit. If you do, put it and all of its mods into your bin.") leaves a modded unit and its mods in that bin. See rule 101.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-24 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 15-water-b.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 15-water-b.test.ts::Pull Under: deletes the target; it and its mods land in YOUR bin · Key: keywords.abilities.unstable.card-says-bin</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U21-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

## 9. Multiplayer and Formats

<a id="r900"></a>
### 900. General

<a id="r900.1"></a>**900.1.** There are four game modes: live draft, constructed, cube draft and team draft. See rules 100, 901, 902. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.6; Manual p.6; Manual p.6; Manual p.6; Manual p.6 · Key: formats.general.modes</sub>

<a id="r900.1a"></a>**900.1a** The 2023 Rulebook calls cube draft "pre-draft": players draft a complete deck of at least 30 cards before the game begins, then play constructed games with it. See rule 902. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.1; Manual p.6 · Key: formats.general.modes.pre-draft</sub>

<a id="r900.2"></a>**900.2.** A game is played in one of these player setups: 1v1, free-for-all (FFA), teams, or archenemy. See rule 100. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.6; Manual p.6; Manual p.6; Manual p.6; Manual p.6 · Key: formats.general.setups</sub>

<a id="r900.2a"></a>**900.2a** A 1v1 game is played between two players. It is the recommended setup for a first game. See rules 903, 904.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.6; Rulebook 2023 p.1 · Tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 412-cr-general.test.ts::cr:concepts.general.digital-scope · Key: formats.general.setups.one-v-one</sub>

<a id="r900.2b"></a>**900.2b** Free-for-all is described in 903. Team games and archenemy are described in 904. See rules 903, 904. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.6 · Key: formats.general.setups.multiplayer</sub>

<a id="r900.3"></a>**900.3.** A 1v1 game counts as a team game: each player is their own team. Free-for-all is not a team game. See rule 904.

> *Example: With The Silent in play, two spells you have played this battle make your next spell cost [4] more, while your opponent still pays the printed cost: in 1v1 your team is you alone.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.20; Rulebook 2023 p.5 · Tests: 433-cr-formats.test.ts · Example test: 433-cr-formats.test.ts::cr:formats.general.one-v-one-is-team — with The Silent out, each player is billed only for the spells that player has played, as a one-player team · Key: formats.general.one-v-one-is-team</sub>

<a id="r900.4"></a>**900.4.** Where the players sit sets which regions neighbour each other. See rules 601, 904.3. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.11; Manual p.19 · Key: formats.general.seating</sub>

<a id="r900.4a"></a>**900.4a** In 1v1 the players sit across from each other. Each has one neighbouring region. See rule 601.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.11; Manual p.19 · Tests: 433-cr-formats.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 433-cr-formats.test.ts::cr:formats.general.seating.one-v-one — a two-player game has two regions, one per player, and an attack is fought in the one other region with no region to choose · Key: formats.general.seating.one-v-one</sub>

<a id="r900.4b"></a>**900.4b** In a game of more than two players the players sit in a circle, so each player has a player to their left and a player to their right. Each player has two neighbouring regions. See rule 601. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.11; Manual p.11; Manual p.19 · Key: formats.general.seating.circle</sub>

<a id="r900.5"></a>**900.5.** Battle normally resolves one region at a time, in the order of 601. Once players are comfortable with the game, they may resolve at the same time any regions that have no player in common. See rules 601, 505.

> *Example: With an attack and a counterattack, the battle in the defending region runs to its end before the counterattack battle begins in the other region.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.21; Manual p.21; Manual p.21 · Tests: 433-cr-formats.test.ts · Example test: 433-cr-formats.test.ts::cr:formats.general.simultaneous-regions — battle is in one region at a time: the first round ends in the defending region before the counterattack starts in the other · Key: formats.general.simultaneous-regions</sub>

<a id="r900.6"></a>**900.6.** *(Digital client)* The client plays 1v1 live draft and 1v1 constructed only. It has no free-for-all, team, archenemy, cube-draft or team-draft games, and no intent cards. Rules 903, 904 and 905, and the parts of 902 about cube draft and team draft, describe the printed game, which the client does not enforce. See rule 100.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-18, 2026-08-26 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts, 168-three-card-divergences.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts::cr:concepts.general.digital-scope, 168-three-card-divergences.test.ts::CR 900.6 Cinder Scuttler: the · Key: formats.general.digital-scope</sub>

<a id="r901"></a>
### 901. Constructed

<a id="r901.1"></a>**901.1.** In constructed, each player brings their own deck, built before the game, and plays from it. See rules 103, 401.

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.6; Manual p.16 · Designer: RAQ 1451507918171013252#1 · Tests: 34-constructed.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 34-constructed.test.ts::createGame constructed: per-seat decks · Key: formats.constructed.what</sub>

<a id="r901.2"></a>**901.2.** A constructed deck has at least 30 cards. No source sets a maximum.

> *Example: A 29-card deck is not a legal constructed deck.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.6; Manual p.16; Rulebook 2023 p.1 · Tests: 34-constructed.test.ts, 433-cr-formats.test.ts · Example test: 34-constructed.test.ts::checkDeck: min 30, max 2 copies · Key: formats.constructed.deck-size</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U22-7 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r901.3"></a>**901.3.** A constructed deck may hold at most 2 copies of any one card. See rule 901.8.

> *Example: A third copy of a card makes the deck illegal.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Printed: Manual p.6; Manual p.16 · Tests: 34-constructed.test.ts, 433-cr-formats.test.ts · Example test: 34-constructed.test.ts::checkDeck: min 30, max 2 copies · Key: formats.constructed.copies</sub>

<a id="r901.4"></a>**901.4.** Constructed has no shared deck and no packs. See rules 103, 401, 409.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.16; Manual p.10 · Tests: 433-cr-formats.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 433-cr-formats.test.ts::cr:formats.constructed.no-packs — a constructed game has no shared deck and no packs · Key: formats.constructed.no-packs</sub>

<a id="r901.5"></a>**901.5.** In constructed, the draw step and the draft step are taken together as one draw phase: each player draws 4 cards from their own deck, then puts 2 cards from their hand on the bottom of their deck. See rules 503, 408.

> *Example: Turn 1 of a constructed game: each player has their 4-card opening hand, draws 4, and must then put 2 back.*

<sub>Basis: Designer · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.6; Manual p.16; Manual p.16 · Designer: RAQ 1451507918171013252#1 · Tests: 34-constructed.test.ts · Example test: 34-constructed.test.ts::createGame constructed: per-seat decks, opening 4 + draw 4, bottoming open · Demonstrated by test: 34-constructed.test.ts::turn 2 reopens the draw phase · Key: formats.constructed.draw-phase</sub>

<a id="r901.5a"></a>**901.5a** The player chooses the 2 cards and puts them on the bottom in any order. Because every card put on the bottom of a deck goes into the recycle pile, which is shuffled before it is drawn from again, the order has no effect on play. See rule 408.

<sub>Basis: Mixed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.6 · Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-16 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Tests: 34-constructed.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 34-constructed.test.ts::nothing moves until the 2 cards go back · Key: formats.constructed.draw-phase.order</sub>

<a id="r901.5b"></a>**901.5b** For state checks the draw of 4 and the put-back of 2 are one step: a player's units are not checked for death while that player still has 2 cards to put back, so they are judged on the hand that remains. See rules 503, 713.

> *Example: Dreadspawn Horror with 1 card in hand: drawing 4 does not kill it, and after the put-back it is a 4/2.*

> *Example: With 3 cards in hand, Dreadspawn Horror's controller draws 4 and puts 2 back, keeping 5 cards: the Horror then dies.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-10-06 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 4; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 380-no-action-ends-dead.test.ts · Example tests: 380-no-action-ends-dead.test.ts::CR 503.5b constructed: drawing 4 does not kill before the 2 go back, 380-no-action-ends-dead.test.ts::CR 503.5b constructed: 3 cards in hand nets to 5 · Key: formats.constructed.draw-phase.one-step</sub>

<a id="r901.6"></a>**901.6.** A player in a constructed game may make a resource of any element, whether or not their deck holds a card of that element. See rules 106, 502.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-23 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 34-constructed.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 34-constructed.test.ts::deckElements: it is a PRESENTATION default · Key: formats.constructed.any-element</sub>

<a id="r901.7"></a>**901.7.** Card text that refers to a constructed format applies in a constructed game. See rule 503.

> *Example: Worldbender in constructed: the player skips the draw-4-put-2-back, the hand gains 3 cards, and the player loses 3 life.*

> *Example: Worldbender in a live draft: the hand gains 3 cards and life is untouched.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: card: Worldbender · Tests: 28-metal-c.test.ts · Example tests: 28-metal-c.test.ts::Worldbender in constructed, 28-metal-c.test.ts::Worldbender in a live draft · Key: formats.constructed.card-text</sub>

<a id="r901.7a"></a>**901.7a** The matches of a cube draft are constructed games, so such text applies in them too. See rule 902. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.39; card: Worldbender · Key: formats.constructed.card-text.cube</sub>

<a id="r901.7b"></a>**901.7b** *(Digital client)* The client has a testing mode called "shared", which is not a format. Card text that asks whether the game is constructed treats a shared game as constructed. See rule 900.

> *Example: Worldbender in shared takes the constructed branch: three cards and 3 life.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-08-25 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 137-multiplier-and-mode.test.ts · Example test: 137-multiplier-and-mode.test.ts::Worldbender in 'shared': the default mode takes the CONSTRUCTED branch · Key: formats.constructed.card-text.shared-mode</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U22-10 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r901.8"></a>**901.8.** *(Digital client)* Single Card Duel is a variant of constructed that the client offers. Each player picks a single card before the game, and their deck is 30 copies of that card. See rule 901.3.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 433-cr-formats.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 433-cr-formats.test.ts::cr:formats.constructed.single-card — a duel deck is 30 copies of one card, and a constructed game accepts it · Key: formats.constructed.single-card</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U22-8 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r901.8a"></a>**901.8a** *(Digital client)* A Single Card Duel deck is the one exception to the limit of 2 copies of a card. See rule 901.3.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 433-cr-formats.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 433-cr-formats.test.ts::cr:formats.constructed.single-card.copies — the duel deck breaks the two-copy cap: checkDeck refuses it, checkSingleDeck and createGame accept it · Key: formats.constructed.single-card.copies</sub>

<a id="r901.8b"></a>**901.8b** *(Digital client)* A Single Card Duel has no draw phase. Each turn, each player simply draws 2 cards; nothing is put back. The opening hand is still 4 cards. See rule 503.

> *Example: Each player starts turn 1 with 6 cards (4 + 2) and nothing to put back, and draws exactly 2 more on turn 2.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 433-cr-formats.test.ts · Example test: 433-cr-formats.test.ts::cr:formats.constructed.single-card.no-draw-phase — opening 4, a flat 2 each turn, nothing put back · Key: formats.constructed.single-card.no-draw-phase</sub>

<a id="r901.8c"></a>**901.8c** *(Digital client)* If neither player's card can make a unit, the game is not played. It is a draw: each player is told the other's card, and both choose again. A card can make a unit if it is a unit or spell-unit card, or if it creates a unit token. See rule 104.

> *Example: A unit card and Self-Assembly (which creates a Robot unit token) can make a unit; a spell that creates no unit cannot.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-18 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test (a probe it wrote), passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 433-cr-formats.test.ts · Example test: 433-cr-formats.test.ts::cr:formats.constructed.single-card.no-units — makesUnits is true for a unit and a unit-token maker, false for a spell that makes none · Key: formats.constructed.single-card.no-units</sub>

<a id="r902"></a>
### 902. Draft and Cube

<a id="r902.1"></a>**902.1.** In live draft, the players share one deck, built from the chosen elements, and draft cards from it during the game. See rules 103, 401, 409.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.6; Manual p.6; Rulebook 2023 p.1 · Tests: 20-draft.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 20-draft.test.ts::createGame draft: 6-card hands · Key: formats.draft.live-draft</sub>

<a id="r902.1a"></a>**902.1a** Live draft is the standard Algomancy format, and 1v1 live draft is the format suggested for learning the game. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Rulebook 2023 p.1; Manual p.10 · Key: formats.draft.live-draft.standard</sub>

<a id="r902.2"></a>**902.2.** A live draft uses 3 elements for 2–3 players and 4 elements for 4–6 players. For 6 or more players, a cube draft with all 5 elements is recommended instead of a live draft. See rules 105, 103.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.11; Manual p.11; Manual p.11 · Tests: 412-cr-general.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 412-cr-general.test.ts::cr:concepts.starting.live-draft.elements · Key: formats.draft.elements</sub>

<a id="r902.2a"></a>**902.2a** In casual games, players take turns choosing the elements, or assign them randomly. The printed rules defer the competitive procedure to Algomancy.io. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.11; Manual p.11 · Key: formats.draft.elements.choosing</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U22-6 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r902.3"></a>**902.3.** In live draft each player begins with 16 cards to draft from: a 6-card hand (the 4-card starting hand plus the first turn's 2 draws) and a 10-card pack. See rules 103, 503.

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.11; Manual p.11 · Designer: RAQ 1451507918171013252#0 · Tests: 20-draft.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 20-draft.test.ts::createGame draft: 6-card hands (opening 4 + turn-1 draws), 10-card packs · Key: formats.draft.sixteen</sub>

<a id="r902.4"></a>**902.4.** The draft step is described in 503, and the pack, its refresh every N+1 turns and an eliminated player's pack in 409. See rules 503, 409.

> *Example: Turns 2 and 3 draw 2 and reopen the draft step; the packs refresh on turn 4.*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Printed: Manual p.16; Manual p.16 · Tests: 20-draft.test.ts · Example test: 20-draft.test.ts::turns 2-3 draw 2 and re-open the draft step · Key: formats.draft.draft-step</sub>

<a id="r902.5"></a>**902.5.** *(Digital client)* The client lets a live draft be created with custom rules. Custom rules change the deal and nothing else: they never change how a card works.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-14 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts::BL-43 §1a control, 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts::BL-43 §1c a custom deal is ignored outside a live draft · Key: formats.draft.custom</sub>

<sub>Discrepancies: D-U22-9 (discrepancies.md)</sub>

<a id="r902.5a"></a>**902.5a** *(Digital client)* Pack size may be set from 3 to 15 cards (standard 10). Every pack is dealt and refreshed at that size, and the draft step leaves exactly that many cards in the pack. See rules 409, 503.

> *Example: With packs of 5, each pack is dealt with 5 cards, the draft step leaves 5 in it, and the turn-4 refresh deals 5.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-14 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 2; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts, 433-cr-formats.test.ts · Example test: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts::BL-43 §2a pack size · Key: formats.draft.custom.pack-size</sub>

<a id="r902.5b"></a>**902.5b** *(Digital client)* The number of elements may be set from 2 to 7 (standard 3). The pool is every deck card whose elements all lie within the chosen set. Two elements default to fire and wood. See rule 105.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-14 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests (a probe it wrote), all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts, 433-cr-formats.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts::BL-43 §2c two elements · Key: formats.draft.custom.elements</sub>

<a id="r902.5c"></a>**902.5c** *(Digital client)* The opening hand may be set from 1 to 15 cards (standard 6), the draws per turn after turn 1 from 0 to 5 (standard 2), and the starting life from 1 to 99 (standard 30). See rules 103, 503.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-14 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts::BL-43 §2b opening hand, draws per turn and starting life · Key: formats.draft.custom.numbers</sub>

<a id="r902.5d"></a>**902.5d** *(Digital client)* With "simple cards only", the pool holds only cards with the silver (Simple) complexity symbol. See rule 209.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-14 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 297-custom-rules-resolve.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 297-custom-rules-resolve.test.ts::BL-43 resolve §3 Simple cards only leaves out exactly the cards that are not simple · Key: formats.draft.custom.simple</sub>

<a id="r902.5e"></a>**902.5e** *(Digital client)* Cards may be banned by name, and an advanced card filter may be set: only cards that match it are in the pool. A banned or filtered-out card is nowhere in the game.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-14 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts, 297-custom-rules-resolve.test.ts · Demonstrated by tests: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts::BL-43 §3 an excluded card is nowhere in the game, 297-custom-rules-resolve.test.ts::BL-43 resolve §5 bans and the card filter add up · Key: formats.draft.custom.bans</sub>

<a id="r902.5f"></a>**902.5f** *(Digital client)* Custom rules do not change the pack refresh: it still comes every N+1 turns. See rule 409.

> *Example: With packs of 5 the turn-4 refresh still comes, and deals 5.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-14 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts · Example test: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts::BL-43 §2a pack size · Key: formats.draft.custom.refresh</sub>

<a id="r902.5g"></a>**902.5g** *(Digital client)* A custom pool must hold at least 2 × hand + 4 × pack + 6 × draws cards (64 for the standard game). Custom rules below that floor are refused before the game is created. When the elements are to be chosen later, every set of that size must pass.

> *Example: The standard game needs 64 cards, the beginner deal 44.*

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-14 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 2 tests, all passed; 2 gate test files · Tests: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts, 297-custom-rules-resolve.test.ts · Example test: 296-custom-draft-deal.test.ts::BL-43 §5 minPool · Demonstrated by test: 297-custom-rules-resolve.test.ts::BL-43 resolve §8 too small a pool is refused · Key: formats.draft.custom.floor</sub>

<a id="r902.5h"></a>**902.5h** *(Digital client)* Custom rules are not printed rules. Packs of other than 10 cards are not in the printed rules, and the client's Beginner preset (two elements, simple cards only, packs of 5) is the client's own softening of the Quick Start.

<sub>Basis: Owner ruling, adopted 2026-09-14 (quoted from the retired ruling register) · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran 1 test, passed; 1 gate test file · Tests: 298-custom-rules-ui.test.ts · Demonstrated by test: 298-custom-rules-ui.test.ts::BL-43 ui §2 the Beginner preset · Key: formats.draft.custom.not-printed</sub>

<a id="r902.6"></a>**902.6.** Cube draft is a format for large groups (6 to 10 or more players). The players draft decks before the game, then use them to play constructed matches, often in a 1v1 tournament bracket. See rule 901. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.39; Manual p.39; Manual p.39; Manual p.6 · Key: formats.draft.cube</sub>

<a id="r902.6a"></a>**902.6a** The cube is all of the game cards, hybrids included, shuffled together: 320 cards from one box. For more than 8 players, two complete sets are used (640 cards). *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.39; Manual p.39; Manual p.39; Manual p.39 · Key: formats.draft.cube.the-cube</sub>

<a id="r902.6b"></a>**902.6b** To draft, deal each player a pack of 10 cards. Then repeat these steps 15 times, until each player has a 30-card deck: (1) each player draws 2 cards from the cube; (2) players may combine their hands with their packs; (3) each player chooses 10 cards from their combined hand and pack and passes them, as a new pack, clockwise to their neighbour. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.39; Manual p.39; Manual p.39; Manual p.39; Manual p.39; Manual p.39; Manual p.39 · Key: formats.draft.cube.procedure</sub>

<a id="r902.6c"></a>**902.6c** Players then play constructed matches with the 30-card decks they drafted. See rules 901, 901.7. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.39 · Key: formats.draft.cube.decks</sub>

<a id="r902.7"></a>**902.7.** A traditional cube draft may be used instead. Each player is dealt three packs of 13 to 15 cards: 15 cards for 6 players, 13 for 8 players. *(Untested: no executed test demonstrates it.)*

<sub>Basis: Printed · Verified: confirmed in round 1; verifier ran no tests; no gate test · Printed: Manual p.39; Manual p.39; Manual p.39 · Key: formats.draft.cube-traditional</sub>
